articles.title: Cuts to Chinese CSP Demand Expecting to Slow Memory Industry Revenue Growth in 2027
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Cuts to Chinese CSP Demand Expecting to Slow Memory Industry Revenue Growth in 2027
TrendForce's latest memory industry research indicates that Chinese Cloud Service Providers (CSPs) have reduced their 2027 memory orders, putting downward pressure on the industry's price outlook. The NAND Flash market is expected to enter a downward pricing cycle as supply continues to expand, prompting TrendForce to lower its 2027 NAND Flash revenue forecast to approximately US$419.3 billion.
Meanwhile, although the DRAM market is expected to remain undersupplied, quarterly price increases are projected to moderate. This has led TrendForce to revise its 2027 DRAM revenue forecast downward to $1.15 trillion.In the NAND Flash market, Chinese CSPs began scaling back their enterprise SSD procurement plans for 2027 in mid-4Q26 amid concerns over GPU supply shortages. These reductions have exceeded the additional orders placed by North American CSPs.
For consumer electronics products such as PCs and smartphones, low-cost memory inventories have been depleted, and device prices face upward pressure in 2027. Brands are expected to reduce NAND Flash capacity specifications across their product portfolios to keep bill-of-materials (BOM) costs under control. Together, these factors will weigh on NAND Flash bit demand growth in 2027.
On the supply side, however, some manufacturers will continue expanding production capacity, while process technology migrations at other suppliers will further increase bit output. As a result, NAND Flash supply is expected to grow significantly in 2027, reinforcing an oversupplied market and pushing overall contract prices lower. TrendForce has therefore revised its 2027 NAND Flash industry revenue forecast downward to $419.3 billion, representing 29% YoY growth.
In the DRAM market, some Chinese CSPs began reducing their 2027 server DRAM bit demand outside long-term agreements (LTAs) in early 4Q26. However, North American CSPs quickly absorbed the resulting supply availability, keeping overall DRAM bit demand on a strong growth trajectory for the year.
DRAM bit supply is expected to continue growing year-over-year as major manufacturers expand wafer capacity and migrate to more advanced process technologies.
TrendForce expects DRAM supply to remain tight throughout 2027, although quarterly contract price increases are projected to narrow progressively, potentially leveling off in the second half of the year. As a result, TrendForce has lowered its full-year DRAM revenue forecast to $1.15 trillion, representing 69% YoY growth.

articles.title: The process gap holding back enterprise AI
articles.text:
The process gap holding back enterprise AI
AI budgets keep climbing. Legacy processes are why returns stall
Current enterprise AI investment is drastically outpacing its impact. Budgets are growing and AI agents are spreading across business operations, yet many organizations have committed to AI faster than they can evaluate it and still cannot show what the spending has returned.
The gap between AI spend and results has little to do with the capability of AI models. Instead, it’s the processes AI is being asked to run that hold it back. In large organizations, from banks and insurers to manufacturers and healthcare providers, almost every process is legacy. That isn’t because they are old, but because they were designed before AI tools.
Senior Vice President of Customer Success at Camunda.
These processes were built around people handing work to one another, and each new customer requirement or regulatory shift has added more steps over time. Layered onto complex and outdated processes, AI must wait for the same sign-offs a person would, so the work moves no faster than before.
Each time an agent finishes its part of a task, the work lands back in a queue waiting for someone to pick it up. Controls built for people also struggle to govern what AI does, opening gaps the process was never designed to close. As a result, organizations end up paying for AI without getting the speed or scale it was bought for.
Under significant pressure to show AI in production, many organizations take the shortcut and bolt the technology onto the processes they already have. New research shows the shortcut isn’t working. Decision-makers widely acknowledge that adding AI to existing processes faces less internal resistance than redesigning them, yet a clear majority expect their AI investments to fall short without more investment in process design.
The cost of the shortcut
Adding AI to existing processes can look faster and less disruptive in the short term. The approach tends to end in failed projects, along with inflated costs to cover the redesign work that eventually becomes unavoidable. At many organizations, process-related challenges have sunk AI initiatives, at an average cost of $1.55 million each. Usage-based pricing adds to the bill, as AI runs on work that never needed it.
The approach also carries risk. Compliance and governance incidents linked to AI have become a regular occurrence, and process-related challenges sit behind most of them. When controls sit in the wrong places, audit trails can’t show how a decision was reached, an issue that is particularly pressing for highly regulated sectors such as financial services or healthcare.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Solving the problem isn’t a quick fix. Decision-makers expect that adapting their most important processes for AI will stretch across several years, while compliance concerns hold back the redesigns that would reduce their exposure. The work also rarely gets the funding it needs, leaving AI running through the same processes that caused the problems in the first place.
Rebuilding processes around AI
Closing the gap means redesigning processes around what AI makes possible, instead of fitting AI into the ones it inherits.
In practice, that means AI agents, people and systems working together within one governed, end-to-end process, with approvals and guardrails built into the design from the start. Predictable steps run straight through, while agents handle exceptions and complex decisions within clearly defined boundaries. In an insurance claims process, for example, an agent can assess a claim and propose a settlement, while the process enforces approval thresholds before anything is paid.
The redesign itself no longer has to take years. AI can now be applied to the redesign work too, reconstructing how a process runs today and generating a redesigned version far faster than manual mapping allows, with people reviewing the evidence before anything goes live. Approved policies can then be reused, speeding up the application across a business.
The people who run processes every day belong in that work from the start. A large share of employees believe they could use AI much more effectively if it were implemented differently, and a significant number have already overridden AI outputs by hand because the underlying process wasn’t set up correctly. They know where handoffs break and where AI output gets checked twice, which makes their input essential to getting the redesign right.
From AI spend to AI results
The pressure on AI budgets is only going to grow. Boards that signed off on early AI investments are now asking what that spending has delivered, and usage-based pricing means every inefficient process adds to a rising bill.
The organizations that see a return will be the ones that treat process redesign as part of their AI investment from the start, funding it properly and involving the people who do the work. For everyone else, investment will keep outpacing impact.

articles.title: Un joystick de una sola palanca, solo 9 juegos y un éxito que impulsó a los videojuegos domésticos: así surgió la Atari 2600
articles.text:
El lanzamiento mundial de Grand Theft Auto VI el 19 de noviembre para PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S vuelve a poner en primer plano la escala que alcanzó el entretenimiento interactivo. El juego de Rockstar Games llegó inicialmente a esas dos plataformas, sin una versión para computadoras anunciada, según el comunicado de su editora, Take-Two Interactive.
La distancia tecnológica entre una producción contemporánea de mundo abierto y las primeras consolas domésticas parece amplia. Sin embargo, el modelo que permite elegir un juego, conectarlo a un televisor y usar un control tiene uno de sus antecedentes centrales en Atari y en la máquina que, con el tiempo, recibió el nombre de Atari 2600, de acuerdo con el Victoria and Albert Museum de Londres.
GTA VI llegó a PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S, las consolas de su lanzamiento
El nuevo capítulo de la serie Grand Theft Auto salió al mercado trece años después de GTA V, publicado en 2013. La decisión de concentrar el estreno de GTA VI en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series X|S mantiene una práctica histórica del sector: cada videojuego depende de las capacidades, los controles y la base de usuarios de un hardware determinado. La llegada a PC no forma parte, por ahora, de los anuncios oficiales de Rockstar.
La relación entre software y consola ya definía el negocio varias décadas antes. En los años setenta, los videojuegos eran principalmente una experiencia de salones recreativos. Nolan Bushnell y Ted Dabney fundaron Atari en 1972, después de trabajar en Computer Space, y lograron uno de los primeros éxitos masivos con Pong. La compañía había nacido alrededor de las máquinas operadas con monedas, pero pronto orientó sus recursos hacia el hogar.
Warner Communications compró Atari en 1976 por USD 28 millones, una operación que dio respaldo financiero al desarrollo de una consola programable. Un año más tarde, la empresa puso a la venta la Atari Video Computer System, conocida por sus siglas VCS. El dispositivo fue rebautizado como Atari 2600 en 1982, cuando llegó al mercado la Atari 5200.
Atari convirtió los cartuchos intercambiables en una costumbre doméstica
La Atari 2600 no fue la primera consola con microprocesador ni la primera que empleó cartuchos removibles. El Fairchild Channel F ya había utilizado ese sistema en 1976. Su aporte fue convertir ese mecanismo en un formato conocido para millones de familias: una sola máquina podía ampliar su catálogo sin necesidad de reemplazar el equipo completo. El lanzamiento de 1977 incluyó nueve juegos y el cartucho Combat.
El equipo se vendía con joysticks de una palanca y un botón, además de controles tipo paddle para ciertos títulos. Esa combinación simplificó la interacción frente al televisor y ayudó a fijar una imagen reconocible de los videojuegos domésticos. La consola difundió las conversiones de éxitos de arcade y también juegos concebidos para su propio sistema, entre ellos Adventure, Pitfall! y Missile Command.
La adaptación de Space Invaders fue uno de sus puntos de inflexión. La versión doméstica, lanzada en 1980, superó los seis millones de cartuchos vendidos durante tres años y aceleró la adopción de la consola, de acuerdo con el Victoria and Albert Museum de Londres. Con más de 500 juegos disponibles a lo largo de su vida comercial, el sistema mostró que el catálogo podía sostener el valor de una plataforma.
Una crisis cambió el mercado que Atari había ayudado a expandir
El crecimiento tuvo un límite. Hacia 1982, la oferta de cartuchos había crecido de forma acelerada y muchas compañías publicaban títulos de calidad irregular. Las ventas comenzaron a caer, mientras Atari enfrentaba rivales como Intellivision y ColecoVision. Las versiones de Pac-Man y E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial quedaron asociadas al exceso de inventario y a decisiones de producción cuestionadas, aunque no explican por sí solas la crisis.
La saturación de productos, la caída de la demanda y el deterioro financiero derivaron en el crash de los videojuegos de 1983 en América del Norte. El Computer History Museum señala que el mercado no recuperó impulso hasta la llegada de la Nintendo Entertainment System en 1985. Warner vendió en 1984 la división de consolas y computadoras de Atari a Jack Tramiel, fundador de Commodore.
La Atari 2600 siguió fabricándose hasta 1992 y vendió cerca de 30 millones de unidades en el mundo, según la cronología corporativa de la marca. Su influencia permanece en productos posteriores: Atari lanzó una nueva VCS para consumidores en América del Norte en 2021 y comercializa reediciones de hardware clásico.

articles.title: Capcom Axes Live Service Game "Exoprimal" After Just 3 Years
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Capcom Axes Live Service Game "Exoprimal" After Just 3 Years
It seems as though Sony isn't the only gaming stalwart struggling to make sense of a changing live-service gaming landscape. Exoprimal launched on Steam in July 2023 with what ought to be a convincing concept: mech suits versus dinosaurs; and it looked like Capcom had big plans for the game. However, it appears as though a compelling gameplay concept just isn't enough in a world flooded with live-service games, as the online PvP shooter failed to even crack 5,000 concurrent players on Steam. 
Now, just over three years since its launch, Capcom has announced that it will be shutting down Exoprimal for good in September 2027. Capcom has not provided a reason for the game shutting down, but it's safe to assume the low player retention is to blame. As of November 24, 2026, Exoprimal players will no longer be able to buy the Survival Pass Premium battle pass tiers. The game itself will be delisted on March 30, 2027, and the servers will shut down on September 29, 2027. There does not appear to be a post-service plan to keep the game alive at all—unlike the recently discontinued Splitgate: Arena Reloaded and Empulse, which both received a final patch allowing peer-to-peer hosting.

articles.title: OpenAI afirmó que GPT-6 diseñó proteínas que se unieron a cinco objetivos médicos en el laboratorio
articles.text:
OpenAI afirmó que su familia de modelos GPT-6 puede diseñar proteínas nuevas usando solo razonamiento y código, sin recurrir a programas especializados en biología. La empresa respaldó la afirmación con pruebas de laboratorio realizadas junto a Onava, su socio de investigación, y con un estudio previo a su revisión por otros científicos.
Las proteínas son las moléculas que hacen buena parte del trabajo en las células: aceleran reacciones químicas, transportan oxígeno y defienden al cuerpo de infecciones. Diseñar una nueva exige definir su forma tridimensional y la secuencia de aminoácidos, sus componentes químicos, que la produce.
Hasta ahora, esa tarea se apoyaba en modelos de IA especializados, cada uno con sus propios requisitos. OpenAI sostiene que un modelo general permite cambiar de tarea con solo modificar la instrucción escrita, sin reentrenarlo.
Según la compañía, un modelo de investigación interno igualó o superó a los especializados en muchas de las 14 tareas de proteínas evaluadas. Todos los datos que siguen provienen de OpenAI.
Qué se probó en el laboratorio
En el primer experimento, GPT-6.2 recibió la estructura de cinco proteínas objetivo, con la zona donde debía engancharse una proteína pequeña, llamada minibinder. El modelo escribió código para generar las formas. Un modelo especializado, SolubleMPNN, propuso las secuencias, y otros ayudaron a elegir qué candidatos fabricar.
Onava probó 322 candidatos. De ellos, 35 (10,9%) se unieron a su objetivo. Hubo 18 aciertos para IL-17A, 8 para VEGF-A, 5 para PD-L1, 3 para IL-7Rα y 1 para TrkA. PD-L1 es una proteína que algunos cánceres usan para evadir el sistema inmune.
OpenAI reconoce que el estudio original de RFdiffusion, un modelo especializado, informó tasas de acierto más altas, aunque aclara que dependen de cuán estrictamente se filtren los diseños antes de la prueba y de cómo se defina la unión.
En un segundo experimento, el modelo debía proponer secuencias nuevas para minibinders ya conocidos. Se observó unión en 75 de 88 diseños para MDM2, 26 de 42 para VEGF-A y 8 de 59 para PD-1. Para tres formas inéditas, 14 de 107 proteínas (13,1%) se unieron.
La empresa dice que, para una misma estructura inédita, el modelo propuso dos secuencias muy distintas entre sí, que difirieron en 44 posiciones, y que ambas mostraron señales de unión. Lo presenta como indicio de que no se limita a memorizar.
Anticuerpos y pruebas por computadora
Con seis anticuerpos pequeños que se unen a IL-4Rα, OpenAI pidió rediseñar los tres bucles con que se agarran a su objetivo. De 182 diseños, 128 (70%) mostraron unión. En 272 fragmentos de cinco anticuerpos terapéuticos, 179 (66%) conservaron la unión a PD-1 o PD-L1.
Las pruebas por computadora incluyeron 30 desafíos del banco MotifBench. En un análisis preliminar, el 43,7% de los diseños del modelo interno más reciente cumplió los criterios, frente al 27,8% de RFdiffusion. En 200 desafíos de plegado, el modelo logró 18,9% y el especializado Proteina, 17,1%.
Las limitaciones figuran en el propio texto. Los diseños de GPT-6.2 puntuaron algo por debajo de RFdiffusion en las mediciones computacionales, y predecir la estructura completa de una proteína sigue siendo, según OpenAI, una debilidad clara.
Además, los modelos especializados participaron en la selección de candidatos y en la propuesta de secuencias del primer experimento. La capacidad intrínseca de GPT-6 se aplica, por tanto, a la forma, no al proceso completo.
El estudio se titula GPT-6 as a Universal Foundation Model for Protein Biology: Beyond Specialized Models y es un preprint, es decir, un texto que aún no pasó por revisión de pares. Las pruebas de laboratorio usaron una versión de GPT-6.2 previa a su lanzamiento.

articles.title: WhatsApp hizo lo que parecía imposible con los stickers: sonarán mejor
articles.text:
WhatsApp evalúa una función que permitiría agregar sonido a los stickers que se comparten dentro de los chats, con grabaciones de voz o archivos de audio de hasta diez segundos adjuntos a cada imagen.
Esta herramienta todavía está en desarrollo y solo se provó en la versión beta de la aplicación para Android, según WAbetaInfo, bajo el nombre de “sound stickers”.
Cómo se agregaría el audio a los stickers de WhatsApp
Al crear un sticker a partir de una fotografía, aparecería un ícono de ondas de sonido en la barra de herramientas. Al tocarlo, la aplicación ofrecería dos opciones: grabar la voz en el momento o elegir un archivo de audio guardado en el teléfono.
El límite para esa grabación o archivo sería de 10 segundos. Si el audio elegido dura más, la herramienta permitiría recortarlo antes de incorporarlo a la imagen, de modo que el usuario ajuste qué fragmento acompaña al sticker.
Un sticker con sonido consiste en adjuntar una grabación de voz o un archivo de audio de hasta diez segundos a una imagen fija o animada, que se reproduce al tocar el sticker dentro de la conversación. El contenido se transmite bajo el mismo cifrado de extremo a extremo que el resto de los mensajes de WhatsApp.
Una vez enviado, el sticker mostraría un ícono de volumen para indicar que tiene sonido asociado. Al tocarlo dentro del chat, se reproduciría el audio adjunto, según describió Android Authority tras probar la función en su dispositivo.
En qué se diferencia de los stickers animados
Hasta ahora, los stickers de WhatsApp podían ser estáticos o animados, pero ninguno de los dos formatos producía sonido. Los animados se mueven al aparecer en el chat, aunque no incluyen audio alguno.
Con el nuevo formato, la aplicación incorpora una dimensión adicional: el sticker aparece igual que cualquier otro en la conversación, pero un toque reproduce el audio adjunto. Esto convierte a los sound stickers en el formato más expresivo que ofrece WhatsApp dentro de esta categoría, de acuerdo con lo relevado por WABetaInfo.
Para los stickers animados creados a partir de videos, la prueba conserva de forma automática cinco segundos del sonido original del archivo. El usuario también tendría la opción de reemplazar ese audio por una grabación propia o por otro archivo almacenado en el teléfono.
De esa manera, un sticker animado podría mantener tanto el gesto visual como la frase o el sonido que lo acompañó originalmente, o bien sustituirlo por un audio distinto elegido por quien lo crea.
Creación propia y llegada a la tienda de stickers
WhatsApp no trabaja solo en sonidos para el catálogo oficial de la aplicación. Los usuarios también podrán combinar una imagen con un clip de audio para producir su propio sticker con sonido y enviarlo a otros contactos.
Un ejemplo de este uso sería convertir un video en un sticker animado para generar, a partir de ahí, un nuevo sticker con sonido. Según WABetaInfo, el proyecto contempla además la llegada de paquetes de stickers con sonido a la tienda de la aplicación, en paralelo a las creaciones que hagan los propios usuarios con sus fotos y videos.
Android Authority encontró, por su parte, un ajuste adicional dentro de la misma pantalla de creación: un interruptor para activar o desactivar el borde que WhatsApp agrega de forma automática a los stickers, un contorno que hasta ahora se incluía sin posibilidad de quitarlo.
Modo silencioso y otros cambios en desarrollo
El sonido de los stickers respetaría el modo silencioso del teléfono: si el dispositivo está en silencio, el audio no se reproduce de forma automática. Existiría además la posibilidad de silenciar el audio de manera manual con el ícono de volumen, una preferencia que se mantendría para los siguientes stickers que se reproduzcan en la conversación.
Android Authority señaló, además, que WhatsApp trabaja en un cambio en la apariencia del cuadro de redacción de los chats. En la actualidad, ese campo ocupa una sola línea y concentra a la derecha los íconos de adjuntos, cámara y otras funciones.
La versión en desarrollo mostraría un cuadro de dos líneas, con esos íconos ubicados en la línea inferior y la línea superior despejada para escribir el mensaje. El medio no precisó el motivo del cambio, aunque no descartó que responda a la incorporación futura de más funciones en esa barra inferior.

articles.title: Hackers Exploited CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm RCE Flaw to Compromise 6 Package Registry Servers
articles.text:
An attacker ran operating system commands on Monday on six production servers of Hex.pm, the package registry that Elixir and Erlang developers fetch their dependencies from.
The flaw used in the attack had been in the registry's code since February 2016, and the team that maintains the service had every server on a patched build within about 15 minutes of the first malicious request.
Checks since then found no sign that any package was changed. Whether the attacker read account data such as email addresses, password hashes, and two-factor authentication secrets could not be ruled out, the team said.
What Hex Users Should Do Now
Everyone with a hex.pm account has been logged out because the maintainers replaced the keys that sign sessions and access tokens. They advise account holders to take these steps:
- Change your hex.pm password.
- Reset two-factor authentication by setting up a new authenticator entry, and store the new recovery codes.
- Log back in to the client with mix hex.user auth or, for Erlang projects, rebar3 hex user auth.
- Update the Hex client when the next release ships, expected within days, with a new registry signing system.
- Watch for phishing. Exposed email addresses may be misused, so check that links in any email about Hex go to hex.pm.
API keys do not need to be replaced, according to the team: they are random 128-bit values stored only as HMAC-SHA256 hashes, which it says cannot realistically be brute-forced. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, which slows guessing but does not stop it for weak passwords, so changing them still matters.
Developers who never created a hex.pm account and only fetch public packages have nothing to reset, Peter Ullrich, one of the report's authors, said in a maintainer clarification on the Elixir Forum. Those who signed up with GitHub should still log back in to their clients, and reset two-factor authentication if they enabled it.
Until the new client ships, the advice is to fetch packages only from repo.hex.pm and to avoid third-party mirrors. The registry signing key has not yet been replaced, and it was among the credentials the attacker could have read.
The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-129514 with the maximum CVSS score of 10.0, sat in the parser hex.pm used to read request bodies sent in an Erlang data format. That parser ran before routing and authentication, so an unauthenticated POST request to any address on the site could reach it.
The decoding function was meant to be safe, and it did block dangerous terms such as functions, but it accepted maps with a __struct__ key, which allowed a request body to pose as any Elixir struct the application had loaded.
The safety check that would have stopped this was removed from the code on February 23, 2016, which is where the flaw's age comes from. Exploitation before Monday has not been established.
A crafted struct ran nothing by itself. It caused an error, and the error reporting code then inspected the struct. That inspection, via the Ecto and DBConnection database libraries, led to a point where the server called a function of the attacker's choice, which then ran operating system commands with the permissions of the registry's service account.
The security advisory lists hex.pm as affected from February 23, 2016 until Monday. The fix commit makes the decoder reject any term containing a map with a __struct__ key, and every hex.pm server was running it by 18:31 UTC on Monday.
Load balancer logs recorded 69 exploit requests between 18:16 and 18:29 UTC on Monday, all from two addresses, the Hex.pm team said in its incident report yesterday. Files created by the exploit appeared on six web servers, in one case just 3 milliseconds after the request. Three of those servers joined mid-attack, when a restart brought up machines still on the vulnerable build.
To check the packages, the team compared every database table against a copy taken two minutes before the first exploit request and traced each difference to normal activity. The 23 releases published during the attack all match the audit log, no older release was changed, and the package and registry files written that evening match the database records.
Database reads, shell commands, environment variables and direct reads from file storage were not logged. For that reason, "we cannot rule out that the attacker accessed data stored in the database," the team wrote. That database holds email addresses, password hashes, API key hashes, two-factor authentication secrets and session data, and private packages could also have been read without leaving a trace.
The checks found no leftover shells and no new accounts or cloud keys in the audit logs. Who was behind the attack is unknown. Activity from the two addresses going back to late last week suggests the attacker built a local copy of hex.pm to test against, according to the team.
A separate security report describing the same flaw arrived by email at 19:07 UTC on Monday, after the attack had ended. By yesterday morning the team had replaced every credential the attacker could have read except the registry signing key. On Monday night it reported the breach to the Swedish data protection authority, to CISA in the United States and to ENISA in the European Union.
Related Library Fixes
Alongside the incident, maintainers of three widely used Elixir libraries disclosed flaws of their own involving structs built from untrusted data, and shipped fixed versions yesterday. These are separate disclosures, not further attacks on Hex.pm.
| Library | CVE | Affected versions | Fixed versions | 
|---|---|---|---|
| ash | CVE-2026-124283 | 3.31.3 up to, but not including, 3.38.0 | 3.38.0 | 
| db_connection | CVE-2026-133555 | 1.1.0 up to, but not including, 2.10.3 | 2.10.3 | 
| flop | CVE-2026-130411 | From 0.8.0, each branch before its fixed version | 0.26.7, 0.27.3, 0.28.1, 0.29.2 | 
Each needs its own conditions to be exploited. The Ash flaw requires keyset pagination with a client-supplied cursor, certain sort field types, and a signing secret left at its unset default, according to the Ash advisory.
The db_connection flaw "is not exploitable in db_connection alone," the DBConnection advisory says, because another component must first decode untrusted data into structs. The Flop flaw has similar conditions around its pagination cursors, according to the Flop advisory.
The exploited flaw sits in the hexpm server code, not in the Hex client, so organizations that run their own copy of the registry are affected until they deploy the patch.

articles.title: Tempted by Aldi's Black Wednesday Special Buys? I've found 5 Black Friday alternatives I'd buy instead
articles.text:
Tempted by Aldi's Black Wednesday Special Buys? I've found 5 Black Friday alternatives I'd buy instead
From coffee machines to LED face masks, these premium alternatives could be worth the extra spend
Aldi is once again getting a head start on Black Friday with its own 'Black Wednesday' sale, with the German supermarket giant offering a selection of seriously affordable tech, kitchen appliances and personal care products as part of its latest round of Special Buys.
And, on paper at least, there are some incredibly tempting offers to be had. An automatic capsule coffee machine for under AU80? An ice cream maker for AU$50? It's easy to see why shoppers might be making a beeline for their nearest Aldi store from today.
But while I'm all for saving money wherever possible, I’m also a firm believer that buying the cheapest option isn't always the most economical decision in the long run. And given the sheer number of excellent Black Friday deals in Australia already available, now is arguably the best time to invest in something a little more premium without paying full price.
That's not to say there's anything inherently wrong with Aldi's Special Buys — we've not tested these particular products, after all — but there are some compelling reasons to consider alternatives from more established brands, whether it's greater functionality, more comprehensive after-sales support or performance we can personally vouch for here at TechRadar.
With that in mind, I've picked out five products from Aldi's Black Wednesday sale and the alternatives I'd be inclined to spend my money on instead.
1. Capsule coffee machine
- Aldi Special Buy: Expressi All-in-One Capsule Machine — AU$79.99
- My alternative: Nespresso Lattissima One — was AU$539 now AU$387.95
I'm admittedly impressed that Aldi is able to offer a capsule coffee machine with integrated milk frothing for under AU$80. But one of the most important considerations when buying a pod coffee machine isn't necessarily the machine itself, but rather the capsules you're able to use with it.
Aldi's machine is designed to work with its Expressi capsules, whereas the Nespresso Lattissima One uses the company's Original capsule system, for which there's an enormous selection of compatible pods from both Nespresso and third-party coffee brands.
The Lattissima One also has an integrated milk system for making cappuccinos and latte macchiatos at the touch of a button, without the need for a separate milk frother.
It's still considerably more expensive than Aldi's machine, admittedly, but with a tidy discount for Black Friday, there's rarely been a more tempting time to invest in the Nespresso ecosystem. Please note that there is a white model available via the same Amazon listing that costs less, but it’s showing as a UK import, which will likely mean it has a UK plug.
2. Variable-temperature kettle
- Aldi Special Buy: Ambiano Glass Kettle with Variable Temperature — AU$34.99
- My alternative: Cuisinart 1.7L Glass Temperature Control Kettle – was AU$149 now AU$89 at Myer
You might question the logic of spending more on an appliance whose primary job is to boil water, but considering a kettle is likely to be one of the most frequently used appliances in your kitchen, I'd argue it's worth investing in a good one.
Like Aldi's offering, this Cuisinart kettle has a generous 1.7L capacity and variable temperature control, although it offers six temperature settings from 50ºC to 100ºC, making it particularly useful if you're partial to speciality teas.
What I particularly like about the Cuisinart, however, is its double-wall construction, which is designed to retain heat while keeping the exterior cool to the touch. Its borosilicate glass construction, drip-free spout and one-handed lid operation are all appealing inclusions, too.
Throw in a three-year manufacturer's warranty and a healthy 40% Black Friday discount, and I reckon there's a compelling argument for spending the extra AU$54.
3. Ice cream maker
- Aldi Special Buy: Ambiano Ice Cream and Frozen Dessert Wand — AU$49.99
- My alternative: Cuisinart Freeze Wand — was AU$149 now AU$79.80 at Amazon
With summer just around the corner in Australia, I can certainly see the appeal of being able to whip up homemade ice cream on demand. And while Aldi's AU$50 frozen dessert maker looks like a fun, affordable way to do just that, I'd also have the Cuisinart Freeze Wand on my radar.
Unlike a conventional ice cream maker, the Cuisinart takes ingredients you've frozen in advance and transforms them into a variety of desserts in as little as five minutes. Its five presets include options for ice cream, milkshakes and sorbets, alongside a dedicated mix-ins function for adding ingredients such as chocolate chips and crushed biscuits.
Its compact design means it won't commandeer too much valuable kitchen space, either, unlike some larger countertop ice cream makers.
Perhaps most reassuringly, the Cuisinart comes with a three-year manufacturer's warranty, which makes spending a little more on this summer-ready kitchen gadget easier to justify.
4. Gaming chair
- Aldi Special Buy: Sohl Gaming Chair — AU$99.99

articles.title: System76 Launches Pop!_OS 26.04 With Major UI and Usability Improvements
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
System76 Launches Pop!_OS 26.04 With Major UI and Usability Improvements
Pop!_OS, the Linux distribution shipped by default with System76's PCs, like the recently released Thelio Prime desktop, has officially been updated to version 26.04 LTS from 24.06. The new update to Pop!_OS has brought with it a host of updates, most of which are aimed at making the distribution and its Cosmic desktop significantly more feature-complete and competitive with the likes of GNOME. The update to 26.04 is largely considered to be a big step for both Pop!_OS and Cosmic, because the Cosmic desktop has been playing catch-up, but it has some highly sought-after power-user design concepts, like the configurable, user-friendly, auto-tiling window management. 
The distribution itself is now on kernel version 7.2.15, although kernel versions aren't tied to a specific version of Pop!_OS, due to its update cycle. The major usability improvements come from changes to the desktop, which, in 26.04, include: new Cosmic Image Viewer and System Monitor apps; new Constellations themes with bundled wallpapers, icons, colors, and fonts; built-in drawing tablet support; an on-screen keyboard with touch and gamepad support; support for automatic system and app updates; remote desktop support; configurable workspace wrapping; variable refresh rate support; improved gaming, especially with Steam Big Picture; improvements to touchscreen support; and individual app volume control.There are also several other accessibility improvements, including shake to find cursor; cursor size options; cursor scaling; and improvements to screen magnifications. Users can also now also define what happens when they start typing in the overview. The built-in Cosmic apps have also been updated to be significantly more customizable and feature-rich, and Pop!_OS also now supports automatic GPU selection for gaming scenarios. 
At release, Pop!_OS 26.04 LTS is running kernel version 7.2.15, Mesa 26.2.3, Wayland 1.26, and the NVIDIA driver 595.104.02, all of which are reasonably up-to-date components, so even newer hardware should have no significant compatibility issues. The full update notes are available here.

articles.title: Hackers Compromise 24 Check Point Management Servers in Suspected AI-Driven Attack Campaign
articles.text:
An unknown threat actor has been using artificial intelligence (AI)-driven offensive tooling in a campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers, impacting 22 distinct organizations across the world.
The intrusion activity, tracked by GreyNoise under the moniker GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13), is assessed to have targeted organizations in the financial services, energy, government, transportation, mining, engineering, and manufacturing sectors across the U.K., Ireland, France, Netherlands, Greece, Germany, Austria, Bulgaria, Poland, India, Thailand, Vietnam, South Korea, Hong Kong, China, Australia, and the U.S.
Confirmed attack activity has been recorded between October 17 and November 2, 2026, with the threat actor using 99 IP addresses to conduct scanning, exploitation, and control. Most of these IP addresses are associated with disposable network infrastructure.
The campaign has not been attributed to any known threat actor or group. It's suspected that the attackers are relying on agentic harnesses and systems for vulnerability scanning, exploitation, and automatic interaction with compromised assets.
The threat actor has also been observed using tools like Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and other Python scripts to carry out internal reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement on victim environments.
"We witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created," GreyNoise said.
In one case, the attackers have been found using an automated scanning and exploitation pipeline to compromise an HFS server using CVE-2026-61500, a critical flaw in Rejetto HFS, in early October 2026 to obtain control of the server and issue commands, including adding an SSH key to the "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys" file.
Subsequently, GT13 is said to have used the compromised server as a relay for follow-on operations centered around saving command results and exfiltrating data from 24 previously compromised Check Point Security Management servers. The attackers also unsuccessfully attempted to deploy a Linux implant named ZULT to the compromised Rejetto HFS server.
"The GT13 adversary had access to the victim Check Point Security Management Servers before they compromised the HFS server," the cybersecurity company said. "We could not determine when or how the attacker gained access to those Check Point assets."
The attackers also moved to burrow deeper into one of the victim networks, using a script for a now-patched Check Point flaw (CVE-2026-16232) to launch over 100 management tasks on multiple Check Point Management Servers to -
- Steal firewall databases and internal certificate authority files
- Mint a new certificate
- Unload security policies, effectively disabling firewall protections
- Conduct internal network reconnaissance and attempt lateral movement
The post-compromise activity also involved attempts to target other enterprise systems, such as Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2023-4966), Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2024-21893), VMware vCenter (CVE-2021-21972 and CVE-2023-34048), Microsoft Exchange (CVE-2021-26855 and CVE-2021-34473), and Microsoft Netlogon (CVE-2020-1472).
In tandem, the threat actor has attempted to exploit various other security flaws, including, but not limited to -
- CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti Connect Secure)
- CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler)
- CVE-2026-41089 (Windows Netlogon)
- CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF)
GreyNoise has theorized that GT13 has in its possession a "mature AI-enabled offensive apparatus" that it uses to weaponize vulnerabilities, scan for susceptible assets, and exploit them to gain access to systems that can be later used as operational relays or true targets.
"The activity reported by the GreyNoise article involves CVE-2026-16232, a previously disclosed vulnerability with patches already available, and does not represent a new vulnerability or exploitation technique," Sergey Shykevich, Director, Threat Intelligence at Check Point Software Technologies, told The Hacker News.
"Our priority remains ensuring customers apply the available updates and follow Check Point’s published hardening guidance to restrict management access and identify suspicious activity."

articles.title: Comment la Russie utilise l'IA pour filtrer le trafic Internet
articles.text:
Le régulateur russe a dépensé 2,27 milliards de roubles (environ 28 millions de dollars) pour un système de filtrage basé sur l’apprentissage automatique. La description du système ne mentionne pas les VPN, mais un expert pense que l’outil pourrait servir à les repérer.
Le programme 2026-2028 de Roskomnadzor, révélé le 13 novembre, ne donne pas de nom à ce modèle. Il tourne sur l’infrastructure du régulateur et ce n’est pas un grand modèle de langage, du genre de ceux qui animent les chatbots.
Repérer un VPN à son comportement plutôt qu’à son contenu
Nous rapportions début avril que le ministre du numérique, Maksut Shadayev, annonçait un renforcement de la répression contre les VPN, après près de 400 services déjà bloqués à la mi-janvier. Le nouvel outil se base sur l’apprentissage automatique. Il s’intègre au système qui pilote les TSPU, des équipements de filtrage installés chez les fournisseurs d’accès à Internet russes.
Ces équipements pratiquent déjà l’inspection approfondie des paquets (DPI). Elle examine les adresses IP, les paramètres de connexion, la taille des paquets de données et la façon dont ils circulent. Elle ne peut pas lire un contenu chiffré, mais ces indices peuvent suffire à repérer un VPN, un peu comme on devine la nature d’un colis à son poids sans l’ouvrir.
Reste à connaître l'usage exact de ce nouveau modèle. Proton explique que le document ne fait aucune mention des VPN. En revanche, selon Dmitry Kuteinikov, du groupe de défense de la liberté d’Internet RKS Global, le modèle pourrait estimer la probabilité qu’une connexion soit un VPN, d’après la taille et le rythme des paquets ou la durée de la session. Mais sans certitude cette probabilité pourrait affecter le fonctionnement des VPN d’entreprise et des services cloud. Un projet de plan national sur l’intelligence artificielle aurait aussi inclus un objectif chiffré : bloquer les VPN avec “95 % d’efficacité”. Les informations rapportées ne précisent pas comment cette efficacité serait mesurée. Le ministère du numérique affirme que la version actuelle du texte ne contient aucune mesure de ce genre.
Proton rappelle que des blocages touchent des plages entières d’adresses chez des hébergeurs depuis août. Depuis début novembre, des messages sur Telegram parlent de serveurs privés, partagés par deux ou trois personnes, qui tombent en quelques heures alors qu’ils fonctionnaient pendant des mois. Aucune mesure publiée ne confirme l’ampleur de cette vague et Roskomnadzor, le régulateur russe d’internet n’a pas commenté. Un test sur quatre serveurs privés donne des résultats inégaux : trois sont devenus inaccessibles après trois jours, huit jours et environ trois mois, le quatrième a tenu quatre mois, jusqu’à ce que son propriétaire l’éteigne. Le projet de budget 2027-2029 réserve par ailleurs près de 60 milliards de roubles (environ 730 millions de dollars) au filtrage du trafic, soit environ le double du montant annuel prévu jusque-là.
Source : Proton

articles.title: Cómo compartir stickers con audio en grupos de WhatsApp
articles.text:
WhatsApp evalúa una función que permitiría agregar sonido a los stickers que se comparten dentro de los chats privados o grupales, con grabaciones de voz o archivos de audio de hasta diez segundos adjuntos a cada imagen. La herramienta, conocida como “sound stickers”, todavía está en desarrollo y solo se probó en la versión beta de la aplicación para Android, según el sitio especializado WABetaInfo.
Pasos para crear stickers con audio
Para probar la función cuando esté disponible, primero hay que ingresar al chat o grupo de WhatsApp deseado. Desde ahí, al crear un sticker a partir de una fotografía, aparecería un ícono de ondas de sonido en la barra de herramientas. Al tocarlo, la aplicación ofrecería dos opciones: grabar la voz en el momento o elegir un archivo de audio guardado en el teléfono.
El límite para esa grabación o archivo sería de diez segundos. Si el audio elegido dura más, la herramienta permitiría recortarlo antes de incorporarlo a la imagen, de modo que el usuario ajuste qué fragmento acompaña al sticker. Un sticker con sonido consiste en adjuntar una grabación de voz o un archivo de audio a una imagen fija o animada, que se reproduce al tocar el sticker dentro de la conversación. El contenido se transmite bajo el mismo cifrado de extremo a extremo que el resto de los mensajes de WhatsApp.
Qué cambia respecto a los stickers tradicionales
Hasta ahora, los stickers de WhatsApp podían ser estáticos o animados, pero ninguno de los dos formatos producía sonido. Los animados se mueven al aparecer en el chat, aunque no incluyen audio alguno. Con el nuevo formato, la aplicación incorpora una dimensión adicional: el sticker aparece igual que cualquier otro en la conversación, pero un toque reproduce el audio adjunto.
Una vez enviado, el sticker mostraría un ícono de volumen para indicar que tiene sonido asociado. Al tocarlo dentro del chat, se reproduciría el audio adjunto, según describió Android Authority tras probar la función en su dispositivo. Esto convierte a los sound stickers en el formato más expresivo que ofrece WhatsApp dentro de esta categoría, de acuerdo con lo relevado por WABetaInfo.
El caso de los stickers animados a partir de videos
Para los stickers animados creados a partir de videos, la prueba conserva de forma automática cinco segundos del sonido original del archivo. El usuario también tendría la opción de reemplazar ese audio por una grabación propia o por otro archivo almacenado en el teléfono. De esa manera, un sticker animado podría mantener tanto el gesto visual como la frase o el sonido que lo acompañó originalmente, o bien sustituirlo por un audio distinto elegido por quien lo crea.
Un ejemplo de este uso sería convertir un video en un sticker animado para generar, a partir de ahí, un nuevo sticker con sonido. Según WABetaInfo, el proyecto contempla además la llegada de paquetes de stickers con sonido a la tienda de la aplicación, en paralelo a las creaciones que hagan los propios usuarios con sus fotos y videos.
Otros ajustes detectados en la herramienta
Android Authority encontró, por su parte, un ajuste adicional dentro de la misma pantalla de creación: un interruptor para activar o desactivar el borde que WhatsApp agrega de forma automática a los stickers, un contorno que hasta ahora se incluía sin posibilidad de quitarlo.
El sonido de los stickers respetaría el modo silencioso del teléfono: si el dispositivo está en silencio, el audio no se reproduce de forma automática. Existiría además la posibilidad de silenciar el audio de manera manual con el ícono de volumen, una preferencia que se mantendría para los siguientes stickers que se reproduzcan en la conversación.
Un cambio adicional en el cuadro de redacción
Android Authority señaló, además, que WhatsApp trabaja en un cambio en la apariencia del cuadro de redacción de los chats. En la actualidad, ese campo ocupa una sola línea y concentra a la derecha los íconos de adjuntos, cámara y otras funciones.
La versión en desarrollo mostraría un cuadro de dos líneas, con esos íconos ubicados en la línea inferior y la línea superior despejada para escribir el mensaje. El medio no precisó el motivo del cambio, aunque no descartó que responda a la incorporación futura de más funciones en esa barra inferior.

articles.title: Heroic Launcher 3.0 Gets Steam and Itch.io Support and UI Overhaul
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Heroic Launcher 3.0 Gets Steam and Itch.io Support and UI Overhaul
Heroic Games Launcher, the open-source game launcher and library management tool for Linux, Windows, and macOS, has officially been updated to version 3.0 in the latest beta release. The move to version 3.0 promises a number of new features and delivers a long-awaited UI overhaul, replete with support for several new themes for extensive customization. The new launcher also has a few added usability improvements, like a new backup system that can help back up logins, system settings, and game settings. 
More importantly, though, GOG has also received support for both Steam and Itch.io games, and there is a new built-in system to manage running Windows games installed via Itch and Steam via Proton and Wine. The launcher also adds Steam integration via Aurelia, an open-source headless Steam client, meaning players can lunch and run Steam games with lower overhead.There is also a new gamepad settings screen for configuring your gamepad, a new download manager, and a new "Add Game" button that has automatic EXE detection for simpler installations. Overall, the new version of Heroic Games Launcher does have a cleaner look, with its newly rounded corners and simpler layout, and the developers behind the project are seemingly aiming to streamline the program to grow its audience somewhat.It should be noted that Heroic Games Launcher 3.0 is still in beta testing, so it may be somewhat unstable. The announcement also comes with an acknowledgement that some of the known issues in V3.0 include that some Steam games, especially those with anti-cheat, will not launch. Native Linux games on Itch.io also aren't supported yet, and the new UI is still under development in Console Mode.

articles.title: Cómo ver tu Spotify Wrapped 2026, qué reproducciones cuentan y qué hacer si no te aparece
articles.text:
Spotify todavía no anunció la fecha de su Wrapped 2026, el resumen anual con las canciones, los artistas y los pódcast más escuchados de cada usuario. Su página oficial solo indica que avisará cuando esté listo y recomienda tener instalada la última versión de la aplicación.
La página de Wrapped 2026 también aclara que alcanza con una cuenta y unas horas de escucha para recibirlo. Mientras tanto, ofrece volver a la lista de canciones de 2025.
El único antecedente oficial es el de la edición anterior: Spotify publicó su Wrapped 2025 el 3 de diciembre de 2025, según su sala de prensa. Fue un miércoles. Cualquier día de 2026 que se mencione es una estimación basada en ese calendario, no un dato confirmado.
Qué hace falta para que cuente tu escucha
Para la edición de 2025, Spotify exigió haber reproducido al menos 30 canciones durante más de 30 segundos cada una y haber escuchado a por lo menos cinco artistas distintos en el año. La empresa no publicó todavía si repetirá esos requisitos en 2026.
Esos requisitos excluían las reproducciones hechas en sesión privada y las de canciones o listas que el usuario sacó de su perfil de gustos. Ese perfil es la interpretación que hace Spotify de lo que escuchas y cómo lo escuchas, y alimenta tanto las recomendaciones como Wrapped.
La edición de 2025 estuvo disponible para usuarios gratuitos y de pago en casi todos los países donde opera el servicio, y se veía en la aplicación para iOS y Android.
Cómo elegir qué reproducciones quedan fuera
Hay dos herramientas. La primera es la sesión privada: lo que se escucha mientras está activa no cuenta para Wrapped. Según la guía de la comunidad de Spotify, se activa desde la foto de perfil de la aplicación y se desactiva repitiendo el mismo paso. Termina sola al cerrar la aplicación por completo o tras un período de inactividad.
La segunda es la exclusión del perfil de gustos, útil para que la música de dormir, la de los niños o una lista de estudio no distorsionen el resumen. El procedimiento, según el centro de ayuda oficial, tiene tres pasos: abrir la lista o la canción, tocar los tres puntos y elegir la opción de excluir del perfil de gustos.
Para revertirlo, el mismo menú muestra la opción de incluirla de nuevo. La exclusión tarda hasta 48 horas en surtir efecto, así que conviene hacerla antes del estreno. Spotify advierte una salvedad: si la misma canción se escucha desde otro lugar, como Canciones que te gustan, esas reproducciones siguen contando.
Ocultar una canción en una lista o posponerla durante 30 días no modifica el perfil de gustos, según la misma página. Esas opciones no sirven para sacar música de Wrapped.
Qué hacer si el resumen no aparece
La edición de 2025 se encontraba en la parte superior de la pantalla de inicio de la aplicación móvil, o buscando “2025 Wrapped” en el buscador. Para 2026 se espera el mismo recorrido, pero Spotify no lo confirmó.
Si no aparece, el primer paso es actualizar la aplicación, porque la compañía pide la última versión. Los moderadores de la comunidad oficial de Spotify añaden que conviene borrar la memoria caché de la app, y que el resumen debería encontrarse por la búsqueda o desde la página de Wrapped.
Si cumples los requisitos y aun así falta, los moderadores de la comunidad de Spotify indican que no pueden modificar los datos ni las listas de Wrapped de un usuario. Algunas secciones dependen del nivel de escucha, por lo que no todos las ven.
Por ejemplo, el resumen de pódcast de 2025 pedía al menos 60 minutos de un pódcast en tres o más episodios y en tres o más días distintos.

articles.title: Com-Affiliated Hackers Hijack Cloud Accounts via Vishing for Data Theft and Extortion
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 has disclosed that it's tracking and has responded to "numerous waves of vishing attacks" orchestrated by Com-affiliated threat actors since August 2026 that have led to data theft and extortion attempts.
The attacks have targeted financial services, healthcare, and legal services located in the U.S., the U.K., and Australia. Other targets include construction, high-technology, transportation, manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, insurance, and real estate sectors.
"The victims share a common profile: they hold large volumes of high-impact corporate data where exposure carries severe regulatory, legal, or market consequences," Unit 42 said. "These attackers targeted financial services organizations about twice as often as healthcare organizations in August 2026, but healthcare overtook financial services in September."
The activity has been attributed to a number of threat clusters, including -
- Bling Libra (aka ShinyHunters)
- CL-CRI-1116 (aka Redact, formerly BlackFile), first observed in January 2026
- CL-CRI-1147 (aka Pink), first observed in May 2026
- CL-CRI-1182 (aka Falcon), first observed in mid-2026
- CL-CRI-1192 (aka Helix and UNC6671), first observed in June 2026
- CL-CRI-1264 (aka Vortex), first observed in September 2026
- CL-CRI-1274 (aka Cinder), first observed in September 2026
Intrusions typically commence with voice phishing, with the attackers posing as IT staff to resolve a purported authentication issue and direct the victim to a phishing page personalized to their organization.
Once the AiTM kit captures credentials and session tokens, the attackers quickly enroll their own multi-factor authentication (MFA) devices, abuse cloud utilities and, in a few instances, deploy malicious browser extensions to exfiltrate data and extort victims.
The harvested authentication data is used to authenticate to victim environments, typically by routing such requests through residential proxy networks and commercial VPNs. They then seek to establish multi-layered persistence by registering their MFA devices, generating cloud infrastructure temporary credentials, authorizing unapproved third-party OAuth applications; enumerate sensitive data; evade defenses by modifying mailbox rules and clearing security alert events; and harvest data from cloud platforms.
"Attackers associated with CL-CRI-1264 establish initial access through vishing, where they pose as internal IT support and direct employees to servers using subdomains tailored to each targeted organization," Unit 42 said.
"These servers act as adversary-in-the-middle (AitM) proxies that pass user credentials and multi-factor authentication (MFA) approvals to the attackers in real time. Attackers have targeted employees on both their corporate workstations and personal mobile devices."
CL-CRI-1264 has also been observed enrolling unauthorized MFA devices within minutes of authenticating to establish persistence, often reusing a single device named Pixel 10a across compromised accounts. The attack chains involve automated data exfiltration using Python scripts to harvest information from Microsoft 365 mailbox, OneDrive, and SharePoint.
Once data is exfiltrated, the threat actor sends Microsoft Teams messages directly to employees at victim organizations, claiming data theft and instructing them to visit a TOR-hosted ransom negotiation site.
The second new cluster to emerge around the same time is CL-CRI-1274, which has also leaned on vishing for initial access and leveraged the Microsoft Graph software development kit (SDK) to collect and exfiltrate data from the victim's SharePoint and OneDrive environments.
"Afterwards, the attackers used a compromised account to send extortion messages internally via email and Microsoft Teams, ultimately directing recipients to a Tor-hosted negotiation site," Unit 42 said.
The cybersecurity company said it also observed the CL-CRI-1192 attackers using a malicious browser extension named "Google Chrome" that's said to have been sideloaded onto the browser after enabling Developer Mode. The add-on performs a number of malicious actions, such as -
- Installing global keyloggers
- Stealing local/session storage and authentication cookies for Microsoft and Google accounts
- Scanning pages for QR codes to capture login/MFA tokens
- Streaming webcam feeds
- Implementing a command-and-control (C2) remote control module via Chrome DevTools Protocol to capture screenshots, dispatch input events, steal clipboard contents, and allow remote site navigation.
"We assess with moderate confidence that the attackers associated with CL-CRI-1192 developed this malicious browser extension as an alternative method to extract credentials from desktop and laptop devices running Chromium-based browsers such as Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge," Unit 42 said.
"The extension might also be shared with and used by other Com-affiliated attackers, although we currently have no evidence to suggest this."
One of the defining traits of the threat actors is their use of "apex" domains that impersonate single sign-on (SSO) portals, IT support pages, and passkey configuration services for each of the targeted organizations.
Also shared among the attackers is an AitM phishing kit called Doko's Panel that allows them to steal authenticated sessions and then abuse them to access connected software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms like SharePoint, Salesforce, DocuSign, and Slack to exfiltrate data of interest.
"The same persona behind Doko's Panel has been observed actively recruiting 'experienced callers' via Telegram, specifying requirements including fluent English with no accent, and advertising six-to-seven-figure weekly returns — evidence of the professionalized vishing-as-a-service model that complements the phishing kit ecosystem," Push Security noted in a report published earlier this May.
Microsoft has also revealed cloud-based intrusions in which threat actors have employed passkey and SSO lures to obtain unauthorized access and add their own authentication methods to set up persistence, as well as conduct high-volume Microsoft Graph activity, SharePoint and OneDrive downloads, and mailbox collection through REST APIs.
"Rather than employing custom tools, the threat actors primarily leveraged native cloud utilities and selectively limited executions and persistence deployments," Unit 42 said. "Cybercriminals like Bling Libra and other Com-affiliated threat actors are pivoting away from encryption, enabling them to move at greater speed across their intrusion lifecycle while still achieving their objectives."

articles.title: US DOJ touts "largest-ever" crackdown on scammers across the globe as it seizes 14,000 devices and $17 billion in illicit funds — operation results in 800 defendants and frees 2,200 forced scam laborers
articles.text:
US DOJ touts "largest-ever" crackdown on scammers across the globe as it seizes 14,000 devices and $17 billion in illicit funds — operation results in 800 defendants and frees 2,200 forced laborers
More than 400 criminal cases have been filed across 85 federal districts in the U.S. alone.
The United States Department of Justice announced today that more than 800 defendants have been charged and over $8 billion in intended victim losses have been recovered in what it describes as the "largest ever" crackdown on scammers and fraudsters in its history. The charges have led to over 400 cases, filed across 85 federal districts, with outcomes including extraditions, guilty pleas, and prison sentences for those involved.
"We are not just going after individual scammers," Fox News reports U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche as saying. "We are dismantling the criminal networks that have been stealing from the American people for far too long."
The push follows President Donald Trump's executive order from March, which required a government-wide crackdown on the kinds of fraud and predatory schemes that people fall victim to each and every day across the country.
FBI Director Kash Patel also gave details of Operation Blackout, an interagency project that targets international fraudsters running centralized facilities. Patel said that FBI agents, alongside their international counterparts, have dismantled 29 centralized compounds across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. The department claims those agents have seized almost $17 billion in funds, that more than 14,000 involved devices have been confiscated, and that 50 "scam actors" have been brought up on U.S. federal charges. The FBI also says its support allowed its foreign partners to arrest or detain more than 320 criminals in foreign jurisdictions.
Perhaps most importantly, these compounds often use human trafficking victims to run online scams. Patel claims that more than 2,200 trafficked workers have been freed as a result of the initiative.
Global scams and hacking are an ongoing problem for the United States and its citizens, not to mention its businesses, big and small. Just last month, more than $5 million in gift cards were stolen from Staples before being used at retailers like Target and Lowes. A Chinese crime ring was behind that attack, which involved more than 15,000 cards.
Earlier this year, a Chinese phishing service was dismantled after it used AI tools to build scam websites linked to almost $2 billion in losses. An October report even detailed a computer, hidden behind a Japanese hotel room fridge, that was responsible for more than 480,000 phishing emails.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The problem is only likely to get worse as the capabilities and availability of AI tools continue to expand. U.S. banks have scrambled to restrict AI agent activity over concerns about what they could do to customer accounts. Some banks raised the alarm after detecting agents accessing customer accounts and even attempting to process transactions. Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo are among those that have blocked the agents while updating their terms of service accordingly.
That growing threat only emphasizes the fact that the department has much work left to do. The $17 billion seized by the FBI is only a portion of the estimated $68 billion Americans lost to scams in 2025, according to Gallup data, so the ongoing game of cat and mouse between the government and criminal enterprises the world over will only continue.

articles.title: US AI data centers over 20MW could now cover more grid costs
articles.text:
'Is it a perfect bill? No...but it’s the bill that we can get right now': US Senate passes legislation to get data centers to pay more for grid infrastructure — but many think it could have gone further
US Senate to force large AI data centers to cover grid costs
- US Senate approves legislation requiring large data centers to pay more
- AI facilities face greater responsibility for electricity infrastructure expansion costs
- Environmental groups warn proposed changes could weaken existing federal protections
The US Senate has approved legislation requiring large data centers to shoulder more of the expenses associated with expanding electricity infrastructure.
The bipartisan proposal seeks to prevent ordinary electricity customers from absorbing infrastructure costs generated by increasingly power-hungry AI facilities.
However, environmental organizations argue that provisions intended to accelerate energy development could weaken existing protections against pollution and environmentally damaging projects.
New legislation to make large data centers pay more for electricity
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 passed the Senate with 62 votes supporting the proposal and 33 opposing it.
Sponsored by Republican Senator Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia, the legislation now seeks additional consideration from the House of Representatives.
Under its provisions, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission would establish financial protections covering data centers with electricity requirements exceeding 20 megawatts.
These facilities would consequently become responsible for a larger portion of infrastructure expenses associated with supplying their electricity requirements.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The proposal also expands federal regulatory authority over electricity transmission development while introducing changes affecting several categories of energy infrastructure projects.
Among these changes are provisions designed to speed up approval processes for renewable electricity, geothermal, hydropower, and offshore energy developments across the country.
Additionally, the legislation would allow FERC to authorize construction of certain interstate transmission projects while removing permitting requirements for onshore oil and gas drilling on nonfederal property.
It also proposes shorter environmental assessment periods and restrictions on circumstances under which previously issued permits could face cancellation or legal challenges.
Environmental organizations question provisions
Although supporters consider the proposal an improvement over existing arrangements, environmental advocates believe its permitting provisions could create substantial problems.
Earthjustice criticized exemptions affecting federal environmental assessments, particularly those involving financial assistance and expansions of existing petroleum transportation infrastructure.
“The bill exempts a wide array of government actions from NEPA, including loans, loan guarantees, and pipeline expansions within existing rights of way,” said Earthjustice in a statement.
The organization also argued that restrictions on environmental assessments could prevent federal agencies from properly considering alternative projects.
Such provisions have attracted criticism because infrastructure acceleration could potentially reduce opportunities to examine environmental consequences before construction activities receive authorization.
Maine Senator Angus King, who supported the legislation, acknowledged that the proposal contained provisions he would have preferred to change.
Nevertheless, he argued that rejecting the available compromise would leave lawmakers without an immediately achievable alternative for addressing electricity infrastructure expenses.
“Is it a perfect bill? No, there are some things in it that I don’t like. If I had written it myself, it may have said some other things. But it’s the bill that we can get right now, and there is no clear alternative to it,” King said
“And that’s why I ended up voting ‘yes.’ It wasn’t an easy choice. I listened to my environmental friends in Maine, many of whom were opposed to the bill; I talked to people in the energy field, particularly in the renewable field, and decided that, on balance, this bill is a lot better than the status quo.”
The Senate previously rejected another proposal addressing data center electricity expenses when Democrats blocked the Ratepayer Protection Act.
That measure sought voluntary commitments requiring computing companies to cover infrastructure improvements needed specifically for their operations.
This new legislation must still pass through the House before reaching President Donald Trump for consideration and possible approval.

articles.title: Word, Excel ou Outlook bloqués par une fenêtre vide ? Microsoft a enfin la solution pour corriger ce bug
articles.text:
Microsoft a corrigé un bug qui faisait apparaître une boîte de dialogue vide au lancement des applications Microsoft 365 et les rendait inutilisables.
Décidément, la fin d’année est rude pour Microsoft. Après la panne géante d’Outlook, Teams et Copilot qui est survenue les 12 et 13 novembre derniers, la firme de Redmond a reconnu qu’un bug interne était à l’origine du problème qui a affecté le monde entier. Quelques jours avant, le Patch Tuesday de novembre a corrigé 1235 failles dont une zero-day au sein d’Outlook. Un nouveau raté vient désormais s’ajouter à cette série noire.
Une fenêtre fantôme bloque l’utilisation de Word, Excel et bien d’autres logiciels
De nombreux utilisateurs l’ont signalé sur Reddit : en lançant Word ou une autre application de la suite Microsoft 365, une étrange fenêtre totalement vide apparaissait à l’écran et refusait obstinément de se fermer. Le résultat ? Impossible d’accéder au logiciel caché derrière.
La firme Microsoft s’est heureusement montrée réactive. Dans une fiche d’assistance mise à jour le 23 novembre, elle a indiqué que le bug, qui touchait non seulement Word, mais aussi Excel, Outlook, Powerpoint, Access et OneNote dans leurs versions Microsoft 365, a été corrigé. Le correctif est disponible dès à présent dans la version 2611 des applications (Build 16.0.20625.20142).
Une ligne de commande peut régler le souci
Il y a cependant un hic : la fenêtre fantôme empêche les utilisateurs de chercher la mise à jour dans les menus de l’application bloquée. Microsoft propose, bien heureusement, une solution : passer par l’invite de commande. Pour installer le correctif, la firme suggère en effet aux utilisateurs de sauvegarder leur travail, de fermer toutes les applications de la marque et d’ouvrir l’invite de commandes en mode administrateur. Il faut ensuite taper l'invite suivante :
"%programfiles%\Common Files\Microsoft Shared\ClickToRun\officec2rclient.exe" /update user updatetoversion=16.0.20625.20142
Les retours des utilisateurs indiquent que la solution marche à merveille. On aurait toutefois aimé en savoir plus sur les tenants et aboutissants de ce mystérieux bug. Malheureusement, Microsoft n’en a pas dit plus sur son origine. On ne sait pas non plus quelles versions des logiciels étaient touchées.
C’est d’autant plus important que le bug semble avoir fait encore plus de victimes : certains internautes se sont retrouvés face à face avec ce même écran blanc au démarrage d’Office, parfois sur des PC qu’ils venaient tout juste de configurer. Microsoft ne semble pas encore avoir fait le lien avec ces nouveaux témoignages, mais le correctif a toutefois suffi à tirer les utilisateurs d’affaire.
