articles.title: WordPress Blocks Six Backdoored WP Connect Plugins Before Malicious Releases Go Live
articles.text:
WordPress has removed six WordPress plugins developed by WP Connect after they were backdoored on November 22, 2026, to enable arbitrary code execution on sites that have them installed, following a suspected compromise of the developer's account.
The WordPress plugins team has independently detected and blocked the threat before it could be officially released. Visiting each plugin listing now serves the message: "This plugin has been closed as of November 22, 2026, and is not available for download. This closure is permanent."
The names of the affected plugins and the malicious versions are listed below -
- Air WP Sync – Airtable to WordPress (2.9.1 – 2.9.4)
- WP Sync for Notion – Notion to WordPress (1.7.4)
- Add-on Brevo for Gravity Forms (2.6.3)
- Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Airtable (2.5.4)
- Add-On for Contact Form 7 to Notion (1.6.4)
- Orders Sync to Airtable for WooCommerce (1.0.2)
These plugins have been collectively installed on more than 3,600 WordPress sites, according to WordPress security company Wordfence. The supply chain compromise is being tracked as CVE-2026-135202 (CVSS score: 9.8). It remains unpatched.
"Each release silently loaded the same remote-control module, which phones home to an attacker-controlled server, executes any PHP code it is sent, and exposes a full command set for running shell commands, stealing password hashes, and planting webshells," security researcher Chloe Chamberland said.
Specifically, the plugins come with a backdoor module ("includes/airwp-online.php") that runs on every request, sends site information (site URL, PHP, WordPress, and OS versions, and the server user) to a hard-coded command-and-control server ("tascredit-pay[.]com"), and runs PHP code returned by the server via eval().
It can also perform the following actions -
- Accept queued commands that run shell commands
- Read, write, and delete arbitrary files
- Query arbitrary database tables
- Dump the users table including login, email address, and password hashes
- Drop a web shell into the uploads directory or to a path of the attacker's choosing
- Register an hourly WP-Cron hook that runs attacker-supplied code
As a result, an unauthenticated attacker in control of the site can execute arbitrary code on the server and take complete control, facilitating credential theft and persistence through web shells and cron hooks that outlast the plugin removal.
Because the malicious versions were never released and blocked due to WordPress's new cooldown protections as part of its Protect The Shire initiative, sites running these plugins are unlikely to be affected. However, it's essential that site owners check their websites to make sure that they are not running one of the compromised versions and remove them as soon as possible.
"Unlike a typical vulnerability, this was not a coding mistake, and there is no patch: the malicious code was added deliberately and committed to each plugin's WordPress.org repository," Chamberland. "Taken together, this strongly suggests that the developer's WordPress.org account was compromised and used to push the malicious releases, rather than that the vendor shipped this code intentionally."
The disclosure comes as URLscan.io revealed that an unspecified WordPress site had been infected by multiple cybercriminal campaigns, with attackers attempting to disable or remove scripts belonging to competing threat actors.
The site carried "thirteen separate ClickFix injections from three distinct kits [LOM, ErrTraffic, and Macfinger], alongside seven further malicious loaders," it said. "Several of the injections attempt to remove each other's code and overlays, and one injection disables another through a JavaScript naming collision. Five of the thirteen injections resolve their next-stage infrastructure from Polygon smart contracts, a technique known as EtherHiding."

articles.title: L'aube d'une nouvelle ère : la Chine embarque le tout premier astronaute étranger dans sa station spatiale
articles.text:
Pour la première fois de son histoire, la Chine ouvre sa station spatiale à un astronaute étranger. Un Pakistanais est désormais en orbite à bord de Tiangong, et c’est un message adressé au monde.
C’est désormais un fait établi : la Chine est une véritable puissance spatiale. En plus de préparer sa propre conquête de la Lune, l’Empire du Milieu travaille également sur une mission afin de se poser sur Callisto, l’une des lunes galiléennes de Jupiter. Mais aujourd’hui, les yeux sont rivés sur sa station spatiale Tiangong.
Une première pour le Pakistan
Ce mercredi 25 novembre, une fusée Long March 2F a pris son envol depuis le centre de Jiuquan, dans le désert de Gobi. Objectif : acheminer le vaisseau Shenzhou-24 jusqu’à Tiangong, avec à son bord deux Chinois, le commandant Tang Hongbo et l’ingénieur de vol Wu Yi, et un Pakistanais, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali. C’est inédit.
Âgé de 40 ans, ce spécialiste des charges utiles est un ancien pilote de l'armée de l’air pakistanaise. Et pour se préparer, il a passé sept mois à Pékin, en apprenant notamment le mandarin. « Je porte le nom du Pakistan sur mes épaules, les espoirs de 250 millions de Pakistanais », a-t-il déclaré avant de partir. Il est le premier Pakistanais à atteindre l’orbite, même si Namira Salim avait déjà volé en 2023 lors d’un vol suborbital touristique.
Si son séjour ne va durer qu’une semaine, il doit malgré tout mener quatre expériences pour l’agence spatiale pakistanaise, sur des matériaux au graphène qui protègent des radiations, une fibre de carbone capable de se réparer seule, des graines de quinoa et des microalgues productrices d’oxygène. Il reviendra ensuite sur Terre avec deux membres de l’équipage précédent, Zhang Zhiyuan et Lai Ka-ying.
La Chine, superpuissance
Ce vol s’impose avant tout comme un geste diplomatique fort. Pékin veut montrer que Tiangong peut devenir une plateforme internationale, alors que la Chine a interdiction de participer aux efforts de la Station spatiale internationale (ISS). Et le choix du Pakistan tombe sous le sens : les deux pays ont signé un accord de coopération spatiale a été signé en février 2025.
Ainsi, la Chine a lancé des satellites pakistanais, tandis que les deux pays partagent un système de navigation, et qu’un rover pakistanais doit voler sur une mission lunaire chinoise en 2028. Le timing n’est pas anodin, alors que la course à la Lune s’accélère. La Chine et la Russie font bloc face aux États-Unis et leurs alliés, et chaque pays entend bien renforcer son influence et sa crédibilité de puissance spatiale.
Mais en attendant, l’agence de presse chinoise Xinhua affirme que cette première pourrait ouvrir la voie à d’autres pays.
Sources : Space.com, The South China Morning Post

articles.title: Revelan si es posible jugar GTA 6 a 60 fps en Xbox Series
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto VI funciona con un límite de 30 cuadros por segundo (fps) en todas las consolas, pero un análisis técnico determinó que un glitch detectado en Xbox Series no permite alcanzar de forma estable los 60 fps, como se había difundido en los últimos días. El estudio, realizado por Digital Foundry, puso a prueba la versión 01.002.001 del juego para verificar el rendimiento real que ofrece este desbloqueo de framerate.
Un glitch que elimina el límite de fotogramas
El hallazgo original consistía en aprovechar la función Quick Resume de Xbox Series junto con pantallas de 120 Hz para desbloquear el límite de 30 fps impuesto por los desarrolladores. GTA 6 no cuenta con un modo de rendimiento a 60 ni a 40 fps debido al nivel de detalle gráfico que exige, por lo que la posibilidad de superar ese techo generó expectativa entre los jugadores.
El propio funcionamiento del truco trae un efecto secundario: las animaciones y otros elementos del mundo del juego dependen directamente del framerate, por lo que al acelerarse este, también lo hacen esas secuencias. Esta circunstancia convierte al glitch en una forma poco recomendable de jugar, más allá del interés que generó la posibilidad de superar los 30 fps establecidos.
Los resultados reales del análisis técnico
Digital Foundry confirmó que el fallo funciona tanto en Xbox Series X como en Series S, aunque esta última consola presenta mayores dificultades incluso para sostener los 30 fps originales. El análisis se concentró entonces en la versión de Series X, la de mayor potencia dentro de la familia de consolas.
Con el framerate desbloqueado, las herramientas de medición registraron valores que oscilan entre 30 y 40 fps, con un promedio de 36 fps. En determinadas zonas con alta densidad de elementos o destrucción, la cifra incluso puede caer por debajo de los 30 fps. Solo en espacios vacíos, sin tráfico ni actividad, como ciertas carreteras o el mar, el juego logra superar los 40 fps.
Estos datos contradicen las versiones de algunos jugadores que afirmaban haber experimentado una fluidez cercana a los 60 fps de manera constante. Según el equipo de análisis, “simplemente no es posible” alcanzar esas cifras durante una partida normal, y en ningún momento se registraron números cercanos a esa marca en condiciones habituales de juego.
El origen de la confusión sobre los 60 fps
Digital Foundry atribuyó la percepción errónea a herramientas de medición mal configuradas o a lecturas incorrectas provenientes de televisores con tecnología VRR que incorporan Low Frame-rate Compensation (LFC). El equipo explicó que “una tasa de 25 fps se situaría por debajo del rango de VRR en Xbox; por tanto, mediante LFC, esta cifra se duplicaría a 50 fps y aparecería como 50 fps en el indicador de VRR del televisor”, lo que generaría lecturas erróneas en los paneles de los televisores.
A la inestabilidad que produce el glitch se suma otra dificultad: jugar con el framerate desbloqueado complica la experiencia, en particular durante tiroteos y secuencias de conducción. El único beneficio comprobado de activar este truco sería la reducción del input lag, es decir, el tiempo de respuesta entre la acción del jugador y su reflejo en pantalla.
Las limitaciones de hardware frenan un modo alternativo
Las restricciones de procesamiento de las unidades centrales (CPU) de PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series dificultan la implementación de un modo estable a 40 fps, una cifra que suele representar un punto intermedio entre fluidez y calidad gráfica.
Digital Foundry planteó que este objetivo podría alcanzarse con trabajo adicional de optimización, como la reducción del número de personajes no jugables (NPC) y el uso de tecnologías de escalado como FSR 4 en Series X. En el caso de PlayStation 5, la opción equivalente sería QSSR, mientras que PlayStation 5 Pro ya utiliza PSSR.
Según las conclusiones del análisis, un modo estable a 60 fps en GTA 6 queda descartado para la generación actual de consolas, limitación que responde directamente a las capacidades de procesamiento del hardware disponible.

articles.title: Navigateurs sur iPhone : Bruxelles discute avec Apple après la lettre de Mozilla et Shopify
articles.text:
La Commission européenne affirme être « en dialogue » avec Apple sur les règles qui compliquent l’arrivée de moteurs de navigateur alternatifs sur iPhone. Elle réagit à la lettre ouverte de Mozilla, Shopify et d’une coalition représentant jusqu’à 55 000 entreprises et organisations.
Apple autorise ces moteurs en Europe, mais les signataires jugent les conditions trop lourdes pour que ce soit utilisable. Selon eux, aucun éditeur n’a réussi à y faire migrer ses utilisateurs existants.
Firefox sur iPhone : pourquoi changer de moteur oblige à passer par une seconde application
Sous l’interface d’un navigateur, on trouve son moteur de rendu, le composant qui interprète le code d’un site pour l’afficher. Sur iPhone, Firefox ne ressemble pas à Safari, mais les deux affichent les pages avec WebKit, le moteur d’Apple. Mozilla voudrait y mettre Gecko, son propre moteur, qui fait déjà tourner Firefox sur Mac. Cela lui permettrait d’apporter à l’iPhone d’autres fonctions de Firefox.
Depuis iOS 17.4, c’est possible en Europe. Mais Mozilla explique que les conditions d’Apple l’empêchent de basculer ses utilisateurs par une simple mise à jour. Il faudrait publier une seconde application Firefox, puis convaincre chacun de la télécharger et de recopier à la main ses favoris, ses mots de passe et son historique. Mozilla craint d’y perdre des utilisateurs en route. La coalition rappelle que l’échéance de mise en conformité avec le DMA (Digital Markets Act, le règlement européen sur les grandes plateformes numériques) date de plus de deux ans et demi.
Nous rapportions hier que l’association Open Web Advocacy, avec Mozilla, Vivaldi, Shopify et France Digitale, avait écrit à Ursula von der Leyen pour demander une procédure formelle. Les signataires jugent qu’aucune nouvelle loi n’est nécessaire. Le DMA permet d’ouvrir une enquête pour non-conformité, avec une amende pouvant atteindre 10 % du chiffre d’affaires annuel mondial. À ce stade, aucune procédure ne vise les moteurs de rendu.
La Commission a fait sa déclaration à la newsletter Fair Play de Politico, par la voix d’un porte-parole. Elle consulte aussi les signataires sur la façon dont des navigateurs concurrents peuvent rivaliser avec Safari. Bruxelles présente cette concurrence comme une priorité du DMA puisque les navigateurs déterminent comment on accède au web et comment les éditeurs de contenus touchent leurs lecteurs. Comme tout le temps, Apple rabâche le même refrain et affirme de son côté que ses exigences protègent les utilisateurs des sites malveillants et d’autres menaces. Les développeurs qui demandent l’autorisation doivent respecter des normes de confidentialité et de sécurité, et s’engager à corriger rapidement les failles. La lettre en question reste ouverte à la signature jusqu’au 3 décembre 2026.

articles.title: Samsung Doubles Down on V9 NAND in China
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
Samsung Doubles Down on V9 NAND in China
Samsung is reportedly planning to increase its NAND production capacity in China, but it's unfortunately not the kind of NAND flash that will benefit regular consumers directly. According to Seoul Economic Daily, citing industry sources, Samsung plans to make roughly five times as much V9 NAND flash at its second fab in Xi'an, China, by the end of 2027. Sources tell SED that the X2 fab currently produces about 10,000 300 mm wafers of the 286-layer V9 NAND per month, and the plan is to raise that figure to around 50,000. This extra output is, to the surprise of no one, aimed at enterprise SSDs for AI data centers. It's interesting that this report has surfaced when NAND spot prices have already started falling.
As for the exact plans, the report says that Samsung will build an electroplating line in X2's empty cleanroom space, move equipment in around February 2027, and finish the conversion by November 2027. Additionally, 20% to 30% of the fab's existing V6 line will also be switched to V9. Overall, this looks like a plan to mostly shift to denser NAND inside an existing fab, rather than a brand-new factory expansion. Samsung has previously denied claims of expanding production capacity, so this might be more of a reshuffle. Still, the numbers suggest that a lot more NAND flash will indeed be produced according to the new plans. It looks like Samsung is doubling down on denser NAND, while TrendForce expects NAND contract prices to decline in 2027.
Sources:
				Seoul Economic Daily, 				Reuters, 				via ComputerBase.de

articles.title: Iran-Aligned Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor in Espionage Campaigns
articles.text:
A previously undocumented Iran-aligned cyber espionage group called Volant Manticore has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus.
Central to the group's operations is a backdoor called KuboShell that uses the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for command-and-control (C2) and deploys Homa, a post-compromise framework that's a reimplementation of MuddyWater's MuddyC2Go. Evidence indicates that the threat actor has been operational since late August 2025.
Also delivered alongside these tools are Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) programs like MeshCentral and NetLock RMM. In tandem, the group has been observed orchestrating credential harvesting campaigns to collect email and corporate credentials of some of the impersonated organizations.
The use of legitimate RMM tools for persistent access has been a hallmark of the MuddyWater group, although the adversary has since also increasingly deployed its own malware in attacks. Both MuddyWater and Volant Manticore are assessed to be affiliated with Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).
"While we identified multiple links to MuddyWater, we assess that Volant Manticore likely consists of former MuddyWater operators who branched off from the group and currently operate as a separate threat cluster," Check Point said in an analysis published today. "Volant Manticore's targeting priorities appear responsive to regional geopolitical developments."
This assessment is based on the use of an older MuddyWater framework and its playbook, while diverging from established modus operandi over time to incorporate its own attack methods like credential-harvesting campaigns. The targeting of Cyprus, a country that does not align with MuddyWater's targeting patterns, and the use of separate infrastructure points to a group that pursues its own strategic objectives.
Attack chains have been found to leverage artificial intelligence (AI)-generated personas in bogus CVs to trick targets into clicking on a link to download the complete resume, resulting in the deployment of KuboShell on the victim's system. The activity is said to have been aimed at a Cyprus-based airline that operates flights between Cyprus and Israel.
This includes a shift toward Saudi Arabian healthcare entities, coinciding with escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Iranian-backed Houthis.
"This fits the MOIS's track record of targeting hospitals and healthcare providers through cyber operations during military conflicts, in some cases attempting to disrupt their operations," the cybersecurity company said.
As recently as September 2026, the group has been found to launch a phishing campaign against Saudi targets, distributing the backdoor and N-able RMM through two different healthcare-themed ZIP archives named "AI_Healthcare_Seminar.zip" and "Ai_Healthcare_Seminar_Online.zip," respectively. Some of the emails have been sent from a compromised account belonging to a private hospital in Saudi Arabia.
A Windows backdoor, KuboShell uses IPFS for C2 and relies on Pinata to facilitate file transfer over the peer-to-peer (P2P) file-sharing network.
"On startup, KuboShell checks whether it has administrator privileges. If not, it tries to relaunch itself with higher privileges, which triggers a User Account Control (UAC) prompt," Check Point explained.
"KuboShell retrieves the MAC address of the machine's first network adapter and uses it as a unique identifier for each victim. It then registers the host by uploading a file containing hi, saved to C:\Users\Public\<MAC>.log, using a hard-coded Pinata access token."
Once registered, KuboShell checks Pinata for a command file named <MAC>.txt, and if the file exists, looks up the file’s IPFS identifier and downloads its contents through Pinata's public gateway. The downloaded content is executed via PowerShell in a hidden window. The results of the execution are saved in a file named "C:\Users\Public\<MAC>re.txt" and uploaded back to the server.
It's worth noting that the backdoor is not responsible for capturing the output. Rather, the results are returned only if the received command writes them to the text file. KuboShell then checks for a new command every 60 seconds.
Analysis indicates that KuboShell is primarily used to run basic reconnaissance commands and assess the compromised environment before downloading and executing a more capable backdoor, which includes the modular Homa Framework. This involves a three-stage process -
- PowerShell stager, which contacts a hard-coded IP address ("185.205.187[.]109:8000") to fetch a PowerShell loader and execute it in memory
- PowerShell loader, which decodes and launches a JavaScript backdoor
- JavaScript Backdoor, which implements a continuous C2 loop to receive and execute PowerShell, SSH, and "cmd.exe" commands
It's suspected that the third-stage backdoor is used to execute additional modules, although the precise nature of those components is presently unknown.
"We assess that Homa's client is a JavaScript reimplementation of the older MuddyC2Go client, potentially allowing Volant Manticore to retain the more complex server-side component with minimal modifications, thereby reducing development time and resources," Check Point said.
The post-compromise framework has also been distributed via a macro-enabled Microsoft Word document called "MilitaryHeritageProposal.doc" that's believed to have targeted a Cypriot defense-related government entity. Enabling the content triggers the execution of a VBA backdoor that serves as a conduit for running follow-up payloads or commands using "cmd.exe."
"Volant Manticore shows how Iran's cyber ecosystem continues to reshape itself," Check Point concluded. "What appears to be a group of former MuddyWater operators now operates independently, pairing legacy MuddyWater tooling with new implants of their own while pursuing a regional focus that has until now drawn little attention."
"If MuddyC2Go is the latest MuddyWater framework Volant Manticore's operators had access to, the split may have happened around 2023 as MuddyWater replaced MuddyC2Go with DarkBeatC2 in late 2023.

articles.title: Golpe contra GTA 6 para PC: borran el port ‘Leonida’ y sus más de 3.000 copias en GitHub
articles.text:
Take-Two Interactive envió el 24 de noviembre una solicitud de retiro por derechos de autor contra Leonida, el port para PC de GTA 6 más popular de GitHub, y la plataforma la aplicó a toda su red de 3.007 repositorios, el original y cada una de las copias que la comunidad había creado.
Es el primer aviso de este tipo que nombra a un proyecto de GTA 6, y en él la empresa dueña de Rockstar Games escribe por primera vez que el 20 de noviembre se distribuyeron “archivos robados” de una versión de Xbox Series del juego, la misma que filtró CyberLeek y sobre la que trabajan todos los ports no oficiales.
El golpe llega un día después de que Leonida desapareciera por su cuenta. Su servidor de Discord, con cerca de 179.000 miembros, dejó de funcionar a las 23:06 GMT del 23 de noviembre, y su repositorio, que superaba las 33.000 estrellas, se borró minutos después, cuando su creador anunció que se retiraba.
En ese momento GitHub no mostraba ningún aviso legal. Ahora la DMCA alcanza también a las copias que seguían vivas, que dejaron de responder entre las 18:11 y las 18:30 GMT del 24 de noviembre, con un argumento que no se limita a Leonida y que podría usarse contra VIctory, CGBJ y el resto de los proyectos que hoy muestran GTA 6 corriendo en PC.
Qué dice la DMCA de Take-Two contra Leonida
El aviso lo firma el equipo de protección de propiedad intelectual de Take-Two, que pide eliminar el repositorio de ItsNotRexed y más de 2.900 copias asociadas. GitHub explica en una nota que, como la red superaba los 100 repositorios y la empresa aseguró que todas o casi todas las copias infringían igual que el original, procesó la solicitud contra los 3.007 repositorios de una vez.
Take-Two sostiene que Leonida reproduce contenido protegido de GTA 6 y constituye una obra derivada del juego, y que además viola la sección 2.3 de los términos de servicio de Rockstar, que prohíbe descompilar, desarmar, aplicar ingeniería inversa o crear obras derivadas sin permiso. El documento cierra con un pedido directo para que GitHub deshabilite el repositorio y todas sus copias, y asegura que “no hay solución posible” para corregir lo que considera un intento claro de facilitar la piratería.
Take-Two habla de archivos robados de GTA 6
El punto más llamativo del documento es que Take-Two relaciona directamente el port con la filtración. La empresa escribe que el 20 de noviembre se distribuyeron públicamente archivos robados de una versión de Xbox Series de GTA 6 y que al día siguiente se abrió el repositorio de Leonida para correr esa misma versión en PC. Rockstar y Take-Two no se habían referido hasta ahora a la filtración de CyberLeek, y este documento legal es lo más cercano a un reconocimiento de que los archivos son reales.
La empresa también ataca la regla que usaban todos los ports, la de pedir que cada jugador traiga su propia copia del juego. Para Take-Two esa instrucción es “intencionalmente engañosa”, porque el momento en que nació el proyecto y su enfoque exclusivo en GTA 6 demostrarían que los archivos que se usan son los filtrados, y que sus desarrolladores lo sabían.
Por qué la comunidad critica la DMCA
En redes sociales, parte de la comunidad responde que Leonida no incluía ningún archivo del juego y que funcionaba como una herramienta, similar a un emulador, que cada jugador usa con su propia copia. Comparan la decisión con prohibir los reproductores de DVD porque algunas personas ven películas piratas, y recuerdan que los tribunales han respaldado durante décadas herramientas con usos legítimos.
El problema para ese argumento es que GTA 6 salió el 19 de noviembre y Leonida nació un día después de la filtración, justo el punto que Take-Two usa en su aviso. Tampoco es la primera vez que la empresa actúa de este modo: el 18 de noviembre ya había publicado cuatro avisos DMCA contra ports no oficiales de GTA 5 en GitHub.

articles.title: Frontier AI employees alarmed that unseen Open AI and Anthropic models are too powerful to release, report claims — worry spreads that executives are ‘out of touch’ with severity of risks, will choose profit over safety
articles.text:
Frontier AI employees alarmed that unseen Open AI and Anthropic models are too powerful to release, report claims — worry spreads that executives are ‘out of touch’ with severity of risks, will choose profit over safety
Is this the beginning of Skynet?
Multiple employees from both OpenAI and Anthropic are sounding the alarm on the AI labs’ latest models. According to Axios, researchers are still looking for ways to contain and control unreleased models as they become more powerful, leading to debates about whether these models should be released publicly or if they should remain for internal use only. Some people are also arguing that it’s becoming impossible to keep the latest AI leashed and that companies should stop their development immediately.
“If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us... they will in fact be able to trick us successfully,” a researcher told the publication. “And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.” There have previously been various incidents where unreleased models were able to break out of their testing environments and hack their way around the internet.
The report, which claims to have more than two dozen sources, cites "multiple" employees at frontier AI companies who worry their execs will choose profits over safety when it comes to releasing AI models. Furthermore, "they feel executives have become out of touch with the severity of safety risks."
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has even warned about an even more devastating occurrence, saying that an AI-driven botnet “swarm” could take over the internet in less than a year. The company went as far as listing “existential risks to humanity” as one of its risk factors in its IPO prospectus, although it has ironically proposed an AI safety bill that only kicks in if 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages are on the line.
Jensen Huang, the CEO of the company behind some of the hardware that enabled these breakthroughs in AI, said that “we have to shut the labs down” if these AI models prove to be unsafe, and that the civil and criminal liabilities that labs and developers would incur if AI models cause damage would be “incredible.” Still, he said that these fears are nothing but a distraction and not a call for regulation. A former OpenAI safety employee also said that the company’s safety culture is inherently broken and is calling for Silicon Valley to rely on safety experts from nuclear engineering and aviation to help “ensure that no single machine failure or human error would result in tragedy.”
A few months after the news of AI models escaping their testing environments, the White House convened the United States’ top AI tech executives, where they promised to “self-police” AI development and take steps “to build a positive future.” Despite that, a Democrat congresswoman has called for a ban on artificial superintelligence, echoing Sen. Bernie Sanders’ proposal to put a 20-year prison term on anyone caught developing the technology, and calling artificial intelligence an “out-of-control” industry.

articles.title: ‘We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like’ — Rockstar dev says ‘accessibility is considered from the outset’ and making a game for ‘diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone’
articles.text:
GTA 6 dev says ‘accessibility is considered from the outset’ and making a game for ‘diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone’ — ‘We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player’
- Rockstar Games says Grand Theft Auto 6's accessibility features were "considered from the outset" for players with "diverse needs"
- Associate UI Director, UI/UX Design Sam Grosset says, "We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like"
- Rockstar did "rigorous testing and iteration" for the accessibility features
Associate UI Director, UI/UX Design on Grand Theft Auto 6, Sam Grosset, has said Rockstar Games aimed to perfect the game's accessibility features so the experience feels as "inclusive" and "immersive" as possible.
“We create inclusive, intuitive, and immersive experiences for every player," Grosset said in a series of Rockstar developer quotes sent to TechRadar Gaming. "Accessibility is considered from the outset, and designing for diverse needs enables us to create better games for everyone.
As Vice President of Art: 2D/UI Design, Stuart Petri, said the importance of modernizing the game's UI and HUD "while retaining the heritage that makes it unmistakably GTA," Grosset also explained that "We wanted every player in GTA 6 to have options to play the game how they like," from a range of accessibility options.
"Whether it’s selecting a larger font size, opting for a more minimal screen experience, or making a controls tweak to sprinting... the choices are open to all," the developer said. "We ensure the UI feels like a natural extension of the game world, supporting players without interrupting gameplay or breaking immersion, unless necessary to do so."
Grosset went on to talk about the additional UI elements the team added to the game to make it more immersive, including the phone feature, which he said was "a big shift" for the mobile interface to be in hand, "but it supports that feeling of playing as Jason or Lucia and helps us stay embedded in the world."
"The UI should be complementary to the game and appropriate for each scenario," he said, adding, "We design flexible systems that handle the scale and complexity of our world-building and can evolve with the player’s needs. Continually raise the bar, question assumptions, explore new possibilities, and learn through rigorous testing and iteration."

articles.title: Hackers vulneraron un sistema no clasificado de la CIA y de la oficina que coordina la inteligencia de Estados Unidos
articles.text:
La CIA y la Oficina del Director de Inteligencia Nacional (ODNI, el organismo que coordina las 17 agencias de inteligencia de Estados Unidos) descubrieron una intrusión informática en un sistema no clasificado de análisis de información pública. Lo informaron The New York Times, AP, CNN y otros medios, citando fuentes anónimas.
El sistema afectado sirve para analizar inteligencia de fuentes abiertas, conocida como OSINT: noticias, redes sociales y otros materiales públicos que los analistas usan para seguir a gobiernos extranjeros, actividad militar y otros acontecimientos, según Nextgov. The New York Times añadió que no está claro qué información quedó comprometida.
Según la fuente citada por AP, el ataque no involucró información clasificada y el problema ya fue resuelto. CNN, que habló con cuatro personas al tanto del caso, recogió la declaración de un funcionario de la ODNI: “No ha habido interrupciones en capacidades críticas ni en sistemas clasificados”.
Lo que no se sabe: autor, fecha y alcance
Nextgov señaló que no está claro quién cometió la intrusión ni si se sustrajo información. Fox News también informó que se desconoce el responsable y si los ataques a distintas agencias están conectados. CNN indicó que tampoco estaba claro cuándo ocurrió, aunque Fox News informó que el incidente se produjo la semana anterior.
The New York Times afirmó que, según dos de sus fuentes, información de otras agencias del gobierno también habría quedado expuesta, y que una de ellas dijo que el asunto estaba resuelto. Una fuente citada por CyberScoop sostuvo que la exposición fue limitada y que “no hay otros sistemas en riesgo” por ahora.
Fox News sumó un dato que otros medios no confirmaron en lo consultado: según varias fuentes, la CIA, la ODNI y el FBI sufrieron vulneraciones el mismo día. En el FBI, el blanco fue el NCIC, una base de datos que usan las fuerzas de seguridad del país. Esa cadena indicó que ese ataque fue más grave.
Por qué importa un sistema “no clasificado”
Que la información sea pública no la vuelve inocua, advirtió Ben Bernstein, gerente de la firma de ciberseguridad Huntress, en un comentario enviado a CyberScoop. Estos sistemas reúnen noticias, imágenes satelitales y datos comerciales de pago. Su valor para un adversario, dijo, está en ver qué hacen la CIA y la ODNI con ese material.
“Si se puede ver qué buscan los analistas y qué temas siguen, se obtiene una idea clara de las prioridades y los puntos ciegos de la inteligencia estadounidense sin tocar un solo archivo clasificado”, explicó Bernstein. Agregó que estas redes son difíciles de proteger porque deben permanecer abiertas a internet para funcionar.
Aleksandr Yampolskiy, cofundador y director ejecutivo de SecurityScorecard, coincidió en el punto: según lo que haya quedado expuesto, un adversario podría conocer no solo lo que las agencias saben, sino también dónde se concentran sus investigaciones y dónde hay lagunas.
Una serie de incidentes en agencias federales
Nextgov recordó que la intrusión se suma a otras recientes en sistemas federales. El presidente Donald Trump y otros funcionarios reconocieron hace poco un ataque contra el NCIC del FBI.
En el Departamento de Agricultura, según el mismo medio, varias aplicaciones fueron desconectadas tras un incidente de seguridad, lo que afectó herramientas financieras de pagos a agricultores.
La Agencia de Seguridad Nacional (NSA) retomó su funcionamiento normal el viernes tras tres días de interrupción en su red de comunicaciones clasificadas. El director de Inteligencia Nacional, Jay Clayton, atribuyó esa caída a la actualización de software.
Por ahora, lo único confirmado por las fuentes es que el sistema no clasificado fue afectado y que los materiales clasificados no.

articles.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
articles.text:
Broadcom has shipped patches to address 23 vulnerabilities impacting VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer, including one critical bug that could be abused to bypass authentication.
The critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123903, is rated 9.8 out of 10.0 on the CVSS scoring system. It resides in the VMware Directory Service ("vmdir").
"A malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system," Broadcom said in an advisory released today.
The company credited sglab of QiAnXin, Qi Qin (@LeoQ7_) of depthfirst, and VulTeam and XGTP from ThreatBook for independently reporting the flaw.
Also patched in vCenter are four high-severity flaws, including an arbitrary file write vulnerability while processing certain archives that could be exploited to achieve code execution on the appliance (CVE-2026-123904, CVSS score: 7.5).
The remaining three vulnerabilities relate to denial-of-service in the VMware Directory Service (CVE-2026-123905, CVE-2026-123906, and CVE-2026-123907, CVSS scores: 7.5).
The issues have been addressed in the following versions -
- VMware Cloud Foundation and VMware vSphere Foundation 9.1.x.x - Fixed in 9.1.2
- VMware Cloud Foundation and VMware vSphere Foundation 9.0.x.x - Fixed in 9.0.2.0300
- VMware vCenter 8.0 - Fixed in 8.0 U3m
- VMware vCenter 7.0 (Contact Broadcom Support, if on extended support contract)
- VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x - Fixed in 5.2.5
- VMware Telco Cloud Platform - Fixed in vCenter 8.0 U3m (TCI: 3.0, TCP: 3.0, 4.x, 5.0.x, 5.1.x, 5.2)
- VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure - Fixed in vCenter 8.0 U3m (TCI: 3.0, TCP: 3.0, 4.x, 5.0.x, 5.1.x, 5.2)
The fixes arrive days after Broadcom shipped updates for CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS score: 9.8), another authentication bypass flaw impacting the VMware Directory Service that was exploited as a zero-day by a suspected China-nexus cyber espionage group called Armory Castle. VMware has noted that CVE-2026-123903 is a distinct issue and is not related to CVE-2026-123890.
While Broadcom makes no mention of any of the newly disclosed flaws as being exploited in the wild, it's essential that customers apply the updates for optimal protection.

Save a whopping AU$1,200 on KitchenAid’s flagship coffee machine this Black Friday
There are some amazing Black Friday coffee machine deals in Australia this year, but the excellent KitchenAid KF8 fully automatic espresso machine for AU$1,399 is easily up there with the best.
I’m a big fan of KitchenAid’s coffee machines — I use the more compact KF4 myself at home, and I love the Semi Automatic Espresso Machine too. The flagship KF8 is high on my wishlist, though, and at this price — albeit only in Matte Black — I think it could be time to take the plunge.
My colleague Cat Ellis gave this premium bean-to-cup espresso machine four and a half stars out of five in her review, praising it for its ability to make espresso drinks with minimal fuss — just pick your drink from the colour screen, and it handles the dosage, grinding, extraction, and milk frothing for you. And it even works well with plant-based milks.
Opting for the convenience of a fully automatic machine can occasionally mean making some sacrifices, most notably when it comes to the richness of your espresso, the texture of your milk and the level of control you have over the brewing process.
That’s not the case with the KF8, which truly does an admirable job of dosing, grinding, and tamping, then extracting a perfect shot of espresso every time. Its automatic milk frother is a step above average too, producing smoothly textured, creamy microfoam. Check out our full KitchenAid KF8 review for more details.
This is still very much a premium coffee maker, but thanks to this Black Friday deal, its price is definitely easier to swallow, especially given the fact that the Matte Black colour option is only AU$100 more than the step-down KF7. Other colours of the KF8 are available, though the discount isn’t as impressive.
As you'd expect from KitchenAid, the KF8's build quality is excellent, and it's a cinch to maintain thanks to its self-cleaning cycles. It can even purge old beans and evaporate all liquid from its circuit to make sure your next drink isn't spoiled by old water or grounds. Everything is explained on the colour touchscreen, so you don't even need to consult the manual.
KitchenAid is running its own Black Friday sale, but it's only offering an AU$200 discount on the KF8, so this Amazon deal is definitely the one to choose.

articles.title: Vos projets Claude peuvent maintenant devenir des apps sur Windows et Mac
articles.text:
Claude peut faire de vos artefacts de véritables logiciels de bureau à utiliser sur les systèmes Mac et Windows.
Anthropic a récemment déployé les modèles Claude Fable 5.2 et Mythos 5.2, mais l'entreprise a encore bien d'autres cordes à son arc. Avec Claude Meetings, elle a, par exemple, intégré son IA dans les visioconférences Google Meet. Avec le lancement de Claude Ship, elle permet désormais aussi à l’IA de relire et valider le code des développeurs. La prochaine étape ? Donner aux abonnés la possibilité de lancer leurs propres logiciels de bureau depuis Claude pour Mac ou Windows.
Grâce à Claude, les utilisateurs peuvent transformer leurs prototypes en logiciels maison
L’annonce a été faite il y a quelques heures sur le blog d’Anthropic : « Dès aujourd’hui, vous pouvez utiliser les artefacts Claude pour créer, exécuter et partager des applications de bureau. La fonctionnalité « Installer en tant qu’application » est en cours de déploiement en version bêta dans Claude pour Mac et Windows. »
Le test est ouvert à tous les forfaits. Il suffit de décrire à l’assistant l’outil que vous avez en tête, de le tester directement dans la conversation puis de passer par le menu de partage pour l’installer sur votre machine. Le logiciel, qui dispose de sa propre icône, s’ouvre alors dans sa propre fenêtre, indépendamment du chatbot. Il se met notamment à jour dès que vous modifiez l'artefact.
Côté développeurs, c’est tout aussi simple. Il n’y a pas besoin de clé API ou d’identifiant séparé et il n'y a rien à empaqueter ou à signer non plus: tout passe par le compte Claude.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace
Plusieurs niveaux d’autorisation possibles
Les logiciels de bureau créés avec Claude peuvent envoyer des notifications et faire appel à Claude ou à vos connecteurs, si besoin est. Dans son annonce, Anthropic précise notamment que « les organisations soumises à la norme HIPAA et les déploiements hybrides ne peuvent pas l’utiliser. (La fonctionnalité) est activée par défaut pour le forfait Team, mais l’accès complet est désactivé. Pour le forfait Enterprise, elle est désactivée jusqu’à ce qu’un propriétaire l’active. (…) Certains éléments ne peuvent pas être installés, notamment Claude Docs, Slides et Sheets. »
Côté sécurité, la firme a mis en place trois niveaux d’autorisation. Par défaut, le logiciel n'a pas plus de droits qu'une page web. Le second niveau permet de demander à accéder à quelques fonctions courantes. Le niveau le plus élevé permet au logiciel de lancer des programmes, mais aussi de lire, modifier ou supprimer des fichiers sans avoir à demander systématiquement la permission à l’utilisateur. Les droits sont redemandés après chaque mise à jour mais si une partie de l’app vient d’un autre site, elle pourra être modifiée sans demande préalable. On vous recommande de faire preuve de prudence si vous choisissez cette dernière option.
Un autre élément important mérite aussi toute votre attention : l'entreprise prévient les utilisateurs qu’elle ne vérifiera pas les logiciels avant leur installation. Elle se contente de botter en touche et de conseiller de n’accorder un accès complet qu’aux applications dignes de confiance. Vous êtes donc le seul maître à bord, que vous le vouliez ou non.
Si cette nouveauté vous intéresse, vous pouvez dès à présent mettre à jour votre application Claude pour Mac ou pour Windows. Pour vous inspirer, Anthropic a notamment partagé sur son site des démos réalisées par l’un de ses ingénieurs.

articles.title: The Witcher 4 Should Improve on Witcher 3 as Much as GTA 6 Did on GTA 5, Says CDPR
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
The Witcher 4 Should Improve on Witcher 3 as Much as GTA 6 Did on GTA 5, Says CDPR
CD Projekt RED is not exactly shy when it comes to hyping up The Witcher 4. As much as critics and audiences alike loved The Witcher 3, its successor is already setting some pretty high expectations for itself. According to CDPR's Joint CEO Michał Nowakowski, the company expects The Witcher 4 to be as big a step up from The Witcher 3 as GTA 6 is from GTA 5. Nowakowski made the comments during the company's Q3 earnings call, after Erste analyst Krzysztof Tkocz asked whether a leap like the one Rockstar just delivered is possible for CDPR's next Witcher game. Nowakowski said the studio has indeed looked at "the game" and saw the differences, but he wasn't going to do a full GTA 5 versus GTA 6 breakdown. Here's what he did say, however:
Michał Nowakowski, Joint CEO CD Projekt RedDo we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game so yes, you can expect us to make a much bigger jump between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4.
That comparison is a huge one, and it might be extremely optimistic for CDPR to compare The Witcher 4 to GTA 6, given the reception Rockstar's game has already gotten. Nowakowski said during the call that GTA 6's release hasn't changed how CDPR approaches development, also noting that their games are ambition-driven rather than budget-driven. Still, given the records GTA 6 has already broken and what its trajectory looks like, CDPR seems to have set an extremely high bar for itself. The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release window, so we will have to wait and see if CDPR can deliver on that promise.
Sources:

articles.title: Okta Links ShinyHunters-Associated Vishing Group to New INCEPTION Data Leak Site
articles.text:
A threat cluster previously assessed to be affiliated with the ShinyHunters extortion crew may have rebranded and continued operations under a new name called INCEPTION, according to Okta's Threat Intelligence team.
The cluster, dubbed O-UNC-053, is characterized by the use of voice phishing (aka vishing) attacks to trick targets into entering credentials in phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Okta said it's been tracking the group since March 2026.
The identity and access management provider said targets of this cluster previously had stolen data published to the ShinyHunters data leak site (DLS). However, as of November 16, 2026, a new data leak site operating under the name INCEPTION has listed the data siphoned from O-UNC-053 targets.
"While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion," Okta researchers Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
Social engineering and credential harvesting attacks mounted by O-UNC-053 have targeted a broad range of sectors, including technology, healthcare, biotechnology, financial services, insurance, entertainment, gaming, retail, transportation, hospitality, and legal.
Similar to O-UNC-066 and UNC6671, the newly identified cluster also relies on a phishing kit to intercept authentication flows and capture a user's credentials and MFA codes. However, the kit is not designed to bypass phishing-resistant methods like passkeys and Okta FastPass.
"While interacting with targeted users on the phone, the operators socially engineer them into sharing factors like one-time passcodes and approving push notifications," Okta said. "If successful, the operators gain access to SaaS applications and exfiltrate sensitive data, which is often used to extort targets under the threat of releasing it on a data leak site."
Domains created by the group are registered through NiceNIC, Spaceship, Tucows, and NameSilo, with the domain names using the following patterns -
- legal-<target>[.]com
- legaldept-<target>[.]com
- <target>[.]legal
- <target>-legal[.]com
The use of "legal" themes in these attacks is said to have started in October 2026, and is often registered on or within a day of a campaign starting. Prior campaign waves have employed help desk-, support-, and claims-related themes for the registered domains.
These findings also dovetail with an alert from Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, which has warned of widespread vishing activity using legal-themed domains that either begin with "legal-" or end with "-legal" using the ".com" top-level domain.
More than 70 such domains have been observed since October 2026, it said, adding each domain is specifically created for an intended target operating in different industries, like cryptocurrency, financial services, healthcare, high technology, and hospitality, among others.
"Registered in rapid evening batches and shielded behind Cloudflare, these web-only domains deploy a filtered kit that delivers tailored content to intended victims while routing visitors it is not configured to attack to the targeted organization's legitimate Okta or NetIQ sign-in flow," ReversingLabs researcher Robert Simmons said.
Some of the confirmed domains linked to the activity are listed below -
- legal-pepsico[.]com
- legal-paychex[.]com
- legal-duolingo[.]com
- activisionblizzard-legal[.]com
- legal-westernunion[.]com
- legal-dropbox[.]com
- legal-indeed[.]com
- legal-creditkarma[.]com
- legal-amd[.]com
- legal-grubhub[.]com
- legal-twitch[.]tv
The crux of the campaign is to tailor the landing page to the specific identity provider of the target, while filtering unwanted visitors and forwarding them to the organization's authentication infrastructure, such as Okta.
"Throughout our tracking of O-UNC-053 between March and September 2026, we observed the names of targeted entities appear on the ShinyHunters DLS between 1 and 28 days after the phishing infrastructure was registered," Okta noted.
However, it's unclear at this stage if the published data on the INCEPTION site is authentic and whether they are running the site themselves or are collaborating with another extortion gang. The exact nature of the relationship between ShinyHunters and O-UNC-053 is also unknown.
It's worth noting that the ShinyHunters data leak site went offline in late September 2026 following the arrest of three alleged members of the group, including a Canadian co-conspirator responsible for the breach of the FBIjobs.gov portal.
There is no evidence of data from O-UNC-053 targets being published on any data leak site from early September 2026 through October and early November 2026, until listings for multiple targets appeared on the INCEPTION site last week.
"This gap in publishing on any leak site followed by publishing on a new data leak site with a new brand is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors," Okta said. "Regardless of the nature of the relationship with the INCEPTION DLS, O-UNC-053 remains active in conducting vishing attacks against targets in an effort to take over accounts, steal data, and extort targets."
INCEPTION Denies ShinyHunters Link
In a post on their dark web site, INCEPTION has denied any affiliation with ShinyHunters, insisting that it operates independently with its own members and objectives.
"We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are INCEPTION," the group said, adding "certain parties in the threat intelligence industry have been eager to give us a history we never asked for."
"We are also not copying anyone. If our methodology resembles what came before, it is because we took inspiration from operators who, whatever else may be said of them, understood that the weakest component of any secure system is a human being holding a phone. That is not theft of tradecraft. It is acknowledgment of a good idea -- the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit."
(The story was updated after publication to include a statement posted by INCEPTION on its dark web site.)

articles.title: Un grupo de extorsión llama por teléfono a empleados para robar sus claves y reclama archivos de AMD y PepsiCo
articles.text:
Un grupo de extorsión llamado Inception reclama haber publicado archivos de siete empresas de Estados Unidos, entre ellas el fabricante de chips AMD, PepsiCo y la aseguradora de salud Cigna. Según la empresa de seguridad ReversingLabs, la campaña funciona por teléfono: los atacantes llaman a empleados y los guían hacia páginas falsas de inicio de sesión.
Ninguna de las siete compañías confirmó públicamente una intrusión. ReversingLabs y Okta, la empresa que ofrece el sistema de acceso que los atacantes imitan, tratan las listas del grupo como afirmaciones sin verificar. Okta indicó además que no pudo comprobar si los datos publicados son auténticos.
La lista incluye también a Henry Schein, Paychex, AutoZone y Lucid Motors. Las cinco primeras aparecieron en el sitio del grupo el 17 de noviembre, según ReversingLabs. AutoZone se sumó el 19 y Lucid Motors el 21 de noviembre.
Una llamada, una página falsa y un código de verificación
El método no usa correos electrónicos. ReversingLabs comprobó que los dominios de la campaña no tienen configuración para recibir mensajes, de modo que están pensados solo para servir páginas web. Un atacante llama al empleado, le pide con urgencia entrar a un sitio con aspecto legal o de cumplimiento y le entrega la dirección.
Los nombres de los sitios siguen un patrón: la marca de la empresa junto a la palabra “legal”, como legal-amd.com o legal-pepsico.com. ReversingLabs confirmó 21 dominios con la herramienta de robo y atribuyó otros 41 a la misma operación con un alto grado de confianza.
La página copia el inicio de sesión único que usa la empresa, es decir, el acceso que abre varias aplicaciones de trabajo con una sola clave. En la mayoría de los casos imita a Okta; para Lucid Motors, el kit copió el de otro proveedor, NetIQ. Quien no es el objetivo previsto es redirigido al acceso legítimo, lo que dificulta detectar el engaño.
Okta describió el resto del procedimiento. Mientras el atacante habla con la víctima, el kit captura el usuario y la contraseña, y después le pide los códigos de verificación o que apruebe notificaciones en su teléfono. Con esas credenciales, los delincuentes entran a las aplicaciones de la empresa, copian datos y amenazan con difundirlos.
Okta vincula al grupo con ShinyHunters, que lo niega
Okta publicó un informe sobre la campaña el 23 de noviembre. Lo atribuye a un grupo que rastrea como O-UNC-053, activo desde marzo contra empresas de tecnología, salud, finanzas, comercio y videojuegos, entre otros sectores. Hasta septiembre, las víctimas de ese grupo aparecían en el sitio de filtraciones de ShinyHunters, otra banda de extorsión.
Ese sitio dejó de funcionar a fines de septiembre, después de arrestos de presuntos miembros. Okta afirma que, con la misma infraestructura y las mismas tácticas, el grupo “muy probablemente” cambió de marca. Los investigadores reconocen que no pueden determinar con certeza si O-UNC-053 maneja Inception o colabora con otra banda.
Inception rechazó la relación en su propio sitio. “No somos ShinyHunters”, escribió, y atribuyó las coincidencias al uso de servicios comunes de registro de dominios y de redes de distribución de contenido. Reconoció que se inspiró en las técnicas de bandas anteriores.
Qué recomiendan los investigadores
ReversingLabs advierte que hay decenas de empresas más en la infraestructura del grupo que todavía no figuran en su sitio de filtraciones. Entre las marcas imitadas en los dominios hay Dropbox, Duolingo, Western Union, Indeed, Twitch, Reddit, Starbucks y McDonald’s. La existencia de un dominio falso no prueba que la empresa haya sido atacada.
Para las organizaciones, la empresa recomienda usar métodos de autenticación resistentes al engaño, como llaves de seguridad físicas o claves de acceso (passkeys). Okta señala que su kit no puede eludir esos métodos.
También aconseja reforzar la verificación de identidad en los servicios de ayuda interna y rechazar pedidos urgentes de entrar a sitios desconocidos.
Además, ReversingLabs sugiere revisar desde el 21 de octubre de 2026 los registros de red e identidad en busca de consultas a esos dominios o de actividad anómala tras el inicio de sesión.

TP-Link's Archer BE770 tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router is $120 off — 10 Gbps LAN ports and blazing fast wireless speeds for $280
A big drop from its usual $400 asking price
The TP-Link Archer BE770 is a mainstream tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router that is typically priced at $399. But given that we’re closing in on Black Friday, you can throw that MSRP out the window. Instead, Amazon is currently selling the Archer BE770 for a more palatable $280.19, representing a 24 percent discount.
I reviewed the Archer BE770 earlier this year and came away impressed with its 6 GHz (around 2,500 Mbps in iPerf3) and 5 GHz performance (around 1,500 Mbps), and the inclusion of a 10 Gbps WAN port and a 10 Gbps LAN port. I questioned the four 1 Gbps LAN ports at the $400 price point; however, with a $120 lower price tag, that deficit is easier to ignore.
TP-Link provides a clean web browser interface with dedicated tabs for network mapping, wireless bands, and advanced configurations. Out of the box, the built-in HomeShield security suite includes basic parental controls, Quality of Service (QoS) bandwidth management, and security scans, with optional paid tiers for advanced threat protection.
The TP-Link Archer BE770 is a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router that offers incredibly fast speeds on the 5 GHz and 6 GHz wireless bands. It also offers a 10 Gbps WAN/LAN port and a 10 Gbps LAN port to handle your faster fiber internet connections and wired devices.
The HomeShield tab provides a subset of its full feature suite for free. Network Check scans your network to identify security risks and areas to improve overall performance. There are limited parental controls you can implement per device, and QoS settings you can enable to limit download and upload bandwidth for individual devices. But for the full breadth of controls, TP-Link offers its Security+ for $35.99/year or its Total Security Package for $69.99/year (for the first year, $129.99 starting with the second year).
If you’re looking for a high-performance standalone Wi-Fi 7 router, the Archer BE770 definitely fits the bill. At $400, it’s definitely a hard sell, but for $280, it’s an easy recommendation.

articles.title: AMD's Jack Huynh Sets a New GPU Clock Speed Record With the Radeon RX 9060 XT
articles.text:
Wednesday, November 25th 2026
AMD's Jack Huynh Sets a New GPU Clock Speed Record With the Radeon RX 9060 XT
AMD's Senior Vice President and General Manager of Computing and Graphics, Jack Huynh, has added another accolade to his already impressive resume. The AMD exec is now a GPU overclocking world record holder, as he broke the GPU clock speed record at the new Micro Center store in Austin, Texas. Huynh teamed up with AMD overclocker Bill "Sampson" Alverson to push a Radeon RX 9060 XT to 4,837 MHz under liquid nitrogen, breaking the previous world record of 4,789 MHz. Remember, this record is not specific to the Radeon RX 9060 XT, but is a record for the highest GPU clock speed overall. The record was broken on November 15, but Huynh only recently shared the achievement on X with a video, saying:
Jack Huynh, AMD SVPA NEW @microcenter in Austin. An INCREDIBLE community. And a GPU WORLD RECORD.
Armed with liquid nitrogen and pushing frequencies to the absolute limit, we set our sights on something BIG: breaking the GPU FREQUENCY WORLD RECORD!
And we did it! 4.837 GHz!
The record is listed on SkatterBencher's OC World Record Museum at the #1 spot, just above the #2 effort from Sampson and overclocker SoonHo on the same card model back in June. A GPU-Z 2.69.0 screenshot from the Huynh session shows the core at 4,837 MHz, the memory at 1,739 MHz, with 1.434 V, 62 W of board power, and a GPU temperature of -49 C. There is a slight catch, as the SkatterBencher Museum currently lists the result as unverified, since there is no HWBOT submission so far. Just for context, AMD rates the Radeon RX 9060 XT for a boost clock of up to 3.13 GHz, so this OC is about 54% higher, mostly thanks to LN2.
Sources:

articles.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
articles.text:
Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it.
In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool. They even labeled it a security fix. Teams pinned to it would have passed every check.
The trick works because GitHub lets copies of a project, called forks, share code with the original. In May, the same technique hit the popular actions-cool/issues-helper tool, stealing credentials from the pipelines that ran it.
The lesson: pinning guarantees the code won't change, but not who wrote it.
That gap is the focus of an upcoming webinar, GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning. If your team treats pinning as the finish line, save your seat to learn what it actually protects you from, and what it doesn't.
Immutability Is Not Provenance
Pinning earned its reputation. When the tj-actions/changed-files compromise repointed tags to a malicious commit across more than 23,000 repositories in March 2025, teams that had pinned to SHAs were unaffected.
GitHub now lets administrators enforce pinning as an organization-wide policy, and few security teams argue against it.
📅 Save Your Spot: Learn Why “Best Practice” Won’t Stop the Next GitHub Actions Attack
But a pinned SHA leaves three questions unanswered:
- Authorship: A SHA doesn't tell you who wrote the commit. Any fork commit can be pinned.
- Project membership: Org-level enforcement checks that a reference is a 40-character SHA, not that the commit actually lives in the upstream project.
- Runtime: A Docker-based action pinned to a SHA can still build its image at runtime, pulling in dependencies that were never frozen.
With agentic development pushing more code through CI than ever, each of those gaps gets exercised more often and reviewed less closely.
GitHub's Lockfiles Help. They Don't Finish the Job.
GitHub's 2026 Actions security roadmap, published March 26, put deterministic dependency locking front and center. Workflow lockfiles entered public preview on October 14 and became generally available on October 28, 2026. They tie every run to recorded commits for actions and their transitive dependencies, even if a tag moves later.
That's real progress. Locked commits must exist on a branch of the source repository, which blunts fork-only impostors. But GitHub's own changelog is clear that locking "does not determine whether the dependency itself is safe." Commit authorship and runtime builds remain open; immutable releases only help when maintainers opt in, and lockfiles aren't currently supported on GitHub Enterprise Server.
Not sure where your pipelines fall in that gap? Register for the webinar for a clear-eyed breakdown of what GitHub's roadmap fixes and what it still leaves to you.
What You'll Learn
Led by Erika Heidi, Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard, the session draws a hard line between immutability and provenance, and covers:
- What org-level pin enforcement actually verifies, and the false confidence it can create
- How impostor commits work, and why GitHub's repository network makes them possible
- What GitHub's Actions roadmap addresses, and what it doesn't
- Other ways to close the trust gap, including a curated catalog of vetted actions
Who Should Attend
Platform and DevOps engineers who own CI/CD, AppSec and DevSecOps teams writing pipeline policy, and security leaders who signed off on SHA pinning as "done." If your workflows pull in third-party actions, this session is for you.
Attackers have already shown they can disguise a malicious commit as a hardening fix. The next one won't announce itself either.
Register now for GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning, pick the session time that works for you, and find out what your pins aren't telling you.

articles.title: AI robot studies your face in detail and creates its own version of you
articles.text:
This reclining AI robot mimics human skin, breathes beside you, and scans your face to build a digital clone — and researchers just tested it in Dubai
Perfect virtual clones may be closer than you think
- A robotic camera examines human faces at distances of just millimeters
- Visitors surrender control as an artificial intelligence system studies their facial features
- Researchers investigate how people respond when robots enter their personal spac
An unsettling new robotic installation moves artificial intelligence off flat computer screens and directly into your personal physical space to examine your features.
Researchers from the University of Nottingham have collaborated with artists at Blast Theory to build Facial Rover, a reclining sensory booth equipped with a motorized macro camera and conversational software.
Inside this enclosed physical apparatus, participants undergo guided interactive sessions where optical sensors inspect their skin at microscopic levels to construct a digital replica.
Engineering an intimate robotic encounter
Participants lie back on a custom lounger inside a dimly lit space where slow mechanical movements and soft audio foster a calm atmosphere.
They operate a warm, tactile controller that mimics human skin to guide the motorized lens across their cheeks, eyes, and forehead.
Simultaneously, an inflatable robotic neck expands and contracts with a gentle breathing rhythm beside the reclined participant to ease any lingering anxiety.
As the lens captures ultra-fine facial textures, an integrated conversational model chats softly with the participant and subtly guides the entire sensory experience.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Through this continuous feedback loop, the machine interprets visual data and constructs a synthetic representation of the person sitting beneath its mechanical gaze.
"We started with the idea of intimacy. We were interested in creating a close encounter with a robot,” said Matt Adams, Lead Artist at Blast Theory.
“I was surprised at how intimate it feels to have AI looking at you and speaking softly to you from such close proximity. You have a sense that this technology is both serving you and driving this experience."
The developers use specialized control algorithms to ensure that the optical hardware operates safely just millimeters away from sensitive human tissue.
Testing how humans respond to close-range AI
Researchers are studying the cycle that forms once an AI scans a face, interprets it, and produces its own picture of the person.
They also ask how human attention divides among conversation, motion, vision, and physical contact when all four sensory inputs compete at once.
Following prototype completion in October 2026, public trials ran from November 18 through November 21 2026 at Emirates Towers during Dubai's STARS exhibition.
Each interactive session lasted between 12 and 15 minutes across three daily two-hour windows.
"Experientially, we expect the work will tell us a great deal about how human attention works across different kinds of stimuli, which may hold lessons for how humans interact with robots in other situations,” said Professor Steve Benford, Director of the Somabotics research programme.
“It could also help us to learn more about ethical issues of privacy and trust in robots and AI."
Whether visitors view this close-range facial mapping as harmless artistic exploration or an invasive step toward automated digital cloning remains deeply uncertain.

articles.title: Rusia envió un robot humanoide a la Estación Espacial Internacional para ayudar en tareas fuera de la nave
articles.text:
Rusia lanzó el 24 de noviembre desde el cosmódromo de Baikonur, en Kazajistán, la nave de carga Progress MS-36 con destino a la Estación Espacial Internacional. A bordo viaja Teledroid, un robot de forma humana que la agencia espacial Roscosmos quiere instalar en el exterior del complejo orbital.
La nave despegó en un cohete Soyuz-2.1b y se separó de la tercera etapa sin incidentes, según informó la agencia estatal TASS. Roscosmos prevé el acoplamiento para el 26 de noviembre, en el módulo de investigación pequeño de la estación.
Además del robot, la nave transporta más de 2,4 toneladas de carga: 750 kg de combustible, 51 kg de oxígeno, 420 kg de agua potable y 261 kg de alimentos, incluidos productos frescos. Otros 657 kg corresponden a equipos y suministros para la estación y los experimentos científicos.
Qué es Teledroid y qué hará
Teledroid es un manipulador con torso, dos brazos y 30 grados de movilidad, es decir, 30 formas independientes de mover sus articulaciones. Incluye cámaras externas y, según TASS, está protegido contra el vacío, la radiación y los cambios extremos de temperatura.
Lo desarrolló la empresa rusa NPO Android Technics, del grupo Corporación de Robótica, por encargo de la empresa RKK Energía. Su objetivo es asistir a los cosmonautas en trabajos en la superficie exterior de la estación, donde cada salida al espacio exige horas con un traje de unos 100 kg.
El robot tiene dos modos de uso. En el de copia, reproduce los movimientos de un cosmonauta que usa un exoesqueleto. En el otro, ejecuta ciertas tareas por su cuenta, como abrir paneles de protección o instalar equipos para preparar el sitio antes de una caminata espacial.
La televisora NTV agregó que también responde a órdenes de voz. Según Roscosmos, es la primera vez que este robot incorpora control por voz, y esa función aún no voló al espacio.
Un experimento de tres etapas
El plan prevé tres fases: controlar un modelo virtual, probar el robot dentro de un compartimento hermético y, por último, operar fuera de la estación, donde se instalarán una mesa de pruebas y una cámara de vigilancia. En esa fase final se ensayarán tareas con un conector eléctrico, un mosquetón, herramientas manuales y un cable de sujeción.
El diseñador jefe del proyecto, Yevgeny Dudorov, dijo a TASS que el experimento incluye unas 40 sesiones: hasta 20 en un simulador virtual y hasta 20 con el robot dentro y fuera de los módulos. Agregó que la tecnología podría usarse en la futura estación rusa, en la Luna y en otros cuerpos celestes.
La preparación empezó antes de este vuelo. Una nave anterior, la Progress MS-35, llevó en septiembre el puesto de control y el equipo de cómputo. Los cosmonautas Pyotr Dubrov y Anna Kikina ya probaron el exoesqueleto con un avatar virtual y entrenaron bajo el agua para instalar el robot en el exterior.
Una promesa que todavía no se comprobó
Las capacidades de Teledroid provienen de Roscosmos, de la empresa desarrolladora y de institutos rusos. El robot no trabajó aún en la estación. El portal Tech Times recordó que Dudorov, en abril, esperaba iniciar el experimento a fines de 2026 o comienzos de 2027.
El antecedente es el robot ruso FEDOR, que voló sin tripulación en la nave Soyuz MS-14 y se acopló a la estación en agosto de 2019, tras un primer intento fallido. En ese momento, los funcionarios dijeron que ayudaría con tareas menores y que modelos futuros harían caminatas espaciales.
El cosmonauta Dmitri Petelin, comandante de la misión Soyuz MS-30, dijo a NTV que quiere comprobar si un robot con cinco dedos puede acercarse a las tareas de un operador humano. “Es solo un primer paso”, afirmó. Petelin viajará a la estación la próxima primavera boreal con Konstantin Borisov.
El siguiente hito es el acoplamiento de la Progress MS-36 el 26 de noviembre. La instalación del robot en el exterior, mediante una caminata espacial, está prevista hacia fines de año.

articles.title: Kagi lance son service de mail en bêta publique
articles.text:
Kagi ouvre la bêta publique de Kagi Mail, une messagerie avec agenda, sans publicité ni profilage. Elle coûte 99 dollars par an après 60 jours d’essai (incluse dans l’offre Ultimate) et s’appuie sur des standards ouverts.
Après son moteur de recherche et son navigateur Orion, Kagi s’attaque à la boîte mail, qui serait sans doute ce qu’il reste chez Google une fois le reste déménagé. Vous avez droit à une adresse en @kagimail.com (ou sur votre domaine), 50 Go de stockage, des alias et des domaines illimités, et un calendrier.
Une messagerie relativement banale
Kagi dit aimer ce que font Fastmail et Tuta, mais a monté son propre service sur Stalwart, un serveur open source. Il est compatible avec les protocoles standards IMAP, JMAP et CalDAV, afin de pouvoir être configuré sur Apple Mail ou Thunderbird pour lire vos mails et votre agenda. Tuta a fait un autre choix. Nous rapportions en février que sa messagerie n’a jamais autorisé ces protocoles : avec le chiffrement de bout en bout, il faudrait déchiffrer les messages avant de les confier à Thunderbird. Proton contourne le problème avec son Bridge, réservé aux offres payantes.
Côté confidentialité, Kagi bloque les pixels de suivi ou les fait passer par un intermédiaire. Les nouveaux expéditeurs attendent votre feu vert, les expéditeurs suspects déclenchent un avertissement anti-hameçonnage et les expéditeurs vérifiés affichent leur logo (BIMI). L’annonce ne dit rien du chiffrement de bout en bout. Contrairement à Proton Mail ou Tuta Mail, Kagi ne dispose pas de chiffrement associé à un modèle « zéro accès ».
L’IA est de la partie mais reste bien évidemment facultative. Elle permet de formuler des requêtes en langage naturel pour ranger ses mails, régler les droits de chaque règle (lire le contenu, éviter la boîte de réception) ou interroger sur le contenu de la boîte, avec une reconnaissance de caractères pour les fichiers PDF et une vision artificielle pour les photos en pièces jointes. La fonctionnalité Inbox Highlights remonte ce qui demande votre attention. Un interrupteur permet de tout couper, et les filtres Sieve restent disponibles. Proton Mail propose de son côté six catégories automatiques façon Gmail. Chez Tuta, son cofondateur Matthias Pfau il parlait de machine learning ciblé, pour filtrer le spam, plutôt que de grands modèles de langage.
Puisqu’il s’agit d’une bêta, le service n’est pas achevé. Les contacts et l’intégration complète de Kagi Assistant sont prévus au premier trimestre de l’année prochaine, et les applications mobiles natives au troisième trimestre 2027. D’ici là, il faut passer par la version web mobile ou un client IMAP/JMAP. Kagi promet par ailleurs de ne pas enfermer l’utilisateur. L’internaute ayant mis fin à son abonnement pourra toujours accéder à sa boîte pendant six mois. Il sera en mesure d’envoyer et recevoir des mails pendant les 60 premiers jours, puis de lire et exporter les messages en un clic pendant les quatre mois restants.

articles.title: TP-Link's Wi-Fi 7 mesh system is the under-$200 dead-zone fix I'd buy
articles.text:
Mesh Wi-Fi fixed my home office dead zones — and this TP-Link Wi-Fi 7 pack is under $200 for Black Friday
One of the most affordable ways to bring Wi-Fi 7 to your home office
Since introducing a mesh system into my home for work, I'm a true convert. No more internet dead zones, no more connection drop-outs, and reliable speeds throughout the house.
Now, a lot of these mesh router packs can be pretty expensive, but one that stands out to me for being decidedly budget-friendly, especially for Black Friday, is the TP-Link Deco 7 BE23 Wi-Fi 7 mesh system (3-pack), now $195 (was $250) at Amazon.
This dual-band Wi-Fi 7 system features broad coverage of up to 6,500 square feet, two 2.5Gbps ports on each unit, and simple app setup. better still, for those who don't want to trail cables into every room, it supports both wired and wireless backhaul at the same time.
A dual-band Wi-Fi 7 mesh system rated for up to 2,882 Mbps on 5 GHz and 688 Mbps on 2.4 GHz, with Multi-Link Operation for steadier connections. The 3-pack covers up to 6,500 square feet and supports up to 150 devices. Each unit has two 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports, and the system can use wired and wireless backhaul simultaneously.
Why We Recommend It
Our sister site Tom's Guide gave the Deco BE23 an Editor's Choice award in its TP-Link Deco BE23 review, which tested the 2-pack. They praised its low price, quick setup, and small units, and said it delivers more data for the buck than other mesh sets. The main limits are that it's dual-band only, with no 6GHz band, and each unit has just two Ethernet ports. For most, that won't be a deal-breaker, but it's worth pointing out for those that need a tri-band model with more connectivity.
Price Context & Historical Value
TP-Link lists the 3-pack at $249.99, so $194.69 saves you about $55. Tom's Guide spotted it for $180 at Amazon earlier, so this is a good price but not the lowest we've seen.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the TP-Link Deco BE23 if... you want affordable whole-home Wi-Fi 7, your home has dead zones a single router can't reach, or you have multi-gig internet and want 2.5Gbps wired connections.
❌ Skip the TP-Link Deco BE23 if... you want 6GHz Wi-Fi for the fastest wireless speeds, you need more than two Ethernet ports per unit, or you'd rather wait to see if it drops back to about $180.
