articles.title: HP Inc. Reports Fiscal 2026 Full Year and Fourth Quarter Results
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
HP Inc. Reports Fiscal 2026 Full Year and Fourth Quarter Results
HP Inc. and its subsidiaries ("HP" or the "Company") announced fiscal 2026 net revenue of $60.5 billion, up 9.5% (up 7.8% in constant currency) from the prior-year period.
Fiscal 2026 GAAP diluted net EPS was $2.62, down from $2.65 in the prior-year and within the previously provided outlook of $2.52 to $2.62. Fiscal 2026 non-GAAP diluted net EPS was $3.33, up from $3.12 in the prior-year and above the previously provided outlook of $3.19 to $3.29. Both GAAP and non-GAAP diluted net EPS included a $0.26 favorable impact from tariff refunds, as compared to the $0.19 impact included in the previously provided outlook. Fiscal 2026 non-GAAP net earnings and non-GAAP diluted net EPS exclude certain adjustments. Refer to "Adjustments to GAAP Net earnings" section in the below tables.Fourth quarter net revenue was $16.0 billion, up 9.3% (up 8.6% in constant currency) from the prior-year period. 
Fourth quarter GAAP diluted net EPS was $0.84, flat from $0.84 in the prior-year period and within the previously provided outlook of $0.74 to $0.84. Fourth quarter non-GAAP diluted net EPS was $0.83, down from $0.93 in the prior-year period and above the previously provided outlook of $0.69 to $0.79. Both GAAP and non-GAAP diluted net EPS included a $0.15 favorable impact from tariff refunds, as compared to the $0.08 impact included in the previously provided outlook. Fourth quarter non-GAAP net earnings and non-GAAP diluted net EPS exclude certain adjustments. Refer to "Adjustments to GAAP Net earnings" section in the below tables.
Bruce Broussard, Interim CEO, HP Inc."In the fourth quarter, we continued to grow our higher-value businesses, with AI PCs reaching nearly 60% of shipments, while taking steps to address memory and storage cost pressures. Advances in processing power and engineering are accelerating AI at the edge, enabling agentic experiences and new device form factors. We believe these innovations will drive multiple waves of device refresh and create sustained growth opportunities. With our engineering expertise, global scale, and deep customer relationships, HP is uniquely positioned to help define the next era of edge computing and create long-term value for customers and shareholders."
Karen Parkhill, CFO, HP Inc."We grew FY26 revenue 9.5%, delivered on our guidance for the year, exceeded our free cash flow target and returned $2.3 billion to shareholders, despite a challenging environment. While our fiscal 2027 outlook reflects a prudent view of continued cost and demand pressures, we have a strong track record of addressing challenges and are confident in our ability to drive improvement in our profitability throughout the year."
Asset management
HP generated $4.0 billion in net cash provided by operating activities and $3.3 billion of free cash flow in fiscal 2026. Free cash flow includes net cash provided by operating activities of $4.0 billion adjusted for net investment in leases from integrated financing of $142 million and net investments in property, plant, equipment and purchased intangibles of $0.8 billion. HP utilized $1.2 billion of cash during fiscal 2026 to repurchase approximately 46.7 million shares of common stock in the open market. When combined with the $1.1 billion of cash used to pay dividends, HP returned 70% of its free cash flow to shareholders in fiscal 2026.
HP's net cash provided by operating activities in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was $0.9 billion. Accounts receivable ended the quarter at $7.0 billion, down 2 days quarter over quarter to 39 days. Inventory ended the quarter at $12.3 billion, up 11 days quarter over quarter to 84 days. Accounts payable ended the quarter at $22.7 billion, up 4 days quarter over quarter to 155 days.
HP generated $0.8 billion of free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Free cash flow includes net cash provided by operating activities of $0.9 billion adjusted for net investment in leases from integrated financing of $73 million and net investments in property, plant, equipment and purchased intangibles of $201 million.
HP's dividend payment of $0.30 per share in the fourth quarter resulted in cash usage of $270 million. HP also utilized $0.5 billion of cash during the quarter to repurchase approximately 15.9 million shares of common stock in the open market. HP exited the quarter with $4.4 billion in gross cash, which includes cash and cash equivalents of $4.4 billion, restricted cash of $2 million, and short-term investments of $3 million included in other current assets. Restricted cash is related to amounts collected and held on behalf of a third party for trade receivables previously sold.
The HP board of directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.31 per share on the Company's common stock, payable on January 6, 2027 to stockholders of record as of the close of business on December 9, 2026. This is the first dividend of HP's 2027 fiscal year.
Fiscal 2026 fourth quarter segment results
Personal Systems net revenue was $11.8 billion, up 14% year over year (up 13% in constant currency) with a 3.0% operating margin. Consumer PS net revenue was down 7% and Commercial PS net revenue was up 23%. Total units were down 29% with Consumer PS units down 31% and Commercial PS units down 28%.
Printing net revenue was $4.3 billion, down 1% year over year (down 2% in constant currency) with a 19.7% operating margin. Consumer Printing net revenue was down 1% and Commercial Printing net revenue was up 2%. Supplies net revenue was down 2% (down 3% in constant currency). Total hardware units were down 2%, with Consumer Printing units down 3% and Commercial Printing units down 1%.Stock-Based Compensation Expense Change
Effective starting the first quarter of fiscal year 2027, HP will exclude stock-based compensation expense from non-GAAP cost of net revenue, gross profit, gross margin, operating expenses, earnings from operations, operating margin, net earnings and diluted net EPS. HP will reflect this change to the prior periods presented on an as-if basis and this change will have no impact on the Company's previously reported consolidated GAAP results. With this change the Company expects a non-GAAP tax rate of 17% based on current tax laws. The net impact of this change would be $0.38 per share in fiscal year 2026.
Outlook
For the fiscal 2027 first quarter, HP estimates non-GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $0.66 to $0.76. Fiscal 2027 first quarter non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimates excludes $0.24 primarily related to restructuring and other charges, amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense and corresponding tax impacts. Other than these known adjustments, certain items such as certain litigation charges (benefits) and tax adjustments cannot be reasonably estimated or predicted or is dependent on future events outside of our control and reconciliation is not available without unreasonable effort.
For fiscal 2027, HP estimates non-GAAP diluted net EPS to be in the range of $3.15 to $3.45. Fiscal 2027 non-GAAP diluted net EPS estimates excludes $0.75 primarily related to restructuring and other charges, amortization of intangible assets, stock-based compensation expense and corresponding tax impacts. Other than these known adjustments, certain items such as certain litigation charges (benefits) and tax adjustments cannot be reasonably estimated or predicted or is dependent on future events outside of our control and reconciliation is not available without unreasonable effort.
For fiscal 2027, HP estimates free cash flow to be in the range of $2.9 to $3.1 billion.

articles.title: OpenAI and Cisco Unveil AI-Assisted Linux Security Tool to Block Exploits Before Patching
articles.text:
OpenAI and Cisco have teamed up to launch Shirudo (meaning "shield" in Japanese), an open-source Linux runtime that allows artificial intelligence (AI) agents to defend systems without downtime.
"It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches," OpenAI said in a post on X.
The AI upstart called the initiative a "first step" toward "self-defending infrastructure" that can adapt itself to new threats while the services continue to run and enable defenders to test and deploy fixes without any disruption.
The development comes as AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, finding critical bugs in foundational software used to power internet-connected software.
Shirudo is being pitched as a way for defenders to test temporary safeguards (aka shields) and check if they block behavior that exposes a vulnerability, while letting legitimate requests pass through. Once a shield is approved by an operator, it can be deployed without having to stop the service.
The idea is to avoid a complete service disruption to block a line of attack simply because both an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same underlying Linux operation.
To achieve this, Shirudo makes use of eBPF (short for extended Berkeley Packet Filter), a technology that makes it possible to run lightweight, sandboxed programs inside the kernel without the need for modifying the system code or restarting it.
"eBPF is a highly efficient, sandboxed virtual machine in the Linux Kernel," Cisco's Isovalent said. "These eBPF programs allow you to interact with the Linux kernel to observe and take action on any events happening on a machine. Some use eBPF to simply observe everything on their system, others use it to enforce policies (routing, security, and more)."
Notably, Shirudo is built atop the foundations of Tetragon, an eBPF-based security platform that Isovalent developed and open-sourced in May 2022. The crucial difference is that it's primarily designed for agents and leverages the capabilities of eBPF to inject code mitigations.
Central to Shirudo is a guardian agent that uses eBPF shields to block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system, while giving security teams the flexibility to monitor how a proposed shield would affect the application before enforcing it. The shields are also cryptographically signed and verified prior to being loaded.
"Agents scan open-source code and take in vendor disclosures," Cisco said. "They trace each vulnerability to the affected assets and attack paths, then write a small, targeted shield. They check that the shield covers the exploit and that the service still runs. The shield only graduates to active blocking when the evidence says it's safe, and it retires when the real patch lands."
This involves the following steps -
- An agent is tasked with finding new vulnerabilities in an application, or working off external sources of new vulnerability disclosures.
- Shirudo on the operator machine builds a security shield consisting of eBPF or application bytecode after reproducing and validating the exploit.
- The shield is delivered as signed .bee packages via an OCI-compliant registry.
- The Shirudo layer on each target pulls these .bee packages, validating each signature using TPMs to establish trust and safety.
In a controlled experiment, a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart, OpenAI said.
OpenAI and Cisco said the goal is to fight AI-based threats with AI and counter the risks posed by AI-driven attacks as soon as a vulnerability is identified at machine speed.
"We need this kind of machine-speed defense because AI models have become incredibly good at finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities, and they get better with every generation," Thomas Graf, CTO of Cisco Security, and Liz Rice, chief open source office at Isovalent, said. "They can also chain flaws together and discover creative new attack vectors that no one has thought about before."
"Yet a critical fix in widely-used software, from the Linux kernel to the libraries every application depends on, still takes days, weeks, or even months to reach the majority of systems. That timeframe is no longer acceptable given that the mean time to exploitation has become negative."

articles.title: Relâmpago: Galaxy Z Flip 7 tem menor preço histórico na Black Week do Mercado Livre
articles.text:
Relâmpago: Galaxy Z Flip 7 tem menor preço histórico na Black Week do Mercado Livre
Galaxy Z Flip 7 (256 GB) tem mais de 60% de desconto em promoção relâmpago no Mercado Livre; celular se destaca pela tela dobrável e desempenho avançado
O Galaxy Z Flip 7 de 256 GB entrou em oferta relâmpago por apenas R$ 3.599,10 (Pix) na Black Week do Mercado Livre. Trata-se do menor preço histórico já registrado pelo Achados do TB desde o lançamento do smartphone, em uma queda de 61% sobre o preço original (R$ 9.199).
O celular da Samsung se destaca pela tela dobrável de 120 Hz, câmera wide de 50 MP e desempenho avançado com chip Exynos 2500.
Esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos para o Galaxy Z Flip 7 256 GB. Nas outras 2 ofertas publicadas desde novembro de 2025, o melhor foi R$ 4.751,10 (Mercado Livre, 17/11/2025).
O Galaxy Z Flip 7 é um celular dobrável em formato de concha lançado em 2025. Ele tem tela interna de AMOLED Dinâmico 2X flexível com 6,9″ e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, o que permite a reprodução de imagens com cores e contrastes excelentes, além de alta fluidez. A externa Super AMOLED de 4,1″ também tem 120 Hz e traz recurso Always-On.
O chip Exynos 2500 e os 12 GB de RAM do Z Flip 7 sustentam apps em multitarefa e funções do Galaxy AI localmente. Os 256 GB de espaço interno são adequados para guardar muitas fotos e vídeos, além de aplicativos do dia a dia.
O kit de câmeras é formado por uma wide de 50 MP com OIS e uma ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e uma frontal de 10 MP que tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K a 60 fps.
O corpo de alumínio reforçado Armor do Z Flip 7 traz o vidro Gorilla Glass Victus 2 sobre a tela externa, que resiste a quedas e arranhões. A certificação IP48 adiciona proteção em cenários como poeira moderada e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.300 mAh resiste a até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a Samsung. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 25 W via cabo USB-C e de 15 W sem fio garante o uso por tempo prolongado.
O Galaxy Z Flip 7 de 256 GB (apenas R$ 3.599,10 no Pix) será atualizado até o Android 23 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.

articles.title: Google Maps prépare son plus gros changement de look depuis 2023, Android Auto pourrait suivre
articles.text:
Google Maps prépare son plus gros changement de look depuis 2023, Android Auto pourrait suivre
Fond presque noir la nuit, verdure éteinte le jour, tracé violet à la place de l'éternel bleu. Un réglage encore verrouillé dans Google Maps pour Android promet de transfigurer l'écran de navigation, et les indices s'accumulent du côté d'Android Auto. Ceux qui ont pesté contre la palette imposée en 2023 peuvent souffler : cette fois, Google semble décidé à laisser le choix.
Les limiers d'Android Authority ont débusqué un menu "Map style" (style de carte) dans la version 26.48.00.1027729593 de Google Maps pour Android. Il propose deux options : "Standard", la palette actuelle, et "High-visibility" (haute visibilité), une déclinaison nettement plus contrastée que le site est parvenu à activer avant l'heure.
Les teintes de la carte changent du tout au tout pendant le guidage. Google n'a encore rien officialisé.
Mode haute visibilité de Google Maps : ce qui change à l'écran
En journée, la végétation adopte un vert plus sombre et plus mat. Les vastes aplats beige et blanc cassé qui tapissent villes et campagnes virent au gris, et le curseur de position troque son bleu contre du violet. La carte gagne en sobriété, sans rien perdre de ses repères.
3️⃣ Starting with light mode, the differences are easy to spot!
➡️ Green areas become darker
➡️ Beige backgrounds turn gray
➡️ The blue location marker becomes purple
The result is a more muted-looking map, without changing the familiar navigation layout. pic.twitter.com/DOm48azh9J
— Android Authority (@AndroidAuth) November 24, 2026
La nuit, la métamorphose devient saisissante. Le fond bleuté du mode sombre s'efface au profit de tons quasi noirs, lacs et parcs s'assombrissent, et l'itinéraire, jusqu'ici cyan, s'habille d'un violet nimbé de lavande. Sur ce fond d'encre, le tracé se détache d'un seul coup d'œil.
4️⃣ Dark mode gets an even bigger makeover.
Google swaps the usual blue-tinted background for much darker, almost black shades. And that bright cyan route you've been following? It turns purple with a lighter lavender center.
Quite a change from the Google Maps we're used to. pic.twitter.com/7zjRxzoCXm
— Android Authority (@AndroidAuth) November 24, 2026
Seule la carte change de peau. Les indications de direction, les boutons de navigation, l'heure d'arrivée estimée et le bandeau d'informations en bas d'écran conservent leur apparence et leur place actuelles.
Le souvenir de fin 2023 plane forcément. Google avait alors imposé à tous une palette plus froide, proche de celle d'Apple Plans, et les critiques avaient fusé sur la difficulté à distinguer les types de routes. Cette fois, le réglage prend la forme d'un choix entre deux styles. Les inconditionnels du "Standard" devraient pouvoir le conserver.
Android Auto et Navigation immersive : un calendrier encore flou
La piste automobile repose sur un précédent. En septembre, Android Authority avait déjà repéré une Google Maps nettement plus sombre dans la bêta d'Android Auto 17.6, même en mode clair. En mode sombre, le panneau du prochain virage troquait déjà son bleu canard contre un gris profond.
Rien ne confirme encore le lien entre les deux découvertes.
Un style commun au smartphone et au tableau de bord reste donc une hypothèse solide, rien de plus. Il s'ajouterait à un chantier déjà copieux, entre la grande refonte d'Android Auto dévoilée le 12 mai et le mode clair de l'interface, en préparation dans la version 18.2.
Selon autoevolution, ce mode pourrait d'abord arriver sur les appareils déjà passés à la Navigation immersive. Présentée le 12 mars 2026 par Miriam Daniel, vice-présidente de Google Maps, cette refonte 3D est la plus importante du guidage depuis plus de dix ans, selon Google. Elle reste pourtant cantonnée aux États-Unis.
L'Europe a bien reçu l'assistant Demander à Maps le 16 novembre. La navigation 3D, elle, n'a toujours aucune date de ce côté de l'Atlantique.
Les automobilistes français risquent donc de patienter avant de rouler en violet. Android Authority le reconnaît lui-même : impossible de savoir quand le nouveau réglage sera proposé à tous.

articles.title: Pasos para reducir el gasto de datos móviles en iPhone
articles.text:
El iPhone permite ver qué aplicaciones consumen datos móviles y limitar su actividad cuando no se usan. Los ajustes están en la app Configuración: el menú Celular muestra el gasto por aplicación, y los modos de datos reducidos y de actualización en segundo plano frenan las descargas automáticas.
Estos pasos se basan en las páginas de soporte de Apple consultadas en noviembre de 2026. Los nombres de los menús pueden variar según la versión de iOS, el modelo y el operador de telefonía.
Muchas aplicaciones siguen trabajando aunque el usuario no las abra: buscan contenido nuevo, sincronizan fotos o descargan actualizaciones. Si el plan de datos es limitado, esa actividad puede agotar los gigas antes de fin de mes.
Primero, descubrir qué app gasta más
Apple indica abrir Configuración y tocar Celular. Más abajo aparece la lista de aplicaciones y servicios, y al tocar Mostrar todo se ve la cantidad de datos móviles que usó cada una debajo de su nombre.
Esa cifra corresponde al período actual y no se reinicia sola: para empezar de cero hay que bajar hasta el final de la pantalla y tocar Restablecer estadísticas. Apple aclara que, para conocer el consumo exacto de un período de facturación, hay que consultar al operador.
En esa misma lista, cada aplicación tiene un interruptor. Al desactivarlo, la app usa solo Wi-Fi; sin esa red, no podrá conectarse. Los servicios del sistema aparecen aparte, y Apple precisa que no se puede apagar su acceso a los datos móviles de forma individual.
Activar el modo de datos reducidos
El ajuste más general está en Configuración > Celular > Opciones de datos móviles. En iPhone con 5G, se toca Modo de datos y se elige Modo de datos reducidos. En conexiones LTE o 4G, el interruptor aparece directamente en esas opciones. Con dos tarjetas SIM, se elige primero la línea.
Según Apple, el modo existe desde iOS 13 y pausa las actualizaciones automáticas y las tareas en segundo plano. También reduce la calidad de la transmisión de video, detiene las descargas y copias de seguridad automáticas y suspende las actualizaciones de Fotos de iCloud.
Las aplicaciones de Apple se adaptan de forma propia: App Store desactiva la reproducción automática de video y las descargas automáticas, y Podcasts solo baja episodios con Wi-Fi. El modo también puede activarse por separado para cada red Wi-Fi, desde el botón de información junto a su nombre.
Limitar la actualización en segundo plano
Para un recorte menos radical, se puede ajustar la actualización en segundo plano: Configuración > General > Actualización en segundo plano. Allí se elige entre Desactivada, Wi-Fi o Wi-Fi y datos móviles. La opción Wi-Fi evita esa actividad en la red celular. Debajo, una lista permite apagarla aplicación por aplicación.
Este ajuste no bloquea todo el consumo: un video que el usuario reproduce o una descarga que inicia siguen usando datos. Tampoco equivale a silenciar notificaciones. Para impedir que una app use la red celular por completo, hay que desactivarla en Celular.
Si la actualización en segundo plano aparece desactivada o no disponible, conviene revisar si están activos el modo de datos reducidos o el modo de bajo consumo, que también la apagan. Un perfil de administración de la empresa o la escuela puede imponer restricciones adicionales.
Para comprobar el efecto, conviene anotar las cifras de la lista de aplicaciones antes de los cambios y compararlas después de un período de uso similar. Apple no publica cuántos datos ahorra cada ajuste, por lo que el resultado depende de las apps instaladas y de los hábitos de uso.

articles.title: Revopoint Launches MIRACO 2 on Kickstarter: Scan in One, Create with Agents
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Revopoint Launches MIRACO 2 on Kickstarter: Scan in One, Create with Agents
An all-in-one 3D scanner combining high-precision capture, powerful onboard computing, and AI-driven workflows—with Super Early Bird pricing starting at $1,425.
The Offer is available from today, November 18 on Kickstarter. Grab the Super Early Bird Offer, with up to 38% off, starting at $1,425. 
Back MIRACO 2 on KickstarterTruly Standalone Design with Powerful Onboard ComputingWeighing just 960 g, MIRACO 2 integrates depth computation, 3D scanning, point cloud processing, and basic editing into one portable device.
Powered by an 8-core CPU and 6-core NPU, it supports three operating modes:
- Standalone Mode: Scan, preview, process, and make adjustments directly on its 6-inch 2K AMOLED touchscreen.
- Wireless PC Mode: Connect to a computer via Wi-Fi 6 for a flexible scanning workflow.
- Wired PC Mode: Connect via USB-C 3.0 for a stable, high-performance workflow.
When connected to a GPU-powered PC, Multi-Line Laser scanning can reach speeds of up to 120 FPS.
High Precision Meets Versatile Scanning Capabilities
MIRACO 2 delivers single-frame accuracy of up to 0.02 mm in Multi-Line Laser Mode and offers six scanning modes to handle a wide range of objects and applications:
- 34-Line Blue Cross Laser
- 15-Line Parallel Laser
- Single-Line Deep-Hole Laser
- Full-Field HD
- VCSEL Rapid
- Hybrid HD
With a maximum capture rate of 10 million points per second in Hybrid HD mode, MIRACO 2 can handle challenging surfaces and geometries, including reflective metals, black objects, intricate structures, and human bodies.
Additional capabilities include:
- Markerless tracking for textured objects in laser-line modes (PC mode).
- A recommended minimum scan volume of 10 × 10 × 10 mm.
- A maximum scanning volume of 5 × 5 × 5 m when paired with the optional Photogrammetric Metrology Kit.
- VCSEL working distance ranging from 300 mm to 1,000 mm.
Revo Agents: An AI-Native Ecosystem for 3D Workflows
Capturing an object is only the beginning. Turning scan data into CAD models or inspection results often means navigating complex software and hours of manual processing.
Revo Agents is designed to change that.Introduced by Revopoint as the world's first agent-powered 3D reality ecosystem, Revo Agents acts as an AI-native engineering co-pilot, allowing users to direct complex 3D operations through simple natural language commands.
Its autonomous, prompt-driven pipeline spans:
- Real-time point cloud fusion
- Automated Scan-to-CAD conversion
- Scan-to-Inspection tolerance analysis
Rather than manually navigating each processing step, users can describe the task they want to accomplish and let Revo Agents help carry the workflow forward.
Paired with MIRACO 2, Revo Agents bridges high-precision reality capture and production-ready engineering output—reducing repetitive post-processing while keeping creators focused on design, analysis, and decisions.
You define the task. Revo Agents helps execute it.
Full-Color Capture and Physically Scaled 3DGS
MIRACO 2's dual RGB camera system combines a 2 MP near-field camera and a 50 MP far-field camera for detailed, full-color 3D capture.
In PC mode, it also supports physically scaled 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), allowing users to export 1:1-scale.splat models for XR applications and digital visualization.
AI-powered cleanup tools further simplify model preparation:
- AI Segmentation: Automatically identifies and removes unwanted environmental point clouds.
- AI Cropping: Streamlines model cleanup and editing.
Together with Revopoint's software ecosystem, these capabilities support an integrated Scan-to-CAD workflow, helping users move from physical objects to usable digital models.
Built for Indoor and Outdoor Work
Designed for both indoor and outdoor applications, it supports ambient lighting conditions of up to 100,000 lux. Its 10,000 mAh battery provides approximately three hours of runtime, with 65 W fast charging.
Two configurations are available:
- 16 GB RAM + 256 GB storage
- 32 GB RAM + 512 GB storage

articles.title: Hackers Exploit N-able MailAssure Flaw While AI Agents Exploit MONAI Label Zero-Day
articles.text:
The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday added two flaws impacting N-able MailAssure and MONAI Label to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
The critical vulnerabilities are listed below -
- CVE-2026-134624 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in N-able MailAssure's LDAP synchronization connection check that could allow an authenticated API user to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.
- CVE-2026-133968 (CVSS score: 9.8) - A path traversal vulnerability in MONAI Label that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to write arbitrary files outside the intended datastore directory, potentially resulting in remote code execution.
The exploitation of CVE-2026-134624 stems from a disclosure last week, in which N-able said it detected a security incident that resulted in a service disruption affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud on November 16, 2026.
As of November 21, 2026, 11:44 p.m. UTC, access to the Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud dashboard and APIs has been restored.
"N-able has remediated the recent security incident affecting our Mail Assure and SpamExperts environments and restored the impacted functionality," a spokesperson for the company told The Hacker News. Our investigation to date indicates that exploitation was confined to a single N-able hosted server and continued monitoring since remediation has found no further malicious activity."
CVE-2026-133968, on the other hand, has been linked to an agentic attack in which a suspected China-nexus threat actor leveraged CAIRN, an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered problem-solving engine, to conduct hacking operations with minimal human involvement.
The activity, which ran for an approximately 48-hour period beginning September 8, 2026, targeted IP addresses associated with universities across East Asia outside mainland China.
"In this campaign, the actor provided a list of targeted IP addresses with variations of the goal to 'obtain shell access,'" CJ Moses, CISO of Amazon Integrated Security, said. "Based on those inputs, the AI agents planned, executed, and adjusted their approach as they learned, without the operator choosing each next step."
Some of these attacks unsuccessfully attempted to brute-force their way into a Redis instance at one university and a GPU server at another. The activity also singled out an unspecified target running MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging AI application, identifying the aforementioned zero-day and exploiting it in about 11 minutes to write arbitrary files to the server.
"In a later session, the agents used the same vulnerability to write a Python reverse shell payload to sitecustomize.py, a file Python automatically imports at interpreter startup," Moses said. "The agents then triggered a training API endpoint to spawn a new Python process. The new process imported the payload and established a reverse shell running as root."
Following the discovery of the zero-day, the operator is said to have provided the AI agents with a proxy to tunnel into a second university network running the same vulnerable software, and then directed them to target other machines in that network.
The attacks are part of a broader cluster of attacks involving the use of AI-driven frameworks like ARTEX, CAIRN, and AntiFox, and CyberStrikeAI in recent months. A subset of these activities is estimated to have breached over 100 companies, including John Deere and SharkNinja. The end goals, per NorForge, revolve around establishing persistent access and financial theft -
- AIA0001, which has targeted organizations, mainly in the U.S., Japan, and Australia, to deploy web shells and gain access to e-commerce and payment infrastructure for subsequent monetization.
- AIA0002, which has targeted merchant payment services, gray-market payment sites, pharmaceutical sites, and a criminal carding site for financial gain.
- AIA0003, which has targeted smaller e-commerce sites and very large U.S.-based commercial platforms to obtain shell access, admin panel access, or database access.
In a report published last week, Amazon Web Services (AWS) also revealed that its MadPot sensor network captured requests from AI agents linked to two offensive campaigns running on ARTEX, an AI-native penetration framework.
"The most prominent ARTEX campaign was a large-scale theft of credentials to access AI models, organized as a self-sustaining operation in which stolen keys paid for the LLM inference powering further credential hunting," AWS said. "Another campaign targeted cryptocurrency exchanges for know-your-customer (KYC) verification bypass using real-time deepfake injection."
According to Datadog Security Labs, ARTEX also appears under other names like ScopeWeaver, LUCK — 自主资产控制台 (LUCK — Autonomous Asset Console), and 观澜SEC渗透测试平台 (Guanlan SEC Penetration Testing Platform).
In-the-wild activity involving ARTEX has also targeted several AWS environments with an aim to access financial data. Initial access vectors used in these attacks include compromised long-term AWS access keys and public Cognito user pools, with the latter being used to register an account, collect tokens, and enumerate AWS accounts.
"In one instance using a valid long-term access key, ARTEX's most frequent action was FilterLogEvents," security researcher Julie Agnes Sparks said. "The most common searches were various naming conventions of cryptocurrency companies, hedge funds, and related financial institutions. The terms combine a company name with words like fund, invoice, billing, and LLC."
Telemetry data gathered by Previdian from its sensors has recorded 52 HTTP requests containing explicit ARTEX markers between October 18 and November 15, 2026, from 10 source IP addresses.
"Further investigation of these sources identified 3,651 related HTTP records involving application discovery, authentication probing, remote code execution attempts, path traversal and attempts to retrieve sensitive configuration data," Ryan Dewhurst, founder and CEO of Previdian, said.
"The most significant activity targeted Oracle WebLogic, Langflow, and Flowise, with additional payloads associated with Apache Struts, Log4j, and PHPUnit."
Interestingly, one of the IP addresses associated with ARTEX activity, 31.22.91[.]156, overlaps with the AWS-documented campaign targeting AI infrastructure, including Langflow exploitation attempts consistent with CVE-2025-3248.
In light of active exploitation, Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies are recommended to apply the latest fixes for the two flaws by November 26, 2026.

articles.title: RAM price tracking 2026 — price tracking on DDR5 and DDR4 memory of all capacities

Check the best prices on DDR5 and DDR4 memory kits.

Now, even more so than before the shortage began, price tags are fluctuating significantly from day to day, and it's becoming increasingly complex to tell when you're getting a fair deal versus overpaying for the same memory kit. We've compiled this comprehensive RAM price tracker that monitors the availability and pricing of different DDR5 and DDR4 memory kits across major U.S. retailers. Our goal is to take the guesswork out of memory shopping and help you make an informed purchasing decision.
We update this index regularly with the lowest prices available in the U.S. market for each memory kit. Our tracker covers a range of capacities and speeds across both budget and premium brands. We list the lowest price for each available memory kit, regardless of manufacturer, so you see the absolute best deals currently on offer.

High-capacity kits, particularly DDR5, frequently show the most severe stock shortages and price premiums. articles.title: Avec le tout nouveau Claude Ship, l'IA d'Anthropic ne se contente plus d'écrire du code, elle le valide
articles.text:
Anthropic a lancé Claude Ship cette semaine, un service capable de relire, corriger et approuver les pull requests des développeurs. Réservé aux offres professionnelles et à GitHub, il laisse aux équipes le dernier mot sur ce que l'IA peut valider seule.
L'entreprise Anthropic a lancé Claude Ship le lundi 23 novembre, qui se présente comme un ensemble d'outils d'intelligence artificielle qui prend en charge les pull requests, ces demandes de modification soumises avant d'intégrer du code à un projet. Le service relit chaque modification, corrige les problèmes signalés, puis décide si elle peut être fusionnée, selon des règles fixées par chaque équipe. Une nouvelle commande, /ship, permet aussi aux développeurs de l'utiliser directement depuis Claude Code.
Claude Ship, ou l'art de ne plus courir après les relecteurs
Quiconque a déjà ouvert une pull request connaît la routine. On attaque la tâche suivante, puis les remarques arrivent. On replonge dans un code qu'on croyait derrière soi, on corrige, on attend une nouvelle relecture. Il reste ensuite à trouver le collègue qui voudra bien valider. Exiger un humain pour chaque modification reste tenable tant que des humains écrivent chaque ligne. Mais chez Anthropic, c'est désormais Claude qui écrit l'essentiel du code de l'équipe Claude Code, et l'entreprise voulait que tout ce qui suit la pull request avance au même rythme.
Claude Ship repose sur trois outils qui interviennent l'un après l'autre sur chaque pull request. Le premier, Code Review, est le seul à être déjà disponible en version finale. L'outil examine chaque modification sous plusieurs angles et met ses propres conclusions à l'épreuve. Il les trie, puis les publie sur la pull request, avec trois niveaux d'exigence au choix, que sont Quick, Standard ou Deep. Vatsal Bhatt, directeur de l'ingénierie chez un client, raconte que l'outil a souvent « repéré de vrais problèmes avant qu'un relecteur humain n'arrive sur la pull request ». Ensuite entre en scène PR Steward, une sorte de dépanneur de garde.
Il se charge de réparer les tests automatiques qui échouent, de démêler les conflits entre deux versions du code et de traiter les remarques laissées par Code Review, par d'autres outils ou par les collègues. Après chaque passage, il explique ce qu'il a changé et comment l'annuler. On l'oriente avec « @claude » suivi d'une consigne, et on l'arrête avec « @claude stop ». Surtout, il n'est conçu ni pour approuver ni pour fusionner.
Le droit de dire oui revient à Claude Approvals. L'équipe écrit sa politique d'approbation dans un fichier rangé dans le projet, et l'IA l'applique. Elle donne son feu vert aux changements de routine si la politique l'autorise, et exige une validation humaine plus poussée pour les cas sensibles. Anthropic le présente comme une version plus maligne de CODEOWNERS, le fichier GitHub qui désigne qui doit relire quoi. Il peut tenir compte des conclusions de Code Review ou de critères rédigés en langage courant. L'éditeur américain conseille de le laisser d'abord en simple observateur, le temps de gagner en confiance. « Nous gardons un humain dans la boucle, et son temps va désormais aux modifications qui en ont besoin », insiste Vatsal Bhatt.
Avec /ship, Claude Ship s'invite dans le quotidien des développeurs
Pour essayer, une commande suffit dans Claude Code : /ship. Selon Anthropic, elle est ouverte à tous les développeurs et se déploie depuis le 23 novembre dans Claude Code et l'application de bureau. Claude pousse la modification, ouvre la pull request et la relit. Il traite ensuite les remarques et les tests en échec. Ce qui peut être fusionné dépend toujours des droits du développeur et des règles du projet. Anthropic avance ses propres résultats et explique que de juin à septembre, son équipe Claude Code a fusionné plus de deux fois plus de pull requests.
Dans le même temps, la part de modifications annulées après coup a baissé de plus de 40 %. L'entreprise précise que la relecture de Claude n'est qu'un garde-fou parmi d'autres. Elle cite aussi un exemple. Un client avait été induit en erreur par la documentation de l'API Analytics d'Anthropic. Un chef de produit a demandé à Claude Tag, l'agent maison intégré à Slack, si une correction était en cours, et Claude Tag en a ouvert une. Code Review n'a rien trouvé de bloquant, un relecteur de la documentation a donné son accord et Claude Approvals aussi. Du coup, la correction était fusionnée le soir même.
Le service Claude Ship complet est réservé aux offres Team et Enterprise, et uniquement pour les projets hébergés sur GitHub. Les administrateurs activent Code Review et PR Steward projet par projet. Ils choisissent le niveau de relecture et le moment où elle se lance, et fixent un plafond de dépenses. Claude Approvals, lui, démarre dès qu'un fichier de règles figure sur la branche principale du projet, et un administrateur peut le couper. Plus personne n'a alors besoin de taper /ship. Alex Devkar, vice-président senior chargé de l'ingénierie et de l'analyse de données, assure que PR Steward aide les équipes de son projet pilote à « passer moins de temps sur les retours de relecture et plus de temps à développer ». Le mois de novembre est en tout cas particulièrement chargé pour Anthropic qui, le 9, sortait Claude Fable 5.2, présenté comme plus rapide et moins cher que son prédécesseur. Le lendemain, l'entreprise annonçait un tableur et un tableau blanc pour Claude.
Concernant la question financière, Claude Ship est facturé au token, ces fragments de texte que l'IA lit et produit. Le prix dépend du nombre et de la taille des pull requests, du niveau et de la fréquence des relectures, et du travail abattu par PR Steward. Claude Approvals n'a pas de coût de base, mais les critères qu'il utilise sont facturés. De plus, une règle qui s'appuie sur la relecture de Claude déclenche une analyse payante, même en mode observateur. /ship, lui, compte comme une utilisation normale de Claude Code.
Et trois types d'organisations sont privées de Ship. Il s'agit de celles qui ont exigé qu'Anthropic ne conserve aucune de leurs données, de celles en configuration HIPAA (la loi américaine sur les données de santé) et de celles qui gèrent leurs propres clés de chiffrement. Pour essayer de convaincre, Anthropic a décidé d'offrir aux comptes Enterprise éligibles au moins 10 000 dollars de crédits, sous conditions. Il faut les réclamer avant le 15 janvier 2027 et les utiliser dans les 30 jours. Coté au Nasdaq depuis le 19 novembre après la plus grosse introduction en Bourse de l'histoire, le créateur de Claude sait que chaque pull request relue, c'est aussi du chiffre d'affaires désormais.
- Excellente compréhension des consignes complexes
- Très bon niveau en rédaction
- Analyse de longs documents efficace

articles.title: Ugreen's DH4300 Plus is 'a better NAS than the price would suggest' at $350
articles.text:
Ugreen's DH4300 Plus is 'a better NAS than the price would suggest', and it's down to $350 at Amazon for Black Friday
A quiet, beginner-friendly NAS for photo backup, media streaming, and file sharing
The Ugreen NASync DH4300 Plus may not be a powerhouse NAS device, but for most home office and small business users, it ticks all the right boxes. After testing it out ourselves, we called it "an elegant design that delivers the basic functionality that most NAS users need at a price they can afford."
Now, if you want to replace cloud storage subscriptions with your own private storage at home, the Ugreen NASync DH4300 Plus is $350 (was $440) at Amazon - which is the lowest price we've seen it since last year's Black Friday.
There's a lot to like about this NAS system, which earned 4 stars in our review. It features four drive bays for up to 120TB, 8GB of RAM, 2.5GbE networking, real-time phone photo backup with AI albums, and no monthly fees
A four-bay NAS powered by an eight-core Rockchip RK3588 processor with 8GB of LPDDR4X RAM. It supports 3.5-inch and 2.5-inch drives for up to 120TB of storage, and ports include 2.5GbE Ethernet, HDMI 2.0b, two 10Gbps USB-A ports, and a 10Gbps USB-C port. UGREEN's apps handle phone photo backup, AI-powered albums, and remote access.
Why we recommend it
We gave the DH4300 Plus 4 stars in our Ugreen NASync DH4300 Plus review, praising its affordable price for a four-bay NAS, 8GB of RAM, 2.5GbE port, and quiet design with easy drive access. It's a great fit for file serving, media, and backups.
The trade-offs are that you can't upgrade the RAM, there are no M.2 slots for SSD caching, and its ARM processor rules out virtual machines and TrueNAS.
Price Context & Historical Value
Ugreen lists the DH4300 Plus at $439.99. It dropped to $374 at Amazon in September, so $349.99 is the lowest price we've seen since last year's Black Friday, where it fell to $340.
Should You Buy It?
✅ Buy the Ugreen DH4300 Plus if...
you want to back up your family's phone photos automatically, you're tired of paying for cloud storage, or you want a simple NAS for movies and shared files.
❌ Skip the Ugreen DH4300 Plus if...
you want to run virtual machines or heavy Docker apps, you need SSD caching or more than one network port, or you'd rather not buy hard drives separately.

articles.title: Mammotion lance ses promos Black Friday : jusqu’à 650 € sur ses robots tondeuses
articles.text:
Et si le meilleur cadeau de fin d’année, c’était finalement de ne plus avoir à passer les week-ends à venir derrière une tondeuse ? Mammotion anticipe le Black Friday dès le 10 novembre, avec des réductions pouvant atteindre 650 € sur ses robots tondeuses.
À l’approche des fêtes de fin d’année, Mammotion lance ses promotions Black Friday et Cyber Monday avec plusieurs modèles de robots-tondeuses à prix réduit. L’occasion de s’équiper avant le retour des beaux jours, et accessoirement de glisser sous le sapin un cadeau qui pourrait bien changer les habitudes de toute la famille.
Au programme, on retrouve des modèles compacts pour les jardins résidentiels, mais aussi des références plus ambitieuses capables de s’attaquer aux très grandes surfaces et aux terrains difficiles. Et pour l’achat de n’importe quel modèle des gammes LUBA 3 AWD et LUBA mini 2 AWD, Mammotion ajoute un support de lavage pour tondeuse offert.
LUBA mini 2 AWD 1000 : un robot compact pour simplifier la tonte au quotidien
Pour les jardins jusqu’à 1 000 m2, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1000 mise sur un format compact et une navigation autonome. Son système associant vision IA Tri-Cam et NetRTK lui permet de cartographier la pelouse avec précision, sans aucun câble périphérique à l’horizon ni installation complexe. Il peut également poursuivre son travail lorsque des arbres ou des avancées de toit perturbent temporairement le signal satellite.
Autre particularité intéressante, il bénéficie d’une transmission intégrale AWD (pour All-Wheel Drive), qui lui permet de négocier des pentes pouvant atteindre 80 %, soit 38,6°. Un avantage évident pour les jardins qui ne ressemblent pas exactement à un terrain de golf parfaitement plat. Elle est également équipée d'un disque de coupe latéral qui coupe à seulement 5 cm des murs et des massifs, limite également les finitions manuelles avec un rotofil.
L’application mobile Mammotion permet enfin de gérer les zones de tonte, les plannings et les différents réglages. En promotion pour le Black Friday, le LUBA mini 2 AWD 1000 passe à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 499 €, soit 300 € d’économie, avec son support de lavage offert. Un pack avec mini-garage (pour protéger la tondeuse de la pluie notamment) est également proposé à 1 249 €.
LUBA mini 2 AWD 1500 : davantage de couverture pour les jardins complexes
Les jardins plus vastes et les configurations comportant davantage d’obstacles pourront se tourner vers le LUBA mini 2 AWD en version 1500. Cette déclinaison conserve les qualités tout-terrain de la gamme, mais adopte un système de navigation différent, associant cette fois un LiDAR à 360° et une vision IA à double caméra.
Cette combinaison lui permet de mieux appréhender son environnement, de détecter les obstacles plus tôt et d’adapter ses trajectoires. Avec une capacité annoncée de 1 500 m2, il s’adresse notamment aux propriétaires dont la pelouse comprend des arbres, des arbustes, des massifs ou encore du mobilier de jardin.
Il profite lui aussi de la transmission intégrale AWD, de la cartographie automatique multizone et du mode DropMow, particulièrement pratique pour lancer une tonte ponctuelle sans devoir enregistrer pour cela une nouvelle carte. En cette période de Black Friday, son prix passe à 1 399 € au lieu de 1 899 €, soit 500 € de remise.
Le pack avec mini-garage est quant à lui affiché à 1 499 €, avec toujours le support de lavage offert.
LUBA 3 AWD 3000 : la solution haut de gamme pour les grands terrains
Pour les propriétaires disposant de surfaces plus importantes et de terrains particulièrement exigeants, le LUBA 3 AWD 3000 représente une solution plus ambitieuse. La marque reprend ici sa transmission intégrale, capable de gérer des pentes jusqu’à 80 %, et l’associe à son système de navigation Tri-Fusion.
Celui-ci combine trois technologies : un LiDAR à 360°, le positionnement RTK et la vision par intelligence artificielle. L’objectif est de conserver une navigation ultra précise, même lorsque les conditions lumineuses ou l’environnement compliquent le travail des capteurs. Mammotion annonce une précision de positionnement de ±1 cm.
Le robot peut également reconnaître et éviter plus de 300 types d’obstacles, dont les jouets et les animaux. Sa largeur de coupe de 400 mm, répartie sur deux disques, lui permet de couvrir jusqu’à 500 m2 par heure. Depuis l’application, il est possible de gérer jusqu’à 50 zones, avec des paramètres de tonte personnalisables pour chacune.
Affiché à 2 149 € au lieu de 2 699 €, le LUBA 3 AWD 3000 bénéficie de 550 € de réduction, auxquels s’ajoute encore et toujours le support de lavage offert.
Et pour les propriétés encore plus vastes, le LUBA 3 AWD 5000 reprend cette même architecture technique dans une version capable de couvrir (comme son nom l’indique) jusqu’à 5 000 m2. Sa navigation Tri-Fusion, sa transmission intégrale et sa gestion multizone lui permettent de s’adapter aux configurations les plus exigeantes.
C’est aussi le modèle qui profite d’une remise particulièrement généreuse pendant cette opération, avec un prix qui chute à 2 599 € au lieu de 3 199 €, soit 600 € d’économie. Et avec le coupon de bienvenue de 50 € pour les premiers clients sur la boutique en ligne officielle Mammotion, la réduction atteint même 650 € (toujours avec le support de lavage offert).
YUKA mini 2 500 : la vision IA aussi pour les jardins plus modestes
Tout le monde n’a pas besoin d’un robot capable de s’attaquer aux pentes d’un terrain accidenté ou de couvrir plusieurs milliers de mètres carrés. Aussi, pour les pelouses jusqu’à 500 m2, le YUKA mini 2 500 constitue une alternative plus accessible.
Son principal atout repose sur son système de vision IA Tri-Cam, qui associe deux caméras monochromes à une caméra RVB. Cette configuration lui permet de cartographier son environnement, de repérer les limites de la pelouse et de reconnaître plus de 300 types d’objets. Là encore, aucun câble périphérique ni antenne RTK ne sont nécessaires pour installer le robot.
La cartographie automatique peut prendre en charge jusqu’à cinq zones consécutives. Un mode DropMow permet aussi de lancer une tonte ponctuelle sans enregistrer de carte, simplement en déposant le robot sur la surface à entretenir.
Plus abordable que les modèles de la gamme LUBA, le YUKA mini 2 500 passe à 599 € au lieu de 799 €, soit 200 € d’économie. Un pack avec mini-garage est également disponible à 649 €.
Les promotions Black Friday et Cyber Monday de Mammotion débutent le 10 novembre. De quoi anticiper les achats de fin d’année et préparer sereinement au passage la prochaine saison de tonte.

articles.title: Dell Technologies Delivers Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Dell Technologies Delivers Third Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results
Dell Technologies (NYSE: DELL) announces financial results for its fiscal 2027 third quarter and provides guidance for its fiscal 2027 fourth quarter and full year.
Third-Quarter Summary
- Record revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103% year-over-year
- Record diluted earnings per share (EPS) of $8.82, up 287% year-over-year, and record non-GAAP diluted EPS of $9.45, up 265%
- Record third-quarter cash flow from operations of $4.5 billion
- Full-year FY27 revenue guidance of $202.0 billion, up 78% year-over-year
- Full-year FY27 diluted EPS guidance of $28.24 and non-GAAP diluted EPS guidance of $29.68, up 225% and 188% year-over-year, respectively
Jeff Clarke, vice chairman and chief operating officer, Dell Technologies"We expect record full-year revenue of $202 billion, up 78%. We are now a different company, with Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) driving the vast majority of our profit and growth. We ended the quarter with a record $132.3 billion AI backlog after booking $60.2 billion of orders, each rigorously vetted for customer quality and access to capital, land and power. Customers turn that backlog into revenue sooner because we test the complete rack before it ships and stand it up within six hours of delivery, which shortens time-to-first-token. Demand continues to accelerate and broaden globally, with more than 7,500 customers deploying Dell AI Factories."
David Kennedy, chief financial officer, Dell Technologies"The team executed exceptionally well, driving record revenue of $54.9 billion, record EPS and a record $4.9 billion returned to shareholders. Operating expenses as a percentage of revenue continues to decline, while non-GAAP operating expenses fell to 7% of revenue, the lowest in our 42-year history. We've continued to run the company more efficiently as we've grown, and that is driving higher profitability, even as AI servers become a larger part of our business. We've generated record year-to-date cash flow from operations of $10.8 billion, and the Board approved a $25 billion increase to our repurchase authorization, reflecting confidence in long-term value creation."
Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG)
- Record revenue: $42.0 billion, up 198% year-over-year
- Record AI-Optimized Servers revenue: $22.0 billion, up 291% year-over-year
- Record Traditional Servers and Networking revenue: $15.0 billion, up 235% year-over-year
- Record third-quarter Storage revenue: $4.9 billion, up 24% year-over-year
- Record operating income: $7.1 billion, up 308% year-over-year
Client Solutions Group (CSG)
- Revenue: $12.9 billion, up 3% year-over-year
- Operating income: $704 million, down 6% year-over-year
Capital Return
Dell Technologies returned a record $4.9 billion to shareholders in the third quarter through share repurchases and dividends.
The Company's Board of Directors has also approved the repurchase of an additional $25.0 billion of shares of the Company's Class C common stock under the stock repurchase program previously approved by the Board of Directors.

articles.title: Más de 150 organizaciones piden a Amazon y eBay que dejen de vender juguetes con chatbots de IA
articles.text:
Una coalición de más de 155 organizaciones y especialistas en infancia pidió a Amazon y eBay que suspendan la venta de juguetes con chatbots de inteligencia artificial integrados, durante estas fiestas y hasta que pruebas independientes demuestren que son seguros para los niños.
La carta fue enviada a Andy Jassy, presidente de Amazon, y a Jamie Iannone, presidente de eBay. La encabeza Fairplay, una organización estadounidense sin fines de lucro que defiende a la infancia frente a la tecnología, y la firman, entre otros, Zero to Three, Set@16, Alliance 4 Children y el movimiento The Anxious Generation, del psicólogo Jonathan Haidt.
Los firmantes representan a todos los continentes excepto la Antártida. Entre los especialistas figuran la pediatra Jenny Radesky, la profesora de la Universidad de Chicago Dana Suskind y la exministra británica Andrea Leadsom.
Según NBC News, Amazon dijo que había retirado algunos de los juguetes con IA que esa cadena de noticias y un grupo de consumidores habían probado recientemente. Amazon y eBay no habían respondido públicamente al pedido en las fuentes consultadas.
Cuatro exigencias concretas
La coalición pide suspender todos los anuncios de juguetes con chatbots generativos dirigidos a menores de 16 años o que probablemente usen. También reclama que sigan fuera de venta hasta que un análisis independiente evalúe los daños psicológicos, de desarrollo y de privacidad, además de los físicos.
Otra exigencia es eliminar las ofertas que presentan al chatbot como amigo, compañero emocional o herramienta de “crecimiento emocional”, y corregir las que se contradicen sobre la edad. La cuarta es avisar a quienes ya compraron uno sobre los riesgos y ofrecerles reembolso.
Las organizaciones pidieron a ambas empresas que respondan antes de Navidad, para trasladar esa información al Congreso de Estados Unidos, al Parlamento británico y a los padres.
“Los mercados son responsables de la seguridad de lo que venden y ya retiran productos peligrosos”, sostiene la carta. Rachel Franz, directora del programa de infancia de Fairplay, dijo que las tiendas han retirado juguetes uno por uno cuando se los señala, pero que eso “no es suficiente”.
Qué encontraron en los anuncios
Fairplay informó que se hallaron más de 50 juguetes con IA a la venta en Amazon en Estados Unidos y casi 30 en Amazon en el Reino Unido a fines de octubre. Muchos títulos decían “para niños de 3 años o más”, mientras que la ficha del propio producto indicaba edades de 16 a 18 años.
Un conejo de peluche para mayores de 3 años se conectaba a chatbots generales como ChatGPT, cuyas condiciones de uso exigen tener al menos 13 años. Varios anuncios ofrecían clonar la voz de familiares o seguir el “crecimiento emocional” del niño, y la mayoría de los juguetes los vendían comerciantes externos poco conocidos.
La coalición cita casos en los que estos juguetes mantuvieron conversaciones sexuales con niños o indicaron dónde encontrar cuchillos y fósforos. Alliance 4 Children probó el conejo de peluche y, según The Guardian, el juguete sugirió que un niño podía dar su consentimiento para ser tocado con fines de placer.
La coalición advierte también que la inteligencia artificial de un juguete puede cambiarse a distancia, de modo que su comportamiento puede variar de un día para otro.
Presión regulatoria creciente
La carta recuerda que California prohibirá desde enero de 2027 los juguetes con chatbots de compañía para menores de 16 años, y que en el Congreso de Estados Unidos se presentó un proyecto para vetar los chatbots de IA en juguetes infantiles.
En el Reino Unido, parlamentarios pidieron a Amazon y eBay quitar estos productos y propusieron usar la Ley de Protección del Consumidor de 1987 para prohibirlos, según la agencia PA. El Gobierno británico dijo que investiga con urgencia los riesgos, y su Oficina de Seguridad y Estándares de Productos recibió aportes sobre la normativa de juguetes entre julio y octubre.
El plazo que fijó la coalición para que Amazon y eBay contesten vence en Navidad.

articles.title: The SSD crisis is being defeated with Black Friday 1TB and 2TB deals at less than $0.15 per GB — some PCIe 4.0 SSDs are now cheaper than when we reviewed them
articles.text:
The SSD crisis is being defeated with Black Friday 1TB and 2TB deals at less than $0.15 per GB — some PCIe 4.0 SSDs are now cheaper than when we reviewed them
When a discount is actually a discount.
The DRAM and NAND shortages have driven SSD prices through the roof, but we've still managed to track down some of the best Black Friday SSD deals around. There are several 1TB and 2TB NVMe SSDs on sale — by far the most popular capacities — for less than $0.15 per GB from brands like MSI, Adata, Biwin, and Kingston. Normally, we're using price per GB as our north star here to make sure you're getting the best value for the drive you pick up.
All of the drives we've rounded up here are PCIe 4.0 SSDs, and they range in performance. Short of one exception for the 1TB and 2TB capacities, these are DRAM-less SSDs. Naturally, SSDs with a DRAM cache are more expensive. There are good deals on high-end drives like the Samsung 9100 Pro 2TB at 49% off, but we're focused on value options here. If you need more capacity, the T-Force G50 Evo 4TB at $399 is the best deal we've found.
A couple of the drives here are cheaper than when we reviewed them, in some cases a few years ago before the SSD pricing crisis took hold. Things are starting to turn in a positive direction with some of these discounts, though we still have a long way to go before we reach early 2025 pricing.
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | 1TB (discount) | 2TB (discount) | 
| Biwin Black Opal NV7400 | $147.99 (-15%) | $245.99 (-18%) | 
| MSI Spatium M470 Pro | $149 (-17%) | $269.99 (-15%) | 
| Kingston NV3 | $139.99 (-35%) | $264.99 (-10%) | 
| Adata Legend 860 | $149.99 (-11%) | N/A | 
The Biwin Black Opal NV7400 is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD with maximum read speeds of up to 7,450 MB/s, and maximum write speeds of up to 6,500 MB/s.

The Biwin Black Opal NV7400 is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD with maximum read speeds of up to 7,450 MB/s, and maximum write speeds of up to 6,500 MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
The headline deal is on the Biwin Black Opal NV7400, in both 1TB and 2TB capacities. It's a DRAM-less SSD, but it still boasts sequential reads/writes of up to 7,400 MB/s and 6,500 MB/s, respectively, and random reads/writes of 1,000K IOPS and 900K IOPS. It also comes with a generous five-year warranty and an endurance rating of 1PBW per TB of capacity.
We found that the drive was a solid all-around performer in our Biwin Black Opal NV7400 review. Prices on SSDs have continued to rise since we reviewed the NV7400 in January, but with current sales, the price on both the 1TB and 2TB versions of the NV7400 is still less than when we reviewed the drive.
If you're looking for the cheapest 1TB NVMe SSD on Black Friday, the Kingston NV3 has the NV7400 beat out by $8. Both the 1TB and 2TB capacities are on sale, though the 1TB discount is the sweetheart deal right now. It too is a DRAM-less drive, and it comes with lower-rated specs than the NV7400 at 5,000 MB/s and 3,000 MB/s sequential reads and writes, and an endurance rating of 320 TBW for the 1TB capacity.
The Kingston NV3 is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD that sports sequential read speeds of up to 6,000 MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 4,000 MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
Kingston's budget drives like the NV3 use somewhat of a grab bag approach to components, swapping out the controller and flash for whatever's available at the time. Compared to prior generations, the NV3 has stronger constraints to keep performance relatively comparable across different internal components. However, there can still be differences, as you can read about in our Kingston NV3 review.
The MSI Spatium M470 Pro is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD that supports sequential read speeds of up to 6,000 MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 5,000 MB/s. 
$50 off w/ promo code BFF586

If you're looking for a drive that has a DRAM cache, you can save $50 on the 2TB MSI Spatium M470 Pro. The drive has 1GB of DDR4 per TB, 5,000 MB/s and 4,400 MB/s sequential read and write speeds, and 600,000 IOPS for random read/write performance. It also comes with a large 3,300 TBW endurance rating for the 2TB capacity, along with a five-year warranty.
The 2TB is actually $30 less than the list price when we reviewed it more than four years ago; check out our full MSI Spatium M470 review. Granted, PCIe 4.0 drives were more expensive four years ago than they were two years ago, but it's still a positive pricing move given how expensive SSDs have become.
The Adata Legend 860 is a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD with 6,000 MB/s and 5,000 MB/s sequential read/write performance and a three-year warranty.

Rounding out the deals is the Adata Legend 860 1TB, which is an older PCIe 4.0 rated for 6,000 MB/s and 5,000 MB/s sequential read/write performance. It squarely clocks in at $0.15 per GB, and it's just $10 more expensive than the NV3 for the same capacity.
It's a DRAM-less drive, instead leveraging SLC caching and HMB, but it comes with a five-year warranty and a respectable 640 TBW endurance rating for the 1TB capacity.

articles.title: NAND prices could finally be set to fall, in the first bit of good news for component fans for some time — but DRAM is refusing to budge so far
articles.text:
NAND prices could finally be set to fall, in the first bit of good news for component fans for some time — but DRAM is refusing to budge so far
Finally some good news for SSD shoppers
- NAND spot prices have fallen about 20% since mid-to-late October 2026, with 512Gb wafers down 32% on the quarter to $14.30
- BofA sees PC and phone NAND contract prices falling 5% to 10% in Q1 2027; TrendForce sees overall NAND down 0% to 5%
- Retail SSD relief will lag by months, and finished devices could still get pricier as cheap memory stockpiles run out
After more than a year in which practically every memory headline has pointed upward, the flash market has finally blinked.
New reports have claimed NAND spot prices have slid roughly 20% in a matter of weeks as Chinese traders rush to clear inventory, with analysts now penciling in contract price cuts for early 2027.
Not long ago, the conversation was about shortages lasting several more years, but there is a catch attached to the good news: NAND is turning, but DRAM, which is also a key component for SSDs, is only wobbling at best for now
Flash: The first to crack?
The sharpest numbers come from a Bank of America note reported by the Seoul Economic Daily which puts the spot price of a 512Gb NAND wafer at $14.30, down 12% in a week and 32% in the previous quarter, while 1Tb parts have dropped 19% to $24.90.
The bank says spot NAND has corrected by around 20% since mid-to-late October 2026, and it now expects general-purpose NAND, the kind found in consumer SSDs, laptops and phones, to fall a further 5% to 10% on contract in the first quarter of 2027.
TrendForce has arrived at much the same place, forecasting overall NAND contract prices to slip 0% to 5% quarter over quarter in Q1 2027, with every product category entering a downward cycle from Q2 and "quarterly price drops potentially widening as the year progresses." It has also cut its forecast for this quarter's contract increase to 8% to 13%, down from the 15% to 20% it projected at the end of September. Contract prices, in other words, are still rising today. The decline is a 2027 story.
Supply and demand are moving against sellers at the same time: TrendForce expects NAND bit supply to grow 25% to 30% in 2027, backed by industry capital spending of $29.9 billion, up 26.7%, as QLC adoption and higher layer counts squeeze more bits out of every wafer.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
On the demand side, Chinese cloud providers have cut their 2027 enterprise SSD orders by more than US hyperscalers have added, citing GPU shortages, elevated inventory, and fierce competition on AI token pricing.
Consumers have played their part too, mostly by not buying: PC sales have been falling off a cliff in 2026, and phone and laptop makers trying to contain costs have been trimming storage specs, which shrinks NAND demand even when unit sales hold up.
One could say that the market structure explains why NAND was the first to crack: NAND has six major suppliers, against the three that control most of the DRAM market, and roughly 20% to 30% of global NAND capacity sits on older lines that are poorly suited to enterprise products and keep churning out commodity flash regardless.
One industry official told the Seoul Economic Daily that the weakness "is being led by some commodity NAND used in smartphones and PCs," while demand for enterprise NAND in AI data centers "remains strong."
The move might not be properly visible in retail channels yet, and with good reason: Spot prices are the fast-moving fringe of the market, and they cover only a small slice of NAND volume. Most flash is sold on contract, and contract prices trail spot by weeks or months, and retail trails further still, especially while distributors work through stock bought near the peak.
No DRAM relief yet
If NAND is the good news, DRAM is the reason to keep the celebrations short. In TrendForce's week to November 17 2026, the mainstream DDR4 chip slipped 1.43% to $44.25 on the spot market, while branded DDR5 was "mostly stable." Even that small dip flatters the picture: DDR4 spot had been trading above suppliers' official quotes earlier in the month, so part of the drift is spot pricing settling back toward contract levels rather than a market in retreat.
On contract, DRAM is still climbing. Bank of America has kept its forecast of an 8% rise in Q4 2026 and another 5% in Q1 2027. TrendForce's latest DRAM bulletin says contract prices will keep rising, albeit with gains that shrink each quarter, while mobile DRAM negotiations have stalled as brands sit on their hands. Slower increases are the closest thing to relief on offer.
The reason, once again, is AI: "HBM consumes three to four times more wafer resources than standard commodity DRAM," TrendForce researcher Ellie Wang said at the firm's Seoul roadshow on November 18. "That is another reason we do not expect DRAM prices to turn lower in 2027," Wang said, adding that new capacity will only begin entering the market from late 2027, with Samsung's Pyeongtaek P5 and SK hynix's Yongin cluster coming online between 2028 and 2030.
The rest of the industry is still talking like it's a seller's market. Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra recently said that "75% of our 2027 [supply] is sold out," SK hynix has warned that the shortage could persist through 2030, and Intel's chief has reportedly said we have another two to three years of this. Apple CEO John Ternus, meanwhile, described current memory pricing as "unprecedented". DRAM revenue rose 369% year over year in Q3, while bit shipments rose only around 4% in the quarter, suggesting the market is pricing scarcity, not volume.
For NAND, however, TrendForce lists several factors that could change the picture: how quickly Chinese cloud providers burn through their inventory, any shift in restrictions on overseas GPU procurement, and whether device makers keep shipping lower-storage specs into 2028. It also flags US policy after the midterm elections, particularly for AI data center projects planned for 2028 that are still in planning or permitting, since approvals there would drive advance buying in the second half of 2027.
Sellers have levers of their own. Some suppliers may slow expansion in response to weak consumer demand, according to TrendForce, and any cut to consumer flash wafer starts, or a wave of restocking by phone makers keen to buy low, could turn this dip into a brief one. Higher-end storage often incorporates DRAM, especially in enterprise-grade products, and it continues to command an increasing share of the total cost of storage currently being procured by hyperscalers.
Despite this, this is, without much doubt, the most encouraging memory and storage news in a long while, and it comes from more than one direction. A bank, a research firm, and the spot market itself all point the same way for NAND. If you are planning a storage upgrade and can afford to wait, patience into 2027 looks more likely to be rewarded than punished.
But the memory crisis has split in two rather than ended. Enterprise SSD pricing is still being propped up by US AI demand, and consumer flash is getting cheaper largely because Chinese cloud firms and shoppers have stopped buying, not because supply has caught up with the AI boom. DRAM has no equivalent pressure valve while HBM keeps swallowing wafers, so the best RAM buyers can hope for in 2027 is smaller increases. Anyone who cannot wait is still better off hunting for discounts, and Black Friday remains your best shot at that.
