articles.title: Rajiv Ramaswami to step down as Nutanix begins hunt for its next CEO
articles.text:
Rajiv Ramaswami to step down as Nutanix begins hunt for its next CEO
Rajiv Ramaswami is stepping down from his role as chief executive of Nutanix Inc., six years after he joined the hyperconverged cloud infrastructure company from its rival VMware Inc.
In a letter to company employees, Ramaswami (pictured) said he’s going to continue in the role for the time being while he works with Nutanix’s board of directors to identify a successor and assist with the transition. “After that, I will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the company for a period of time,” he said in the letter.
Ramaswami, who is 60 years old, did not give any reason for his coming departure, but the letter seems to indicate that he’s not ready to retire just yet.
“Our next CEO will inherit a strong platform, a loyal customer base and, most importantly, an exceptional team,” Ramaswami wrote. “Until then, my focus remains on leading this company and nothing about our day-to-day priorities changes. I am committed to helping our next leader succeed, and my ask of you, as always, is to continue to focus on executing as we go through this leadership transition.”
Ramaswami added that Nutanix has hired an executive search firm to lead the hunt for his successor. The news came as the company delivered its first-quarter earnings report, posting modest year-over-year gains in profit and revenue.
The company reported adjusted earnings of 73 cents per share, beating Wall Street’s target of 61 cents per share by a strong margin. Revenue for the period came to $772.4 million, up 15% from a year earlier and above the Street’s forecast of $762.7 million.
Nutanix’s outlook for the current quarter is strong, with the company guiding for sales of between $820 million and $830 million, compared with the Street’s consensus estimate of $820.4 million. However, the full-year picture is a little less rosy, with Nutanix guiding for annual sales of $3.18 billion to $3.23 billion. The midpoint of that range trails the Street’s forecast of $3.22 billion in fiscal 2027 revenue.
Investors did not take the news very well. The cautious full-year guidance compared with the uncertainty over leadership prompted many to sell, and Nutanix’s stock was down 8% after-hours, having already fallen more than 5% during the regular trading session, on a down day for many tech stocks.
Virginia Gambale, of the board at Nutanix, hailed the “tremendous impact” Ramaswami had on the company during his six-year tenure. “Rajiv led the company’s transformation to subscription software, built a loyal and expanding global enterprise base and established a technology portfolio that we believe positions us well for the AI era,” she said. “We’re focused on selecting an exceptional leader who can build on that foundation.”
A new chapter begins
In a conference call with analysts, Ramaswami said he believes the company is embarking on the third major chapter in its history. The first chapter, before his arrival, saw the company establish itself as the leader of the hyperconverged infrastructure industry. Chapter two began when he took over, and saw Nutanix expand from those roots to become a platform company, he said.
“[We have] transformed the company to be profitable while growing and expanding the product portfolio quite significantly, from HCI to a platform that works across clouds, supports external storage and has cloud-native capabilities and now moving into the future with AI capabilities,” Ramaswami said. “Chapter two is well-established at this point and there’s a lot of opportunity in terms of driving growth. I feel like we are in a very good place.”
According to Ramaswami, Nutanix now stands at an inflection point as it looks to cash in on the new era of artificial intelligence. “I’ve been talking to the board for a bit about this, as well as in terms of our strategic direction and the timing for succession, and so we came to the conclusion together that this is perhaps the right time,” he told analysts. “[We wanted] to announce it ahead of time as we look for the appropriate next leader.”
Ramaswami’s departure from the company should at least be a lot smoother than his arrival. Nutanix announced it had appointed Ramaswami as its CEO in late 2020, just two days after he quit his role as chief operating officer of its biggest rival, VMware.
VMware was indignant about the manner of his departure, and responded with a lawsuit that accused Ramaswami of breaching his legal and contractual duties to the company by “secretly meeting” with Nutanix’s board to discuss taking over, while continuing to play a leading role in shaping its product and business strategy. The lawsuit was ultimately settled out of court about a year later.
In April, Ramaswami appeared on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s mobile livestreaming studio, where he talked about how Nutanix is shifting away from HCI to focus on more of a “disaggregated infrastructure” strategy to support demand for autonomous AI agents:

articles.title: Pour le Black Friday 2026, cet aspirateur robot Xiaomi noté 5/5 passe sous les 800 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'aspirateur robot Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max "5 étoiles" à 799,99 €
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max passe à 799,99 € chez Amazon et Xiaomi, soit une baisse d'environ 4 % et 23,52 € d'économie. Efficace pour laver les sols et naviguer sans heurter les obstacles, cet aspirateur robot affiche actuellement la note de 5/5 dans nos tests.
Avec le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max, la marque propose un aspirateur robot haut de gamme pensé pour simplifier le nettoyage complet des sols. L'appareil associe une navigation précise, un système de lavage par rouleau nettoyé à 85 °C et une station d'entretien tout-en-un. Ce modèle avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur le banc de test.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max descend à 799,99 € chez Amazon et Xiaomi, soit environ 4 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours fixé à 823,51 €. Cette baisse de prix qui permet d'économiser 23,52 €.
Lavage à l'eau chaude et aspiration silencieuse au banc d'essai
Pour assurer l'entretien des sols durs, le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max utilise un système de lavage par rouleau qui élimine efficacement la plupart des taches ménagères. Sa station de charge complète gère la maintenance de façon autonome en lavant le rouleau avec une eau chauffée à 85 °C. L'appareil nettoie ainsi les surfaces sans que l'utilisateur ait besoin de nettoyer la serpillière à la main après chaque cycle, comme détaillé dans notre test complet.
Le robot limite également les nuisances dans la pièce de vie. Lors de nos mesures, le niveau sonore s'est établi à seulement 48.5 dB(A) en mode Normal, ce qui permet de le laisser travailler sans gêner une conversation. Même en poussant la puissance au maximum, le niveau sonore en mode Turbo atteint 58 dB(A), maintenant un fonctionnement discret pendant l'aspiration.
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max
Points forts
- Excellente aspiration sur sols durs.
- Navigation précise et gestion efficace des obstacles.
- Lavage convaincant sur la plupart des taches.
- Station complète et fonctionnement silencieux.
Points faibles
- Aspiration limitée sur moquette épaisse.
- Nettoyage des angles perfectible.
- Détection des tapis peu alerte.
- App parfois confuse.
Une navigation précise malgré quelques limites sur les tapis épais
Le système de guidage assure des déplacements rigoureux dans les différentes pièces du logement. Le robot contourne proprement les meubles et les objets laissés au sol sans heurter les plinthes. Il affiche à ce jour la note maximale de 5/5 au sein de notre comparatif grâce à sa grande régularité sur les surfaces lisses.
L'aspiration montre en revanche ses limites sur les moquettes très épaisses, où la détection automatique du revêtement manque parfois de réactivité. Les angles réclament aussi un passage manuel d'appoint, mais ces détails ne pénalisent pas les foyers principalement recouverts de parquet ou de carrelage.
Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete : l'autre option face au Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max
Le Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete est actuellement vendu à 798,99 €, soit un tarif inférieur de 1,00 € par rapport au Robot Vacuum 6 Max. Le modèle de Roborock partage la même note de 5/5 à ce jour et utilise lui aussi un rouleau de lavage avec une station automatisée pour gérer l'entretien quotidien sans intervention manuelle.
Le Saros 20 Flow Complete prend l'avantage sur les tapis grâce à une aspiration plus efficace sur les fibres épaisses, mais il peine davantage sur les taches très incrustées. Le Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete conviendra mieux aux logements équipés de nombreuses moquettes, tandis que le Xiaomi Robot Vacuum 6 Max reste supérieur pour laver les sols durs tachés grâce à son rouleau nettoyé à 85 °C.
Roborock Saros 20 Flow Complete
Points forts
- Navigation impeccable et évitement d'obstacles fiable.
- Aspiration très efficace sur carrelage, parquet et tapis épais.
- Station d'accueil automatisée et complète.
- Franchissement de seuils.
- Fonctionnement silencieux.
- App simple et riche en options.
Points faibles
- Aspiration insuffisante dans les fentes de parquet.
- Difficultés sur les taches incrustées.
- Câbles fins parfois mal détectés.
- Blocage systématique devant les rideaux.
- Entretien fréquent pour le filtre HEPA et le plateau de lavage de la station.

articles.title: Ladybird é um navegador feito do zero para desafiar o Chrome
articles.text:
Ladybird é um navegador feito do zero para desafiar o Chrome
Ao contrário da maioria dos navegadores atuais, o Ladybird não é baseado no Chromium e conta com um motor próprio.
Parece até lei: todo novo projeto de navegador que surgiu nos últimos anos tem como base o Chromium e, por conta disso, renderiza páginas por meio do motor Blink. Mas o Ladybird é diferente. Esse é o nome de um browser que está sendo desenvolvido do zero e que, portanto, tem um motor próprio.
Entenda, como motor, o mecanismo que permite ao navegador interpretar o código de uma página web e, então, apresentar um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Mas é extremamente difícil desenvolver um motor, ainda mais com uma web tão cheia de recursos como a que temos hoje. Isso explica, pelo menos em parte, o fato de, além do próprio Google Chrome, browsers como Edge, Opera, Vivaldi e Brave seguirem a base do projeto Chromium, com motor Blink.
O Firefox é uma exceção, pois conta com um motor próprio, o Gecko — exceto o Firefox para iOS, por “culpa” da Apple. Falando em Apple, o Safari também é uma exceção, pois tem o motor WebKit como base. O Ladybird chega para ser uma quarta opção nesse cenário.
O Ladybird surge como um projeto independente, sob liderança de Andreas Kling. O desenvolvedor é mais conhecido por ter criado o sistema operacional aberto SerenityOS, projeto que ele deixou de liderar em 2024 justamente para se dedicar ao navegador.
Inicialmente, o Ladybird era desenvolvido em linguagem C++, mas os desenvolvedores decidiram migrar para Rust com auxílio da inteligência artificial. Faz sentido se levarmos em conta que o Rust é uma linguagem de programação mais moderna e segura. A contrapartida é que alguma falha ou limitação ainda pode ser notada como efeito dessa migração.
Seja como for, o Ladybird já liberou a sua primeira versão. É uma versão alpha, ou seja, em fase inicial de desenvolvimento, mas que não deixa de representar um avanço. Essa versão só está disponível para macOS (com chip Apple Silicon) e Linux. O novo browser chegará ao Windows, mas em uma fase posterior.
Funciona? Sim. O Ladybird tem visual sóbrio e oferece múltiplas abas, favoritos, navegação privada (anônima), entre outros recursos básicos. Você também pode escolher entre abas na horizontal ou na vertical, ativar ou não o bloqueador de anúncios e até definir o mecanismo de busca padrão.
Como todo projeto em fase inicial, pode haver falhas, principalmente na renderização de páginas. Mas o saldo tende a ser positivo: fazendo um teste com alguns sites, incluindo o Tecnoblog, notei que tudo estava em seu lugar.
Foi um teste rápido, mas o suficiente para eu considerar o projeto promissor. Que fique claro, porém: ainda não é recomendado usar o Ladybird como um navegador para a rotina diária.
Você pode baixar o Ladybird para Linux ou macOS aqui. É gratuito e de código aberto.

articles.title: El móvil bueno, bonito y por menos de 300 euros durante el Black Friday. Un Nothing que destaca hasta por su cámara principal
articles.text:
El precio de los móviles se ha disparado por la crisis de la memoria RAM, pero afortunadamente podemos encontrara algunos smartphones que se siguen manteniendo con precios comedidos, sobre todo ahora durante el Black Friday. Si queremos un móvil que no sobrepase los 300 euros, el Nothing Phone (4b) es una de las mejores opciones de compra ahora que ha bajado hasta los 299 euros.
Nothing Phone (4b) (8 GB, 128 GB)
Mantiene el particular diseño de los móviles Nothing
El Nothing Phone (4b) es un móvil que, pese a ser considerado como económico dentro de la marca, mantiene el particular diseño que hemos visto en otros modelos más caros. De hecho, hasta incorpora el Glyph Bar, aunque en esta ocasión se sitúa a la derecha de las cámaras y, pese a que no es tan espectacular como en otros modelos de Nothing, la utilidad se mantiene para cuando recibimos notificaciones o para avisos de la batería, entre otros.
Respecto a su tamaño, hablamos de un móvil que incorpora una pantalla AMOLED con diagonal de 6,77 pulgadas y que alcanza una tasa de refresco de hasta 120 Hz. articles.title: Bambu Lab shows off H3C tool changer, first laser at Formnext 2026 — Prusa Research, Snapmaker, Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic, and Flashforge also on display
articles.text:
Bambu Lab shows off H3C tool changer, first laser at Formnext 2026 — Prusa Research, Snapmaker, Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic, and Flashforge also on display
The latest in 3D printing tech comes to Frankfurt.
Once a year, all the world’s 3D printing manufacturers gather for Formnext in Frankfurt, Germany, to showcase new technologies, software, and ideas. This year’s show was more compact, with three halls instead of four, but consumer 3D printers had a larger presence. Spread across two halls, we found Bambu Lab, Prusa Research, Snapmaker, Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic, and Flashforge, plus a few newbies like Axiloop.
Startup SnowX was a popular booth, presenting the first consumer-grade desktop metal 3D printer coming soon to Kickstarter.
I counted ten tool-changing 3D printers on the show floor, five of which I’ve already reviewed. Elegoo surprised us all by launching its Centauri X Ultra four-color tool changer at the show, while Axiloop’s MC 8 arrived on my front porch that morning.
Only Anycubic is standing pat with a single-nozzle multicolor machine. Instead, it presented its new partnership with Thingiverse.
Full-color UV printers were on display as well, with Flashforge showing off its CJ270, which was teased last year.
Editor’s Note: Snapmaker provided travel accommodations for this trip. Coverage remains editorially independent.
Bambu Lab H3C: Nine tool heads
Bambu Lab showed off its latest printers, the H3C, a tool changer (starting at $2,499) with nine lightweight tools we reviewed earlier in the month, and its first laser, the R1, reviewed in September, which retails at $2,499.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
More interesting is the launch of “Bambu Circle,” a pilot program that will start in the Netherlands and slowly expand across Europe. The goal is a network of local hubs to assist entrepreneurs with their 3D printing side hustle. Bambu Circle would enlist repair specialists and community ambassadors to provide a helping hand and an in-person retail shop with space for meetups. ,
At the moment, there is no plan to launch a similar program in the United States; however, we have many retailers here who offer official warranty support, parts, and tons of filament. A map on the Bambu Lab lists 31 US resellers, though that number is a bit skewed since there are also 31 MicroCenters in the US.
Prusa Research: Print Anywhere without the Cloud
Prusa Research previewed the Rugged, a CORE One L+ adapted for printing in the harshest environments. The printer has a sealed case that keeps out both humidity and dust while providing extra protection during transport for machines used in the field. The CORE One L+ tucked inside is equipped with a high-temperature, hardened steel nozzle for printing advanced engineering filaments. It also comes with Prusa’s Zero-Trace system, which is an air-gapped machine with no flash drive storage, no USB slot, no Wi-Fi, and no camera. They can only accept files from your own cryptographically paired Prusa Connect server. These extremely secure, extremely tough machines are meant for classified and proprietary work environments.
However, you don’t need to have a security clearance to jump on board Prusa Connect Local, a free-to-use version of Prusa Connect for anyone who wishes to keep their 3D printers off the internet. The server can run on Linux, Windows, Mac, or a Raspberry Pi, and can handle a print farm of two to 400. It’s currently set up for any Prusa Printer, but it is open source, so you are free to tinker around with it and add your own extensions.
Snapmaker: Full Spectrum
Snapmaker showed off what you can do with its four-color U1 tool changer. Ratdoux, the developer behind Full Spectrum, was on hand to chat with us. He devised a system of color-blending filaments that take thin layers of cyan, yellow, and magenta mixed with either gray or white, which can create nearly any other color. He said it was inspired by a conversation on Reddit where users were mixing colors in Blender, and he came up with a simpler way to do it in the slicer. Snapmaker immediately hired him to lead a development team for its fork of OrcaSlicer.
Amazingly, Full Spectrum went from an experimental slicer hack to a must-have for every tool changer in the space of nine months. Snapmaker’s Full Spectrum is tailored for the U1 on open-source OrcaSlicer, while Bambu Lab installed a “Color Mixing” tool in Bambu Studio and Prusa Research developed their own “ColorMix” technology based on hex codes.
Full Spectrum and similar tools can be used on any multimaterial 3D printer. However, because it looks best with super thin layers, tool changers are more efficient and less wasteful.
Snapmaker has since introduced a Full Spectrum filament bundle optimized for four-color machines: a CMYW for lighter, bright colors and a CMYG (gray edition) for darker shades. Ratdoux said the secret is in the filament’s light Transmission Distance (TD), which measures how translucent the material is. Colors that allow more light to pass through them create a better illusion of blending. The parrot and fox pictured above were printed using CMYG and a .08mm layer height. There was no orange, purple, green or black filament used in those prints.
Axiloop MC8 Pro: Eight Color Kickstarter
We also found Axiloop, an eight-color tool changer that’s already raised over $700,000 on Kickstarter. The fully enclosed CoreXY machine has a 300x300mm build plate, 4-second tool swaps, and claims to have “near-zero” wipe-free tool changes. Its price for the MC8 Pro is $1,499 for early backers, while the open frame MC8 is $1,099.
Our review unit arrived while I was at Formnext, so I’m excited to put it to the test soon.
Peopoly: Its a Big Boi
Peopoly’s Giga 800 is a large-scale pellet feeder that’s a bit north of our normal prosumer range at $15,000, but I felt it was worth mentioning because it's from our friends at Siraya Tech, who make superior filaments and resin. I noticed quite a few YouTubers happily climb into the machine to show how big it truly is.
The machine has an extrusion output of three kilos an HOUR, which would be equivalent to three spools of normal filament, and can use a 3mm nozzle for chonky prints. We’ve reviewed a similar-sized open-frame “giga” machine before, so I know that being hampered by a normal .4mm nozzle is not something you want with a print volume this large. The enclosed machine is capable of running everything from PLA and TPU to PET-CF and PPA-GF.
Creality: Lasers, Scanners and a Kid Printer
Creality had quite a few machines out, but the most interesting were the Creality Falcon T1 UV Laser we reviewed this summer and the new Falcon A1C portable laser we’ll be reviewing soon. The T1 is able to do inner engraving in glass in just a few minutes, and the team was happy to show me the workflow after I supplied them with a photo. They took my selfie, ran it through Creality’s AI to create a 3D bust, then zapped it into a 2 x 3 inch chunk of glass. It was an impressive demo.
They also showed off several handheld scanners, which Creality feels will enable makers to create more practical prints without needing a ton of CAD skills. My favorite is the Creality Pika we reviewed in October.
I’m also particularly intrigued by the mBox kid printer, with a small 153x153mm build plate but lots of safety features to make it child-friendly. The printer is priced at $329, which isn’t bad for a full-feature printer. However, good luck finding one to buy: this printer is only available on the TikTok Shop in the US until December 10.
Another disappointment was the Creality M1 filament maker with its companion R1 shredder. The unit was on display, but not running, which makes me believe they haven’t quite figured out how to make the dream of home filament making a reality.
Elegoo Centauri X Ultra: Four color tool changer
Elegoo surprised us all with the Centauri X Ultra, a four-color tool changer variation of the wildly successful Centauri Carbon. The Centauri X Ultra is scheduled to release early in 2027. It has a 256x256mm bed, making it the same size as its siblings. The machine is completely enclosed and cleverly contains the side-mounted spools in a Tupperware-like sealed box. The machine has filament drying and a nozzle that can hit 350C, making it a good candidate for high-temperature filaments. It also claims to have 5-second color swaps without waste, but we’ll test that as soon as we get our hands on one.
BIQU: Even more Panda-Verse
BIQU once again impressed us with their line of Panda-Verse accessories for your Bambu Lab machine. The Panda Treat ($159.99), which applies edible ink to cookies, cakes, and cups of frothy coffee, is out and ready for review. The BIQU x FOXLT Infinity Bed ($259) adds a tiny conveyor bed to your P1S or P2S printer for endless printing. But the most ambitious this year is the BIQU Vault, starting at $499. This is a filament storage system like no other, with an RFID tag tracking system that helps you catalog your filament and tell you where it is in your workshop.
FlashForge: CJ270 UV Printing
FlashForge revealed its CJ270 full-color 3D printer, priced at $ 3,999 and now shipping. It is listed as a MultiJet Printer, which uses UV ink to build up models, with a build size of 180 x 120 x 100 mm. Unlike other UV printers, the CJ270 has seven printheads (one for each ink channel), so if one gets clogged, you don’t need to replace the entire printhead. It uses CMYK ink, plus white, clear, and a water-washable support material. The sample models shown were impressive, with lots of detail and strong color.
Anycubic x Thingiverse
Anycubic didn’t have any new machines to show off, but they did have a huge announcement to make: they are collaborating with Thingiverse to bring millions of models into Anycubic’s file-sharing library, MakerOnline. Select designs will be converted into multicolor models for one-click printing from Anycubic’s mobile app.
The company is also looking into adding an AI tool dubbed AnyLab to its website to help users create their own designs.
Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Vous avez jusqu’au 28 novembre pour tester gratuitement la conduite autonome de Xpeng dans les rues de Paris
articles.text:
Comme nombre de personnes, la conduite autonome doit certainement vous intriguer. Comment fonctionne un tel dispositif ? Est-ce uniquement du marketing ? De la science-fiction seulement opérante sur circuit fermé ? Ou bien une toute nouvelle façon d’aborder l’automobile ? Voilà autant de questions qui pourraient enfin trouver leurs réponses grâce à Xpeng, qui organise des sessions d’essais auxquelles vous pouvez prendre part.
Il suffit pour cela de réserver un créneau, puis de se rendre à la boutique Xpeng de Paris située au 10 Boulevard Gouvion-Saint-Cyr. Jusqu’à trois personnes pourront ainsi expérimenter le système Next Generation Pilot (NGP) de la marque, concurrençant frontalement le FSD de Tesla. Cependant, il ne faudra pas tarder, l’opération prenant fin le 28 novembre. Ce serait tout de même dommage de passer à côté.
30 minutes dans les rues de Paris pour découvrir la conduite autonome
Surtout que c’est la première fois que la marque organise ce genre d’événement hors de Chine. He Xiaopeng, le PDG d’Xpeng, tient d’ailleurs à le souligner : « nous lançons des essais publics du NGP ici à Paris. Nous devenons ainsi la première marque chinoise à le faire en Europe. Nous sommes ici en Europe, pour l’Europe, avec l’Europe ». De quoi avoir un avant-goût du futur pendant 30 minutes de roulage ?
Partiellement, car un représentant de la marque sera toujours assis derrière le volant, au cas où… Le constructeur a pourtant mis le paquet, en sortant de son coffre à jouets le modèle ayant le plus gros potentiel de ventes en Europe, le SUV L03. Présenté en version haut de gamme Performance Ultra, l’engin est équipé en série de deux puces Turing d’une puissance de calcul de 750 TOPS. C’est ce duo qui permet la conduite entièrement autonome.
Caméras, capteurs et puces Turing : la recette du SUV L03
Et contrairement à Tesla, Xpeng s’appuie non seulement sur des caméras, mais également sur une flopée de capteurs pour assurer une bonne perception de l’environnement. Il est vrai que BYD avait déjà proposé une chose similaire en marge du Mondial de Paris. Mais l’expérience était uniquement réservée à la presse. Et il valait mieux, vu ce que nous avons constaté de nos propres yeux.
Sortie abrupte d’un giratoire, non-respect d’un passage piéton, manque d’anticipation sur les obstacles… Le système maison God’s Eye ne porte pas encore bien son nom ! Côté Xpeng, cela devrait donc mieux se passer, même si l’on suppose que la marque a soigneusement sélectionné son itinéraire pour ne pas trop mettre son NGP en difficulté. Précisons que l’utilisation du système n’est pas encore autorisée pour les clients. Elle le sera potentiellement plus tard.

articles.title: Black Friday : le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra bradé à -56% aspire à 16 000 Pa et sèche sa brosse en 30 minutes
articles.text:
Le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra est un aspirateur laveur sans fil qui aspire et lave en un seul passage. Il se démarque par sa station qui lave sa brosse à l'eau chaude, puis la sèche, et son prix qui passe de 299 euros à 132,50 euros pour le Black Friday Amazon.
Pour faire votre ménage chez vous, sans trop vous fatiguer, voici le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra. C'est un modèle sans fil conçu pour aspirer et laver les sols en un passage. Avec sa puissance d'aspiration de 16 000 Pa, sa brosse lavée à 60°C et son séchage à l'air chaud en 30 minutes fait qu'il s'adresse aux foyers qui cherchent à simplifier l'entretien au quotidien. Et avec le prix qui chute de 166,50 euros sur Amazon pendant le Black Friday, il devient particulièrement intéressant.
Voici le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra à 132,50 € au lieu de 299 € sur Amazon pour le Black Friday
Pourquoi choisir le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra ?
- Sa puissance d'aspiration de 16 000 Pa qui récupère les saletés solides et liquides en même temps que le lavage.
- L'entretien automatisé à l'eau chaude avec le nettoyage de la brosse à 60°C et et le séchage en 30 minutes.
- La brosse qui limite les oublis nettoie des deux côtés, au plus près des plinthes, et le racleur à dents de peigne aide à enlever les cheveux et les poils emmêlés.
Un aspirateur laveur qui simplifie l'entretien des sols au quotidien
Avec ses trois modes Auto, Ultra et Aspiration, le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra est aussi bon sur le nettoyage courant que sur les tâches les plus tenaces, même sur l'aspiration des liquides. Son capteur ajuste automatiquement la puissance en fonction de la saleté détectée, et l'écran LED avec les annonces vocales permettent de suivre l'état de l'appareil. Ses réservoirs de 900 ml pour l'eau propre et de 700 ml pour l'eau sale, avec une autonomie de 35 minutes, lui permettent de couvrir jusqu'à 200m² (dans les conditions de test du fabricant). C'est donc un aspirateur laveur pour vous si vous entretenez de base vos sols assez régulièrement. Parce qu'il est là pour un entretien quotidien sur un sol un minimum propre, quand même.
Quelles sont les limites du Dreame H12 Pro face à la concurrence ?
Face aux modèles de Tineco ou de Bissell, le H12 Pro Ultra mise sur son entretien automatisé à l'eau chaude, mais il reste spécialisé dans les sols durs. Il ne remplace pas un aspirateur classique pour les tapis et les moquettes, ni un appareil capable d'aspirer à sec. Son autonomie de 35 minutes peut se révéler un peu trop juste dans les très grandes surfaces, et le séchage à l'air chaud est assez bruyant, donc peu adapté à une utilisation tardive.
✅ Les points forts
- Son aspiration de 16 000 Pa pour les solides et les liquides
- Le lavage automatique de la brosse à l'eau chaude jusqu'à 60°C
- Le séchage à l'air chaud annoncé en 30 minutes
- La brosse qui nettoie au plus près des plinthes
- La détection automatique du niveau de saleté et l'ajustement de l'aspiration
- Le réservoir d'eau propre de 900 ml et le réservoir d'eau sale de 700 ml
❌ Les limites
- Son autonomie limitée à 35 minutes en mode Auto selon le fabricant
- Le temps de recharge d'environ 4h
- Le séchage de la brosse assez bruyant
- La position de stationnement peu intuitive
- Pas adapté au nettoyage des tapis et des moquettes
- L'utilisation de solutions nettoyantes Dreame uniquement
Jusqu'au 30 novembre 2026 le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra passe à 132,50 € sur Amazon pendant le Black Friday
Si vous cherchez à entretenir facilement vos sols durs, le Dreame H12 Pro Ultra, surtout à 132,50 euros, est une option intéressante. Son aspiration de 16 000 Pa, sa brosse qui nettoie des deux côtés et sa station qui assure le lavage à 60°C avec le séchage en 30 minutes forment un ensemble bien équilibré. Ne plus avoir à nettoyer manuellement la brosse après chaque passage est un vrai avantage.
Ses 35 minutes d'autonomie ne conviendront pas forcément aux très grandes maisons, et il ne peut pas remplacer un aspirateur classique pour les tapis, les moquettes ou le nettoyage à sec. Si votre logement est principalement composé de carrelage ou de parquet compatible, cette promotion mérite votre attention.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, cette caméra Eufy notée 5/5 passe sous les 250 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La caméra de surveillance Eufy eufyCam 3 "5 étoiles" à 249,00 € (-16%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la caméra de surveillance Eufy eufyCam 3 passe à 249,00 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 16 % et 46,63 € d'économie. Équipée d'un panneau solaire intégré limitant l'entretien et efficace pour la détection avec reconnaissance des visages, elle affiche une note actuelle de 5/5 dans nos tests.
La caméra de surveillance Eufy eufyCam 3 a été conçue pour sécuriser les extérieurs sans imposer de contraintes de câblage. Elle mise sur son capteur de 8 Mpx, sa batterie assistée d'un panneau solaire et son traitement de reconnaissance faciale. Ce modèle avait pleinement convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage aux tests.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'eufyCam 3 descend à 249,00 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit environ 16 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (295,63 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 46,63 €.
Une installation autonome et des images en 4K
Avec son panneau solaire directement intégré au-dessus du boîtier, l'Eufy eufyCam 3 supprime la corvée de la recharge manuelle si l'appareil reçoit suffisamment de lumière naturelle. Son châssis répond à la norme IP67, ce qui garantit une protection totale contre les infiltrations de poussière et les fortes averses. Ce modèle délivre des séquences vidéo très précises en plein jour grâce à sa définition 4K de 3840 x 2160 pixels, comme nous l'avons constaté dans notre test complet. Le champ de vision atteint quant à lui 135 degrés pour couvrir une large zone d'un jardin ou d'une allée.
Eufy eufyCam 3
Points forts
- Batterie et panneau solaire intégré.
- Design étanche (IP67).
- Qualité d'image de jour.
- 16 Go de mémoire embarqué, avec possibilité d'ajouter jusqu'à 16 To et cloud optionnel.
- Détection efficace avec de nombreuses options.
- Reconnaissance des visages.
Points faibles
- HomeBase obligatoire.
- Pas de port RJ45 sur les caméras.
- Micro trop peu sensible.
- Vision infrarouge un peu décevante.
- Reconnaissance des visages inefficace avec la vision infrarouge.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Détection avancée et stockage local sans frais mensuels
L'intelligence artificielle embarquée permet d'identifier les visages connus afin de limiter le déclenchement intempestif des notifications. L'eufyCam 3 conserve vos enregistrements en local sans abonnement obligatoire : elle inclut 16 Go de mémoire interne extensible jusqu'à 16 To. Sa vision nocturne en mode infrarouge manque toutefois d'efficacité et perturbe la reconnaissance faciale, un défaut qui ne gênera pas les propriétaires acceptant d'allumer le projecteur intégré à la nuit tombée.
Reolink Duo 2 : l'autre option face à l'Eufy eufyCam 3
La Reolink Duo 2 mise elle aussi sur des images soignées et une détection de mouvement très sensible. Elle se distingue par une restitution audio plus convaincante que le micro de sa concurrente, mais elle impose une installation plus contraignante et ne bénéficie pas de l'alimentation solaire intégrée.
La Reolink Duo 2 coûte 99,01 € de moins que l'Eufy eufyCam 3 à son tarif remisé, mais l'eufyCam 3 simplifie nettement la pose grâce à sa batterie solaire et conserve l'avantage de la reconnaissance faciale.
Reolink Duo 2
Points forts
- Champ de vision de 180°.
- Excellente qualité d'image.
- Nombreux réglages disponibles.
- Détection très efficace.
- Enregistrement sur carte microSD, NVR ou FTP.
- Belle qualité audio.
Points faibles
- Image un peu ramassée.
- Impossible de désactiver totalement la détection.
- Support mural pas très pratique.
- Pas de cloud pour cette version sans batterie.

articles.title: Un agricultor uruguayo quería sustituir los herbicidas. Ha acabado inventando el negocio del siglo: las ovejas cortacésped que no miran hacia arriba
articles.text:
En la agricultura hay problemas que se resuelven con maquinaria de última generación, otros con productos químicos y algunos con una buena dosis de imaginación. En Uruguay, un productor de limones ecológicos acabó desarrollando un insólito invento después de descubrir que sus mejores aliadas contra las malas hierbas tenían un pequeño defecto: un apetito descomunal.
Todo empezó en 2019. Martín Guarini, un agricultor de Araminda, en el departamento uruguayo de Canelones, había decidido reconvertir su explotación de limoneros a la producción ecológica. Pronto se encontró con un problema: eliminar las malas hierbas sin recurrir a los herbicidas convencionales resultaba caro y laborioso.
Probó con maquinaria y preparados ecológicos a base de vinagre, pero ninguna alternativa le convenció. Fue entonces cuando pensó en recurrir a una tecnología que llevaba miles de años funcionando: las ovejas.
Los cortacéspedes tenían un defecto. Durante los primeros días, el experimento parecía un éxito. Los animales eliminaban la vegetación sobrante, fertilizaban el suelo con sus excrementos y abrían una nueva vía de ingresos mediante la producción ganadera.
Sin embargo, las ovejas pronto descubrieron que las ramas inferiores de los limoneros jóvenes también eran comestibles, provocando daños considerables en los árboles. Guarini tenía el cortacésped perfecto, pero necesitaba instalarle una especie de limitador de altura.
Prohibido comer hacia arriba. Lejos de abandonar el proyecto, el agricultor se asoció con Diego Fraga, un diseñador industrial, para desarrollar un dispositivo que restringiera el acceso de las ovejas a las ramas sin impedirles pastar.
Los antecedentes de este tipo de bozales se remontaban a 1906, pero encontrar un diseño adecuado exigió alrededor de 18 meses de trabajo y más de 20 prototipos. El resultado fue una máscara móvil que permite al animal alimentarse cuando baja la cabeza, pero dificulta que lo haga cuando la levanta.
La ingeniería de la oveja. El dispositivo establece una altura máxima de alimentación de entre 80 centímetros y 1,20 metros, dependiendo de la raza y el tamaño del animal. La pieza principal pesa unos 100 gramos y el conjunto, incluyendo el arnés, ronda los 400 gramos.
Para su fabricación, los socios recurrieron al plástico reciclado y a talleres de costura de mujeres. Además, según las pruebas descritas por sus impulsores, los animales no mostraron alteraciones de comportamiento durante los periodos de utilización continuada.
Tres negocios en una misma finca. En sus 20 hectáreas de frutales, Guarini ha desarrollado un sistema productivo que funciona en diferentes alturas. Cerca del suelo obtiene carne de las ovejas, los árboles producen limones y las abejas contribuyen a la polinización y generan miel.
Los animales, a su vez, se benefician de la sombra de los frutales y de unos pastos favorecidos por el riego. Los creadores del dispositivo estiman que la inversión en los bozales puede recuperarse en seis meses gracias al ahorro en mantenimiento, herbicidas y fertilizantes.
De Uruguay a 38 países. Guarini pretendía dedicar su primer año comercial a conquistar el mercado uruguayo, pero la repercusión mediática del invento precipitó su internacionalización. México, Ecuador y España estuvieron entre sus primeros clientes.
En septiembre de 2024 ya comercializaba el dispositivo en más de diez países y, en noviembre de 2026, esa cifra había aumentado hasta los 38. Actualmente, la compañía dispone de tres centros logísticos y sus máscaras se emplean también en plantaciones de aguacates, pistachos, almendros y olivos.
Una lección para la agricultura. El sistema tiene sus limitaciones: resulta incompatible con determinados cultivos que crecen a ras de suelo, como los melones o las sandías, y exige gestionar adecuadamente la disponibilidad de pasto. No obstante, su éxito comercial ilustra las posibilidades económicas de combinar agricultura y ganadería en un mismo terreno.
Mientras buena parte de la industria trabaja en desarrollar robots autónomos capaces de eliminar las malas hierbas, este agricultor uruguayo ha construido un negocio internacional aprovechando una habilidad que las ovejas dominan desde hace milenios. Solo tenía que conseguir que no zamparan mirando hacia arriba.

articles.title: Staff at Anthropic and Open AI sound alarm on advanced models too powerful to release
articles.text:
Staff at Anthropic and Open AI sound alarm on advanced models too powerful to release
Employees working at frontier artificial intelligence model companies Anthropic PBC and OpenAI Group PBC have been butting heads with executives over advanced models whose reasoning is such that the models pose to danger to humanity, according to a report by Axios today based on more than two dozen sources familiar with the current standoff at the companies.
The report states the models in question are far more powerful than anything that has so far reached the public, showing great leaps forward in reasoning in many areas that have been difficult, “if not impossible,” to control during tests. It appears that some staff err on the side of caution and believe the training should stop completely while others believe they can be reined in.
“If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us… they will in fact be able to trick us successfully,” one of the researchers told Axios. “And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.”
After Open AI’s AI agents seemingly went berserk earlier this year and hacked the open-source AI platform Hugging Face Inc., there have been calls to pause AI development until safety can be assured. The state of California this month launched a lawsuit calling Open AI a “public nuisance,” whose models currently pose cybersecurity risks while threatening the “well-being of society.”
The debate on how far we should go before we step on the brakes has largely been overshadowed by companies, and the countries where they are developed, steaming ahead winning the AI race. In the Axios report, many of the anonymous claimed executives are “out of touch” with safety issues as they put profit first.
Nonetheless, Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei has been vocal about the “existential risks to humanity” that AI might bring. In his recent essay, “We Must Pace the Frontier,” Amodei said “pacing” is important, warning that authoritarian regimes such as China must agree to cooperate in moving forward slowly with the frontier models. President Trump has been less than supportive of such measures, calling the threats to humanity a “hoax.”

articles.title: Tuxedo unveils a formidable Linux laptop with up to 128GB RAM — but will it be enough to tempt users away from a Laptop Surface Ultra or MacBook Pro?
articles.text:
Tuxedo unveils a formidable Linux laptop with up to 128GB RAM — but will it be enough to tempt users away from a Laptop Surface Ultra or MacBook Pro?
Tuxedo's new InfinityBook Pro 15 takes up to 128GB of upgradeable RAM and a 300Hz screen
- Tuxedo's InfinityBook Pro 15 Gen11 is a modest refresh, pairing a Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 with up to 128GB of upgradeable DDR5
- The base model costs €1,504.20 before VAT, roughly $1,650, with December 2026 shipping that comes with a disclaimer
- Black Friday pricing has cut the M6 MacBook Pro to $1,849, eradicating much of Tuxedo's entry-level pricing lead
Bavarian Linux specialist Tuxedo Computers has opened pre-orders for the InfinityBook Pro 15 Gen11, a 15.3-inch Ultrabook built around AMD's 12-core Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 with room for up to 128GB of DDR5 memory and up to 8TB of SSD storage.
Tuxedo's configurator currently prices the base model, with 16GB of RAM and a 500GB SSD, at €1,792 including 19% German VAT - meaning US consumers will have to fork over about €1,506 before tax, or roughly $1,650.
On paper, it undercuts both machines this laptop will inevitably be measured against: Microsoft's Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra and Apple's MacBook Pro, but the harder question is whether the spec sheet holds up once memory speed, graphics, battery life, and software enter the picture.
Same chassis, slightly faster silicon?
The Gen11 is an evolution, not a reinvention; however, Tuxedo's press release, carried by TechPowerUp, says the machine "ships ready to use with full Linux support" in the same 1.75kg, sub-20mm aluminum body, with three power profiles of 35W, 54W, and 90W, the last requiring full fan speed.
VideoCardz also reports the 90W limit, which is ambitious for a chip AMD rates at a 28W default TDP. Whether a chassis this thin can sustain it quietly is a claim only independent testing can settle.
The processor is a small step forward: The HX 470 keeps four Zen 5 and eight Zen 5c cores, and TechRadar's review of the GMKtec EVO-X1 Pro describes it as a refresh of the Strix Point design behind the HX 370.
Graphics remain integrated, however, in the form of a 16-CU Radeon 890M, and that is the first major gap with both rivals. Buyers who need a discrete GPU will find it elsewhere in Tuxedo's own range, in machines such as the InfinityBook Max 16.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
On the memory front, Tuxedo uses two standard DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM slots, so buyers can start small and upgrade later instead of committing at checkout, as Apple's unified memory and the Surface Laptop Ultra's LPDDR5X both require.
Anyone ordering today hits a catch, though: the configurator lists both the 96GB and 128GB kits as sold out. The most memory Tuxedo will currently fit at the factory is 64GB, a €460 upgrade that, oddly, costs only €100 more than the €360 step to 32GB.
The same Tuxedo page pitches the CPU at workloads including "local AI language models (LLMs)," and AMD said at CES that ROCm 7.2 would bring official Ryzen AI 400 support on Linux as well as Windows.
Capacity is not speed, however; The offered dual-channel DDR5-5600 configuration peaks at about 89.6GB/s. Apple quotes up to 307GB/s for the M5 Pro and 614GB/s for the M5 Max, roughly 3.4 and 6.9 times as much. Token generation in local models is usually limited by memory bandwidth, so a large model that fits in 128GB of DDR5 should load, but it will likely run far more slowly than on Apple's top chip.
Reaching 128GB elsewhere is costly, though: Only the 40-core M5 Max can be configured with 128GB, and a 16-inch touchscreen model with that chip and a 2TB SSD costs $7,399. Microsoft's top Surface Laptop Ultra pairs 128GB with 1TB for $5,899. Tuxedo, for now, cannot sell a 128GB build at all, so reaching that figure means sourcing a pair of 64GB SO-DIMMs yourself at today's memory prices.
On the price front, while the Gen11 does a fairly decent job, Black Friday has since shifted the numbers considerably: Amazon has cut the M6 MacBook Pro to $1,849, with the 32GB model at $2,249. Matching the Mac's 1TB adds €50 to the Tuxedo, which still leaves it roughly $150 cheaper before shipping, taxes, and import charges.
The Tuxedo's clearer advantage is memory. A 64GB, 1TB build costs €2,302 with German VAT, or about $2,125 before tax. That is less than the discounted 32GB Mac and well below the 24GB Surface's $2,599.99 starting price.
That will not quiet the familiar complaints that have accompanied its predecessors, however: reviewing last year's InfinityBook Pro 14, TechRadar's Wayne Williams called it "far too expensive compared to the competition," noting that cheaper Windows laptops can dual-boot Linux.
For developers who want a light, upgradeable, Linux-first laptop with headroom for containers, datasets or memory-hungry models, the Gen11 makes a credible case, and nothing Apple or Microsoft sells runs Linux as comfortably. But TechRadar's roundup of Surface reviews put that machine's buying test bluntly: "Grab it if local models above 24GB are your daily work."
One could argue that user needs are decided by compute requirements, not just the ability to host a model. Anyone who needs GPU muscle or memory bandwidth will still find the Surface and the MacBook Pro in a different class, at very different prices, and Tuxedo's InfinityBook Pro 15 Gen11 is just one of many X86-based options, albeit with a larger RAM configuration capacity.

Rahim Amir is a UAE-based tech writer who enjoys building PCs as much as he enjoys writing about them. He has been professionally writing about PC hardware since 2023, focusing on buyer’s guides, hardware reviews, and sponsored content and features related to tech.
Having built hundreds of gaming PCs and being an avid gamer in his spare time, Rahim tends to have stronger opinions about hardware than most. This is particularly on display when he gets his way with powerful, but minimalistic RGB builds even as Small Form Factor (SFF) PCs come a close second.

iMP Tech Launches Mini Arcade Elite Cabinet for Switch and Switch 2
Arcade retro gaming gets a high-powered, modern evolution today with the official unveil of the Mini Arcade Elite. Engineered specifically for the Nintendo Switch ecosystem, including the classic Switch, Switch OLED, and latest-gen Switch 2, this premium arcade cabinet transforms your handheld console into an authentic desktop arcade machine!
Built for serious fighting, schmup and platform fans, retro lovers and casual gamers alike, the Mini Arcade Elite pairs authentic arcade responsiveness with a traditional wooden arcade cab. Designed to complement the latest hardware innovations of the Switch 2 alongside classic Switch support, it delivers standard setting arcade performance directly to your desk or gaming setup.
- Universal Switch Family Docking: Support for Nintendo Switch, Switch OLED, Switch 2.
- Arcade Grade Control Deck: Premium, ultra-responsive joystick and tactile buttons designed for lightning-fast combos and frame-perfect execution.
- Expanded Ergonomic Control Panel: Generous control deck layout offering enhanced hand clearance and maximum comfort during intense, extended gameplay.
- Real Wooden Cabinet Chassis with Retro styling: Crafted with solid wood framing to deliver authentic weight, structural durability, and classic coin-op vibes.
- Illuminated Light-Up Marquee: Vibrant retro backlit header brings true arcade ambiance to any room.
- Switch 2 Next Gen Functions: Built-in hardware integration supporting Switch 2 Wake and Chat, for seamless social play.
- Modder & DIY Ready: Engineered with easy-access hardware internals, allowing custom button swapping and stick upgrades for DIY enthusiasts.
- Dimensions H 26.5 x W 27.4 x D 27.1 cm
"We wanted to bridge the gap between classic coin-op arcade nostalgia and the power of modern hybrid consoles either with modern day titles or retro classics. With the Mini Arcade Elite, players get true arcade responsiveness, the freedom to mod and the most realistic arcade experience for your Switch at home!"

articles.title: Como editar um story do Instagram depois de postado
articles.text:
Como editar um story do Instagram depois de postado
Editar stories já postados no Instagram permite corrigir textos e ajustar stickers em até 15 minutos sem perder visualizações, curtidas ou a ordem da publicação original
Você sabia que é possível editar um story do Instagram mesmo após publicá-lo, corrigindo textos e ajustando figurinhas? A função está disponível diretamente nos aplicativos para Android e iPhone por meio do menu “Mais” na própria publicação.
Para editar um story já publicado, a alteração precisa ser feita no limite de 15 minutos após o envio original na rede social. O ajuste mantém todas as visualizações e curtidas intactas, exibindo apenas um discreto aviso de que o conteúdo foi modificado.
A seguir, o Tecnoblog te ensina o passo a passo para editar stories já publicados no Instagram.
Você pode editar um story depois de postado diretamente pelo aplicativo do Instagram para celular Android ou iPhone. Veja o passo a passo para alterar um conteúdo que já foi postado na rede social:
Abra o aplicativo do Instagram no seu celular e toque na sua foto de perfil, no canto superior esquerdo, para visualizar os seus stories recentes.
Com a publicação aberta na tela, toque no botão “Mais”, ícone de três pontos no canto inferior direito, para abrir a aba com as opções e ferramentas disponíveis para o conteúdo.
Toque em “Editar story” e, caso seja sua primeira vez usando a ferramenta, confirme tocando no botão “Entendi” para avançar.
Use as ferramentas de edição para corrigir textos, reposicionar figurinhas ou modificar elementos visuais do story, lembrando que a mídia original (foto ou vídeo de fundo) não pode ser substituída.
Após revisar todas as modificações feitas na tela, toque em “Salvar alterações” no canto inferior direito e aguarde alguns instantes até que o aplicativo atualize o story publicado para seus seguidores.
Ao editar stories já publicados no Instagram, a rede social aplica ajustes visuais e técnicos para sinalizar a atualização sem prejudicar o alcance da postagem. Confira os principais efeitos que ocorrem ao alterar um story:
- Selo de alteração: o Instagram exibe uma etiqueta “Editado” acompanhada de um ícone de lápis logo abaixo do seu nome de usuário, sinalizando para os seguidores que o conteúdo passou por modificações;
- Preservação do engajamento: todas as métricas de interação acumuladas antes da mudança, como a lista de visualizações, curtidas e respostas enviadas por mensagem direta (DM), permanecem intactas na publicação;
- Posição e público intocados: o story não é republicado como novo nem volta para o final da fila, mantendo a ordem na sequência e respeitando as configurações de privacidade definidas inicialmente;
- Remoção de republicações: caso outros perfis tenham compartilhado o seu story antes da alteração, esses recompartilhamentos feitos a partir do original são automaticamente removidos do ar pelo Instagram.
Não, você não perde suas visualizações ao editar stories no Instagram dentro da janela de 15 minutos após a postagem. Todo o engajamento original, incluindo curtidas e respostas, permanece intacto na publicação, que passa apenas a exibir o selo “Editado” para informar a atualização aos seguidores.
Não, o story editado não é atualizado automaticamente nos compartilhamentos feitos pelos seus seguidores. Para evitar inconsistências de exibição, o Instagram remove do ar todas as cópias ligadas à versão original, exigindo que outros perfis voltem a compartilhar stories a partir da publicação corrigida.
O Instagram não estabelece um limite fixo de alterações ao editar story depois de postado, restringindo o recurso apenas ao prazo de 15 minutos após a publicação. Durante essa janela de tempo, você pode reabrir a interface de edição e salvar ajustes nos textos ou figurinhas quantas vezes precisar no mesmo arquivo.
A opção para editar um story depois de postado fica disponível apenas quando a publicação atende a regras técnicas e prazos definidos pelo Instagram. Veja os motivos mais comuns que fazem o botão de edição sumir do seu menu:
- Prazo expirado: a janela de edição dura apenas 15 minutos após o envio. Passado esse limite de tempo, o recurso é bloqueado e você precisará apagar e publicar o conteúdo novamente;
- Liberação gradual: o Instagram distribui novas ferramentas em lotes pelo servidor, o que significa que a função ainda pode não ter sido ativada para a sua conta;
- Aplicativo desatualizado: versões antigas do Instagram não suportam os recursos mais recentes do sistema, exigindo a atualização manual do aplicativo na App Store ou Play Store;
- Recursos incompatíveis: a inclusão de stickers interativos específicos, como a figurinha “Sua Vez”, bloqueia o modo de edição devido às limitações técnicas de sincronização;
- Integração com o Facebook: stories configurados para compartilhamento cruzado com o Facebook têm a edição bloqueada para evitar falhas de exibição entre as duas redes sociais.
Se você perdeu a janela de 15 minutos para editar a publicação, a saída prática é apagar o story no Instagram e subir o conteúdo corrigido do zero. Antes de excluir a postagem, salve o arquivo na galeria do celular para reaproveitar a foto ou o vídeo original sem perder o arquivo.
Na hora de republicar, aproveite para montar stories criativos, adicionando textos, trilhas sonoras ou enquetes que ficaram de fora da primeira versão. Vale lembrar que, se você usar stickers interativos ou ativar o envio simultâneo para o Facebook, o sistema bloqueará novas edições posteriores.

articles.title: A qué edad darles el primer celular a los hijos: una especialista explicó qué factores deben evaluar los padres
articles.text:
A los cuatro años, el celular ya dejó de ser una escena excepcional en la mesa familiar, en el auto o durante una espera: el 37% de los chicos de esa edad usó un teléfono móvil en los últimos tres meses, una proporción que trepa al 74% a los 10 y al 87% a los 12. El informe Conectados y en riesgo, de la Universidad Austral, advierte que la vida digital empieza antes de que muchos niños puedan dimensionar lo que encuentran del otro lado de la pantalla.
Victoria Bein, doctora en Psicología e investigadora de la Universidad Austral, pone el foco menos en el aparato que en lo que habilita. “El primer celular implica una independencia y el acceso a un montón de cuestiones”, explicó en Infobae Al Mediodia al analizar un acceso que, con el paso de los años, queda cada vez menos bajo supervisión adulta.
El estudio, elaborado junto con María Sol González y María del Rosario Romero Victorica, reúne datos sobre chicos de entre 4 y 17 años y reconstruye cómo se expande el uso de dispositivos en la Argentina. Para Bein, el dato que ordena el resto de las discusiones es la precocidad: “Lo temprano que llega el celular propio, en promedio a los 9,6 años, es tempranísimo”.
En muchas casas, el teléfono aparece primero como una solución cotidiana: distrae, calma, permite ganar tiempo. Pero esa utilidad no agota el problema. “El celular dejó de ser un objeto de adultos y pasó a formar parte de la crianza cotidiana”, señaló la investigadora, quien remarcó que suele funcionar como “un recurso para calmar, entretener o ganar un rato de tranquilidad”.
El salto más marcado se produce al comienzo de la adolescencia. A medida que se generaliza la tenencia de un dispositivo propio, también cambia la capacidad de los adultos para saber qué hacen los chicos en línea. “Cuando la mayoría ya tiene, después de los 12, los padres reportan una caída grande del control de lo que se hace con el celular”, advirtió Bein.
Por eso, la investigadora evita reducir la conversación a una edad exacta. Antes de entregar un teléfono, propone mirar si existe una necesidad concreta, si el chico cuenta con herramientas para responder ante lo que puede aparecer y si los adultos están en condiciones de acompañarlo. “Más que la edad, yo miraría tres cosas”, sostuvo, y enumeró la necesidad, la madurez y la preparación familiar.
Su recomendación es demorar el acceso todo lo posible y no confundir un teléfono básico con una puerta libre a Internet. “Idealmente, hasta la secundaria”, dijo sobre el celular propio, mientras que sugirió que la conexión y las redes lleguen de manera gradual. “Un año más es un año más para construir la confianza que después va a hacer falta”, agregó.
Bein también relativizó la idea de que el riesgo está concentrado únicamente en el celular. Una tableta, una consola o una computadora pueden abrir los mismos accesos, mientras que el acompañamiento no se reemplaza con controles técnicos. “El mejor ‘filtro’ sigue siendo un adulto con quien el chico pueda hablar de lo que le pasa”, afirmó.
Las plataformas pueden llevar contenidos sensibles sin una búsqueda previa
La preocupación central del informe no se limita al tiempo de exposición. Entre los adolescentes, el 67% dijo haber visto contenidos sobre maneras de adelgazar o modificar el cuerpo; el 64%, propuestas para ganar dinero fácil; y el 55%, mensajes discriminatorios. En ese recorrido de publicaciones que nunca termina, Bein señaló que “las plataformas están diseñadas para retener la atención”.
Los datos sobre violencia y autolesiones agravan esa advertencia. El 53% de los consultados se cruzó con imágenes violentas o sangrientas; el 31%, con contenidos sobre formas de lastimarse; y el 27%, con información sobre maneras de quitarse la vida. “El dato es que los vieron, no que los buscaron”, precisó la especialista.
La diferencia es relevante porque las recomendaciones se alimentan de clics, reacciones y consumos similares dentro de una misma comunidad digital. Un adolescente puede entrar a una aplicación por un interés puntual y, sin buscarlo, terminar ante otro tipo de publicaciones. “Estos contenidos pueden llegarles mientras están en sus redes, sin que ningún adulto se entere”, sostuvo Bein.
La lógica de las plataformas favorece esa permanencia: cada interacción habilita una nueva sugerencia y el límite queda librado, muchas veces, a la capacidad individual de cortar. La investigadora pidió no atribuir esa dificultad solo a una decisión personal de los chicos. “Esto no se resuelve solo en cada casa: también es un problema de cómo están diseñadas las plataformas”, afirmó.
Uno de cada cuatro adolescentes quiso usar menos el celular y no pudo
Las consecuencias también aparecen en la vida diaria. El 30% de los consultados vinculó el uso de pantallas con un peor rendimiento escolar; el 24% intentó reducir el tiempo con el teléfono, pero no lo consiguió; y el 20% dejó de comer o dormir por seguir conectado. “Uno de cada cuatro quiso usar menos las pantallas y no lo logró”, subrayó Bein.
La investigadora pidió, sin embargo, no convertir ese indicador en un diagnóstico automático. Los manuales clínicos no reconocen una adicción al celular o a las pantallas, aunque la pérdida de control merece atención. “En el informe hablamos de uso problemático”, aclaró, porque la dificultad para reducir el consumo “es una señal de alerta”, pero no basta por sí sola para definir una adicción.
El impacto se extiende al descanso y a los vínculos: el 13% informó conflictos con familiares o amigos vinculados a ese hábito. En las escuelas, Bein observa consultas cada vez más tempranas por problemas de atención y por dificultades para sostener intercambios fuera de la pantalla. “La conversación se aprende practicándola”, explicó, al referirse a habilidades como leer gestos, esperar turnos y tolerar silencios.
Las horas de conexión completan el cuadro. En la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, casi la mitad de los estudiantes de 13 a 19 años usa el celular más de seis horas durante los fines de semana, según los datos citados por la especialista. “La oferta de contenidos no termina”, resumió Bein, quien ubicó esa disponibilidad como un obstáculo adicional para fijar límites sin una presencia adulta sostenida.
El acompañamiento familiar puede reducir las conductas de riesgo
El informe también registra que 40 mil chicos de entre 9 y 17 años tuvieron encuentros presenciales con adultos conocidos en línea durante el último año. A eso se suman las apuestas digitales, que suelen aparecer temprano. “La primera apuesta online es a los 13 o 14 años”, alertó Bein, al mencionar datos de la Secretaría de Políticas Integrales sobre Drogas de la Nación Argentina (Sedronar).
Frente a ese escenario, la investigadora propone incorporar la educación digital a la formación cotidiana, no como una charla ocasional después de un problema. “Debería ser parte de la educación socioemocional de los chicos”, planteó, porque una parte importante de sus vínculos, conflictos y formas de pertenencia transcurre en línea.
El acompañamiento puede modificar el modo en que los adolescentes atraviesan situaciones de acoso. Entre víctimas de ciberacoso que sentían que sus padres no entendían sus problemas, el 44,7% pensó seriamente en suicidarse durante el último año; entre quienes se sentían comprendidos, la proporción bajó al 24,9%. “Son asociaciones, no causas”, aclaró Bein, aunque consideró que el dato muestra el peso protector de sentirse escuchado en casa.
Para la especialista, la conversación tiene que empezar cuando aparece el primer dispositivo, incluso si solo se utiliza para contenidos infantiles. Los adultos deben explicar qué riesgos existen, escuchar sin minimizar y no usar la quita del teléfono como castigo ante una revelación delicada. “Hablar de suicidio no instala la idea: abre la posibilidad de pedir ayuda”, afirmó.
La responsabilidad, finalmente, no recae de manera exclusiva en las familias. Bein incluyó a las plataformas, al Estado y a las instituciones educativas, sin dejar de mirar el ejemplo que dan los mayores en su propia relación con las pantallas. “Ni culpables ni sobreseídos. Responsables, junto con otros actores”, definió.
–

articles.title: Las obras de un parque en Galicia sacan a la luz una docena de tumbas medievales y ahora no saben si dejarlas a la vista o montar un museo
articles.text:
Desde que se inauguró en 1983, los niños de Silleda juegan en el parque de la iglesia de Santa Baia. Hasta el pasado verano, porque lo que había debajo era una necrópolis medieval. En agosto se detuvo la reforma del parque al aparecer un puñado de huesos (y eso que la Xunta autorizó el proyecto en noviembre de 2025 alegando que no afectaría a ningún yacimiento). Ahora hay doce tumbas, una posible inscripción en latín y un debate muy gallego: qué hacer con los muertos que aparecen donde nadie se los espera.
Qué hay debajo. La excavación de urgencia, entre el 22 de septiembre y el 15 de octubre, documentó doce sepulturas en 260 metros cuadrados, fechadas entre finales del siglo XII y principios del XIII. Ocho están delimitadas por lajas, una tiene cubierta y tres son fosas simples. Todas miran de este a oeste, como manda el rito cristiano.
Con la iglesia hemos topado. En la cimentación del ábside de la iglesia actual (de 1854), apareció una posible lauda que alude, presuntamente, a la fórmula latina “Post Mortem Christi”. Documentos de los años 998 y 1199 ya citan una iglesia de Santa Baia, lo que refuerza que hubo un templo románico anterior. También salieron 1.236 restos óseos del cementerio más reciente, de al menos 25 personas, ahora en una fosa común parroquial. Es el primer yacimiento arqueológico identificado en casco urbano.
Tapar o enseñar. El 5 de noviembre, la Xunta dio luz verde a seguir con las obras siempre y cuando las tumbas quedaran cubiertas con geotextil y áridos. El parque será de hierba natural y no se pueden abrir zapatas de cimentación. El Concello tiene pendiente redactar un proyecto modificado y someterlo a la Diputación, quienes financian la obra.
La alcaldesa, Paula Fernández, prometió recuperar el espacio cuanto antes, siempre y cuando “respectar o que apareceu”, es decir, se respete lo hallado. El Ayuntamiento todavía valora si este hallazgo debería entrar en el Plan Xeral de Ordenación Municipal (PXOM).
El BNG llevará esta semana una moción para estudiar la musealización in situ de una parte representativa. Propone estructuras acristaladas, paneles explicativos e incluso reubicar el parque infantil si los informes lo aconsejan. La moción dice expresamente que no cuestiona el criterio de los técnicos de Patrimonio. Recuerda que cubrir los restos es una solución habitual para conservarlos. El BNG defiende que el patrimonio no es obstáculo para las obras.
Vivos y muertos. Que haya sepulturas bajo una plaza no sorprende en Galicia. Los estudios sobre arquitectura funeraria describen los camposantos rurales gallegos como espacios de “total convivencia” con los espacios de la vida. La Edad Media enterraba dentro de las iglesias y en el cementerio contiguo, justo el patrón que dibuja Santa Baia. En Noia, Santa María a Nova se levantó en 1327 sobre una Quintana dos Mortos, y hoy su museo guarda más de 500 lápidas gremiales que identifican a los difuntos por su oficio, con tijeras, anclas o picos.
Solo hace falta recordar a la Santa Compaña, la procesión de ánimas que ronda por los caminos, y el Samaín (o Samhain), en el que los vivos se reencuentran con los muertos cada 31 de octubre. En esta tradición, tapar una tumba no tiene nada que ver con olvidarla; es la forma de respetar la comunidad que se fue con la que todavía vive. Pasó antes en Málaga, donde las obras del metro destaparon una de las mayores necrópolis romanas de España. En Toledo se dice que mejor no mover mucho no vaya a ser que se despierten restos de otras ciudades. Es lo que tiene excavar entre la historia.

articles.title: Microsoft is making 32-bit software compatibility in Windows Server 2028 optional
articles.text:
WTF?! Microsoft recently detailed some of the changes coming to the Windows Server platform. Redmond's server OS is set to lose "native" compatibility with 32-bit applications, although customers should be able to restore the feature quickly if they wish. For the time being, at least.
Starting with Windows Server 2028, Microsoft's OS will no longer include full 32-bit software compatibility from the get-go. The change, which is likely to prove rather controversial, is allegedly designed to improve security on the platform while leaving "legacy" applications behind.
The Windows Server team announced the change during the Ignite 2026 conference. Windows Server 2028, expected as soon as 2027, will be an "exclusively 64-bit" operating system, with the Windows 32-bit on Windows 64-bit (WoW64) component disabled by default. WoW64 is becoming a Feature on Demand (FoD) option, which means users can install it manually at a later date.
The WoW64 subsystem has been an integral part of the Windows experience since 64-bit operating systems became the norm in the PC space. Thanks to WoW64's compatibility layer, 32-bit applications keep working as intended on 64-bit editions of Windows. The lightweight subsystem includes the interfaces and APIs required by 32-bit software in a 64-bit environment, delivering excellent compatibility and native-level performance thanks to the 32-bit hardware support still available in modern x86-64 CPUs from Intel and AMD.
According to the Windows Server team, this fundamental backbone of Windows' backward compatibility has become a significant security liability. Turning WoW64 into an FoD option is allegedly going to prevent 32-bit malware from running on Windows Server, reducing the attack surface available to cybercriminals and other malicious actors.
As Microsoft President Brad Smith recently highlighted, legacy components are making bug fixing and patching much harder in this brand-new AI-driven era. WoW64 has been included in all 64-bit Windows versions, except the Windows Nano Server installation option, which has no GUI at all. Microsoft is now clearly trying to remove all legacy components from Windows, and WoW64 might just take the same path as the now-deceased WordPad application.
Windows' native rich text editor was first turned into an FoD option, but was later removed completely from modern Windows 11 releases. Windows Server shares the same codebase as Windows 11, which means the WoW64 subsystem could eventually disappear from the consumer-oriented OS as well.
For now, Windows 11 users should be safe from this platform-breaking change. A lack of proper support for 32-bit x86 software would completely negate Windows' ability to run older video games, which in turn would destroy the platform's appeal for a truly massive userbase.
As far as I'm concerned, I am now waiting for the right incentive to finally switch to Linux for good. A lack of 32-bit support would infuriate me, no matter how "secure" Windows might become.

articles.title: Epochal launches with $100M to help developers train predictive AI models
articles.text:
Epochal launches with $100M to help developers train predictive AI models
Artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc. launched today with $100 million in funding.
The capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp. He established Epochal earlier this year with two other xAI co-founders, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss. The company’s staff also includes former researchers from Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC and Google DeepMind.
Epochal’s first offering is a cloud service called the Epochal Time Portal. According to the company, it enables developers to train AI models that can predict future events. The service does so by providing models with access to historical web data from the past 30 years.
If a bank wishes to train an AI that can predict quarterly earnings, it could use the service to fetch financial results from the first three quarters of 2025. It could then ask the AI to estimate fourth-quarter results from the same year.
After the model generates its predictions, developers can compare them against real fourth-quarter earnings to check the model’s accuracy. They can make adjustments if necessary and then repeat the training workflow until the model starts generating accurate forecasts.
The Epochal Time Portal features more than 1 trillion historical web pages on launch. Each entry includes a timestamp that indicates when it was created. According to the company, its timestamps make it possible to track how a web page changed over time.
AI models access the content through a purpose-built search engine. It enables them to specify the time periods from which they wish to retrieve web pages. According to Epochal, its platform provides one-minute granularity for the most frequently updated pages.
Like consumer search engines, the Epochal Time Portal prioritizes the web pages that are most relevant to each given query. The difference is that it considers web pages’ creation date when evaluating relevance. If a query contains the term “Meta” but asks for pages created before 2021, the year Facebook Inc. rebranded, the Epochal Time Portal will not bring up pages that relate to the social networking giant.
Today’s frontier models can determine that they’re being trained on historical data rather than up-to-date information. For example, a model might compare the creation date of a web page to the virtual clock of the operating system on which it deployed. Such discrepancies can lower the effectiveness of training runs.
According to Epochal, its service mitigates the issue by deploying AI models in sandboxes synced to their training data. If a company is training a model on we pages from 2025, the Epochal Time Portal will run it on a Linux version from that year. It applies the same precautions to the software tools and programming language versions that models use.
The Epochal Time Portal is initially available in a single free tier with low usage limits. Epochal plans to follow up the launch by sharing the results of several AI experiments that its researchers have carried out using the service.

Square POS Black Friday deals: save up to $291 on three small business systems at Best Buy
Time to get paid
Any small business worth its salt needs a reliable and modern Point of Sale (POS) system. And now, thanks to Best Buy’s Black Friday sale has cut the price of three genuinely versatile picks for a range of business types.
Three Square POS systems for small businesses get a price cut, with the contactless Square Reader now $48 (was $59), the Square Terminal down to $265 (was $299), and the fixed-checkout Square Register dropping to $609 (was $900).
Square’s appeal is its relatively straightforward approach to payment processing. In our review of the wider Square POS platform, we praised the quick setup, simple onboarding, and intuitive interfaces that are common across all Square devices.
Today's best Square POS deals
If you’re a trader, freelancer, or a small business that’s just starting out, this could be the best option. The Square Reader accepts contactless payments, chip cards, and mobile wallets and works by connecting to your iOS or Android device via Bluetooth
A more portable alternative, the Terminal combines a touchscreen, card reader and built-in receipt printer. Its rechargeable battery makes it useful for businesses that need to take payments away from the counter.
Designed for fixed checkouts, the Register is the most comprehensive option in this round-up. This unit serves up a large touchscreen for staff - so they can easily navigate sales with speed and precision - and it comes with a separate customer-facing display and integrated payment processing.
Why we recommend Square’s POS systems
Square Register is the most complete solution, with separate seller and customer-facing touchscreens that make checkout more organised. This unit is best suited to busy retail counters, although its fixed, mains-powered design means it isn’t portable - you’ll need to find some dedicated counter space.
Square Terminal combines payment processing, a touchscreen and a receipt printer in one small device. Its rechargeable battery makes it particularly useful for cafés and restaurants. The trade-off? The smaller screen means it can’t effectively replace a full countertop system.
Square Reader is the most portable and affordable option here. It connects via Bluetooth to compatible smartphones and tables to accept contactless, mobile wallet, and chip card payments. If you’re a market trader or freelancer and want something particularly portable, this should be your next purchase - even if it does lack a built-in screen.
Our Square POS platform review explores the platform, while our Square Reader review looks at the portable payment device itself.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy Square Reader if… you need a pocket-sized contactless and chip-and-PIN device for taking payments on the move.
✅ Buy Square Terminal if… you're running an eatery or business where the phone-sized unit provides receipts for your customers.
✅ Buy Square Register if… you want a point-of-sale system in a fixed location on the counter or checkout.
