articles.title: Rockstar Squashes "Leonida," the Biggest GTA 6 PC Recompilation Effort
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Rockstar Squashes "Leonida," the Biggest GTA 6 PC Recompilation Effort
Just days after its inception, Leonida, the fan-made project trying to get GTA 6 running on PC, is gone. Creator Not Rexed, who's apparently just 15 years old, announced on X that he was quitting, saying things "outside his control" kept getting in the way. After this, the project's 179,000-member Discord server and GitHub repository vanished and cannot be accessed at the time of writing. Interestingly, it looks like Rockstar was behind the shutdown, since the creator's next X post starts with "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason." Therefore, it's safe to assume that Rockstar at least had some hand in the takedown of this project. We should remember that Rockstar's parent company, Take-Two, recently DMCA'd Paralympics Productions, the company that unofficially ported GTA 5 to the Nintendo Switch.
Leonida was a static recompilation effort, probably the biggest GTA 6 project of its kind, that aimed to translate the full GTA 6 console build natively to Windows. We have seen several recompilation projects done successfully lately, such as The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake that just came out. It's reasonable to say that AI certainly has been a huge factor behind the rise of recomps. Other GTA 6 recompilation projects still remain active, including one known as VIctory that is making the rounds on social media lately. However, their future is uncertain given how closely Rockstar seems to be watching these projects.It's important to look at the timeline of events too. It all stems from notorious leaker Cyberleek, who dumped a near-complete Xbox build online, and then followed up with the missing executable on November 23. Within hours, the recompilation projects picked up steam, and footage of the game apparently close to booting started circulating online. The projects seem to be making progress, as a later clip emerged showing the opening sequence and first-time settings too. Readers are advised to stay away from any downloads claiming to be GTA 6 PC builds, as they can be the source of malware. Even though Leonida is gone, it will be interesting to see what other projects can do in this space, if Rockstar doesn't shut them down first.

articles.title: Free Mobile va disparaître le 1er décembre : voici ce qui va changer pour les abonnés
articles.text:
Le 1ᵉʳ décembre prochain, Free Mobile va fusionner avec Free. Pour être plus précis, c’est Free Mobile, en tant qu’entité juridique indépendante, qui va disparaître. En toute logique, la marque « Free Mobile » disparaîtra aussi dans la foulée. Quels sont les impacts pour les 15,8 millions de clients de Free Mobile ? N’y allons pas par quatre chemins : il n’y en a aucun. Cependant, deux informations sont tout de même à retenir. Par ailleurs, les clients de l’opérateur pourraient devoir faire preuve de vigilance.
Free Mobile va disparaître, mais les clients n’auront rien à faire
Free va absorber Free Mobile le 1ᵉʳ décembre prochain afin d’unifier ses services (Internet et mobile) au sein d’une seule entité du groupe Iliad. En ce qui concerne l’impact de cette fusion sur les clients Free Mobile, l’opérateur se veut clair : « Pour vous, rien ne change ! Vous n’avez rien à faire : tout se fait automatiquement ». Que ce soit pour les forfaits, les prix, les services, les conditions d’utilisation, la carte SIM ou encore le numéro de téléphone, aucun changement n’est à signaler. Free précise par ailleurs que les prélèvements et les cartes bancaires enregistrées « continuent de fonctionner normalement ».
En réalité, seuls deux petits changements sont à noter. Premièrement, le nom Free Mobile disparaîtra de vos factures pour laisser sa place au nom Free. Deuxièmement, les données des clients Free Mobile seront transférées vers Free. L’opérateur assure que ce transfert s’effectuera dans le respect de ses engagements en matière de confidentialité et de sécurité des données. Il s’agit donc de deux changements relativement mineurs, mais, attention, certains pourraient profiter de cette fusion pour mettre en œuvre des campagnes de phishing.
Certains arnaqueurs pourraient lancer des campagnes de phishing
Les arnaqueurs, jamais à court d’imagination, pourraient se servir de la disparition de Free Mobile pour mettre en place des arnaques. Nous pouvons par exemple imaginer un message frauduleux du type : « Free Mobile et Free vont fusionner : veuillez remplir ce formulaire afin de mettre à jour votre compte ».
Si vous recevez ce type de message, n’y accordez aucun crédit. L’opérateur le rappelle : « Free ne vous demandera jamais vos coordonnées bancaires par e-mail ou SMS. Si vous recevez un message de ce type, il ne vient pas de nous : ne cliquez sur aucun lien et supprimez-le, tout simplement ». Si vous avez le moindre doute, contactez directement Free ou rendez-vous dans un point de vente.

La génération précédente reste une référence solide au sein de notre comparatif, avec sa note actuelle de 5/5. La Garmin Fenix 8 Pro propose déjà un suivi précis par GPS et cardiofréquencemètre ainsi que des fonctions de communication autonomes, pour un fonctionnement sans smartphone.
La Garmin Fenix 8 Pro coûte 257,02 € de moins que la Garmin Fenix 9 Pro au tarif du jour, mais la nouvelle version apporte des ajustements d'interface et une structure en titane qui justifient l'investissement pour qui recherche les derniers raffinements de la marque.
Garmin Fenix 8 Pro
Points forts
- Boîtier haut de gamme.
- Écran Oled toujours lisible.
- GPS double bande précis.
- Garmin Pay.
- SMS et appels sans téléphone.
- Autonomie de 12 jours.
Points faibles
- Boîtier très gros.
- Capteur cardio en retrait sur les variations très rapides d'intensité.

articles.title: Tesla et SpaceX préparent la plus grande fusion de l'histoire pour la fin 2026
articles.text:
Le projet de fusion entre Tesla et SpaceX avance à grands pas. Un groupe vient ainsi d'être mis en place pour atteindre le plus rapidement possible cet objectif !
C'est une idée dont on entend parler depuis longtemps, et que l'on sait en cours de développement depuis un certain nombre de semaines. Les deux entreprises géantes d'Elon Musk, Tesla et SpaceX, vont fusionner, avec l'approbation de leur patron commun. Et on vient de passer une nouvelle étape, qui pourrait permettre de conclure rapidement les opérations.
Cinq administrateurs vont gérer la fusion de Tesla et SpaceX
On est passé au mode sérieux du côté de Tesla et SpaceX, selon des informations qui nous sont communiquées par le Financial Times. Cinq administrateurs ont ainsi été nommés pour cette opération, deux en provenance de SpaceX et trois de Tesla.
Leurs noms ont été données par le média, il s'agit de : Roelof Botha et Randy Glein (SpaceX) d'un côté, et Robyn Denholm, Jack Hartung et Kathleen Wilson-Thompson (Tesla). Tous ensemble, ils vont devoir gérer la naissance d'un monstre, avec une capitalisation de 3 500 milliards de dollars - ce qui en ferait la quatrième entreprise au monde à l'heure actuelle.
L'objectif est d'achever la fusion avant la fin de l'année
Il faut noter que l'acteur le plus important de tout ça Elon Musk, ne sera pas autour de la table. Il n'a en effet légalement pas le droit d'y participer selon les règles de gouvernances texanes, qui s'appliquent à Tesla - l'entreprise étant enregistrée dans cet État depuis 2024. Pour rappel, Elon Musk détient 20% des votes chez Tesla, et plus de 80% chez SpaceX.
Mais même si l'homme le plus riche du monde ne sera pas là physiquement, les cinq administrateurs qui vont négocier le projet sont tous des proches de longue date du businessman. Et ils vont semble-t-il tous travailler pour ses meilleurs intérêts, puisque les échanges « s'orientent vers une échéance potentielle fixée à la fin de l'année ». Ce qui permettrait ainsi à la nouvelle entité de naître avant que les démocrates ne prennent le pouvoir au Congrès, en janvier 2027.
Source : Financial Times

articles.title: Melhor celular custo-benefício em 2026: qual smartphone comprar?
articles.text:
Melhor celular custo-benefício em 2026: qual smartphone comprar?
Reunimos 10 smartphones para quem busca qualidade e bom preço; lista inclui celulares Samsung, Xiaomi, Motorola e Apple com o melhor custo-benefício de 2026
Um celular com bom custo-benefício é aquele que oferece bons recursos com preço justo. Em 2026, é possível encontrar modelos como o Galaxy A57, Poco X8 Pro e até o iPhone 16e com ótimas ofertas.
Para te ajudar a escolher o melhor celular custo-benefício, o Tecnoblog reuniu dez smartphones vendidos no Brasil que se enquadram nesses requisitos. A lista inclui celulares de marcas como Motorola, Samsung, Xiaomi e Apple, com preços entre R$ 800 e R$ 3.200.
Conheça a ficha técnica, avalie os pontos positivos e negativos, e descubra qual smartphone é o ideal para você.
O Galaxy A57 5G é uma opção para quem busca um celular intermediário para usar por vários anos. A Samsung promete atualizações até o Android 22 e atualizações de segurança até 2032, o que ajuda a prolongar a vida útil do aparelho.
O modelo traz acabamento lateral em metal, traseira em vidro, espessura de apenas 6,9 mm e certificação IP68 contra água e poeira. Equipado com uma tela Super AMOLED Plus de 6,7 polegadas, o celular oferece resolução Full HD+ e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, que favorece a fluidez da navegação.
Seu processador Exynos 1680 trabalha em conjunto com 8 GB de RAM, enquanto o armazenamento interno pode ser de 128 GB ou 256 GB. O conjunto fotográfico é composto por uma câmera principal de 50 MP com estabilização óptica de imagem (OIS), uma ultrawide de 12 MP e uma macro de 5 MP, além da frontal de 12 MP.
A bateria de 5.000 mAh suporta carregamento de até 45 W. O smartphone também conta com NFC para pagamentos por aproximação e ferramentas de inteligência artificial para edição de imagens.
Dica do especialista 💡
Apesar das melhorias, o Galaxy A57 muda pouco em relação ao Galaxy A56, lançado em 2025. Sendo assim, caso você encontre preços muito menores, ainda pode ser um bom negócio comprar o Galaxy A56 em 2026.
Com uma tela AMOLED de 6,8 polegadas e resolução 1.5K, o Motorola Edge 70 Fusion pode atender quem costuma assistir a vídeos ou jogar pelo celular. O painel tem taxa de atualização de 144 Hz, suporte ao HDR10+ e proteção Gorilla Glass 7i.
Apesar da tela grande, o aparelho pesa 177 gramas e possui certificações IP68 e IP69. O desempenho fica a cargo do Snapdragon 7s Gen 3, acompanhado de 8 GB ou 12 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento interno para multitarefa e jogos mobile, embora o processador tenha uma proposta intermediária.
Para fotografias, o modelo utiliza uma câmera principal de 50 MP com sensor Sony LYTIA 710 e estabilização óptica, além de uma ultrawide de 13 MP que também funciona como macro.
A câmera frontal tem 32 MP, e todas são capazes de gravar vídeos em 4K. A bateria de 5.200 mAh suporta carregamento de 68 W, com adaptador de tomada incluso na caixa. Porém, não há suporte ao carregamento sem fio.
O Poco X8 Pro é uma das opções para quem prioriza o desempenho em jogos. O smartphone da Xiaomi utiliza o processador MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra, combinado com 8 GB ou 12 GB de RAM e armazenamento de 256 GB ou 512 GB no padrão UFS 4.1.
Durante os testes do Tecnoblog, o aparelho rodou títulos como Genshin Impact e Call of Duty: Mobile sem apresentar quedas perceptíveis na taxa de quadros.
A tela AMOLED de 6,59 polegadas possui resolução de 2.756 x 1.268 pixels, taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e suporte ao Dolby Vision. Outro diferencial é a bateria de 6.500 mAh, que chegou a durar cerca de três dias em condições de uso cotidiano. O modelo suporta carregamento de até 100 W, além de carregamento reverso.
Já o conjunto fotográfico é formado por uma câmera principal de 50 MP com OIS, uma ultrawide de 8 MP e uma frontal de 20 MP. Embora a câmera principal tenha apresentado bons resultados em ambientes iluminados, os registros em locais com pouca luz apresentaram perda de nitidez e ruídos em nossos testes.
O Galaxy S25 FE reúne recursos dos celulares mais avançados da Samsung em um aparelho de preço mais acessível. Entre os diferenciais estão a compatibilidade com o Samsung DeX, que permite utilizar uma interface semelhante à de um computador, e os recursos do Galaxy AI.
O smartphone conta com o processador Exynos 2400 e 8 GB de RAM, configuração que atende desde atividades cotidianas até tarefas mais exigentes, como jogos e edição de vídeos. A tela Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 6,7 polegadas tem resolução Full HD+ e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz.
Além da câmera principal de 50 MP e da ultrawide de 12 MP, o Galaxy S25 FE traz uma teleobjetiva de 8 MP com zoom óptico de 3x, útil para fotografar objetos distantes sem depender exclusivamente do zoom digital.
A bateria de 4.900 mAh suporta carregamento de 45 W com fio, recarga sem fio e carregamento reverso por indução. O modelo possui certificação IP68 e tem sete anos de suporte de software e segurança prometidos pela Samsung.
O Moto G86 pode atender quem procura um celular para acessar redes sociais, assistir a vídeos e jogar ocasionalmente. O modelo traz tela P-OLED de 6,7 polegadas, resolução 1.5K e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz. O painel apresentou boa visibilidade em ambientes iluminados durante os testes feitos pelo Tecnoblog.
O processador MediaTek Dimensity 7300 trabalha em conjunto com 8 GB ou 12 GB de RAM, enquanto o armazenamento interno pode ser de 256 GB ou 512 GB, dependendo da versão.
Apesar de atender bem às atividades cotidianas, o aparelho apresentou aquecimento na execução de tarefas mais exigentes e precisou rodar Fortnite com configurações gráficas reduzidas.
A câmera principal de 50 MP com estabilização óptica apresentou bons resultados em fotografias diurnas, enquanto a ultrawide de 8 MP deixou a desejar. O smartphone também possui câmera frontal de 32 MP, certificações IP68 e IP69 e bateria de 5.200 mAh, que durou cerca de um dia e meio em nosso uso cotidiano.
Em contrapartida, a política de atualizações é mais limitada que a dos concorrentes da Samsung, com suporte previsto até o Android 17 e correções de segurança até 2028.
O Galaxy A17 5G é uma alternativa para quem precisa economizar na compra de um celular sem abrir mão de recursos avançados. O painel Super AMOLED de 6,7 polegadas tem resolução Full HD+ e taxa de atualização de 90 Hz, inferior aos 120 Hz dos intermediários mais avançados da Samsung.
Equipado com o processador Exynos 1330, o smartphone tem 5G e está disponível nas versões de 4 GB de RAM e 128 GB de armazenamento ou 8 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento, ambas com suporte à expansão por microSD.
A câmera principal de 50 MP conta com estabilização óptica de imagem, recurso que ajuda a reduzir os efeitos dos movimentos das mãos durante a captura. O modelo também traz uma ultrawide de 5 MP, uma macro de 2 MP e uma frontal de 13 MP.
A bateria de 5.000 mAh suporta carregamento de 25 W, e a Samsung promete até seis atualizações do Android e seis anos de correções de segurança.
A resistência contra água e poeira é um dos principais diferenciais do Redmi Note 15 Pro 5G. O smartphone possui certificações IP68 e IP69K, além de proteção Gorilla Glass Victus 2 na tela AMOLED de 6,83 polegadas. O painel tem resolução de 2.772 x 1.280 pixels e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz.
Outro atrativo é a bateria de silício-carbono de 6.580 mAh, que alcançou 14 horas e 36 minutos de reprodução contínua de vídeos via Wi-Fi, com brilho máximo, durante os testes do Redmi Note 15 Pro 5G feitos pelo Tecnoblog.
O aparelho acompanha carregador de 45 W e pode funcionar como um power bank graças ao carregamento reverso com fio de até 22,5 W. O desempenho fica a cargo do MediaTek Dimensity 7400-Ultra, acompanhado de 8 GB de RAM e 512 GB de armazenamento na versão oficial brasileira.
O celular também traz uma câmera principal de 200 MP com OIS, que permite aproximar imagens em até 4x por meio do recorte do sensor, além de uma ultrawide de 8 MP e uma frontal de 20 MP.
O Galaxy A37 5G pode ser interessante para quem prioriza a longevidade do celular, mas não precisa do desempenho adicional oferecido por outros celulares da Samsung.
Ele compartilha algumas características do Galaxy A57, como a tela de 6,7 polegadas com resolução Full HD+, taxa de atualização de 120 Hz e certificação IP68. Porém, utiliza um processador Exynos 1480, menos avançado que o Exynos 1680 presente no outro intermediário da marca.
No Brasil, o aparelho foi lançado com opções de 6 GB de RAM e 128 GB de armazenamento ou 8 GB de RAM e 256 GB de armazenamento. Para fotografias, o Galaxy A37 oferece uma câmera principal de 50 MP com estabilização óptica, uma ultrawide de 8 MP, uma macro de 5 MP e uma frontal de 12 MP.
Assim como o A57, o smartphone possui bateria de 5.000 mAh com suporte a carregamento de 45 W e conta com até seis atualizações do Android e seis anos de atualizações de segurança.
O iPhone 16e pode atender quem pretende ingressar no ecossistema da Apple gastando menos. O aparelho utiliza o chip A18, também presente no iPhone 16 convencional, mas com um núcleo a menos na GPU. O processador oferece suporte aos recursos do Apple Intelligence, além de capacidade para executar jogos e aplicativos exigentes.
A tela OLED Super Retina XDR de 6,1 polegadas faz do iPhone 16e uma opção mais compacta em relação aos demais celulares da lista. Porém, a taxa de atualização é limitada a 60 Hz que pode impactar na fluidez das animações.
O modelo possui apenas uma câmera traseira de 48 MP com estabilização óptica, que oferece aproximação de 2x por meio do recorte do sensor. Tanto a câmera traseira quanto a frontal de 12 MP gravam vídeos em 4K a 60 fps.
Disponível com 128 GB, 256 GB ou 512 GB de armazenamento, o smartphone conta com Face ID, certificação IP68 e conectividade 5G. Segundo a Apple, a bateria oferece até 26 horas de reprodução de vídeos. O modelo suporta carregamento sem fio de 7,5 W no padrão Qi, mas não possui a tecnologia de encaixe magnético MagSafe.
A câmera principal de 200 MP é um dos diferenciais do Moto G Max dentro da linha de celulares intermediários da Motorola. O sensor conta com estabilização óptica de imagem e trabalha em conjunto com uma câmera ultrawide de 8 MP. Para selfies, o aparelho oferece uma câmera frontal de 32 MP.
A tela AMOLED de 6,8 polegadas possui resolução 1.5K e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, além de proteção Gorilla Glass 7i. O modelo também conta com certificações IP66, IP68 e IP69 contra água e poeira e resistência testada conforme o padrão militar MIL-STD-810H.
Apesar das especificações de tela e câmera, o Moto G Max utiliza o processador MediaTek Dimensity 6400, menos avançado que o Dimensity 7300 presente no Moto G86.
O aparelho possui 8 GB de RAM, 256 GB de armazenamento e suporte a cartão microSD. A bateria de 5.200 mAh acompanha carregador de 33 W, enquanto a conectividade inclui 5G, NFC e suporte a eSIM.
O celular com o melhor custo-benefício é aquele que une o melhor preço às especificações necessárias para atender o seu perfil de uso. Por isso, é importante ficar atento aos seguintes atributos:
- Desempenho: quem busca um celular para jogos ou máxima produtividade deve recorrer a um smartphone intermediário premium. Essa categoria traz aparelhos com processadores otimizados e memória RAM acima de 6 GB.
- Câmeras: quem busca um celular para fotos deve ir além da quantidade de megapixels e considerar tamanho do sensor, abertura de lente, processamento de imagem e recursos de IA para fotos. Usuários comuns podem encontrar celulares baratos bons para fotos, enquanto profissionais devem recorrer aos celulares topo de linha, que têm as melhores câmeras do mercado.
- Bateria: é possível encontrar celulares com bateria grande nas mais diversas faixas de preço. Se essa for a sua única exigência, modelos de entrada podem atender às suas necessidades com o melhor custo-benefício.
- Atualizações: se você quer um celular que dure muitos anos, é importante ficar atento à política de atualização da fabricante. Marcas como Samsung e Apple costumam ser as mais generosas, oferecendo entre seis e sete anos de updates de versão do sistema operacional.
Três marcas se destacam em custo-benefício no Brasil: Samsung, Motorola e Xiaomi. Essas empresas oferecem uma ampla variedade de smartphones, desde modelos baratos e básicos até celulares intermediários e topo de linha, garantindo opções para todos os orçamentos.
A Motorola costuma entregar modelos de melhor custo-benefício na linha Moto G e Edge, equilibrando preço e desempenho.
A Samsung concentra boa parte de seu portfólio na linha Galaxy A, que traz smartphones básicos e intermediários com recursos modernos e preços competitivos.
Já a Xiaomi se destaca pelas linhas Poco e Redmi Note, que trazem configurações potentes com valores mais acessíveis que concorrentes diretos.
Sim, marcas como Samsung, Motorola e Xiaomi têm celulares que custam até R$ 1.000. Porém, esses aparelhos tendem a ter recursos básicos. Por isso, eles devem ser usados para tarefas mais simples, como chamadas, navegação na web e acesso a redes sociais.
O Samsung Galaxy S25 FE é uma ótima opção para quem prioriza fazer fotos e vídeos. O celular é equipado com uma câmera traseira principal de 50 megapixels (OIS) complementada com uma câmera teleobjetiva de 8 megapixels para zoom óptico de 3x e uma câmera ultrawide de 12 megapixels.
O Galaxy S25 Ultra. Esse é um aparelho que foi topo da Samsung em 2025, e já teve redução de preço no varejo. Como o smartphone oferece recursos avançados, ele ainda é um bom modelo para se comprar em 2026.

articles.title: Un troyano para Android copia la pantalla de inicio del celular para ocultar el robo de datos bancarios
articles.text:
Una firma de seguridad advirtió sobre Bazuka, un programa malicioso para Android que utiliza una captura de la pantalla de inicio o bloqueo del celular como superposición para ocultar las acciones que ejecuta en segundo plano.
ThreatFabric, empresa de seguridad móvil de Países Bajos, encontró el programa mientras investigaba un caso de fraude con una aplicación que retransmite datos de tarjetas bancarias de pago sin contacto. Esperaban una pieza simple. Hallaron un conjunto de herramientas completo.
El informe describe un descargador que instala el programa, un núcleo que se comunica con los atacantes y 23 módulos que se bajan según la campaña. Entre ellos hay módulos para pantallas falsas de inicio de sesión, registro de teclado, interceptación de mensajes SMS y códigos de verificación en dos pasos, control remoto y cambio de direcciones de criptomonedas.
El módulo que cambia direcciones detecta las de bitcoin, ether, TRC20 y solana copiadas al portapapeles y las reemplaza por otras elegidas por los atacantes. Otro módulo captura el PIN, la contraseña o el patrón de desbloqueo del teléfono mediante los permisos de accesibilidad de Android.
Una inteligencia artificial ayuda a elegir víctimas
El panel de control que usan los operadores incluye un asistente basado en modelos de lenguaje. Según la firma de ciberseguridad, estos agentes de IA ayudan a identificar víctimas de interés y a gestionar infecciones a gran escala. El panel también calcula un puntaje que indica cuán atractivo es cada dispositivo como objetivo.
Los investigadores encontraron esa función en el panel, no una IA que robe por sí sola. Los textos y elementos de la interfaz aparecen en inglés y en ruso, y la firma de ciberseguridad no atribuyó Bazuka a ningún grupo conocido.
Bazuka puede activar la depuración inalámbrica de Android, un modo pensado para desarrolladores, e interceptar el PIN de emparejamiento para concederse permisos sin que el usuario los autorice. ThreatFabric prevé que esta práctica se vuelva habitual en los troyanos bancarios, porque permite que módulos sobrevivan aunque se elimine la aplicación inicial.
Disfrazado de contenido para adultos de TikTok
Para llegar a las víctimas, los distribuidores, que los investigadores llaman traffers, crean páginas que ofrecen supuestas aplicaciones, por ejemplo de televisión por internet. Los expertos en seguridad digital documentaron un archivo llamado como una versión premium de TikTok con contenido para adultos, que se descarga fuera de las tiendas oficiales y pide permiso para instalar aplicaciones de terceros.
El panel también contiene ajustes para que el instalador pida pocos permisos y pueda pasar la revisión de Google Play. La firma dice que esas opciones prueban la intención de usar la tienda oficial, pero que no vio señales de que ocurriera. El informe tampoco da una cifra de infectados ni lista bancos o países afectados.
Qué hacer si se sospecha una infección
El medio especializado eSecurity Planet advirtió que abrir la aplicación del banco en el mismo teléfono puede no ser una forma confiable de comprobar el estado de la cuenta. Un código recibido en un aparato comprometido tampoco sirve como segundo factor de confianza.
Su recomendación es llamar al banco desde otro dispositivo, con el número impreso en la tarjeta o en un resumen, y no con uno recibido por mensaje. Después conviene revisar los accesos y cambiar contraseñas desde un teléfono o una computadora seguros, empezando por el correo electrónico principal.
Para limpiar el celular contra el software malicioso en Android se debe verificar que Play Protect esté activo, instalar las actualizaciones de seguridad y eliminar las aplicaciones sospechosas. Si los síntomas persisten, Google indica que puede hacer falta restablecer el teléfono de fábrica o pedir ayuda al fabricante.
Borrar la aplicación no revierte una transferencia ni devuelve una contraseña ya capturada, advirtieron los expertos. Los datos del informe de ThreatFabric corresponden a muestras analizadas hasta fines de octubre, y la firma aún no obtuvo el instalador intermedio de la cadena de infección.

articles.title: Marlowe raises $277M to build inference clusters with chips from Nvidia rivals
articles.text:
Marlowe raises $277M to build inference clusters with chips from Nvidia rivals
Artificial intelligence infrastructure startup Marlowe AI Inc. has closed a huge $227 million seed round led by Accel.
Bessemer, Altimeter, Emergence Capital and a number of other institutional bakers chipped in as well. They were joined by a large group of angel investors that included the chief executives of Palo Alto Networks Inc, Uber Technologies Inc., Box Inc. and Dropbox Inc. GeekWire reported on Monday that Marlowe is valued at $1.15 billion.
Marlowe was founded last year by CEO Dan Lewis and Chief Technology Officer Kutta Srinivasan. Lewis previously headed the Microsoft Corp. unit responsible for Copilot Studio, the tech giant’s AI agent development tool. Srinivasan was the techical lead of the company’s AI infrastructure group.
Marlowe is building AI data centers for inference workloads. The company will optimize each facility for a specific inference workload category by tailoring its chip mix, network configuration and software. Marlowe believes that its approach will provide better hardware efficiency than general-purpose graphics card clusters.
“Even modest gains in network architecture, power oversubscription, AI-driven fleet operations, and workload-specific inference optimization multiply to create a durable, 2-3x overall advantage in performance, availability, resiliency, and cost,” Lewis and Srinivasan wrote in Marlowe’s launch blog post.
The company plans to bring its first data center online next month. It’s based on hardware from Etched Inc., an inference chip startup that was valued at $21 billion in August.
Graphics cards often use only a small fraction of their maximum clock speed to avoid overheating. Etched’s chip is less prone to overheating and can therefore operate at higher clock speeds, which boosts model performance. The company says that its accelerator provides “multiple times the FLOPs density” of graphics cards.
Etched ships its chips as part of custom-made inference racks. According to the company, the systems feature an interconnect that can perform some data movement tasks more than four times faster than competing silicon. Etched’s rack design also includes custom power management and cooling components.
Marlowe’s second facility will come online in the second quarter of 2027. It will host racks based on Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s Helios design. A Helios rack hosts 72 AMD graphics cards along with central processing units and Pensando data processing units, or DPUs. The DPUs offload networking tasks from the other chips to leave more computing capacity for AI models.
Helios racks’ networking and power delivery links are arranged in a configuration that reduces the need for manual cable maintenance. Additionally, the coolant lines feature a so-called quick-disconnect design. They can be plugged and unplugged without the specialized tools usually needed for the task.
GeekWire reported that Marlowe has also signed a letter of intent for a third data center. According to the publication, each of the company’s planned facilities will provide tens of megawatts of computing capacity. One megawatt is enough to power several hundred homes.
Marlowe will use the proceeds from its seed round to finance hardware purchases and hire engineers.

articles.title: Rockstar nukes 15-year-old’s GTA 6 recompilation project, Discord and GitHub servers taken down — Project Leonida had almost 180,000 Discord members, host account banned for two years
articles.text:
Rockstar nukes 15-year-old’s GTA 6 recompilation project, Discord and GitHub servers taken down — Project Leonida had almost 180,000 Discord members, host account banned for two years
Project Leonida is no more, even after the project got GTA 6 to run on a PC, with the person behind it now banned from Discord for two years.
Project Leonida, a recompilation project aiming to bring the console version of GTA 6 to the PC, has been shut down, with its Discord and GitHub servers taken offline. The 15-year-old kid behind the project has admitted that Rockstar took down the server, adding that the life of a teenager is hard enough "without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord." The Project Leonida Discord server had almost 180,000 members when it was taken offline, TechPowerUp reports. NotRezed, the account behind the project and associated online presences, has also confirmed that they have been banned from Discord for two years.
The project to make GTA 6 run on a Windows PC months ahead of the game's expected early 2027 release window is one of a run of similar recompilations, some of which have proven successful. Earlier this year, we saw Zelda: Ocarina of Time brought to Apple platforms, months before the game's remake was announced for the Nintendo Switch 2. That same game is now circulating online after an AI-assisted jailbreak allowed it to be dumped immediately following its release. Similar AI assistance has helped the recompilation efforts of multiple projects in recent months, and GTA 6 is unlikely to be the last.
In the case of this ill-fated project, it came just days after notorious leaker Cyberleek made a near-complete build of the Xbox version of GTA 6 available online. A missing executable for the game was then also released on November 23, with recompilation efforts taking note. And while Project Leonida is no more, there's no indication that other parallel projects will follow suit.
As for NotRexed, they say that they "really want to make cool stuff," but that things have happened that they "can't control," and they will be stepping away as a result.
GTA 6 was released on the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S platforms on November 19 and immediately shot to the top of sales charts. It's since been confirmed that the game reached $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales with 32.5 million units sold pre-release. Sony has also announced that the game set a new record for the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation, with players logging 683 million hours of gameplay by November 23. The game has captured the attention of gamers everywhere, with one even using mind control and eye tracking to hijack an in-game airplane.

Oliver Haslam has written about technology of all shapes and sizes for over 15 years, both online and in print. He's fascinated by how personal computing continues to change as tower PCs give way to foldable phones and beyond.

articles.title: Lakshmi Venu files suit seeking partition of Venu Srinivasan family assets
articles.text:
Lakshmi Venu files suit seeking partition of Venu Srinivasan family assets
Lakshmi Venu has filed a suit in the Madras High Court seeking partition of Venu Srinivasan family assets and access to records, after efforts towards an amicable settlement failed to make progress.
Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan, has filed a suit in the Madras High Court seeking partition of the joint-family assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the TVS family.
A statement from Lakshmi Venu’s counsel said she seeks her claimed share and access to family records that she says have been withheld despite repeated requests.
The suit follows a November 16 partition notice to her father, who is Chairman Emeritus of TVS Motor and Non-Executive Chairman of TVS Holdings.
The statement said his reply did not recognise Lakshmi Venu's claim, and settlement efforts had failed. It noted the case concerns ownership, and not directed at the operations of any company, and that any partition should be given effect in an orderly manner.
Mallika Srinivasan supports her daughter. In a statement, she said, “It is unfortunate that the response to Lakshmi’s notice has not recognized her lawful rights and no progress has been made towards an amicable resolution. In these circumstances, she has been compelled to approach the Court to protect her rights.”
Queries have been sent to Venu Srinivasan seeking his response to Lakshmi Venu’s claims and the issues raised in the suit. This story will be updated if a response is received.
Lakshmi Venu’s statement dated November 16 identifies interests held through the VS Trust and other holding structures, including stakes in TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and TVS Holdings, formerly known as Sundaram-Clayton. She also alleges that the concentration of beneficial interest in favour of her brother Sudarshan Venu was to the exclusion of her own lawful rights.
The central question is whether the wider TVS family settlement of 2020 also settled the economic interests of the Venu Srinivasan branch.
A stock-exchange disclosure confirms that the four family members signed a further memorandum in March 2024, following the wider TVS family settlement based on a December 10, 2020 agreement, effective from February 4, 2022. It describes the 2024 memorandum as covering brand use and business restrictions, and says TVS Holdings was not a party and that its business was not adversely affected. The disclosure does not establish that the family assets were partitioned.
Lakshmi Venu and Mallika Srinivasan said no final economic settlement was reached. Venu Srinivasan and Sudarshan, according to Financial Express, maintain that the arrangements were consensual, documented and binding.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Europe forced Apple to open iPhone to rival browser engines, but Mozilla says the door is rigged
articles.text:
Walled Prison: On paper, Apple should now be required to give competing browsers and browser engines full access to the popular iOS ecosystem. But Mozilla says the iPhone maker is imposing so many restrictions on alternative browser engines that meaningful competition is unlikely to emerge anytime soon.
Thanks to Europe's Digital Markets Act, Apple has been required to improve browser choice on iOS in the Old Continent since 2024. Similar rules now apply in Japan as well. However, one of the few independent players in the browser market says Apple has no real intention of promoting competition on its tightly controlled mobile platforms.
In a recent blog post, Mozilla argued that, despite the new regulations, Apple's iOS ecosystem is still not truly "open" to competing browser engines. Alternative browsers such as Firefox are available on iOS, and millions of users have reportedly chosen them over Safari. However, one major limitation remains: these browsers are required to use WebKit, Apple's browser engine, which powers Safari and other third-party browsers on its platforms.
According to Mozilla, Apple is forcing browser developers to rebuild their products around WebKit. Consequently, third-party developers cannot easily bring their own distinctive features to Apple's mobile platforms because doing so requires their own browser engines, such as Mozilla's Gecko. These restrictions primarily affect iOS devices, including the iPhone and iPad, while other major operating systems – including Apple's own macOS – remain unaffected.
Apple has been compelled to improve browser choice on its mobile devices under the DMA, but the company has continued to push back against European regulatory requirements. Mozilla now claims that Cupertino is imposing its own set of conditions on developers seeking approval to bring competing browser engines to iOS. According to the foundation, these requirements are designed to make the process "as painful as possible."
Among these conditions is a restriction on disclosing non-public information related to the iOS version of Gecko. Even more problematic are Apple's browser update requirements. Mozilla says that simply installing a newer version of Firefox on an iOS device may not be possible under the current rules. Instead, Apple would apparently require Mozilla to release an entirely separate app, forcing Firefox users to transfer their data – including passwords, bookmarks, and browsing history – from the existing version to the new Gecko-based browser.
"The conditions Apple imposes, including a level of user friction Apple would never accept for its own apps, mean that the open door feels more like a trap door", Mozilla said.
Firefox users on iPhone have already demonstrated their willingness to choose alternatives to Safari, despite Apple's restrictions on the browser market. Mozilla would now like Cupertino to allow a genuinely open browser experience on iOS, including support for third-party browser engines such as Gecko.

articles.title: 'Simple doesn't mean basic' - how this gaming keyboard won my heart
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Glorious has taken its mechanical keyboard game back to school, with a remarkably straightforward 96% keeb that offers a truly excellent experience for typing and gaming. The Glorious GMMK Eternal feels like a high-end, well-constructed product, with triple-layer sound damping under each keycap and per-key RGB lighting, but the pricing is surprisingly reasonable. Of course, this back-to-basics approach and sensible price tag mean that it lacks the unique features that make some other keyboards stand out, but this is still a fantastic choice for any PC gamer.
Reasons to buy
- + Satisfying switches with good sound damping
- + Excellent build quality
- + Compact without feeling cramped
- + Good value for money
Reasons to avoid
- - Wired only
- - No extra features
Why you can trust TechRadar We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Glorious GMMK Eternal: Two-minute review
Sometimes simple really is better. That seems to have been the ethos behind the new Glorious GMMK Eternal, a 96% form factor gaming keyboard that I could immediately tell would be worthy of standing among the best gaming keyboards on the market.
There are no fancy bells and whistles here; no tiny LED display, no multi-device connectivity, no optical key switches with adjustable actuation. Glorious has focused on the basics, delivering a product that simply functions exceptionally well for both typing and gaming.
A big part of this is the build quality. While it might look fairly pedestrian in aesthetic terms as far as gaming keyboards go, the GMMK Eternal feels like a high-end device straight out of the box despite its $99.99 / £89.99 (around AU$150) price tag.
Beyond the per-key RGB lighting (which is practically a given for any decent gaming keyboard these days), the design is not at all ostentatious. The backplate is solid aluminum with a very slim bezel around the edges, and the keycaps are double-shot ABS plastic, both in matte black. There's no in-your-face branding, save for the Glorious logo stamped on the underside.
As I mentioned earlier, the GMMK Eternal uses a 96% key layout; in other words, you get the functionality of a full-size keyboard, but with a much smaller overall footprint. The numpad, arrow keys, and function row are all still in place, but some of the navigation keys are eliminated, and there are no dedicated media controls – one thing I do like to see on gaming keyboards, so it's a shame they weren't included here, even if it does allow for a more svelte overall device.
On the underside, there are double-level feet that allow for three different inclines. Connectivity is wired-only, via an included USB-C to USB-A cable. Anyone looking for multi-device functionality should look elsewhere – as I noted before, Glorious is keeping things as simple as possible here.
Simple doesn't mean basic, though. The linear red Glorious Fox key switches are excellent, providing a solid amount of actuation force (55g, a little beyond the average linear switch) with a pleasingly muted striking sound thanks to the triple-layer sound-damping underneath, which uses a silicone base with two layers of PU foam surrounding each switch.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As a linear switch enjoyer, I was very enamored with the GMMK Eternal's typing experience. It doesn't quite give the 'thwock' you might expect from a more expensive mechanical keyboard, but nonetheless the sound is very satisfying. If you prefer a different type of switch, like clicky blue or the classic tactile brown, every switch on the Eternal is easily hot-swappable with an included tool.
In terms of actual use, I had a great time with the Glorious GMMK Eternal. It felt reliable and responsive both for everyday typing and for all kinds of games, including competitive shooters like The Finals and Marathon and MMOs like World of Warcraft Forever. I also tested out the Glorious Core utility software, which lets you tweak the (somewhat limited) settings of the keyboard
I did use my own wrist rest for some of my time testing the GMMK Eternal, since it doesn't come with one included in the box (unsurprising, given the stripped-down approach here), but I did actually find that it was perfectly comfortable to use without one on the lowest incline.
Overall, the Glorious GMMK Eternal is an easy recommendation, purely because it's such good value for money.
Glorious GMMK Eternal review: Price & availability
- $99.99 / £89.99 (around AU$150)
- Available now in the US and UK
- Excellent value for money
The Glorious GMMK Eternal will cost you $99.99 / £89.99 (around AU$150), and is available now in the US and UK; shoppers in Australia will have to try their luck with third-party retailers.
There's only one configuration available, which uses the manufacturer's own Fox Red key switches, but these are hot-swappable so you're always free to replace or upgrade them later on.
It's not exactly cheap for a wired mechanical keyboard, but it notably does come in at a lower cost than gaming-oriented competitors like the HyperX Origins 2 1800, and it's a lot cheaper than the (admittedly excellent) Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75%. In terms of bang for your buck, the GMMK Eternal offers a great value proposition.
Glorious GMMK Eternal review: Specs
| Layout | 96% | 
| Switch | Mechanical (Linear Red) | 
| Programmable keys | Yes | 
| Dimensions | 14.6 x 4.8 x 1.7 inches (372 x 122 x 44mm) | 
| RGB or backlighting | Yes (customizable) | 
Should I buy the Glorious GMMK Eternal?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Not exactly super-budget, but offers exceptional value for money with a premium-feeling design. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Design and features | A bit feature-light, but delivers top-notch build quality with a straightforward but stylish appearance. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | The linear switches feel satisfyingly weighty and responsive, but are surprisingly quiet for a mechanical keyboard. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Overall | The GMMK Eternal is a fantastic back-to-basics effort from Glorious, easy to recommend for anyone who wants a premium keyboard that won't cost the world. | 4.33 / 5 | 
Buy the Glorious GMMK Eternal if…
You love quiet switches
The GMMK Eternal only comes with Glorious Fox Red switches, but they're so delightfully quiet and thunky that you won't want to swap them out.
You want value for money
For the premium build quality and typing experience it offers, this keyboard is very sensibly priced indeed.
Don't buy it if…
You want lots of features
Without a built-in display or dedicated media controls, the GMMK Eternal is pretty basic as far as gaming keyboard go.
You want something super cheap
Although the GMMK Eternal is very competitively priced, PC gamers with very tight budgets might still want to look elsewhere.
Glorious GMMK Eternal review: Also consider
HyperX Origins 2 1800 
The HyperX Origins 2 1800 is another wired gaming keyboard with mechanical switches and hot-swappable hardware, though it's slightly more expensive than the GMMK Eternal. However, it still boasts premium build quality, and the retro translucent casing will no doubt appeal to some PC gamers.
Read our full HyperX Origins 2 1800 review
MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra
If absolute value for money is your goal, the FUN60 Ultra is even cheaper than the GMMK Eternal and offers a solid build with ultra-responsive analog switches – though the customization software does leave a little to be desired.
Read our full MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra review
How I tested the Glorious GMMK Eternal
- Tested for just under a week
- Used for various tasks as well as gaming
- 8+ years of experience reviewing gaming hardware
I tested the Glorious GMMK Eternal for just under a week, swapping out my regular keeb – the Asus ROG Strix Scope RX – and using it for everyday tasks as well as gaming and creative work.
In terms of the games tested, I played a broad selection, including The Finals, Warframe, Soulframe, Marathon, and World of Warcraft Forever (which, incidentally, rules).
I've been a die-hard PC gamer for more than 20 years, building my first system when I was 16, and I've been working as a professional hardware reviewer for more than eight years – starting my tenure at Maximum PC magazine before making the leap to digital journalism and joining the TechRadar team in 2021. I put every bit of knowledge and experience I've gained over the years into my product reviews, so you can be sure you're getting an informed and unbiased analysis.

Christian is TechRadar’s UK-based Computing Editor. He came to us from Maximum PC magazine, where he fell in love with computer hardware and building PCs. He was a regular fixture amongst our freelance review team before making the jump to TechRadar, and can usually be found drooling over the latest high-end graphics card or gaming laptop before looking at his bank account balance and crying.
Christian is a keen campaigner for LGBTQ+ rights and the owner of a charming rescue dog named Lucy, having adopted her after he beat cancer in 2021. She keeps him fit and healthy through a combination of face-licking and long walks, and only occasionally barks at him to demand treats when he’s trying to work from home.

articles.title: Fuite de données chez Decathlon : les informations de 163 000 clients ont été piratées
articles.text:
Dans la nuit du dimanche 22 au lundi 23 novembre, un pirate, qui se fait appeller « 4me1 », a revendiqué une cyberattaque à l’encontre de Decathlon. Le cybercriminel a publié quatre fichiers volés à l’enseigne sur PwnForums, un forum cybercriminel, rapporte le site spécialisé Frenchbreaches.
À lire aussi : Cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne – des données personnelles ont été volées, des hackers chinois sont suspectés
163 000 fiches clients dans la nature
L’archive contient 163 646 fiches de contact et de livraison, dont 137 550 adresses e-mail distinctes. La base de données contient aussi des noms, des numéros de téléphone, des adresses postales et des références de commandes. Un second fichier publié sur le forum contient 255 011 lignes de commandes, datant de 2021 à novembre 2026.
 🔴 Decathlon confirme une cyberattaque après l’alerte de FrenchBreaches !
Plus de 163 000 fiches clients auraient été exposées, avec des noms, adresses, téléphones, e-mails et détails de livraison, après une intrusion chez un prestataire externe. https://t.co/w59W6C8QbH
— FrenchBreaches (@Frenchbreaches) November 23, 2026
Certains fichiers contiennent des informations précises sur le domicile des acheteurs, dont le type de logement, la présence d’un ascenseur et toutes les consignes laissées aux livreurs, comme l’accès à un bâtiment ou un interphone. Plus de 600 lignes concernent des livraisons qui sont prévues cette semaine, entre le 23 et le 28 novembre… en plein milieu du Black Friday. Attention, une même personne peut apparaître dans plusieurs fiches distinctes. De facto, le nombre exact de clients touchés reste encore à déterminer.
À lire aussi : « Rien ne laisse à penser que les choses vont s’arranger » – face aux cyberattaques IA, la France contre-attaque
Decathlon confirme un « accès malveillant »
Peu après la revendication, Decathlon a confirmé qu’un « accès malveillant à des données personnelles, notamment l’identité, numéros de téléphone et adresses, s’est produit en France le 22 novembre 2026 ». Selon l’enseigne, l’attaque a eu lieu « chez l’un de ses prestataires externes », et non directement dans la base des comptes clients de Decathlon. Le nom de ce prestataire n’a pas été dévoilé pour le moment. Sans surprise, Decathlon va prévenir la Commission nationale de l’informatique et des libertés (CNIL),
« Nos équipes sont immédiatement intervenues pour bloquer l’accès compromis et aucune donnée bancaire ni mots de passe n’ont été impactés », assure l’entreprise, ajoutant que les clients concernés vont être prévenus par e-mail.
Ce n’est pas la première fois que Decathlon se retrouve dans le viseur des cybercriminels. En octobre dernier, une fuite de données avait déjà touché un prestataire de Train Me, la filiale de coaching sportif de l’enseigne, compromettant les informations de certains utilisateurs. Deux ans plus tôt, Decathlon Belgique a reconnu des accès frauduleux à des comptes clients. Lors de tous les incidents recensés, les pirates sont passés par des prestataires, dont les mécanismes de sécurité sont plus faillibles.
Les données volées lors du piratage risquent d’alimenter une nouvelle vague d’arnaques, dont des escroqueries au colis. Si vous avez passé commande sur decathlon.fr, faites preuve de vigilance. Ne cliquez jamais sur un lien reçu par SMS ou par e-mail pour suivre un colis. Passez toujours par votre compte, sur le site ou, encore mieux, sur l’application Decathlon. Surtout, ne communiquez jamais vos coordonnées bancaires pour débloquer une livraison. En cas de doute, contactez directement Decathlon par le biais du service client.

articles.title: Batteries solaires et stations Anker SOLIX : les offres du Black Friday
articles.text:
Face au prix de l’électricité et à l’incertitude qui l’entoure, mieux gérer sa consommation devient une préoccupation pour de nombreux foyers. Pour le Black Friday, Anker SOLIX propose jusqu’à 2 300 € de réduction sur ses solutions de stockage d’énergie, avec plusieurs modèles adaptés aux besoins de la maison, comme aux déplacements.
Nous pouvons tous en témoigner, la facture d’électricité reste une source de préoccupation pour les Français. Selon un sondage OpinionWay pour Anker, 74 % des personnes interrogées redoutent une future hausse des prix de l’électricité. Plus révélateur encore, 72 % déclarent avoir déjà modifié leurs habitudes de consommation au cours des deux dernières années, notamment en consommant moins, ou encore en décalant certains usages pendant les heures creuses.
Dans ce contexte, le stockage de l’énergie peut constituer un avantage on ne peut plus intéressant. Lorsqu’un logement dispose de panneaux photovoltaïques, une batterie permet de conserver l’électricité produite en journée pour l’utiliser le soir, lorsque les panneaux ne produisent plus. Selon la solution et le contrat d’électricité, il est tout à fait possible de recharger sa batterie pendant les heures creuses pour utiliser cette énergie précisément lorsque le prix du kilowattheure est plus élevé.
A l’occasion du Black Friday, Anker SOLIX propose justement plusieurs solutions pour répondre à ces différents besoins. Voici cinq équipements à découvrir, en promotion jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026 dans le cadre d’une opération qui offre jusqu’à 2 300 € de réduction.
En complément, Anker SOLIX offre aux lecteurs de Clubic le code promo CLUBIC, qui donne droit à 5 % de réduction sur tous les produits achetés sur son site officiel.
SolarBank Max AC : une solution pour mieux exploiter ses panneaux solaires existants
Vous disposez déjà de panneaux photovoltaïques et souhaitez conserver une plus grande partie de l’électricité qu’ils produisent ? La SolarBank Max AC répond précisément à cette problématique. Contrairement à une batterie solaire classique directement raccordée aux panneaux, elle fonctionne en couplage AC, ce qui lui permet de s’intégrer à une installation photovoltaïque déjà existante, y compris équipée de micro-onduleurs. Pour le Black Friday, la SolarBank Max AC passe à 1 899 € au lieu de 2 499 € chez Anker.
Avec une capacité de stockage de 7 kWh (extensible jusqu’à 42 kWh avec des batteries supplémentaires) et un poids de 73 kg, elle permet de conserver ce précieux surplus produit pendant la journée, pour venir alimenter les équipements de la maison en soirée. Sa gestion intelligente peut également optimiser les cycles de charge et de décharge en fonction des tarifs de l’électricité.
La SolarBank Max AC constitue donc une piste particulièrement intéressante pour les foyers déjà équipés, et qui souhaitent faire évoluer leur installation sans nécessairement repartir de zéro. Enfin, pour le Black Friday, le compteur intelligent Anker SOLIX Gen 2, d’une valeur de 109 €, est offert pour l’achat de la batterie.
Un modèle SolarBank Max, proposé à 2 599 € au lieu de 2 899 € (-10 %), est également disponible, et s’adresse davantage aux installations photovoltaïques utilisant un onduleur de chaîne.
SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro : une batterie domestique évolutive pour toute la maison
Pour les foyers qui souhaitent disposer d’une solution de stockage, la SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro propose une capacité de 5 kWh. Son système accepte jusqu’à 12 panneaux photovoltaïques et une puissance solaire maximale de 5 000 W. Pour le Black Friday, la SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro passe à 1 799 € au lieu de 2 399 € chez Anker.
De quoi couvrir là encore une partie des besoins du logement, tout en conservant une réserve d’énergie pour les heures où la production solaire devient insuffisante.
L’un de ses avantages tient à son évolutivité, puisqu’il est possible d’ajouter facilement des batteries supplémentaires pour atteindre jusqu’à 30 kWh de stockage. Elle dispose également d’une sortie hors réseau de 2 500 W, utile pour alimenter certains appareils en cas de coupure électrique.
Une solution à envisager pour les foyers qui souhaitent construire un véritable système de stockage domestique, capable d’évoluer avec leurs besoins. Là aussi, le compteur intelligent Anker SOLIX Gen 2 est offert pour l’achat de cette SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro.
SolarBank 3 E2700 Pro : un premier pas vers l’autoconsommation solaire
C’est un fait, tous les logements n’ont pas les mêmes besoins énergétiques. Avec sa capacité de 2 688 Wh, la SolarBank 3 E2700 Pro constitue une alternative plus compacte pour les foyers qui souhaitent stocker une partie de leur production photovoltaïque, sans forcément investir immédiatement dans un système de grande capacité. Pour le Black Friday, la SolarBank 3 E2700 Pro passe à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 599 € chez Anker.
Elle accepte jusqu’à 3 600 W de puissance solaire en entrée et peut elle aussi accueillir des batteries additionnelles, pour atteindre jusqu'à 16 kWh de stockage. Son système de gestion intelligent lui permet de piloter les flux d’énergie et d’adapter leur utilisation aux habitudes du foyer.
C’est incontestablement une option à considérer pour une installation solaire résidentielle de taille intermédiaire, avec la possibilité d’augmenter progressivement ses capacités de stockage.
Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 : une station électrique pour la maison et les déplacements
On quitte ici les batteries résidentielles pour s’intéresser à une station électrique portable. La C2000 Gen 2 embarque une batterie LFP de 2 048 Wh (pour un poids de 18,9 kg), associée à une puissance de sortie de 2 400 W. Deux poignées latérales facilitent son transport, avec un poids équivalent à celui d’un micro-ondes selon Anker. Pour le Black Friday, l’Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 passe à 949,99 € au lieu de 1 499,99 € chez Anker.
La C2000 Gen 2 peut ainsi alimenter plusieurs appareils simultanément, que ce soit à la maison ou aussi dans un atelier ou même lors d’un séjour en camping-car.
Elle dispose notamment de cinq prises secteur, de ports USB-C (pouvant délivrer jusqu’à 140 W) et d’une fonction de basculement automatique en alimentation de secours en 10 ms. Elle peut également être rechargée par panneaux solaires ou via un alternateur compatible. Sa capacité peut être portée à 4 kWh avec une batterie additionnelle.
Et pour ceux qui recherchent un format plus compact, la C1000 Gen 2 est également en promotion à 499,99 € au lieu de 999 € (soit une remise de 50 % !). Elle embarque 1 024 Wh de capacité et délivre jusqu’à 2 000 W de puissance (pour un poids de seulement 11,3 kg).
Anker SOLIX S2000 : une réserve d’énergie pour les imprévus
Dernière possibilité avec la S2000, une autre station électrique portable (de 16 kg) qui mise sur une capacité de 2 000 Wh, mais dans un format facile à déplacer par une seule personne. Elle délivre jusqu’à 1 500 W de puissance et peut alimenter différents équipements, du réfrigérateur à l’ordinateur en passant par les appareils électroniques du quotidien. Pour le Black Friday, l’Anker SOLIX S2000 passe à 699,99 € au lieu de 1 199,99 € chez Anker.
Elle dispose également d’une fonction ASI (alimentation sans interruption), avec un basculement en moins de 10 ms en cas de coupure électrique. De quoi maintenir certains équipements essentiels en fonctionnement, sans la moindre intervention manuelle. Sa batterie LFP est annoncée pour 6 000 cycles avant de conserver 80 % de sa capacité.
Une solution qui vise à trouver sa place à la maison pour anticiper les imprévus, mais aussi lors de certains déplacements (la prise voiture promet une recharge de 0 à 80 % en 18 heures) qui peuvent nécessiter une alimentation électrique autonome.
Jusqu’au 30 novembre pour profiter des offres Anker SOLIX

articles.title: Japón tiene un problema con el futuro de sus semiconductores. Su respuesta es una fábrica de chips sobre ruedas
articles.text:
Cuando hablamos de fabricar semiconductores, solemos pensar en enormes instalaciones, máquinas de una precisión extraordinaria e inversiones de miles de millones de euros. Pero detrás de todo ese despliegue tecnológico hay algo que no se puede resolver únicamente con dinero: la formación de las personas que deben dominar los procesos de fabricación. Y aprender a fabricar un chip no es precisamente sencillo cuando el acceso a los equipos necesarios con fines educativos es limitado. Japón, que lleva años intentando recuperar protagonismo en esta industria, se enfrenta precisamente a ese desafío.
Una organización japonesa especializada en tecnologías de fabricación de semiconductores ha planteado una solución poco convencional: llevar parte de una fábrica de chips hasta las puertas de las universidades. La Minimal Fab Promoting Organization ha anunciado que mostrará por primera vez su sistema mobileFab entre el 9 y el 11 de diciembre, durante la feria SEMICON Japan 2026, en Tokio. Se trata de una instalación que reúne tres equipos de fabricación en un contenedor transportable en camión, concebida para ofrecer formación práctica tanto en centros educativos como en empresas.
Mientras la taiwanesa TSMC amplía su presencia industrial en Japón y Rapidus aspira a iniciar la producción en masa de chips de 2 nanómetros entre finales de 2027 y principios de 2028, la disponibilidad de personal especializado cobra especial importancia. Una estimación de 2024 de la asociación industrial JEITA apuntaba a que solo nueve empresas del sector en Japón necesitarían alrededor de 43.000 profesionales durante la siguiente década. A ello se suma otra dificultad identificada por el Ministerio de Educación del país, según recoge el comunicado de la organización: la escasez de docentes capacitados para impartir formación práctica en semiconductores.
Una fábrica de chips que va al encuentro de sus futuros ingenieros
Para entender cómo es posible reducir tanto las dimensiones de una instalación de fabricación de semiconductores tenemos que fijarnos en Minimal Fab, una tecnología desarrollada por el Instituto Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología Industrial Avanzada de Japón (AIST). Las obleas, esas láminas de material semiconductor sobre las que se fabrican los circuitos, tienen en este sistema apenas 12,5 milímetros de diámetro, frente a los 300 milímetros habituales en muchas grandes fábricas. Se procesan individualmente en equipos de unos 30 centímetros de anchura que, mediante entornos limpios localizados y sistemas de transporte cerrados, permiten prescindir de una gran sala blanca.
En el interior del contenedor habrá tres máquinas dedicadas a la fotolitografía, una técnica fundamental en la fabricación de chips. La primera aplica una capa de material fotosensible sobre la oblea, la segunda utiliza la luz para proyectar el diseño deseado sin necesidad de una máscara física y la tercera elimina selectivamente partes de ese material mediante el revelado. El resultado es un patrón en la capa fotosensible que servirá de base para operaciones posteriores. Durante la feria de Tokio, la organización prevé realizar demostraciones de este proceso de entre 15 y 20 minutos.
Para hacernos una idea de lo que podrían aprender los estudiantes, podemos fijarnos en dos centros de formación técnica japoneses. El de Sasebo ya utiliza cuatro equipos Minimal Fab en un programa que reúne a alumnos de distintas disciplinas. En Kumamoto, los estudiantes diseñan sus propios circuitos integrados, reciben obleas cuyos transistores han sido fabricados previamente por el AIST, participan en la formación de las interconexiones y evalúan sus características eléctricas. La idea es reproducir esta experiencia con mobileFab, combinando sus equipos con procesos adicionales de grabado y evaluación eléctrica realizados en destino.
Aunque la formación es el objetivo de la instalación móvil, las posibilidades de la tecnología en la que se basa van más allá de las aulas. En 2021, la compañía japonesa Yokogawa Solution Services desarrolló con equipos Minimal Fab un prototipo de unidad aritmético-lógica, un circuito encargado de realizar operaciones matemáticas y lógicas. El trabajo, realizado por encargo de la agencia espacial japonesa (JAXA), buscaba estudiar métodos para garantizar la calidad y la reproducibilidad de los procesos de cara a una posible fabricación de dispositivos para vehículos espaciales en pequeñas cantidades. La compañía verificó el funcionamiento del circuito mediante mediciones con un osciloscopio.
El siguiente objetivo es llevar esta propuesta más allá de la feria de Tokio. Sus responsables esperan comenzar los programas educativos alrededor de abril de 2027 y aseguran haber despertado ya el interés de varias instituciones académicas y empresas. La intención es ampliar las oportunidades de formación práctica en distintas regiones del país, incluidas aquellas donde incorporar equipos propios resulta complicado. Mientras Japón trabaja para recuperar protagonismo en la industria mundial de los semiconductores, una parte de ese esfuerzo podría desarrollarse en lugares tan alejados de las grandes fábricas como las aulas de un centro educativo.

articles.title: AMD AGESA 1.3.0.1f Patch Arrives to Limit Max vCore on Ryzen 8000 Series
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
AMD AGESA 1.3.0.1f Patch Arrives to Limit Max vCore on Ryzen 8000 Series
AMD has quietly released the AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A, which primarily introduces a 1.4 V maximum core voltage limit for select Ryzen 8000-series processors. Motherboard manufacturers are starting to roll out BIOS updates that incorporate this change. Both ASUS and MSI have noted the restriction in their release notes for AM5 motherboards. MSI's MEG X870E GODLIKE X EDITION received BIOS version 2A36 on November 18, which includes AGESA ComboAM5 PI 1.3.0.1f Patch A. The changelog specifically mentions limiting the maximum vCore to 1.4 V for select AMD Ryzen 8000-series CPUs. The update also adds additional POST codes to improve visibility into memory training, making it easier to differentiate between normal initialization activity and a system that has stopped responding.
ASUS has documented the same changes in its latest beta BIOS releases for several AM5 motherboard families, including the X870, X670, B850, and B650 models. This covers its ROG Crosshair, ROG Strix, TUF Gaming, and ProArt product lines. The company also describes a new memory-training sequence where the motherboard's debug display counts from 00 to 09, advancing approximately once per second before resetting to 00 and continuing with the normal boot process. However, the main focus is on limiting the maximum vCore voltage for Ryzen 8000 series CPUs. If you are using an AMD system with Ryzen 8000 series desktop APUs, please check your vendor's BIOS updates.
Sources:
				ASUS, 				MSI, 				via HXL on X

articles.title: Dell and HP beat expectations, but their fortunes are diverging as AI dynamics crush the PC market
articles.text:
Dell and HP beat expectations, but their fortunes are diverging as AI dynamics crush the PC market
Dell Technologies Inc. and HP Inc. delivered strong earnings and revenue beats as they posted their latest financial results today.
However, the companies have very different prospects going forward as they try to come to terms with the diverging fortunes of the artificial intelligence server and personal computer markets they serve.
Dell reported third-quarter adjusted earnings of $9.45 per share on revenue of $54.94 billion, a stunning result that blew past Wall Street’s expectations of just $6.59 per share in earnings and $49.32 billion in sales.
The company’s revenue more than doubled from a year earlier thanks to the sky-high demand for the AI servers and related data center infrastructure equipment it sells. Dell’s Infrastructure Solutions Group delivered sales of $41.97 billion during the quarter, far in excess of the Street’s target of $35.27 billion. Of that, around $22 billion came from direct AI-optimized server sales, the company said. That segment was up 291% annually.
“We are now a different company, with the Infrastructure Solutions Group driving the vast majority of our profit and growth,” said Dell Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke (pictured). He added that Dell now has more than 7,500 customers buying its AI servers.
The Street liked what it saw, with Dell’s stock rising more than 3% after hours, putting the brakes on an 11% decline earlier, during the regular trading session.
Dell’s performance in the quarter sets a new precedent for infrastructure systems companies, said longtime technology industry analyst Dave Vellante, chief analyst at theCUBE Research, SiliconANGLE Media’s sister market research firm.
“Dell has transformed from a PC company into a dominant enterprise infrastructure provider and industry bellwether,” he said. “What’s most astounding to me is that I’ve always considered AWS to be Dell’s most formidable competitor. Dell is now significantly larger than AWS on a trailing 12-month revenue basis and is growing at a rate that’s more than double that of AWS, Azure and on a par with Google Cloud.”
Clarke told analysts on a conference call that the company has a significant competitive advantage over its rivals on the software side, which enables customers to get their servers up and running in data centers within hours of taking delivery of them. “That allows customers to convert backlog into revenue sooner and more reliably,” he added.
Dell is raising its forecast for AI servers in the coming fiscal years, and now sees sales rising to a staggering $78 billion, ahead of the Street’s target of $74 billion. At present, the company has an even bigger order backlog of $132.3 billion for AI servers. “Every order is verified for access to capital, end customer quality, trade and export compliance and access to land and power,” Clarke told analysts in response to a question about the reliability of that backlog.
Vellante said Dell’s operating leverage is just as impressive, with its operating income, net profit and earnings per share all growing at rates over two-times its revenue growth.
“Its massive backlog and strong product execution allow it to be selective,” the analyst said. “Thus the quality of its revenue and its backlog is very high, and the company is well-positioned for the next several quarters. Current market signals point to a structural change in tech where vendors that are in a position to help customers transform and drive new levels of productivity are poised to win over the long term. We increasingly see Dell as one of those leaders.”
Besides servers, Dell still has a big business in the PC market. Its Client Services Group was once the company’s biggest segment, but its revenue is now dwarfed by AI server sales. During the quarter, it generated revenue of $12.89 billion, below the Street’s forecast of $14.33 billion.
The reason for that miss is that the global PC market is currently enduring a sharp decline. Last month, Gartner Inc. reported a stunning 22% drop in global PC shipments in the third quarter, citing the increased costs of components such as memory chips, which have led to higher prices and compelled many people to hold onto their older laptops for longer.
HP’s stock skids as PC reality bites
The miserable state of PC sales makes HP’s latest quarterly results seem even more impressive than they were. However, the company’s cautious outlook suggests that its incoming Chief Executive Emma Walmsley (pictured, right) will have her work cut out when she assumes the role full time on Jan. 4, when she’s slated to take over from interim CEO Bruce Broussard.
HP reported fourth-quarter adjusted earnings of 83 cents per share, surpassing the analyst consensus estimate that called for a profit of just 75 cents per share. Revenue for the period came to $16 billion, up 9% and above the Street’s target of $15.4 billion.
HP’s stock briefly surged more than 17% after-hours, before promptly surrendering all of those gains in under an hour. It was down just under a percentage point at the time of writing.
Investors had low expectations of HP given the shoddy state of the PC market. The company has been trying to mitigate the situation somewhat by raising its prices, but it couldn’t stop its profit margins from declining in the quarter.
The market was eagerly anticipating HP’s guidance to try and get a lid on whether or not the PC market has any prospect of recovery in the near future, but the company disappointed by refusing to provide any. All it would say is that it forecasts free cash flow in the current quarter to be $3 billion, plus or minus $100 million. Analysts are targeting free cash flow of $3.3 billion.
HP hasn’t been helped by the fact that it has been without a CEO since PayPal Holdings Inc. surprisingly swooped in to poach its former leader Enrique Lores in February. Broussard has held the fort for close to nine months now, but the company did at least finally name a successor in Walmsley, who will begin her tenure next year. She formerly led the pharmaceutical giant GSK Plc.
Walmsley has a tough act to follow, however, for Broussard has done rather well in his efforts to cope with the PC market downturn and the higher component costs. Although the stock was up and down today, it’s still up 25% in the year to date.

articles.title: Jensen Huang confessed to more affairs before the board reinstated him as Nvidia CEO, report claims — 'contrite' chief disclosed at least two additional affairs beyond Megaspeed exec and Nvidia's VP of health care
articles.text:
Jensen Huang confessed to more affairs before the board reinstated him as Nvidia CEO, report claims — 'contrite' chief disclosed at least two additional affairs beyond Megaspeed exec and Nvidia's VP of health care
Huang was said to be "contrite" about his behavior, and the board was satisfied after it explained the importance of "candor and honesty" in the future.
Following the news that Nvidia founder Jensen Huang has returned to the company as CEO a little more than a week after he resigned from the role, it's now believed that he admitted to additional extra-marital affairs beyond the two that were already known. The admission came during an hours-long meeting with Huang as Nvidia's board members discussed him potentially coming back to a company he left in disarray when he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. The woman, Alice Huang, worked for Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer that is now under criminal investigation over its possible involvement in the smuggling of export-controlled Nvidia AI chips into China. Now, with Huang back in the top job at Nvidia, a WSJ report claims that the company's board rehired him despite the revelation that his affairs outnumbered the two already reported.
The report details a November 22 meeting in which Huang and the Nvidia board sat down to discuss his return. Huang told the board that there were more affairs than those it already knew about, with people with knowledge of the discussions saying that he was contrite about his behavior. Then, after the board explained to Huang that it was important that he be honest and candid after at least one affair with an Nvidia employee, it was agreed that the best thing for the company would be for Huang to return. Huang has confessed to being unfaithful to his wife, Lori, reportedly carrying on an affair with Megaspeed's Alice Huang and Nvidia's VP of health care, Kimberly Powell. The report explicitly states Huang admitted to multiple further affairs, bringing the total of known instances to at least four.
The company said its board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang. It's unclear whether its decision was affected by Nvidia's 24% stock price fall following Huang's affair scandal first broke. President Trump also stated he heavily lobbied for Huang's return, personally dialling in to an Nvidia board meeting to persuade the company to reinstate him.
“I’m terribly sorry for putting all of you through all of this,” Huang reportedly said in a video of his return to the Nvidia offices. “I’ve made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back.”
Huang's return to Nvidia came after a week of uncertainty for the company. Calls for his return were made by everyone from SpaceX CEO Elon Musk to U.S. President Trump. The latter was very vocal in his stance on Huang and has since taken the credit for Nvidia's decision to reinstate him. This came after he initially called for former Apple CEO Tim Cook to take the reins of the company.
One of Huang's first acts as the returning Nvidia CEO will be to appear before a House Foreign Affairs panel. He'll do so on December 1 to answer questions about his affair with Alice Huang in the context of import-controlled AI chips finding their way into China.
