articles.title: Bambu Lab P3C Review: A more affordable tool changer
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Bambu Lab P3C is the lower-cost little brother of the H3C. It has the same type of tools and outstanding TPU printing process as its larger sibling, but drops the heated chamber, filament dryer, and automatic filament loading. If you want an upgradable tool changer on a more manageable budget, the P3C is a great place to start.
Reasons to buy
- + Excellent TPU solution
- + Super quick color changes
- + Works with multiple materials and nozzle sizes in the same print
- + Works with almost all spool types
- + Hardened steel nozzles
Reasons to avoid
- - Really tall
- - Loading filament is tedious
- - Changing tools is a pain, literally
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Bambu Lab didn’t even tease the arrival of the new P3C, a smaller, more budget-friendly version of the H3C, which retails at roughly half the price. In fact, this post might be the first time you’ve heard more than just a rumor about the tool changer’s mysterious little brother.
The Bambu Lab P3C combo is a tool changer with room for seven tools and a 256 x 256 x 260mm build volume, roughly the same as the P2S. It ships as either a five-tool unit, with two empty slots for later customization, or as a seven-tool “multi-material combo” with six 1.75mm tools and one 2.85mm tool. Bambu is bringing back old school 2.85mm filament in the form of super squishy TPU 75A.
The five-tool unit is priced at $1,149, while the seven-tool is launching at $1,299.
It offers the same excellent TPU printing process for both standard and phat TPU and has quickly joined the select group of send it and forget it printers in my fleet. I’ve had very few failures, even when printing more technical filaments.
The P3C is not quite as tall as the H3C, but it does require almost 4ft (1,212 mm) of vertical space for the AMS lid to fully open. So plan accordingly and have a good space picked out in advance.
Bambu’s most annoying cost-saving measure took the A right out of AMS. There’s no motor of any sort in the AMS 3P, leaving you to manually load and unload the filament all the way to the nozzle. The process takes a long time if you are loading all of the filament slots. The upside of not having powered rollers is that the AMS 3P will run almost any 1kg or smaller spool without issue.
The printer can run different-sized nozzles from .2 mm to .8 mm, and has an optional 2.85 mm TPU filament tool. The FlexFeed extruder with Active Grip Control just pushes whatever filament it’s asked to while changing on the fly. It may be the best extruder I’ve reviewed, however, the printer as a whole is not quite what we need for the best 3D printers of 2026.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Specifications: Bambu Lab P3C
| Header Cell - Column 0 | P3C | H3C | 
|---|---|---|
| Build Volume | 256 x 256 x 260 mm (10.07 x 10.07 x 10.23 inches) | 330 x 320 x 325 mm (12.99 x 12.59 x 12.79 inches) | 
| Material | PLA/TPU/ABS/ASA/PA/PC/PET/Fiber reinforced | PLA/TPU/ABS/ASA/PA/PC/PET/PPS/Fiber reinforced (up to 350 degrees) | 
| Extruder Type | Direct drive | Direct Drive | 
| Nozzle | .4mm | .4 mm | 
| Build Platform | PEI textured spring steel sheet (110 degrees) | PEI textured spring steel sheet (120 degrees) | 
| Bed Leveling | Automatic | Automatic | 
| Filament Runout Sensor | Yes | Yes | 
| Connectivity | WiFi, LAN, USB Stick | WiFi, LAN, USB Stick | 
| Interface | 5-Inch Touch Screen | 5-inch Touch Screen | 
| Machine Footprint | 413 x 538 x 925 mm (16.25 x 21.18 x 36.4 in) | 493 x 571 x 1016 mm (19.40 x 22.48 x 40 inches) | 
| Machine Weight | 26.5 kg (58.42 lbs) | 36.28 KG (79.98 lbs) | 
| MSRP | Five tool - $1,149 Seven tool - $1,299 | $2,499 | 
| Release Date | November 24, 2026 | November 3, 2026 | 
Bambu Lab P3C: Included in the Box
The Bambu Lab P3C comes with five .4mm tools preinstalled in the bottom of the AMS 3P. Also included are a toolkit and cables needed to assemble the printer, along with quick start guides for both the printer and AMS 3P, and a few spare parts. It does not come with a USB memory stick, which is needed for recording time lapses.
We received the multi-material combo for review, which came with five tools installed, plus two additional tools I had to set up myself (one 1.75mm and one 2.85mm), along with several spools of PLA Palette and 2.85mm TPU 75A.
Design of the Bambu Lab P3C
The P3C is missing several perks of the bigger H3C in order to save costs and keep the price reasonable. The most disappointing is the lack of a motor to drive the filament spools. This makes the “A” in the AMS 3P questionable, as you are forced to manually feed the filament all the way to the nozzle, as well as handle retraction when unloading.
The AMS 3P also does not come with a filament drier, although an optional 75C dryer will be available for $159.90.
The basic Bambu Lab P3C comes standard with only five tools and is expandable to seven. The Swaptek system keeps the cooling fans and extruder on the toolhead, with each tool having its own filament path, heater, and a hardened steel nozzle. When printing, the idle tools are preheated, allowing for extremely fast tool swaps.
The nozzles on each tool can be swapped out with different sizes, and multiple sizes can be used in the same print.
Bambu Lab will also release tools for cutting, drawing, debossing, and foil transfer in the future.
The Bambu Lab P3C supports printing TPU with a bypass port on all filament slots except 2 and 6, which allows TPU to skip the tube, reducing friction. If you have the optional 2.85mm tool, you can mount it to any slot with a bypass.
Please note that the 2.85mm tool has a wider filament path – it's not just the nozzle tip that changes dimensions.
The tools dock on a rack in front of the printer which retracts after each tool change, allowing for a clear view of the build plate.
The Flexfeed extruder is impressive. It switches from 1.75mm to 2.85mm filament on the fly and uses what Bambu Lab calls Active Grip Control with feedback from the extruder motor.
Like the H3C, there are magnetic covers on the left and right sides of the AMS and a front cover that attaches in slots to allow easy access to the chamber for maintenance. The front cover is a bit tricky, and you need to lift the AMS up to get it free. For this reason, I didn’t bother to secure the AMS to the base of the printer. You really need to remove that front panel to change out the tools.
Changing tools is one of the few frustrating things about the Bambu Lab P3C (or the H3C, as it’s the same process). There is very little room to work, and there are sharp plastic edges that left me bloodied on one occasion. I would suggest picking your favorite configuration and leaving it there if you can.
The AMS is massive and requires a lot of additional vertical space to fully open the lid to get at the spools. Bambu Lab recommends a clearance of 1,212 mm or almost four feet from the base in order to open the lid. Surprisingly, this smaller P3C is only 3.58 inches shorter than the big H3C. With the printer sitting on a standard countertop, a step-stool will be mandatory equipment for most people. Bambu offers a rolling cart for the H3C that puts the printer at a more manageable height, and I would highly recommend getting it for the P3C.
The base unit of the Bambu Lab P3C looks similar to the P and X series printers, with a plastic outer frame and a steel chassis. The build plate is a standard 256 x 256 mm, with 260 mm available on the Z-axis. The P3C does not have active chamber heating, but being enclosed with a max of 300C on the nozzle and 110C on the bed, it has the ability to print many of the more common technical filaments. The chamber is ventilated with HEPA and active carbon filtration.
The 3D printer has a great camera, which is used for AI detection and monitoring using the Bambu Handy app and the device page of Bambu Slicer. The camera can produce time-lapses of your prints but does require a USB memory stick to store them.
Assembling the Bambu Lab P3C
The Bambu Lab P3C and AMS 3P ship in separate boxes but are almost fully assembled. After removing the packaging, there are two screws holding the dock retainers that need to be removed and 6 screws securing the bed in place.
There is a helpful reminder to do this when the printer is first turned on. AMS 3P is mounted on top of the printer and requires a good deal of vertical space. There are four screws to attach the AMS 3P to the printer, but I left these off since the front panel of the AMS is easier to remove when you can tip the AMS back a little.
The individual tools attach to the dock magnetically and must be placed manually, which can take a little fiddling to get used to.
The touch screen attaches to the front of the printer without tools, and the ribbon cable to connect it is just long enough to work.
Leveling the Bambu Lab P3C
The Bambu Lab P3C levels its bed as part of its initial calibration and again at the start of every print. The system works perfectly.
Loading Filament on the Bambu Lab P3C
The Bambu Lab P3C does not have auto-loading, as there is no motor.
When loading multiple new filaments for a print, the process can take a while and is very hands-on. When using normal 1.75 mm filament, the material is pushed into the orange tube in the AMS when called for by the printer.
When using TPU, either 1.75mm or 2.85 filament, drop the filament into a slot with a bypass port in the bottom and drag it by hand to the tool. The normal Bowden tube must be removed from the tool and clipped to the side. When running 1.75mm TPU a short piece of bowden tube must be inserted into the tool to help feed the filament correctly. The 2.85mm TPU doesn’t need the short tube and can feed directly.
The printer has a helpful filament guide to walk you through the loading operation.
Bambu Lab-branded filament with RFID tags will automatically enter the filament type and color. Other brands must be entered manually via the printer’s touchscreen.
Unloading filament is the reverse of loading. You’ll need to manually retract material once it is cut by the printer. There is a batch unloading command that will allow you to wait until all of the selected filaments have been cut.
Preparing Files / Software for Bambu Lab P3C
Bambu Studio is based on PrusaSlicer and its predecessors. New for the P3C and the H3C is the ability to mix different tool sizes. It is one of the best slicers available with good filament mapping, control and print monitoring, with access to Makerworld, Bambu Lab’s file sharing service.
Printing on the Bambu Lab P3C
The P3C does not come with filament samples. Bambu Lab sent a few spools of their new PLA Palette and 2.85mm 75A TPU to try. Be sure to check out our best filaments for 3D printing to fill up your AMS 3P.
This print of Carl and Donut from the Dungeon Crawler Carl book series took 15 hours and 35 minutes to print using a .16mm layer height for smooth detail. I used the default settings, but slowed the outer walls to 65mm/s. The print is exceptionally good, though the supports left a few marks under horizontal areas like the arms and shin. Normally I’d tilt a model this back 45 degrees to save time and support, but the fin on this particular model is vexing and would have added an hour to the print time and another 10g of support.
This is printed in seven colors of PLA, maxing out the P3C slots. Polymaker HT-PLA Pro White, Prusament Galaxy Black and Galaxy Silver PLA, Elegoo PLA Brown and Silk Red, Inland Bone White, and Matterhacker’s Purple MH Build Series PLA.
Printing with seven colors allows you more creative freedom when printing complex models. Though the brown did a lot of heavy lifting on this print, I think the P3C really captured Carl nicely.
I tried some of Bambu Lab’s matte PETG on a Cute Blue Jay from Makerworld. Since the model prints best straight up and down, and requires pretty extensive supports, I used a scrap of Prusa Lipstick Red PLA as an interface layer.
Using a .16mm layer height, the print took 8 hours and 55 minutes running at a little under 100mm/s on average. The matte PETG makes the model look like it was painted. This is printed in black, white and baby blue matte PETG and the supports came off with no residue what so ever.
Though the P3C doesn’t get hot enough to print PPS, it does print most PA, PC, and PET filaments very well. I printed a spool and a half of Sunlu Easy PA, making all of the mechanical parts for two radio-controlled Death Racers. Initially, I made just a few items per plate, but with just a little glue stick, the bed adhesion was so good that I felt comfortable loading up the plates as full as possible and had zero failures. All were printed with a .2mm layer height and slowed to 100mm/s by me in the slicer. Other than a tiny bit of stringing, the parts are perfect mechanically.
The Bambu Lab P3C’s HEPA filter does a good job filtering the stinkier filaments like ABS and ASA. I printed this wire holding vice using Fusion ABS matte ionized cobalt black and Prusa lipstick red ASA.
This is printed with a .2 mm layer height and an average print speed of 120mm/s. The entire print took a little less than 2 hours and 3 minutes, and the parts fit together perfectly.
With the H3C and now the P3C, I have seen the future of printing with TPU. The AMS 3P bypass ports are just the ticket for printing soft materials.
I printed several plates of treads for my RC Death Racer project. Normally, I print these a few at a time to limit the fallout from print failures, but this proved unnecessary. I ran 48 treads in Bambu Lab Cyan 2.85mm TPU 75A and another 48 using Bambu Lab 90A TPU. Both prints used a .2mm layer height and were limited to 100 mm/s in the slicer. The 75A print finished a little quicker at 19 hours 10 minutes, with the 90A filament taking 19 hours and 40 minutes.
Both are terrific prints with no stringing at all and zero failures.
Bottom Line
The P3C can print almost any filament I own beautifully. It lacks a few creature comforts like auto-loading, filament drying (which can be upgraded), and a heated chamber. It’s also tall enough to require a step stool to load those back filament slots.
The Bambu Lab P3C is best for anyone who wants poop-free multicolor, multi-material printing without paying H3C money. I highly recommend it for anyone who plans to print a lot of TPU and doesn’t need that larger build plate. If you can live without the automatic feeding you normally get from a Bambu printer, then the money you’ll save in filament is worth the hassle.
This machine gives you most of the advantages of the Bambu Lab H3C at roughly half the $2,499 price tag. The open-source four-color Snapmaker U1 is still worth it right now while it’s on sale for $699. Another option is the Creality K3, which is another four-color tool changer with a similar build size for $849.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Winbond Widens Edge AI Reach, Certifies NOR Flash
articles.text:
Winbond Electronics is betting that a little less customization will put its 3D-stacked memory architecture into a lot more designs, while expanding its 16-nm DRAM portfolio and adding security certification to NOR flash offerings.
The company’s new CUBE-Lite is a semi-custom memory offering derived from its Customized Ultra Bandwidth Elements (CUBE) platform, which debuted a few years ago. It aims to give edge AI designs CUBE’s bandwidth with lower non-recurring engineering (NRE) costs than a fully customized CUBE design.
“It’s still customized, but it’s more of a ‘standardized’ customized, if that’s not too much of a contradiction,” Brian Watson, marketing manager for Winbond’s customized memory solutions, said in a briefing with EE Times.
CUBE works best for workloads with low-to-medium density requirements but high bandwidth requirements, he said. Rather than replicate high-bandwidth memory’s combination of capacity and bandwidth, Winbond is targeting smaller working sets that still require rapid data movement. “It’s not trying to mimic HBM in terms of both density and bandwidth, but just the bandwidth.”
Watson offered on-device language translation in a wearable as a hypothetical example. The audio-processing working set might be relatively small, but responsiveness requires bandwidth. These types of devices are cost sensitive, he added. “You might not be able to amortize the NRE cost of a fully custom 3D-stacked memory architecture across the number of devices that you’re selling in the unit price of the device.”
CUBE-Lite delivers up to 8 GB/s of memory bandwidth at approximately 70 mW, and Winbond’s engineering data shows the simplified interface can reduce SoC controller power consumption by more than 10× compared with an LPDDR4X implementation.
A full CUBE design is tailored to each customer’s bandwidth, density, power, and SoC requirements. CUBE-Lite instead offers a menu of density and I/O options—Watson used 128, 256, and 512 I/Os as hypothetical examples. “It wouldn’t be fully customized, right, because you would have to select among the available options,” he said. CUBE-Lite also requires the customer to provide a memory controller.
Filling DRAM density gaps
Winbond is also expanding its 16-nm DRAM portfolio with 8-Gb LPDDR4 devices with an x16 interface, 16-Gb LPDDR4 with an x32 interface, and 16-Gb DDR4. The additions fill density gaps and give customers more options across product tiers.
The 16-Gb devices double per-device capacity compared with 8-Gb parts, potentially reducing component counts and board space. DDR4 targets include switches and server peripherals, while LPDDR4 applications include automotive systems, drones, and surveillance equipment. The new 16-Gb products are scheduled for availability by year-end 2026, with mass production planned for the second quarter of 2027.
Securing NOR flash with CRA
Separately, Winbond introduced a Cyber Resilience Act Conformance and Integration Kit for its TrustME W77Q Secure Flash family. The package combines hardware security, software, integration guidance, testing resources, and documentation to support manufacturers’ product-level compliance work.
In a briefing with EE Times, Nir Tasher, VP of technology for Winbond’s secure memory products, said many equipment suppliers lack the security expertise needed to translate regulatory requirements into implementations. Supplying silicon and a data sheet alone does not address that gap, he said.
The W77Q’s SESIP Level 2 certification can help manufacturers document component security, but it does not establish CRA conformity for the finished product, Tasher said.
Instead, the kit maps CRA requirements to Secure Flash features. It also includes sample code, a test suite to verify integration, and the written collateral needed for conformance documentation. “This is like a secret sauce,” Tasher said. “You add that to your system, and you are 90% of the way there.”
Those resources, together with documentation, allow customers to move through conformance work more efficiently, he said.
W77Q has achieved SESIP Level 2 certification, though Winbond notes that this alone doesn’t establish a finished product’s conformity with the CRA. Tasher said other regions, including the U.S. and Japan, could follow the EU’s regulatory approach.
Winbond to absorb Infineon memory business
The trio of product updates follows Winbond’s September agreement to acquire Infineon Technologies’ NOR Flash and F-RAM business in an all-cash transaction valued at $1.12 billion.
Winbond will operate the business as a standalone entity headquartered in Silicon Valley. Infineon will retain its SRAM, HYPERRAM, nvSRAM, and SONOS-based radiation-hardened memory products. Subject to regulatory approvals, the companies are targeting closing in the second half of 2027.
Neither Winbond nor Infineon was willing to discuss the transaction beyond the news release.

articles.title: Cómo recuperar una cuenta de WhatsApp bloqueada y pedir una revisión
articles.text:
Cuando WhatsApp bloquea un número, la aplicación muestra el mensaje “This phone number can’t use WhatsApp” (en español, que ese número no puede usar el servicio) y ofrece una opción para pedir una revisión. Según el Centro de Ayuda de la plataforma, la mayoría de las revisiones se completa en 24 horas.
El botón para apelar aparece en la pantalla de bloqueo de la propia aplicación, tanto en WhatsApp como en WhatsApp Business. Si ese botón no está, la ayuda oficial indica que la sanción es definitiva y no se puede apelar.
Los pasos que describe WhatsApp son dos: tocar la opción “Request review” (pedir revisión) dentro de la aplicación y esperar la notificación con la decisión.
Cada apelación cubre un solo número de teléfono, por lo que escribir a la empresa por otros canales o a través de la cuenta de otro usuario no acelera el trámite ni cambia el resultado, advierte la compañía.
Por qué WhatsApp bloquea una cuenta
WhatsApp suspende cuentas cuando considera que su actividad infringe los términos de servicio, por ejemplo si hay spam, estafas o riesgos para la seguridad de otros usuarios. La empresa detecta los envíos automáticos no deseados con aprendizaje automático y con denuncias de los propios usuarios.
Su guía de uso responsable enumera las prácticas que pueden provocar un bloqueo: enviar mensajes masivos o automáticos, usar listas de contactos que no son propias, insistir con un contacto que pidió que no lo escriban y abusar de las listas de difusión. También figuran la extracción automática de datos de usuarios y el uso de versiones modificadas de la aplicación.
Las listas de difusión merecen una precisión: solo llegan a quienes guardaron el número del remitente. La compañía señala que usarlas con frecuencia puede llevar a que las personas denuncien los mensajes, y que se bloquea a las cuentas denunciadas varias veces.
Otro caso es el del número reciclado. Si la línea es nueva, es posible que el titular anterior haya infringido las normas y que el bloqueo venga de esa cuenta, según la ayuda oficial.
Qué pasa con los chats y qué es un bloqueo temporal
Mientras la cuenta está bloqueada, no se puede acceder al historial de chats ni a las copias de seguridad. Estas solo se recuperan cuando el número se desbloquea. Una vez aprobada la apelación, hay que verificar la cuenta ingresando el número de teléfono para volver a entrar.
El aviso “Temporarily banned” (bloqueado temporalmente) es distinto. Según WhatsApp, puede indicar que la persona usa una versión no oficial de la aplicación o que extrae información de otros usuarios de forma automática. La empresa pide pasar a la aplicación oficial o dejar esa práctica; de lo contrario, la cuenta puede quedar bloqueada para siempre. La ayuda no indica cuánto dura un bloqueo temporal.
Entre las aplicaciones no oficiales, la empresa menciona GB WhatsApp, FM WhatsApp y TM WhatsApp. Su recomendación es desinstalarlas y volver a registrar el número en la aplicación oficial, que se descarga desde el sitio de WhatsApp. Solo el historial creado con la aplicación oficial puede respaldarse de forma segura.
Cómo evitar un nuevo bloqueo
WhatsApp recomienda escribir solo a quienes ya contactaron al usuario o pidieron ser contactados, y compartir el propio número para que los demás inicien la conversación. También pide consentimiento antes de sumar a alguien a un grupo y respetar a quien decide salirse.
En los grupos, los administradores pueden activar la opción de que solo ellos envíen mensajes, lo que reduce los mensajes no deseados. La empresa sugiere además pensarlo dos veces antes de reenviar contenido cuyo origen o veracidad se desconozcan.
La ayuda aclara que ningún servicio de terceros puede bloquear ni desbloquear una cuenta: solo WhatsApp tiene esa facultad. Quien ofrezca quitar un bloqueo a cambio de dinero o de datos no actúa en nombre de la compañía. Estas indicaciones corresponden a las páginas del Centro de Ayuda consultadas en noviembre de 2026.

articles.title: Microsoft declara un "Código Rojo" tras la caída global de 24 horas que afectó a Outlook, Teams y otros servicios
articles.text:
Puede que el pasado 13 de noviembre tuvieras problemas para consultar tu correo electrónico o que algún compañero de trabajo te comentara que Outlook no funcionaba correctamente. Quizás ni siquiera utilices las herramientas de Microsoft, pero es posible que las empresas con las que trabajas o las administraciones con las que realizas trámites sí dependan de ellas. Estamos tan acostumbrados a que estos servicios funcionen que pocas veces nos detenemos a pensar en las consecuencias que puede tener una interrupción.
Lo que sucedió aquel día ha llevado a Microsoft a declarar internamente un "Código Rojo", según ha revelado Reuters tras consultar varios memorandos de la compañía. Se trata de una movilización de máxima prioridad con la que pretende reformar sus procedimientos de ingeniería y su manera de responder a las grandes interrupciones de servicio. Jason Henderson, presidente de M365 Core, reconoció en una comunicación a sus empleados que ningún incidente anterior en la historia de Exchange Online había tenido semejante impacto sobre sus clientes.
La interrupción se prolongó durante 23 horas y 50 minutos, aunque la recuperación de los servicios fue progresiva. El epicentro del problema fue Exchange Online, una plataforma que va mucho más allá del envío y la recepción de correos electrónicos: también proporciona información de la que dependen determinadas funciones de Teams, Copilot y otras herramientas de Microsoft 365. Esta interdependencia ayuda a entender la dimensión del incidente, que también afectó a administraciones públicas de Australia, Japón y Estados Unidos y retrasó la actividad de firmas de negociación financiera.
Una caída que Microsoft no quiere repetir
El origen del fallo se remonta a julio, cuando Microsoft comenzó a desplegar una actualización que introdujo un defecto de Windows en los servidores de red utilizados por Exchange Online. Según el informe técnico de la compañía, el problema permaneció oculto durante meses hasta que coincidieron varias circunstancias: parte de la capacidad de la infraestructura no estaba disponible debido a operaciones rutinarias, una incidencia de enrutamiento en Teams obligó a redistribuir tráfico y la demanda aumentó con el inicio de la jornada laboral en Estados Unidos. Microsoft ha descartado que el incidente estuviera relacionado con un ciberataque o con agentes de inteligencia artificial.
Lo que vino después pone de manifiesto la complejidad de gestionar una infraestructura de estas dimensiones. Cuando los servidores comenzaron a fallar, los sistemas automáticos de gestión del tráfico desviaron las conexiones hacia otros que todavía funcionaban, pero la carga adicional también acabó saturándolos. En el peor momento del incidente, más del 80% de los servidores de la infraestructura de pasarelas de red afectada en Norteamérica habían dejado de responder. La redistribución del tráfico hacia otras regiones cuyos servidores presentaban el mismo defecto contribuyó a que el problema alcanzara una dimensión global en unas dos horas.
Dado que aplicar la corrección exigía reiniciar dos veces los servidores afectados, y las dificultades no fueron exclusivamente técnicas. Amanda Silver, vicepresidenta corporativa de Microsoft, explicó en uno de los memorandos consultados por Reuters que los equipos intercambiaron más de 11.000 mensajes repartidos entre 11 chats de Teams durante la gestión de la crisis. Pese a haber movilizado a algunos de sus mejores ingenieros, la dispersión de los datos de diagnóstico entre diferentes sistemas internos dificultó mantener una visión conjunta de las hipótesis que se estaban investigando y las decisiones que se iban tomando.
La respuesta contempla medidas a corto plazo y cambios de mayor calado. Microsoft asegura haber corregido el defecto, haber implementado protecciones temporales contra fallos en cascada y no haber identificado pérdidas permanentes de correos electrónicos empresariales. La compañía prevé modificar la distribución del tráfico entre regiones antes de que termine 2026 y separar determinadas cargas de trabajo durante el primer trimestre de 2027 para limitar la propagación de futuros fallos. Los documentos consultados por la agencia también recogen planes para incorporar agentes de IA que faciliten el diagnóstico y establecer reuniones diarias de seguimiento con responsables de ingeniería.
Una hora es el tiempo en el que Microsoft aspira a resolver futuros incidentes de Microsoft 365 a escala mundial. La compañía también quiere acelerar el despliegue de sus correcciones más urgentes: Henderson reconocía en otro memorando interno que, en una incidencia reciente, distribuir una de ellas por todo el mundo había requerido entre cinco y seis días. Son dos procesos distintos, pero ambos ilustran la necesidad de mejorar su capacidad de respuesta. Para las organizaciones que han confiado parte de sus operaciones a esta infraestructura, tan importante como prevenir una caída es limitar sus consecuencias cuando se produce.

articles.title: Un mois après le casse du siècle, les hackers de Binance accélèrent : 247 millions de dollars déjà blanchis
articles.text:
Fin du mois d’octobre, des pirates ont dérobé 6,43 milliards de dollars de cryptomonnaies à Binance, la principale plateforme d’échange crypto au monde. Le FBI a rapidement accusé la Corée du Nord de la cyberattaque, décrite comme le plus gros vol de l’histoire des cryptos. Depuis leur coup d’éclat, les pirates s’activent pour brouiller les pistes et disparaître dans les méandres de la blockchain. Dans cette optique, les cybercriminels ont notamment créé leurs propres « memecoins », ce qui leur a permis de blanchir des millions de dollars. Désormais, ils passent à la vitesse supérieure.
247 millions de dollars déjà « mélangés »
Selon Elliptic, une société spécialisée dans l’analyse des blockchains, au moins 3 930 bitcoins, soit environ 247 millions de dollars, ont été transférés dans des « coinjoins », des mélanges de bitcoins issus de plusieurs utilisateurs. La tactique consiste à mélanger les bitcoins de nombreux utilisateurs dans une seule transaction. Une fois sortis, il devient presque impossible de savoir d’où ils viennent et de les suivre à la trace. Les hackers nord-coréens se servent de ces bitcoins mélangés pour échapper aux autorités et aux chercheurs.
L’essentiel des bitcoins volés sont passés par Kruw, le service de mélange de cryptos le plus utilisé de Wasabi Wallet, un logiciel gratuit. Le rythme du blanchiment s’est emballé le 17 novembre 2026. En l’espace d’un seul jour, les pirates ont déplacé 488 000 ethers, soit environ 840 millions de dollars, par le biais du mélangeur. Ces ethers ont d’abord été progressivement convertis en bitcoins grâce à Thorchain, un service d’échange automatique entre cryptomonnaies, sans contrôle d’identité. Ils ont ensuite été envoyés à des mélangeurs, souvent en quelques heures. C’est la même méthode que celle utilisée par la Corée du Nord après le piratage de Bybit, début 2025.
Plus de 27 000 portefeuilles, au moins 16 blockchains, une cinquantaine de services et environ 90 000 transactions sont impliqués dans l’opération, qui est « clairement automatisée », indique Elliptic. Pour Tom Robinson, cofondateur d’Elliptic, les fonds ont été probablement confiés à des réseaux de blanchiment basés en Chine, comme lors de précédents vols nord-coréens.
Le gros du butin n’a pas encore disparu. Selon les chercheurs d’Elliptic, 2,85 milliards de dollars ont été saisis avant qu’il ne soit trop tard, tandis qu’environ 2,22 milliards de dollars dorment encore sur des adresses détenues par les pirates. Seuls 247 millions de dollars sont déjà passés par les mélangeurs sous le contrôle des hackers nord-coréens. Pour la Corée du Nord, l’étape la plus risquée est encore à venir. Pour transformer les cryptos en argent fiduciaire, elle devra passer par des courtiers spécialisés, dans les mois qui viennent. C’est à ce moment-là que les fonds pourront encore être interceptés.
La justice tente de bloquer le butin
Tandis que les truands accélèrent les choses, le ministère de la Justice américain a organisé une riposte. Les États-Unis ont lancé une procédure qui doit permettre de saisir plus de 1,1 milliard de dollars d’USDC, la cryptomonnaie émise par Circle, et adossée sur le cours du dollar. Brett Leatherman, agent du FBI, assure que la « Corée du Nord dépend de techniques de blanchiment sophistiquées pour convertir les cryptos volées en fonds qui financent les activités illicites du régime ».
« Les pirates nord-coréens ont volé plus de 6 milliards de dollars à Binance, mais une coordination rapide entre le gouvernement et le secteur privé a permis d’empêcher la disparition d’une part importante de ces fonds », explique A. Tysen Duva, chargé de la division criminelle du ministère.
 Today, the Justice Department announced actions taken to forfeit over $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency that was criminally obtained by North Korean actors from Binance last month. This is part of the greater government effort to assist Binance in recovering over $6 billion in stolen assets. To date, the U.S. has assisted in the freezing, seizing, and/or the return of over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency from multiple sources since the theft from Binance.
“This forfeiture action is the latest example of our efforts to combat the North Korean government’s attempts to profit from the injustices it repeatedly inflicts upon innocent victims.” -Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General M. Scott Proctor
Read more: https://t.co/CGpDNrGMU4
— National Security Division, U.S. Dept of Justice (@DOJNatSec) November 23, 2026
Suite à la demande de la justice, Circle a gelé les fonds, mais n’a pas « la capacité technique de les transférer », explique le ministère. L’entreprise propose donc d’émettre l’équivalent des cryptos volées en nouveaux jetons, une fois la saisie validée par la justice. En d’autres termes, la course qui oppose les cybercriminels nord-coréens aux autorités continue de battre son plein.
 Today, the FBI joined DOJ, USSS, and IRS to announce actions taken to forfeit over $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency that was stolen from Binance in October. Efforts to trace, freeze, seize, and forfeit the stolen assets are ongoing. To date, collective U.S. government and private sector efforts have resulted in the freezing, seizing, and/or return of over $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency.

articles.title: Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to exit after over 11 years
articles.text:
Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy to exit after over 11 years
Under Krishnamurthy’s leadership, Flipkart grew more than fivefold and strengthened its position in India’s ecommerce market. The company is now preparing for a leadership transition.
Flipkart CEO Kalyan Krishnamurthy is set to step down after more than 11 years with the e-commerce company. His departure marks the end of a decade-long leadership stint during which the business grew more than fivefold.
The company announced on Wednesday that Krishnamurthy is concluding his tenure, adding that a successor will be announced in the coming weeks.
In the interim, Balaji Thiagarajan, currently Flipkart’s Chief Product and Technology Officer, and the company’s board will lead the organisation.
During Krishnamurthy’s leadership, Flipkart strengthened its position in India’s ecommerce market, expanded its reach across the country, and introduced several innovations for consumers and sellers. The company also established its Big Billion Days sale as a major fixture of India’s festive shopping season.
“It has been a privilege to be part of Flipkart’s journey. I am proud of the scale of the business we have built, but equally proud of how we have built it. Strong ethics, integrity and high standards of governance have been central to Flipkart’s growth,” said Krishnamurthy in a statement.
He added that the company had helped transform how millions of Indians shop while creating opportunities for sellers, entrepreneurs and businesses across the country.
Commenting on his departure, Chris Nicholas, President and CEO of Walmart International, said, “Both Flipkart and Walmart are better because of Kalyan. We are grateful for his leadership, the governance he instilled, and his many contributions to the company. We wish him nothing but the best as he moves on to his next adventure.”
Flipkart's parent Walmart reiterated its commitment to the ecommerce business and its long-term prospects in India. The company said Flipkart continues to have a strong market position and significant growth opportunities.
Established in 2007, Flipkart has expanded into a digital commerce group that includes Myntra, Flipkart Wholesale, Cleartrip, and super.money. The company said its platform has more than 500 million registered users and over 1.4 million sellers, including Shopsy sellers. Its marketplace offers more than 150 million products across over 80 categories.
Krishnamurthy’s departure comes as India's ecommerce market continues to evolve, with competition intensifying across online retail and quick commerce. Flipkart has been expanding its services and strengthening its position against rivals, including Amazon and emerging digital commerce platforms.
The company did not disclose Krishnamurthy’s next plans.

articles.title: IA : Anthropic chute déjà sous son prix d’introduction en Bourse !
articles.text:
L'arrivée d'Anthropic à la Bourse devait être la consécration du nouveau marché de l'intelligence artificielle. Pourtant, cinq jours après, le soufflé semble déjà retomber.
Après plusieurs années à travailler en mode start-up, les géants de l'intelligence artificielle doivent passer une nouvelle étape avec l'arrivée en Bourse, qui représente une sorte de test grandeur nature de leur rentabilité. Anthropic est la première firme 100% IA - SpaceX ayant d'autres activités - à passer ce test, avec une IPO en date du 19 novembre. Et l'enthousiasme s'est essouflé extrêmement rapidement.
Anthropic tombe pour la première fois sous les 80 dollars
Quand Anthropic arrive en Bourse, son cours de lancement est de 83 dollars. Un cours que l'action a tout de suite quitté, avec une première journée pleine d'enthousiasme, dépassant même brièvement le plafond des 100 dollars.
Mais depuis, il n'a fait que baisser, ce qui pouvait être attendu vu comment fonctionner les introductions en Bourse. Sauf que l'action d'Anthropic a tellement baissé qu'elle est finalement passée aujourd'hui sous les 83 dollars, et même, à l'heure où cet article est écrit, sous les 80 dollars !
L'effet retour de Jensen Huang déjà fini ?
Il faut rappeler que cette opération s'inscrit dans un climat politique particulier, dans lesquels les data centers sont de plus en plus décriés partout dans le monde, et plus encore aux États-Unis - où la nouvelle majorité démocrate au Congrès devrait en faire un cheval de bataille politique.
« Si nous constatons un ralentissement dans le développement des centres de données, cela pourrait évidemment avoir un impact sur le rythme de développement d'Anthropic, et par conséquent sur son chiffre d'affaires futur ainsi que sur sa valorisation » a ainsi commenté l'analyste de marché senior chez StoneX, Fiona Cincotta.
Ce passage sous la barre des 83 dollars se fait par ailleurs le lendemain du retour de Jensen Huang à la tête de NVIDIA, retour qui avait fait exploser son cours à la hausse… avant de voir celui-ci repartir à la baisse aujourd'hui. Le marché semble ainsi montrer qu'il est dorénavant plus exigeant sur la rentabilité des technologies d'IA.
Source : Reuters

articles.title: Cómo bloquear apps en Android con huella o PIN: tres opciones y lo que llega con Android 17
articles.text:
Android permite proteger aplicaciones individuales con huella, rostro, PIN, patrón o contraseña por tres vías: el espacio privado de Android 15 o posterior, la Carpeta Segura de Samsung y, desde noviembre, una función nativa de bloqueo de apps que Google prueba en sus teléfonos Pixel y que Samsung incluyó en una versión beta.
Cada opción protege de forma distinta. Esta guía detalla los pasos según la ayuda oficial de Google y de Samsung, y explica qué se sabe de la novedad que Google prepara para Android 17.
Espacio privado: la opción de Google disponible hoy
El espacio privado es una zona separada del teléfono para esconder aplicaciones. Según la ayuda de Android, requiere Android 15 o superior y no funciona en dispositivos administrados por una empresa, en usuarios secundarios ni en equipos con más de cuatro usuarios o perfiles.
Para configurarlo, hay que abrir Ajustes, tocar Seguridad y privacidad y, en el apartado Privacidad, elegir Espacio privado. El sistema pide autenticarse con el bloqueo de pantalla. Luego se toca Configurar, se decide si se inicia sesión con una cuenta de Google y se elige el bloqueo: el mismo de la pantalla o uno nuevo, con huella, PIN, patrón o contraseña.
Google recomienda usar una cuenta distinta para ese espacio. Si se usa la misma que en el resto del teléfono, parte de los datos, como fotos sincronizadas, contactos o historial de descargas, queda disponible fuera del espacio privado.
Con el espacio bloqueado, sus aplicaciones se detienen por completo: no envían notificaciones y desaparecen del lanzador, de las apps recientes y de la búsqueda. La ayuda advierte que no conviene guardar ahí apps que deban funcionar en segundo plano, como las de seguimiento de salud. Para instalar una app, se abre el espacio y se toca Instalar.
Google también reconoce límites: la existencia del espacio privado puede detectarse mediante conexión a una computadora, registros del dispositivo u otras aplicaciones, y algunos lanzadores no lo admiten. Para borrarlo, hay que autenticarse con su bloqueo; las apps y sus datos se eliminan sin copia de seguridad.
Carpeta Segura en los Galaxy de Samsung
En los teléfonos Samsung Galaxy compatibles, la ayuda de la empresa indica abrir Ajustes, entrar en Seguridad y privacidad, luego en Más ajustes de seguridad y tocar Carpeta Segura. Hay que aceptar los permisos, iniciar sesión con la cuenta de Samsung si se solicita y definir un PIN, una contraseña o un patrón.
Samsung aconseja activar la opción de restablecer con la cuenta de Samsung. Sin ella, quien olvide la clave no podrá recuperar el acceso y solo podrá eliminar la carpeta y crear otra.
Después se toca el signo más para agregar aplicaciones. Lo que aparece dentro es una copia de la app. Los archivos se mueven desde la Galería con la opción Mover a Carpeta Segura. Para ocultar el ícono, se desliza con dos dedos el panel de ajustes rápidos y se toca Carpeta Segura. El huella digital puede habilitarse en equipos compatibles.
Android 17 suma un bloqueo de apps propio
La función nativa de bloqueo apareció en agosto en una versión beta de Android 17 para Pixel, según 9to5Google. Google la retiró para pulirla y la devolvió en octubre en la beta 3 de la actualización trimestral QPR3. El 18 de noviembre, Samsung la incluyó también en la beta de One UI 9.5.
Para usarla, se mantiene presionado el ícono de una app, se toca Bloqueo de apps (App lock en la versión en inglés) y se confirma con huella u otro método. La lista completa se administra en Ajustes, Seguridad y privacidad. Una vez bloqueada, la app oculta el contenido de las notificaciones, quita sus widgets y accesos directos y esconde su vista previa en las apps recientes.
A diferencia del espacio privado, no aísla los datos. Medios digitales señalan que los agentes de IA y servicios a los que el usuario dio permiso antes pueden seguir leyendo la información de la app bloqueada. Además, usa la clave del teléfono: no admite un PIN propio para cada aplicación.

articles.title: Noté 5/5, ce chargeur Anker tombe à 59,99 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le chargeur Anker Zolo 140 W "5 étoiles" à 59,99 € (-33%)
Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, le chargeur Anker Zolo 140 W permet d'alimenter plusieurs appareils en même temps grâce à sa connectique complète et son écran de contrôle. Le Black Friday 2026 fait descendre son prix à 59,99 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 33 % et 30,00 € d'économie.
L'Anker Zolo 140 W s'adresse à ceux qui cherchent à alimenter tous leurs appareils électroniques avec un unique boîtier. Conçu pour centraliser l'alimentation sur un bureau, ce modèle mise sur plusieurs connecteurs et intègre un afficheur numérique pour surveiller la charge en temps réel. Ce chargeur avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage aux tests.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'Anker Zolo 140 W descend à 59,99 € chez Amazon Marketplace, soit environ 33 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (89,99 €). Cela représente une économie de 30,00 € sur cet accessoire.
Quatre sorties et 140 W sous le contrôle d'un écran
Avec une puissance maximale de 140 W, ce bloc délivre suffisamment d'énergie pour recharger rapidement des ordinateurs portables et des smartphones en simultané. L'Anker Zolo 140 W réunit trois ports USB-C et un port USB-A, ce qui permet de brancher quatre terminaux en même temps sans devoir jongler avec plusieurs adaptateurs secteur. Comme souligné dans notre test complet, son écran de contrôle en façade affiche directement le statut et la puissance délivrée à chaque produit relié, offrant une visibilité directe sur la vitesse de charge effective.
Anker Zolo 140 W
Points forts
- Connectique complète.
- Écran de contrôle.
- De la puissance.
- Rendement convenable.
Points faibles
- Poids élevé.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Un format sédentaire pensé pour rester sur le bureau
Ce chargeur assure un rendement convenable et prend en charge les protocoles actuels comme le Power Delivery 3.1 pour maximiser la compatibilité avec vos équipements. Le principal bémol relevé par le laboratoire concerne son poids élevé, qui le destine naturellement à rester branché à poste fixe près d'un espace de travail plutôt qu'à voyager régulièrement dans un sac.
Anker Nano II 65 W : l'autre option face au Anker Zolo 140 W
Le Nano II 65 W mise sur un gabarit très compact taillé pour les déplacements réguliers, là où le Zolo 140 W privilégie la puissance brute et un afficheur pour une installation fixe. Ce modèle nomade fournit 65 W via trois connecteurs, une réserve d'énergie suffisante pour un usage mobile classique.
Le Nano II 65 W coûte 40,24 € de moins que le Zolo 140 W, mais l'Anker Zolo 140 W garde l'avantage d'une puissance totale de 140 W et de quatre ports pour alimenter tout un bureau.
Anker Nano II 65 W
Points forts
- Compatibilité avec de multiples protocoles.
- Trois connecteurs.
- Faible encombrement.
Points faibles
- Rendement encore perfectible.

articles.title: Yale's Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a 'detriment' to US industrial might — not a champion
articles.text:
Investors cheered Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, but renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale thinks they’re celebrating a mistake. He sees a company that is largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher. Far from a champion of American industry, he says, Nvidia is “a detriment to U.S. global industrial might.”
As evidence, Sonnenfeld points to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open source AI models are, in a sense, copies of top U.S. labs’ work, even as Nvidia has insisted that smuggling is a “non-factor.”
Indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with just as much enthusiasm in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily.
The reinstatement itself followed heavy pressure from Washington. Nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out Huang’s return just last week. Then, in a torrent of private weekend calls led by Vice President JD Vance, top administration officials leaned on the board to welcome Huang back, with President Trump calling the board directly to vouch for him. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC on Monday.
Sonnenfeld says the directors who went along, and who returned Huang to the board even as it investigates whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted him, now face a “historic level of individual liability.”
The legal deluge has already begun. As we noted a couple of weeks ago, a potential class-action lawsuit was filed almost immediately. Days later, a shareholder derivative suit followed. Filed on Nvidia’s behalf against the directors themselves, the suit alleges the board ignored red flags about Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.
The class action is very much aimed at making Nvidia and Huang compensate investors for their losses, while the derivative suit puts the directors’ own behavior on trial, with any recovery going to Nvidia. Three more suits followed on November 18, the day after Nvidia’s most recent earnings call; all five were filed in Northern California, where Nvidia is based.
Huang and Nvidia are also juggling a Justice Department antitrust investigation, a reported SEC probe into Nvidia’s accounting, a possible FBI review, a California subpoena, an export-control case that landed partner Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist on Monday, and congressional inquiries, including a Senate Banking hearing next week at which Huang has agreed to testify.
Here’s more of what Sonnenfeld had to say, in a Q&A that’s been edited for length and clarity.
So much has happened since we last talked. Huang was ousted, he’s come back. Do you think the board’s reliance on government assurances here is defensible or an abdication of its own duties?
They failed to rely on experts. That’s one of the reasons this board is going to be sued and lose, and these directors are likely to face a historic level of individual liability. They have a very inadequate directors and officers liability policy. They have also just failed in their diligence. They hired the Wachtell [law] firm. The Wachtell firm barely got off the blocks to do an investigation. And then they have already reversed themselves, so they didn’t use the expertise needed.
It’s wild that they also put Huang right back on the board of directors.
The board showed, in addition to incompetence and collaboration, just cowardice in their capitulation because Trump has nothing to wave over them. If this was SpaceX, where 46% of its business comes from the government [you could maybe see the case for Trump’s involvement]. For Nvidia, it’s not even 1% of its business that comes from the U.S. government, so [the board] didn’t have that threat. [Trump] can call off [federal] investigations, but he can’t call off the shareholder litigation. Some are already filed, and the estimates are there’ll probably be 30 of them, and they’re going to be extremely costly.
And this is not, by the way, just a blue or red state issue. We already have 14 GOP senators who’ve already come out against this, and very prominent conservatives, like Pete Ricketts and Josh Hawley and Tom Cotton and John Cornyn. Those are some issues that may help explain why Nvidia’s stock is tumbling today.
Might the board say, “We saw the classified intelligence findings, and they assure us Jensen will be absolved of wrongdoing”?
They haven’t seen those findings, and we also haven’t seen what will be the result of the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate Special Committee on Investigations, the Senate Banking Committee, and all their House counterparts. The board hasn’t seen any of that, and even if they saw it, which they have not yet, that still wouldn’t matter.
Do you think the Commerce Department will continue to tighten its chip export controls to keep China from accessing so much compute or walk back some of those recent moves?
We already see that Megaspeed has finally been put on the sanctions list, as it should have been before. And we have documentation now that Nvidia, rather than a champion of U.S. global industrial might, is actually a detriment to U.S. global industrial might, because their chips have now turned out to be in the hands and in the systems of not just the Chinese military, as they got channeled to Northwestern Polytechnical University, which is a military institution — this is going into weapons that will, of course, be funneled to Iran and Russia, and they didn’t have access to that a year ago. [Editor’s note: China has long denied supplying weapons to either country. Nvidia chips have been found in Russian drones, however, and the U.S. ambassador to China said in September that President Trump had discussed selling arms to China, an account Trump has denied.]
The open source models that people have celebrated and marveled at — that China somehow has this ingenuity to be creating their own chips, so that Kimi and DeepSeek and these other celebrated open source models were producing a miracle of Anthropic-like results — turns out we know why. They are pirating it. They are “distilling it” from Anthropic using high-end Nvidia chips.
Nvidia has denied reports that its most advanced chips have been smuggled into China.
There’s an Israeli company, Lava, that just three weeks ago showed [dozens of] Blackwell chips are in China. We’re seeing, with the return of Jensen Huang, Anthropic plummet. Why would that be? Of course, this is because it’s hurting OpenAI. It’s hurting Grok. It’s hurting Perplexity. It’s hurting Gemini. And you’ve seen none of these tech titans celebrate this. We have the misogynist tech bros holding locker-room-type rallies about Jensen Huang’s return, but nobody else has spoken out in favor of this. [You’re not hearing from] the CEOs of Microsoft or IBM or J.P. Morgan or Walmart or General Motors or Caterpillar. Nobody thinks that this is a good move.
You don’t think Nvidia needed Huang back?
He was not the guy designing the chips. It’s important to point out that that’s a guy named Chris Malachowsky, a co-founder who’s still there who designed these GPUs and has a whole team of next-generation people like Jonah Alben doing the chip design. As for the great software that has leveraged these chips, that’s also not Jensen Huang. That’s a guy named Ian Buck, who’s been very much celebrated in the last two weeks. He’s the one who designed the CUDA software that leverages the chips. Those people weren’t going anywhere, and wherever Jensen Huang is has nothing to do with them.
Some are trying to make Huang’s forced resignation about the extramarital affairs to which he has admitted, calling it HR policy gone wild.
A CEO who doesn’t stand by his own code of conduct makes it completely unenforceable.
Wired quoted an Nvidia employee who said they’d never take an HR training course again if Huang was reinstated.
This thing is a sexual affair with a subordinate — whether it’s coercion, or even if it truly was somehow consensual, it’s not fair. Every decision on resource allocation, on staffing, on product decisions, is not objective. It’s either favoritism, or, if the relationship fails, retribution. All the other people on that team rise and fall with a sexual relationship; it’s something they have no control over.

articles.title: Anthropic's Siren tests whether Claude models will break out of an insecure sandbox
articles.text:
Anthropic’s Siren tests whether Claude models will break out of an insecure sandbox
Researchers at artificial intelligence developer Anthropic PBC today published details on Siren, a new evaluation that tests whether AI agents will break out of an insecure sandbox to get at something that would help them complete a task.
The researchers found that recent Claude models will reach outside the sandbox in about a fifth to a third of Siren’s test scenarios, though they are far less likely than earlier models to then make misaligned use of what they find.
Siren has been part of Anthropic’s system cards since the release of Claude Haiku 5.5 in October, with the company also using it as one input when deciding whether to deploy new models.
Siren includes 26 sandbox environments built from five common setups, such as bubblewrap jails, Docker containers and small virtual machines emulated with QEMU. Because they show up most often in public reports of sandbox escapes, misconfigurations make up most of the weaknesses planted in the environments.
While the model works on a routine DevOps task, a honeypot such as a credential or file that would help it finish the job is placed outside the sandbox. What Anthropic calls “tempters” are then layered on top to make the honeypot harder to resist. None of the tempters gives the model permission to leave the sandbox, according to the company.
Across Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5 and Mythos 5.2, misaligned use came in at 0.6% to 1.6% of scenarios. Anthropic defines that as using the outside material in a way no reasonable reading of the scenario allows.
The earlier Mythos 5.1 and Mythos 5 models were much higher, at 12.7% and 25.8%. According to Anthropic, Siren’s rates are not an estimate of real-world use, since the evaluation is designed to make the behavior easy to measure. All of the models were also tested without the safeguards that ship with its released models.
Along with Siren itself, Anthropic detailed three ways to make an escape less likely. Adding a short description of the sandbox to the system prompt, including six rules for staying inside it and an instruction to stop if a task needs something the model was not given, made each model 68% to 96% less likely to reach outside. Giving the model a tool to report sandbox weaknesses to the people who run the sandbox also helped, cutting the rate of reaching outside by 7 to 33 percentage points.
Anthropic also put auto mode, a feature in many of its products that uses a classifier to check tool calls before they run, through an offline replay of the Siren episodes. Auto mode blocked the first command that read the honeypot in 96% to 100% of misaligned uses, though the company cautions that it tuned the classifier’s rules on those same episodes.
With all three mitigations running, misaligned use fell to zero in five of the six models tested, with Mythos 5 at 0.1%. The tradeoff was that two models completed about nine percentage points fewer of the tasks that could be finished inside the sandbox. According to Anthropic, none of the mitigations fixes the sandbox itself.
The research follows Anthropic’s disclosure in July that three Claude models had gained unauthorized access to the systems of three organizations while being run through cybersecurity evaluations. The company blamed a misconfigured evaluation environment that had been left with live internet access.
Brian Soby, co-founder and chief executive of AI agent supervision startup Pretxt Inc., which launched last week with $5 million in seed funding, told SiliconANGLE that Siren is “an attempt to harden sandboxes, but that is ultimately a flawed protection approach.”
“Sandboxes attempt to contain the impact of a misaligned model. But misalignment is the core issue,” Soby said. “Increasingly clever models have repeatedly demonstrated the ineffectiveness of the sandboxing concept and the serious consequences of relying on containment to overcome fundamental misalignment.”
Soby likened sandboxing to “prison labor,” in which low trust means stripping workers of most of their capabilities and access. A far more effective approach, he said, is active supervision that keeps agents aligned with their role and an organization’s rules.

articles.title: Plaud Note Pro AI voice recorder hits all-time low of $150 for Black Friday
articles.text:
Plaud's pocket-sized Note Pro AI voice recorder is built for the moments you miss in meetings — now at its lowest ever price
An easier option for meeting notes and interview transcripts
We've had some excellent experiences with Plaud's line of business voice recorders - they turned our reviewer from transcription sceptic to die-hard fan.
So, I was pleased to see that the Plaud Note Pro has dropped to its lowest ever price of $150 (was $189) at Amazon for Black Friday.
The Plaud Note Pro can save you loads of time by recording notes from your meetings and interviews - so you get all of the detail you need without the pain of manual transcription.
The pocket-sized Plaud Note Pro measures just 0.12 inches, weighing in at 1.06 oz. The package includes the transcription device, a magnetic case and ring, charging cable, and a free Starter Plan with 300 transcription minutes per month.
Why we recommend the Plaud Note Pro
This slim, 30g recorder attaches magnetically to your smartphone and captures meetings, interviews, and phone calls. It’s got four microphones, it comes with 64GB of storage, and it’s got a built-in AMOLED display - so it represents an impressive next step when compared to the original Plaud Note device.
Once recordings are transferred to the Plaud app, its AI can produce transcripts, summaries, meeting minutes, action points, and mind maps based on your conversations.
The app supports over 100 languages, and if you switch to endurance recording mode, you should get 50 hours of battery life from the Note Pro.
We awarded the original Plaud Note 5 stars in our review, praising its simple operation and impressive transcription and summarisation. Bear in mind, though, that you’ll need to upgrade to a Pro plan if you want to record more meetings.
Price context and history
This is the lowest price the Plaud Note Pro has been at Amazon - beating a previous low of $160. So, a genuine Black Friday deal here, and a worthwhile discount on a useful productivity tool.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy it if… you want to accelerate how quickly you get transcripts and notes from your meetings
❌ Skip it if… you don’t want to pay an ongoing subscription cost or you don’t need to record many conversations

articles.title: UAE's Sooner raises $20 million to expand home financing solutions
articles.text:
UAE's Sooner raises $20 million to expand home financing solutions
- UAE-based fintech startup Sooner has secured $20 million in seed funding, comprising $5 million in equity led by Nuwa Capital, with participation from 500 Global, Annex Investments, Plus VC, Serkal Group, Axeed Group, 21Ventures, Iliad Partners and angel investors, alongside a $15 million Shariah-compliant debt facility from Amwal Capital Partners.
- Founded in 2026 by Mohammed Aziz, Gabriel García Leyva and Vlad Cherevkov, Sooner operates a down payment support platform licensed by the Dubai Land Department, enabling first-time homebuyers to pay 10% instead of 20% upfront on eligible properties, with the remaining down payment spread over 60 equal Shariah-compliant monthly instalments.
- The funding will give Sooner the capacity to support AED 1 billion ($272 million) in home purchases in 2027. The company also plans to launch a Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) product next year, enabling existing homeowners to access financing against their property equity, alongside plans for regional and international expansion.
Press release:
Sooner, the UAE's first down payment support platform, has announced a $20 million seed round. First-time homebuyers in Dubai usually have to pay a 20% down payment plus 7 to 10% in closing fees in cash upfront. This changes with Sooner, which is licensed by the Dubai Land Department, with buyers having to put down 10% instead of 20% with the rest paid monthly over five years.
The round comprises $5 million in equity led by Nuwa Capital, with participation from 500 Global, Annex Investments, Plus VC, Serkal Group, Axeed Group, 21Ventures, Iliad Partners and angel investors, including operators from AWS, Lean Technologies and Sarwa, and a $15 million Shariah-compliant debt facility from Amwal Capital Partners, which gives Sooner the capacity to support $272 million of home purchases in 2027.
Most first-time homebuyers can afford the monthly mortgage payments but are held back by the availability of immediate cash. The down payment plus closing fees come to 27 to 30% of the price, about $230,000 (AED 850K) on an $800,000 (AED 3M) home, against roughly 6 to 10% in the United States and the United Kingdom.
Sooner's mission starts with helping renters become homeowners about two years sooner. Homebuyers pick from Sooner-compatible homes, where they pay 10% instead of 20% upfront and the remainder in 60 equal Shariah-compliant monthly instalments, while getting access to first-time homebuyer mortgages from all leading UAE banks with the lowest mortgage rate guarantee.
Sooner's founders come from leading fintech and proptech startups. Mohammed Aziz (CEO) exited his payments company Pluto to Tamara and was the first UAE-based founder to be backed by Y Combinator. Gabriel García Leyva launched rent now pay later at Keyper, and Vlad Cherevkov previously led products at Revolut and Deel.
"We built the product we wished we had," said Mohammed Aziz, CEO and co-founder of Sooner. "I went through this by buying our first family home, saving towards the down payment while also paying rent. My co-founder Gabriel and his wife went through the same as they bought the unit they rented. Every year a first-time buyer spends saving for a down payment, which is a year of rent paid towards someone else's mortgage. We are solving that problem and making sure that people in the UAE can realise their dream of home ownership sooner."
Since its launch in July 2026, Sooner has received about 9,000 applications, representing $4.5 billion in buying demand, and has already supported around $10 million of home purchases.
That mission evolves beyond the first home into helping the same customers build wealth through real estate. In 2027 Sooner will launch the UAE’s first Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC) product, allowing existing homeowners to unlock value from their current properties to easily secure financing for a new home. This is modelled on America's largest HELOC platforms: publicly listed Figure and Aven, a $2.2 billion unicorn backed by Khosla Ventures, Founders Fund and General Catalyst.
"The UAE market has been historically undercredited and investor-focused. It’s now ripe for a shift to end-user homeowners," said Gabriel García Leyva, co-founder of Sooner. "We reduce the barrier to access and leverage technology to deliver instant mortgage and Sooner down payment pre-approvals, as well as enabling a buyer-focused home discovery and closing experience that helps our customers get keys in hand in as little as 2 weeks."
The timing follows a shift towards end-user buying in Dubai. Residential mortgage lending hit a record $5.9 billion in the third quarter of 2026 (Cavendish Maxwell), and Dubai's Real Estate Sector Strategy 2033 targets a home-ownership rate of 33%.
"Down payment support and home equity release are standard in developed housing markets and still largely missing in the Gulf," said Arnav Danthi, partner at Nuwa Capital. "Sooner is building that for UAE homebuyers, and Mohammed, Gabriel and Vlad are one of the strongest early-stage fintech teams we've seen in the region."
"The Dubai property story is shifting from investor speculation to resident ownership," said Sharif Eid, Head of Fixed Income at Amwal Capital Partners. "Sooner is at the heart of this shift and is built on two simple observations: the down payment is the biggest barrier to ownership, yet it measures savings, not affordability; and people who own their home are people who stay. Sooner paired those insights with the right structure and technology, and that is why we backed them."
The UAE alone is a $4.1 billion revenue opportunity for Sooner's products, and the platform plans to expand to structurally similar markets, regionally and internationally.
Salaried homebuyers can get verified in about two minutes at www.joinsooner.com to get access to the platform.

articles.title: Wiz webinar: Bringing a sharper, connected focus to AI security
articles.text:
Wiz webinar: Bringing a sharper, connected focus to AI security
From AI discovery to threat detection, Wiz brings security into focus in a new virtual webinar
AI applications are becoming an increasingly important part of cloud environments. As adoption increases, so does the attack surface - far beyond traditional cloud assets. Today, organisations are building and deploying more AI-powered applications, agents, integrations and third-party tools. This leaves their security teams with a new challenge on their hands: understanding not just what exists, but what these applications can access and how their risks connect.
An AI application could interact with cloud systems, Application Programming Interfaces (API), sensitive data and other tools. Agents can retrieve information, call tools and trigger workflows. For security teams, looking at these assets individually may not reveal how their permissions, infrastructure and data access could interact to create security risk.
What to expect
To explore how organisations can address these challenges, global cybersecurity organization Wiz is hosting a focused 60-minute technical demo called ‘Securing Modern AI Applications with Wiz, featuring Dharmesh Vaya, Sr. Solution Engineer, Wiz.
The session will demonstrate how Wiz brings together an understanding of AI applications and cloud security context to secure AI from code to runtime, wherever it is built and run.
Event details
- Date: December 11, 2026
- Time: 03:00 PM
- Format: Virtual event
- Speaker: Dharmesh Vaya, Sr. Solution Engineer, Wiz
Understand what applications can do
Discovering an AI asset is just the first step. Security teams also need to understand what an application is designed to do, the tools it leverages, its capabilities, and access to data. During the demo, participants can discover how the Wiz AI Security Agent provides visibility into AI assets and custom applications, with deeper insights into agents, tools, and their capabilities. This feature examines agents and applications across code repositories, PaaS platforms, and self-hosted infrastructure like VMs, containers and serverless environments.
Connecting risks to identify critical attack paths
AI-related security risks do not exist in a silo. A vulnerability or misconfiguration can become more significant when connected to exposed infrastructure, privileged identities, or sensitive data.
The demo will showcase how the Wiz Security Graph connects AI-specific risks with exposure, identities, infrastructure, and sensitive data to uncover critical attack paths. Rather than flagging and treating security findings individually, this approach helps teams understand how different risks and vulnerabilities are intertwined. The Graph prioritises those with greater potential. For organisations working with multiple AI applications, agents, and integrations, this context can help security teams identify which connections need attention.
Securing AI: from code to runtime
As AI applications move from development into production, their behaviour, permissions, and exposure can change. Security, therefore, needs to extend across the application lifecycle. The session will demonstrate how Wiz brings together AI discovery, risk reduction, and runtime threat detection through one unified platform.
By connecting visibility into AI applications with contextual risk prioritisation and runtime threat detection, the platform aims to give security teams a more complete view of their AI-related exposure.
For organisations expanding their use of AI across cloud environments, understanding how applications, agents, identities, tools, and data interact is an important part of managing security risks.
Join for this 1-hour technical demo to see how Wiz connects these elements and helps teams secure AI applications from code to runtime.
Register now and learn how Wiz uncovers, connects, and secures AI risks.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, la liseuse Amazon Kindle Paperwhite passe à 144,99 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La liseuse Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2024) 16 Go à 144,99 € (-17%)
Actuellement notée 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, l'Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2024) améliore le confort de lecture grâce à un écran plus contrasté, une réactivité accrue et une résistance à l'eau IPX8. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 144,99 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 17 % et 30,33 € d'économie.
Amazon renouvelle sa liseuse avec la Kindle Paperwhite (2024), un appareil entièrement centré sur le confort de lecture numérique. Face à la version précédente de 2021, la marque améliore la taille d'affichage, le contraste et la fluidité générale pour faciliter le défilement des pages. Ce modèle avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur les bancs de test.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la liseuse descend à 144,99 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.com, soit environ 17 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (175,32 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 30,33 €.
Un affichage plus réactif et précis pour lire partout
Avec sa résolution de 300 ppp (pixels par pouce), l'écran assure un tracé des caractères net, proche d'une page imprimée, pour limiter la fatigue visuelle lors des sessions prolongées. L'appareil gagne aussi en réactivité pour tourner les pages plus rapidement, comme l'a relevé notre test complet. Sa certification IPX8 garantit une étanchéité totale à l'eau, ce qui autorise une utilisation près d'une piscine ou dans son bain sans risquer d'abîmer le matériel en cas d'immersion accidentelle.
Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2024)
Points forts
- Très bonne réactivité.
- Écran amélioré (contraste, luminosité, taille).
- Résistance à l'eau IPX8.
Points faibles
- Position du bouton d'alimentation discutable.
- Pas de réglage automatique de la luminosité.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une grande capacité de stockage malgré quelques manques d'ergonomie
La mémoire interne de 16 Go permet d'emporter des milliers de livres électroniques au format EPUB ou AZW sans saturer l'appareil. La recharge passe par un port USB-C standardisé, pratique pour utiliser le même câble que la plupart des téléphones récents.
La Kindle Paperwhite (2024) fait toutefois l'impasse sur le réglage automatique de la luminosité et conserve un bouton d'alimentation placé sur la tranche inférieure, qui peut être pressé par inadvertance. Cette absence de capteur oblige à ajuster l'éclairage manuellement lors des transitions entre ombre et lumière, ce qui reste sans conséquence si vous lisez principalement sous un éclairage constant.
Vivlio Light Zen : l'autre option face au Amazon Kindle Paperwhite (2024)
La Vivlio Light Zen vise un public souhaitant un écosystème ouvert, capable d'emprunter des livres numériques directement auprès des bibliothèques municipales sans restriction de format. En contrepartie, son écran se révèle moins contrasté et sa note actuelle est de 3/5, contre 4,5/5 pour le modèle d'Amazon.
La Vivlio Light Zen coûte 45,00 € de moins que la Kindle Paperwhite (2024) à son tarif remisé, mais la liseuse d'Amazon conserve un affichage plus précis et l'étanchéité complète IPX8 pour les lecteurs qui recherchent le meilleur confort visuel.
Vivlio Light Zen
Points forts
- Légèreté et compacité de l’ensemble.
- Écosystème ouvert.
- Gestion simplifiée des emprunts en bibliothèque (DRM LCP).
- Réactivité correcte.
Points faibles
- Définition de l’écran en deçà de la concurrence.
- Absence de filtre anti-lumière bleue pour la lecture nocturne.
- Aucun moyen d’écouter des livres audio.
