articles.title: Durante años hemos cambiado de navegador sin cambiar de motor. Ladybird acaba de ampliar nuestras opciones
articles.text:
Puede que lleves años utilizando Google Chrome y que en algún momento hayas decidido probar otro navegador. Quizás te haya convencido la apuesta de Brave por la privacidad, las funciones de Microsoft Edge o las posibilidades de personalización de Vivaldi. Lo interesante es que, en el ordenador, podemos cambiar entre todos estos navegadores sin cambiar de motor de navegación. Todos utilizan Blink, la tecnología impulsada por Google que se encarga de interpretar y mostrar las páginas web que visitamos. Hay bastante más diversidad en los iconos de nuestro escritorio que en la tecnología que hay detrás de ellos.
Este lunes 23 de noviembre, Andreas Kling anunció el lanzamiento de la primera versión alfa de Ladybird, un navegador independiente que ya podemos descargar para macOS y Linux tras más de cuatro años de desarrollo. La particularidad del proyecto es que sus responsables han construido su propio motor desde cero. Como destaca The Verge, estamos ante un acontecimiento poco habitual en los últimos años: la llegada de un navegador que aspira a competir con los establecidos sin recurrir a ninguno de sus motores.
En la actualidad, tres motores están detrás de los navegadores más utilizados del mundo: Gecko, WebKit y Blink. El primero ya estaba presente en Netscape 6, lanzado en el año 2000, y hoy lo encontramos en Firefox. Apple introdujo WebKit en Safari en 2003, a partir de una tecnología llamada KHTML, mientras que en 2013 Google tomó el código de WebKit como punto de partida para desarrollar Blink dentro del proyecto Chromium. La influencia de Google es especialmente significativa: según Statcounter, Chrome representaba por sí solo el 68,79% de las páginas vistas registradas por este servicio a escala mundial en octubre de 2026.
La realidad detrás de los navegadores
El caso del iPhone nos ayuda a entender hasta qué punto un navegador y su motor pueden seguir caminos distintos. Si utilizamos Chrome en nuestro ordenador, estaremos navegando con Blink, pero si utilizamos el navegador de Google en un iPhone, será WebKit el que se encargue de mostrar las páginas web. Durante años, Apple ha exigido a los desarrolladores utilizar esta tecnología en iOS. Aunque ha abierto la puerta a motores alternativos bajo determinadas condiciones en la Unión Europea y Japón, Mozilla señalaba el pasado 20 de noviembre que ningún desarrollador había conseguido lanzar allí un navegador con un motor distinto de WebKit.
Ladybird tiene unos orígenes bastante más modestos de lo que podría sugerir la dimensión de su objetivo. Nació a partir de un visor HTML que Kling estaba desarrollando para SerenityOS y acabó convirtiéndose en un proyecto con identidad propia. En julio de 2024, el desarrollador y Chris Wanstrath, cofundador de GitHub, anunciaron la creación de una organización sin ánimo de lucro respaldada por una donación inicial de un millón de dólares de Wanstrath y su familia. Su modelo de financiación busca preservar la independencia de un proyecto de código abierto que ofrece su navegador gratuitamente y no pretende monetizar a sus usuarios.
Hasta ahora, quienes querían probar los avances de Ladybird tenían que compilar su código fuente. Con la llegada de la alfa, como decimos, podemos descargar la aplicación directamente y, según el método de instalación elegido, recibir actualizaciones automáticas. Los usuarios de Windows tendrán que esperar a una fase posterior. Conviene tener presentes las advertencias de sus responsables: algunas páginas web todavía no funcionan, pueden producirse cierres inesperados y el equipo aún no ofrece garantías sobre su seguridad. Por el momento, es una oportunidad para experimentar con esta tecnología más que una invitación a abandonar nuestro navegador habitual.
Resulta interesante recuperar uno de los argumentos que Google esgrimió en 2013 para justificar la creación de Blink: disponer de diferentes motores ayuda a evitar que las particularidades de uno de ellos acaben convirtiéndose en estándares de facto. Más de una década después, Ladybird aspira a contribuir a esa diversidad con una beta prevista para 2027 y una versión estable para 2028, según su calendario de desarrollo. Son objetivos que todavía están por cumplir, pero el proyecto ya ha conseguido algo significativo: poner al alcance del público una nueva tecnología en un terreno dominado desde hace años por las mismas alternativas.

articles.title: Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is 'an option'
articles.text:
During an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, President Trump said that pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has been ensnared in a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy, is “an option,” albeit one that he doesn’t think he will have to exercise.
“It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” the president reportedly told the outlet.
Huang, who was ousted from his own company less than two weeks ago, was reinstated Monday. He faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China.
Huang is scheduled to testify at a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week.
When asked about the hearing, Trump reportedly said: “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person.”
At another point in the interview, when asked what he knew about Huang’s other extramarital affairs, Trump reportedly said: “I really didn’t get into that. I got into the business of chips, much more than the business of sex.”
TechCrunch has reached out to the White House for comment.

articles.title: Google shows its quantum chip can win a logic game classical computers can't
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Google researchers have demonstrated that the company's experimental quantum computer can outperform the best possible classical strategy in a logic puzzle known as the magic square game. The machine achieves this by exploiting quantum contextuality, a property in which the outcome of a measurement is not predetermined but instead depends on the context of other measurements performed alongside it.
Published in the journal Science, the research gives physicists a working hardware demonstration of a phenomenon they consider central to what quantum computers may eventually be capable of.
The game makes the gap between the two types of computing easy to measure. Two teammates must fill a three-by-three grid with numbers that satisfy a set of mathematical conditions, much like a variation of Sudoku. They are not allowed to communicate with each other. Under classical rules, even the best strategy can only achieve a limited number of wins. Google's machine did better.
That advantage comes from the way qubits encode information. In a conventional computer, a bit holds either a 0 or a 1 before anyone checks it. Reading it simply reveals a value that was already there. Qubits work differently. The outcome of a measurement depends on what other compatible measurements are performed alongside it. In the magic square game, the teammates can use this dependence to coordinate their answers more often than classical strategies allow, even though they never communicate. Better-coordinated answers mean more wins.
Shashwat Kumar, a Google researcher and one of the paper's authors, explains the concept using a coin toss. A coin caught and covered by a hand has already landed on heads or tails, and lifting the hand simply reveals the result. In a contextual quantum system, however, he says, measuring something else at the same time as the coin's face, such as its size, would change whether it came up heads or tails.
"The outcomes of quantum measurements are not predetermined," Kumar told The New York Times. "They are not ready to be read from a list. They come into existence while you are making the measurements, and they are shaped by other measurements around them."
The experiment was conducted on Google's quantum computer in Santa Barbara, California. The machine is built using superconducting qubits, which are metal circuits cooled to temperatures approaching absolute zero.
Michel Devoret, a Google researcher who received a Nobel Prize for his work in quantum mechanics, sees contextuality as the field's main source of advantage. "You can describe quantum contextuality as the superpower of quantum mechanics," he said.
The game itself has no practical application, and the research team acknowledges that. It is a toy problem designed to demonstrate what the hardware can do rather than solve a real-world challenge.
Google, along with numerous other companies, academic laboratories, and government institutions, has spent decades developing quantum computers in the hope of eventually accelerating drug discovery, designing new materials, and advancing artificial intelligence. None of those goals is achieved by this experiment. The researchers are making a narrower claim: a machine capable of solving a puzzle like the magic square game could pave the way for more meaningful calculations.
Mark Howard, a physicist at the University of Galway in Ireland who was not involved in the study, said the significance lies in the fact that quantum computers behave in ways classical computers cannot. If scientists can harness that behavior, they could perform calculations that would be impossible for even the most powerful traditional supercomputers.
"The dream is that contextuality is the fuel that makes a quantum computer superpowered," Howard said.
For now, Google's team is putting more weight on where the effect happened than on the puzzle it solved: a processor the company is still working to improve.
"All of that weirdness can fit on a chip," said Rodrigo Cortiñas, a Google researcher who worked on the study. "That is what we are building."

Team Group Industrial Enhances S845 Embedded Storage Solutions

To maximize system management efficiency, the S845 Series further incorporates Team Group's proprietary S.M.A.R.T. function, enabling real-time monitoring of SSD health status.
Driven by the rapid development of industrial automation, Edge AI, and smart devices, real-time data processing, system stability, and data security have become top priorities in embedded applications. Team Group continues to expand its embedded storage and edge computing solutions to support high-reliability and long-term operational needs. Soundbar com melhor custo-benefício: 7 modelos abaixo de R$ 2.000 em 2026
Encontre modelos de soundbar com o melhor preço para melhorar o som da TV sem gastar muito; lista reúne modelos Samsung, LG, TCL e JBL
Uma soundbar pode deixar os diálogos mais claros e dar mais impacto ao som de filmes, séries e jogos. Por menos de R$ 2.000, é possível encontrar desde barras estéreo que cabem em móveis pequenos até conjuntos com subwoofer sem fio, caixas traseiras ou Dolby Atmos.
A escolha depende do que você quer melhorar no som da TV. Um modo de realce de voz pode ajudar a acompanhar as falas em séries, enquanto um subwoofer dedicado reforça os graves e caixas traseiras reproduzem efeitos atrás do sofá.
O Tecnoblog reuniu sete modelos com bom custo-benefício em 2026. Confira os prós e contras.
A JBL Cinema SB595 é uma opção de soundbar com Dolby Atmos e que reúne três canais frontais: um subwoofer externo e dois alto-falantes. Eles projetam o som em direção ao teto para criar a sensação de que certos efeitos vêm de cima.
A JBL informa 220 W de potência total, com 100 W na barra e 120 W no subwoofer sem fio de 6,5 polegadas. O modelo também tem um canal central dedicado, que costuma concentrar boa parte dos diálogos em trilhas multicanal, conforme a mixagem.
O conjunto dispensa caixas traseiras, o que simplifica a instalação, mas limita a reprodução de sons vindos de trás de quem assiste. A conectividade inclui uma saída HDMI eARC, uma entrada HDMI adicional, entrada óptica e Bluetooth 5.4.
Com 1 metro de largura, a SB595 exige espaço no móvel e acompanha um kit de montagem na parede.
A LG S60TR é indicada para quem quer ouvir efeitos sonoros vindos de trás ao assistir a filmes e séries. O sistema 5.1 reúne uma barra com canal central, um subwoofer e duas caixas traseiras incluídas. Posicionadas atrás da área de escuta, essas caixas reproduzem os canais surround de trilhas multicanal.
Com 440 W RMS de potência total, o modelo aceita Dolby Digital e DTS Digital Surround e traz o AI Sound Pro, que ajusta o processamento conforme o conteúdo. Também há modos específicos para cinema, música, jogos e esportes.
A barra tem HDMI ARC, entrada óptica e Bluetooth 5.3. Em TVs LG compatíveis, o WOW Interface permite trocar modos de som e acessar outros ajustes pela tela da televisão.
As caixas traseiras recebem o sinal da barra sem fio, mas são ligadas entre si por um cabo, e uma delas precisa de tomada — assim como o subwoofer.
A LG S40T é uma opção da marca para quem quer um subwoofer sem instalar caixas pela sala. O sistema 2.1 tem dois canais frontais e um subwoofer externo sem fio. A barra mede 72 cm de largura, o que facilita a instalação em móveis menores.
A potência total é de 300 W RMS e a barra aceita Dolby Digital e DTS Digital Surround para uma experiência de som mais aprimorada. O AI Sound Pro ajusta o processamento conforme o conteúdo, e o usuário também pode selecionar modos como Cinema e Jogo.
Entre as conexões estão HDMI ARC, entrada óptica, Bluetooth 5.3 e USB para reprodução de áudio. O WOW Interface permite fazer ajustes pela tela de TVs LG compatíveis e o aplicativo LG ThinQ também oferece controles pelo celular.
A TCL S55H é voltada a quem quer efeitos de som espacial com poucos equipamentos. Ela combina dois canais frontais e um subwoofer sem fio em um sistema 2.1 de 220 W, com suporte a Dolby Atmos e DTS Virtual:X.
Segundo a marca, a barra ajusta o reforço dos graves conforme o volume, com a proposta de mantê-los mais presentes em volumes baixos e mais controlados em volumes altos. O modelo tem 81 cm de largura e também oferece modos de som para diferentes conteúdos e calibração acústica pelo aplicativo TCL Home.
Para conectar a barra à TV, a TCL oferece HDMI eARC, além de Bluetooth 5.4. O modelo também conta com recurso que permite usar a barra e os alto-falantes da televisão ao mesmo tempo em TVs TCL compatíveis. A disponibilidade, no entanto, depende do modelo da TV.
A JBL Cinema SB180 reúne dois canais frontais e um subwoofer sem fio de 6,5 polegadas. A JBL declara 110 W RMS de potência total, divididos entre 50 W na barra e 60 W no subwoofer.
Os modos Cinema, Música e Notícias permitem ajustar o processamento ao conteúdo. Como a barra tem dois canais frontais, os diálogos são reproduzidos por eles, enquanto o subwoofer tem a função de reproduzir as frequências graves.
A conexão com a TV pode ser feita por HDMI ARC ou entrada óptica, o Bluetooth 5.3 permite transmitir áudio do celular, e a porta USB reproduz arquivos MP3. A barra tem 92 cm de largura, um detalhe a considerar em móveis menores.
A Samsung HW-B400F é uma soundbar de entrada para quem tem pouco espaço no móvel. O sistema 2.0 reúne quatro alto-falantes distribuídos em dois canais e um woofer integrado. A própria barra reproduz os graves, o que dispensa uma caixa separada.
O modo de realce de voz dá ênfase aos diálogos, enquanto o Surround Sound Expansion usa processamento para ampliar a percepção espacial do áudio. A barra também oferece o modo Padrão e um Modo Noturno, que reduz os graves e o volume para uso à noite.
Com 64,1 cm de largura, a barra tem HDMI ARC, entrada óptica, USB para reprodução de músicas e Bluetooth 4.2. O controle remoto de TVs Samsung compatíveis pode operar funções como volume e efeitos sonoros.
A porta HDMI é destinada ao retorno de áudio da TV, mas sem uma entrada adicional para ligar um console ou outro aparelho diretamente à barra.
A Philips TAB4000/78 é uma alternativa para quem quer substituir o áudio integrado da TV por uma barra estéreo com poucos componentes. O sistema 2.0 tem dois canais frontais e dispensa subwoofer externo. A barra mede 76 cm de largura.
A Philips informa 60 W de potência máxima, com reprodução estéreo — os diálogos são distribuídos pelos canais esquerdo e direito. A configuração é voltada ao uso cotidiano com filmes, séries e programas de TV.
A conexão HDMI ARC recebe áudio PCM estéreo de televisores compatíveis. A barra também tem Bluetooth 5.4 para transmitir áudio do celular e uma porta USB para reproduzir arquivos MP3, WAV e FLAC.
A escolha pela melhor soundbar custo-benefício deve considerar o tamanho da sala, as conexões da TV e o tipo de conteúdo que você mais assiste. Vale conferir os seguintes aspectos antes de comprar.
Na soundbar com graves integrados, os alto-falantes responsáveis pelas frequências mais baixas ficam na própria barra, o que economiza espaço.
O subwoofer dedicado usa uma caixa separada e tende a dar mais profundidade e impacto a cenas de ação e músicas. Mesmo quando recebe o áudio sem fio, ele precisa de tomada.
A potência necessária depende do tamanho da sala, da distância até o sofá e do volume em que você costuma assistir à TV. Para uma sala pequena, uma barra compacta pode atender bem em volume moderado.
Em ambientes maiores, vale observar se ela mantém os diálogos claros no volume desejado, já que os watts RMS, sozinhos, não indicam quão alto ou limpo será o som.
Escolha uma 2.0 se você quer uma instalação compacta para assistir à TV no dia a dia. A 2.1 faz mais sentido se você procura mais impacto nos graves.
Já a 5.1 com caixas traseiras é indicada para ouvir efeitos vindos de trás em filmes, séries e jogos com áudio multicanal compatível.
Sim, especialmente se o som da TV parece abafado ou se você tem dificuldade para entender os diálogos. Uma barra estéreo com realce de voz e HDMI ARC pode atender bem a esse uso.
Se a prioridade for sentir o impacto de explosões ou ouvir efeitos atrás do sofá, vale investir em um modelo com subwoofer dedicado ou caixas traseiras, conforme o efeito que você deseja.
Sim. Para ouvir diálogos com mais clareza ou dar mais impacto aos graves, um canal central ou um subwoofer podem fazer mais diferença no dia a dia.
O Dolby Atmos vale a atenção de quem costuma assistir a conteúdos compatíveis e quer ter mais efeitos de imersão em filmes e séries.
Sim, se a ideia é melhorar o som da TV com poucos equipamentos. Para reproduzir efeitos atrás do sofá com separação física, procure um conjunto com caixas traseiras.
Uma barra estéreo sozinha concentra a reprodução sorona na frente, mesmo quando oferece surround virtual.

articles.title: Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
articles.text:
Workday shares fall as soft subscription forecast overshadows third-quarter beat
Shares of human resources and finance software company Workday Inc. fell more than 7% in late trading today after a softer-than-expected subscription revenue forecast for the current quarter overshadowed fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue that came in ahead of Wall Street’s targets.
For the quarter that ended on Oct. 31, Workday reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.82, up 22% from $2.32 in the same quarter of the previous year, on revenue of $2.705 billion, up 11.2% year-over-year. Analysts were expecting earnings of $2.75 per share on revenue of $2.69 billion.
Subscription revenue rose 12.8% from a year earlier, to $2.532 billion. Net income on an unadjusted basis came to $237 million, down from $252 million in the same quarter a year ago. Included in the quarter were $51 million in restructuring expenses, which followed the company’s disclosure in late September that it would cut about 2.5% of its workforce, mostly in its product and technology team.
Total subscription revenue backlog grew 6.1%, to $27.548 billion, with the 12-month figure up 12.3%, to $9.216 billion. Free cash flow came to $691 million, up from $550 million. During the quarter, Workday spent $750 million buying back about 3.8 million shares.
The quarter also saw Workday hold its annual Rising customer conference in Las Vegas in October, when the company made Sana the new home experience for its platform. Built on technology from Sana Labs AB, which Workday acquired for about $1.1 billion last year, Sana is an AI interface that brings tasks, decisions, meetings and agent activity together in one place. Autopilot Agents, also launched at the event, are designed to handle routine HR, finance and IT processes in the background.
On the opening day of Rising, Workday announced that it had agreed to acquire agentic identity platform ConductorOne Inc., better known as C1.ai. That deal closed on Monday. A partnership with Anthropic PBC, also unveiled at Rising, is set to bring Claude together with Sana AI agents and Workday’s HR and finance data.
“The past few quarters have been our strongest on the innovation and invention front, and in Q3, our AI products drove nearly $150 million in new ACV, more than three times what we delivered a year ago,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Aneel Bhusri, who returned to the top job in February after Carl Eschenbach stepped down. The priority now, Bhusri added, is to get more customers running agents in production.
According to Workday, the number of core customers that have bought at least one of its AI products rose nearly 25% from the previous quarter, to more than 2,200.
Pointing to what he called “ongoing adoption across our AI portfolio,” Chief Financial Officer Zane Rowe said the company is raising its full-year targets.
For its fiscal fourth quarter, Workday expects subscription revenue of $2.6 billion, up 10%, and an adjusted operating margin of 31.7%. Full-year subscription revenue is now forecast at $9.958 billion, up 13%, compared with the $9.94 billion to $9.95 billion guided in August. The full-year adjusted operating margin forecast was also raised, to 31.5%, ahead of the 31.1% expected by analysts.
Though the full-year numbers moved higher, the fourth-quarter subscription forecast came in narrowly below the $2.61 billion analysts had been expecting. Growth of 10% in the period would also be a step down from the 12.8% Workday posted in the third quarter.
Workday Chief Technology Officer Gabe Monroy made the case for taking agents to where employees already work during an interview in August. Speaking with theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio, for the Google Cloud: AI Agents in Action series, Monroy said enterprise agents need the deterministic rules of a system like Workday to go with the probabilistic reasoning of AI. “We don’t want to ask customers to have to switch their front doors or log into Workday when they’re happy to use Gemini systems,” he said.

articles.title: Datenbanken mit 3,5 Milliarden Zugangsdaten offen im Netz gefunden: Was du jetzt tun solltest
articles.text:
Mit Daten von Infostealern: Datenbanken mit 3,5 Milliarden Zugangsdaten offen im Netz gefunden
Im Januar 2024 hatten Sicherheitsforscher:innen in einem als „Mother of all Breaches“ bezeichneten Datenleck rund 26 Milliarden Datensätze mit sensiblen Informationen entdeckt. Branchenbeobachter:innen zufolge soll es sich dabei aber größtenteils um schon bekannte Daten gehandelt haben.
Größte Sammlung von Zugangsdaten
Die „Mutter aller Sicherheitslücken“ setzte sich aus Daten von tausenden verschiedenen alten Lecks, Sicherheitslücken und Datenbanken zusammen. Jetzt will der Sicherheitsforscher Jeremiah Fowler die größte Sammlung von Zugangsdaten gefunden haben, die ihm je in einer einzelnen offenen Datenbank untergekommen sei.
Wie Wired berichtet, enthält die von dem Sicherheitsforscher der Firma Black Hills Information Security entdeckte ungesicherte Datenbank rund zwei Milliarden personenbezogene Daten wie Benutzerdaten und Passwörter. Die Daten stammen demnach zum Teil aus Aktivitäten von Cyberkriminellen.
Von Infostealern entwendete Daten
Außerdem sollen sich Fowler zufolge auch von sogenannten Infostealern gestohlene Daten in der geleakten Datenbank befunden haben. Bei Infostealern handelt es sich um Schadsoftware, die sämtliche auf einem infizierten Gerät eingegebenen Anmeldedaten ausspähen kann.
Neben E-Mail-Adressen und Passwörtern finden sich entsprechend auch Cookies und Sitzungstoken in der Datensammlung. Damit könnten Angreifer:innen laufende Sitzungen übernehmen, ohne auf Passwörter oder Zwei-Faktor-Authentifizierung angewiesen zu sein. Nutzer:innen sollten entsprechend nicht nur Passwörter ändern, sondern sich auch auf allen Geräten abmelden, um aktive Sitzungen zu beenden. Zudem sollten Betroffene ihre Geräte auf Schadsoftware prüfen.
„Digitale Leben“ der Opfer kapern
Für den Sicherheitsforscher am Erschreckendsten seien aber 400.000 Dokumente gewesen, in denen gezielt Informationen zu einzelnen Opfern wie Anmeldedaten, Cookies oder Browserdaten zusammengetragen worden seien. Diese Daten könnten ein detailliertes Profil einer Person und ihres digitalen Lebens ergeben, heißt es bei Wired. „Wer all das hat, hat diese Person in der Hand“, erklärte Fowler.
Wem die Datenbank gehörte, konnte der Sicherheitsforscher nicht feststellen. Nach einem Hinweis an den Hostinganbieter sei diese aber aus dem Internet entfernt worden. Unklar ist, wie lange sie zuvor online gewesen ist und wer noch Zugriff darauf gehabt hat.
Datenbank mit sensiblen Daten aus China
Ähnliches gilt für eine zweite öffentlich zugängliche Datenbank, die Greg Pollock, Forschungsleiter beim Sicherheitsunternehmen Upguard, entdeckt hat. In dieser finden sich mehr als 1,5 Milliarden Zugangsdaten von überwiegend chinesischen Privatpersonen und Unternehmen. Einer Stichprobe Pollocks zufolge waren auch Daten mit Angaben zu Kindern und Verstorbenen darunter.
Ob die in den beiden Datenbanken gefundenen Datensätze noch aktuell sind und wie viele Informationen doppelt oder schon bekannt waren, müssen weitere Auswertungen zeigen. Wer wissen will, ob die eigenen Anmeldedaten schon im Netz kursieren, kann das etwa auf dem Portal „Have I Been Pwned“ überprüfen.

articles.title: Trump pressured Nvidia to bring Jensen back, called into board meeting to push reinstatement, reports claim — President concerned over falling stock prices, with Huang’s return reversing slide
articles.text:
Trump pressured Nvidia to bring Jensen back, called into board meeting to push reinstatement, reports claim — President concerned over falling stock prices, with Huang’s return reversing slide
‘It’s a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it’s taking the whole market.’
The Nvidia board has reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO just 11 days after he resigned, a move that, although it had strong support from both employees and supporters, had surprised many. While the company’s board of directors voted unanimously to bring the founder back, it seems that this decision was pushed along by pressure from Washington. According to CNN, President Donald Trump, alongside Vice President JD Vance and several members of his cabinet, spent the weekend talking to industry insiders, investors, and even to the board itself to get Jensen back as the chief of Nvidia.
“I’ve been speaking to the board directly and indirectly, and I felt very strongly about it,” Trump said in an interview with CNBC. “I think we have one of our great stars back in play.” Nvidia’s stock price took a beating when Jensen Huang admitted to the affairs, and his future at the company was in question. It went from bad to worse when he finally resigned on November 12, with the rest of the market following. This has brought concerns that Jensen’s downfall would drag Nvidia and the economy with him, which could potentially turn into a catastrophe as the AI bubble pops.
The President said that bringing Jensen back as the CEO of Nvidia would be the only solution to this conundrum. True enough, Nvidia stock prices shot up to around $165 after Jensen’s reinstatement — a more than 25% rally from its previous close of around $130. “It’s a rocket ship going in the right direction, and it’s taking the whole market,” the president added. “It could be that there’s never been anything like it.”
Despite the seemingly positive impact of Jensen Huang’s return to the company, Trump’s decision to intervene in the inner workings of a private institution has raised apprehension among politicians, even those from his own party. The biggest concerns raised include the Nvidia CEO’s involvement in national security issues, including his affair with a suspected Chinese spy, the billions of dollars’ worth of advanced Nvidia chips that have been allegedly smuggled despite the government’s export controls, and the fact that the President assured the Nvidia board that his administration does not believe that Jensen is a threat to national security and that he also was not facing any criminal charges, despite ongoing investigations. People also raised questions about the White House’s influence on the board of directors of a private company, something that was characterized as “an unprecedented campaign.”
Trump’s push for Jensen Huang’s return at Nvidia is inherently risky, with the president himself saying that he had consulted Attorney General Todd Blanche and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton about it. He said that they’ve been studying the issue for quite some time and that they had found nothing wrong, especially as Trump said that he can’t have anyone indicted after making the recommendation.

articles.title: Los centros de datos más grandes de Estados Unidos emitieron 25,7 millones de toneladas de CO2 en un año
articles.text:
Los 403 centros de datos más grandes de Estados Unidos emitieron unos 25,7 millones de toneladas de CO2 entre mayo de 2024 y abril de 2025, según un estudio de investigadores de Harvard publicado en la revista Nature Sustainability. Más de la mitad de la electricidad que consumieron provino de combustibles fósiles.
Los autores, entre ellos Gianluca Guidi y Francesca Dominici, estimaron que esas instalaciones, llamadas “hiperescala” por su tamaño y porque sostienen servicios de inteligencia artificial, comercio en línea y almacenamiento en la nube, consumieron unos 82 TWh (teravatios hora) en el escenario central. Equivale a cerca del 1,8% de toda la electricidad que usa el país.
El estudio plantea un rango según el nivel de carga de cada instalación: entre 68 y 99 TWh de consumo y entre 21 y 31 millones de toneladas de CO2. Cerca del 54% de la generación atribuida a esos centros vino de fuentes fósiles.
Medios como WBUR, de Boston, que entrevistó a los autores, informaron que la contaminación climática de estas instalaciones es tres veces mayor que la estimada antes. El centro de datos promedio de la muestra consumió tanta energía como 30.000 hogares, y en conjunto usaron al menos tanta como el estado de Michigan en un año.
Un cálculo hecho desde afuera de las empresas
Las compañías casi nunca publican cuánta energía gastan sus centros de datos. Por eso el equipo recurrió a imágenes satelitales y a datos de una empresa privada sobre la superficie de cada instalación y su consumo máximo autorizado. Luego usó mapas para identificar de qué centrales eléctricas se abastecen y calculó las emisiones según el combustible que quema cada una.
“Queríamos números independientes, no solo las declaraciones de sostenibilidad de las empresas”, dijo Guidi, investigador posdoctoral de Harvard. El autor aclaró que el trabajo es apenas una estimación mínima: el consumo de los más de mil centros de datos del país es probablemente mayor al que captura la muestra.
El método tiene límites que los propios autores reconocen. Can Hankendi, investigador de centros de datos de la Universidad de Boston que no participó, dijo a WBUR que el trabajo está “muy bien construido”. Señaló que los supuestos son razonables, aunque habrá problemas de precisión, y que las cifras sirven como punto de partida.
El estudio calculó una intensidad de emisiones de unos 314 gramos de CO2 por kilovatio hora para estos centros, frente a unos 348 gramos del promedio nacional. Su electricidad resultó algo menos contaminante que la media del país, pero el volumen de consumo es el que eleva el total.
Virginia y Ohio, los estados más expuestos
El impacto no se reparte por igual. Virginia, el estado con más centros de datos, y Ohio tienen más centrales que queman combustibles fósiles. Estados como Oregon cuentan con redes eléctricas más limpias, así que las instalaciones allí son responsables de menos gases de efecto invernadero.
Guidi dijo que las cifras ya están “desactualizadas en cierto modo” por la velocidad del sector. Según la firma de seguimiento de mercado Clearview, había 1.163 centros de datos en operación el año pasado y hay 578 nuevos en construcción, además de otros proyectados.
Dominici, profesora de bioestadística en la Escuela de Salud Pública T.H. Chan de Harvard, explicó que muchos desarrolladores recurren a generadores propios para construir más rápido. Algunos funcionan sin conectarse a la red, pero suelen quemar gas natural o diésel y pueden ser menos eficientes y más contaminantes que las centrales tradicionales.
Dominici afirmó que las grandes empresas de servicios en la nube intentan pasar a energías renovables, “pero todavía no lo estamos viendo”. Los datos de la red y el código del análisis están disponibles en un repositorio público; los datos de cada instalación, protegidos por un acuerdo de uso, se entregan solo a investigadores aprobados.

articles.title: Firefox 161 introduit 4 nouveautés qui vont transformer votre navigation
articles.text:
Firefox 161 est officiellement disponible. Et le moins que l’on puisse dire, c’est que les développeurs de Mozilla ne se sont pas tournés les pouces. Cette nouvelle mouture du navigateur introduit pas moins de quatre nouveautés qui devraient vous faire gagner un temps précieux et vous aider à protéger encore un peu plus la confidentialité de vos données pendant la navigation.
Des règles VPN individuelles par sites Web
La première grande nouveauté introduite par Firefox 161, c’est la possibilité de créer des règles VPN individuelles par sites. Cela signifie concrètement qu’il est désormais possible, sur la version desktop du navigateur, de définir si le VPN doit s’activer ou se désactiver automatiquement en fonction des sites que vous consultez.
Avec ce nouveau système de fonctionnement, vous n’aurez pas besoin de jongler avec l’activation ou la désactivation du VPN pour les sites sur lesquels vous l’utilisez habituellement.
Mozilla suggère que la fonction vous permettra aussi de faire quelques menues économies. En consultant un site marchand avec une IP d’une autre région, vous pourrez comparer plus facilement le prix de vos emplettes. À noter que la Fondation offre des données VPN illimitées dans Firefox jusqu’à la fin du mois de janvier 2027 si vous vous connectez avec un compte Mozilla.
La lecture vocale des articles arrive sur Android
Déjà présent sur la version desktop du navigateur, la lecture vocale des articles du Mode Lecture arrive enfin sur Android. La fonction vous permettra d’écouter le contenu d’un article ou d’une recette, plutôt que d’avoir à lire. L’interface du module offre un contrôle de la lecture et de la pause, avec la possibilité d’avancer ou de revenir en arrière dans la lecture, d’en ajuster la vitesse ou encore de choisir la voix.
Cerise sur le gâteau, la lecture vocale, dont le traitement est réalisé localement sur l’appareil pour préserver votre vie privée, fonctionne même écran éteint.
Un bouton Fire pour tout supprimer sur desktop
Jusqu’à maintenant réservé à la navigation privée, le bouton Fire débarque officiellement sur Desktop. Intégré directement à la fenêtre classique du navigateur, dans la barre d’outils, le bouton Fire permet d’effacer rapidement l’historique de navigation et de téléchargement, les cookies, les fichiers temporaires ainsi que les données de formulaires, le tout sans avoir à naviguer jusque dans les Paramètres du navigateur.
En un clic, vous pouvez effacer toutes traces de vos dernières recherches. Attention toutefois, la fonction vous laissera choisir entre une réinitialisation complète (qui ferme la fenêtre et vous déconnecte des sites), et la possibilité de choisir uniquement les données à supprimer tout en maintenant la fenêtre ouverte.
La fonction, dont le déploiement doit se faire de manière progressive, n’est pas nécessairement encore activée chez tous les utilisateurs sitôt la mise à jour installée. Si le bouton n’apparaît pas chez vous, rendez-vous sur la page about:config, cliquez que Accepter le risque et poursuivre, recherchez le paramètre browser.fireButton.enabled et changez sa valeur false par true.
Redémarrez ensuite le navigateur, vous devriez y trouver le bouton Fire greffé tout à droite de la barre d’outils.
Firefox se fait une place dans votre voiture
La quatrième et dernière grande nouveauté introduite par Firefox 161 est sa disponibilité sur le tableau de bord des véhicules équipés de Google intégré. Vous pouvez à présent vous rendre sur le Google Play Store pour y télécharger le navigateur dans votre véhicule. Sécurité oblige, l’utilisation de Firefox en voiture est restreinte. Vous ne pourrez l’utiliser qu’à l’arrêt, pratique pour tuer le temps pendant une recharge électrique ou une pause au cours d’un long trajet. Mozilla précise que les données de navigation ne sont jamais partagées avec le constructeur automobile, et qu’elle ne les conserve pas non plus.

articles.title: Cynoia launches Hannibal AI ahead of further African expansion
articles.text:
Cynoia launches Hannibal AI ahead of further African expansion
- Tunisian SaaS startup Cynoia has launched Hannibal AI, an AI-powered workplace assistant integrated into the latest version of its collaboration and work-management platform, alongside support for third-party AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor.
- Founded in 2019 by Nasreddine Riahi and Ayoub Rabeh, Cynoia provides a unified workspace for project management, task tracking, communication, video calls and file sharing. Its AI assistant analyses internal workspace data, generates reports and supports translation across nine languages, including several African languages.
- Since raising €850,000 in 2023 from investors including Digital Africa, Bpifrance, 216 Capital, Go Big Partners, KJ Holding and UGFS, Cynoia has grown its user base from 3,000 to more than 7,000, primarily in West Africa. The company employs 15 people across Tunisia, Senegal and France.
- In 2027, Cynoia plans to expand its partnerships with telecommunications operators across North and West Africa, strengthen its presence in Egypt, complete its international security and AI governance certifications, and raise a new funding round.
Press release:
Cynoia, whose team-collaboration platform counts more than 7,000 users, primarily in West Africa, rolled out version 3.1 of its work-management platform (projects, tasks, discussions, calls, notes and files) on November 12. The release embeds Hannibal AI, an AI assistant built in Africa for African teams, and opens the platform to leading third-party AI assistants.
A platform built for the realities of African teams
Cynoia serves more than 7,000 users, including teams at Yas Senegal, Expresso Senegal and MTN Côte d’Ivoire. Its user base is concentrated in West Africa (Senegal, Côte d’Ivoire, Benin, Togo, Mali and Nigeria), with a growing presence in the DR Congo, Egypt, Tunisia and France. The platform, video calls included, is engineered to run on low bandwidth and is available on iOS and Android. Hannibal AI translates into French, English, Arabic, Wolof, Swahili, Hausa, Yoruba, Zulu and Spanish, and the app itself is available in six languages. Pricing is displayed in local currencies (CFA franc, Egyptian pound, naira, Kenyan shilling, dirham and more), and users can pay via mobile money with Wave or by bank card.
An assistant that works from your team’s own data
Hannibal AI answers natural-language questions drawing on the workspace’s projects, tasks, notes, calendar, discussions and files. Its responses come with tables, charts and direct links to the relevant tasks. It can also generate summaries, such as a progress update or the week’s plan.
Cynoia named its assistant after Hannibal, the Carthaginian general remembered for his strategic genius and for crossing the Alps where no one expected him. Carthage stood on what is now Tunisia, where Cynoia was founded. The ambition: to deliver intelligence born in Africa, in service of team strategy.
Open to market-leading AI tools, with data governance firmly under control
Through the open standard connector MCP (Model Context Protocol), third-party assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor can connect to a workspace, read its content and create tasks. Access requires explicit consent for each workspace. Every user can review and revoke their own connections, and workspace owners can suspend all of them at once.
Data is hosted on AWS and with local cloud providers such as Stellarix in Senegal. Cynoia has appointed a data protection officer with the CNIL in France, the CDP in Senegal and the INPDP in Tunisia, and its ISO 27001, ISO 42001 and SOC 2 certifications are in progress.
“A team doesn’t need an AI that writes for it; it needs an AI that knows where it stands,” says Nasreddine Riahi, co-founder and CEO of Cynoia. “A well-equipped team of five can now deliver what used to take fifteen. It’s a historic opportunity for African entrepreneurs, who have always had to do more with less.”
A trajectory on the rise
Since closing its €850,000 funding round in 2023, with backing from Digital Africa, Bpifrance, 216 Capital, Go Big Partners, KJ Holding and UGFS, among others, Cynoia opened its Dakar subsidiary in 2024, launched its iOS and Android apps in May 2026, and shipped Hannibal AI and the MCP connector in November 2026. Over that period, its user base grew from 3,000 to more than 7,000. The startup employs 15 people: 10 in Tunisia, 3 in Senegal and 2 in France. It was named best SaaS startup at AfricArena 2024, won the Provence Africa Connect award, and is a laureate of the TABC program in Senegal and the DRC.
Looking ahead to 2027
Cynoia already relies on distribution partners, including telecom operators and LafricaMobile in Senegal, under a revenue-sharing model. In 2027, the startup plans to forge new partnerships with telecom operators across North and West Africa, expand into new markets starting with Egypt, complete its ISO 27001, ISO 42001 and SOC 2 certifications, and raise a new funding round.

articles.title: Mandats d’arrêt, personnes disparues, casiers… des hackers ont piraté la base de données du FBI
articles.text:
Le FBI a détecté une intrusion dans le National Crime Information Center (NCIC), sa base de données nationale d’informations criminelles. Géré par le FBI depuis 1967, ce gigantesque fichier informatique est exploité par toutes les polices du pays, dont le FBI et les autres agences fédérales, la police de chaque État, et les polices locales comme les shérifs ou les polices municipales.
À lire aussi : Piratage de frigos de supermarchés – une opération secrète a évité une catastrophe au Royaume-Uni
Une base de données très sensible
On y trouve les personnes recherchées et les mandats d’arrêt, les personnes disparues, dont des enfants, les antécédents judiciaires, les ordonnances de protection, ainsi que les véhicules et les armes volés. En 2025, la base comptait plus de 19,3 millions de fiches, selon Malwarebytes. Dans la foulée, le ministère de l’Agriculture a également été compromis. Le système de paiement des agriculteurs a été visé par des pirates, et s’est retrouvé momentanément hors service.
Interrogée par Axios, Cynthia Kaiser, ancienne responsable de la division cyber du FBI, estime qu’il est « important de prendre cela au sérieux ». Un autre ancien cadre du FBI, contacté par CNN, ne s’inquiète « pas seulement de savoir si les pirates ont eu accès à des informations sensibles, même si c’est un problème, mais s’ils ont pu compromettre l’exactitude des informations sur lesquelles s’appuient les agents ». Concrètement, un pirate pourrait modifier ou effacer une fiche, ce qui pourrait permettre à des individus d’échapper à un contrôle de police.
Donald Trump y voit « un aspect positif »
À la surprise générale, Donald Trump a réagi en assurant que le piratage du FBI avait peut-être des bons côtés. Évoquant l’enquête du FBI sur l’ingérence russe dans la présidentielle de 2016, l’actuel président espère que la cyberattaque s’accompagnera de la divulgation d’informations confidentielles. L’enquête devait déterminer si la Russie avait cherché à influencer l’élection présidentielle américaine, et si l’équipe de campagne de Donald Trump avait des liens avec Moscou. Trump n’a jamais digéré cette enquête, et ne cesse d’y revenir en assurant qu’il s’agit d’un canular.
« Mais peut-être apprendrons-nous des choses que nous n’aurions jamais apprises autrement, parce que, vous savez, il y a eu le canular Russie, Russie, Russie », déclare Donald Trump.
Le républicain a aussi estimé que c’était l’occasion d’en apprendre plus « sur la fraude électorale, toute la fraude électorale qui a eu lieu ». Il s’est défendu en prétendant vouloir toujours « voir les choses de manière positive ». Pour le moment, personne ne sait qui est derrière la cyberattaque. Le FBI n’a pointé du doigt aucun suspect. Rien ne relie actuellement cette intrusion à ShinyHunters, le gang de cybercriminels qui a piraté le portail de recrutement du FBI, il y a quelques mois.
À lire aussi : Cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne – des données personnelles ont été volées, des hackers chinois sont suspectés
Une cyberdéfense affaiblie
La cyberattaque survient dans le cadre d’une explosion des incidents de sécurité aux États-Unis… et d’une réduction massive des effectifs consacrés à la cybersécurité depuis le retour de Donald Trump au pouvoir. L’agence fédérale de cybersécurité a été obligée de se séparer de près de 1 000 employés depuis l’arrivée de la nouvelle administration. C’est aussi le cas du FBI.
« Quand on ajoute des adversaires de plus en plus sophistiqués à des infrastructures vieillissantes, la vraie question n’est pas seulement d’empêcher les attaques, mais de s’assurer que les services publics essentiels puissent résister aux perturbations », avertit Chris Grove, de Nozomi Networks.

articles.title: Le smartphone premium Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, noté 9/10, perd 470€ pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra fait partie des smartphones Android les plus polyvalents du moment. Pour le Black Friday, Amazon fait passer son prix de 1 569 euros à 1 099 euros.
Le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra est le modèle le plus ambitieux de la gamme du constructeur coréen. Il mise sur une fiche technique solide, avec une puce Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, un grand écran AMOLED de 6,9 pouces, un quadruple module photo et un stylet S Pen intégré. Mais cette génération de smartphone apporte quelques nouveautés bienvenues, comme le filtre de confidentialité intégré à l'écran et une recharge rapide convaincante. Si vous cherchez un nouveau smartphone aussi puissant qu'élégant, l'offre du Black Friday sur Amazon est intéressante puisque le Galaxy S26 Ultra perd 470 euros jusqu'à la fin du mois de novembre 2026.
Voici le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra à 1 099 € au lieu de 1 569 € sur Amazon
Pourquoi choisir le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra ?
- Son écran qui protège votre vie privée : sa dalle propose le Privacy Display, un filtre qui réduit l'angle de vision pour empêcher les gens autour de vous de lire par-dessus votre épaule.
- Son appareil photo polyvalent qui permet de s'adapter à quasiment toutes les situations, que ce soit les images ou les vidéos.
- Sa longévité : entre la puce, les 12 Go de RAM et les 7 ans de mises à jour promis, Samsung mise sur le long terme.
Un smartphone taillé pour la photo, la vidéo et la productivité
Avec son écran Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 6,9 pouces en définition QHD+, son taux de rafraîchissement adaptatif jusqu'à 120 Hz et son Privacy Display, le Galaxy S26 Ultra offre un excellent confort pour consulter des contenus, travailler ou utiliser votre smartphone dans les transports sans exposer vos informations personnelles. Son Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 épaulé par 12 Go de RAM lui permet d'être à l'aise quasiment tout le temps, même si les performances diminuent si vous le sollicitez trop longtemps.
Sa batterie de 5 000 mAh permet de tenir une journée complète avant de passer par la case charge filaire de 60 W ou sans fil de 25 W. Les amateurs de photographie profitent d'un capteur principal de 200 Mpx, un ultra grand-angle de 50 Mpx et deux téléobjectifs avec des zooms optiques 3x et 5x. Les vidéastes, eux, peuvent filmer en 8K et profiter des formats LOG et AV422 HQ. Enfin, le S Pen intégré, les fonctions Galaxy AI, la certification IP68 et les sept années de mises à jour promises par Samsung en font un appareil complet, malgré un gabarit imposant de 214 g, l'absence de Bluetooth sur le stylet et un chargeur secteur non fourni.
Un concurrent sérieux face aux meilleurs smartphones haut de gamme
Le Galaxy S26 Ultra a de sérieux arguments face à ces concurrents, notamment son stylet S Pen, son Privacy Display et sa polyvalence, mais le Xiaomi 17 Ultra et l'Oppo Find X9 Ultra peuvent séduire davantage les amateurs de photographie et de grande autonomie. Le modèle de Samsung reste notamment pénalisé par sa batterie de 5 000 mAh et par une baisse des performances en charge prolongée, deux concessions à prendre en compte face aux autres flagships.
✅ Les points forts
- Les qualités de son écran
- La fonction Privacy Display
- Le Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 avec 12 Go de RAM
- Le module photo
- La recharge filaire 60 W et 25 W en sans fil
- Le S Pen intégré
❌ Les limites
- Son design proche des générations précédentes
- La batterie de 5 000 mAh ne progresse pas
- Les baisses de fréquence du processeur
- Le zoom numérique qui perd en détails au-delà du 30x
- Pas de chargeur intégré
Grâce au Black Friday, le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra passe de 1 569 € à 1 099 € sur Amazon
À 1 099 euros contre 1 569 euros à son lancement, le Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra est une proposition intéressante. Cette baisse de 470 euros permet de profiter d'un haut de gamme complet et polyvalent. Ce n'est pas pour rien qu'il a obtenu 9/10 avec le label Prix d'excellence décerné par la rédaction.
Il faut toutefois garder en mémoire que son autonomie ne progresse pas vraiment, que son design reste assez conservateur et que ses performances diminuent lors des usages intensifs. Si vous avez déjà un Galaxy S25 Ultra, le changement n'est pas indispensable. Si ce n'est pas le cas, cette remise le rend plus facile à envisager.

articles.title: Ya es oficial el nuevo Samsung Odyssey G6, el primer monitor gaming del mundo con 1.100 Hz
articles.text:
Samsung acaba de anunciar un nuevo monitor para su línea Odyssey. Este, llamado Odyssey G6 (G60H), tiene bastantes cosas a destacar, aunque hay una que lo hace por encima del resto: según el fabricante coreano, es el primer monitor gaming del mundo en alcanzar los 1.100 Hz. Aún no sabemos ni precio ni fecha de lanzamiento, pero os lo contamos todo sobre él.
Llega con resolución dual y una nueva función llamada Odyssey Clear Motion
El nuevo Odyssey G6, que llegará con una diagonal de 27 pulgadas, sigue la misma línea que el Odyssey G8 G80HF que analizamos hace unos meses. Eso quiere decir que estamos ante un monitor con doble resolución, algo que estamos viendo cada vez en más monitores. La idea de esto es muy fácil de entender: pulsando un botón, podremos cambiar la resolución del monitor.
En el caso de este nuevo monitor de Samsung, podremos cambiar entre resolución Full HD y QHD. Y es precisamente ahí donde está lo más destacable del mismo, puesto que en la primera es donde alcanza los 1.100 Hz, mientras que si elegimos resolución QHD, tendremos una tasa de fresco de hasta 600 Hz. De esta forma, el usuario puede elegir entre una experiencia más fluida o una más nítida.
Otro punto clave del nuevo monitor de Samsung es que estrena nueva tecnología llamada Odyssey Clear Motion. Esta, en esencia, tiene como objetivo reducir el desenfoque de movimiento que se produce a la hora de jugar cuando movemos rápidamente la cámara. Es el primer monitor del fabricante en utilizar esta novedad, aunque la compañía promete llevarlo a más monitores gaming.
Para terminar, cabe mencionar que es compatible con HDR10+ Gaming, NVIDIA G-Sync y FreeSync Premium de AMD. Además, cuenta con un DisplayPort 2.1 y dos puertos HDMI 2.1, por lo que podemos conectar varios dispositivos al mismo, como un ordenador o una consola. Para terminar, como es costumbre en los Odyssey de Samsung, cuenta con un diseño minimalista que permite ajustar el monitor tanto en inclinación como en rotación de forma sencilla.

articles.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meeting that covered remorse, therapy, and even the company’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media.
The topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky issue seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy.
Investors and analysts saw the issue differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy.
Nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and says he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings.
Huang has previously defended the company’s structure in numerous interviews, including one in March with podcaster Lex Fridman.
“When you’re designing a company, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang said in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.”
Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

articles.title: Developer turns the MacBook's trackpad into a tiny robotic speaker
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Hitting mute on a MacBook is supposed to shut it up. A new open-source tool can still get one talking, though, and the voice comes straight out of the trackpad. It works by buzzing the small haptic motor that normally fakes each click, just fast enough to turn those taps into robotic speech.
Cody Collier, the developer behind the project, posted a demo on X over the weekend. In the clip, his MacBook reads lines aloud in a buzzy, robotic voice between bursts of chiptune-style beeps. It's a familiar kind of stunt for anyone who has watched floppy drives play entire songs, except this one fits under your palm.
Getting there meant working around Apple, though. The company's public haptics API only lets apps trigger three fixed taps. That's nowhere near enough control for audio, so Collier's tool, called No Speaker, reaches into a private, undocumented macOS framework called MultitouchSupport instead. From there, it can drive the motor up to 4,000 times a second.
 – cody (@codycollier) November 22, 2026
Collier also measured every semitone the trackpad could hit, from 98 Hz up to nearly 4 kHz. Surprisingly, the glass gets fairly loud across most of that range, especially around 1 kHz, where the cleanest notes sit.
Making it talk took a bit more work. The tool first has the built-in macOS voice read the text into memory. Every 10 milliseconds, it then picks out the two strongest formants – the resonances that give vowels their shape – plus the pitch and loudness. The motor plays those back as a pair of tones. Hissy sounds like "s" and "f" turn into quick, high-pitched bursts instead.
Anyone curious can grab No Speaker free on GitHub. It needs a Force Touch trackpad, so in theory any MacBook from 2015 onward should work, along with the Magic Trackpad 2 or newer. So far, though, Collier has only tested it on an M5 Max MacBook Pro. He also recommends setting the laptop on a table, since it gets much quieter on your lap.
The tool never pushes the motor past its normal maximum strength, Collier says. And since MultitouchSupport is undocumented, any macOS update could break the whole thing.
Oddly enough, Microsoft has already filed for a trackpad patent built to do this on purpose. As Windows Latest spotted last year, the company filed a design in 2023 that treats the glass pad itself like a speaker cone. It would use vibrations below 400 Hz for clicks and play audio from there up to 10 kHz. That's more than twice as high as No Speaker can reach on a MacBook.

articles.title: Automotive Power, Charging, Load-Control Solutions at electronica
articles.text:
Vehicle electrical architectures are consolidating into fewer, more capable domain controllers, and each step in that direction raises the demands placed on the power and driver ICs around them. Supply rails must be sequenced and monitored to meet functional safety targets, cabin charging ports are expected to deliver laptop-class power from a 12 V system, and body loads once switched by relays now require diagnostics and programmable current limits.
At electronica in Munich, Southchip addressed these requirements with an automotive electronics exhibit organized around three application areas: intelligent cockpit, intelligent driving, and intelligent powertrain. The booth featured evaluation hardware for four product families: power management ICs (PMICs), USB and wireless charging, ambient lighting, and high-side drivers (HSDs). All of Southchip’s automotive products are AEC-Q100 qualified, and the company has the capability to meet the ASIL-D functional safety level, reflecting its position that quality and reliability come first.
Intelligent Cockpit: Charging and Ambient Lighting
Charging is the area in which Southchip established its reputation. The company’s USB and wireless charging solutions are well recognized by customers in the consumer electronics market, where the company has a strong, proven track record. Southchip now applies that experience to the vehicle cabin, where occupants expect phones, tablets, and laptops to charge as quickly as they do at a desk.
For high-power USB Type-C ports, Southchip demonstrated an EPR 240 W charging solution that pairs the SC8708Q, an 80 V automotive-grade buck-boost controller, with the SC2006Q automotive-grade protocol IC. The design supports 240 W Extended Power Range fast charging in a dual-port configuration. Where board area and component count carry more weight, the SC87580Q integrates the charging function in a single chip. It delivers up to 100 W with only one external MOSFET, reaches a peak efficiency of up to 97%, supports multiple mainstream charging protocols, and can be paralleled for dual PD-port applications. A complete USB module built on the SC8741Q and SC2021Q extended the concept with DisplayPort input and output, allowing a phone to charge while mirroring its screen to the head unit, or VR/AR glasses to charge while receiving video from it.
For wireless charging, the SC50080Q driver IC is compliant with the WPC Qi standard and supports up to 50 W under the Magnetic Power Profile (MPP) and up to 80 W under CPP. High-precision current sensing, foreign object detection, multichannel demodulation outputs, and UVLO, OVP, OCP, and OTP protection are integrated on-chip.
Ambient lighting was represented by the SC90039, a 30-channel ambient light driver MCU that integrates a 32-bit processor, a 2 A buck converter, and a LIN transceiver. Its 30 independent constant-current channels each drive up to 60 mA, with two-channel time-division multiplexing. The device is AEC-Q100 Grade 1 qualified and ASIL-B compliant, and it is supported by visual development tools for light-effect design and system debugging.
Intelligent Driving: Automotive PMIC Portfolio
ADAS domain controllers, cameras, and radar modules each impose distinct requirements on rail count, input range, and supervision. Southchip addresses them with more than ten automotive PMIC variants offering four to nine output channels and input-voltage coverage from 2.7 V to 60 V across the lineup. Spread-spectrum operation and wettable-flank packages are standard across the range, and the domain-control devices add watchdog and FCCU or ERR pin monitoring.
The SC62595Q is an ASIL-D MCU PMIC for ADAS domain control. It integrates seven power rails with more than 100 configurable power and logic functions on a single chip and accepts inputs from 3 V to 60 V. For the SoC side of the controller, the ASIL-D SC6209Q operates from a 2.7 V to 5.5 V input and integrates four 6 A synchronous buck converters and two 400 mA LDOs. Fixed-frequency constant-on-time control provides fast transient response, and multi-page one-time programmable memory with four user pages, selected through a PRESET pin, lets a single part number serve several rail configurations.
For millimeter-wave radar modules, the SC6207Q radar PMIC provides multiple rails from inputs up to 36 V. Its high efficiency reduces self-heating and the associated thermal noise, which supports precise and uniform radar imaging. At the sensor edge, where camera modules leave little board area for power conversion, the SC6206AQ camera PMIC stands out for its footprint: its QFN-18 package is notably smaller than comparable camera PMICs currently on the market. Within that compact package, the device integrates three buck converters and one LDO, operates from 4 V to 19 V, and is ASIL-B capable, with 1% undervoltage and overvoltage monitors and 1.5% output-voltage accuracy. Southchip complemented these devices with the SCP25501 serializer and SCP25502 deserializer, a MIPI A-PHY compliant link that carries camera video at up to 4 Gbps with 1.25 µs of latency.
Intelligent Powertrain: High-Side Drivers and Protection
Southchip’s high-side driver portfolio comprises over 20 part numbers in single-, dual-, and quad-channel configurations. Load-current classes extend from 1 A to 30 A, with on-resistance from 1.2 mΩ at the high-current end to 100 mΩ and above for low-current loads, so designers can match the switch to the load rather than oversizing it.
The SC77101Q single-channel driver offers an adjustable current limit with high monitoring accuracy, along with diagnostic and protection functions that report faults in real time. The four-channel SC77450CQ combines 50 mΩ on-resistance, a 4 V to 28 V input range, 0.5 µA standby current, and 40 V load-dump capability, built on a vertically integrated process.
Two further devices round out the powertrain display. The SC77010Q eFuse supports inputs from 4.5 V to 70 V, covering 12 V, 24 V, and 48 V systems, and provides diagnostics and high-precision current sensing for intelligent control of external FET loads. The SC77870HQ full-bridge driver operates from 4.5 V to 35 V and delivers up to 12 A for domain controller, chassis, and valve applications, with strong transient thermal performance under software-controlled current-limit stall conditions.
Quality, Reliability, and Functional Safety
Across all three application areas, Southchip treats quality and reliability as its top priorities. All of its automotive products are AEC-Q100 qualified, and the company’s development capability extends to ASIL-D. Functional safety classifications are assigned per device, from QM and ASIL-B for camera and lighting functions to ASIL-D for the PMICs that supply ADAS domain controllers. Integrated voltage monitoring, watchdog supervision, current sensing, and fault diagnostics carry the same priorities from the PMICs through to the load switches.
Conclusion
Southchip’s presence at electronica demonstrated a portfolio that spans cabin charging and lighting, safety-rated power management for ADAS, and protected load control for body and powertrain systems. To support European automotive customers, Southchip maintains a dedicated local team in Europe, enabling fast response and hands-on technical support from evaluation through production.

articles.title: LibreOffice endurece regras para código gerado por IA no projeto
articles.text:
LibreOffice endurece regras para código gerado por IA no projeto
Uma das regras da The Document Foundation determina que o desenvolvedor seja capaz de explicar todo o código gerado com inteligência artificial.
Responsável pelo LibreOffice, a The Document Foundation (TDF) continua se mostrando reservada quanto ao uso de inteligência artificial no projeto. No movimento mais recente, a organização anunciou medidas para evitar que códigos gerados com IA sejam enviados ao LibreOffice de modo, digamos, irresponsável.
Na primeira olhada, parece que a TDF está indo contra uma tendência universal. A IA já está presente até no desenvolvimento do Linux, só para termos um exemplo.
Mas a organização não proíbe toda e qualquer contribuição para a sua suíte de escritório que tenha sido gerada com auxílio de IA. O objetivo de suas restrições é prevenir possíveis consequências oriundas do uso indiscriminado desse tipo de tecnologia.
Em linhas gerais, a TDF quer que os desenvolvedores que enviarem códigos ao LibreOffice sejam responsáveis por essas contribuições como se elas tivessem sido escritas totalmente por eles, de modo a favorecer aspectos como desempenho e segurança, presumivelmente.
A TDF anunciou cinco novas regras direcionadas ao uso de modelos de linguagem de larga escala (LLMs) no LibreOffice. São elas:
- autorização prévia: o desenvolvedor deve pedir permissão antes de usar um LLM em seu trabalho no LibreOffice;
- transparência de código: o uso de LLM deve sempre ser informado nos commits (registros das alterações feitas no código);
- compreensão do código gerado: o desenvolvedor precisa ser capaz de explicar todo o código produzido com auxílio de IA;
- restrição de IA em comunicações internas: LLMs não podem ser usados para mensagens de commit, comentários em código, relatórios de bugs ou comunicados a outras pessoas do projeto;
- restrições em partes do código: determinadas partes do código-fonte do LibreOffice não podem contar com contribuições geradas por LLMs.
As políticas de IA da TDF estão resumidas nesta página.
Apesar de haver alguma flexibilidade quanto ao uso de inteligência artificial nas entranhas do projeto, o pacote de escritório em si continua livre desse tipo de tecnologia do ponto de vista funcional. Nesse sentido, vale relembrar que o LibreOffice 26.8 foi lançado tendo a ausência de ferramentas de IA como um diferencial.

articles.title: Congress scrutinizes Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia as Megaspeed restrictions raise questions
articles.text:
Congress scrutinizes Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia as Megaspeed restrictions raise questions
Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are criticizing Nvidia Corp.’s decision to rehire Jensen Huang as its chief executive.
The criticism came against the backdrop of a controversial move by the U.S. Commerce Department. The agency applied new export restrictions to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud operator. The company played a prominent role in the spy controversy that led to Huang’s resignation. According to trade experts, the Commerce Department left out a key clause that is usually included in such restrictions.
Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. Early reporting about the relationship indicated that she was found to have passed intelligence to China. The U.S. Justice Department later stated that it has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang is a spy. Earlier this week, the New York Times reported that she maintained contact with a Chinese intelligence official.
Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang on Monday after U.S. President Donald Trump and tech industry figures urged directors to bring him back. The move drew widespread criticism from members of Congress.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York), who is set to become House Speaker, called the reinstatement “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.” Rep. Don Bacon (R-Nebraska), the chair of House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies and Innovation, said that “it’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO.” Former Utah Republican Senator and Massachusetts Governor Mitt Romney tweeted: “Let me get this straight: we rushed AI along without regulating safeguards in order to stay ahead of China and at the same time, we sold China the very chips they’d need to get ahead of us. Smells of profit, corruption and perhaps worse.”
Multiple lawmakers told CNBC that they plan to scrutinize Huang’s conduct closely. The executive is scheduled to testify before multiple Congressional committees next Tuesday. Furthermore, Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Oregon) told the outlet that Democrats plan to scrutinize the Trump administration’s role in the matter.
The Commerce Department today added Megaspeed and several of its regional affiliates to its Entity List. Companies on the list can only purchase sensitive products such as graphics cards if they obtain a license from the U.S. government. According to Gizmodo, the move has drawn scrutiny because the restrictions applied to Megaspeed include a loophole.
All the companies on the Entity List are prohibited from buying Nvidia’s latest chips unless they secure a license. Most of them are also unable to buy lower-end graphics cards, high-bandwidth memory and related hardware. The latter restrictions are specified in a clause called the FDPR provision. The Commerce Department has reportedly not applied the FDPR provision to Megaspeed when it added the company to the Entity List.
Huang returned to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters on Monday. The news sent the chipmaker’s stock soaring more than 30%, although it parred some of the gains today. Nvidia shares are down 5.8% from Monday.
Wired today published excerpts from Huang’s all-hands meeting with employees. The executive apologized for his affairs and for his management style, which has also come under scrutiny in recent days. He added that he will undergo a “360-degree review” and that Nvidia’s code of conduct is still in effect.

articles.title: ASRock Industrial Unveils Robotics-in-a-Box to Democratize Physical AI Development
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
ASRock Industrial Unveils Robotics-in-a-Box to Democratize Physical AI Development
ASRock Industrial, a global provider of industrial computing and edge AI solutions, today announced the launch of RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box. Designed to simplify robotic AI development and make hands-on experimentation more accessible to researchers, educators, and developers, RBK-100 is an integrated Physical AI development platform powered by the ASRock Industrial NUC BOX-358H featuring the Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H. RBK-100 integrates local AI computing, an RGB depth camera, a 6-DOF leader-and-follower robotic arm set, and pre-installed AiRoboStarter software in a ready-to-use development platform. By integrating edge AI computing, visual perception, robotic manipulation, and software workflows, RBK-100 reduces system integration complexity and enables users to focus on AI model experimentation, robotic skill development, and real-world Physical AI applications.Key Capabilities of RBK-100 Robotics-in-a-Box
- AI-Ready Edge Computing: Powered by the Intel Core Ultra X7 Processor 358H in the NUC BOX-358H, RBK-100 delivers local AI computing capabilities for robotic development, AI model experimentation, and Physical AI workflows. The platform comes with 32 GB DDR5 memory in the standard configuration or 64 GB DDR5 memory in the Advanced configuration, along with a 512 GB PCIe Gen 4 SSD.
- Integrated Robotic Vision and Manipulation: An integrated RGB-D camera captures color and depth information for robotic perception and object interaction. Combined with a 6-DOF leader-and-follower robotic arm set, the platform enables developers to record demonstrations and explore AI-based pick-and-place, object handling, and learned robotic skills.
- Physical AI Development with AiRoboStarter: The standard configuration includes 32 GB DDR5 memory and pre-installed AiRoboStarter software, providing a streamlined environment for developing, training, and executing robotic skills. Its workflow spans demonstration recording, dataset review, model training, and robot skill execution, with support for model workflows including ACT, Pi0.5, and SmolVLA support planned for a future release.
- Optional Agentic AI Integration with AiRoboStarter Advanced: Available with the 64 GB configuration, AiRoboStarter Advanced extends the development environment with an integrated agentic AI workflow connecting voice interaction, AI reasoning, visual perception, and trained robotic skills. Capabilities include speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), large language models (LLMs), vision, object detection, web search, custom APIs, and robot skill integration. Supported models, features, and performance depend on the software release and validated configuration.
"Physical AI represents an important step forward in bringing intelligence into the physical world," said James Lee, Chairman of ASRock Industrial. "Building on our expertise in edge AI computing, we see tremendous potential in making Physical AI development more accessible and practical. Through Robotics-in-a-Box, developed in collaboration with Intel, we aim to simplify the development journey from AI experimentation to real-world robotic applications, empowering researchers, educators, and developers to explore new possibilities and accelerate innovation in Physical AI."
"Scaling Physical AI requires more than powerful AI. It requires an open technology foundation that makes complex robotic systems easier to develop and deploy," said John Healy, vice president and general manager of the Industrial and Robotics Division, Intel. "Powered by Intel Core Ultra processors, ASRock's Industrial Robotics-in-a-Box gives researchers and developers an integrated platform to accelerate experimentation and turn promising robotics concepts into practical, real-world applications."

articles.title: 'No recruiting team can talk to thousands of people': But study finds 90% of recruiters admit they turned away real candidates they thought were AI
articles.text:
'No recruiting team can talk to thousands of people': But study finds 90% of recruiters admit they turned away real candidates they thought were AI
Is AI really helping recruitment?
- Around 90% of hiring teams have turned down applicants from real people because of concerns over the applicant’s use of AI
- Jobseekers are using AI in different ways, from polishing CVs to including AI-targeted text to ensure the application is seen by a human
- 79% of recruiters use AI in the hiring process
AI’s impact on the world of recruitment has been highlighted in the latest Hire Standard report from Greenhouse, which reveals 89% of hirers have turned away real applicants because of their use of AI.
Yet a significant 79% of hirers use AI in their process, typically for filtering applications.
At a time when only 5% of job candidates are able to reach the interview stage, it seems that attempts to game the AI application screening are not going well – on either side.
Who is cheating?
Greenouse’s report also shows that companies who spot or suspect cheating on applications are three times as likely to overcompensate, and filter out the genuine applicants.
Yet the reported results from the survey also show a successful side to the use of AI in hiring. Among the recruitment teams using AI, 36% say they have found candidates that they would otherwise have overlooked.
UK and Irish figures from the results of the survey of 1,300+ recruiters have been provided, shared within Greenhouse’s Fall 2026 Hire Standard report. While they do paint a remarkable picture of AI use by applicants to get around the challenges of AI filtering, there are of course two sides to this.
Hiring teams have put themselves into a position where they are happy to use AI to filter applications. Yet an incredible 96% of recruiters consider candidates using the technology to be cheating.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Today, only five in 100 applications ever reach an interview, and adding more human interviews can’t close that gap," noted Daniel Chait, CEO and co-founder of Greenhouse.
His solution may not be welcome by applicants, however. According to Chait, “The fix is scaling the top of the funnel by opening up a voice AI interview to every applicant.” Recent discourse, particularly among job searchers on LinkedIn, would suggest that this may not be a particularly popular solution.
“Letting more people get a real first conversation sooner. People should stay accountable for every hiring decision, but AI can afford opportunities that people alone cannot," Chait added.
The scale of the task
Recruitment in an age when everyone is connected is clearly difficult, with huge demand for every role.
Ophir Samson, Head of Voice AI at Greenhouse, says that while it might be framed as an AI versus human challenge, “for most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table. No recruiting team can talk to thousands of people. The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story. Every candidate should get the second.”
The question is, if a human isn’t even listening, does the candidate want that 15 minutes?
