articles.title: 1 000 créneaux en 24h : pourquoi ces voitures électriques chinoises tournent en rond dans les parkings la nuit ?
articles.text:
La vidéo a de quoi surprendre. À 6 heures du matin, deux voitures électriques Avatr 06 et 12 manœuvrent côte à côte en parfaite synchronisation dans le sous-sol désert d’un parking. Capturées par les caméras de surveillance, ces vidéos montrent plusieurs modèles dotés du système intelligent Huawei Qiankun en train de tourner en rond. Loin d’être un phénomène surnaturel, l’explication vient tout simplement d’un concours organisé par Huawei pour récompenser l’usage de son aide au stationnement.
La course aux points qui fait tourner les têtes (et les voitures)
Du 31 octobre au 13 novembre 2026, la deuxième édition du championnat de conduite intelligente Huawei Qiankun a rassemblé plus de 190 000 participants. Dans la catégorie dédiée au stationnement, les cent meilleurs utilisateurs cumulant le plus de créneaux automatiques réussis gagnaient des points utilisables chez la marque. Prêts à tout pour grimper dans le classement, certains propriétaires ont répété les manœuvres à la chaîne, un conducteur affirmant même avoir franchi le cap des 1 000 sessions en 24 heures.
Problème de réglage horaire ou mauvaise lecture du règlement du concours, les vidéos diffusées montrent des véhicules s’activer entre minuit et 6 heures du matin, alors que le comptage s’arrêtait à 22 heures. Ces véhicules qui dansent en pleine nuit n’apportent donc aucun point supplémentaire à leurs conducteurs.
Capteurs capricieux, manœuvres à distance ou bug ?
Trois raisons peuvent expliquer ces rondes nocturnes sans fin. Lancées depuis un smartphone via l’application, les manœuvres de stationnement à distance ont pu être déclenchées volontairement par des conducteurs. Le mauvais éclairage, des marquages au sol effacés ou des espaces étroits peuvent également poser problème à la voiture qui relance alors le créneau encore et encore. La dernière piste est tout simplement celle du bug logiciel, mais cela n’a pour l’instant pas encore été confirmé.
À lire : GTA 6 pousse le réalisme des voitures électriques très loin, mais oublie un détail essentiel
Comme l’indique la réglementation chinoise, les fonctions de stationnement automatique sont bridées à 30 km/h dans le pays et demandent une supervision humaine permanente. Chez Avatr, la documentation technique indique une vitesse d’exécution plafonnée à 5 km/h avec arrêt d’urgence en cas d’obstacle. Quoi qu’il en soit, cet étrange balai des voitures dans les parkings rappelle que les fonctions d’aide au stationnement sont encore loin d’être infaillibles.

articles.title: Goldman Sachs, Societe Generale buy Rs 920-Cr stake in Lenskart
articles.text:
Goldman Sachs, Societe Generale buy Rs 920-Cr stake in Lenskart
The investors acquired a total of 1,26,97,702 equity shares on Monday, amounting to a 0.73% stake in Lenskart, as per the stock exchange data.
Global financial giants Goldman Sachs and Societe Generale together bought nearly a 1% stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart Solutions for Rs 920 crore through separate block deals on the NSE.
The investors acquired a total of 1,26,97,702 equity shares on Monday, amounting to a 0.73% stake in Lenskart, as per the stock exchange data.
Goldman Sachs through its affiliates purchased 65.21 lakh shares in Gurugram-based Lenskart, while Societe Generale (SocGen) acquired 61.76 lakh shares of the company at an average price of Rs 725 apiece on the NSE.
The transactions amounted to a total value of Rs 920.58 crore.
On the selling side, San Francisco-based Steadview Capital Management offloaded an equal number of shares through its two affiliates at the same price on the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
Following the stake sale, global investment firm Steadview's holding in Lenskart has come down to 2.58% from 3.31%.
Shares of Lenskart fell nearly 4% to close at Rs 715.90 apiece on Monday.
Earlier this month, US-based Goldman Sachs and French financial services group Societe Generale were among the investors that acquired shares of Lenskart from Japanese technology investor SoftBank for Rs 1,896 crore.

articles.title: Astelia's autonomous network mitigation blocks AI-driven exploits without a patch
articles.text:
Astelia’s autonomous network mitigation blocks AI-driven exploits without a patch
Exposure management company Astelia Inc. today announced the launch of autonomous network mitigation, a new capability that allows organizations to block artificial intelligence-driven exploits at the network level, even when a patch isn’t available or can’t be applied.
The new capability has been designed to address what Astelia says is the problem of frontier AI models cutting the time to exploit to almost zero, leaving manual triage and remediation unable to keep up. Astelia argues that autonomous remediation isn’t a viable option for large enterprises, where every patch requires a change window so it doesn’t break important business processes. In many cases, there is also no patch to apply because the vendor hasn’t released a fix yet or, for older and end-of-life systems, never will.
“For years, security teams have been told to patch faster,” said co-founder and Chief Executive Alon Noy, adding that the advice “stops working when the exploit arrives before the change window does.”
Autonomous network mitigation is designed to block the path an attacker would use to reach a vulnerable system instead of changing the system itself. Mitigations are applied automatically within policies the organization sets. Nothing on the asset is changed, allowing business-critical systems, including operational technology, to stay online.
Underpinning the service is Astelia’s reachability analysis, which maps an organization’s real network topology and applies agentic AI to analyze the requirements of each exploit. By correlating exploit conditions with network topology, the platform identifies which vulnerabilities are reachable by attackers and through which paths. In one enterprise deployment, approximately 40 million vulnerabilities were reduced to fewer than 2,000 that were reachable, according to the company.
Key features of autonomous network mitigation include the ability to identify the most effective choke point on an attack path and drive the mitigation through an organization’s web application firewall or intrusion prevention and detection system. A single rule at a choke point is said to protect every vulnerable server behind it, compared with one change per server when patching. Because mitigations are only applied to paths that have been proven reachable, the service doesn’t add rules for exposure that doesn’t exist.
Every mitigation applied by Astelia can also be rolled back, something that isn’t always possible with a patch. That is said to allow teams to act quickly without putting business operations at risk.
Autonomous network mitigation can be deployed through Astelia Agents, the company’s suite of AI agents, as a dedicated agent that applies mitigations on its own. The agent can also be connected with other agents to respond to urgent threats such as zero-day vulnerabilities and critical disclosures. Astelia gave the example of the PHP2Shell remote code execution flaws disclosed in October, which left end-of-life PHP servers with no official fix.
Each organization sets its own guardrails on how mitigations are applied. Users can require human approval for specific environments or actions, according to the company. Every action is logged and can be audited. Analysis on the Astelia platform continues to run on read-only integrations, with mitigation actions using scoped permissions that each organization enables and controls.
Autonomous network mitigation initially supports web application firewall and intrusion prevention and detection rules, with support for firewall rules planned in the future.
Founded in 2024 by former leaders of the Israeli National Red Team, Astelia is a venture capital-backed company that raised $35 million in combined seed and Series A funding in February. Investors in the company include Index Ventures, Team8 and Holly Ventures.

articles.title: Sièges chauffants par abonnement : New York interdit de faire payer des options déjà installées d’usine
articles.text:
Sièges chauffants, puissance du moteur, suspension pilotée : de plus en plus de voitures sortent d’usine avec du matériel bloqué par logiciel, que le constructeur propose ensuite de débloquer contre paiement. Les marques ont trouvé là une nouvelle façon de faire payer les automobilistes tous les mois, et les pouvoirs publics commencent à réagir. La Chine a déjà encadré les mises à jour à distance des voitures en avril 2025.
Au tour de New York. Ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, la gouverneure démocrate de l’État, Kathy Hochul, a signé une loi contre ces abonnements. À partir du 27 février 2027, un constructeur ou un concessionnaire ne pourra plus facturer chaque mois des sièges chauffants déjà montés sur une voiture achetée ou louée dans l’État.
Le texte de loi, porté par le sénateur James Skoufis et le député William Magnarelli, a été voté par les deux chambres en mai et juin 2026. Il interdit tout abonnement (un paiement récurrent, hebdomadaire, mensuel ou annuel) pour une fonction qui remplit deux conditions à la fois :
- Le matériel doit déjà être installé au moment de l’achat ou de la location,
- La fonction doit marcher une fois activée sans coût permanent pour le constructeur, le concessionnaire ou un prestataire.
Côté sanctions, l’amende plafonne à 250 dollars (environ 230 euros) par point de vente et par infraction.
Abonnement aux sièges chauffants interdit, conduite assistée épargnée
Le texte cite lui-même les sièges chauffants comme exemple, tandis que James Skoufis ajoute le démarrage à distance. En revanche, la loi exclut noir sur blanc toute une liste de services :
- les mises à jour de la navigation et les fonctions d’info-divertissement,
- la radio satellite, le Wi-Fi embarqué et la télématique (les données que la voiture échange avec le constructeur),
- l’assistance routière,
- les aides à la conduite et la conduite automatisée qui reposent sur le logiciel,
- tous les services qui ont besoin d’un réseau mobile pour fonctionner.
Pourtant, le communiqué de la gouverneure cite la « conduite mains libres » et la « navigation améliorée » parmi les fonctions visées, alors que le texte les écarte. Tesla devrait donc encore être autorisé à vendre son option Full Self-Driving.
Le texte de loi ne précise pas non plus ce qu’il en est des achats comptant après livraison du véhicule comme l’Acceleration Boost de Tesla, un gain de puissance purement logiciel vendu 1 800 €. Ce genre de fonctionnalité rentre pourtant clairement dans le giron de la proposition américaine.
En Europe, ces abonnements existent déjà
Volkswagen proposait en Allemagne 27 ch de plus pour l’ID.3 Pro, contre 18,90 euros par mois ou 629 euros en une fois. Le moteur est le même que celui de la version plus puissante, et la puissance redescend dès qu’on résilie l’abonnement. À New York, cette formule mensuelle tomberait vraisemblablement sous le coup de la loi.
BMW a fait marche arrière début 2026. Au Royaume-Uni, le constructeur allemand facturait 15 livres par mois (environ 17 euros) pour chauffer les sièges avant et 10 livres (environ 11 euros) pour le volant, avant de supprimer ces abonnements face aux critiques.
Ces options restent pourtant à débloquer contre un paiement unique, et la suspension adaptative est toujours proposée par abonnement sur certains modèles. La marque avait aussi été épinglée cet été pour une publicité Spider-Man diffusée à bord de ses modèles.
La loi new-yorkaise ne vaut d’ailleurs que pour les voitures vendues ou louées dans l’État, et ses modalités restent à préciser. La loi autorise le département d’État de New York, l’administration chargée de l’appliquer, à publier ses règles d’application d’ici au 27 février 2027.

articles.title: Black Friday : le télétravail pour moins de 400€ avec ce PC portable Dell 15 vendu par Amazon
articles.text:
L’ordinateur portable Dell 15 est proposé à 399 € durant le Black Friday d’Amazon. Cette offre peut vous permettre de vous équiper d’une machine adaptée au télétravail et aux déplacements pour moins de 400 €.
Pour rédiger des documents, participer à des réunions en visio ou mettre des présentations en page, il n’est pas nécessaire de vous équiper d’une machine de guerre. Le Dell 15 DC15250 disponible à 399 € chez Amazon peut parfaitement convenir à un usage bureautique grâce à sa configuration composée d’un processeur Intel Core 3 100U, de 8 Go de RAM et d’un SSD de 512 Go. Windows 11 Famille est également installé sur ce PC portable qui se destine aux étudiants et aux travailleurs aux besoins classiques.
Le PC portable Dell 15 et sa configuration bureautique sont proposés à 399 € jusqu’au 30 novembre chez Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le Dell 15 DC15250 ?
- Pour son écran fluide : la dalle Full HD de 15,6 pouces atteint les 120 Hz, ce qui rend les défilements plus agréables.
- Pour son stockage : le SSD de 512 Go laisse de la place pour les logiciels, les documents et les autres fichiers utiles au quotidien.
- Pour son pavé numérique : il facilite la saisie de chiffres dans les tableaux et les outils de comptabilité.
Un grand écran pour les cours et le quotidien
Grâce à son écran de 15,6 pouces doté d’un filtre antireflet, le Dell 15 se présente d’emblée comme un ordinateur portable confortable pour la lecture et la rédaction. Sa définition Full HD est standard dans cette gamme de machines, et elle est adaptée au travail comme au visionnage de vidéos. À l’intérieur, l’association d’un processeur Intel Core 3 100U et de 8 Go de RAM est adaptée aux usages bureautiques et multimédias classiques. Le PC intègre également une webcam et une connectique composée de ports USB-A, d’une sortie HDMI et d’un lecteur de cartes SD.
Un PC qui impose de rester raisonnable en multitâche
Ce Dell 15 est adapté aux usages simples du quotidien, et, même s’il peut être utilisé pour regarder des vidéos en streaming de façon confortable, il n’est pas adapté au gaming intensif. D’ailleurs, ses 8 Go de RAM peuvent même s’avérer limités si vous multipliez l’ouverture d’onglets de navigateurs et de logiciels : il faut en tenir compte, car il n’est peut-être pas aussi multitâche que vous !
✅ Les points forts
- Écran Full HD antireflet à 120 Hz.
- SSD de 512 Go.
- Pavé numérique et lecteur de cartes SD.
❌ Les limites
- Seulement 8 Go de RAM.
- Chargeur vendu séparément.
Pour le Black Friday, le Dell 15 revient à 399 € chez Amazon, mais n’oubliez pas d’acheter un chargeur adapté si vous n’en possédez pas encore.
Le Dell 15 convient tout à fait à la bureautique courante, aux étudiants ainsi qu’aux personnes qui utilisent essentiellement leur ordinateur pour surfer sur Internet. Il est aussi relativement facile à transporter.
En revanche, pour les logiciels créatifs exigeants ou le multitâche soutenu, mieux vaut privilégier une configuration plus musclée, qui vous évitera des frustrations.

articles.title: Empleados de Anthropic y OpenAI temen que sus modelos más potentes sean muy peligrosos para lanzarlos
articles.text:
Los modelos de inteligencia artificial (IA) aún sin lanzar de Anthropic y OpenAI son tan potentes que muchos de sus empleados ya no creen que puedan liberarse de forma segura al público. Lo señaló Axios, con base en más de 24 fuentes que conocen los debates internos de ambas compañías.
Según esas fuentes, los investigadores no encontraron todavía soluciones técnicas para controlar los sistemas más avanzados. Algunos creen que el problema tiene arreglo. Otros dudan y plantean que las empresas deberían dejar de entrenar modelos nuevos por completo.
Axios reportó que el debate incluye una opción intermedia: no publicar los futuros modelos de frontera, es decir, los más avanzados, y reservarlos para uso interno. Las fuentes dijeron que ambas empresas tienen modelos sin lanzar mucho más capaces que los que ofrecen hoy a los usuarios.
Dos problemas de la IA que inquietan a los investigadores
El primero es el método de entrenamiento por refuerzo, en el que el modelo aprende por ensayo y error y recibe recompensas por superar pruebas. Según las fuentes citadas, cuanto más capaz es el sistema, mejor aprende a hacer trampa para obtener esa recompensa, incluso si eso implica saltarse las barreras de seguridad.
El segundo es la pérdida de transparencia. Los investigadores supervisaban a los modelos obligándolos a escribir su razonamiento paso a paso. Ahora, de acuerdo con las fuentes, los sistemas más avanzados muestran menos de su trabajo y en algunos casos ofrecen razonamientos falsos para satisfacer a quienes los vigilan.
“Si seguimos intentando hacer los modelos mucho más inteligentes que nosotros, van a poder engañarnos con éxito”, dijo un investigador a Axios, sin identificarse. “Muchos de los esquemas que hemos usado hasta ahora dejan de servir”, agregó.
Varios empleados de compañías de IA de frontera afirmaron que los ejecutivos perdieron contacto con la gravedad de los riesgos y que temen que prioricen las ganancias sobre la seguridad.
Qué responden las empresas referentes en inteligencia artificial
Un vocero de Anthropic dijo a Axios que mantener un modelo en secreto no lo vuelve seguro y que la responsabilidad de la compañía comienza en el entrenamiento. “Podemos frenar o retener un modelo aunque nos cueste”, señaló el portavoz, quien mencionó demoras en el preentrenamiento de un modelo reciente para reforzar la seguridad.
Un vocero de OpenAI indicó que la empresa adoptó nuevos requisitos de seguridad que podrían ralentizar los lanzamientos. El 18 de noviembre de 2026, la compañía publicó que ahora frena modelos cuando necesita más tiempo, entre ellos GPT-6.1 Astra, y que exige “pruebas más sólidas” de comportamiento alineado durante el entrenamiento.
OpenAI también recuerda que, tras el incidente de Hugging Face de julio, pausó el entrenamiento y la evaluación de sus modelos más capaces entre el 20 de septiembre y el 1 de octubre de 2026. Un sistema interno había aprovechado un error de configuración para obtener acceso limitado a internet.
Una preocupación que ya era pública
En julio de 2026, 1.386 empleados de compañías de IA de frontera firmaron la carta “Pacing the Frontier”. Entre ellos figuran el director ejecutivo de Anthropic, Dario Amodei, y el científico jefe de OpenAI, Jakub Pachocki. Piden al gobierno de Estados Unidos que apoye un esfuerzo internacional para crear herramientas con las que regular el ritmo del desarrollo.
La carta no pide frenar ahora. Según Peter Wildeford, del AI Policy Network, citado por Fortune, quienes la firmaron no quieren una pausa, pero sí la posibilidad de aplicarla si hace falta.
Axios cerró su reportaje con una advertencia: quienes están más cerca de la frontera de la tecnología dan la alarma, y no está claro quién los escucha. Ninguna de las dos empresas anunció hasta ahora que dejará de publicar sus modelos.

articles.title: Lo nuevo de BYD se llama Shark y es una pick-up híbrida con la mayor batería de su segmento
articles.text:
BYD sigue sus lanzamientos en la recta final del año. Si la semana pasada era el nuevo Seal U 2027, ahora es el turno de Shark, que llega con un nuevo modelo de tipo pick-up a un precio muy interesante y con la tecnología de hibridación de la compañía que tanto se ha aclamado.
El nuevo BYD Shark llega con una carrocería de doble cabina y unos impresionantes 5,46 metros, y, como decimos, lo hace con la tecnología DMO (Dual Mode Off-road) con hasta 90 km de autonomía 100% eléctrica (675 km en combinada) y grandes capacidades todoterreno con unos impresionantes 436 CV y 650 Nm de par. Una potencia que le permite, pese a su peso y tamaño, acelerar de 0 a 100 en solo 5,7 segundos y ganándose por el camino las 5 estrellas de Euro NCAP.
BYD Shark: dos motores eléctricos y una gran autonomía combinada
En su apartado de hibridación, cuenta con un motor de gasolina turboalimentado de 1,5 litros y cuatro cilindros (de 150 CV y 240 Nm), usado principalmente como generador de electricidad para los motores eléctricos y la carga de la batería, aunque también puede generar propulsión; y dos motores eléctricos: uno delantero de 231 CV (170 kW) y 310 Nm, y otro trasero de 204 CV (150 kW) y 340 Nm.
Complementa el conjunto una batería de tipo Blade Battery de 32,2 kWh, según BYD la de mayor capacidad del segmento pick-up en Europa, integrada en un chasis de largueros y travesaños, ya que usa la tecnología CTC (Cell-to-Chassis) y, como decíamos, homologa una autonomía eléctrica en ciclo combinado de 90 km y alrededor de 110 km en ciclo urbano y una autonomía combinada de 675 km. Esto supone unos consumos ponderados de 3,5 l/100 km² y de 9,6 l/100km a nivel mínimo de carga. Respecto a su carga, admite corriente alterna trifásica de 11 kW, con unos tiempos de 3,2 horas del 15% al 100%, y carga rápida en corriente continua de hasta 55 kW: sobre 21 minutos del 30% al 80%.
Respecto a su apuesta tecnológica en el interior, integra una pantalla digital para la instrumentación de 10,25” (26 cm), un Head-Up Display y una pantalla central para el sistema de infoentretenimiento de 15,6”.
Un detalle interesante de este BYD Shark es que incorpora la función Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) de 6 kW, que permite alimentar dispositivos eléctricos externos, bien para el trabajo o para el ocio en acampada, mediante dos tomas de corriente.
BYD Shark, precio y disponibilidad
¿Y su precio? Llega en una única versión llamada Design, que parte desde los 41.521 euros sin IVA (50.240 euros IVA incluido) y cuenta con una garantía oficial de 6 años o 150.000 km para el coche y de 8 años o 250.000 km para la Blade Battery. Y ya está disponible en los concesionarios de BYD.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms authentication issues after November updates
articles.text:
Microsoft has confirmed that customers may experience authentication issues after installing November security updates that address a high-severity remote code execution vulnerability.
Tracked as CVE-2026-118737, this security flaw was found in the Windows Remote Procedure Call Runtime and stems from a timing-dependent authentication weakness that unauthenticated attackers can exploit to remotely execute code without user interaction on unpatched systems.
Microsoft says the November security updates represent the first phase of NTLM message-signing improvements, which reduce exposure to relay attacks by ensuring authenticated NTLM sessions always establish a cryptographic session key and negotiate real message signing.
However, as Microsoft explained in an updated support document, the new security improvements introduced to address this vulnerability may also cause authentication failures on patched devices.
"Microsoft is aware of compatibility issues affecting some third-party apps and devices, including authentication proxy servers, single sign-on (SSO) solutions, and application packaging solutions that use NTLM authentication," it said.
"This issue can occur when such a proxy device does not correctly implement the NTLM protocol. For example, an affected device might set the NTLMSSP_NEGOTIATE_TARGET_INFO flag in its CHALLENGE_MESSAGE but provide an empty or incomplete TargetInfo field."
While a fix is not yet available, Microsoft said affected apps and devices return an NTLMSSP_CHALLENGE message with an empty "Target Info List" in network trace signatures or Target Machine fields with "Not Found" values in event logs.
As a temporary workaround, the company advised customers to go through the following procedure on affected systems:
- Set the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm REG_DWORD registry value under HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 to 1 (the value used for clients that do not offer SIGN)
- Check whether the affected device or application supports a configuration that uses Kerberos authentication or whether the vendor provides a software or firmware update compatible with the NTLM signing requirements introduced by CVE-2026-118737.
- If neither option is available, contact the device or software vendor to request an update that complies with the NTLM protocol requirements described in 3.1.5.1.2 Client Receives a CHALLENGE_MESSAGE from the Server.
However, Microsoft said the ClientAllowUnsignedNtlm registry setting is a short-term solution and may be removed in the future.
"Updating the affected product or using a compatible authentication configuration is the recommended long-term resolution," it noted.
Since it addressed installation issues affecting the November 2026 cumulative updates, Microsoft has also confirmed that this month's security updates are causing Windows activation failures and SQL Server performance issues.
The company is also investigating a known issue that may break printing documents with complex formatting for customers who have installed the latest Windows updates.

articles.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report
articles.text:
U.S. officials suspect Iranian hackers may be behind as many as 50 cyberattacks targeting shipping vessels in recent weeks, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.
The ships carrying oil, liquefied gas, and other explosive chemicals were hacked as they traveled across Asia and Europe. Several oil tankers headed toward the U.S. coast in August also had their navigation systems breached, prompting cybersecurity teams within the FBI and Coast Guard to board the vessels.
The report said officials are investigating if Iran is expanding its recent wave of hacks against the U.S. by targeting large vessels to sow fear among shippers, disrupt routes, or to cause an explosion at a port. (Ships have backup controls in the event that automated systems are hacked or fail.)
Hackers may have been abusing a bug dubbed FortiBleed, which allows hackers to break into networks by compromising vulnerable Fortinet-made routers. A joint FBI-Coast Guard security alert from September warned that Fortinet routers are used on shipping vessels.
Iran has been firing back on all sides since the start of the U.S./Israel-led war earlier this year, which killed the country’s supreme leader. Many of Iran’s retaliations have been in the form of cyberattacks, with U.S. officials blaming Iran for hacks targeting hundreds of American water providers and U.S. medical tech companies.
A spokesperson for the FBI did not respond to a request for comment about the shipping hacks or whether it had a more accurate figure.

articles.title: GTA VI hacker who used a Fire Stick to breach Rockstar walks free on the day he's sentenced
articles.text:
TL;DR: Arion Kurtaj broke into Rockstar Games using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into a hotel television, a Bluetooth keyboard, and a mouse, and took nearly an hour of footage from the unreleased Grand Theft Auto 6. On Tuesday, a London court sentenced the 21-year-old Lapsus$ hacker to seven years in prison and then released him "on licence," the British version of parole, which lets an offender serve the rest of a sentence in the community under conditions and allows a return to prison if those conditions are broken.
The judge decided that Kurtaj had already served enough time between his stay in a secure hospital and his period "on remand," the British term for being held in jail while awaiting trial or sentencing. He was sent off with a warning: "Don't let this happen again."
Kurtaj had no computer when he attacked Rockstar in 2022. Police had seized his equipment, and he was out on bail, staying under police protection at a Travelodge in Bicester. Rival hackers had threatened him over the Bitcoin he had stolen, and the protection was meant to keep him safe from them.
Inside the hotel room, a streaming device and a few wireless peripherals were all he needed to get back online and into one of the games industry's most closely guarded projects.
He took internal company data, including 90 clips totaling nearly 60 minutes of GTA 6 gameplay. Rockstar had kept the game tightly under wraps until its release last week. Kurtaj then got into the studio's internal Slack workspace and posted a demand: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code." Rockstar refused to engage. He then published the clips and the source code on a forum under the name TeaPotUberHacker.
Rockstar said recovering from the breach cost $5 million and thousands of staff hours. The leak also gave away a marketing secret the company had been protecting: one of the game's playable characters is a woman.
 – Crown Prosecution Service (@CPSUK) November 16, 2026
The Rockstar attack was one of several Kurtaj carried out at ages 16 and 17 as a member of Lapsus$. During the same period on bail, he also breached Revolut and Uber. The group's attacks on those firms and on BT/EE did not depend on new exploits. The hackers used social engineering, tricking people into clicking malicious links or handing over sensitive information, and that gave them access to internal systems. In the Uber case, the court heard that Kurtaj posted an image of a penis while trying to pressure the company into paying a ransom.
Damage to the companies is estimated at around £10 million. The gang also used the stolen corporate data to target cryptocurrency investors. Prosecutors said individual victims lost at least $300,000.
Because of the severity of his autism, Kurtaj was first ordered to be held indefinitely in a secure hospital. He was later found fit to stand trial and was moved to an ordinary prison in January. He pleaded guilty last Monday to the Rockstar hack and several others.
He also admitted physically assaulting staff while in custody, including several biting incidents. In prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending police a taunting text and posting updates on Snapchat.
His defense argued that the internet was where Kurtaj felt most at ease. They said he first met people who taught him to cheat at games and then "people who were involved in hacking." They said he was "very isolated" during the pandemic and that his "connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously."
JJustice Turner acknowledged Kurtaj's technical abilities during the hearing. "You are a very talented young man," he told Kurtaj.
His release comes with restrictions on his online activity. A Serious Crime Prevention Order will be in force for five years and will bar him from using Telegram and Discord, among other restrictions. He used Telegram for his ransom demand to Rockstar.
City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online."

articles.title: Valentí Fuster, cardiólogo, 83 años: "Es absurdo pensar que viviremos hasta los 120 años, cuando nadie está hablando de la calidad de vida"
articles.text:
El cardiólogo Valentí Fuster está convencido de que se habla mucho de vivir más años y muy poco de la calidad con la que se viven. Lo defendió el 13 de noviembre de 2026 en la conferencia “Cuestión a resolver: longevidad versus calidad de vida”, que pronunció en el Aula Magna de la Universitat Abat Oliba CEU de Barcelona. Y lo resumió con una frase: “Es absurdo pensar que viviremos hasta los 120 años, cuando nadie está hablando de la calidad de vida, y este es el problema”.
Quién habló y dónde. Fuster, nacido en Barcelona en 1943, compagina la dirección general del Centro Nacional de Investigaciones Cardiovasculares (CNIC), en Madrid, con la presidencia del Mount Sinai Fuster Heart Hospital de Nueva York, donde además es médico jefe del hospital Mount Sinai. La charla fue la primera conferencia de la Facultad de Ciencias de la Salud y de la Vida de la universidad, tal y como destacó Juan Corona, rector honorario del centro. Y llegó poco después de que la facultad estrenara, en septiembre, su grado en Medicina. Tras el acto, organizado por Consilium Doctorum, el cardiólogo recibió la medalla de miembro de honor de esa entidad.
La salud, también en el colegio. Una de sus reflexiones más rotundas apuntó a la escuela: “Me río cuando en los medios hablan de vivir muchos años, cuando ni siquiera se habla a los niños de la salud. ¿Cómo es posible que en la primaria de ningún país del mundo haya una asignatura que sea Salud?”. Eso sí, hay matices, porque en Australia el currículo oficial incluye un área de Salud y Educación Física que todos los alumnos cursan desde el primer año de escuela, aunque no como una asignatura de salud independiente.
Pero Fuster no quiso que su mensaje sonara a advertencia sin salida: “No se trata de dar un mensaje negativo. La cuestión es que podemos empezar a tratar las enfermedades, gracias a la ciencia, mucho antes de lo que ahora lo estamos haciendo”. A partir de ahí, ordenó su intervención en tres pilares fundamentales para la salud.
El corazón se mira en el cuello. En la parte cardiovascular repasó los ocho grandes factores de riesgo, que son la obesidad, la hipertensión, la diabetes, el colesterol elevado, la falta de ejercicio, la mala alimentación, el tabaquismo y dormir poco. Este último es el más reciente, y la Asociación Americana del Corazón lo añadió en 2022 a su lista de métricas de salud cardiovascular. Según los estudios que presentó, revisar las carótidas (las arterias del cuello) y analizar esas imágenes con IA para buscar lesiones será determinante para entender también lo que ocurre en las coronarias.
Y es que el estudio REACT, publicado por el CNIC, ha visto que la mayoría de las personas con aterosclerosis en las arterias del corazón también la tiene en las del cuello o las piernas. Fuster fue más allá y se atrevió con una previsión: “Es una tecnología económica y fácil con la inteligencia artificial, que pronto estará disponible a nivel público. Se harán controles de las carótidas a partir de los 20 años”.
Lo que el riego dice del cerebro. Los trabajos que citó relacionan también la microcirculación con la salud cerebral. En personas con algunos factores de riesgo cardiovascular se han visto alteraciones en arterias pequeñas que se asocian a un menor flujo de sangre en el cerebro. Y esos mismos factores se han relacionado con un metabolismo de la glucosa más bajo justo en las zonas del cerebro vulnerables al alzhéimer. Por ahora es una asociación, y el propio cardiólogo señaló que “determinar por qué ocurre eso será clave en los próximos años”.
¿Y qué se puede hacer mientras tanto contra la neurodegeneración? Pues Fuster lo resume en tres recomendaciones con las siglas MSM, que corresponden a movimiento, sociedad y motivación. Vamos, que se trata de hacer ejercicio, hablar con los amigos y tener un propósito.
El pilar más difícil de desgranar. El tercer pilar es el propio envejecimiento del organismo, el más complicado de entender según Fuster, porque tiene que ver con “el daño celular, los telómeros que se acortan, la mitocondria que se daña, la inflamación…”. Varios de esos procesos, como el acortamiento de los telómeros o la disfunción mitocondrial, figuran entre los doce rasgos del envejecimiento que recoge una revisión publicada en ‘Cell’ en 2023. Y todo eso vuelve a estar relacionado, según el cardiólogo, con el colesterol, la diabetes, la hipertensión o la falta de ejercicio físico.
El reto es doble. A la medicina le toca detectar todos esos daños y tratar las enfermedades antes de que aparezcan, mientras que a nosotros nos corresponde centrarnos en prevenir con buenos hábitos y vivir con plenitud, conscientes de lo que significa tener salud.
Para conseguirlo, Fuster recomienda seguir el concepto del paraguas, que le enseñó el patólogo Harold Sheehan durante uno de los veranos que pasó en Inglaterra como estudiante de Medicina: “Se trata de poner foco en todo lo que hacemos, ser constantes, tener paciencia y no sucumbir a las prisas, y sobre todo, trabajar en equipo”. Y lo que sirve para formarse como buen investigador clínico, asegura Fuster, “sirve para todo lo que deseamos hacer en nuestra vida”.

articles.title: Pour le Black Friday 2026, cette tête thermostatique Netatmo notée 5/5 tombe à 45,99 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'objet connecté Netatmo Têtes thermostatiques connectées pour radiateur Vanne additionnelle "5 étoiles" à 45,99 € (-21%)
Actuellement notées 5/5 par notre rédaction, les Netatmo Têtes thermostatiques connectées pour radiateur permettent de régler la température pièce par pièce via une application simple à programmer. Le Black Friday 2026 fait descendre leur prix à 45,99 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 21 % et 12,57 € d'économie.
Netatmo propose ses têtes thermostatiques connectées pour radiateur afin de gérer la température du logement pièce par pièce. Ce dispositif vise à simplifier le réglage du chauffage selon des créneaux horaires définis, évitant les allers-retours manuels vers chaque radiateur. Le produit avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur le banc d'essai.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'appareil descend à 45,99 € chez Amazon, soit environ 21 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (58,56 €). Cette baisse de prix qui permet d'économiser 12,57 € constitue une forte remise.
Une installation simple et un contrôle précis au demi-degré
Le dispositif se distingue par sa facilité de mise en place, qui ne requiert au maximum qu'un tournevis de précision pour certaines vannes compatibles. Comme nous l'avons souligné dans notre test complet, l'application mobile permet ensuite de programmer rapidement les plages de chauffe adaptées au rythme du foyer. La gestion de la chaleur s'effectue de manière fine grâce à un réglage de la température par paliers de 0,5 °C, ce qui permet d'ajuster chaque pièce selon le confort recherché.
Netatmo Têtes thermostatiques connectées pour radiateur
Points forts
- Têtes thermostatiques faciles à installer.
- Un seul outil à prévoir : un tournevis de précision (et encore, juste pour certaines vannes).
- Application de gestion complète et aisée à programmer.
- Température réglable finement par incréments d'un demi-degré.
Points faibles
- La facture grimpe rapidement avec le nombre de radiateurs.
- Têtes thermostatiques assez volumineuses.
- Pas de mesure de température déportée.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
L'organisation du chauffage pièce par pièce
Ce modèle affiche la note maximale à ce jour dans nos tests (5/5). Il permet de piloter la chauffe sans faire le tour physique de chaque équipement du logement. Les têtes thermostatiques restent toutefois assez volumineuses sur le radiateur et n'intègrent pas de capteur déporté pour relever la température loin du corps de chauffe. Ce format conviendra parfaitement aux logements équipés de radiateurs compatibles avec de la place autour des vannes.
Heatzy Pilote : l'autre option face au Netatmo Têtes thermostatiques connectées pour radiateur
Le Heatzy Pilote adopte une approche différente en ciblant les radiateurs électriques par l'intermédiaire de leur fil pilote, avec une note actuelle de 4/5. Ce boîtier permet de programmer et piloter son équipement depuis un smartphone sans exiger de compétences techniques complexes, mais il ne permet pas d'ajuster une consigne chiffrée précise à distance.
Le Heatzy Pilote coûte 2,50 € de plus que les têtes thermostatiques Netatmo, lesquelles conservent l'avantage d'un réglage au demi-degré près et d'une note actuelle de 5/5.
Heatzy Pilote
Points forts
- Installation à portée des moins bricoleurs.
- Application complète.
- Programmation.
- Système de zone de chauffe.
Points faibles
- Limites imposées par la technologie fil pilote.
- Ne tire pas profit des fils pilotes 6 ordres.
- Pas d’interface web pour faciliter certaines opérations.
- Wi-Fi capricieux.

articles.title: "Demasiado grande para caer": EEUU ha trazado una línea clarísima salvando a Jensen Huang y, por tanto, a Nvidia
articles.text:
Tras once días marcados por las caídas bursátiles casi continuadas, el domingo por la noche, el consejo de Nvidia recibió una llamada poco habitual: la de Donald Trump. De acuerdo a lo publicado por Semafor, el presidente en persona les pidió en privado el regreso de Jensen Huang con la misma insistencia con la que lo había hecho en público. Poco después, los directivos votaron por unanimidad que sí.
Lo llamativo es la velocidad del cambio de opinión del consejo. Esos mismos consejeros habían aceptado la dimisión de Huang el 11 de noviembre y ya le buscaban sustituto. Días después reafirmaron que no lo readmitirían. Tal y como ya apuntaron desde The New York Times, en los despachos de Washington y Wall Street comenzó a asentarse una idea impulsada desde el seno del despacho oval: "Nvidia es demasiado grande como para caer".
La presión desde fuera. Según publicaba Axios, Trump presionó para que Huang volviera a tomar las riendas de Nvidia dada su importancia para la economía de EEUU, y lo defendieron presentando al directivo como una víctima del "estado profundo". Elon Musk y Travis Kalanick también activaron sus palancas de presión pidiendo su regreso. Tras la votación que marcaba su retorno, Trump llamó a Huang "gran patriota y tesoro nacional".
Tal y como subrayan en Foreign Policy, Washington nunca dio a Huang la sesión de seguridad habitual cuando investigaba a Alice Huang. El Gobierno consideraba a Nvidia demasiado importante estratégicamente como para cuestionarla o exigirle responsabilidades sobre sus actos.
El Banco de la IA. La clave del papel de Nvidia en el ecosistema de la IA en EEUU es que no solo vende chips: ha dado respaldo financiero a muchas empresas de computación en la nube. Tanto es así, que en el ámbito financiero de Silicon Valley se conoce a la compañía como "banco central de la IA" por las inversiones de la compañía en empresas que desarrollan esta tecnología, para luego venderles sus chips. Si cae Nvidia, buena parte de la economía de la IA cae con ella.
El lunes, tan pronto como se supo de su reincorporación, las acciones de Nvidia se dispararon más del 31%, unos 950.000 millones de dólares. Trump reconoció que la bolsa pudo influir en su decisión, aunque dijo que pesó más el beneficio a largo plazo. Stacy Rasgon, directora general y analista de Bernstein Research, admitió a CNBC que todos sabían del riesgo de depender de una sola persona, pero que todos eligieron ignorarlo.
Dudas que siguen abiertas. Aunque Huang tiene a más de 60 personas a su cargo directo, Nvidia no ha designado a un sucesor para su CEO, lo cual es algo temerario teniendo en cuenta el alcance de la influencia de Nvidia. Pero más preocupante es el hecho de saber que no puedes despedir a tu CEO porque tiene en su mano la estabilidad de uno de los mayores motores económicos de EEUU.
A nivel político, la injerencia de Trump en la restitución de Huang se vigila con recelo. No solo por la guerra de poder interna que se intuye en este caso entre Marco Rubio y JD Vance. La senadora demócrata Elizabeth Warren quiere saber qué funcionarios dieron la información de seguridad nacional que Nvidia citó en su comunicado de restitución de Huang.
Tres comités republicanos de la Cámara han citado a Huang y al asesor jurídico Tim Teter a declarar sobre si realmente Huang representa un riesgo para la seguridad de EEUU por su relación con Alice Huang. Sus respuestas dirán cuánto pesó la presión externa ejercida por Trump en el voto del consejo.

articles.title: Rust 1.100 Ships the Never Type After Ten Years and Five Failed Attempts
articles.text:
The Rust team has released Rust 1.100.0, the language's first three-digit stable version, with a release that finally lands the never type after a decade of work. Announced on 12 November 2026, the release also stabilises the core of the custom allocator API, introduces a DropGuard helper, and gives Cargo opt-in dependency cooldowns and warnings for unused dependencies.
The headline is the stabilisation of !, the canonical uninhabited type for computations that never return a value, such as panic!(), return or an endless loop. Although functions have long used it as a return type, naming it elsewhere, for instance writing Result<T, !> to describe an operation that cannot fail, took ten years and five failed stabilisation attempts to land. The release also makes std::convert::Infallible an alias for !, which is what the type was always intended to be, so existing APIs using Infallible now accept ! transparently.
To make that alias work, the team shipped a small breaking change for the 2015, 2018 and 2021 editions, flipping the never-type fallback from () to ! and matching behaviour already introduced in Rust 2024. The release notes describe the impact as largely unnoticeable but warn that more code may be flagged as unreachable. Developers hitting issues on upgrade are advised to update dependencies first, since fixes for widely used crates have already been published.
The core of the long-awaited allocator_api is also now stable, letting library authors define custom allocators used with Vec and Box through the new Allocator trait. This forms the foundation of the Allocators 1.0 project goal. Critics on the internals forum have argued that Rust still lacks Zig's granular control over allocation because the current design cannot support inline storage, with moves invalidating internal pointers, but the stabilised core is seen as a workable starting point for broader collections support.
On the Hacker News release post, one user noted that some of the changes weren’t mentioned in the blog post for the release:
This release is so big that multiple useful stabilized API aren't event mentioned in the blog post like:
- bool::toggle() https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/primitive.bool.html#met...
- Box::map() https://doc.rust-lang.org/stable/std/boxed/struct.Box.html#m...
- str::trim_prefix(), str::trim_suffix, Path::trim_prefix()
The new global-min-publish-age setting holds back newly published versions by a configurable window, an opt-in defence against malicious crate releases:
[registry]
global-min-publish-age = "3 days"
On Hacker News, developer woodruffw argued cooldowns need to coexist with immediate security patching:
You should do both: you should let normal updates cool down,
and
you should immediately patch security advisories.
One of the biggest ergonomic problems with cooldowns is that many tools let the former goal obstruct the latter. Both should be part of the state machine of resolution itself, rather than things that get layered on.
ImportStatic found on the beta that cargo install ignores the setting entirely and that an update could even downgrade a forced security fix, something the release notes also flag as a known caveat. The approach sits alongside GitHub's Dependabot cooldown protection but builds the age check into dependency resolution itself.
Other notable additions include core::mem::DropGuard for running a closure on every exit path, std::mem::conjure_zst for zero-sized types in unsafe code, plus smaller ergonomic wins such as bool::toggle, str::trim_prefix, str::trim_suffix and Box::map.
Upgrading uses rustup update stable; Rust 1.99 is no longer supported, and 1.101 follows the six-week cadence around 24 December 2026.
Rust is an open-source systems programming language maintained by the Rust Foundation and a global community, designed to empower developers to build reliable and efficient software through strong type safety, memory safety guarantees without a garbage collector, and a mature package ecosystem through Cargo.

articles.title: The Kobo Libra Colour got me back into reading after many years
articles.text:
I used to love reading.
Since I was late to getting a smartphone, my introverted self passed many a long bus ride to school with my nose in a book. But like many, I fear, my easily distracted self became addicted to tech. Not for a lack of interest — I just simply found it hard to focus on reading anymore. I’ve read the odd book over the past number of years, like the memoirs from Canadian Simu Liu and Nintendo legend Reggie Fils-Aimé, but not much more.
But at the end of this summer, I started getting back into reading more — fittingly enough, by using technology. Meeting both of these interests halfway, I took on the opportunity to review a Kobo Libra Colour. And so, as I’ve been using it on-and-off over the past few months, I’ve been finding myself falling back in love with reading. What’s more, some of its unique tech-powered features have enhanced that experience.
First and foremost: the slim form factor. It can’t be overstated just how much I love the 200g weight and size of the 7-inch tablet. As someone who travels often for work, my bags are often stuffed with my laptop, a gaming handheld, snacks, cables and clothes, among other things. And so, having something so compact is truly wonderful.
This is especially true on flights. I’ve had a few to Europe this year, which, naturally, go for 7-plus hours from Toronto. At the same time, the little table you get on the seat in front of you is rather tiny. But with the Libra Colour and its foldable case, I can easily put it on the table alongside other things, like a drink and my phone. (The only downside with the tan case I received with the Kobo is that it’s dirtied fairly easily on my travels.)
But before I go further, I should stress that there were some growing pains. For one, I found the touchscreen a bit finicky. At times, I thought it had actually frozen, only to realize it simply didn’t register my input and I had to use my nails or a stylus. Further, the setup process was decidedly laborious, with the QR code not showing up at first and then the loading process being somewhat slow from there.
But once I was past those pain points, I had a blast going through the storefront to search for books. For a while, I’ve been interested in checking out Dune and Neuromancer, the former due to Canadian Denis Villenueve’s grand cinematic trilogy and the latter since it’s the pioneering cyberpunk work from American-Canadian author William Gibson. Finding and buying these books was satisfyingly quick, as was Michael Mann’s Heat 2, which I’ve wanted to read as a big movie buff, or even something as niche as James Mielke’s biography of legendary Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu.
That said, I quickly realized, to my frustration, that some books weren’t available when I searched, like Dungeon Crawler Carl. After a quick Google search on my phone, I realized it was only on Amazon Kindle. I wasn’t exactly surprised, mind you, as exclusivity defines so much of the entertainment industry, especially in the gaming space, which is my bread and butter. But it was a good early reminder to expect the same in the ebook space — something that wouldn’t really be an issue when buying a paperback or hardcover copy.
But of course, the most important thing is the actual experience of reading itself, and on that front, I love what the Kobo offers. Right away, I was pleased by the variety of lighting options which made it perfect for my red-eye European flight. That, coupled with the compact form factor, made it easy to use, especially as I would inevitably keep shifting in my claustrophobic seat in a futile effort to get comfortable.
I also loved the built-in features to enhance the reading experience. As I started Neuromancer, I was delighted to discover I could click on a word to get a dictionary definition of it. Footnotes are also embedded into the text so you can click on them to see more. Getting all of this within the Kobo, rather than having to break immersion and check my phone, was a game-changer for me. (For instance, one fun fact is that the Vancouver-based Gibson, as he explains in his foreword, wasn’t aware at the time of writing that the book ended up being translated into Chinese, but the footnote confirms, as of May 13, 2018, that Chinese has been added.)
Meanwhile, I appreciated how the Kobo would not only keep track of my reading progress, but also tell me how much I had left in a given chapter. As someone who likes to leave off in a clean spot when putting a piece of media down, knowing that I only had X number of pages left, without having to physically leaf ahead and potentially spoil myself, was really handy.
All of these are welcome features that kept me locked in. And the fact that the ebook has a crazy long battery life when not in use meant that I could come back weeks later and it still had a decent amount of juice is fantastic. So many times I’d go on a trip with several devices and forget to charge one of them, so knowing the Kobo has ample battery in case of such situations is great for peace of mind during travels.
The only thing that hasn’t kept me locked in, honestly, is me. Indeed, I haven’t used the Kobo as much as I had been planning to when I received it during the summer, but that’s not a reflection of the product itself. Part of that comes down to not travelling nearly as much as I did last year — a conscious choice to avoid the U.S. when possible. I’ve also been rather swamped the past couple of months with some big features and approximately 87,000 game releases, including a little title called GTA VI, as part of my duties as a juror for The Game Awards.
But if anything, the fact that I’m still thinking of the Kobo and looking forward to getting back to reading is a testament to how much I’ve enjoyed my time with the device. And given that I’ll undoubtedly be burned out on games come the holidays, I’m excited to pick it back up and catch up on some books. Neuromancer awaits.
The Kobo Libra Colour normally retails for $289.99 but is on sale for $259.99 for Black Friday.

articles.title: Ugreen's 17-in-1 dock has 'more ports than you'll know what to do with'
articles.text:
'A Thunderbolt 5 docking station with more ports and features than you'll know what to do with': Connect everything with the feature-packed Ugreen Maxidok 17-in-1 Dock on sale for Black Friday
Give your laptop a serious docking boost with 17 ports, 140W charging, and Thunderbolt 5
Modern laptops are powerful, but the quest for clean lines and slim designs means that they sometimes struggle for physical connectivity options. That, in turn, can make it tricky to work with multiple displays or external drives and accessories.
Step forward the Ugreen Maxidok 17-in-1. We tested out this port-heavy docking station and found "a Thunderbolt 5 docking station with more ports and features than you'll know what to do with."
Now, Ugreen's 17-in-1 dock is down to $320 (was $500) at Amazon for Black Friday, and £299 (was £420) at Amazon.co.uk. I'd pitch this one as a very useful upgrade for professionals and power users who work with large files, lots of accessories, and multiple screens and peripherals.
This charging dock with 140W power delivery features 2x Thunderbolt 5 (up to 80Gbps), 1x Thunderbolt 5 upstream (120Gbps bidirectional, 140W PD), 1x DisplayPort 2.1, 3x USB-C, 3x USB-A, 1x SD 4.0, 1x microSD, 3x 3.5mm audio jack, 1x SSD slot, and a 2.5GbE port.
UK price: now £299 (was £420)
Why we recommend the Ugreen Maxidok 17-in-1
The box crams in 17 connections including Thunderbolt 5 upstream and dual downstream ports, three USB-C and three USB-A ports, DisplayPort 2.1, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and an SD card reader.
In our review, we found ourselves left impressed by its extensive connectivity and premium construction, but did note the absence of an HDMI port and some slightly disappointing SSD performance.
It can deliver up to 140W of power to a connected laptop and supports dual 6K displays or a single 8K screen. It’s also got an integrated M.2 slot for SSDs up to 8TB. That last feature is especially useful if you need additional high-speed storage - it turns the dock into a handy external SSD drive.
Price context and history
This is the cheapest we've seen Ugreen's dock in both the US and the UK. Previously, it had dropped to around $350 / £350. Note, though, that this Black Friday price is only available to Prime members. You can sign up for a free trial here.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy it if… you’ve got a powerful laptop that you want to use as a multi-screen, multi-device workstation
❌ Skip it if… you’re on the hunt for a docking station with HDMI - or if you want an external SSD with maximum speed

articles.title: Japan puts chipmaking labs inside trucks with mobileFab — trucks pack 30-cm lithography gear to tackle a 10-year semiconductor engineer shortage
articles.text:
Japan puts chipmaking labs inside trucks with mobileFab — trucks pack 30-cm lithography gear to tackle a 10-year semiconductor engineer shortage
Nipponese has semiconductor manufacturing on wheels is an interesting contrast to the U.S.' deployable Burger King trucks.
Multiple nations worldwide have chip-making programs in their respective universities, a discipline that is seeing increasing demand by the day. Japan is one such nation, and it currently has a program in which students can design circuits to wire chip wafers with miniaturized lithography stations. That gear is now going on wheels to schools and companies thanks to mobileFab trucks.
Each truck-mounted mobileFab container contains three machines: a photoresist coater, a maskless lithography machine, and a photoresist developer. Students take pre-etched wafers made by Japan's NIAIST (Institute for Advanced Industrial Science and Technology) and go through the necessary steps to wire the transistors therein together and produce a finalized chip core. The procedures are analogous to getting a breadboard with some pre-mounted, unconnected components and turning that into a product.
The three machines going into trucks are part of the larger Minimal Fab laboratories in place in some Japanese colleges. They're going on the move so that other schools and companies can train students/employees in the art of chipmaking. For now, the 12.5-mm wafers come from the NIAIST, but they can come from other foundries. Each machine is roughly 30 cm wide, and the machines use localized cleaning and sealed between-machine transportation so as not to have to rely on large-scale cleanrooms.
According to the press release by the Minimal Fab Promotion Organization, this system is not only meant for democratizing access to chip manufacturing education. The machines also allow for rapid prototyping and iteration of chip designs, and facilitate small-scale manufacturing — all with modest capital investment.
The "why" of this initiative is fairly predictable: the program's organizers predict that semiconductor fab engineers will be in high demand over the next 10 years, and there aren't even enough teachers going around, making systematic education difficult. Additionally, the division of labor in semiconductor fabs means that many engineers don't participate in all stages of the chip-making process, nor do they have opportunities to operate chip-making equipment themselves. The mobileFab will be on display at the SEMICON Japan 2026 conference in December.

He's obsessed with detail and has a tendency to ramble on the topics he loves. When not doing that, he's usually playing games, or at live music shows and festivals.

articles.title: Microsoft ruft nach massiver IT-Panne intern Code Red aus
articles.text:
Alarm nach weltweitem IT-Ausfall: Microsoft ruft intern Code Red aus
Mitte November 2026 sorgte eine massive IT-Panne dafür, dass Nutzer:innen und Firmen weltweit rund 24 Stunden lang nicht auf Microsoft-Dienste wie Outlook, Teams oder Copilot zugreifen konnten. Laut Microsoft-365-Manager Jason Henderson handelte es sich zudem um den folgenschwersten Ausfall der Cloud-E-Mail-Lösung Exchange Online.
Ursache für Mega-Microsoft-Panne
Noch nie seien so viele Kund:innen so lange ohne E-Mail-Zugang gewesen, schrieb Henderson in einem internen Memo, das Reuters vorliegt. Die Ursache für den Ausfall sieht Microsoft in einem Programmfehler, der seit Juli 2026 unentdeckt im System geschlummert haben soll. Aber warum hat es so lange gedauert, die Dienste wieder zum Laufen zu bringen?
Internen Dokumenten nach hätten sich die Microsoft-Ingenieur:innen durch eine Art „Nebel des Krieges“ kämpfen müssen, wie Vice President Amanda Silver klagte. Die für die Behebung der Schäden eingesetzten Mitarbeiter:innen hätten in elf verschiedenen Team-Chats mehr als 11.000 Nachrichten ausgetauscht, wie es bei Reuters heißt.
Mitarbeiter verlieren den Überblick
Dabei sei es schwergefallen, den Überblick zu behalten. Die Diagnosedaten seien über verschiedene interne Systeme verstreut gewesen. Dadurch soll über einen längeren Zeitraum ein gemeinsamer Überblick über mögliche Ursachen gefehlt haben. Auch schon getroffene Entscheidungen sollen nicht bei allen angekommen sein.
Mithilfe des jetzt ausgerufenen Code Red will Microsoft die technischen Abläufe und die interne Reaktion auf größere Störungen optimieren. Ziel ist es, künftige weitere weltweite Störungen innerhalb von einer Stunde zu beheben.
KI-Agenten sollen Daten schneller auswerten
Dabei sollen unter anderem KI-Agenten zum Einsatz kommen. Diese sollen technische Daten schneller auswerten und Fehlerquellen erkennen. In täglichen oder wöchentlichen Besprechungen sollen entsprechende Fortschritte kontrolliert werden, wie heute.at berichtet.
Darüber hinaus will Microsoft auch die Geschwindigkeit bei der Verteilung von Softwareupdates erhöhen. In anderen Fällen habe ein entsprechender Patch schon einmal fünf bis sechs Tage bis zum weltweiten Rollout gebraucht, wie es intern heißt. Künftig sollen besonders dringende Sicherheitsprobleme ebenfalls innerhalb einer Stunde adressiert sein.

articles.title: Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
Unix software enthusiasts, rejoice! An experimental project called "XNU Linux" has successfully booted a complete macOS 27 desktop on an ARM64 Linux system. This breakthrough offers a new way to run Apple's operating system without relying on traditional virtualization methods. This is significant news for the community, as there is a large group of enthusiasts eager to create custom macOS desktops, also known as Hackintoshes. The project utilizes Apple's open-source XNU kernel, modified to function as a loadable module within Linux, enabling macOS and Linux processes to run on the same hardware.
Instead of translating macOS applications into a format Linux can execute, XNU Linux takes a different approach by integrating Apple's kernel into the Linux environment. It consists of two primary components: xnu.ko, which runs the hosted XNU kernel, and fki.ko, which provides an interface to Linux resources such as memory, networking, timers, and storage. This setup allows macOS processes to run natively on the host CPU without an intervening hypervisor. The setup has been tested on an NVIDIA DGX Spark running Ubuntu, as well as an Apple Silicon Mac running Linux in a virtual machine. The system successfully reached the macOS desktop, including Finder, Dock, WindowServer, and loginwindow, with Safari and Chrome also operational. Applications such as Spotlight and file-system operations remained functional during a brief 30-minute stress test.Graphics support is also part of the project, with a bridge that routes macOS Metal workloads through Vulkan and Mesa to the host GPU. However, this currently requires a compatible Virtio-GPU setup. The NVIDIA DGX Spark demonstration still uses CPU-based rendering. There are also hardware restrictions, as the project currently requires an ARM64 processor with pointer authentication, 4 KB memory pages, and at least 16 GB of RAM. Users must supply their own macOS 27 installation, and conventional x86-based PCs are not supported, largely due to the optimizations done by Apple for its Apple Silicon M-series of chips for macOS.
Sources:

articles.title: Coalizão pressiona UE contra restrições da Apple a navegadores
articles.text:
Coalizão pressiona UE contra restrições da Apple a navegadores
Grupo com Mozilla, Vivaldi, Brave e outras empresas entende que Apple não cumpre lei de concorrência digital da Europa ao restringir navegadores no iOS.
Uma coalizão que reúne organizações como Mozilla, Vivaldi, Brave, Y Combinator, Shopify e várias outras empresas publicou uma carta aberta direcionada a Ursula von der Leyen, presidente da Comissão Europeia. O grupo pede uma fiscalização rigorosa contra a Apple por causa das restrições que dificultam o uso de navegadores de terceiros no iOS.
Não é que não seja possível usar browsers que concorrem com o Safari no iPhone. Chrome, Firefox, Edge e tantos outros estão disponíveis há anos no iOS. O problema é que esses navegadores são obrigados a usar o WebKit como motor de renderização.
Esse motor é o que permite que o navegador leia o código de uma página web e apresente o resultado na forma de um conteúdo visual e interativo para ser acessado pelo usuário. Nos demais sistemas operacionais, navegadores como Chrome, Edge e Opera contam com o Blink como motor, pois são baseados no projeto Chromium. O Firefox tem um motor próprio, o Gecko.
Em 2024, a União Europeia colocou em vigor a Digital Markets Act (DMA), ou Lei dos Mercados Digitais, uma legislação que visa favorecer uma concorrência justa de âmbito digital nos países do bloco.
Graças às várias regras da DMA, a Apple se viu condicionada a permitir que navegadores de terceiros usem seus próprios motores no iOS. Isso na teoria. Na prática, empresas concorrentes acusam a Apple de impor condições que inviabilizam o uso de motores diferentes do WebKit por esses browsers.
Um trecho da carta da Open Web Advocacy, a entidade que está por trás da coalizão, diz:
Mais de dois anos e meio após a entrada em vigor da DMA, em 7 de março de 2024, nenhum fornecedor de navegador conseguiu migrar seus usuários na União Europeia do WebKit da Apple para seu próprio motor. Isso permite que a Apple limite os recursos da web no iOS, prendendo desenvolvedores e consumidores ao seu próprio ecossistema da App Store.
Coincidência ou não, a carta aberta foi publicada quase que ao mesmo tempo em que a Mozilla explicou o porquê de não ter um Firefox “puro” no iOS. Sim, a causa está justamente nas restrições impostas pela Apple.
O grupo pede, principalmente, que a Comissão Europeia inicie o quanto antes um processo de fiscalização contra a Apple para obrigar a companhia a seguir, de fato, o que determina a DMA. Note que a carta aberta não pede a criação ou a alteração da legislação vigente, mas o seu efetivo cumprimento.
Na prática, a coalizão quer que as autoridades europeias atuem para derrubar as barreiras técnicas e jurídicas impostas pela Apple, de modo a beneficiar não somente fornecedores de navegadores, mas também empresas que dependem da web em modelos de negócio variados.
A Comissão Europeia não se manifestou sobre o assunto até o momento. A Apple tampouco. Contudo, em ocasiões anteriores, a companhia argumentou que as suas exigências relacionadas a motores de navegador visam preservar parâmetros de segurança e privacidade para os usuários de iPhone.

articles.title: Karnataka clears Pixxel’s Rs 350 Cr satellite manufacturing project
articles.text:
Karnataka clears Pixxel’s Rs 350 Cr satellite manufacturing project
Welcoming the company’s decision to expand its manufacturing operations in Karnataka, Patil said it reaffirmed Bengaluru’s position as a leading hub for aerospace, space technology and advanced manufacturing.
The Karnataka government has approved Bengaluru-based space technology company Pixxel’s proposal to set up a satellite manufacturing facility in the state with an investment of Rs 350 crore, State Industries Minister MB Patil said on Tuesday.
The proposal, involving an application for six acres of land, was received on November 3 and cleared by the State Level Single Window Clearance Committee within two weeks, he said.
Welcoming the company’s decision to expand its manufacturing operations in Karnataka, Patil said it reaffirmed Bengaluru’s position as a leading hub for aerospace, space technology and advanced manufacturing.
“We are delighted that Pixxel has chosen Karnataka for its next phase of expansion. The state government is committed to extending all necessary support to ensure the timely implementation of this project,” he said in a release.
The minister said the government had been engaging with Pixxel over the past several months to understand its expansion plans, address its requirements and facilitate the investment.
Karnataka has a strong ecosystem of skilled talent, research institutions, technology companies and advanced manufacturing capabilities, he said.
The government would continue to engage with Pixxel and other emerging space technology companies and extend support to strengthen the state’s position as a leading aerospace and space technology hub, Patil added.
He reiterated the government’s commitment to attracting investments in emerging technologies, promoting ease of doing business and creating a conducive environment for innovation-led manufacturing.

articles.title: Ce smartphone Samsung noté 4,5/5 perd 262,24 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le smartphone Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra 256 Go à 859,99 € (-23%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra passe à 859,99 € chez Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 23 % et 262,24 € d'économie. Doté d'un écran très lumineux, d'une excellente autonomie et d'une grande aisance en photo, ce smartphone affiche une note actuelle de 4,5/5 dans nos tests.
Samsung a conçu le Galaxy S25 Ultra pour incarner le sommet de son savoir-faire matériel et logiciel sur le segment des smartphones premium. Face au Galaxy S24 Ultra, l'appareil gagne encore en puissance et en endurance tout en conservant son stylet intégré. Ce modèle a largement convaincu notre laboratoire lors de ses tests.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le smartphone descend à 859,99 € chez Boulanger.com, soit environ 23 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (1 122,23 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 262,24 € sur ce modèle haut de gamme.
Affichage lumineux et processeur Snapdragon 8 Elite : l'efficacité au quotidien
L'écran de 6,9 pouces affiche une définition de 3120 x 1440 pixels pour offrir une excellente lisibilité, épaulée par une dalle particulièrement lumineuse en extérieur. Comme détaillé dans notre test complet, la fluidité reste irréprochable grâce à l'intégration du processeur Snapdragon 8 Elite, capable d'exécuter les applications lourdes et les jeux sans faiblir. Le boîtier répond en outre à la norme IP68 (étanche à l'eau et à la poussière), assurant une protection efficace contre les immersions accidentelles.
Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra
Points forts
- Écran ultra lumineux.
- Performances de haute volée.
- Excellente autonomie.
- Polyvalence photo et vidéo.
Points faibles
- Charge que l'on aimerait plus rapide.
- S Pen sans Bluetooth.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une grande autonomie malgré une recharge qui reste lente
Avec sa batterie de 5000 mAh, le téléphone tient la distance sur une longue journée de travail ou de divertissement. La polyvalence en prise de vue est assurée par un capteur principal de 200 Mpx secondé par des téléobjectifs dédiés pour varier les cadrages du grand-angle au zoom. En contrepartie, la charge de l'accumulateur manque de rapidité par rapport aux standards actuels, ce qui obligera les utilisateurs pressés à patienter davantage sur secteur, tandis que le stylet S Pen perd sa liaison Bluetooth.
Xiaomi 17 : l'autre option face au Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra
Le Xiaomi 17 mise sur un format plus compact tout en intégrant lui aussi une puce haut de gamme Snapdragon et une charge rapide plus véloce que celle de son rival. Actuellement noté 5/5 par notre rédaction, il propose une prise en main plus ramassée face au très grand écran de 6,9 pouces du modèle sud-coréen. Son tarif s'établit à 739,98 €, soit un prix inférieur de 120,01 €.
Le Xiaomi 17 séduira ceux qui cherchent un gabarit plus maniable et une charge rapide pour 120,01 € de moins, mais le Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra conserve l'avantage de son stylet intégré et de son module photo de 200 Mpx.
Xiaomi 17
Points forts
- Écran ultra lumineux.
- Bonne autonomie.
- Grand-angle réussi.
- Format compact plaisant.
Points faibles
- De la chauffe.
- Ultra grand-angle décevant.
