articles.title: CNCF Research Shows Virtual Machines Remain Central as AI Workloads Evolve
articles.text:
Virtual machines (VMs) continue to account for a substantial share of cloud-native production infrastructure, despite the widespread adoption of containers and Kubernetes. New research from the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) and Linux Foundation Research finds that VMs host an average of 53% of production applications, while emerging AI and agentic workloads are creating additional demand for virtualisation, particularly where stronger execution isolation is required.
The report surveyed 492 cloud-native practitioners and technology leaders in September 2026. Among organisations expanding their VM footprint, 34% identified AI and agentic workloads as a contributing factor. The findings suggest that rather than replacing virtual machines with containers, organisations are increasingly combining the two to accommodate different application and security requirements.
The research challenges the assumption that cloud-native adoption necessarily means moving away from virtual machines. While containers provide portability and efficient application packaging, VMs continue to offer isolation and support for workloads that depend on dedicated operating systems or established virtualisation environments.
The survey found that 51% of respondents run at least half of their production applications on VMs. This rises to an average of 64% in organisations with more than 10,000 employees, compared with 45% among organisations with fewer than 500 employees.
Furthermore, 71% of respondents who provided both current and expected workload figures anticipate their VM share remaining within the same range over the next year. This points towards continued coexistence rather than a wholesale migration to one deployment model.
One of the more significant findings concerns the relationship between AI adoption and infrastructure security.
AI agents increasingly generate and execute code, interact with tools, and access external systems. This creates new risks when generated code is executed in environments containing sensitive data or shared infrastructure.
Virtual machines offer a stronger isolation boundary than conventional containers, which share the host operating system kernel. The report identifies hardware-level VM isolation, containers running inside VMs, and MicroVM sandboxing as approaches organisations are using to contain AI workloads.
Among organisations expanding their VM footprint, 47% cited security and isolation as a contributing factor, while 34% specifically identified AI and agentic workloads.
The survey also points to growing interest in stronger isolation technologies. MicroVM sandboxing adoption is expected to increase from 20% current use to 30% planned use, while confidential computing is expected to grow from 12% to 26%. These figures represent reported intentions rather than confirmed deployments.
Some 61% of respondents described their VM and container administration teams as collaborative or fully integrated, suggesting that managing different workload types is increasingly becoming a shared platform engineering responsibility.
Kubernetes is also beginning to play a role in virtual machine management. Among respondents using VMs, 8% reported using KubeVirt, the CNCF project that allows virtual machines to be managed through Kubernetes resources and APIs.
This brings VM lifecycle management into existing Kubernetes operational practices without requiring applications to abandon their virtualised environments.
The findings reinforce a shift in how cloud-native infrastructure is evolving. Kubernetes and containers remain important, but they are not necessarily the right execution model for every workload.
Technologies such as KubeVirt and Kata Containers show how virtualisation can integrate with container orchestration, while MicroVMs provide lightweight environments to isolate short-lived or potentially untrusted workloads.
For platform engineering teams, the research highlights the need to accommodate different execution environments without fragmenting operational practices. AI adds another dimension, making isolation, resource utilisation and workload security increasingly important infrastructure considerations.
The survey was sponsored by CNCF and Broadcom, and its results should be read as reported industry perspectives rather than a complete census of cloud-native deployments. Nevertheless, its findings provide a useful indication of where infrastructure priorities are moving.

articles.title: Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
articles.text:
Strange new materials can crawl, walk, and dig like living creatures
- Date:
  November 23, 2026
- Source:
  Universiteit van Amsterdam
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed remarkable materials that can crawl, walk, and dig using their own internal energy, potentially paving the way for a new generation of autonomous soft robots. They also discovered that making individual components more active can paradoxically make the entire material less responsive, challenging a long-standing principle of engineering.
- Share:
Most materials simply react when something pushes, pulls, or bends them. But a very different category of matter can draw on its own energy to change shape and respond to outside forces in surprising ways. Known as active matter, these unusual materials are attracting growing scientific interest. Now, physicists from the universities of Amsterdam, New South Wales, and Cambridge have uncovered remarkable new behaviors that could change how future machines and robots are designed.
Everyday materials such as metal, concrete, glass, and rubber are generally considered passive. They can stretch, bend, shift, or change shape when forces act on them, but the energy needed to produce those changes comes from outside the material.
Active matter works differently. It contains an internal source of energy that allows it to respond to its surroundings in ways ordinary materials cannot. Many examples occur naturally in living systems. A flock of birds, for instance, can move together as a coordinated group, adjusting its behavior in response to wind, changes in the landscape, available food, or a suitable place to rest.
Scientists can also recreate some of these remarkable properties in the laboratory. Researchers from the University of Amsterdam (The Netherlands), the University of Cambridge (UK), and the University of New South Wales (Sydney, Australia) have spent several years developing active materials from surprisingly simple components, including miniature motors, rods, and rubber bands. Their experiments have revealed unusual mechanical behaviors with potentially valuable applications, leading to two recently accepted scientific papers.
Scientists Create Materials That Can Crawl, Walk, and Dig
One of the discoveries involves two familiar mechanical behaviors known as buckling and snapping.
Imagine squeezing a paper ticket between your fingers. As the pressure increases, the ticket becomes unstable and bends to one side. If you then press against the curved surface, it initially pushes back before suddenly flipping in the opposite direction.
This is how ordinary passive materials behave. External forces supply the energy needed for the ticket to buckle and snap, and each action occurs only once in response to the applied force.
The researchers discovered that adding internal activity can fundamentally transform this behavior. They assembled a series of connected rods into a flexible chain, placing small motors at the joints where neighboring rods meet. These motors created interactions that were not symmetrical. Moving one rod could affect its neighbor in a different way than moving that neighbor would affect the original rod (by rotating over a different angle, for example).
The result was striking. When external forces acted on these active chains, they still bent and snapped, but the movement no longer had to end after a single event. Instead, the structures could repeatedly buckle and snap, producing ongoing oscillations.
The underlying physics involves a transformation of the system's critical point, where snapping normally takes place, into what researchers call a critical exceptional point. This unusual behavior makes it possible for the chains to generate movements resembling crawling, walking, and even digging.
The findings were published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, with Sami Al-Izzi of the University of New South Wales and Yao Du of the University of Amsterdam serving as joint first authors. One of the team's buckling chains was also featured on the journal's cover.
Beyond revealing unexpected physics, the discovery points toward a promising approach to building materials capable of performing multiple tasks autonomously. Such structures could be especially useful in flexible, "soft" robots, potentially allowing their bodies to produce complex movements without relying on a centralized control system.
Active Matter Challenges a Fundamental Engineering Principle
A separate investigation by the same international research team uncovered another surprising property of active materials, this time challenging a principle widely used in engineering.
Whether designing large bridges or tiny nanomechanical devices, engineers depend on established rules that connect the properties of individual components to the behavior of an entire structure.
One such rule is Le Chatelier's Principle. In the mechanical context described by the researchers, it suggests that changes made to individual parts of a system should produce corresponding changes in the overall structure. For example, making a structure's individual components stiffer would generally be expected to increase the stiffness of the entire assembly.
But the researchers found that active matter does not always follow this expectation. In some cases, increasing the activity of individual components can actually reduce the activity of the material as a whole.
To investigate this counterintuitive effect, the scientists built another structure using motors and rods. Rather than arranging the components in a chain, they connected them into a flat, two-dimensional network resembling a lattice. They then examined how the elastic behavior of the entire structure changed depending on the properties of its individual elements.
Their experiments revealed that the overall response depended on more than simply how active each component was. What mattered was whether the active elements formed connected pathways capable of transmitting mechanical responses throughout the structure.
Why More Activity Can Produce Less Response
The researchers identified a process called percolation as the key to understanding this unexpected behavior.
A useful comparison is the movement of water through ground coffee. If the coffee grounds are packed too tightly, water cannot easily travel through the entire layer. The arrangement of the grounds determines whether the water can find a continuous path.
Something similar happens inside active materials. If too many of the interconnected components have relatively low activity, they can prevent elastic responses from spreading through the structure. Even when other components are extremely active, their influence may not extend across the entire material.
This explains why making some parts more active does not necessarily produce a more active structure overall. The way the components are connected and distributed can be just as important as their individual properties.
The second study, led by first author Jack Binysh from Corentin Coulais's research group at the University of Amsterdam, was published in Physical Review X.
The researchers believe that this unexpected departure from Le Chatelier's Principle could have important implications for understanding and designing systems built from active microscopic structures. These include biological gels, epithelial monolayers, which are sheets of closely connected cells, and neuromorphic networks that mimic aspects of biological information processing.
Together, the findings reveal how dramatically materials can behave when their internal components actively consume energy and interact in unconventional ways. The discoveries could influence research across physics, soft matter science, mechanical engineering, the life sciences, and robotics, while opening new possibilities for creating adaptable materials and smarter robotic systems.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Universiteit van Amsterdam. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal References:
- Sami C. Al-Izzi, Yao Du, Jonas Veenstra, Richard G. Morris, Anton Souslov, Andreas Carlson, Corentin Coulais, Jack Binysh. Nonreciprocal buckling makes active filaments polyfunctional. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2026; 123 (11) DOI: 10.1073/pnas.2531723123
- Jack Binysh, Guido Baardink, Jonas Veenstra, Corentin Coulais, Anton Souslov. More is Less in Unpercolated Active Solids. Physical Review X, 2026; 16 (2) DOI: 10.1103/flhb-kjyd

articles.title: Xbox Helix started as a PC in disguise, with free multiplayer and Steam, until plans changed
articles.text:
What we know so far: Microsoft has confirmed that the next Xbox, codenamed Helix, will support PC games, but the extent of that support remains unclear. Current messaging indicates a console-first experience, but rumors suggest the project initially leaned in a much more PC-centric direction. It remains uncertain how much Microsoft's current roadmap resembles that original plan.
Sources tell Windows Central that, before Asha Sharma became Xbox CEO earlier this year, Microsoft planned for its next console to essentially be a PC with an Xbox-style UI and support for Xbox console games. This would have required the company to drop its online multiplayer paywall.
As prior rumors suggested, the Asus ROG Xbox Ally was a rough draft of the experience the Xbox division intended for its next console while under Phil Spencer. The next Xbox would have run on Windows and booted into Microsoft's new Xbox Mode by default, but users could exit to the traditional desktop and install any Windows app, including Steam.
Microsoft's official messaging remains vague but implies the opposite approach while retaining some PC compatibility. The company recently described its next console, now codenamed Helix, as a console that plays PC games, not a PC that plays console games.
The device will feature a new interface that provides immediate access to games but also supports greater customization for advanced users and eliminates traditional barriers. However, it remains unclear what this means and how much Microsoft's plans have changed since Sharma replaced Spencer in February.
Xbox's new CEO aims to make the division more profitable, which could be difficult if Helix supports Steam and doesn't require an online multiplayer subscription. Steam's market share eclipses that of the Microsoft Store, and Valve's service is almost synonymous with PC gaming, so including access to it could mean forfeiting revenue from game sales. On the other hand, Microsoft's confirmation that Helix will play PC games means little in the practical terms without Steam.
The most concrete rumors regarding Helix concern its hardware. It reportedly includes a custom APU with 10 Zen 6 CPU cores, 20 threads, and a 40-TFLOP RDNA 5 GPU. It's far too early to predict pricing because storage and RAM costs have been chaotic for the past year, but an MSRP well over $1,000 is a real possibility.
Microsoft confirmed that developers will receive Helix alpha development kits next year, suggesting the console could hit store shelves in late 2027 or sometime in 2028.

articles.title: Como escolher o notebook ideal para reuniões e videoconferências
articles.text:
Resumo IA
- O notebook ideal para reuniões e videoconferências precisa ter bom processamento, autonomia suficiente e boa câmera embutida.
- Recursos extras como otimização de áudio e vídeo são importantes para garantir a qualidade das chamadas.
- Os notebooks Dell 14 e Dell 15 são opções interessantes, com processadores Intel Core recentes, memória RAM de até 16 GB e recursos de otimização de áudio e vídeo.
Escolher seu próximo notebook para reuniões e videoconferências pode ser mais fácil do que você imagina. Atualmente já é possível encontrar computadores que misturam portabilidade com capacidade suficiente para realizar as principais tarefas do dia a dia, incluindo chamadas de trabalho.
Por padrão, modelos do tipo precisam contar com características como bom processamento e autonomia suficiente para passar algumas horas em ligação, além de uma boa câmera embutida. Mas alguns recursos extras podem ser interessantes, como suporte a otimização de áudio e vídeo.
Outra característica importante é o tamanho de tela, que pode ajudar bastante a seguir com suas tarefas sem precisar se desligar das chamadas. Para isso, notebooks com 14 ou 15 polegadas podem ser ideais para garantir a portabilidade necessária sem deixar sua produtividade de lado.
O que o notebook ideal para reuniões e videoconferências precisa ter
Na hora de comprar seu novo notebook pensando em participar de reuniões do trabalho, da faculdade ou da escola, algumas características específicas podem fazer diferença. Por isso, é importante conhecer bem os fatores que vão garantir ligações sem engasgos, travamentos e outros problemas na captação de áudio ou vídeo. Para comprar seu novo computador, vale prestar atenção em:
- Design: modelo precisa combinar portabilidade com dois outros fatores: tamanho de tela e a presença de uma boa câmera.
- Desempenho: o processamento do computador precisa dar conta das chamadas sem travamentos.
- Bateria: uma boa autonomia vai garantir que você participe de reuniões em qualquer lugar, mesmo sem ter uma tomada por perto.
- Recursos extras: ferramentas de otimização de áudio e vídeo são essenciais para diminuir ruídos, editar o fundo das chamadas e mais.
- Conectividade: é importante contar com uma boa oferta de entradas para conectar fones e os padrões mais recentes de Wi-Fi e Bluetooth.
Design e tamanho de tela
A escolha de um notebook para reuniões passa, necessariamente, por um modelo com boa câmera disponível – de preferência com gravação em Full HD. Além disso, a tela precisa ter um tamanho suficiente para dar conta de tarefas, apresentações e outras atividades durante as chamadas. Dessa forma, modelos com 14 ou 15 polegadas disponíveis prometem ser ideais.
Ainda no design, é importante falar de conectividade. Muitos computadores mais recentes costumam trazer apenas entradas USB-C, limitando o uso de fones à conexão Bluetooth, por exemplo. Portanto, uma dica é procurar por uma variedade maior de interfaces, como USB padrão (tipo A) e plug de 3,5 mm para utilizar fones com fio sem problemas.
Por fim, mas não menos importante, vale ficar de olho nos detalhes de tamanho e peso do notebook para transportar em qualquer bolsa ou mochila. Uma espessura reduzida pode parecer detalhe, mas faz diferença na hora de abrir seu computador no café para uma reunião, por exemplo. Da mesma forma, ter bordas ultrafinas para aproveitar ao máximo o espaço de tela também é um fator que vai além do charme do modelo.
Desempenho e bateria
Para ter uma garantia de horas rodando aplicativos de videoconferência, é essencial buscar modelos com boa autonomia. Sem uma bateria suficiente, você pode acabar refém de uma tomada na hora de participar de reuniões importantes. Por isso, notebooks com recursos de recarga rápida como o ExpressCharge da Dell e algumas horas de uso disponíveis devem funcionar muito bem em uma rotina agitada.
Já no desempenho, é importante buscar processadores mais recentes. Um Intel Core 5, por exemplo, já deve ser suficiente dar conta de tarefas de produtividade e rodar os principais apps de vídeo sem problemas. Isso, claro, aliado a uma memória RAM de ao menos 8 GB e armazenamento em SSD para abrir rapidamente seu sistema operacional e navegar por aplicativos, planilhas e mais.
E os recursos extras?
Pode parecer pouco, mas ter um computador atual pode garantir ferramentas importantes para chamadas de vídeo. Otimização de áudio, redução de ruídos, edição de fundo, entre outros recursos vão fazer diferença na qualidade da sua chamada.
Em uma reunião de negócios, por exemplo, aparências contam bastante – e uma ligação com a voz clara e sem ruídos externos pode mudar os rumos da conversa para melhor. Da mesma forma, não travar na hora de apresentar um trabalho da faculdade também pode ajudar na avaliação final do professor.
Conheça o Dell 14
Considerando os aspectos mais importantes para um notebook voltado para reuniões e videoconferências, o Dell 14 vendido no Brasil aparece como uma alternativa interessante de custo-benefício. Com processadores Intel Core mais recentes, é possível escolher versões com Core 5 ou Core 7, ambas com promessa de boa fluidez e gráficos embutidos que devem ser suficientes para suas chamadas e apresentações.
O Dell 14 também traz memória RAM de 8 a 16 GB, armazenamento de até 1 TB em SSD e recursos como o Express Charge para recarga rápida, redução de ruídos na captação de áudio, câmera com resolução Full HD, entre outros.
Conheça mais do Dell 14 no site oficial da Dell.
Dell 15
Uma opção semelhante para quem deseja maior espaço de tela é o Dell 15. O computador também oferece RAM a partir de 8 GB, chips Intel Core 5 ou Core 7, além de recursos de otimização de áudio e vídeo. Com design elegante na cor preta, o notebook não deixa a portabilidade de lado mesmo com um display grande o suficiente para realizar suas tarefas durante as chamadas de vídeo.
Conheça o Dell 15 em detalhes no site oficial da Dell.

articles.title: Verra raises $5M to help consulting firms forget their institutional amnesia
articles.text:
Verra raises $5M to help consulting firms forget their institutional amnesia
Verra, an artificial intelligence startup building the institutional memory layer for consulting firms, said today it has raised $5 million in seed funding to help those companies overcome their amnesia and make their decades of knowledge accessible to every employee.
Today’s round was led by Kearny Jackson and saw participation from Andreessen Horowitz’s a16z Speedrun, Petra and a number of strategic investors. It comes just seven months after Verra, officially known as Lighthouse Software Technologies Inc., launched its platform.
Verra was founded last year by Chief Executive Kashyap Nathan (pictured, right), who previously worked as a researcher at OpenAI Group PBC and Palantir Technologies Inc., and Christopher Farrington (left), a former software engineer at Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu Ltd. In an interview, Nathan explained that he and Farrington had seen firsthand how well-paid consultants would struggle with new customer engagements, wasting hours of time researching to surface institutional knowledge that their company already possessed.
“Consulting firms sit on decades of proposals, models and reports, and almost none of it is usable by the people who need it next,” Nathan said. “We built the layer that makes that knowledge usable, and we built it to run inside the firm’s own cloud, because no consulting firm is going to send client work to a shared service.”
Verra makes consulting firms’ institutional knowledge accessible through an artificial intelligence-native memory layer that indexes their past deliverables and distills their previous methodologies into reusable skills for autonomous agents. Then, those agents can utilize those skills to get started in tools such as Microsoft Word, PowerPoint and Excel, and generate a highly detailed draft for new client engagements in ten hours or less.
Nathan said that’s a big improvement. At most consulting firms, it typically takes about 80 hours to get that first draft ready. “The traditional approach involves a SharePoint search box and a junior analyst with a week to spare,” he explained. “The AI-native version of that is a chat tool that answers a question from a few retrieved pages and leaves the consultant to rewrite the output. But both start from a blank page.”
Verra is also much more efficient, Nathan said. Whereas traditional chatbots can generate text snippets, Verra creates its sourced deliverables directly inside Office files that will be organized alongside the client brief.
“Verra starts from the firm. It indexes everything the firm has produced, distills how each practice does its work, and then lets a consultant point at a new situation and get to most of a finished deliverable in Excel or PowerPoint, before the human analyst starts writing a line,” Nathan said. “Every claim links to the page or cell it came from. The firm’s engineers and ours then build the specific workflows a team wants.”
The architecture of Verra’s agents is important, too. The company built them to run inside client’s clouds after looking at three realities of the professional services business. Consulting firms cannot allow their client’s data to leave their own environments, they will not trust an answer that can’t be verified, and AI will not be used if it forces them to drop the tools and systems they’re already using.
It’s this approach that has been the secret to Verra’s promising early adoption. Its agents are already being used by two major global consulting firms in Berkeley Research Group and The Keystone Group. In the case of the former, more than 90% of its consultants are using Verra daily, and have generated more than 105,000 files since August while replacing the Tableau platform with a natural-language Snowflake interface. Berkeley calculates that Verra’s platform has helped the company to save around 215,000 analyst hours annually.
“Verra hands our teams finished, sourced first drafts on engagements that used to start from a blank page,” said Berkeley’s global managing director of AI solutions, Raghav Vadlamani. “It has changed how quickly we move for clients.”
Moving forward, Nathan wants to integrate Verra’s AI agents even deeper with the consulting firms it serves, so they can learn how the entire company works and improve its overall efficiency rather than just focusing on one engagement at a time. He also sees an opportunity to move into adjacent sectors such as investment research and accounting. He wants to give customers’ engineers a way to build on Verra’s platform too.
Kearny Jackson Partner Sriram Krishnan said he used to work in the consulting industry himself and that he’s all too familiar with the rinse-and-repeat process that accompanies each new client engagement. “What stood out to us was how quickly Verra became critical to the firms using it,” he said. “Their consultants adopt it, use it and demand more of it. It’s becoming the memory and operating layer for how consulting firms work.”

articles.title: Vancouver considering stricter rules, oversight for AI data centres
articles.text:
Vancouver City Council has unanimously directed City of Vancouver staff to examine stronger oversight of new data centres, including third-party assessments of their effects on the surrounding area, public reporting on their operations, and ways to secure benefits for local residents.
OneCity city councillor Lucy Maloney’s member motion, approved last week after amendments, asks City staff to develop recommendations on how the municipal government should assess and regulate data centres as artificial intelligence (AI) facilities grow.
“This is about ensuring we move forward responsibly and thoughtfully. As we’ve seen in the United States, hyperscale data centres can bring significant challenges. Compared to many other industrial businesses, data centres are often far more resource intensive, placing greater strain on public infrastructure. They can consume vast quantities of water and energy while producing pollution, waste heat, and noise. They also tend to create fewer jobs than other industrial uses of the land,” said Maloney during the City Council meeting.
“Furthermore, the economic benefits to host communities often fall short of the returns realised by investors by a long shot. This is a global issue, not just limited to the U.S. Cities worldwide are sharing best practices to develop effective frameworks and ensure data centres represent the best use of valuable land,” continued Maloney.
The decision comes as local developer Westbank pursues two proposed AI data centres in highly urban and central locations of Vancouver: a brand-new, 10-storey building with 100 per cent AI data centre uses at 150 West Georgia St. in Downtown Vancouver, located immediately adjacent to BC Place Stadium and integrated with Creative Energy’s industrial steam plant on the same site (using the data centre’s excess heat to provide heating for many Downtown Vancouver buildings), and the conversion of the existing M3 office building (previously part of Hootsuite’s headquarters) at 111 East 5th Ave. (near Main Street) at the developer’s Main Alley tech campus in the Mount Pleasant Industrial Area.
Both projects are under Prime Minister Mark Carney’s Enabling Large-Scale Sovereign AI Data Centres initiative. The federal government has determined a need for such
“sovereign” facilities for national security reasons — a strategy to keep AI computing infrastructure and sensitive data in Canada and under Canadian control, reducing the reliance on foreign providers. This is intended to protect Canadian governments, post-secondary institutions, public institutions, researchers, and businesses.
Telus is no longer a partner in those Westbank projects. Earlier this month, as first reported by Daily Hive Urbanized, both companies confirmed the change, with Telus noting it is pursuing other projects elsewhere, while Westbank said it would continue to pursue the two projects under a yet-to-be-announced new partnership. A spokesperson for the projects also told Daily Hive Urbanized they support Maloney’s motion.
The existing zoning for 150 West Georgia St. already permits data centre use, while the M3 proposal is undergoing additional City staff review, after the previous makeup of City Council removed it from the July 2026 agenda and directed City staff to perform more public consultation, which is now scheduled to occur in December 2026.
City staff’s forthcoming broader review based on Maloney’s motion will also look at facilities already operating or being converted, including 175 West Cordova St., located at the southern edge of Gastown.
Under Maloney’s approved motion, City staff will examine requiring AI data centre applicants to commission third-party studies before rezoning or permitting. These would assess water use, greenhouse gas emissions, possible air pollutants, noise, and heat, along with measures to reduce those impacts, including recovering heat for other uses.
The studies would also compare the jobs a proposed AI data centre facility would create with those from other industrial activities that could reasonably use the same land.
Another part of the work will examine a business licence specifically for data centres. The proposed approach would require annual public reporting of water consumption, electricity consumption, and noise levels, while giving the municipal government a way to hold applicants accountable for commitments made during the approval process.
City staff will also explore fees or other contributions that could provide public benefits and help address the demands these data centres place on Vancouver.
The goal is to have new municipal requirements in place before new rezoning applications are considered by City Council or new development permit applications are approved by City staff.
As previously reported by Daily Hive Urbanized, the original version of Maloney’s motion in July 2026 called for a temporary pause on considering major new AI data centre projects. However, during last week’s meeting, Maloney explained that City staff had subsequently told her that the provincial legislation of the Vancouver Charter requires applications to be processed, which makes such a moratorium not possible.
During the meeting, City Council approved an amendment from COPE city councillor Solomon Yi-Kieran directing City staff to develop and report back with a separate definition for AI data centres — effectively distinguishing them from conventional data centres to better account for significant differences in electricity and water use, noise, and emissions.
ABC city councillor Mike Klassen also supported Maloney’s motion, asserting the municipal government should welcome technology investment while taking concerns about its effects on residents and surrounding neighbourhoods seriously.
He pointed to Canadians’ heavy reliance on technology and services based outside the country, citing the recent Microsoft Outlook outage as an example of that dependence. He also called for cooperation with the federal government, which he argued still has considerable work to do on regulating the sector.
When it comes to local considerations, Klassen said concerns about noise, water, and electricity consumption, heat, environmental impacts, and how data centres fit alongside neighbouring properties deserve attention.
“Having clear guidelines and reasonable safeguards benefits residents, businesses and investors alike,” said Klassen.
He added that clearer expectations would give companies greater certainty when proposing new facilities, helping Vancouver accommodate technology investment while addressing its potential impacts.
This AI data centre review was one of 11 wide-ranging member motions from Maloney, Mayor Pete Fry, and COPE city councillor Sean Orr approved by City Council on Nov. 18.

articles.title: Nvidia engineer who quit over Jensen Huang's exit says he 'may have moved too quickly' — robotics engineer who went viral after post is now open to returning after CEO's reinstatement
articles.text:
Nvidia engineer who quit over Jensen Huang's exit says he 'may have moved too quickly' — robotics engineer who went viral after post is now open to returning after CEO's reinstatement
Darrell Dai says he's "open to exploring the possibility of returning"
Former Nvidia robotics engineer Darrell Dai made a viral post just nine days ago announcing his resignation from Nvidia, which has gathered over 7 million impressions on X alone (Dai also posted to his LinkedIn account). Dai resigned due to what he described as a lack of transparency around CEO Jensen Huang's exit. But now that Huang is back at the helm, Dai has followed up, saying that he "may have moved too quickly," although his resignation has already taken effect.
Dai says that although he's open to the possibility of returning to Nvidia, he wants to approach his next decision with "a clearer mind." Huang resigned 11 days ago following reports of two separate affairs, one of which reportedly involved an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.
Despite reports of belligerent behaviors toward employees, Nvidia retains an exceptional rating on Glassdoor, and many employees rallied around the CEO's return. A petition to reinstate Huang gathered over 150,000 signatures online, including high-profile names like Elon Musk.
Huang publicly admitted to having an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. In his statement, the Nvidia co-founder apologized to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang, and his two children, Spencer Huang and Madison Huang, both of whom still work at Nvidia.
Days following the admission, a report from The New York Times accused Huang of having another affair with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to Huang, citing five anonymous sources within Nvidia. Huang resigned as CEO the following day. Neither Huang nor Powell have commented on the alleged affair.
Dai's last day at Nvidia was November 19, just a few days ago. President Donald Trump said on Monday that he contacted Nvidia's board, and went as far as to claim he "made the deal," according to CNBC. Following the announcement of Huang's return, Nvidia's stock rose more than 30% upon market open.

articles.title: Microsoft’s historic cloud outage exposed an engineering “fog of war”
articles.text:
According to internal memos reviewed by Reuters, Microsoft has declared a “Code Red” overhaul of its engineering response practices after the November 12 outage that lost access to Exchange Online, Teams, and Outlook for users worldwide.
Per the memos, Microsoft 365 Core President Jason Henderson described the outage as having the most customer impact in the history of Exchange Online. In a separate memo, Henderson wrote that an urgent production fix in a recent incident took five to six days to reach worldwide saturation. Microsoft’s target for its most urgent security fixes is to move from detection to safe worldwide deployment in one hour. “Needless to say, we aren’t here yet,” Henderson wrote.
The memos, which Reuters reviewed but Microsoft has not published, outline the response to the November 12 disruption. The company’s post-incident report, dated November 20, attributed the downtime to an undetected Windows scalability defect introduced in July, which caused lock contention in the gateway processes. A Teams traffic failover then dumped additional load onto infrastructure already under stress, as maintenance had left nearly 14 percent of gateway server capacity offline at the time of the incident.

articles.title: ¿Tu PC va más lento? Este ajuste de Chrome podría estar consumiendo RAM sin que lo sepas
articles.text:
El consumo de memoria ha sido el talón de Aquiles de Chrome durante muchos años y las cosas no parecen mejorar. El navegador de Google nuevamente vuelve al centro de la polémica luego de que se descubriera que consume una cantidad grosera de RAM tras cerrarlo. Este comportamiento es relativamente nuevo y está relacionado con la integración de Gemini.
Un usuario descubrió que Chrome puede consumir hasta 700 MB de RAM después de cerrarlo. En una publicación en Reddit, el usuario detalló que, tras cerrar el navegador de la forma habitual, el Administrador de Tareas de Windows mantenía varios procesos de chrome.exe ejecutándose en segundo plano. Estas tareas consumían entre 300 MB y 700 MB de RAM, por lo que el usuario tenía que cerrarlas de forma manual.
Las tareas de Chrome o de cualquier otro navegador basado en Chromium que se mantienen en segundo plano son un mal que lleva años. La mayoría de las veces se trata de un ajuste en la configuración relacionado con las aplicaciones o extensiones, pero en esta ocasión era diferente. El usuario dijo que probó de todo, incluyendo un borrado de caché, cookies y deshabilitando todos los complementos.
Tras restaurar la configuración de Chrome, el usuario encontró que el problema estaba relacionado con una opción ligada al perfil. La integración de Gemini en Chrome activa dos funciones que mantienen al asistente de IA funcionando todo el tiempo. El navegador mantiene los componentes cargados en la memoria para que Gemini pueda responder de forma inmediata cuando el usuario lo invoca.
Gemini en Chrome está acabándose la RAM de tu ordenador
Si usas Gemini como asistente predeterminado en Chrome, tal vez no te importe que consuma memoria de más. La integración con el navegador lo hace muy útil para resumir páginas o hacer preguntas sin tener que abrir una aplicación o pestaña adicional. No obstante, esta función requiere mantener los procesos activos, incluso cuando cierras la ventana de Chrome.
Para el usuario común que tiene poca RAM en su ordenador, esto podría representar un problema. Google no explica de forma clara en su documentación que Chrome necesita memoria libre para reservarla a Gemini. Para colmo, muchas personas desconocen que esta función está activa y pueden interpretar el consumo de recursos como un fallo, tal y como ocurrió con este usuario.
La buena noticia es que cualquiera puede eliminar el consumo adicional de RAM al desactivar dos opciones dentro de la configuración de Chrome. Para lograrlo, sigue estos pasos:
- Abre Google Chrome.
- Haz clic en el menú de tres puntos y entra en Configuración.
- Ve a Innovaciones de IA y después a Gemini en Chrome.
- En el apartado de Preferencias, desactiva las opciones "Mostrar Gemini en la parte superior del navegador" y "Mostrar Gemini en Chrome en la bandeja del sistema y activar la combinación de teclas".
Ya que te encuentras en ese menú, también puedes bajar hasta el apartado Permisos y desactivar la opción "Compartir pestaña actual de forma predeterminada". Esta última impedirá que Chrome lea todas tus pestañas y las envíe a sus servidores. También puedes deshabilitar la función de IA en el dispositivo, una característica que ayuda a detectar estafas, pero que consume 20 GB de espacio en tu ordenador.
Si quieres una alternativa más sencilla, desinstala Chrome y cámbialo por Brave, Firefox u otro navegador menos agresivo en consumo de memoria.

articles.title: “Lamento haberlos hecho pasar por todo esto”: Jensen Huang volvió a Nvidia entre abrazos y ovaciones
articles.text:
Jensen Huang regresó a la sede de Nvidia en Santa Clara, California, y se paró frente a cientos de empleados en el atrio para, antes de recibir aplausos, pedir perdón. “Cometí errores muy graves y voy a trabajar para recuperarme”, dijo el cofundador y presidente ejecutivo, reinstalado por unanimidad el lunes 23 de noviembre tras 11 días fuera del cargo. Una empleada se adelantó entre la multitud y lo abrazó. El resto del edificio, con trabajadores apilados en tres pisos de balconadas, estalló en cánticos de su nombre.
Huang pidió disculpas a su equipo antes de agradecer el apoyo
El discurso improvisado de Huang en el lobby de la sede fue breve y directo. Comenzó con un chiste —“Este es mi primer día de trabajo; no tengo computadora, así que el departamento de IT me va a dar una nueva”— pero enseguida cambió el tono. “Lo siento muchísimo por haberlos hecho pasar por todo esto. Cometí errores muy graves”, dijo. Las imágenes fueron compartidas originalmente por Ming-Yu Liu, vicepresidente de investigación de Nvidia, en X. Luego agradeció la segunda oportunidad y prometió ser “un mejor CEO esta vez”. El video se volvió viral en pocas horas.
Los empleados llenaron tres pisos del edificio para recibirlo
La escena fue registrada desde distintos ángulos por trabajadores que la subieron a redes sociales. Según informó CNBC, que tuvo acceso al video, el atrio de la sede concentró a empleados en la planta baja y en los balcones superiores, todos aplaudiendo y coreando “Jensen”. Alec Fong, gerente sénior de ingeniería de software de la compañía, publicó imágenes del momento final del discurso, cuando la multitud estalló en ovación. Gavin Baker, director de Inversiones de Atreides Management y uno de los accionistas que presionaron por la reincorporación, escribió en X que “los empleados de Nvidia lo querían de vuelta más que a ninguna otra cosa”.
La junta directiva lo reinstalaba mientras la investigación interna continúa abierta
La junta directiva de Nvidia votó de forma unánime para reincorporar a Huang como presidente, CEO y miembro del directorio, con vigencia inmediata. En un comunicado, el directorio afirmó estar satisfecho con su “franqueza y capacidad de liderazgo”. La decisión llegó antes de que concluya la investigación interna que la propia junta había ordenado tras las acusaciones contra el ejecutivo, que incluyen relaciones extramatrimoniales —una de ellas con una mujer señalada como presunta agente de inteligencia extranjera— y el incumplimiento de políticas corporativas internas. Funcionarios del gobierno de Estados Unidos confirmaron a la junta que la reincorporación no representa un riesgo para la seguridad nacional.
Cinco días antes de volver, Huang ya había reconocido sus errores públicamente
El regreso del lunes no fue la primera vez que Huang admitió sus faltas. Cinco días después de su renuncia, publicó un mensaje en X donde escribió: “No estuve a la altura de los estándares que se le exigen a todos en Nvidia y cometí errores graves en mi vida personal”. Agregó que había “creado problemas para la junta” que lamentaba profundamente y que se comprometía a cooperar con la investigación independiente. Señaló también que volvería si el directorio consideraba que era lo mejor para los accionistas, los empleados y la empresa.
Las acciones de Nvidia subieron 31,5% el día de su regreso
La reacción del mercado fue inmediata. Las acciones de Nvidia treparon un 31,5% el lunes, en lo que constituyó uno de los mayores rebotes individuales de la compañía en su historia reciente, e impulsaron una recuperación generalizada en Wall Street. El escándalo había borrado USD 1,5 billones en capitalización de mercado desde que estalló el 8 de noviembre. El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó haber llamado personalmente a Huang y a la junta para organizar el retorno y lo calificó como “un genio” y “un gran patriota”. Legisladores de ambos partidos, en tanto, mantuvieron sus objeciones a la reinstalación mientras la investigación no haya concluido.

articles.title: GTA 6 hace historia en PS5 y se convierte en el lanzamiento más exitoso de PlayStation
articles.text:
Grand Theft Auto 6 no para de crecer. A pocos días de que llegara al mercado, el juego de Rockstar Games batió todos los récords de ventas, preventas y ya superó en ganancias a la taquilla de las películas más exitosas de Hollywood. Ahora, GTA 6 logró convertirse en el lanzamiento más exitoso de la historia de PlayStation, impulsando la venta de consolas.
De acuerdo con el blog oficial de PlayStation, más de 39 millones de usuarios han jugado GTA 6 en PS5 desde su lanzamiento. El juego también estableció un récord por el mayor número de jugadores simultáneos que ha tenido un solo título en las consolas PlayStation, superando incluso los récords en otros títulos multijugador o free-to-play, que normalmente lideran en este apartado.
Según Sony, los jugadores de GTA 6 en PS5 acumularon más de 683 millones de horas de juego entre el día de estreno y el 22 de noviembre. Cada uno ha pasado una media de 17,4 horas explorando el estado de Leonida durante los primeros días desde su lanzamiento.
Estas cifras superan a cualquier otro juego de consola en los últimos años, incluyendo aquellos de los estudios first party de Sony. Si bien no hay datos oficiales, juegos como Marvel's Spider-Man 2 o God of War Ragnarök tuvieron un lanzamiento importante, aunque no al nivel de GTA 6. Otro juego que podría colarse en la comparativa es Fortnite, que se convirtió en un fenómeno cultural entre 2018 y 2019, registrando millones de jugadores concurrentes.
GTA 6 también ha impulsado las ventas de consolas PS5
Además de los récords en horas de juego, Sony también registró un aumento en las ventas de hardware. La compañía afirmó que GTA 6 generó el mayor número de nuevas PS5 conectadas en un solo día desde el lanzamiento de la consola, excluyendo los periodos habituales de compras de fin de año. El juego de Rockstar Games fue el primer título ejecutado en el 70% de las nuevas PS5 activadas durante este período.
Las cifras podrían sonar escandalosas para alguien que no ha seguido el fenómeno de Rockstar Games. Desde los primeros rumores que anticipaban su llegada, la mayoría de jugadores sabía que GTA 6 representaría un momento clave en la industria de videojuegos.
Grand Theft Auto 6 superó los 32 millones de reservas, algo que no había logrado ningún otro juego o producto de entretenimiento. No obstante, la situación se volvió aún más espectacular en el lanzamiento, generando 3.790 millones de dólares en ventas durante las primeras 24 horas. Esto representa más de 4,6 veces lo que obtuvo GTA V durante su día de estreno, o 5,2 veces lo que generó Red Dead Redemption 2 en su primer fin de semana.
Fuera de los récords comerciales, GTA 6 también ha cosechado elogios de la crítica especializada. Hace unos días se reportó que el juego alcanzó el 99 en Metacritic, una calificación que mantenía The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time desde 1998. La mayoría coincide en que Rockstar Games ha logrado su cometido, convirtiendo a GTA 6 en uno de los juegos más importantes de la generación.
El estudio todavía tiene trabajo por delante, con una versión de PC que se estrenará durante el primer trimestre de 2027. También está pendiente el multijugador de GTA 6, que intentará superar lo que ya consiguió GTA Online.

articles.title: Kenya’s Cloud9 acquires Canadian money services business Monix Pay
articles.text:
Kenyan digital bank Cloud9, which enables cross-border payments and borderless banking for African consumers and businesses, has acquired Canadian money services business Monix Pay to expand into North America.
Disrupt Africa reported in October 2025 on the launch of Cloud9, a digital bank enabling instant global payments, borderless banking and modern financial tools for a new generation of African consumers and businesses.
The startup recently secured an undisclosed investment from crypto and fintech accelerator Alliance, taking total funding to date to US$1 million, and it has now acquired Monix Pay, a Canadian money services business registered with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), the country’s financial intelligence and anti-money-laundering regulator.
The deal sees Cloud9 expand into North America for the first time, and means it is now registered to provide foreign exchange (FX) services, money transfers, general payment services, and virtual currency and digital asset transactions. It is a key step in the startup’s long-term plan to own the regulated infrastructure its customers depend on, rather than fully renting it from intermediaries.
“Every African business that trades globally pays a hidden tax on every transaction – in fees, in FX and in time,” said Tesh Mbaabu, founder and CEO of Cloud9. “Acquiring Monix Pay means we no longer entirely depend on others’ rails to serve our customers. We’re building the regulated infrastructure to move money between Africa and the world instantly, transparently and at fair rates.”
With a regulated Canadian entity, Cloud9 can now move money directly between North America and Africa, with fewer intermediaries and faster settlement; offer competitive FX on CAD, USD, EUR, GBP, CNY and African currencies for business and personal customers; combine fiat and digital asset rails within a regulated framework, pairing the speed of stablecoins with compliance and oversight; and build banking and payments partnerships in one of the world’s most trusted financial markets.

articles.title: Threads comes to iPad and takes a page from X's playbook with cashtags
articles.text:
It may have taken 15 years for Instagram to launch on the iPad, but Instagram’s other app, Threads, has taken a slightly faster path to the Apple tablet. In an overnight update, the company rolled out a big-screen version of the X competitor. It’s also added another new feature, borrowed from X: the stock-tracking feature known as cashtags.
While the iPad version of the app works well in portrait orientation, some users are disappointed to find that the landscape layout doesn’t work as they’d expect. Instead of offering a multi-column interface as on Threads’ web app, the iPad app focuses on the user’s main feed in a single-column layout. There are also options to swipe right and left from the main screen to access the search screen and the feeds menu, respectively.
The iPad app isn’t the company’s only update in the latest release. According to a post from Threads engineer Guy Dickinson, Threads will now support cashtags — a feature popularized by Twitter years ago for tracking live stock information. These specialized tags start with the dollar sign (“$”) followed by a ticker symbol. When you click on a cashtag, you can follow the discussions around the stock.
In addition, Threads is adding live stock quotes, charts, and other context at the top of each cashtag’s page. As you search for a particular cashtag, the autocomplete search results will display the stock’s current price and the percentage it’s up or down. Dickinson says the feature will currently support NYSE and Nasdaq stocks, ETFs, and crypto. Cashtags will be supported on the web, iOS, and Android. However, they’re just now rolling out, so you may not immediately see them.
The update points to Threads’ broader ambition to compete with X, not only as a destination for discussions about various topics, but also as a place where people can track real-time news and information. Cashtags in particular could attract traders and investors to Threads who typically rely on X.
Despite facing stiff competition from X, Meta announced earlier this year that Threads topped 500 million monthly users, and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg says the company believes the app is on track to reach a billion users over time.

articles.title: Jensen Huang revient à la tête de Nvidia : comment expliquer ce retournement de situation ?
articles.text:
Ce lundi 23 novembre, nous avons assisté à un rebondissement assez inattendu : Jensen Huang a récupéré son poste de PDG au sein de Nvidia, alors qu’il avait remis sa démission 11 jours auparavant à la suite d’affaires extraconjugales, notamment avec Alice Huang, suspectée par Washington d’être une espionne au service de la Chine. Mais comment expliquer ce retour alors que le conseil d’administration de l’entreprise avait clairement annoncé que cela n’arriverait pas, tout en entamant les démarches pour trouver un remplaçant ? Si nous ne savons pas exactement ce qu’il s’est passé en coulisse, plusieurs éléments permettent d’expliquer la situation.
Donald Trump a soutenu le retour de Jensen Huang
Cela n’est pas un secret : Jensen Huang et Donald Trump affichent une certaine complicité. Nvidia a par exemple donné 25 millions de dollars (environ 23 millions d’euros) pour financer la construction de la salle de bal de la Maison-Blanche (Apple et Google ont également fait un don de plus de 20 millions de dollars). En septembre dernier, en pleine conférence, Donald Trump a appelé Jensen pour rappeler une nouvelle fois sa volonté de ne pas freiner la course à l’intelligence artificielle. Les deux hommes avaient alors montré leur plein accord.
Et nous n’allons pas parler des termes utilisés par Trump pour qualifier Jensen Huang : « une légende », « un génie », « Le meilleur atout pour l’entreprise [Nvidia], mais aussi pour les États-Unis. », etc. Bref, Donald Trump avait tout intérêt à garder Jensen, un de ses alliés, à la tête de Nvidia. Le président américain a d’ailleurs salué le conseil d’administration de Nvidia pour sa « décision juste et appropriée » de rétablir Jensen Huang à la tête de l’entreprise. Il reste à voir dans quelle mesure Donald Trump à joué un rôle dans cette réintégration.
Selon Trump, Jensen Huang ne représenterait aucun risque pour la sécurité nationale
Donald Trump a également précisé un point : le PDG de Nvidia ne représenterait aucun risque pour la sécurité nationale. Le président américain a expliqué : « Le gouvernement des États-Unis n’a aucune raison de croire que le retour de Jensen chez NVIDIA présente un quelconque risque pour la sécurité nationale ». Il précise ensuite : « le procureur général des États-Unis a confirmé que le gouvernement américain ne dispose d’aucune preuve indiquant qu’il aurait commis des actes illégaux ».
De son côté, Nvidia a expliqué que « le conseil d’administration a consulté de hauts responsables du gouvernement américain » et qu’il est dorénavant « persuadé que la réintégration de M. Huang ne présente aucun risque pour la sécurité nationale ». Rappelons que Washington envisage de nouvelles restrictions sur les exportations de puces Nvidia vers la Chine, tandis que certains démocrates ont d’ores et déjà annoncé leur intention de mener une enquête approfondie sur l’affaire Jensen Huang.
Nvidia, une entreprise trop importante pour être fragilisée
Bien entendu, il n’est pas seulement question d’une amitié entre Jensen Huang et Donald Trump. Pour rappel, Nvidia est l’une des entreprises qui génèrent le plus de bénéfices au monde, sans parler de son rôle majeur dans la course à l’intelligence artificielle. Et comme le souligne Le Figaro, l’affaire Jensen Huang a donné au cours et à la capitalisation de Nvidia des allures de montagnes russes.
Lorsque Jensen Huang a reconnu son infidélité et que le conseil d’administration a ouvert une enquête, l’action de Nvidia a chuté de 4,3 %. À l’annonce de son retour au poste de PDG, le titre a bondi de 31,5 % en une seule séance, une réaction qui souligne clairement l’importance de Jensen Huang dans la confiance accordée à Nvidia par les marchés.
De multiples pressions pour demander le retour de Jensen Huang
Enfin, nous pouvons noter les multiples appels à réintégrer Jensen Huang en tant que PDG de Nvidia. La Silicon Valley s’est mobilisée en faveur de Jensen Huang. Des employés de Nvidia ont réclamé son retour, tandis que 157 000 personnes, parmi lesquelles Elon Musk, ont également pris position en sa faveur.
Quoi qu’il en soit, nous pensions que la démission de Jensen Huang marquerait la fin d’une ère dans le secteur de la tech. Elle ne constituera finalement qu’un épisode, certes très mouvementé. Du moins, pour l’instant. Au vu des innombrables péripéties de cette affaire, nous ne sommes pas à l’abri de nouvelles révélations.

articles.title: Es oficial: ‘Los Anillos de Poder’ tendrá cuarta temporada en Prime Video
articles.text:
Buenas noticias para los fans de El Señor de los Anillos: Amazon ha renovado oficialmente Los Anillos de Poder para una cuarta temporada. El anuncio se da unas pocas horas antes de que la serie de Prime Video estrene los últimos dos capítulos de su temporada 3, que hasta aquí ha recibido muy buenas críticas.
Los detalles de la cuarta temporada de Los Anillos de Poder son todavía escasos, y con razón. Lo que Amazon sí ha confirmado es que el equipo creativo que lideran J.D. Payne y Patrick McKay continuará al frente del proyecto basado en el trabajo literario de J. R. R. Tolkien.
Por lo pronto, Los Anillos de Poder tiene su cuarta temporada en etapa de preproducción. El rodaje se pondrá en marcha durante la primavera de 2027 en Reino Unido, así que todavía quedan varios meses por delante antes de que las cámaras comiencen a grabar en Shepperton Studios.
Amazon confía en seguir explorando la Segunda Edad de la Tierra Media con una siguiente entrega de Los Anillos de Poder. La compañía no indica si el objetivo es concluir la adaptación con la cuarta temporadas, o si está la puerta abierta a la posibilidad de continuar desarrollando tramas en el futuro.
Los Anillos de Poder, confirmada para una cuarta temporada en Prime Video
Por lo pronto, Los Anillos de Poder no tiene fecha de estreno confirmada para su cuarta temporada. Considerando que el rodaje se realizará a partir de la primavera de 2027 y que las primeras tres entregas tuvieron dos años de diferencia entre sí, no es descabellado pensar que llegará hacia finales de 2028. De todas maneras, todavía no hay confirmación oficial por parte de Prime Video.
La atención de los fanáticos hoy está puesta en los últimos dos episodios de la temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder, que llegarán a la plataforma esta misma noche. Los mismos mostrarán el momento más esperado por los fanáticos: la forja del tan codiciado Anillo Único. Los episodios estarán disponibles en Prime Video a partir de las 21:00, hora del Este de Estados Unidos. Esto significa que se podrán ver a partir de las 20:00 en México, las 23:00 en Argentina y las 03:00 del 25 de noviembre en España.
Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
Peter Friedlander, jefe de televisión de Amazon MGM Studios, celebró la renovación de Los Anillos de Poder para una cuarta temporada. "El Señor de los Anillos: Los Anillos de Poder se ha convertido en una serie emblemática para Prime Video. Ahora que la tercera temporada nos ofrece el gran acontecimiento que los fans llevaban tanto tiempo esperando —la forja del Anillo Único—, nos enorgullece confirmar la cuarta temporada con J.D. Payne, Patrick McKay y todo el equipo creativo. Estamos deseando sumergir aún más a los espectadores en el fascinante mundo de la Segunda Edad de Tolkien", remarcó.

articles.title: Maharashtra GST Department conducts search at Turtlemint subsidiary
articles.text:
Maharashtra GST Department conducts search at Turtlemint subsidiary
The filing has added that the regular business operations of Turtlemint and TIB remains unaffected.
The Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax (GST) has initiated inspection,search and seizure proceedings at the premises of Turtlemint Insurance Broking Services, according to a regulatory filing on November 24.
The search was conducted at Turtlemint Insurance Broking Services Private Limited (“TIB”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company at its registered office situated at Mumbai.
“TIB is extending full cooperation to the concerned authorities and is providing the requisite information, documents and clarifications as may be required in connection with the proceedings,” said the filing.
Turtlemint will keep the Stock Exchanges informed of further developments, if any, in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
The filing has added that the regular business operations of Turtlemint and TIB remains unaffected. It also said that the company and TIB “remains commiƩed to conduct its business in compliance with the applicable laws and regulations.”
Founded in 2015 by Dhirendra Mahyavanshi and Anand Prabhudesai, Turtlemint operates an insurance distribution platform. It competes with companies such as Policybazaar and InsuranceDekho in India's digital insurance segment.

articles.title: Claude franchit un nouveau cap et permet désormais de créer des applications maison pour Mac et Windows, toujours sans coder
articles.text:
Les artefacts de Claude entrent dans une nouvelle dimension.
Depuis leur lancement en juin 2024, ces petites applications interactives que le LLM code lui-même permettent de créer en quelques échanges toutes sortes de prototypes, comme une liste de tâches, un tableau de bord ou un planificateur de budget.
Il restait cependant une limite pour l’utilisateur, puisque ces outils étaient enfermés dans la conversation où ils avaient été créés. Pour s’en servir, il fallait rouvrir Claude et remonter jusqu’à la bonne discussion, ou bien en garder le lien.
Le 24 novembre 2026, Anthropic a annoncé la fonction « Install as app », en cours de déploiement en bêta dans les applications Claude pour Mac et Windows, qui permet de les installer sur son ordinateur.
Ce que ça change concrètement
Dans les grandes lignes, Anthropic promet un vrai logiciel plutôt qu’une page dans le chat. Jusqu’ici, l’artefact se comportait comme une page web affichée à l’intérieur de Claude. Désormais, une fois installé, il a sa propre icône et s’ouvre dans sa propre fenêtre, comme n’importe quel programme.
Il peut envoyer des notifications, se placer dans la barre des menus du Mac ou dans la zone de notification de Windows, et faire appel à Claude ainsi qu’aux connecteurs branchés sur le compte de l’utilisateur. Quand on modifie l’artefact dans Claude, l’application se met à jour toute seule, et on peut la partager avec d’autres personnes.
Comme souvent, Anthropic mise sur la simplicité pour l’utilisateur. Pour installer une app, on décrit l’outil voulu à Claude, on le teste sous forme d’artefact, puis on choisit « Install as app » dans le menu de partage. Il n’y a pas besoin d’empaqueter ni de signer le logiciel, ni d’avoir une clé API, puisque l’app passe par le compte Claude.
Des applications qui peuvent toucher à vos fichiers
En matière de cybersécurité, le plus gros changement concerne les privilèges accordés à ces apps. Anthropic a prévu trois niveaux de permissions. Par défaut, l’app reste limitée à ce qu’elle ferait dans un navigateur. Le deuxième niveau lui donne accès à des fonctions contrôlées par Claude, comme une fenêtre toujours au premier plan ou un raccourci clavier utilisable partout. Le troisième, l’accès complet, lui permet de lancer des programmes et de lire, modifier ou supprimer des fichiers sans redemander l’autorisation.
Ce niveau est réservé aux apps que l’on a créées soi-même ou, sur les offres Team et Enterprise, à celles créées au sein de son organisation. Claude redemande l’autorisation après chaque mise à jour, mais Anthropic n’examine pas les applications et recommande de « n’accorder l’accès complet qu’aux applications auxquelles vous faites confiance ».
À noter que ces apps ne fonctionnent pas hors ligne. Il faut être connecté à son compte Claude pour les ouvrir, et chaque requête qu’elles envoient au modèle est décomptée des limites de l’abonnement. La bêta est ouverte à toutes les offres, mais sur Enterprise elle reste désactivée tant qu’un propriétaire du compte ne l’a pas activée.

articles.title: Canada’s Scott Pilgrim is coming to Fortnite
articles.text:
Fortnite just got a little more Canadian.
Developer Epic Games has announced that skins based on Scott Pilgrim and Ramona Flowers are coming to its popular battle royale game sometime this week.
In a short trailer, we can see the Toronto couple in creator Bryan Lee O’Malley’s signature comic book style. Scott sports his jacket, star t-shirt, guitar and flaming sword, while Ramona has her punk outfit and hammer. Naturally, the trailer also riffs on Scott Pilgrim‘s fighting game-style battles with the evil exes and Envy Adams music.
Epic Games didn’t confirm the V-Bucks cost for Scott and Ramona or what else, if anything, this collab might include. In the meantime, though, O’Malley shared fun new artwork of the pair dropping from the Fortnite Battle Bus.
It’s been a good year for everyone’s favourite sword-wielding Torontonian. In March, Montreal-based Tribute Games released Scott Pilgrim EX, a brand-new beat ’em up featuring an original story by O’Malley.

articles.title: Gamer hijacks plane in GTA 6 using just mind control and eye tracking — Xbox controller mapped to read brain signals using EEG, maps mental commands to an Xbox controller without surgery
articles.text:
Gamer hijacks plane in GTA 6 using just mind control and eye tracking — Xbox controller mapped to read brain signals using EEG, maps mental commands to an Xbox controller without surgery
She used eye tracking and gyroscopes for thumbstick control.
EEG machines are used to detect and record brain activity, so one enterprising tech enthusiast decided to use them to play GTA VI. Creator Perri Karyal showed her feat on X, where she streamed her gameplay while wearing a wireless electroencephalogram (EEG) designed for research.
Perri could be seen jumping a fence with Jason on a motorbike, before proceeding toward a parked fighter to steal and fly it. Her brain activity is overlaid on the screen while she’s playing, and viewers could also see the creator intensely focused on the game.
She trained the software to recognize specific brain signals and mapped them to an action on her Xbox controller. For example, imagining pushing a cube forward would correspond to a button press, getting angry lets her interact with cars and other vehicles, while picturing a hopping cricket would also make her character jump. The joysticks, on the other hand, are controlled via eye tracking and through gyroscopes on the head unit.
While Perri makes it look effortless, using the EEG device for gaming is way harder than what many people think. “People don’t realize how challenging it is!” Karyal replied to a comment. One viewer also mentioned the huge mass of brainwaves that appeared on the screen when she took off on the jet, to which she responded, “I was so stressed out. DO YOU KNOW HOW MANY TIMES I TRIED TO DO THIS.” Even though using wireless EEG for gaming does not have any apparent side effects, the creator said that she gets headaches after hours of gaming because of how much the headset squeezes her head.
This isn’t the first time that we’ve seen people playing games using just their mind. Neuralink has recently shown off one of its patients shooting at NPCs and even “threading the needle” with a speedboat using a brain-computer interface (BCI) chip. The big difference between Perri’s creation and Neuralink’s BCI, though, is that the latter requires invasive neurosurgery.
It may be surprising to think how a tech creator could beat Neuralink at its own game, but the latter has already applied the technology to multiple trial patients. We’ve seen them playing complicated games like World of Warcraft and Counter-Strike 2, while others used it for productivity and creativity, like editing a YouTube video.
These technologies are still in the development and trial phases or are being experimented on by enterprising creators and tech tubers. However, it also gives hope to individuals with limited mobility, as it gives them hope that they could regain some form of mobility and independence in the future.

articles.title: ChatGPT Health has finally arrived on Android — and it can help you understand what all those numbers on your fitness tracker actually mean
articles.text:
ChatGPT can now make sense of all that health and fitness data on your Android phone — and it could make your smartwatch a lot more useful
Personalized insights with some important AI limitations
Your Android phone can now use ChatGPT to help you make more sense of all your health data. OpenAI has enhanced ChatGPT Health with an expansion to Android and desktop. Crucially for Android users, the expansion includes support for Android Health Connect, Google's system for sharing health and fitness information between compatible apps. It gives ChatGPT access, with your permission, to information about your daily habits that previously would have required some tedious manual input.
The appeal of bringing that information into ChatGPT is fairly obvious to anyone who owns a fitness tracker but rarely looks beyond their daily step count. Most fitness apps are excellent at collecting information, but figuring out what to do with it can be more complicated. Having an AI assistant that can explain those numbers in everyday language could make them considerably more useful.
Android's healthy connections
ChatGPT Health is available to eligible users aged 18 and older in the US on the Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans. The Android expansion is happening gradually, so you may need to wait a little longer before it appears on your account. Some of the more advanced features, particularly those involving OpenAI's autonomous personal agents called dots, require a Pro subscription.
To get started, update the ChatGPT app on your Android phone and look for Health in the sidebar or under the Explore menu. Once you've opened Health, select the option to connect your information and choose Android Health Connect. You'll then be asked which categories of information you're willing to share before ChatGPT begins syncing your data.
Health Connect acts as an intermediary between ChatGPT and compatible fitness apps. If you use a Garmin smartwatch or an Oura Ring, for instance, you'll need to make sure its companion app is sharing information with Health Connect. Exactly how much ChatGPT can learn about your exercise habits will depend on what your devices record and what their respective apps make available.
Once everything is connected, you can ask questions about your fitness information in an ordinary ChatGPT conversation. You can also add @Health to a prompt to explicitly request that the AI consult your connected information. There's no need to spend every conversation about your daily walks in a dedicated corner of ChatGPT.
The most immediately useful aspect of the update may be the ability to explore relationships between different parts of your daily routine. You could ask ChatGPT to compare your sleeping habits on weekdays with those on weekends, for example. You could then ask it to examine whether the days when you're most physically active coincide with longer nights of sleep.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
That sort of analysis is possible with many existing fitness apps, but it often involves navigating several screens and interpreting graphs yourself. ChatGPT allows you to pursue whatever detail catches your attention without being constrained by the layout of a particular dashboard. It essentially gives your fitness statistics a conversational interface.
There are some mundane but potentially rewarding applications, too. If you've been trying to walk more regularly, you could ask ChatGPT to identify which days of the week you've historically found it easiest to fit in a longer walk. That might be more useful than another notification from your smartwatch informing you that you've spent too much time sitting down.
Oversharing your health
Of course, sharing information about your body with an AI company warrants considerably more thought than connecting a music streaming service. Your fitness data can reveal quite a lot about your life, including when you're usually asleep and how your routine changes over time. Even information that seems relatively innocuous in isolation can become surprisingly intimate when combined with months of other records.
OpenAI says it doesn't sell personal information collected through Health, and users can choose which accounts and categories of data they share. However, its updated privacy notice also explains that conversations involving Health can contribute to ChatGPT's memory if that feature is enabled. The company's current policy gives users control over whether conversations and memories are used for model training, making it worth reviewing your personalization and data settings before connecting anything.
There are practical limitations to consider as well. Consumer fitness devices are imperfect measuring instruments, and ChatGPT can't recover information that your smartwatch failed to collect. An impressive explanation of a sleep pattern is only as reliable as the underlying measurements, and the AI itself can misunderstand those numbers.
I'd be particularly wary of treating an apparent relationship between two measurements as proof that one caused the other. ChatGPT might identify that you tend to sleep less following particularly active days, but there could be plenty of unrelated reasons for that pattern. It's an interesting observation to explore rather than a scientific conclusion about your body.
The same caution applies to the wider medical capabilities of ChatGPT Health. Although the service supports connections to certain medical records, OpenAI describes it as a supplement to professional healthcare and says it isn't intended to diagnose or treat medical conditions. Having more personal information available to an AI doesn't confer a medical degree upon it.
ChatGPT probably won't transform you into an athlete simply because you've granted it access to your step count. Nor should you feel obliged to give an AI company access to every measurement your smartwatch has ever recorded. But this update might make your fitness tracker a little more valuable than just another expensive watch.
