articles.title: Google Maps prépare un changement de couleurs qui pourrait vous simplifier la route
articles.text:
Google Maps prépare un mode « haute visibilité » qui modifie les couleurs de la carte pendant la navigation. Repérée sur Android, cette option encore en développement pourrait rendre l’itinéraire plus facile à distinguer, notamment en mode sombre.
Au moment d’aborder un carrefour, on aimerait comprendre la carte sans avoir à départager les routes, les espaces verts et les indications à l’écran. La hiérarchie des couleurs compte alors autant que la quantité d’informations affichée et parfois, Google Maps donne un peu de fil à retordre pour comprendre quel croisement emprunter. Après avoir remis de l’ordre dans ses paramètres en début d’année, le logiciel de navigation pourrait offrir un nouveau choix pour adapter l’apparence du guidage.
Un itinéraire violet sur une carte plus sombre
Les journalistes d’Android Authority ont activé un réglage caché dans Google Maps proposant deux styles, « Standard » et « High-visibility ». Leurs captures montrent une nouvelle palette dans les thèmes clair et sombre.
En mode clair, les espaces verts prennent une teinte plus foncée et moins vive. Les surfaces beige ou blanc cassé passent au gris, tandis que l’indicateur de position devient violet. L’ensemble paraît plus sobre.
Le changement est plus marqué en mode sombre. Le fond bleuté laisse place à des tons presque noirs et l’itinéraire cyan devient violet, avec un remplissage lavande. L’eau et la végétation s’assombrissent également. Les boutons de navigation et les indications de direction gardent leur disposition.
L’intérêt potentiel est de faire ressortir le trajet parmi les éléments de la carte. Les captures permettent de comparer les couleurs, mais il faudra essayer ce style sur différents écrans et dans différentes conditions pour juger son apport réel, notamment sur l’écran d’une voiture, où l’information doit être comprise en moins d'une seconde.
Une option encore cachée sur Android
Le réglage a été découvert dans la version 26.48.00.1027729593 de l’application Android. Il n’est pas accessible aux utilisateurs et Google n’a communiqué aucune date de lancement. Sa présence dans le code ne garantit pas qu’il arrivera sous cette forme et Google pourrait tester encore quelques mois son nouveau schéma de couleurs avant de le rendre public.
Android Authority rapproche cette découverte de couleurs plus sombres observées sur Android Auto en septembre. Cela pourrait annoncer un même style pour le téléphone et l’écran de la voiture, mais le lien reste une hypothèse du média.
Si Google conserve ce choix entre deux styles, chacun pourra décider lequel lui convient le mieux. Le violet aura alors une tâche assez simple à remplir. Qu’on le trouve joli ou non, il faudra surtout qu’il nous aide à prendre la bonne sortie.

articles.title: Sony a menti sur la version PS5 de GTA 6
articles.text:
« Plays best on PS5 » : Sony n’a cessé de brandir ce slogan à la moindre occasion pendant la campagne marketing de GTA 6, qui s’est copieusement accélérée à partir de cet été. La firme nippone est le partenaire commercial de Rockstar Games pour cette sortie événement. Sony la présente comme « le plus grand lancement de l’histoire de PlayStation » : plus de 39 millions de joueurs uniques ont lancé le jeu sur PS5 entre sa sortie, le jeudi 19 novembre, et le 22 novembre.
Sauf que la réalité n’est pas vraiment celle affirmée par Sony. Digital Foundry, spécialiste des analyses techniques très poussées, a publié cette semaine une comparaison des quatre versions console de GTA 6 (PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X et Series S). La PS5 Pro, plus puissante, arrive logiquement en tête. Juste derrière, la Xbox Series X devance la PS5 standard. Les deux machines affichent une image quasi identique, autour de 1440p, mais la console de Microsoft tient bien mieux ses 30 images par seconde.
GTA 6 tourne mieux sur Xbox Series X que sur PS5
Concrètement, la PS5 souffre de davantage de chutes de framerate, même si les deux consoles peinent à maintenir les 30 images par seconde promises dans les séquences les plus exigeantes. La Xbox Series X profite en prime du VRR (fréquence de rafraîchissement variable) en 120 Hz, absent de la version PS5, qui rend ces baisses bien moins visibles. Un bug de la fonction Quick Resume permet même d’y dépasser les 30 images par seconde. En d’autres termes, quand Sony dit que GTA 6 se joue mieux sur PS5, c’est faux. Il se joue mieux sur PS5 Pro, ce qui n’est pas tout à fait la même chose.
Il faut par ailleurs rappeler que la Xbox Series X pourrait offrir des performances encore meilleures avec le FSR 4.1, que Rockstar Games n’utilise pour l’instant que sur la version Xbox Series S. La mise à l’échelle boostée à l’IA pourrait permettre à la plus puissante console de Microsoft d’aller encore plus loin, éventuellement de titiller la PS5 Pro. Pourquoi Rockstar Games ne l’utilise pas ? Jez Corden, journaliste chez Windows Central, écrit : « J’ai enquêté pour savoir si l’accord marketing de PlayStation pénalise artificiellement la version Xbox Series X en bloquant arbitrairement le FSR 4.1, mais c’est un sujet pour une autre fois. » Digital Foundry avance une explication plus technique. Le FSR 4.1 demande plus de temps de calcul à chaque image que la solution maison de Rockstar Games, ce qui obligerait à partir d’une définition plus basse pour tenir les 30 images par seconde.
Rappelons quand même que la Xbox Series X coûte nettement plus cher qu’une PS5 standard. En version numérique, la console de Microsoft est vendue 749,99 €, pile entre la PS5 (599,99 €) et la PS5 Pro (899,99 €), toutes trois sans lecteur de disque. Avec lecteur, elle grimpe à 799,99 €, à 100 € seulement de la PS5 Pro. Plus chère et dotée d’une meilleure puce graphique, la Xbox Series X fait logiquement mieux que la PS5.

articles.title: OPINION: Separate the hype from reality in China’s robotics race
articles.text:
Let’s start with the obvious; most of what you’ve seen of Chinese robots is not real. If you’re like me, your Instagram feed is full of humanoids doing backflipS or folding the laundry. The conclusion is either that China has solved robotics and we (Europe) are finished, or that they have adopted everything and we are just behind.
So we went to look. In August, six of us from Extantia visited around fifteen companies across Shanghai, Hangzhou and Beijing, then walked the floor of the World Robot Conference with its 300 exhibitors.
So, what is real?
The gap between the hype and reality
Much of what you see on Instagram is AI-generated while a lot of the rest is sped up. What looks autonomous is often teleoperated, or remote controlled
The reality is this: Chinese companies sold more humanoid robots than anyone last year. Roughly 75% went to research institutes, universities and schools. Another 20% went to entertainment: the robot that greets you at the supermarket, 50 robots dancing at a Chinese New Year show. Only 5% went to real industrial applications, 5% of maybe 13,000 units.
That is 650 robots in the whole of China doing work. At home it is non-existent, and will stay so for a while. A 180 cm, heavy machine in the living room? People have babies at home (I have checked, nobody wants this).
At the same time, the hardware problem has been solved, it is game over. What China did in batteries, cars and drones, it is doing now in humanoids. The supply chain exists and government centres publish the blueprint. It is like building Lego: you buy the parts, you assemble them. And it is only going to get cheaper.
The people building humanoids built the battery and car industries first. Around 85% of what goes into a humanoid, the actuators, magnets, chips and sensors, also goes into an electric car, so the suppliers and know-how were already there. Car companies finance the founders and are often their first customers.
What has not been solved is the software that makes a robot act on its own. We visited what the Chinese call humanoid gyms: halls where 200 people spend the day folding sheets, cleaning toilets and moving boxes while the robots record every movement as training data. Every room is different so the model learns variation. Impressive, but no model yet lets a humanoid finish a job without a person in the loop, which is why so much online is teleoperated. That is an opening for anybody with the right data and engineers, including European teams.
A more basic point the videos hide: for most real jobs, the human shape is the wrong shape. For clean floors, a robot vacuum is better than legs. In a factory you want wheels, because they are cheaper and more stable, and a gripper rather than a hand. A five-fingered hand is one of the most expensive parts of a humanoid and lasts a million open and close cycles, which is not long in industry.
The essence of the work is matching each task to the right amount of automation. The robots we saw actually earning money did precisely that: robot dogs carrying a hose into a fire, machines inspecting grid infrastructure, a robot directing traffic. Not spectacular on camera, but the return exists today.
China has hardware, Europe can win on application
Founders in China also think differently. American founders, and increasingly European ones, optimise for valuation: maximum hype, ambitious technology, all eyes on the next round. Chinese founders optimise for cash. The question is not how to disrupt an industry, but how little innovation gets you to market and paid, so the real work is funded from revenue.
If a supermarket wants a greeter robot, they will sell it one. CATL and BYD, which supply over half of the world’s EV batteries, did not start with lithium iron phosphate or solid state. BYD started with rechargeable cells for toys and phones, CATL’s predecessor with batteries for consumer electronics, and that cash paid for the breakthroughs later. Northvolt took the opposite route, and we all know what happened there.
There is a catch, of course. Europe depends on China for raw materials, batteries and components, and the debate about tariffs and export controls is justified.
But the dependence runs both ways. The Chinese car market is in a severe price war and most companies in it are losing money at home. When we told exhibitors we were European buyers, their eyes lit up. They need our market. Even China’s newly published five-year plan assumes these companies grow through exports, and with the US closed, that means Europe.
So a European company trying to beat China at manufacturing robot hardware is placing a bad bet. Better to benefit from China than compete with it: if my parts come from China, every fall in their costs improves my margins. The opportunity for Europe is not building the best humanoid. It is taking the best hardware available and putting it to work where we have the know-how and the customers: construction, heavy industry, petrochemicals and facility management. The more an industry has declined in Europe, the more automation can change its economics. That is the real case for reshoring.
Three things I tell our founders
First, have a China strategy. Competitor slides I see usually list only American companies, because the information firewall between Europe and China is real. Decide whether you are sourcing from China, partnering there, selling there or competing with it. You cannot build a hardware company without that answer.
Second, go there in person. See the factories, meet the suppliers and sit across from the founders you will compete with or buy from. No report or video replaces a week on the ground.
Third, deliver value now and automate later. Start with teleoperation if you need to. A team that stays in the lab until the autonomy is perfect may build something brilliant in five years for a market that has already been taken.
So, founders: what is your China strategy?

articles.title: How to Run NVIDIA Cosmos 3 on Local AI Devices Using Hugging Face Diffusers
articles.text:
Running video generation models locally can be challenging when model weights and intermediate data exceed available GPU memory. NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Nano is a world foundation model that generates videos from text, images, and other inputs to support physical AI development. Learn more about NVIDIA Cosmos for physical AI.
This tutorial walks you through how to run Cosmos 3 Nano on a GPU with as little as 12 GB of VRAM by storing most model weights in system RAM and transferring them to the GPU as needed. Using Hugging Face Diffusers, you’ll generate your first video, explore sound and additional input types, and use an FP8 checkpoint to further reduce memory requirements.
This streaming adapter builds on top of the native group offloading approach from the Hugging Face library to enable generation on a smaller GPU. The tradeoff is that this requires increased system RAM use and PCIe transfers for a smaller GPU-memory requirement. Note that this approach does not provide interactive latency or stream weights directly from disk during inference.
Step 1: Generate your first video
Use an existing Linux environment with Python 3.12 and a CUDA-enabled PyTorch build compatible with your GPU. The tested consumer-GPU hosts had approximately 128 GB of system RAM; this is not a measured minimum.
Clone Cosmos-Framework and install its standalone offloading package in your active environment. Run all examples and benchmark commands below from the package directory:
git clone https://github.com/NVIDIA/cosmos-framework.git
cd cosmos-framework/packages/diffusers-cpu-offloading
uv pip install '.[benchmarks]'
Pass the Hugging Face repository ID directly to build_pipeline. The first load downloads the checkpoint. Subsequent loads reuse cached files. Safety checking is enabled by default.
import torch
from cosmos3_streaming import StreamingConfig, build_pipeline
device = "cuda:0"
config = StreamingConfig(device=device)
pipe = build_pipeline(
    "nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano",
    config=config,
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
)
With no revision argument, the BF16 load uses the repository’s default branch. The default configuration chooses appropriate memory-saving behavior automatically.
Start with BF16 and PyTorch scaled dot-product attention (SDPA), the baseline used on all four tested GPUs.
Set the video options
This example generates 189 frames at 720p. For faster iteration on a 12 GB GPU, change height and width to 480 and 848, or 240 and 432.
common_video_args = {
    "negative_prompt": "",
    "num_frames": 189,
    "height": 720,
    "width": 1280,
    "fps": 24.0,
    "num_inference_steps": 35,
    "guidance_scale": 6.0,
    "add_resolution_template": False,
    "add_duration_template": False,
}
Generate and save the video
Next, generate and save the video using the following script:
t2v = pipe(
    prompt='{"scene":"A robot arm working in a kitchen"}',
    generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(123),
    output="videos",
    **common_video_args,
)
# Save the returned video frames as an MP4 file:
from diffusers.utils import export_to_video
export_to_video(t2v, "cosmos3_t2v.mp4", fps=common_video_args["fps"])
Step 2: Offload weights storage
The central idea is to store model weights in system RAM and use the GPU for computation.
To run large models within tight VRAM limits, this execution model manages memory and compute across the CPU and GPU in four ways:
- Checkpoint weights that are not currently needed remain in system RAM, in BF16 or the checkpoint’s FP8 representation.
- The next transformer block is transferred to the GPU when required.
- Every matrix multiplication and attention operation runs on CUDA.
- The adapter manages memory for denoising, the variational autoencoder (VAE) that encodes and decodes video, and safety checking.
With this approach, system RAM acts as the backing store for model weights. More demanding requests, including 720p Transfer on a 12 GB GPU, use an automatic lower-memory execution mode while keeping model computation on CUDA.
Move weights from system RAM to the GPU
Next, move weights from system RAM to the GPU. Figure 1 shows the path from checkpoint storage to GPU computation. Checkpoint files remain on disk between runs. During generation, system RAM is the backing store for weights that are not currently on the GPU. This is why a fast SSD helps with model loading, while sufficient system RAM and PCIe bandwidth matter during generation.
Reuse understanding context during generation
Diffusers provides sequential, model-level, and group-level CPU offloading to move model components between CPU and GPU memory. The Cosmos adapter builds on those mechanisms and coordinates when the model’s understanding and generation pathways run.
NVIDIA Cosmos 3, an open omnimodal world foundation model for physical AI, has two complementary pathways inside its transformer:
- The understanding pathway interprets the prompt and other conditioning inputs. These inputs remain fixed during generation.
- The generation pathway processes the evolving video, sound, or action representation at every denoising step while using the understanding result as context.
The transformer contains both understanding and generation computation. With fixed conditioning and precision, the adapter prepares the understanding context once and reuses it during generation. If native FP8 precision changes during denoising, that context is refreshed to match.
Video 1 shows how generation traverses the transformer blocks at each denoising step. A 35-step request runs denoising steps 1 through 35. Each step traverses 36 transformer blocks, indexed 0 through 35. After block 35, the scheduler updates the generation state and the next step starts at block 0. After the final denoising step, the pipeline decodes the output.
Classifier-free guidance (CFG) in Hugging Face combines predictions with and without prompt conditioning at each denoising step. The adapter reuses each streamed block across these predictions instead of transferring its weights for each branch. Transfer can add a control branch, which the automatic low-memory mode handles through the same API.
Keep the official Diffusers pipeline
The adapter uses the official Diffusers modular pipeline for:
- Prompt processing
- Conditioning and latent preparation
- Sequence preparation
- The denoising loop and UniPC scheduler
- Masking and classifier-free guidance output handling
- VAE decode
- Safety checking
- Output conversion
Manage memory across the complete request
Block offloading alone is not enough for the complete Cosmos pipeline. The adapter applies the following behavior automatically.
Reuse fixed understanding work
With fixed precision, the understanding pathway runs once for fixed conditioning inputs and its context is reused during denoising.
Stream generation blocks
Transformer weights remain in system RAM until their block is needed. The active block moves to the GPU, performs its CUDA work for the current denoising step, and makes room for the next block. Guidance predictions share the same block placement whenever possible.
Overlap transfers with computation
When the GPU has enough headroom, the next block can begin moving while the current block computes. Larger workloads automatically use the safer lower-memory schedule. There is no user-facing transfer schedule to configure.
Manage decoding and safety checks
VAE processing and safety checking have different memory requirements from denoising. The adapter manages those phases separately and automatically uses memory-efficient VAE execution on constrained cards. Users do not choose device-specific tuning values.
Handle larger Transfer requests
Transfer Modality performs more guidance work than text-to-video (T2V) and image-to-video (I2V). At 720p on a 12 GB GPU, the adapter automatically selects a lower-memory execution mode. The full GeForce RTX 5070 modality results include its generation time and guardrail settings.
Step 3: Generate other modalities ( sound, action, etc )
Reuse pipe, device, and common_video_args from Step 1 for the examples in this section. Replace the input image and video paths with your own files. The prompts are illustrative; use the benchmark scripts for the exact measured inputs. Video-only calls return a list of frames. Calls requesting sound or action return a mapping of the requested outputs.
Image-to-video
Condition generation on an image with image=.
from diffusers.utils import load_image
image = load_image("/path/to/conditioning_image.jpg")
i2v = pipe(
    prompt='{"scene":"A vehicle approaches a rockfall on a coastal road"}',
    image=image,
    generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(1111),
    output="videos",
    **common_video_args,
)
Video-to-video
Pass a source video and choose the conditioning frames for video-to-video (V2V) generation.
from diffusers.utils import load_video
source_video = load_video("/path/to/source_video.mp4")
v2v = pipe(
    prompt='{"scene":"A robot pours liquid into a cup"}',
    video=source_video,
    condition_frame_indexes_vision=[0, 1],
    condition_video_keep="first",
    generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0),
    output="videos",
    **common_video_args,
)
Text-to-video with sound
Set enable_sound=True and include an audio description to generate video and sound together.
t2v_sound = pipe(
    prompt=(
        '{"scene":"A robot arm working in a kitchen",'
        '"audio_description":"Soft servo whirring and a ceramic clink."}'
    ),
    enable_sound=True,
    generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0),
    output=["videos", "sound", "sampling_rate"],
    **common_video_args,
)
Image-to-video with sound
Combine the image input with enable_sound=True to generate both outputs.
i2v_sound = pipe(
    prompt=(
        '{"scene":"A vehicle travels along a coastal road",'
        '"audio_description":"Road noise, wind, and distant waves."}'
    ),
    image=image,
    enable_sound=True,
    generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0),
    output=["videos", "sound", "sampling_rate"],
    **common_video_args,
)
Action generation
Use CosmosActionCondition to select the action domain and provide the conditioning video.
from diffusers import CosmosActionCondition
action_result = pipe(
    prompt="Put the pot to the left of the purple item.",
    action=CosmosActionCondition(
        mode="policy",
        chunk_size=16,
        domain_name="bridge_orig_lerobot",
        resolution_tier=480,
        video=load_video("/path/to/bridge_input.mp4"),
        view_point="ego_view",
    ),
    fps=5,
    num_inference_steps=30,
    guidance_scale=1.0,
    use_system_prompt=False,
    generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0),
    output=["videos", "action"],
)
Control-guided generation
Pass a control video with the control_videos argument. Safety checking remains enabled in this example; the benchmark’s guardrails-off exception is documented with the results.
transfer = pipe(
    prompt='{"scene":"Transform the input using edge guidance"}',
    negative_prompt="",
    control_videos={
        "edge": load_video("/path/to/control_edge.mp4"),
    },
    num_frames=121,
    height=720,
    width=1280,
    fps=30.0,
    num_inference_steps=35,
    guidance_scale=3.0,
    control_guidance=1.5,
    generator=torch.Generator(device=device).manual_seed(0),
    output="videos",
)
Diffusers routes each call to the appropriate workflow and loads the required components through the same pipeline.
Step 4: Use the FP8 checkpoint
Use nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano with the FP8 branch for the dedicated FP8 checkpoint. From the same package directory, install the FP8 extra, which includes NVIDIA Model Optimizer, before loading the checkpoint:
uv pip install '.[benchmarks,fp8]'
Select the FP8 branch through the same Hub API by passing revision="fp8":
pipe = build_pipeline(
    "nvidia/Cosmos3-Nano",
    revision="fp8",
    config=StreamingConfig(device="cuda:0"),
    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    checkpoint_precision="fp8",
)
The adapter uses the checkpoint’s native Diffusers precision policy. W8A8 uses 8-bit weights and 8-bit activations. W8A16 reuses the stored 8-bit weights, dequantizes them for a linear operation, and uses 16-bit activations. The tested Nano video checkpoint selects W8A16 for the first three and last three denoising steps and W8A8 for the middle steps. Note that attention remains BF16 SDPA; the entire pipeline does not run in FP8.
Step 5: Choose a GPU and resolution
Use Table 1 to choose a starting resolution. The default configuration adapts automatically to the requested resolution, modality, and available GPU memory.
| GPU class | Recommended use | 
|---|---|
| 12 GB | Start at 240p or 480p for iteration. Full 720p is supported, including Transfer, but can be substantially slower. | 
| 16 GB | 480p is a practical iteration mode; 720p is supported with automatic memory management. | 
| 24 GB | Full-resolution generation has more working room and is materially faster in the tested configuration. | 
| 32 GB | Best measured consumer-GPU latency for the 720p BF16 workload. | 
These are guidance ranges rather than fixed limits. Resolution, frame count, modality, checkpoint precision, available system RAM, and PCIe bandwidth all affect fit and runtime.
Step 6: Benchmark setup and results
The presented results cover text-to-video across four GeForce RTX cards and all seven generation modalities on the GeForce RTX 5070. Use Table 4 to estimate memory requirements and wait times. Hosts, software revisions, and safety settings can affect latency, so these single-run measurements are not a controlled GPU ranking or a multiseed BF16-versus-FP8 comparison.
Reproduce the benchmarks
From the package directory used in Step 1, run the BF16 and FP8 benchmarks separately to measure your system. These commands cover all seven modalities and three resolution tiers. Install the FP8 dependency from Step 4 before running the FP8 command.
python benchmarks/benchmark_bf16.py --output-dir artifacts/benchmark-bf16
python benchmarks/benchmark_fp8.py --output-dir artifacts/benchmark-fp8
The benchmark guide in benchmarks/README.md explains the pinned inputs, per-case logs, summary tables, --resume, and --preflight-only. Safety checks are enabled by default. Reproducing the labeled Transfer timings requires an explicit Transfer-only run with --transfer-without-guardrails. The FP8 runner records the exact checkpoint revision and uses the native Diffusers policy.
Test settings
The benchmark workloads use the bundled model-card inputs. Each saved video was checked for its output dimensions, frame count, and frame rate. Sound cases also produced WAV files, and Action cases produced action JSON. Table 2 lists the generation and timing settings.
| Control | BF16 T2V | RTX 5070 modalities | 
|---|---|---|
| Output | 189 frames, 24 fps | 189 frames for video/sound; 17 for Action; 121 at 30 fps for Transfer | 
| Resolution tiers | 432×240, 848×480, 1280×720 | 432×240, 848×480, 1280×720; action uses corresponding tiers | 
| Denoising | 35 UniPC steps, CFG 6, seed 123 | 35 steps for video/sound/Transfer; 30 for Action; fixed per-modality inputs and seeds | 
| Safety | Enabled | Enabled except the explicitly labeled guardrails-off Transfer rows | 
| Timing | Pipeline call through returned frames | Pipeline call through returned modality tensors | 
| Excluded | Construction, checkpoint loading, MP4 encoding | Construction, checkpoint loading, file encoding | 
Tested hardware
Table 3 lists the tested GPUs. Each host had approximately 128 GB of system RAM. CPU offloading exchanges GPU memory pressure for system RAM use. The measured consumer-GPU hosts had approximately 128 GB of system RAM.
| GPU | Architecture | Compute capability | VRAM | System RAM | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GeForce RTX 5070 | Blackwell GB205 | SM120 | 12 GB | 128 GB class | 
| GeForce RTX 5080 | Blackwell GB203 | SM120 | 16 GB | 128 GB class | 
| GeForce RTX 4090 | Ada AD102 | SM89 | 24 GB | 128 GB class | 
| GeForce RTX 5090 | Blackwell GB202 | SM120 | 32 GB | 128 GB class | 
Text-to-video results across RTX GPUs
Table 4 compares text-to-video measurements across RTX cards. Pipeline time includes prompt processing, understanding, denoising, VAE decode, and safety checking, but excludes checkpoint loading and MP4 encoding. The RTX 5070 entries also appear in the full modality results in Table 5.

Get started with Cosmos 3 Nano on GeForce RTX GPUs
Weight streaming enables you to experiment with NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Nano on RTX GPUs with as little as 12 GB of VRAM by storing model weights in system RAM while keeping computation on the GPU.
To get started, install the Cosmos-Framework offloading package and run the BF16 text-to-video example at 240p or 480p. Then explore image- and video-conditioned generation, sound, actions, and control inputs through the same Diffusers API. Try the FP8 checkpoint and use the included benchmarks to compare generation time and memory use on your hardware.
- Download the Cosmos 3 Nano checkpoint and its FP8 branch on Hugging Face.
- Find examples and code in the Cosmos-Framework offloading package.
- Review the Diffusers memory optimization guide for CPU offloading and the Cosmos 3 pipeline documentation for supported generation workflows.
- Join the community, open issues, and contribute to the Cosmos ecosystem on GitHub and Discord.

articles.title: Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations
articles.text:
Threat actors have exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise two dozen Check Point Security management servers in an ongoing campaign targeting 22 organizations.
Threat intelligence firm GreyNoise detected the activity, noting that it resembled cyberespionage operations, although the attacker's motivation could not be conclusively determined.
The researchers track the activity as GT13 and confirmed it was ongoing between October 17 and November 2, when their visibility ended. However, given the threat actor's persistent access to Check Point devices, they believe the campaign remains active.
GreyNoise says the 22 victim organizations are spread across 17 countries, and show no clear evidence of specific targeting. They include government entities, financial services providers, and companies in the energy, transportation, mining, and manufacturing sectors.
The attacks were launched from 99 IP addresses that appear to come from compromised Check Point devices and ExpressVPN exit nodes.
A Rejetto HTTP File Server, compromised by exploiting CVE-2026-61500, was used as an operational relay for managing intrusions and collecting stolen data from the compromised environments.
While GreyNoise could not determine when or how the Check Point servers were breached, it observed the exploitation of CVE-2026-16232 during the post-compromise stages.
The vulnerability is an authentication bypass in Check Point SmartConsole that allows attackers to obtain an application login token and authenticate with administrator privileges.
Check Point warned about the flaw in July, marking it as an actively exploited zero-day.
The researchers also observed attempts to exploit CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass to Run Script), and CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF).
GreyNoise recorded over 1,400 network sessions, 800 command-line artifacts, and 1,200 file-related activities, such as:
- Stealing firewall databases, credentials, configuration data, and internal certificate authority files.
- Generating a new certificate in one victim's environment.
- Unloading security policies, effectively disabling firewall protections.
- Conducting internal network reconnaissance and attempting lateral movement.
- Targeting additional enterprise systems, including Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2023-4966), Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2024-21893), VMware vCenter (CVE-2021-21972 and CVE-2023-34048), Microsoft Exchange (CVE-2021-26855/34473), and Microsoft Netlogon (CVE-2020-1472).
On October 26, the attacker performed a bulk certificate management operation across all 24 compromised Check Point servers, which failed, but still helped GreyNoise identify victims.
Τhe researchers assess that GT13 operated an AI-powered offensive tool, based on behavior, observed automation, and custom tooling, but the use of AI in this campaign remains unconfirmed.
Although GreyNoise lost visibility into the campaign operations on November 2, the researchers believe it could still be ongoing and have notified international government partners and CERTs to alert impacted organizations.
The company also shared indicators of compromise (IoCs) that could help identify additional intrusions or block future attempts.
BleepingComputer has contacted Check Point to ask if they have better visibility into those attacks and which flaw was exploited for initial access, and we are waiting for their response.
Update 25/11 - A Check Point spokesperson responded to our inquiry with the below statement:
"We are aware of the activity outlined by the GreyNoise article. The attackers used CVE-2026-16232, a SmartConsole authentication bypass vulnerability that Check Point publicly disclosed in July 2026, with a note that exploitation had been observed in the wild. This vulnerability and available protections are therefore not new. The GreyNoise article also reports that the attackers used an adaptation of the publicly available Metasploit module for CVE-2026-16232, so the exploitation method described is also previously known." - Check Point

articles.title: What Wave’s mobile money licence means for the DRC
articles.text:
24 novembre 2026
Hello 👋,
Welcome back to Francophone Weekly by TechCabal, your weekly deep dive into the tech ecosystem across French-speaking Africa. For readers who want to understand Francophone Africa beyond headlines—through markets, startups, and systems. New editions of the newsletter will land directly in your inbox every Tuesday at 12 PM WAT.
By default, this newsletter is in French. If you’re reading this in your email inbox, click the “Read in English” button below to switch to the English version. If you’re reading on our website, you can either click the button below or toggle the language selector at the top right-hand side of the page to view the English edition.
Onze ans après son dernier agrément, la Banque centrale du Congo ouvre le mobile money à un cinquième acteur. Wave arrive moins de cinq mois avant l’interdiction des paiements en dollars cash dans le commerce. Le prix qu’il fixera pour le franc congolais comptera davantage que celui d’un transfert.
1. Onze ans, une porte qui s’ouvre
            Un employé de Wave en train d’aider des clients. Source de l’image : Wave, la fintech basée au Sénégal.
       
        
    
Le 17 novembre 2026, la Banque centrale du Congo (BCC) a accordé à Wave un agrément d’établissement de monnaie électronique (EME), annoncé le lendemain. Wave devient le cinquième émetteur agréé en RDC, après Airtel Money et Orange Money (tous deux début 2012), Vodacash, qui opère M-Pesa, plus tard en 2012, et Afrimobile Money en septembre 2015.
Aucun nouvel entrant en onze ans. The Condia attribue ce gel au poids des opérateurs télécoms sur l’infrastructure du mobile money. Aucune interdiction formelle n’a jamais existé.
L’agrément permet à Wave d’émettre, de gérer et de distribuer de la monnaie électronique en son nom propre. Le détail compte. Au Cameroun, son seul autre marché d’Afrique centrale, Wave opère via Commercial Bank Cameroun, autorisée par la COBAC en juin 2025 à proposer le service. Kinshasa lui offre son premier agrément direct dans la région.
Wave recrute à Kinshasa depuis septembre pour son réseau d’agents, la gestion de liquidité, la conformité et le service client. Jérémie Lukusa, son directeur général en RDC, tempère : « Un agrément ouvre la voie. »
Un duopole qui gagne au retrait
Wave entre sur un marché où deux opérateurs captent plus de 80 % des revenus des transactions de mobile money. Fin juin 2026, la RDC comptait 34,8 millions d’abonnements mobile money actifs — environ 31 pour 100 habitants. Airtel Money menait avec 43,5 % des revenus de transaction au deuxième trimestre, suivi de M-PESA avec 39,7 %, Orange Money à 16,4 % et Afrimoney à 0,4 %.
En 2024, 39,2 % des adultes congolais détenaient un compte dans une institution financière ou auprès d’un prestataire de mobile money, selon la Banque mondiale.
Envoyer de l’argent coûte déjà peu, environ 1 % chez les opérateurs historiques. Le retirer coûte cher. Les frais de retrait sont dégressifs et atteignent jusqu’à 9 % sur les petits montants, contre 1 à 2 % sur les gros, selon The Condia. La commerçante du Marché central de Kinshasa qui retire de petites sommes plusieurs fois par semaine paie le tarif maximal. Wave inverse la logique : 1 % sur les transferts, dépôts et retraits gratuits. La bataille se jouera au guichet de retrait.
Les banques ne restent pas inactives. En octobre 2025, EquityBCDC a lancé le Compte Libanga, un compte d’entrée de gamme destiné aux travailleurs de l’informel gagnant moins de 300 dollars par mois, comme les conducteurs de moto-taxi et les petits commerçants. Il s’ouvre avec 1 dollar ou 2 900 CDF et donne accès à une carte locale gratuite et à des retraits gratuits, pour un forfait de 0,25 dollar par mois, le crédit et l’assurance étant prévus dans un second temps. Les banques développent aussi des passerelles banque-portefeuille et portefeuille-banque, afin que le consommateur congolais dispose d’un choix plus large et de tarifs plus attractifs. La concurrence de Wave viendra aussi des guichets bancaires.
Les prix vont-ils baisser ? Oui, d’abord sur les petits retraits
Le Sénégal sert de référence. Avant Wave, Orange Money facturait 6 à 10 % par transaction. En juin 2021, Orange a réduit ses tarifs d’environ 80 %, puis en novembre 2021 il facturait 0,8 % à l’envoi et rien au retrait. En Côte d’Ivoire, les agents de mobile money ont fait grève en 2022 après une baisse des commissions de Wave, et Société Générale a fermé son portefeuille YUP, en partie à cause de la guerre des prix. Fin 2025, Wave détenait 80,6 % de l’encours de monnaie électronique au Sénégal.
La RDC ne rejouera pas ce scénario au même rythme. Le Sénégal avait un seul opérateur dominant. La RDC en a deux, chacun adossé à un groupe télécom multinational, avec sa propre base de cartes SIM et les moyens d’absorber une baisse de prix. Un scénario probable : les opérateurs historiques réduiront les frais de retrait sur les petits montants dans le trimestre suivant le lancement de Wave, et défendront le tarif de 1 % sur les transferts.
Les vraies contraintes de Wave sont sur le terrain. Son modèle repose sur des agents qui détiennent espèces et monnaie électronique, dans un pays de 2,3 millions de km² aux routes inégales et en conflit dans le Nord et le Sud-Kivu. Wave dit cibler les clients sans smartphone, ce qui passe en pratique par l’USSD, un canal contrôlé par les télécoms. Un accès équitable à l’USSD sera le premier test de la volonté de la BCC d’ouvrir la concurrence. Le second sera l’interopérabilité entre portefeuilles, abordée plus bas.
La newsletter continue après cette publicité.

2. Deux monnaies, un agenda réglementaire
            Des clients et des piétons passent devant des rangées de taxis et de magasins au marché de Birere, à Goma, en République démocratique du Congo. Source de l’image : Arlette Bashizi/Bloomberg
       
        
    
La RDC vit avec deux monnaies. Fin septembre 2026, 87,6 % des dépôts bancaires étaient libellés en devises, surtout en dollars. La BCC grignote ce chiffre depuis trois ans :
- Affichage des prix et paiement des impôts en francs congolais (CDF), en vertu de règles antérieures.
- Terminaux de paiement paramétrés uniquement en CDF à partir du 1er août 2024, quand seuls 13 % acceptaient la monnaie nationale.
- En avril 2025, le responsable d’une association d’agents M-PESA a déclaré à l’Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) que les agents payaient 30 % des retraits en dollars en francs congolais (CDF).
- Un rappel de décembre 2025 : les messageries financières ne peuvent pas refuser le CDF.
- Le 9 avril 2026, la mesure phare : à partir du 9 avril 2027, les paiements en espèces en devises pour les biens et services sont interdits, et la BCC devient seule importatrice de billets étrangers.
- Un projet de réglementation des changes d’octobre 2026 qui imposerait le CDF pour les loyers, les frais scolaires, les soins de santé et l’eau et l’électricité des ménages.
Un détail relie Wave à cet agenda. Le 18 novembre, jour où l’agrément a été rendu public, la BCC a précisé aux banques les modalités de la règle d’avril 2027. Particuliers et entreprises peuvent continuer à détenir des dollars, et à payer en dollars par voie électronique, mobile money compris. Seuls les billets verts à la caisse sont interdits. Le gouverneur André Wameso l’avait déjà indiqué en avril.
Lues ensemble, ces règles déplacent le commerce en dollars du billet vers le téléphone. D’où un paradoxe pour le régulateur. Si les émetteurs de monnaie électronique ne rendent pas le franc moins cher à utiliser, l’interdiction de 2027 pourrait simplement numériser le dollar, sur les rails de M-Pesa et d’Airtel Money.
La BCC dit attendre de Wave une diversification de l’offre et plus de concurrence et elle n’a pas lié cet agrément à la dédollarisation. Ce lien reste toutefois plausible et cohérent. Un tarif fixe de 1 % avec retrait gratuit, lancé d’abord en CDF, ferait du franc congolais la monnaie la moins chère à recevoir et à dépenser pour un commerçant. C’est exactement le signal prix que visait la règle des terminaux de 2024. Si Wave tarifie aussi plus cher, ou retarde, ses portefeuilles en dollars, il devient le meilleur allié privé de la politique de dédollarisation.
Toutefois, le risque existe dans les deux sens. Le CDF s’est apprécié d’environ 29 % face au dollar depuis septembre 2025, une hausse que plusieurs analystes congolais jugent artificielle. Si le franc rechute, les ménages retourneront au dollar et une base de portefeuilles majoritairement en CDF perdra de sa valeur. Pour Wave, des revenus en francs face à une facilité de dette de 117 millions d’euros (127 millions de dollars) — menée par Rand Merchant Bank, avec BII, Finnfund et Norfund — créent un risque de change que tous les investisseurs devront suivre.
L’interopérabilité est l’autre levier. En mai 2025, la Première ministre Judith Suminwa a annoncé le lancement par la BCC de MOSOLO, un switch monétaire national inscrit dans la Stratégie nationale d’inclusion financière (SNIF) 2023-2028, et indiqué que tous les intervenants financiers avaient reçu instruction de s’y connecter avant le 22 avril 2025. À terme, un utilisateur de mobile money doit pouvoir envoyer des fonds aux clients de n’importe quel autre opérateur, et toutes les institutions, télécoms et banques comprises, devront y être connectées. En août 2026, la presse financière congolaise jugeait pourtant l’interopérabilité encore bloquée. Pour un nouvel entrant sans base installée, Mosolo compte davantage que n’importe quel tarif : le 1 % de Wave ne touchera tout le marché que si son portefeuille peut payer vers M-Pesa et vers les comptes bancaires dès le lancement.

3. Au-delà de Kinshasa : ce que cela signifie pour la CEEAC
            La Communauté économique des États de l’Afrique centrale (CEEAC) compte dix pays membres depuis le départ du Rwanda en juin 2025, et elle s’étend sur deux zones monétaires. Source de l’image : DW News.
       
        
    
La Communauté Économique des États de l’Afrique Centrale (CEEAC) compte dix États membres depuis le retrait du Rwanda en juin 2025, répartis entre deux mondes monétaires. Les six États de la CEMAC partagent le franc CFA sous l’égide de la BEAC. La RDC, l’Angola, le Burundi et São Tomé-et-Príncipe ont leur propre monnaie.
La CEMAC est déjà une économie du mobile money : plus de 51 millions de comptes et 3,74 milliards de transactions en 2024, le Cameroun représentant 77 % de la valeur des transactions, selon la Banque des États de l’Afrique Centrale (BEAC). Depuis 2018, le Groupement interbancaire monétaire de l’Afrique centrale (GIMAC) gère un switch régional d’interopérabilité, qui a traité 11,21 millions de transactions mobile money pour 419,21 milliards FCFA (698 millions de dollars) en 2024.
Trois conséquences. D’abord, la RDC donne à Wave un modèle d’agrément direct en Afrique centrale, alors qu’en zone CEMAC il dépend encore d’une banque partenaire. Un lancement réussi au Congo renforce sa demande d’un statut équivalent auprès de la BEAC. Ensuite, Kinshasa et Brazzaville se font face de part et d’autre du fleuve Congo, les deux capitales les plus proches au monde, avec deux monnaies et aucun switch commun, puisque le GIMAC ne couvre que la CEMAC. Un portefeuille actif sur les deux rives serait l’étape logique, même si Wave n’a rien annoncé au Congo-Brazzaville. Enfin, Wave s’est construit dans l’Union Économique et Monétaire Ouest-Africaine (UEMOA), où huit pays partagent une monnaie et une banque centrale. En RDC, il doit gérer un marché bimonétaire sous un régulateur qui pousse activement tous les utilisateurs vers l’une des deux. Si le modèle tient là, il s’exporte vers les autres marchés hors zone CFA de la région.
Wave a l’échelle pour essayer : 25 millions d’utilisateurs actifs mensuels, 150 000 agents et une présence dans 11 pays. Le 6 novembre, ses services au Sénégal et en Côte d’Ivoire ont été connectés au système de paiement instantané PI-SPI de la BCEAO. En RDC, ce rôle revient à Mosolo, dont le déploiement dira s’il peut le tenir.
À surveiller dans les six prochains mois
Les six prochains mois donneront une image nette de l’entrée du pingouin bleu sur l’immense marché congolais.
Premier signal : le tarif de lancement de Wave en CDF face à l’USD, et l’existence ou non d’un portefeuille en dollars dès le premier jour. Il dira comment Wave lit le marché, et quelle latitude l’entreprise compte laisser à ses clients tout en composant avec le régulateur.
Deuxième signal : les accords d’accès USSD avec les trois opérateurs télécoms. Le terrain sera-t-il « amical », les télécoms jugeant qu’ils ont intérêt à coopérer avec Wave ? Ou anticiperont-ils une concurrence si rude qu’ils ne laisseront aucune marge de jeu au nouvel entrant ?
Troisième signal : les grilles de retrait des opérateurs historiques sur les petits montants changeront très probablement dans les 90 jours suivant le lancement, et il faudra en comprendre la logique.
Quatrième signal : le texte juridique définitif de la règle d’avril 2027 et ses sanctions, dont rien n’avait été publié au 19 novembre.
Enfin, et ce n’est pas le moindre, la RDC sera un marché à suivre de près pour les progrès de l’interopérabilité entre portefeuilles via le switch Mosolo.
Les prix vont baisser à Kinshasa. Reste à savoir quelle monnaie deviendra la moins chère à utiliser, car c’est ce qui décidera si Wave renforce le franc ou devient le nouveau transporteur du dollar.
La newsletter se termine ici.

articles.title: Pinterest will now let parents limit the AI-generated content their teens see
articles.text:
Pinterest announced this week that it’s expanding its parental controls, but one new feature stands out: Parents can now control how much AI-generated content their children are exposed to. This additional setting arrives alongside more standard options, like tools to adjust notifications or whether or not videos auto-play.
The change makes Pinterest one of the first major social platforms to allow parents to control how much AI-generated content is shown to their children as part of the overall user experience.
Aside from Pinterest, social media platforms have focused more on limiting minors’ access to specific AI-powered features, as when Snap added a parental control setting that prevented its AI chatbot from responding to teens or when Meta announced a global pause on teens’ access to existing AI characters after retooling the product based on parents’ feedback.
WhatsApp currently allows parents to adjust the level of access teens have to Meta AI, in terms of using AI to create content or having the AI respond to their teen’s questions.
But when it comes to AI-generated content filling users’ feeds and recommendations, there are few controls available on social media platforms in general, much less those provided as part of the parental controls.
This problem, parents say, is harming children’s well-being in favor of profits. For instance, in April, the children’s advocacy group Fairplay sent a letter to YouTube CEO Neal Mohan and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, signed by over 200 organizations and experts, calling on YouTube to remove AI-generated content from YouTube Kids and bar AI-generated videos from being recommended to users under 18.
Pinterest has fought its own battle against AI content, which still finds its way into users’ feeds even when the settings that restrict AI-modified content, which the company introduced in 2025, are enabled.
Putting a similar set of tools into parents’ hands is at least a good first step in allowing the users themselves to dictate the type of experience they want to have on the app.
The new feature arrived alongside other parental controls, including one to stop auto-playing videos and another that lets parents adjust the volume of push, browser, in-app, and email notifications. The Parental Controls Page was also redesigned to make it easier to find and configure certain controls and to allow parents to configure settings related to personalized ads.

articles.title: Cómo votar en los Premios Steam 2026 y elegir el mejor juego de la década
articles.text:
Los Premios Steam 2026 ya permiten que la comunidad nomine títulos en 14 categorías, incluida una nueva votación para elegir el mejor juego de la década. La iniciativa de Valve abre el proceso que definirá los finalistas y, más adelante, los ganadores de una ceremonia basada por completo en las decisiones de los usuarios de PC.
La convocatoria adquiere relevancia por el décimo aniversario de los galardones y por la incorporación del premio Salón de la Fama. Esta categoría reúne a los títulos que ganaron el reconocimiento principal en ediciones anteriores y los enfrenta en una votación que busca identificar al juego más destacado de los últimos diez años dentro de la plataforma.
Cómo participar para elegir el mejor videojuego
Para participar, es necesario acceder a la página de nominaciones de los Premios Steam desde una cuenta de la plataforma que no tenga restricciones. Valve permite seleccionar un juego por categoría, aunque un mismo título puede recibir nominaciones en más de un apartado si encaja con los criterios de cada premio.
La primera etapa termina el 30 de noviembre a las 19:00 en España peninsular, equivalente a las 10:00 en la costa oeste de Estados Unidos. Hasta ese momento, los usuarios pueden modificar sus decisiones cuantas veces consideren necesario desde la misma sección de la tienda digital.
El sistema muestra recomendaciones a partir de los juegos que cada persona tiene en su biblioteca y de los títulos más populares de Steam. También incluye un buscador para encontrar cualquier juego elegible. Esa opción permite nominar producciones jugadas fuera de la plataforma, siempre que cumplan los requisitos de publicación establecidos para cada categoría.
En la mayoría de los premios, los candidatos deben haberse lanzado entre el cierre de las rebajas de otoño de 2025 y el inicio de las nominaciones de 2026. Hay dos excepciones: Con amor y dedicación reconoce juegos antiguos que siguen recibiendo contenido, mientras que Salón de la Fama tiene una lista cerrada.
Salón de la Fama enfrenta a los ganadores de otras ediciones
La categoría más singular de esta edición es Salón de la Fama, creada para celebrar los diez años de los premios. Allí competirán los ganadores históricos del reconocimiento principal o, en los primeros años, los títulos equivalentes elegidos por la comunidad antes de que existiera la categoría Juego del Año.
La lista incluye a Grand Theft Auto V, The Witcher III: Wild Hunt, PUBG: Battlegrounds, Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, Red Dead Redemption 2, Resident Evil Village, Elden Ring, Baldur’s Gate 3, Black Myth: Wukong y Hollow Knight: Silksong.
Cada uno representa una etapa distinta de la plataforma, desde los grandes mundos abiertos y los juegos multijugador hasta las aventuras de acción, los títulos de rol y las producciones independientes. A diferencia del resto de apartados, los usuarios no pueden añadir otros nombres a esta selección.
El resultado permitirá conocer cuál de esos juegos recibe el respaldo de los jugadores de Steam como el mejor título de la década. La votación también convierte a los premios en una revisión de la evolución del catálogo de PC y de las preferencias de una comunidad que participa directamente en la elección.
Catorce categorías cubren desde realidad virtual hasta juegos relajantes
La edición 2026 incorpora tres premios inspirados en categorías populares de años anteriores. Son Solo cinco minutos más, para juegos que invitan a prolongar una partida; Difícil de describir, para propuestas que escapan de un género definido; y Mi nuevo trabajo, centrada en simuladores de actividades cotidianas.
El resto de la lista mantiene apartados habituales. Los usuarios podrán nominar candidatos a Juego del Año, Juego de Realidad Virtual del Año, Con amor y dedicación, Mejor juego para dispositivos portátiles, Mejor con amigos, Estilo visual excepcional, Mejor juego difícil, Mejor banda sonora, Juego excepcional con buena trama y Siéntate y relájate.
La categoría dedicada a dispositivos portátiles tendrá especial atención entre quienes juegan desde Steam Deck y otros equipos compatibles. Por su parte, Mejor juego difícil reconoce propuestas que exigen perseverancia, mientras que Siéntate y relájate distingue experiencias de ritmo pausado.
Cuando cierre el plazo de nominaciones, Valve realizará el recuento y seleccionará los cinco juegos con más apoyo en cada categoría. Los finalistas se publicarán el 17 de diciembre, fecha que coincide con el inicio de las rebajas de invierno de Steam.
La fase definitiva permanecerá abierta hasta el 2 de enero de 2027 a las 19:00 en España peninsular. Al finalizar ese periodo, Valve anunciará los ganadores de los 14 premios, incluido el primer título que ingresará en el Salón de la Fama.

articles.title: Ingrid (58) compra una autocaravana por 12.500 euros, que inmediatamente necesita una reparación de 3.000 euros
articles.text:
Ingrid (58 años) y su marido llevaban tiempo con ganas de comprarse una caravana. Cuando encontraron una de segunda mano por 12.500 euros decidieron dar el paso, pero antes de pagar quisieron asegurarse de que todo estaba en orden. Y sí, sobre el papel lo estaba, ya que el vendedor les dijo que no había filtraciones de agua, pero su primera escapa terminó costándoles… 3.000 euros.
La pareja se marchó a Zelanda (una provincia de Países Bajos) para estrenarla y durante el viaje se toparon con una tormenta que empezó a filtrar el agua por las paredes. Los cojines de la zona de estar acabaron empapados, el interior sufrió daños por la humedad y la situación llevó a Ingrid a contar la historia a Metronieuws, un portal en el que habló de cómo una caravana que parecía perfecta se convirtió en un problema serio.
Una reparación de 3.000 euros que no esperaban
Tras descubrir las filtraciones, el matrimonio tuvo que afrontar una reparación de 3.000 euros, que se sumaron a los 12.500 que ya habían pagado. En total, la caravana les salió por 15.500 euros. Y todo después de que el anterior propietario les hubiera asegurado que no tenía problemas de humedad.
Lo complicado de estos desperfectos es que no siempre se ven durante una visita. Por eso, el ADAC, el club automovilístico alemán, recomienda comprobar si una caravana de segunda mano ha sufrido filtraciones y realizar una medición de humedad antes de comprarla. El agua puede terminar dañando la madera, las instalaciones eléctricas o incluso provocar la aparición de moho.
Y hay otro detalle que conviene tener en cuenta: no es lo mismo comprar a un particular que a un concesionario. En Alemania, los vendedores particulares pueden excluir ciertas responsabilidades por defectos, aunque no cuando han ocultado deliberadamente un problema conocido o han garantizado expresamente que no existía. Por eso merece la pena dejar por escrito cualquier garantía sobre el estado de la caravana, especialmente si se refiere a posibles daños por agua.

articles.title: AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
articles.text:
AI discovers a hidden heart signal that could predict sudden death
- Date:
  November 14, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Berkeley
- Summary:
  Scientists have uncovered a hidden warning sign in routine heart scans that could predict sudden cardiac death before it strikes. The AI-powered discovery outperformed conventional screening methods, potentially revealing thousands of people at risk of a fatal heart malfunction that doctors might otherwise miss.
- Share:
More than 300,000 people in the United States die from sudden cardiac arrest each year. This deadly emergency occurs when the heart's electrical system suddenly fails, causing the heart to stop pumping blood. It can strike older adults with known heart conditions as well as seemingly healthy young athletes. Although implanted defibrillators can prevent some of these deaths, doctors have long struggled to determine which patients need them most.
Now, researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a previously overlooked warning signal in routine heart scans that could make it easier to recognize people at risk before a fatal event occurs.
The discovery was made using artificial intelligence trained on more than 440,000 electrocardiograms, or EKGs, collected in Sweden. By comparing the electrical patterns recorded in these scans with information from death certificates, the researchers taught an AI system to recognize subtle differences between healthy individuals, patients with known heart risks, and people who eventually died from sudden cardiac causes.
The team then evaluated the technology using thousands of additional patient records from the United States and Taiwan, testing whether the patterns could reliably identify people at heightened risk in different populations.
AI Detects Hidden Heart Risks That Standard Tests Miss
The results suggest that AI can identify vulnerable patients more effectively than the conventional tests doctors typically rely on. Current screening methods largely focus on how much blood the heart pumps with each contraction, a measurement used to assess whether someone might benefit from an implanted defibrillator.
Using these traditional measurements, doctors can identify a group of patients with an annual sudden cardiac death rate of 4.6%. The AI system, however, identified a group with an annual death rate of 7%, demonstrating a greater ability to distinguish patients facing serious danger.
Importantly, the algorithm also recognized a broader population of people at elevated risk, including thousands who would not normally raise concerns under existing medical guidelines. Most of these individuals would have been classified as relatively low risk using conventional methods.
Another major advantage is that the AI system works with ordinary EKG images, which are already routinely collected in hospitals and medical centers around the world. This means the technology could potentially improve screening without requiring an entirely new type of medical test.
The findings, published in Nature, could eventually help physicians make more informed decisions about who should receive an implanted defibrillator. They also raise an intriguing scientific question about what changes inside the heart produce the electrical patterns that AI has learned to recognize.
"Medical decisions are really hard, and I think that's why AI is so exciting for me," said Ziad Obermeyer, an associate professor at UC Berkeley's School of Public Health and the study's lead author. "We can not only make better decisions, but also start to understand what's actually going on with these patients before their heart stops."
Why Sudden Cardiac Death Is So Difficult to Predict
Sudden cardiac arrest is different from a heart attack. A heart attack happens when blood flow to part of the heart becomes blocked or severely restricted. Cardiac arrest, by contrast, results from a failure of the electrical signals that coordinate the heartbeat.
Immediate CPR and an electrical shock from an automated external defibrillator can sometimes restore the heart's rhythm. However, roughly 90% of people who experience sudden cardiac arrest outside a hospital die within minutes, making early recognition of those at risk especially important.
For Obermeyer, an emergency physician whose research combines artificial intelligence, medicine, and health policy, sudden cardiac death remains one of medicine's most frustrating unsolved problems.
Because victims often die without warning, researchers have limited opportunities to observe what happens inside the heart immediately before it stops. An autopsy may uncover blocked blood vessels, hardened tissue, or other structural abnormalities, but it cannot fully reveal how the heart was functioning in the moments leading up to death.
"One thing that makes the problem very tragic, but also very well suited for AI, is that we have the cure for this problem," Obermeyer said. "If you knew you were one of the people who was going to drop dead, you would go to a cardiologist and you'd get a defibrillator implanted. The problem is that doctors can't figure out who needs one before it's too late."
The Problem With Current Heart Risk Screening
Doctors currently rely heavily on a measurement of how effectively the heart pushes blood out with each beat. Patients whose hearts pump below a specified threshold may be considered candidates for an implantable cardioverter defibrillator, a device that can deliver an electrical shock when a dangerous heart rhythm develops.
But obtaining this measurement generally requires a more extensive medical evaluation. Many people who eventually experience sudden cardiac arrest never receive such testing because they have no obvious reason to suspect they are in danger.
The approach also has limitations for patients who are identified as high risk. About two-thirds of implanted defibrillators in these patients never need to deliver a shock. As a result, many individuals undergo expensive, invasive procedures for potentially fatal emergencies that may never occur.
At the same time, thousands of people who are not recognized as being at risk die unexpectedly each year.
"In some fraction of those people, we could have prevented those deaths if we had just known it in time," Obermeyer said. "There are a lot of lives being lost from people who are dropping dead of sudden cardiac death that are preventable if we just had better AI tools to find these things."
The researchers hope that identifying more accurate warning signs could help doctors direct preventive treatments toward the patients most likely to benefit.
How Researchers Trained AI to Recognize Deadly Heart Patterns
Developing the algorithm required three independent collections of medical data gathered from different parts of the world.
The researchers began with six years of EKG recordings from Sweden's unified healthcare system. By linking these scans to death certificates, they could examine the electrical patterns of patients who later experienced sudden cardiac death and compare them with those of other patients.
The AI learned to identify combinations of spikes, waves, and other characteristics in the recordings that appeared to be associated with increased risk. Once the system had been trained, the team tested it against two additional datasets: two years of anonymized EKG records from a San Diego hospital system and a separate collection of patient data from Taipei.
This international testing helped researchers evaluate whether the algorithm's predictive abilities extended beyond the Swedish population used to develop it.
"Good AI starts with good data," said Obermeyer, who is also part of the joint UCSF-UC Berkeley Computational Precision Health program. "Unfortunately, data like the ones we used for this study are incredibly hard to access. It's a big part of why there's so little clinical AI in use today."
Obtaining and organizing the information was itself a massive undertaking. According to Obermeyer, assembling the datasets took approximately 10 years and involved contributions from two organizations he helped establish, Dandelion Health and Nightingale Open Science. Both organizations work to advance medical research through better access to data and artificial intelligence.
"It's one of the tremendous luxuries of being at Berkeley," Obermeyer said. "You can pursue these projects that just are a slow burn and then have -- hopefully -- a big return when they get over the finish line."
From Hidden Heart Signals to Lifesaving Treatments
The researchers have already begun exploring how the system might be used in actual healthcare settings.
Obermeyer is collaborating with medical systems in Sweden, Taiwan, and the United States to introduce the algorithm into hospital EKG databases. The goal is to examine existing heart scans for signs of elevated risk and identify patients who may benefit from additional monitoring.
Under the proposed approach, physicians would contact patients whose EKGs receive a high-risk assessment and offer them the opportunity to wear a patch that continuously records their heart's electrical activity.
These longer recordings could provide valuable clues about the biological processes responsible for the warning signals detected by the AI. Understanding those processes could help researchers explain why certain hearts are more vulnerable to suddenly developing fatal electrical disturbances.
For some patients, the additional information might ultimately support a recommendation to receive an implanted defibrillator, potentially preventing a sudden and otherwise unexpected death.
Obermeyer has also created a website where people interested in learning about their own risk can provide basic personal information and an email address. The research team can then contact them about EKG analysis when the technology becomes more widely available.
Could AI Reveal New Secrets About the Human Heart?
Beyond its potential to improve the prevention of sudden cardiac death, the discovery highlights how artificial intelligence could help scientists investigate medical mysteries that have resisted conventional approaches.
Rather than simply identifying patients who might need treatment, the algorithm has uncovered patterns in heart activity that researchers do not yet fully understand. Studying those signals could lead to new insights into the electrical disturbances responsible for sudden cardiac death and potentially reveal additional opportunities for prevention.
Obermeyer believes this ability to uncover previously unrecognized biological patterns could become one of AI's most important contributions to medicine, opening new directions for research while helping physicians make better decisions.
"There is also going to be a new way of doing science that comes out of these tools," Obermeyer said, "and it's fun to think about how that starts happening."

articles.title: VMware Updates Patch Critical ESX, vCenter Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Broadcom on Tuesday announced the release of patches for 23 vulnerabilities across multiple VMware products, including critical-severity flaws in ESX and vCenter.
The vCenter patches resolve seven bugs, including a critical authentication bypass issue in the VMware Directory Service tracked as CVE-2026-123903 (CVSS score of 9.8).
Additionally, the fixes target three denial-of-service (DoS) issues in the VMware Directory Service, a local privilege escalation in a vpxd service script, an arbitrary file write while processing certain archives, and a security policy enforcement failure in the vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS).
The ESX updates resolve seven security issues as well, including three critical-severity weaknesses leading to code execution on the host.
CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911 (CVSS score of 9.8) are heap out-of-bounds write and use-after-free flaws in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123912 (CVSS score of 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the XHCI USB controller that requires local administrative privileges on a virtual machine.
An attacker “may exploit this issue to execute code as the virtual machine’s VMX process running on the host. On ESX, the exploitation is contained within the VMX sandbox whereas, on Workstation and Fusion, this may lead to code execution on the machine where Workstation or Fusion is installed,” Broadcom explains.
The remaining four include a stack-based buffer overflow in the VMkernel, a DoS vulnerability in guest RPC, a security bypass in the host configuration store, and a signature verification bypass.
Broadcom also patched eight flaws in Avi Load Balancer that could lead to code execution with root privileges, privilege escalation to root, command execution, password hash leaks, access to the routing management interface and other resources, and unintended file access, and one in VMware Tools leading to DoS.
According to Broadcom, some of the issues were resolved with the vCenter updates released last week. vCenter version 8.0 U3m contained the fixes, and customers who applied it do not need to update again. vCenter 9.1.x deployments, however, as well as ESX, VMware Tools, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer instances, need to be updated.
“Patches are cumulative, so the updates listed in this advisory also contain the fixes from VMSA-2026-0009 when they are newer than the fixed versions listed in VMSA-2026-0009. However, this advisory does not mention the SDDC Manager updates from VMSA-2026-0009; please ensure you are handling those,” the company notes.
Broadcom makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but it’s not uncommon for the company to not warn about exploitation in its public advisories.
On Tuesday, Broadcom also updated its advisory on Node2Shell to add VMware Cloud Foundation version 9.1.2 to the list of fixed releases.

articles.title: Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox "puro" para iPhone
articles.text:
Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox “puro” para iPhone
Mozilla afirma que regras impostas pela Apple são complexas e inviabilizam o Firefox de ter seu próprio motor no iOS.
A Mozilla lançou a primeira versão do Firefox para iPhone em 2015. Mas, até hoje, o navegador não conta com uma implementação totalmente “pura” no iOS, com motor próprio. Em tom de desabafo, a organização explicou o motivo. Saiba desde já que, sim, a Mozilla culpa a Apple por isso.
Quando falamos de motor, nos referimos ao componente central do navegador, que interpreta o código de páginas web escrito em padrões como HTML, CSS e JavaScript, e transforma esse conjunto de informações em um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Hoje, a maior parte dos navegadores é baseada no projeto Chromium, a exemplo do Microsoft Edge, do Opera, do Brave e, claro, do Google Chrome. No Chromium, o motor utilizado é o Blink.
O Firefox é diferente, pois conta com um motor próprio: o Gecko. Mas, no iOS, o navegador é executado a partir do WebKit, motor mantido pela Apple que, como tal, é a base do Safari.
É aqui que está o ponto de conflito: se dependesse da Mozilla, o Firefox também contaria com o Gecko no iPhone.
A Apple exigia que os navegadores para iOS usassem o WebKit sob o argumento de que essa condição favorecia aspectos como segurança, privacidade e desempenho. Isso mudou em 2024, quando a Digital Markets Act (DMA) passou a vigorar. Trata-se de uma legislação da União Europeia que busca aumentar a concorrência no âmbito digital.
Entre várias outras medidas, a DMA determina que os usuários tenham a opção de escolher o navegador padrão de seus dispositivos. Isso também deu abertura para que outros motores de navegação pudessem ser usados no iOS.
Então, problema resolvido, certo? De acordo com a Mozilla, não. A organização explica que as condições determinadas pela Apple para que um navegador para iPhone conte com um motor diferente do WebKit são tão complexas que, até hoje, nenhum desenvolvedor conseguiu encontrar um caminho viável para isso.
Em um comunicado recente, a Mozilla conta o principal problema relacionado às condições da Apple:
Para usar o Gecko [no iOS], não podemos simplesmente atualizar o Firefox que as pessoas já usam e adoram. Teríamos que criar um aplicativo completamente separado, um segundo Firefox.
Depois, teríamos que pedir a todos os usuários do Firefox que baixassem a nova versão, transferissem seus favoritos, senhas e histórico e fizessem a transição manualmente, passo a passo, de modo confuso.
Onde, exatamente, está o problema? O Firefox é um software de distribuição global. Para se adequar à DMA, a Apple passou a permitir o uso de mecanismos alternativos ao seu, mas com a condição de que eles sejam distribuídos exclusivamente na região autorizada, e não em escala global.
A Mozilla teria então que ter um Firefox para iOS válido globalmente (a versão atual, com WebKit) e outro, com o Gecko, específico para a União Europeia. Pelo menos até o momento, é inviável para a Mozilla trabalhar com essa dualidade.
Na prática, isso significa que os usuários teriam que baixar um novo app e transferir manualmente seus dados para ele. A organização também considera esse aspecto inviável.
Por conta disso, a solução vislumbrada pela Mozilla é a de pressionar a Apple: “continuaremos lutando por condições realmente justas, não por uma brecha que prejudique os navegadores independentes”.
