articles.title: AI’s hunger for compute could break uranium’s boom-bust cycle
articles.text:
Saskatchewan is home to some of the world’s largest, richest uranium deposits. Developing those deposits has turned Canada into the world’s second-largest producer of the radioactive metal. The industry has been beset by gruelling boom-and-bust cycles, but those cycles may soon end as demand for nuclear power—and the uranium to fuel it—continues to ramp up.
“AI needs reliable, carbon-free power, and nuclear [power] needs uranium. It’s a hand-in-hand solution.”
Eduardo Buriticà
Located near the Northwest Territories, Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin contains so much uranium that just a small stretch of its more than 100,000-square-kilometre territory has the potential to power more than 40 million homes for around 25 years. Following a particularly lucrative market boom in 2024, the World Nuclear Association predicted that Canada would overtake Kazakhstan as the world’s leading uranium supplier.
That hasn’t happened yet. Commodities market prices have actually fallen somewhat since 2024, but Canada’s uranium sector is still very much experiencing a boom. Between 2019 and 2024, the price of uranium climbed 233 percent, according to reporting by Bloomberg. Gold, another valuable commodity, grew in comparison by just 75 percent.
“The World Nuclear Association projects that reactor requirements will grow 28 percent by 2030 and will more than double by 2040,” said Eduardo Buriticà, the director of external affairs for Canadian Uranium Corporation. Canadian Uranium owns a nearly 16,000-hectare uranium mining project known as Rook II in the Athabasca Basin.
Growth in the industry has experienced peaks and valleys over the past half-decade, but overall trendlines show an increase. That growth is driven, at least in part, by a global renaissance in nuclear development. According to nuclear data platform Yellowcake Analytics, there are more than 400 nuclear reactors operating worldwide; another 80 or so are under construction, and hundreds more are in the planning and development stages.
That resurgence has been spurred on by renewed interest in nuclear’s potential for clean energy after years of declining investment following Japan’s Fukushima disaster. It accelerated again after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Increasingly, though, industry insiders see another source of demand emerging: AI.
“Demand is rising due to countries building and restarting nuclear reactors, but the data electricity demand from data centres and AI is only adding to it,” Buriticà said. “Demand for energy is not going to go down anytime soon, especially with the focus on data centres. We’re only seeing that trend go up.”
“AI needs reliable, carbon-free power, and nuclear [power] needs uranium. It’s a hand-in-hand solution,” he added.
Reza Mohammed is Canadian Uranium’s site exploration manager. Mohammed coordinates teams of geologists and contractors, handles site permitting, and helps come up with potential geographic targets for uranium exploration. A geologist with more than 30 years of experience in the Canadian uranium industry, Mohammed sees much the same opportunity as Buriticà does in AI’s scale of demand. Nuclear power, he argues, has distinct advantages for servicing that particular kind of need.
“[AI and data centres] need power, and they need modular power,” Mohammed said. “[Nuclear] is a scalable power source; you can have mobile reactors or massive reactors.”
“Demand for energy is not going to go down anytime soon, especially with the focus on data centres. We’re only seeing that trend go up.”
Eduardo Buriticà
Mohammed’s not speculating. Small, modular nuclear reactors, also called SMRs, have caught the attention of tech giants like Amazon, Meta, and Google, all of which have invested in the technology. SMRs are compact nuclear reactors that can be assembled where needed, allowing them to operate in remote or isolated areas, or in conjunction with other forms of power. They’re also grid-independent, meaning they can prevent transmission loss and reduce dependency on traditional or shared electric grids.
That influx of interest from governments and private businesses has not gone unnoticed by Saskatchewan or Canada. Both governments have moved to prioritize nuclear and uranium development, with the feds aiming to double production by 2035 and Regina looking to further cement nuclear energy as a key economic driver for the province.
Demand is slated to grow: the World Nuclear Association forecasts that by 2040, the world could face a shortfall in uranium supplies by as much as 40,000 tonnes, with that forecast coming prior to any accounting for the additional demands of AI. That presents an opportunity for Saskatchewan and Canada to fill a gap. With the basin’s vast resources, supply is no issue. But whether an industry accustomed to such volatile cycles can handle this kind of sustained demand is an open question.
Feature image courtesy IAEA. Photo by Conleth Brady. Shared under CC BY-SA 2.0.

articles.title: El hacker que filtró ‘GTA 6’ queda en libertad tras declararse culpable
articles.text:
La historia del hacker que filtró GTA 6 siendo un adolescente ha dado un giro bastante curioso. Apenas días después de declararse culpable, el pirata informático recuperó su libertad con una advertencia por parte del juez británico a cargo del caso, quien le pidió que no repitiera sus actividades delictivas.
"Que no vuelva a suceder", le manifestó el magistrado a Arion Kurtaj, según publica BBC. El joven de 21 años se declaró culpable de varios delitos vinculados con el hackeo a varias tecnológicas como parte del grupo Lapsus$ en 2022. Entre las firmas impactadas estuvo Rockstar Games, que padeció la divulgación de una gran cantidad de vídeos de GTA 6 cuando su desarrollo todavía estaba lejos de finalizado.
Uno de los puntos más curiosos de aquel incidente fue que Kurtaj hackeó Rockstar desde la habitación de un hotel, usando un Fire TV Stick. El por entonces adolescente intentó extorsionar al estudio para evitar la filtración de los materiales de GTA 6, pero estos acabaron divulgándose en Twitter y servidores de Discord.
Cuando la policía finalmente dio con el paradero de Arion Kurtaj, la justicia decidió mantenerlo internado por tiempo indefinido en una institución psiquiátrica debido a la severidad de su autismo. Asimismo, se determinó que esta era la mejor opción de supervivencia del hacker de GTA 6, debido a que piratas informáticos rivales lo doxxearon y amenazaron su integridad física en múltiples oportunidades.
Arion Kurtaj, el hacker que filtró GTA 6, sale en libertad
A comienzos de este año, la justicia británica determinó que el joven estaba en condiciones de afrontar el juicio por su accionar. La semana pasada, Kurtaj finalmente se declaró culpable de sus delitos en línea, incluyendo la filtración de GTA 6. El pirata informático afrontaba penas de hasta 14 años de cárcel por los intentos de extorsión a las empresas impactadas por su accionar. El tribunal finalmente se inclinó por un castigo de 7 años de cárcel, aunque no serán de prisión efectiva.
El juez a cargo del caso finalmente le otorgó la libertad condicional, de modo que no pasará más tiempo retenido. Eso sí, Kurtaj ha recibido una orden de prevención de delitos graves que tendrá una duración de cinco años. Mientras la misma se encuentre en vigencia, el hacker de GTA 6 verá restringidas sus actividades en línea. Así, por ejemplo, tendrá prohibido el uso de plataformas de comunicación como Discord y Telegram.
La filtración de GTA 6 en 2022 fue un golpe duro para Rockstar Games, tanto económico como emocional. La filtración le costó unos 5 millones de dólares al estudio y requirió de miles de horas de trabajo adicionales para mitigar su impacto. El éxito que tuvo el juego tras su lanzamiento, que embolsó casi 3.800 millones de dólares al cierre del primer día, no borró el mal momento que pasó la empresa.
Aaron Garbut, uno de los líderes de GTA 6, habló recientemente de lo duradero que fue el golpe anímico del hackeo. "Es como si alguien estuviera hurgando en tu ropa sucia. Es como si se metieran dentro de tu cabeza. Ves tus primeros trabajos expuestos ahí fuera y se supone que nadie debería ver eso nunca. Resulta extrañamente invasivo. Por eso es bastante difícil de gestionar a nivel emocional", reconoció.

articles.title: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
articles.text:
The US Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate the nation’s stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday. The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated.
Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.
What material is the Army planning to detonate?
There are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades. The US started using lead azide as a primary explosive almost a century ago before “moving away” from it about 15 years ago because of how difficult the material is to store and transport, Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), said in a Tuesday press briefing. At that point, the US transferred its remaining stockpile of lead azide to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. Lead azide will explode at 350 degrees Celsius (662F). But it is also sensitive to flame, friction, or sudden shock, including fluctuations in temperature.
Some of the material on site in Iowa is more than 60 years old. The material can crystallize as it degrades over time, becoming unstable enough to explode even at ambient temperatures. The Army noted some deterioration of the material in 2009 — but not any “dangerous crystallization” at the time, according to Cekada.
“It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”
The chemical was stored in liquid form, embedded in sawdust and burlap bags inside the drums. Water and ethanol were also added to the containers to keep the lead azide from freezing in the winter. But during a March inspection, Cekada said ATF noticed “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels.” That made the material too unstable for them to open the barrels to add more water and ethanol, Cekada said. Removing a lid might cause the barrels to detonate.
Why is the Army detonating it now?
Officials have been trying to figure out what to do with the crystallized lead azide since that alarming March inspection. The Army initially hired a contractor to safely dissolve the chemicals but canceled the contract earlier this year, according to reporting by The New York Times. Using a chemical neutralization agent “proved to be an unsafe method,” Army Col. Aaron Teller, commander of the 71st Explosive Ordinance Disposal Group, said at the Tuesday briefing, because crystallization on the outside of the barrels made it too risky to open the lids.
“Everyone that we’ve spoken to through their experience has determined that this is the only safe path forward,“ Cekada said at the briefing. If they leave the chemicals as is, he said, they’re still at risk of exploding. “It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”
What are the risks?
Compared to an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion, a controlled detonation is supposed to limit the amount of lead dust unleashed on surrounding communities and the environment. Still, the dust plume could reach as far as 100 miles away from the site. The Army has released maps showing where lead dust is expected to travel based on its modeling.
The last time the Army disposed of lead azide this way at a comparable scale was in 1977, according to Teller. At the time, they detonated 7,000 pounds of the material in Colorado in open air “with zero mitigation.” Even then, 75 percent of the lead particulate stayed on site, Teller said at the briefing. The Army now believes it can “significantly reduce” the spread of that last 25 percent of lead using walls made up of four 16,000-gallon water tanks to capture lead particulate and hopefully prevent it from escaping into the atmosphere.
The 80-year-old earth-covered magazines holding the lead azide are cracked and deteriorating, Teller noted, and they are likely to break open after the detonation. To prepare, they’ve covered it with tarp and a special containment screen for lead. They also plan to flood it with 2 feet of foam to capture particulate pollution. Adam Telle, Acting Secretary of the Army, also said the Army has set out “state of the art gel blocks in huge quantities all around to ensure that we absorb as much of this blast as we possibly can.”
There is no “safe” level of exposure to lead
Last week, the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club sought a court order to stop the explosion from taking place, pending an Environmental and Health Impact Statement and an investigation into alternatives to detonating the material. President Donald Trump chimed in on social media, calling for a pause until a federal appeals court gave the Army the green light after previously granting a temporary stay. The court on Monday denied the emergency motion to stop the explosion, clearing the way for the Army to move forward.
What precautions can people nearby take?
The Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (Iowa HHS) recommends that anyone in potentially affected areas stay indoors and keep windows shut for 24 to 48 hours after the detonation. Iowa HHS also suggests switching off HVAC systems that might bring outdoor air inside or set them to modes that recirculate air, and using an air purifier with a HEPA filter.
FEMA is helping relocate Middletown residents and others within a voluntary 5-mile evacuation zone. People who are pregnant, children, and individuals with chronic diseases should evacuate the affected areas, Sean Kaufman, principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response at the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, said at the briefing. “Outside of that area, if you’re close to that proximity and you’re uncomfortable, I think you need to do what you need to do to take care of your family,” Kaufman said.
There is no “safe” level of exposure to lead, a neurotoxin that poses health risks when inhaled or ingested. Kids are at increased risk because their brains are still developing and are also more likely to touch contaminated surfaces and then stick their fingers in their mouths. But most adverse health effects — which can include fatigue and gastrointestinal upset alongside impacts on brain development — are connected to chronic lead exposure rather than as a result of a one-off event.
“It is likely this exposure will not result in any observable acute clinical signs,” Will Sander, associate professor of preventive medicine and public health at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, says in an email to The Verge. “Overall, the risk is minimal, and there should be no long-term concerns.”
What happens after the explosion?
“The Army has done this before a long time ago and took lead measurements afterward that were low but hazardous (in my opinion),” Chris Kohler, an adjunct instructor at Indiana University who is an expert on hazardous waste, environmental remediation, and chemical hygiene, says in an email to The Verge. “The detonation will spread lead in the atmosphere. Not a desirable outcome.” Kohler and other experts say it’ll be important to continue monitoring the explosion site and surrounding areas to see if there needs to be any more remediation.

articles.title: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in New York from 2027
articles.text:
Car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year.
“People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said.
In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee.
We end users might not like having to open our wallets each month, but the capital markets sure do, and car companies love making the capital markets happy. Which is why there has been such a push toward connected vehicles. Remote start and predictive maintenance alerts are nice, but your regular payments to the car company—plus any data of yours it can sell—is the goal.
Some automakers have gone even further. Infamously, BMW and its heated seats. Like the McDonald’s coffee lawsuit, it’s a fact half-remembered; BMW North America never tried such a thing, just in countries like South Korea and the UK, and in 2023 BMW’s board said that subscriptions would only be for software-related features from then on.
My 2022 Mustang Mach-e "came with" Ford's Blue Cruise, which is excellent.
NOWHERE on the Monroney sticker or in my contract does it say anything about Blue Cruise being for a limited time, then being subscription afterward.
It didn't say "3 years of Blue Cruise" or anything similar.
I do understand how updating the maps creates an on-going cost, but the system already only works on divided highways and uses built-in hardware, and doesn't really need updated maps to maintain hands-off lane-keeping.
Ford gave all the 2022 owners an extra year for "free", but I still find it pretty frustrating.

articles.title: Plus besoin de retourner votre carte bancaire : Google Wallet va bientôt remplir votre CVV à votre place
articles.text:
Google Wallet va bientôt remplir tout seul le code de sécurité de votre carte bancaire.
Wallet, le portefeuille numérique de Google, s’enrichit régulièrement de nouvelles fonctionnalités : suivi des dépenses avec l’assistant IA Gemini, paiement sans contact plus sûr, déverrouillage des serrures connectées et bien plus encore. Une autre nouveauté devrait aussi vous permettre de régler vos achats en ligne bien plus rapidement. On vous explique.
Google Wallet va pouvoir remplir seul votre cryptogramme
Jusqu’à récemment, quand on voulait payer un achat sur le web, il fallait aller chercher sa carte bancaire, la retourner et fournir les 3 ou 4 chiffres figurant à l’arrière. Ceux qui ont une bonne mémoire pouvaient aussi retenir le cryptogramme. Mais tout cela devrait bientôt changer : une nouvelle fonctionnalité est listée dans les notes de version v.2646 des services Google Play, qui ont été publiées hier.
Google Wallet se prépare en effet à inscrire votre CVV ou CVC à votre place lors de vos prochains paiements. À une seule condition : il faudra déverrouiller votre smartphone et vous identifier avec un code, un schéma ou une empreinte digitale. On ne va certainement pas se plaindre de cette couche de sécurité supplémentaire.
Une fonctionnalité qui soulève quelques inquiétudes
Sur le papier, Google semble avoir trouvé le bon équilibre entre confort d’utilisation et sécurité. Cependant, il ne faut pas oublier la raison même pour laquelle le cryptogramme a été créé : le code sert, en effet, à prouver que vous tenez bien votre carte bancaire dans votre main. Si les chiffres sont désormais enregistrés dans votre téléphone, il faudra redoubler de prudence pour éviter les intrusions malveillantes, en privilégiant l’empreinte digitale, quand cela est possible.
Côté informations, Google reste, comme d'habitude, assez taiseux. Impossible, par exemple, de savoir si la nouvelle fonctionnalité sera compatible avec tous les sites, toutes les applications ou encore tous les écrans de paiement. On ne sait pas non plus quelle version de Google Wallet il faudra posséder pour pouvoir y avoir accès.
Quand cette nouveauté sera-t-elle disponible ? Là aussi, motus et bouche cousue. Son arrivée dans les notes de version des services Google Play ne veut pas forcément dire qu’elle sera rapidement disponible sur nos smartphones. Il faudra donc, comme toujours, faire preuve de patience et attendre sagement de voir cette option arriver en France et ailleurs

articles.title: Apple préparerait le retour des éditions (PRODUCT)RED avec la HomePod mini 2 et les AirPods Max 2
articles.text:
Mark Gurman, journaliste à Bloomberg, a révélé l’information ce lundi 23 novembre. D’après lui, Apple prépare des versions rouges de la HomePod mini 2 et des AirPods Max 2. Ces deux éditions seraient lancées le mardi 1er décembre ou autour de cette date. Apple n’a pour l’instant rien confirmé.
    Pour aller plus loin
Amazon Echo, Google Nest, HomePod… quelles sont les meilleures enceintes connectées en 2026 ?
            
Le 1er décembre est la Journée mondiale de lutte contre le sida, et 2026 marque les 20 ans de l’organisation (RED). Apple en est partenaire depuis 2006. Une partie des recettes de ses produits (PRODUCT)RED est reversée au Fonds mondial de lutte contre le sida, la tuberculose et le paludisme. Selon Apple, sa contribution sert entièrement à financer des programmes contre le VIH/sida en Afrique subsaharienne. Ces nouvelles éditions s’ajouteraient ainsi à la collecte que la marque organise chaque année à cette occasion.
Gurman évoque en outre deux accessoires rouges : la dragonne des AirPods Pro 3 et le bracelet Sport de l’Apple Watch. Pour la HomePod mini 2 comme pour les AirPods Max 2, la couleur serait le seul changement.
Un retour après plusieurs années d’absence
Ce retour mettrait fin à une longue absence. Depuis février 2025, Apple ne vendait plus aucun appareil (PRODUCT)RED. Il ne restait alors que quelques étuis d’iPhone, et le dernier a été retiré de la vente en mars 2026. Le dernier appareil (PRODUCT)RED lancé par Apple était l’Apple Watch Series 9, en 2023. L’iPhone SE de troisième génération et les iPhone 14 et 14 Plus ont aussi existé dans ce coloris.
Deux finitions très différentes
La HomePod mini 2 jouerait la carte du rouge intégral, avec un revêtement en tissu maillé entièrement rouge.
Les AirPods Max 2 seraient plus discrets. D’après Bloomberg, le casque aurait une finition argentée, des coussinets en maille blanche et un arceau blanc. Le rouge serait réservé à la Digital Crown, la molette qui sert à piloter la lecture et à régler le volume. L’argent ferait ainsi son retour sur le casque d’Apple : les AirPods Max 2 ne sont vendus aujourd’hui qu’en minuit, lumière stellaire, bleu, violet et orange. Ce mélange d’argent et de blanc rappelle d’ailleurs les premiers AirPods Max de 2020. La couronne rouge, en revanche, est une nouveauté.
    Pour aller plus loin
J’ai testé le casque Apple AirPods Max 2 : tout simplement le meilleur (et de loin)
            
Quels concurrents et quels prix ?
Lancés en mars 2026 à 579 euros, les AirPods Max 2 jouent dans la cour des casques haut de gamme à réduction de bruit, face au Sony WH-1000XM6 ou au Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2e génération). Sortie fin octobre à 169 euros, la HomePod mini 2 concurrence quant à elle les enceintes connectées compactes, comme les Amazon Echo et les Google Nest.

articles.title: Cómo actualizar Chrome en la PC, Android y iPhone y comprobar que tiene la última versión
articles.text:
Google Chrome se actualiza solo cuando hay una versión nueva, pero el cambio solo se aplica después de cerrar y volver a abrir el navegador. Quien lo mantiene abierto durante días puede seguir con una versión vieja. La ayuda oficial de Chrome explica cómo revisarlo en computadora, Android e iPhone.
Según la página de ayuda de Google Chrome, las actualizaciones automáticas existen para garantizar que el usuario cuente con las últimas correcciones de seguridad. Antes de instalar una versión nueva, conviene comprobar que el sistema operativo sea compatible y que el equipo cumpla los requisitos mínimos.
En PC: menú, Ayuda y reiniciar
Chrome suele actualizarse en segundo plano cuando el usuario cierra el navegador y lo abre de nuevo. Si hace tiempo que no lo cierra, puede aparecer una actualización pendiente. Para forzar la revisión, el primer paso es abrir Chrome y hacer clic en el icono de Más, arriba a la derecha.
Después hay que entrar en Ayuda > Información de Google Chrome. Esa pantalla muestra la versión instalada, una serie de números debajo del título “Google Chrome”, y busca actualizaciones apenas se abre. Si hay una disponible, aparece el botón Reiniciar, que se debe pulsar para aplicarla.
Si el botón Reiniciar no aparece, significa que el navegador ya usa la versión más reciente. Chrome guarda las pestañas y ventanas abiertas y las recupera al reiniciarse, aunque las ventanas de incógnito no se vuelven a abrir. Quien no quiere reiniciar en ese momento puede elegir Ahora no: la actualización se aplicará la próxima vez que reinicie el navegador.
En Windows, la ayuda indica cerrar todas las pestañas y ventanas de Chrome en el escritorio y reiniciar el navegador. En Mac, si Chrome está en la carpeta de aplicaciones, la opción Actualizar Chrome automáticamente para todos los usuarios, dentro de Información de Google Chrome, permite que lo hagan todas las cuentas.
En Linux se usa el gestor de paquetes del sistema. En Chromebook, Chrome se actualiza junto con el sistema operativo del equipo.
En el celular: Play Store o App Store
En Android, Chrome funciona con Android 10 o versiones superiores y debería actualizarse solo, según la configuración de Play Store. Para comprobarlo hay que abrir Play Store, tocar el icono de perfil arriba a la derecha y entrar en Gestionar apps y dispositivo. En la sección Actualizaciones disponibles se busca Chrome y, si aparece, se toca Actualizar.
En iPhone y iPad, Chrome requiere iOS 18 o una versión posterior. Se abre App Store, se toca Perfil arriba a la derecha y se baja hasta Actualizaciones disponibles. Si Chrome figura en la lista, se toca Actualizar y, si el sistema lo pide, se introduce la contraseña del ID de Apple. Las descargas se instalan solas.
Para ver los datos del navegador en el teléfono, la ayuda indica abrir Chrome, tocar Más y entrar en Configuración. En Android, la opción siguiente es Información de Chrome. En iPhone y iPad, la ruta termina en Google Chrome, dentro de Configuración.
Qué hacer si el equipo no es compatible o falla la actualización
Si el sistema operativo del teléfono es anterior a Android 10 o a iOS 18, Chrome no cumple los requisitos que Google detalla en su ayuda. La página remite a una guía aparte, titulada Solucionar problemas y errores de actualización de Chrome, para los casos en que la instalación falla.
La ayuda también indica que algunas funciones de Chrome no están disponibles en iPhone ni en iPad por restricciones de esos dispositivos. Entre ellas figuran la configuración de cookies, la autodetección de codificación, la opción de no realizar seguimiento y los perfiles múltiples.
Quien quiera probar cambios antes que el resto puede instalar Chrome Beta, la versión de prueba del navegador. En Android, según la ayuda, esa descarga no reemplaza a la versión habitual de Chrome.

articles.title: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services with 7.3 million visits
articles.text:
Law enforcement authorities from 11 countries have disrupted 57 illegal streaming services that operated hundreds of websites and drew over 7.3 million visits each year.
Such illegal IPTV services offer access to television channels, live sports, and movies without permission from the copyright owners for a small monthly fee.
According to the European Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance (AAPA) trade association, legitimate service providers lose around €4.83 billion annually as roughly 60 million people in Europe use illegal platforms for streaming content.
"The operation resulted in the disruption of 57 illegal IPTV services and the identification of 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content, with a combined annual traffic of more than 7.3 million visits. Investigators have so far traced over EUR 26 million in cryptocurrency transactions, with further analysis ongoing," Europol said in a Tuesday press release.
"The operation targeted a criminal market worth billions of euros annually, in which illegal streaming providers sell unauthorised access to premium television channels, live sports and films, often collecting subscription payments through cryptocurrency."
As part of this joint action, which also involved Europol, the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO), INTERPOL, and AAPA, the investigators also partnered with crypto industry experts from Binance, Coinbase, and Chainalysis to trace cryptocurrency payments and identify the financial networks powering these illegal IPTV services.
They did this by looking for links between the illegal IPTV services, crypto wallets, financial transactions, and the individuals who control these services, who used the wallets to receive and transfer payments, making it easier to move money between countries and hide the origin of their profits.
Europol and the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) joined forces in 2016 to create the Intellectual Property Crime Coordinated Coalition (IPC3), which operates within Europol and targets counterfeiting and online and offline piracy.
In June, another major international operation coordinated by Bulgaria with Europol's support, dubbed "Operation KRATOS 2," resulted in the removal of more than 27,000 illegal streaming URLs, the shutdown of nine organized crime groups, and 29 arrests.
That followed Operation KRATOS, another international anti-piracy operation carried out in summer 2024, which shut down a massive illegal streaming network with over 22 million users worldwide.
Earlier this year, in January, Europol, Eurojust, and Interpol also coordinated Operation Switch Off, a global law enforcement action that led to the seizure of three industrial-scale illegal IPTV services.
More recently, in May, Italian authorities dismantled the CINEMAGOAL piracy platform, which provided illegal access to many online streaming platforms, including Netflix, Spotify, and Disney+.

articles.title: Cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne : des données personnelles ont été volées, des hackers chinois sont suspectés
articles.text:
La cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne s’est bien soldée par une fuite de données. Ce lundi 23 novembre, l’exécutif a reconnu que l’EU Academy, une plateforme en ligne qui propose des formations et des ateliers conçus par les institutions de l’Union, a subi une fuite de données personnelles. Cité par Reuters, Thomas Regnier, porte-parole de la Commission pour les questions numériques, indique que « la plateforme EU Academy a été affectée par la campagne de cyberattaques détectée contre la Commission », qui a abouti à une « fuite de données personnelles des utilisateurs ». Toutes les victimes ont été informées « aujourd’hui via le site de l’EU Academy ».
À lire aussi : Piratage de frigos de supermarchés – une opération secrète a évité une catastrophe au Royaume-Uni
Quelles données ont été compromises ?
Parmi les données compromises, on trouve les noms et les adresses e-mail des utilisateurs. Sans surprise, Bruxelles met en garde toutes les personnes concernées contre d’éventuelles campagnes de phishing. En effet, des pirates pourraient se servir des informations subtilisées pour envoyer des e-mails piégés et crédibles. Dos au mur, la Commission a mis la plateforme hors ligne jusqu’à nouvel ordre.
« L’incident fait toujours l’objet d’une enquête. L’accès public à la plateforme a été désactivé », indique le site de l’EU Academy.
Pour rappel, plusieurs autres applications internes ont été coupées par précaution. Certaines de ces applications internes sont encore et toujours indisponibles. Détectée le 22 octobre, la cyberattaque n’a toujours pas été entièrement maîtrisée un mois plus tard.
« Panda », la piste chinoise
Officiellement, la Commission européenne refuse de pointer du doigt un coupable. « En ce qui concerne l’attribution, il faudrait que l’enquête soit terminée pour savoir qui est derrière tout ça. Donc, pour l’instant, pas d’attribution de notre côté », a expliqué Thomas Regnier. En interne, les soupçons de Bruxelles se portent sur la Chine. D’après deux sources citées par Euronews, la Commission soupçonne fortement un réseau de pirates soutenu par la Chine. Le gang est connu sous le nom de Panda.
Selon les investigations menées par la Commission européenne, la cyberattaque reposait sur ARTEX, un outil qui s’appuie sur l’IA pour repérer les failles exploitables dans du code informatique. Sujet d’une alerte du FBI, cet outil est de plus en plus exploité dans le cadre de cyberattaques autonomes. Microsoft et CrowdStrike ont remarqué que le logiciel, qui peut être branché sur des modèles d’IA, est impliqué dans des campagnes d’espionnage visant des centaines d’organisations dans le monde. Storm-0940 et Panda Vapor font partie des nombreux gangs chinois à se servir d’ARTEX. Selon l’enquête en cours, les pirates ne visaient pas de systèmes ou de personnes bien précis. Les hackers voulaient plutôt voir jusqu’où ils pouvaient pénétrer les réseaux de la Commission. Il s’agissait donc vraisemblablement d’un test.
Une année noire pour la cybersécurité de la Commission
C’est déjà la troisième cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne survenue cette année. En janvier dernier, l’infrastructure mobile de l’institution a déjà été compromise. Deux mois plus tard, c’est l’infrastructure cloud, qui héberge le site Europa.eu, qui a été piratée. En coulisses, les deux attaques sont également attribuées à la Chine, mais à des groupes criminels différents.

articles.title: Pendant le Black Friday 2026, ce casque Sony noté 5/5 passe sous les 300 €
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le casque Bluetooth Sony WH-1000XM6 "5 étoiles" à 296,99 € (-12%)
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Sony WH-1000XM6 passe à 296,99 € chez Amazon, Fnac.com et Darty.com, soit une baisse d'environ 12 % et 40,74 € d'économie. Reconnu pour sa réduction de bruit active et la grande précision de ses médiums, ce casque Bluetooth affiche la note maximale de 5/5 à ce jour dans nos tests.
Sony a conçu le WH-1000XM6 pour faire évoluer la formule de ses casques audio sans fil, en visant une précision sonore supérieure et une isolation plus efficace. Ce modèle circum-auriculaire pliable mise sur une ergonomie soignée au quotidien. Cet appareil avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de ses différents tests acoustiques.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le casque Bluetooth descend à 296,99 € chez Amazon, Fnac.com et Darty.com, soit environ 12 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (337,73 €). Cela représente une économie de 40,74 € sur ce modèle.
Réduction de bruit de pointe et restitution audio détaillée
Le Sony WH-1000XM6 se distingue par son traitement acoustique complet, intégrant des médiums précis, des aigus naturels et une excellente dynamique d'écoute. Lors des mesures de notre test complet, sa réduction de bruit active s'est montrée particulièrement efficace dans les environnements bruyants. Côté endurance, notre laboratoire a mesuré 36 heures d'autonomie continue avec la réduction de bruit activée, une valeur qui grimpe à 47 heures sans cette fonction pour espacer les recharges en voyage.
Sony WH-1000XM6
Points forts
- Restitution précise des médiums.
- Aigus naturels, superbe dynamique.
- Réduction du bruit la plus polyvalente du marché.
- Parfait compromis entre confort et maintien.
- Conception pliable.
- Utilisation intuitive et fonctionnalités nombreuses.
Points faibles
- Basses un peu trop généreuses.
- Finition légère pour du haut de gamme.
- Absence d'audio via USB-C.
- Microphones perfectibles.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Ergonomie nomade et quelques réserves techniques
Au quotidien, ce modèle assure un bon équilibre entre confort et maintien, tout en conservant une structure pliable pratique à ranger dans sa housse. Sa connectivité prend en charge le Bluetooth multipoint ainsi que plusieurs codecs audio comme le LDAC et le LC3 pour préserver la qualité sans fil. En contrepartie, le casque délivre des basses un peu trop généreuses par défaut, présente des micros perfectibles pour les appels et ne permet pas la diffusion audio directe via son port USB-C. Ce profil conviendra surtout aux mélomanes nomades qui privilégient l'isolation active et le rendu musical aux conversations téléphoniques prolongées.
Sony WH-1000XM4C : l'autre option face au Sony WH-1000XM6
Le Sony WH-1000XM4C adopte une formule plus ancienne mais toujours solide, avec des réglages soignés dans les médiums et les aigus. Il conserve une conception adaptée aux trajets quotidiens et une réduction de bruit active efficace, bien que ses coussinets ne soient pas amovibles et que la qualité des appels accuse le poids des années.
Le WH-1000XM4C est vendu 47,00 € moins cher que le Sony WH-1000XM6 à son tarif remisé, mais ce dernier offre une autonomie supérieure de 36 heures avec réduction de bruit et une précision sonore plus poussée.
Sony WH-1000XM4C
Points forts
- Restitution claire et naturelle.
- Excellent équilibre médiums/aigus.
- Réduction du bruit toujours à la page.
- Confort irréprochable, design pliable.
- Commandes intuitives et complètes.
Points faibles
- Basses trop présentes.
- Connectivité limitée (pas de LE Audio ni d'audio en USB-C).
- Mode Transparence peu efficace.
- Micros en difficulté en milieu bruyant.
- Quelques caractéristiques datées.

articles.title: Contrata como empleada de hogar durante 4 meses a la mujer de un amigo y consigue que tenga derecho a paro en Vigo
articles.text:
Un juez de Santiago de Compostela ha anulado la multa de 7.501 euros que la Inspección de Trabajo impuso a un empresario de Vigo por contratar durante cuatro meses como empleada del hogar a la mujer de un amigo, una oficinista de más de 52 años que, gracias a esas cotizaciones, acabó cobrando el subsidio por desempleo. Tal y como ha contado La Voz de Galicia, la sentencia, dictada el 22 de septiembre de 2026, concluye que aquel contrato fue real.
Un contrato justo después de la negativa. La mujer había pedido en Vigo el subsidio para mayores de 52 años, pero se lo denegaron a mediados de noviembre de 2022. Y apenas dos semanas más tarde, el 1 de diciembre, el amigo de la familia la contrató a tiempo parcial como su empleada del hogar, en una relación laboral que terminó a finales de marzo de 2023. Poco después, ya en el paro, volvió a solicitar el subsidio, y esta vez se lo concedieron al acreditar esos cuatro meses cotizados.
Lo que vio la Inspección. Para los inspectores, aquello olía a fraude de ley. Y es que el empresario nunca había necesitado una empleada del hogar ni contrató a otra después de prescindir de esta, que además era la esposa de un amigo con el que había coincidido en el trabajo. En febrero de 2024 lo acusaron de actuar en connivencia con ella para que cobrase un subsidio al que, siempre según la Inspección, no habría tenido derecho sin ese acuerdo, algo que la ley de sanciones laborales califica de infracción muy grave. Le impusieron 7.501 euros de multa y le ordenaron devolver lo que ella había cobrado del subsidio.
Primero ganó la trabajadora. Pero la historia ya había pasado por los juzgados de Vigo. Cuando el Servicio Público de Empleo Estatal (SEPE) le reclamó el dinero a la mujer, ella lo llevó a juicio, y en 2025 el juez de la plaza número 4 de lo Social de Vigo le dio la razón y confirmó su derecho a las prestaciones que la Administración le había reconocido en su momento.
El razonamiento de Santiago. El juez de la plaza número 4 de lo Social de Santiago de Compostela parte de ahí: si en Vigo se descartó el fraude por parte de la trabajadora, tampoco puede haberlo por parte del empresario. Vamos, que no ve que ambos estuviesen compinchados. Y para dar el contrato por real se apoya en que el marido de ella había comentado a varios testigos que su esposa estaba buscando trabajo.
Según la sentencia, el hombre no tuvo empleada del hogar hasta que se divorció, y durante esos meses le fue transfiriendo el salario, porque el contrato era real y no un artificio para conseguir el subsidio.

articles.title: Bcomp secures €20 million from EIB to scale flax fibre-based alternatives to carbon fibre, glass fibre and plastics
articles.text:
Bcomp, a Fribourg-based CleanTech startup specialising in high-performance bio-based materials, has secured €20 million from the European Investment Bank (EIB) to build a high-volume manufacturing plant in the Romanian city of Timișoara and continue research and development in Fribourg.
This EIB backing takes the form of €20 million in venture debt, supporting the company’s €47.6 million investment programme to expand manufacturing capacity in Romania and further develop its R&D activities in Switzerland. In April 2024, the company closed a €37.6 million Series C investment funding round led by EGS Beteiligungen AG (EGSB), and in April 2022, it closed its oversubscribed Series B financing round of €31.69 million (CHF 32.4 million/USD 35 million).
“Europe needs to turn technological innovation into industrial production if we are to strengthen our competitiveness and accelerate the green transition. By supporting Bcomp in Romania and Switzerland, we are helping European innovation reach industrial scale and unlock new opportunities for sustainable growth,” said EIB Vice-President Ioannis Tsakiris.
Founded in 2011 by Christian Fischer and Julien Rion, Bcomp develops composite materials based primarily on flax fibres instead of conventional carbon fibre, glass fibre and plastics. The company says its materials, which have a significantly lower environmental footprint, are designed for use in a range of industries, including automotive, motorsport, and recreational equipment.
Its proprietary natural fibre-based reinforcement materials — ampliTex and powerRibs — help decarbonise manufacturing and reduce environmental impacts while enabling lightweight performance, extensive design freedom and plug-and-play integration into existing processes in a wide range of high-performance applications.
“Scaling up our natural fibre composites production is an important step towards making these materials available to more manufacturers and applications, while supporting the EU’s transition towards a circular economy. The EIB’s support will allow us to expand production and continue investing in R&D, strengthening our ability to serve industrial customers and accelerating the adoption of our high-performance natural fibre materials,” said Christian Fischer, Bcomp’s Chief Executive Officer.
Its main manufacturing and development facilities are located in Fribourg, and it plans to carry out its investment project between 2027 and 2030. As a result, the company expects to significantly expand its workforce through 2030, with the Timișoara plant in Romania’s western region of Vest representing a key driver of future employment growth. Around 61% of Bcomp’s planned investment will take place in Vest, supporting regional development and economic cohesion in the European Union.
Bcomp says its production facility in Timișoara is on track to launch in 2027 and will meet growing global demand for its sustainable composite technologies.
The new production facility will significantly increase the company’s production of roving, the foundational yarn used to weave ampliTex. By increasing in-house roving supply, Bcomp highlights that it will have greater control over quality and a more resilient, near-shored supply chain. The production line itself will base production on its existing Fribourg site.
Sergiu Ureniuc, Plant Manager at Bcomp, concluded, “Preparations are already underway to have Timișoara operational by mid-2027 and we are working closely with the experts in Fribourg. Soon, we will be producing in Romania the ampliTex™ roving from European flax, building upon the innovations and lessons learned at Bcomp’s first production site, in Switzerland. There is growing momentum and energy within the local team as we prepare to commission equipment and hit the ground running.”

articles.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
articles.text:
As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress that it seeks in the near term for the federal government (PDF).
The list of so-called “funding anomalies” is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA’s Artemis program for a “higher rate of operations.”
The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA’s Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China’s lunar ambitions are as expansive as NASA’s, and there is a good chance the country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there.
Another continuing resolution?
Fiscal year 2027 began on October 1 of this year, but the US Congress and White House have not agreed upon a budget. The government, including NASA, has been operating on a “continuing resolution” since that time. The existing continuing resolution remains in effect until December 11, by which time the parties need to agree to a final budget or another continuing resolution, or else the government will shut down.
Given the broad disagreement in funding priorities, it seems most likely that Congress will settle on another continuing resolution, punting a budget deal into the new year and a new Democratic-led House and Senate. The release of the White House “anomalies” document signals to Congress which priorities the Trump administration wants to see addressed in a new continuing resolution that would be agreed to in the coming weeks, which the president would have to sign.
The budget plus-up for Artemis appears to be a significant win for NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, who arrived at the space agency 11 months ago, after the White House had already put together its “President’s Budget request” for the fiscal year 2027 process. This is the first time he has had a chance to work with the Trump administration on budget priorities, and in doing so has convinced officials that NASA deserves more funding in its race back to the Moon.

articles.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
articles.text:
A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in New York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.
Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.
The Department of Justice’s 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company’s CFO, Wanzhou Meng, whom the agency accused of fraud. Though the indictment against Meng was eventually dismissed, she admitted to misleading banks over Huawei’s operations in Iran as part of a deferred prosecution agreement. The US government blacklisted Huawei in 2019 over national security concerns.
In total, the jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts, including money laundering, violating US sanctions, bank fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US. The company was acquitted of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. Huawei’s sentencing is set for September 14th, 2027, where it may face “financial penalties including criminal fines, forfeiture, and restitution,” according to the DOJ.
“For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft, and deception,” Tysen A. Duva, the assistant attorney general of the DOJ’s criminal division, says in a statement. “Huawei’s crimes threatened the U.S. financial system, took advantage of American companies that compete honestly in the global telecommunications market, and undermined our national security.”
In a statement to NBC News, a Huawei spokesperson said the charges are “without legal or factual merit” and that it plans to appeal the decision. Huawei didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.
Update, November 24th: Added information from the DOJ.

articles.title: ¿A qué hora se estrenan los episodios 3x07 y 3x08 de 'Los Anillos de Poder', el final de la temporada 3?
articles.text:
La temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder llega a su final con el estreno de sus episodios 7 y 8, los últimos de esta entrega. En ella, los ejércitos de Sauron han avanzado por todo el continente, conquistando cuanto encuentran a su paso. Solo unos pocos bastiones aislados se interponen entre el Señor Oscuro y la victoria total: Khazad-dûm, donde los enanos permanecen ahora recluidos en las profundidades de sus salones bajo la montaña, y los reinos élficos de Lindon y Rivendel, protegidos por sus Tres Anillos.
Mientras tanto, en las profundidades de Mordor, en su recién erigida torre de Barad-dûr, el Señor Oscuro trabaja sin descanso, obsesionado con forjar un poder capaz de doblegar a los últimos enemigos que aún se le resisten: «Un Anillo para gobernarlos a todos…». Ahora, todos los pueblos libres de la Tierra Media —enanos, elfos, hombres y magos— deberán encontrar la forma de unirse en una carrera contrarreloj para impedir que Sauron alcance su objetivo: someter toda forma de vida bajo su dominio absoluto.
Acerca de dónde podrá verse, a diferencia de otros títulos, aquí no depende para nada del territorio. En Estados Unidos, España, Latinoamérica y en el resto del mundo, el final de Los Anillos de Poder temporada 3 estará disponible en Amazon Prime Video. La plataforma alberga los derechos exclusivos de toda la serie, incluyendo su tercera entrega. Por tanto, evidentemente el desenlace de esta formará parte de su catálogo.
Hora de estreno de Los Anillos de Poder 3x07 y 3x08
En cuanto a la hora de estreno de los episodios 7 y 8 de Los Anillos de Poder, en Estados Unidos se emitirán el martes 24 de noviembre a las 21:00h E.T. En España y Latinoamérica, llegará a Amazon Prime Video en la conversión horaria de cada país:

Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
Este horario es diferente al habitual para la serie y la plataforma, que ha adelantado el estreno unas horas en parte por la celebración de Acción de Gracias en Estados Unidos. Así las cosas, la temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder llegará a su final a la espera de saber si Amazon Prime Video la renueva o no para una cuarta entrega.

articles.title: Why Photonic Design Is Becoming a System-Level Challenge
articles.text:
A component can meet its individual design targets and still behave differently as part of a complete optical link.
Photonic engineers make design decisions at many levels.
A laser has its own performance requirements. So does an optical fiber. The interface between them introduces another set of variables. Ultimately, those individual components have to perform together as part of a complete optical link.
If the individual pieces meet their design targets, will the complete system perform as expected?
Not necessarily.
A Keysight EDA-Photonics Design (VPIphotonics) study of short-reach datacenter links provides a useful example. Two multimode VCSEL channels were designed with comparable signal characteristics and evaluated with a wideband multimode fiber. Yet when evaluated as complete transmission links, the two channels produced different results.
Understanding the difference in performance requires looking beyond any single component.
The VPIphotonics study modeled 26.5625 GBaud PAM4 transmission over 150 meters of wideband multimode fiber, using VCSEL channels operating at 850 nm and 910 nm. Each VCSEL was modeled with four transverse modes, and the link considered coupling conditions and receiver models.
25 Gbaud PAM4 with a multimode VCSEL and OM4 fiber.
At first glance, the two channels seemed comparable.
The calculated 3 dB bandwidth was 27.0 GHz at 850 nm and 27.8 GHz at 910 nm.
But that wasn’t the end of the story.
When the complete link was simulated, the outcomes diverged after transmission over 150 meters: the 850 nm channel exhibited better performance compared to the 910 nm channel. By examining the performance of both channels in back-to-back, it is concluded that the difference in performance results from the impairments of the multimode fiber.
System-level simulation of the 850 nm and 910 nm channels after 150 m reveals different transmission performance despite comparable VCSEL modulation bandwidths.
The study found that fiber bandwidth metrics alone did not fully predict system performance. Instead, link quality depended on interactions among:
- VCSEL mode structure
- modal dispersion
- chromatic dispersion
- fiber differential modal delay (DMD)
- wavelength-dependent behavior
That’s an important distinction.
A component-level metric describes an important part of the design, but not necessarily what happens when that component interacts with other components in a link.
For a short-reach optical link, the transmitter, launch conditions, fiber, modal behavior, and receiver all contribute to the final result.
Studying system-level performance reveals the limitations of the system and helps determine the maximum transmission distance, the optimum launch power, and the appropriate driving conditions. Moreover, it enables the prediction of system performance at higher data rates using the same components. These findings may feed back into component design, for example by motivating efforts to extend the bandwidth limitations of the VCSEL. As a result, the design process becomes iterative, progressing from component design to system design and then back to component optimization. This interdependence highlights the need for integrated design tools.
The VCSEL example illustrates a broader challenge in photonic engineering.
At the device level, engineers need an accurate representation of optical and physical behavior.
At the component level, they need to understand how devices work together.
At the system level, the question changes again:
Does the completed design deliver the required performance in its target application?
In the VPIphotonics framework described in the study, an optical link is constructed from parameterized building blocks including lasers, couplers, fibers, photodetectors, filters, receiver blocks, and analysis tools.
That allows the engineer to move beyond “Does this component meet specification?” to “How does this component affect the performance of the complete system?”
Consider the VCSEL-to-fiber interface.
Launch conditions influence which fiber modes are excited. In the VPIphotonics model, coupling between the VCSEL and fiber can account for factors including lateral offset, angular tilt, longitudinal spacing, coupling losses, and the modal fields of the two devices.
The fiber introduces additional considerations, including modal field distributions, effective indices, DMD, chromatic dispersion, attenuation, group delay, and mode coupling.
None of those effects exist independently in the operating link. The engineering value comes from understanding how they combine to influence system-level outcomes.
For the multimode-link application, the VPIphotonics framework includes virtual test benches for measurements such as:
- Differential Modal Delay (DMD)
- Effective Modal Bandwidth Calculated (EMBc)
- Encircled Flux (EF)
The study also evaluates complete-system outputs including eye diagrams and symbol error rate.
This creates a useful connection between simulated component behavior and the measurements engineers use to evaluate the finished link.
For the 850/910 nm example, that system context exposed performance differences that VCSEL bandwidth metrics by themselves did not predict.
At what level do I need to simulate my design to answer the question I am trying to solve?
Detailed device simulation remains important when the problem is the physical behavior of the photonic component.
Component- or circuit-level simulation becomes important when individual devices interact together to perform some function within a single component.
System-level simulation adds the application context needed to investigate how components and circuits affect the performance of the complete optical system.
These are different views of the same engineering problem.
With VPIphotonics now part of Keysight, the broader opportunity is to look at photonic design across multiple levels of abstraction.
The goal is not simply to apply more simulation. It is to use the appropriate level of abstraction for each engineering question and understand how decisions made at one level influence performance at another.
The 850/910 nm example illustrates why that matters. Comparable component metrics did not result in identical link behavior. The difference became clear when interactions among the VCSELs, launch conditions, fiber characteristics, and receiver were evaluated at the system level.
As photonic systems grow more complex, that system context can become increasingly important for making informed design decisions before committing to hardware.
By linking component design directly to system performance, engineers can work from application requirements rather than isolated device metrics. This closes the loop between system architects and component designers, leading to faster development cycles, more efficient trade-offs, and solutions that are optimized for real-world deployment.

articles.title: Nigeria’s OnIt brings structure, trust to Africa’s informal service economy
articles.text:
Nigerian startup OnIt Innovations is building trust and access within Africa’s informal service economy, making it easier for households and businesses to access reliable everyday services while creating more structured earning opportunities for informal service professionals.
Launched in Lagos in May 2024, OnIt offers customers services including laundry, home cleaning, technical and repair services, procurement, grocery shopping and errands. Behind these services is a workforce infrastructure, with the startup recruiting, training, assessing and verifying “service associates” before deployment, then managing service delivery through defined operating standards, customer support and performance monitoring.
“OnIt started from a very practical problem I encountered while working as a practice manager in Lagos. Managing a demanding career alongside family responsibilities made reliable household support extremely important. I began to see that the problem was much bigger than simply finding someone who could perform a task. The real challenge was trust, quality, accountability and consistency,” founder and CEO Dorcas Obeahon told Disrupt Africa.
She said customers typically rely on referrals, social media or unverified workers, while capable service professionals often lack formal training, verified work records and predictable demand.
“There are several companies operating within individual parts of the service economy. Our approach is broader because we are building the underlying service and workforce infrastructure rather than simply providing a directory where customers find workers,” Obeahon said.
The startup has largely grown through founder capital, internally generated revenue and grants, and has been supported by programmes including the Women in Tech accelerator by Standard Chartered Bank and Village Capital, and Orange Corners Nigeria. Its workforce training arm, BlueVarsity, has trained more than 3,000 people, and OnIt now has a pool of more than 500 verified service associates, who have earned over N40 million (US$30,000) through the platform.
OnIt has completed more than 7,000 service orders for over 500 customers, and has generated more than NGN100 million (US$75,000) in cumulative revenue, earned primarily through margins and commissions on services. It also offers recurring household service plans, B2B contracts and workforce training, and is developing employee-benefit products for organisations.
“Customers who experience reliable service tend to use OnIt across different needs. A customer may initially come to us for laundry, and later use OnIt for cleaning, repairs, procurement or errands,” said Obeahon.
OnIt is focused on deepening its model in Lagos before expanding to other major Nigerian cities, and eventually to selected African urban markets. Standardisation has been the biggest challenge.
“We learned quite early that verification alone was not enough. We needed training, operating procedures, quality assurance, performance tracking and accountability after deployment,” Obeahon said.

Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (November 24, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Tuesday, November 24, 2026.
From Google Cloud cutting jobs in India to Keralam’s new initiative, 'Avalkkoppam' (With Her), to tackle domestic and cyber violence against women, here are the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
Google Cloud confirms 30 role cuts in India, rejects claims of wider layoffs
Google Cloud has confirmed that around 30 roles in India were eliminated last week due to work reprioritisation. It, however, rejected online claims that much of its local workforce had been affected.
“These rumors are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organizational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritization of work,” the company said in response to a user on X.
Latest News
Keralam to roll out 'Avalkkoppam' initiative against domestic, cyber violence targeting women
Keralam will roll out a new initiative, 'Avalkkoppam' (With Her) to tackle domestic and cyber violence against women as part of a 16-day statewide campaign beginning November 25.
The initiative is part of the Women and Child Development Department's 'Orange the World' campaign, aimed at ending violence and gender discrimination against women and girls.
This year's campaign will focus on ensuring that survivors of violence can seek assistance without fear and on strengthening legal action against perpetrators.
Funding news
CortexSpark Ventures launches Rs 1,000 Cr deeptech fund
CortexSpark Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on deeptech and artificial intelligence segment, has launched a Rs 1,000 crore fund with an additional greenshoe option of Rs 400 crore.
CortexSpark Ventures, founded by former Infosys executives Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri, will focus on startup investments across spacetech, defence tech, embodied AI and robotics, enterprise AI, medtech & Bio-AI, and energy and advanced materials.
Cosine Robots raises Rs 22.36 Cr to build made-in-India robot actuators
Bengaluru-based Cosine Robots has raised Rs 22.36 crore in a round led by deeptech fund Avaana Capital, with participation from WEH Ventures and angel investors. Founded by Kiran Mathew Koshy and Delip Thomas, the startup makes integrated servo actuators that combine motors, gearboxes, sensors, electronics and proprietary control software. Its joint-level controller runs a 25 kHz loop, or 25,000 updates per second.
The company offers cycloidal and planetary actuators for industrial arms, cobots, quadrupeds and humanoids. The money will fund a new R&D and production facility covering machining, assembly, calibration and endurance testing, and expand the engineering team. Cosine aims to offer robot makers a cost-competitive alternative to established suppliers.
Other news
IIIT-Delhi to host eighth symposium on computational gastronomy
IIIT-Delhi's Complex Systems Laboratory will host GastroSym2026, the eighth edition of its symposium on computational gastronomy. The symposium brings together chefs, scientists, historians, entrepreneurs and policymakers. The field of computational gastronomy turns culinary knowledge into structured data that can be modelled and analysed.
Speakers include chef Manjit Singh Gill, Prof. Ganesh Bagler, anthropologist Prof. Kurush F. Dalal, and Amura Health's Saravanan Balakrishnan. Sessions cover food safety, sensory science, fragrance, personalised nutrition, the gut microbiome and ageing. TasteTron will demonstrate a cooking-machine prototype; Foodoscope Technologies and Bettrlabs will also present. The event also features research posters and startup showcases.
Cashfree launches wallet that lets Indian users authorise AI agents to pay
Payments platform Cashfree has launched Cashfree Wallet, which it calls India's first wallet that lets users authorise personal AI agents to make payments for them. Users link the wallet to their agent with a mobile OTP, add money via UPI, card or net banking, and set budgets and spending rules.
Agents pay only from the wallet balance; so they never see card, UPI or bank details. For now, Cashfree Wallet supports bill payments; travel, food, grocery and ecommerce are under testing. Developers can integrate through Cashfree's Agentpay MCP server; more than 100 agent and bot builders have already done so, said the company. Payment data is stored in India.
Resilience AI reaches nearly five million people and spaces, adds three advisors
Bengaluru-based Resilience AI, founded in November 2023, says its Resilience360 platform now covers nearly five million people and physical spaces across the US, UK, Canada and India, as it works towards futureproofing one billion by 2030. Co-founder Anshu Sharma and advisor Manu Gupta have left the company, while Sujata Saunik, Umit Bhatia and Firoz C joined as advisors in 2026.
More than 500 professionals in over 30 organisations hold Resilience360 certification. The platform is sold through four offerings: Basic, Forge, Spaces and Pro. The company aims to make physical climate risk assessment measurable and bankable across sectors, supported by its founders and advisory network.
GalaxEye picks Bellatrix Aerospace to power its next 30 Gen-II satellites
Bengaluru-based GalaxEye has awarded Bellatrix Aerospace a multi-year contract to supply Arka Hall-effect electric propulsion systems for its next 30 OptoSAR Gen-II satellites, announced at the India International Space Conclave 2026. Measured by satellite count, it is the largest business-to-business order between Indian private space companies since the sector opened in 2020.
The thrusters will place satellites in their slots, maintain spacing, avoid debris and handle end-of-life deorbiting. Bellatrix's thrusters were qualified in orbit on ISRO missions, and the company raised a $20 million pre-Series B in March 2026. GalaxEye's Mission Drishti launched in May 2026, but contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm.
QNu Labs and NIELIT sign MoU to build India's quantum-ready workforce
QNu Labs, a quantum cybersecurity company, has signed a memorandum of understanding with the National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT), a society under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, to strengthen quantum technology education and skills.
The two will develop training programmes in quantum technologies, including quantum-safe cybersecurity, and explore Quantum Labs at identified institutions through a hub-and-spoke model. Plans include industry-oriented curricula, hackathons, faculty development, train-the-trainer programmes, certification, internships and on-the-job training, wherever feasible and mutually agreed. The partnership aims to link industry expertise with institutional learning and prepare talent for India's evolving quantum landscape.
Vidyakul raises Rs 10 Cr in debt funding from Michael & Susan Dell Foundation
Vidyakul, a vernacular-first learning platform for state-board students, has secured Rs 10 crore in debt funding from the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation. The money will go towards expanding courses, assessments and personalised academic support for Classes 9 to 12, and towards its Hindi AI tools, which resolve about 1.2 million student questions a month.
It also plans pathways for students beyond Class 12. The company says 99.8% of its Bihar Class 12 students passed the 2026 board exams, against a statewide rate of 85%. More than 1.17 lakh students enrolled in its paid programmes in 2025-26, and its YouTube channels have over 15 million subscribers.
Pixxel signs MoUs with Centum Electronics and CS TECH Ai to advance space and geospatial technologies
Bengaluru-based Pixxel has signed two memoranda of understanding at the India International Space Conclave 2026. The agreement with Centum Electronics covers joint development of advanced electronics for satellite payloads and subsystems, drawing on Centum's decades of experience with ISRO missions.
The pact with CS TECH Ai (Ceinsys Tech) will explore geospatial data applications, orbital sustainability and enterprise dashboards that use satellite data and AI for infrastructure decision-making. Both follow an MoU with IIT Kanpur on hyperspectral research and AI-driven remote sensing. Pixxel raised $100 million in Series C funding earlier this year, taking its total capital to $195 million.
Flipkart Foundation's Sampark 2026 focuses on systemic change as Delhi outlines gig workers welfare board
The Flipkart Foundation hosted the fourth edition of its Sampark conference at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, themed on building institutions and local capabilities so that development outlasts individual programmes. The foundation says it has reached 41.5 lakh people across 17 states and union territories.
Delhi Cabinet Minister Kapil Mishra said the government is working towards a Gig Workers Welfare Board covering social security, healthcare and workplace safety, and urged skilling so delivery partners can move into store and warehouse roles. Panels and a keynote discussed community ownership, scaling through government partnerships and youth development, and the foundation recognised its NGO partners.

articles.title: Tesla FSD v15 : cette mise à jour évite les nids-de-poule, freine devant les radars et ajoute la réalité augmentée
articles.text:
À défaut de sortir de nouveaux modèles, Tesla continue d’affiner son FSD. La dernière mise à jour en date promet en ce sens de corriger les faiblesses structurelles de la version actuelle. Le FSD v15 lit ainsi mieux les panneaux, évite plus habilement les nids de poule et réagit plus rapidement aux zones scolaires. Au bout du compte, la marque assure une gestion « 25 fois plus performante des situations critiques ».
Cerise sur le gâteau, une représentation ultra-réaliste en réalité augmentée de l’environnement s’invite sur l’écran central. Mais qu’apporte concrètement cette nouvelle mise à jour ? Dans le détail, la navigation est améliorée grâce à l’utilisation d’un modèle d’apprentissage de bout en bout basé sur les données d’autres véhicules ayant déjà emprunté un itinéraire similaire.
Stationnement personnalisé et détection des radars au programme
Ensuite, une fois arrivé à destination, le stationnement pourra se faire de plusieurs manières via l’historique de stationnement personnalisé. Le véhicule offrira de fait une poignée d’options pour se garer en fonction du lieu sur lequel il se trouve. D’autre part, le dispositif de surveillance de l’attention du conducteur gagne en efficacité lorsque la personne porte un chapeau ou des lunettes de soleil.
La caméra placée au-dessus du rétroviseur demeure en revanche la même. Les petits animaux et les débris sur la chaussée sont d’autre part mieux détectés pour éviter une collision. Les zones inondées seront aussi contournées si la profondeur d’eau est trop importante pour envisager un passage. Enfin, le FSD pourra ralentir à l’approche d’un radar et deviendra compatible avec l’usage d’un porte-vélos.
 FSD v15 now starting to roll out – upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network
Safety
25x better handling of safety critical cases
Tesla Reality View 
Adds a live visualization of the drive that lets you see & control what FSD is planning to do
Navigation for start… pic.twitter.com/Sfjk4wZecW
— Tesla (@Tesla) November 21, 2026
Tesla Reality View : une nouvelle interface en réalité augmentée
Mais le plus impressionnant demeure la fonction Tesla Reality View permettant de visualiser tout ce qui se passe autour du véhicule. La représentation actuelle modélisant l’environnement de manière simpliste devient ainsi complètement obsolète. Qu’en est-il alors de la promesse d’une efficacité 25 fois supérieure formulée initialement ? Tesla ne fournit aucun chiffre précis. Le magazine Electrek a mené sa petite enquête.
Puisque le FSD v14 pouvait parcourir quelques milliers de kilomètres sans intervention critique du conducteur, il serait raisonnable de penser que le FSD v15 soit capable de rouler environ 80 000 km sans aucune manipulation d’urgence. La promesse est grande, mais possible à tenir vu les derniers ajustements du FSD. Rappelons en effet que le système ne peut plus faire de gros excès de vitesse en dépassant seulement la limite de 10 % au maximum.
Une allure plus faible permettra à l’ensemble de mieux gérer les situations critiques comme décrit. De quoi permettre à Tesla de creuser à nouveau l’écart avec ses concurrents chinois, qui investissent aussi massivement dans la conduite entièrement autonome.
