articles.title: Spam téléphonique : Surfshark lance son outil de protection
articles.text:
Surfshark ajoute à ses forfaits One et One+ un filtre qui repère les appels frauduleux sur Android et iOS. L’application compare chaque numéro inconnu à une base de numéros signalés, puis prévient l’utilisateur ou, sur Android, peut bloquer l’appel.
Nous rapportions en août que Surfshark filtrait déjà les SMS frauduleux sur iOS et Android, avec un tri dans le dossier Indésirables sur iPhone et une alerte sur Android. L’éditeur s’attaque maintenant aux appels et publie une étude sur les numéros inconnus.
Un filtre usr iOS, un vrai blocage sur Android
Quand un numéro inconnu vous appelle, l’application le compare à une base de numéros déjà signalés. Surfshark assure qu’elle n’enregistre pas les conversations, ne surveille pas les appels privés et n’utilise pas vos données personnelles pour entraîner des modèles d’IA. Sur Android, elle repère les fraudes et le démarchage. En fonction du réglage, l'utilisateur reçoit un avertissement, ou l’appel est bloqué avant même que le téléphone sonne. Sur iPhone, une notification s’affiche sur l’écran d’appel avec l’une des sept catégories (fraude, démarchage, santé, services publics, administrations, collecte de fonds, services financiers). L'utilisateur peut décider de répondre ou non. En revanche, il n’y a pas de blocage automatique sur iOS.
L’étude porte sur 50 numéros inconnus en tête des recherches dans 32 pays. Ensemble, ils ont généré 13,2 millions de requêtes. Sept numéros sur dix sont liés à des fraudes et concentrent 72 % des requêtes (9,5 millions), contre 18 % pour les appels légitimes et 10 % pour les numéros suspects non vérifiés. Dans le volume frauduleux, 41 % des recherches concernent du harcèlement, 23 % des pièges financiers et 16 % du démarchage. Selon Dominykas Simkus, responsable produit senior, les fraudeurs partent d’informations déjà divulguées et associées à un numéro, puis posent des questions anodines pour en obtenir davantage. Ils peuvent aussi usurper le numéro affiché pour imiter une banque ou la police, parfois avec des appels générés par IA.
- moodEssai 30 jours
- devicesNombre d'appareils illimité
- phishingAnti-phishing inclus
- local_atmAnti-ransomware inclus
- groupsContrôle parental inclus
Le démarchage téléphonique est interdit sans accord préalable depuis le 11 août, sauf si vous êtes déjà client et que l’appel concerne votre contrat. Nous avons constaté pourtant en novembre que les appels continuaient, avec 43 000 signalements à la DGCCRF entre début août et fin septembre. Pour l’usurpation, l’Arcep impose depuis désormais une nouvelle règle .Depuis janvier, quand un appel venu de l’étranger affiche un numéro de mobile français (06 ou 07) sans qu’on puisse vérifier qu’il appartient à l’appelant, le téléphone affiche “numéro masqué” à la place. Cette barrière agit chez les opérateurs, alors que Surfshark agit directement sur le téléphone.
Bien sûr, il existe des alternatives gratuites. Nous présentions en avril les filtres intégrés à iOS et Android, l’application Orange Téléphone, accessible à tous les abonnés mobiles, et Saracroche, un projet indépendant financé par les dons, qui bloque automatiquement les appels suspects. Surfshark intègre la fonction à ses forfaits. La formule One comprend un VPN, un bloqueur de publicités, un antivirus et la surveillance des fuites de données, tandis que One+ ajoute Incogni, qui retire vos données personnelles du web. Pour activer cette nouvelle protection, il faut choisir la protection des appels dans l'application et accorder les autorisations demandées.

articles.title: La saison 3 des Anneaux de pouvoir se termine par une excellente nouvelle
articles.text:
On n’en a pas fini avec Le Seigneur des anneaux : Les Anneaux de pouvoir. Alors que la troisième saison vient de s’achever avec les deux derniers épisodes diffusés sur Amazon Prime Video, la quatrième saison a été officialisée ce mardi 24 novembre.
Amazon MGM Studios a confirmé la bonne nouvelle dans un communiqué publié quelques heures avant les ultimes épisodes proposés en avance. « Le Seigneur des anneaux : Les Anneaux de pouvoir est devenue une série emblématique pour Prime Video. Alors que la saison 3 offre le moment clé que les fans attendaient — la création de l’Anneau Unique –, nous sommes fiers de confirmer une saison 4 avec J.D. Payne, Patrick McKay et toute l’équipe créative », a déclaré Peter Friedlander, directeur de la télévision mondiale chez Amazon MGM Studios.
Pas de date de diffusion pour la saison 4 des Anneaux de pouvoir
Les deux showrunners, J.D. Payne et Patrick McKay, restent aux commandes. Ils avaient initialement présenté la série à Amazon comme un récit en cinq saisons. Leur idée, racontée au Hollywood Reporter en 2022, était d’étirer sur cinq saisons le prologue de La Communauté de l’anneau de Peter Jackson, celui où Galadriel raconte l’histoire des anneaux. Si ce plan tient, la saison 4 sera l’avant-dernière.
Amazon MGM Studios n’a rien indiqué sur le calendrier de sortie de cette quatrième saison. On sait en revanche que son tournage débutera au printemps 2027, aux studios de Shepperton, au Royaume-Uni. La série est pour l’instant en pré-production. On peut néanmoins miser sur une attente d’environ deux ans, comme entre la fin de la saison 1 et le début de la saison 2 (1 an et 10 mois), puis entre la saison 2 et la saison 3 (2 ans et 1 mois). Soit une sortie pour l’automne 2028.
Dans son communiqué, Amazon MGM Studios ne manque pas de se réjouir que Le Seigneur des anneaux : Les Anneaux de pouvoir soit « l’un des titres les plus performants et les plus regardés de l’histoire de Prime Video, porté par une communauté de fans mondiale, vaste et très engagée ». Amazon avance 33 millions de spectateurs dans le monde en 12 jours pour la saison 3, et une place de numéro 1 sur Prime Video dans plus de 100 pays depuis son lancement, le 11 novembre.
Ces 33 millions cachent pourtant un recul. Selon un calcul de Forbes, la saison 3 compte environ 17,5 % de spectateurs de moins que la saison 2 sur ses 12 premiers jours. Amazon avait pourtant mis six épisodes en ligne sur cette période, contre quatre pour la saison 2 et trois pour la saison 1.

articles.title: 5 minutes pour recharger un colosse de 5 mètres : BYD métamorphose son SUV électrique fétiche
articles.text:
Décidément, BYD ne chôme pas en ce moment. À vrai dire, cela dure depuis un petit bout de temps. Car la firme basée à Shenzhen ne passe quasiment pas une semaine sans dévoiler une nouveauté au sein de sa gamme. Alors qu’elle est actuellement en négociation pour racheter l’usine d’Ineos en Moselle, elle poursuit en parallèle le développement de son catalogue. C’est ainsi qu’elle vient de lancer en Chine la 3ème génération de son SUV électrique star, le Tang.
Lancé en 2015 sous la forme d’un modèle hybride rechargeable, il est par la suite passé à l’électrique. Le nouveau Tang évolue surtout sur le plan esthétique. Il reprend la signature lumineuse « Dragon Whiskers », avec une bande rétroéclairée entre les feux avant. Sur les deux finitions supérieures, le toit accueille un capteur LiDAR, au service de l’aide à la conduite God’s Eye B. L’entrée de gamme se contente de série de l’aide à la conduite God’s Eye C, qui repose uniquement sur des caméras.
Plus grand qu’auparavant, le BYD Tang mesure 5,05 mètres de long, soit 7,5 centimètres de plus que l’ancienne mouture. Le tout pour 1,98 mètre de large et 1,76 mètre de haut. Contrairement à l’Atto 8 et à l’ancien Tang, tous deux à sept places, il se limite à cinq places, sur un empattement de 2,95 mètres.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Stockez le surplus au lieu de le revendre à bas prix. Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ se branche sur votre installation existante, 100 % plug-and-play, et s’amortit plus vite grâce au Black Friday.
À bord, le confort est de mise avec un frigo ainsi que des sièges inclinables à 130 degrés. Les finitions supérieures ont droit à un écran tactile de 30 pouces partagé avec le passager, tandis que l’entrée de gamme se contente d’un écran de 15,6 pouces. Il est associé à un combiné de 10,25 pouces pour le conducteur.
Une charge éclair
Le coffre offre 910 litres, et jusqu’à 2 113 litres une fois la banquette rabattue, selon le site officiel de la marque. S’y ajoute un frunk de 205 litres à l’avant. BYD nous donne également quelques informations sur la fiche technique de cette nouvelle mouture du grand SUV.
Il est décliné en plusieurs versions, avec une puissance comprise entre 402 et 691 chevaux pour la variante à transmission intégrale. Le reste du catalogue est uniquement en propulsion. Le 0 à 100 km/h est réalisé en 4,3 à 7,2 secondes, pour une vitesse maximale de 250 km/h.
Mais surtout, le nouveau BYD Tang embarque une batterie Blade 2.0 LFP (lithium-fer-phosphate), d’une capacité de 88,7 à 105,8 kWh. De quoi promettre une autonomie généreuse, comprise entre 730 et 850 kilomètres CLTC. Soit environ 620 à 722 kilomètres WLTP.
La recharge s’effectue quant à elle de 10 à 70 % en 5 minutes et de 10 à 97 % en seulement 9 minutes, grâce à la technologie Flash Charging. Ce temps suppose toutefois de passer par les bornes Flash Charging de BYD, qui délivrent jusqu’à 1 500 kW, un réseau dédié que la marque déploie d’abord en Chine.
Ce Tang inaugure aussi le nouveau châssis « by wire » de BYD. Avec l’option à transmission intégrale de la finition haut de gamme, la direction et le freinage sont commandés électroniquement, et les roues arrière directrices ramènent le rayon de braquage à 5,6 mètres. La suspension pneumatique à double chambre DiSus-A est réservée aux versions les plus chères.
Pour le moment, celui-ci est uniquement disponible en Chine. Il démarre à partir de 187 900 yuans, ce qui représente environ 25 770 euros. Mais attention, ce tarif sera fortement revu à la hausse si la voiture arrive en Europe, à cause des droits de douane.
En France, BYD vend toujours la génération précédente, à sept places. Elle est affichée à 72 000 euros, ramenés à 58 235 euros jusqu’au 30 novembre grâce à une remise de 13 400 euros et à la prime CEE. Elle offre une autonomie de 530 kilomètres avec sa batterie de 108,8 kWh.

articles.title: Google verknüpft KI-Modus mit Drive, Wallet und Gemini
articles.text:
Optimierung versus Datenschutz: Google verknüpft KI-Modus mit Drive, Wallet und Gemini
Im Frühjahr 2026 hatte Google seinen aus der Gemini-App bekannten Dienst Personal Intelligence für den KI-Modus der Suche ausgerollt. Damit sollen Nutzer:innen persönlichere Antworten erhalten, weil frühere Suchanfragen und Aktivitäten berücksichtigt sein sollen.
Mehr Personal Intelligence im KI-Modus
Zudem lassen sich damit Google-Apps wie Gmail, Kalender und Fotos mit dem KI-Modus in der Google-Suche verbinden. Dahinter steckt die Idee, dass sich die Antworten mit mehr persönlichem Kontext und eigenen Daten noch mehr auf die Nutzer:innen zuschneiden lassen. Jetzt weitet Google dieses Angebot aus.
Wie der Konzern mitteilt, lassen sich künftig auch die Google-Dienste Wallet, Drive und die Gemini-App im KI-Modus mit der Personal Intelligence verbinden. Im Falle der Wallet soll es so möglich sein, sich bei Suchanfragen auf bestimmte Vorteile oder Prämien der dort gespeicherten Karten oder Konten hinweisen zu lassen.
KI darf kein Geld investieren
Google verspricht, dass der KI-Modus ausschließlich Informationen aus der Wallet-App lesen kann. Das Verschieben, Verwalten oder Investieren von Geld der Nutzer:innen soll der KI untersagt sein.
Die Verbindung von Google Drive mit dem KI-Dienst soll derweil dafür sorgen, dass über verschiedene Dokumente verteilte Informationen bei bestimmten Antworten herangezogen werden können. So ließe sich laut Google damit etwa eine personalisierte Steuererklärung beziehungsweise zumindest die Grundlage dafür erstellen.
Google begegnet Datenschutzbedenken
Aber ist es wirklich sinnvoll, der Google-KI den Zugriff auf diese teils sensiblen Daten zu erlauben? Immerhin sind die Apps nicht von vornherein verbunden. Nutzer:innen müssen den Zugriff also aktiv gewähren. Zudem lassen sich die Verbindungen Google zufolge jederzeit wieder ausschalten. Und: Die für die Antworten genutzten persönlichen Informationen sollen über das neue Symbol „Personalisierung“ als solche gekennzeichnet werden.
Für Google-Nutzer:innen in der EU, der Schweiz oder Großbritannien sind entsprechende Überlegungen aber ohnehin theoretischer Natur. Denn Personal Intelligence im KI-Modus sowie in der Gemini-App steht derzeit nur Nutzer:innen in den USA zur Verfügung. Ob und wann der Dienst in weiteren Regionen wie Deutschland ausgerollt werden soll, hat Google bisher nicht mitgeteilt.
;) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: From Vulnerability Noise to Resilience: Rethinking Security in the AI Era
articles.text:
Written by: George Manuelian, Chief Strategy Officer, RapidFort
The modern software stack has become an iceberg. The application code customers and security teams see at the surface is only a small portion of what is being shipped. Beneath it sit operating systems, frameworks, libraries, packages, and transitive dependencies, with much of it drawn from open source or third parties.
As AI accelerates software development, that hidden complexity has become an even more critical security challenge.
For business and technology leaders, the question is no longer simply how many vulnerabilities exist. It is where does meaningful risk live, which vulnerabilities can be exploited in our environment, and how we can reduce that risk without turning developers into full-time vulnerability managers.
The answer requires a fundamental shift from vulnerability accumulation to continuous software resilience.
First step: Recognizing composition of modern software
The typical containerized stack is layers of base operating system software, packages, libraries, language frameworks and dependencies, and the application itself. The application a company writes may represent only a small portion of what it ultimately ships.
That is important because vulnerabilities multiply. A vulnerable package in a base image is not necessarily one vulnerability in practice; it can be replicated across every application and container that uses that image.
In light of this, executives should ask a different question of their security programs: How much of the reported risk is relevant to the way our software operates? Traditional scanning frequently identifies the presence of a vulnerable component without establishing whether that component is loaded, executing, reachable or exposed.
A software bill of materials (SBOM) identifies what exists; a runtime bill of materials (RBOM) can pinpoint what is actually being used. That distinction can dramatically reduce noise.
For example, in the real world from a customer, an NGINX image containing 152 packages and 48 CVEs had only 47 packages actually running in the application. More than 80% of the software was not being exercised. The lesson is not that every unused package is harmless, but that security teams need operational context before assigning remediation urgency.
This is also why severity alone has become an inadequate basis for prioritization. A high or critical Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) score can command attention, but the business question is whether the vulnerable code is relevant and exploitable in the environment.
There are four contextual factors increasingly shaping remediation decisions: Whether a vulnerability is exposed, whether it is a known exploited vulnerability, whether exploitation is automatable, and whether exploitation would have meaningful technical impact.
The shift from severity to exploitability and reachability is important because it changes the operating model. Instead of asking engineering teams to chase the largest number on a scanner dashboard, leaders should ask whether the organization has enough visibility to determine what is running, what is reachable, and what is exposed.
As a result, security becomes a business-risk exercise rather than a race to close tickets.
Eliminate Up to 99.9% of Container CVEs Without Code Changes
RapidFort Curated Images give your team 35,000+ near-zero CVE container images, rebuilt and hardened every 24 hours.
Swap in a hardened base image and remove exploitable vulnerabilities at the source, with no code, OS or pipeline changes.
Learn More
Hardening is the important next step
Hardening should not mean merely passing a configuration benchmark. It should also mean removing software and functionality that the application does not need
. Every unnecessary library, shell, package manager, build utility, or default component increases the amount of software that must be maintained and potentially gives an attacker additional tools if a container is compromised.
Runtime profiling is a proven approach for identifying these unused components and removing them systematically.
AI makes this discipline more important
AI-assisted development can rapidly generate code and pull in packages, but developers may not always know which dependencies were introduced or whether they remain necessary as the application evolves.
For example, a development environment in which developers may have to ask the AI system which Python version or packages were used because the model generated much of the implementation is a warning sign for governance.
Speed of development cannot come at the expense of knowing what is being shipped.
No one is going to slow AI development. The answer is to put security controls into the pipeline so developers do not have to perform every security task manually. Clean, curated base images; runtime profiling; removal of unused components; vulnerability context; and automated rebuilding can become repeatable parts of CI/CD.
The objective is to make the secure path the default path.
Introducing Zero Trust software architecture
Zero Trust has traditionally been associated with network access and identity. But when organizations continuously ingest open source and third-party software, they also need to question the software entering their environments.
Software should be verified, trusted components should be maintained in controlled registries, and the software should be continuously evaluated as it moves through development, testing and production – following the common principles of Zero Trust.
This represents a meaningful change in how software supply chain security should be managed. The goal should not be a perfect vulnerability dashboard.
The goal should be a development system that continuously produces software with less unnecessary code, fewer meaningful vulnerabilities, and a smaller attack surface.
For example, one customer reduced an initial 5,286 findings to three unresolved vulnerabilities within 48 hours by combining profiling, curated images, and removal of unused components.
The strategic lesson learned
Vulnerability remediation should become a manufacturing process, not a recurring emergency. If organizations wait until a scanner produces a massive backlog, they have already allowed complexity to become technical debt.
If instead they control what enters the software supply chain, understand what actually runs, prioritize based on reachability and impact, remove what is unnecessary, and continuously rebuild from cleaner components, security becomes part of software production itself.
This approach also changes the conversation between security and engineering. Developers should not be expected to fix every finding simply because a scanner found it. They need context, automation and a clear understanding of which risks require action.
Security leaders need visibility into runtime behavior and the ability to distinguish a theoretical exposure from a vulnerability that can actually affect the business.
The future of software security in the AI era
The future of software security belongs to organizations that manage complexity continuously. AI will accelerate development, it’s a given. Open source will remain foundational, that’s understood. Neither trend is going away, nor should it of course.
But both make it more important to establish disciplined software intake, strong supply-chain controls, runtime visibility, effective hardening, and automated remediation.
Ultimately, the objective is not simply to reduce the number of CVEs on a report. It is to build software that contains less unnecessary functionality, relies on cleaner components, exposes fewer opportunities to attackers, and can be continuously refreshed without overwhelming those responsible for delivering it
. Software supply chain security works best when profiling, verification, clean images, and removal of unused components are built directly into the pipeline.
The executive mandate for the AI era must stop treating vulnerability management as a downstream cleanup exercise. Build security into the way software is assembled, tested and deployed.
When continuous remediation becomes part of the normal development life cycle, organizations can move faster without accepting vulnerability volume as an unavoidable cost of innovation.

articles.title: Nvidia cae antes de la apertura y Anthropic baja de su precio de salida a bolsa
articles.text:
Las acciones de Nvidia caían cerca de un 5% antes de la apertura de Wall Street, mientras Anthropic descendía por debajo de los USD 83 fijados en su salida a bolsa.
El retroceso llegó un día después de la fuerte recuperación de las tecnológicas, impulsada por el regreso de Jensen Huang a la dirección de la compañía de semiconductores.
El cambio de tendencia importa porque devuelve al mercado las dudas que habían quedado temporalmente relegadas por el repunte del lunes: el volumen de gasto destinado a centros de datos, la capacidad de las empresas para rentabilizar la inteligencia artificial y la presión de unas condiciones financieras más exigentes. Los futuros del Nasdaq-100 bajaban 1,7%, frente a una caída de 0,9% en los contratos del S&P 500.
La subida de Nvidia perdió fuerza tras añadir cerca de USD 950.000 millones
El lunes 23 de noviembre de 2026, Nvidia registró una subida de 31% después de que la compañía anunciara el retorno inmediato de Jensen Huang como presidente ejecutivo, consejero delegado y miembro del consejo de administración. El avance aportó cerca de USD 950.000 millones de capitalización bursátil a la empresa y dio impulso a una sesión en la que el Nasdaq Composite escaló casi 6,5%.
La reacción alcanzó a gran parte del sector tecnológico. El S&P 500 subió 4,7% y el Dow Jones avanzó más de 1.400 puntos, equivalentes a cerca de 3%. La recuperación se produjo después de una semana de ventas que golpeó a las empresas vinculadas con la inteligencia artificial y llevó a varios índices a terreno de corrección.
Sin embargo, el impulso no se mantuvo en las operaciones previas a la apertura del martes 24 de noviembre de 2026. Nvidia cedía parte de las ganancias del día anterior y un fondo cotizado que agrupa a fabricantes de chips también registraba pérdidas superiores al 3%.
El comportamiento de la acción refleja un mercado que sigue dividido entre la expectativa de una expansión sostenida de la infraestructura de inteligencia artificial y la cautela por el coste que implica financiarla.
Anthropic perdió el nivel de USD 83 de su oferta pública inicial
La presión fue mayor para Anthropic PBC, la empresa desarrolladora del modelo Claude. Sus acciones cayeron por debajo de los USD 83 de su oferta pública inicial, con lo que borraron el margen que conservaban sobre el precio de colocación tras sus primeras jornadas de cotización.
La compañía había subido 17% en su debut bursátil del jueves 19 de noviembre de 2026, pero cerró con una caída de 9% el viernes. El lunes, mientras Nvidia lideraba el repunte tecnológico, Anthropic terminó la sesión con pérdidas y se mantuvo cerca de su nivel de salida.
El mercado sigue atento a sus necesidades de financiación. La empresa ha comprometido aproximadamente USD 900.000 millones en infraestructura y capacidad de computación durante las próximas dos décadas, una cifra que ha situado el acceso al crédito entre las principales preocupaciones de los inversores.
La caída bajo el precio de la oferta pública también pone el foco en la valoración de las compañías dedicadas de forma exclusiva a la inteligencia artificial. A diferencia de grandes tecnológicas con negocios consolidados, estas empresas dependen en mayor medida de que el crecimiento futuro justifique inversiones muy elevadas en chips, energía y centros de datos.
Asia mantuvo el entusiasmo, aunque Wall Street abrió otra discusión
La reacción en Asia fue distinta. El Nikkei japonés avanzó 4%, el Kospi de Corea del Sur ganó 6% y el Taiex de Taiwán, donde cotiza el fabricante de chips TSMC, subió 9%. Los mercados de la región siguieron el impulso generado por la recuperación de Nvidia y por las expectativas de una demanda sostenida de procesadores avanzados.
La sesión estadounidense, no obstante, volvió a concentrar la atención en factores menos favorables. Los inversores evaluaban las previsiones de ingresos de Hewlett Packard Enterprise, que quedaron por debajo de las estimaciones más optimistas, y aguardaban nuevos datos de inflación en Estados Unidos.
También se esperan resultados trimestrales de compañías como Dell, Analog Devices y Autodesk. Estas cifras pueden ofrecer señales sobre el gasto empresarial en servidores, software y equipos destinados a cargas de trabajo de inteligencia artificial.
El regreso de Huang redujo una fuente de incertidumbre alrededor de Nvidia, pero no resolvió la cuestión central para el sector: si la inversión en centros de datos podrá traducirse en ingresos suficientes para sostener las valoraciones actuales.

articles.title: Nigeria plans 500,000-job pipeline in data protection
articles.text:
Nigeria’s data protection regulator wants more mid-career professionals to step into the country’s growing privacy workforce, betting that local talent can fill a global shortage of certified experts.
Speaking at a capacity-building session for media professionals in Abuja on Friday, November 20, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji outlined the agency’s push to expand the country’s data privacy ecosystem and position Nigeria as an exporter of compliance talent.
Section 32 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 requires businesses to employ Data Protection Officers (DPOs), but without enough certified professionals, local companies risk non-compliance, data breaches, and lost foreign investment.
To prevent a talent crunch and preserve local experts, the NDPC said it is using a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model to create 500,000 jobs. According to Olatunji, compliance with the Act has already triggered a sharp rise in certified professionals across the country, though supply still lags behind market demand.
While he did not specify the exact number of DPOs the market requires, the regulator’s 500,000-job target highlights how wide the talent deficit remains.
“When we started, we had less than 1,000 data protection officers in all of this country,” he said. “At the commission, we have over 90% of our staff that are certified. And in Nigeria, we have over 10,000 certified data protection officers.”
Exporting talent
Olatunji noted that the ecosystem has already created more than 27,000 jobs in under three years, driven largely by Data Protection Compliance Organisations (DPCOs) licenced to conduct audits and enforce compliance on behalf of the government.
Beyond local businesses, the regulator said it is pitching Nigeria as a talent hub for international markets grappling with privacy skill shortages.
“We want data privacy within the ecosystem, or if you need the service of a DPO, you look towards Africa, and of course, Nigeria,” Olatunji said, pointing to talent gaps abroad. “Even in the UK, 94.7% of breaches are due to lack of qualified personnel in data privacy and protection. So everywhere, all over the world, they are looking for data privacy and protection experts.”
Several former NDPC staffers have already transitioned into international roles across the United States and the United Kingdom, including executive leadership positions at global financial institutions, he added. To sustain the talent pipeline, the commission said it has begun taking data privacy training directly into Nigerian tertiary institutions to introduce students to the field as a viable career path.
For working professionals, Olatunji framed data protection not as a complete career pivot, but as a flexible, high-demand add-on. Because organisations are legally required to appoint DPOs, certified individuals can consult for multiple firms simultaneously.
“The good thing about this is you can be a DPO and do some other stuff. And you can be a DPO for four, five, three, ten organisations. You can be a freelance DPO. Nobody ties you down to any particular spot,” he said.

articles.title: Amazon's Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang’s comeback as Nvidia’s CEO is understandably making waves, leaving people wondering about the longer-term implications of his quick reinstatement and the U.S. government’s active role in his return. But there was another development yesterday that could also matter for Nvidia down the road: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart‘s tech and its team for a reported $7.5 billion.
The broader industry seems to agree that Decart’s tech for optimizing AI models to run on non-Nvidia chips is worth several billion dollars. Anthropic reportedly tried to acquire the startup in the same ballpark, and Nvidia, which invested in the startup’s $300 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation, was also rumored as a prospective buyer.
Amazon was ultimately the one to pull the trigger and bring on board Decart’s co-founders Dean Leitersdorf, Orian Leitersdorf, and Moshe Shalev and their team, but the company is not interested in the world models they had been working on. At the heart of the deal is the startup’s tech that helps AI models run better on all kinds of chips.
By incorporating the startup’s Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), Amazon is now hoping to extract more performance out of its Trainium chips, as the company tries to turn AWS into a $1 trillion revenue business.
In its announcement, Amazon said it has worked with Decart since 2025 to optimize the Trainium chips. This deal is ostensibly aimed at accelerating that work, which could eventually result in the company offering its Trainium-based data centers, which Anthropic already uses, to more customers. Amazon has already been working to make Trainium easier to switch to.
One way Nvidia managed to leapfrog its competitors was by spending $6.9 billion to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox, which eventually grew to become a core piece of its international manufacturing strategy. Amazon could well be following a similar path.
Annapurna Labs makes for a more interesting parallel than Mellanox, however, as the latter formed the basis of Amazon’s custom chip-designing unit following its 2015 acquisition. Add Intel into the mix, and this becomes a broader story. “Most of the hardware powering the AI wave was built in Israel. Annapurna; Mellanox; Habana Labs; etc…,” VC Eric Reiner observed on X a few months ago.
In an email to TechCrunch, Eze Vidra, co-founder and managing partner at Remagine Ventures, said the deal is “a strong signal for the Israeli deep-tech ecosystem, showing that specialized local talent continues to attract major global players.”
Amazon still has a ways to go before it can make a dent in Nvidia’s near-monopoly on AI chips, but the deal could help the e-commerce giant speed up its efforts. Dean Meyer, a partner at Sequoia who co-led the firm’s seed investment into Decart, said on X that the deal “will be looked back on as one of the most strategically important acquisitions in many, many years.”

articles.title: El Gobierno prorroga las ayudas al transporte público durante 2027: 1.213 millones para mantener los descuentos en tren y autobús
articles.text:
El Gobierno ha prorrogado las subvenciones al transporte público hasta 2027, y lo ha hecho de ultimísimas. El Consejo de Ministros ha aprobado este martes un real decreto-ley, manteniendo vigentes los descuentos en metros, autobuses y trenes, así como el Abono Único, que iban a caducar el próximo 31 de diciembre. El Estado aportará 1.213 millones de euros.
Prórroga. Es una medida que afecta a millones de personas que dependen de abonos con descuento para su desplazamiento diario. Además, ha estado a punto de no entrar en vigor. Y es que tal y como cuentan desde El País, el Ministerio de Economía, que ha estado dirigiendo Transportes de forma interina desde la dimisión de Óscar Puente, prefería esperar hasta después de las elecciones para decidir. Pero claro, eso habría dejado los descuentos en el limbo durante meses.
Qué sigue igual. La mayoría de los descuentos actuales se mantienen:
- Ferrocarril: abono mensual de Cercanías y Rodalies a 20 euros (10 euros para jóvenes, gratuito para menores de 14 años). Media Distancia mantiene un descuento del 40 %, con una rebaja adicional para jóvenes. Las líneas Avant bajo obligación de servicio público mantienen un descuento del 50 %. El Estado aportará 211 millones de euros.
- Autobuses estatales: abonos gratuitos para niños, 40 % de descuento en billetes de diez viajes y en abonos mensuales y 70 % de descuento para jóvenes. El presupuesto es de 100 millones de euros.
- Abono Único: 60 euros al mes para Cercanías, Rodalies, autobuses estatales, Media Distancia y líneas Avant bajo obligación de servicio público.
Qué cambia. Hay una novedad, pues en el segundo semestre de 2027, el Consejo de Ministros podrá recortar la parte estatal del descuento general del 20 % hasta en 10 puntos, en función de una evaluación de la Autoridad Independiente de Responsabilidad Fiscal (AIReF). En la práctica, el descuento podría reducirse a mitad de año.
El País señala que los gobiernos autonómicos pueden añadir otro 20 % adicional, por lo que lo que paguen los viajeros también dependerá de su comunidad autónoma.
Dinero para comunidades autónomas e islas. El Estado transferirá 470 millones de euros a los gobiernos autonómicos y 240 millones de euros a las entidades locales para financiar su parte, desde abonos gratuitos para niños, hasta el 50 % de descuento en títulos multiviaje para jóvenes y 20 % de descuento en otros abonos.
Canarias y Baleares mantienen un descuento del 100 % en los abonos de transporte terrestre, con 120 millones de euros y 63 millones de euros asignados respectivamente. Asturias y Cantabria mantienen el ferrocarril gratuito para usuarios habituales hasta que lleguen los nuevos trenes de ancho métrico, a un coste de 5,6 millones de euros y 3,1 millones de euros.
Más allá del transporte urbano. El decreto también añade 721 millones de euros en ayudas para residentes en territorios no peninsulares, desde 589 millones de euros para vuelos, a 91 millones de euros para viajes marítimos y 40 millones de euros para mercancías. Por separado, el Gobierno ha aprobado también avales estatales de hasta 1.000 millones de euros, disponibles hasta 2029, para ayudar a los navieros a construir, comprar o transformar buques como parte de la descarbonización de la flota mercante.
Qué viene a continuación. Dos cosas a vigilar. Primero, la evaluación de la AIReF, que decidirá si se recorta la aportación estatal en el segundo semestre de 2027. Segundo, el contexto político, pues con el Gobierno abocado a estar en funciones tras las elecciones, este decreto asegura al menos un año para los viajeros.

articles.title: El gran fraude de la canela: Bruselas dice que dos tercios de la que se comercializa en Europa tiene problemas
articles.text:
La canela fue la quinta especia más importada por la UE en 2023. También ha sufrido un control de laboratorio. Los laboratorios de Europa han puesto a prueba a esta especia. El Centro Común de Investigación (JRC) ha analizado 104 productos de venta. De ellos, un 66,3 % tenían algún problema.
Entre ellos se detectaron problemas de calidad o incumplimientos de seguridad alimentaria. En algunos se sospechaba de fraude y en otros había un posible riesgo asociado a su contenido en cumarina. Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que dos tercios de la canela que se comercializa en Europa tenga estos problemas.
Los problemas pueden ser muy diversos. Desde los que implican un incumplimiento de los estándares internacionales de calidad hasta posibles sospechas de adulteración o dudas en cuanto a la seguridad alimentaria. Esto último no implica que haya un fraude demostrado o que sean necesariamente peligrosos para el consumidor.
Ya se habían dado casos preocupantes. En el año 2021 se publicó un informe europeo donde se detectaron indicios de adulteración en algunas especias. Así ocurrió con pimienta, comino, cúrcuma, azafrán o pimentón. En el caso de la canela, la Comisión ha hecho públicos los resultados el 24 de septiembre de 2025. Las muestras fueron adquiridas en 10 países de la UE.
Lo que decía la etiqueta y lo que había dentro
Entre los problemas destacan los casos con exceso de plomo. Otro caso es el de muestras con altos niveles de cumarina. Se trata de un componente natural de la canela cassia, algo que puede llegar a ser tóxico para el hígado. En la legislación europea se regula el máximo admisible de cumarina en ciertos productos elaborados, pero no hay un valor concreto para la que viene de forma natural en la canela. El estudio apunta a posibles riesgos asociados al consumo. En especial para niños.
Por otro lado, también se encontraron discrepancias entre las declaraciones de la etiqueta y el propio producto. Alrededor del 9 % de las muestras que se anunciaban como canela de Ceilán tenían cassia (total o parcialmente). Se trata de una variedad más barata y con un sabor más fuerte. Es decir, se puede estar comprando una cosa y en realidad tener otra diferente (sin saberlo).
Para detectar este tipo de sustituciones (y otros problemas) es necesaria más que una sola técnica analítica. El JRC avisa de que es necesario disponer de métodos estandarizados en los laboratorios de control. La Comisión hace un llamamiento a los responsables políticos y fabricantes. Es necesario asegurar que la especia es auténtica (y cumple con la legislación en materia de seguridad alimentaria) y de calidad.

articles.title: Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
articles.text:
Tiny flaws in diamonds could unlock a quantum computing revolution
By treating qubits like individual molecules, scientists can now predict their behavior faster and more accurately
- Date:
  November 13, 2026
- Source:
  Princeton University
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a faster way to identify diamond-based materials that could power quantum computers and sensors at room temperature. The breakthrough has already revealed promising new quantum building blocks that could help unlock computing capabilities far beyond those of today's supercomputers.
- Share:
A new computational technique could accelerate the search for diamond materials capable of powering future quantum computers and highly sensitive sensors. Developed by a researcher at the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory (PPPL), the method makes it much easier to identify promising materials for quantum technology, potentially opening the door to advances across many areas of science.
The approach has already revealed new candidates for quantum computing and sensing applications. The findings were recently published in ACS Central Science and have attracted attention from other researchers in the field.
One of the biggest challenges in developing quantum technology is finding materials that can maintain delicate quantum states under practical conditions. Many candidates require extremely low temperatures to function reliably. Diamond materials stand out because certain quantum properties can remain useful even at room temperature.
This capability could help advance technologies that are important to national research priorities and the development of next-generation computing. Quantum sensors promise levels of sensitivity and precision beyond those of conventional instruments, while quantum computers could eventually solve certain extraordinarily complex problems much faster than today's most powerful supercomputers.
Why Imperfect Diamonds Could Be the Key to Quantum Computing
Although diamonds are made of carbon atoms, a flawless diamond crystal is not enough to create a useful quantum computing system. The key lies in tiny irregularities within the crystal structure.
These imperfections, known as defects, can occur when a carbon atom is absent from its normal position, when another element replaces a carbon atom, or when both changes occur together. The atoms surrounding these defects can form qubits, the basic units used to store and process quantum information in quantum computers and sensors.
Finding the most useful defects, however, has been difficult. Accurately modeling their quantum behavior traditionally requires enormous computational resources, making it challenging to evaluate large numbers of possible candidates.
A Simpler Way to Discover Better Diamond Qubits
Mark Martirez, a staff research scientist at PPPL, developed a way to dramatically reduce the complexity of these calculations. Instead of simulating a much larger diamond structure, he isolates a small region containing just 16 to 30 atoms around a defect.
By "carving out" this tiny atomic cluster and treating it like a separate molecule, Martirez can use powerful computational methods that chemists have spent decades refining. These established techniques make it possible to analyze the quantum properties of diamond defects much more efficiently without sacrificing the high level of accuracy needed for the calculations.
"Because we're treating the qubits as molecules, the cost of calculating these defects is equivalent to the cost of just modeling a simple molecule," Martirez said. "This method really opened the floodgates" in terms of how qubits can be assessed.
The new technique allows researchers to calculate how different qubits respond to laser light and microwave pulses far more quickly than before. Using this approach, the team identified promising defects involving boron and oxygen that could serve as new types of qubits.
New Diamond Defects Reveal a Spectrum of Quantum Colors
Light plays an important role in how scientists interact with diamond qubits. Researchers use lasers and microwave pulses to manipulate their quantum states and retrieve stored information.
Much of the previous work in this area has centered on a defect known as the nitrogen-vacancy center. This structure forms when a nitrogen atom takes the place of a carbon atom in a diamond crystal, while an adjacent position that would normally contain another carbon atom remains empty.
Under laser illumination, this type of defect can emit red light when it occupies a particular quantum state.
The newly investigated defects offer different optical properties. Oxygen defects can produce blue light, while those involving boron emit ultraviolet light.
These differences could make it possible to combine several types of qubits within a single quantum device. Because each type responds differently to light, researchers might be able to interact with one group of qubits without disturbing another.
"One could imagine, then, combining different qubits of different responses, so you can basically probe one qubit but not the other," Martirez said.
Beyond identifying new candidates, the findings suggest a broader change in how researchers approach quantum technology. Diamond qubits have traditionally been studied primarily through physics, but understanding their underlying chemistry could provide additional ways to design them.
Martirez believes that researchers could eventually engineer qubits for particular functions using principles similar to those applied when chemists create specialized molecules, including compounds designed for new medications.
How Quantum Chemistry Could Transform Future Research
The potential benefits extend well beyond the development of quantum computers themselves. Martirez sees an intriguing possibility in which advances made possible by quantum chemistry eventually lead to quantum technologies that help improve the field of chemistry.
In other words, quantum chemistry could develop the very tools needed to "enrich itself" in the coming decades.
A practical quantum system containing multiple qubits could make molecular calculations substantially more accurate. That would allow scientists to study increasingly complex chemical structures, including large biological molecules and proteins, with a level of detail that is difficult to achieve using conventional methods.
"We could describe larger molecules, biomolecules, proteins and everything like that in a more accurate way, and that could improve all the chemical-adjacent industries, such as pharmaceutical science and materials science. Even our fundamental understanding of molecular systems could be enriched."
Such improvements could have far-reaching implications for pharmaceutical development, materials research, and the fundamental study of how molecules behave.
Martirez also hopes the research will encourage more chemists to explore solid-state physics. Although building advanced quantum computers is often viewed as a challenge primarily for physicists, he argues that chemistry offers valuable expertise that could help accelerate progress.
"At this moment in time, there's a great emphasis on building the first state-of-the-art qubit computer," he said. "But it's not just physicists who should be participating in this research. Chemists have decades of developed intuition about chemical systems that could be easily translated into understanding defects in solids as well."
By bringing these disciplines together, scientists may be able to develop more effective ways to discover, understand, and eventually engineer the quantum materials needed for future technologies.
The research was funded through PPPL's Laboratory Directed Research and Development program under prime contract number DE-AC02-09CH11466, with additional support from the DOE Office of Science, Office of Fusion Energy Sciences.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Princeton University. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- John Mark P. Martirez. A Chemist’sGuide to Solid-State Qubits: DiamondColor Centers as Embedded Vacancy-Centered Molecules. ACS Central Science, 2026; 12 (10): 1578 DOI: 10.1021/acscentsci.6c00548

articles.title: Amsterdam’s Good Heat raises €2 million to replace industrial gas-fired steam boilers with heat batteries
articles.text:
Good Heat, an Amsterdam-based startup that delivers zero-carbon heat as a service to industrial heat users, has raised €2 million to support its growing project pipeline.
The round is led by SET Ventures, Europe’s leading energy VC, with participation from Shell Ventures and existing investor Investible. In October 2025, the company announced €1.83 million ($2 million) in pre-Seed funding backed by Understorey Ventures, Investible, 2100VC, and Foobar VC.
“Industrial heat is an enormous market: a fifth of all the energy the world uses, and almost 90% of it still comes from fossil fuels. The cost of that dependence is obvious at every site we see. We have built a pipeline across two continents, and this financing lets us scale the team to deliver it. Our message to industry: take the heat, leave the project to us,” said Bauke van Gent, Founder and CEO, Good Heat.
Founded in 2025 by Bauke van Gent and Tom Geiser, Good Heat is a developer and platform for clean industrial heat. Batteries that store electricity have helped transform power grids. Good Heat expects heat batteries could play a similarly important role, charging with cheap renewable power and delivering heat when needed.
It argues this could be particularly useful for industries and factories that need significant heat for everything from frying potato chips to producing chemicals. European industry faces crippling gas bills and needs to diversify its energy supply to avoid energy disruptions
The Dutch startup replaces gas-fired steam boilers at industrial sites with heat batteries—advanced thermal energy storage systems powered by electricity. It claims to develop, finance, own, and operate each system, selling steam at a stable price with no upfront investment for the customer.
Since its launch over a year ago, Good Heat reports building a pipeline of more than 100 MWt across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, and Poland, supported by structured partnerships with leading energy companies that deliver leads each year, alongside Good Heat’s own origination. The same model is already driving multiple site developments.
In Australia, the company is developing Project Arcadia, a 200MWh eTES (electrified thermal energy storage) project for a food company in Victoria. The eTES system will be charged with renewable electricity, converting it to and storing it as high-temperature heat, released on-demand (24/7) as hot steam into the factory. The company says this is the largest electric thermal storage project under development in Australia and expects to reach financial close in 2027. It has an active pipeline of prospective projects totalling more than 75 MWt. It has an office in Sydney.
It also highlighted that the projects are backed by long-term offtake agreements and hedged energy supply agreements, helping provide the predictable, inflation-protected cash flows infrastructure investors seek. A growing portfolio lowers the cost of capital for each new project while supporting technology validation.
It notes that the company is technology-neutral and selects the thermal energy storage technology best suited to each site’s requirements through a competitive procurement process.
“Industrial heat isn’t held back by technology, it’s held back by the complexity of delivering and financing the projects. We’ve seen this play out in wind and solar: once independent developers took over, the market scaled. Our research into industrial process heat pointed to exactly this model, and Bauke and Tom have the track record to build it. Good Heat is our first investment in the sector, and we’re excited to lead this round,” said Anton Arts, Managing Partner at SET Ventures.

articles.title: European Commission Uncovers Data Breach in Cyberattack Investigation
articles.text:
The European Commission (EC) on Monday confirmed that a recently disclosed AI-assisted cyberattack resulted in the compromise of personal information.
The attack, disclosed last week, prompted the temporary shutdown of several applications. At the time, the organization said it had found no evidence that personal information belonging to Commission staff had been compromised.
Spokesperson Thomas Regnier revealed during a press briefing on Monday that the investigation has since uncovered a data breach affecting EU Academy, an online learning platform used by people outside the EC to take courses and learn about European Union policies.
Compromised information includes names and email addresses of EU Academy users, but the full extent of the breach is still being investigated.
Access to EU Academy has been suspended during the investigation and the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) has been notified. Potentially affected individuals have not been informed directly.
“Important to keep in mind at this point in time that the exact scale of the data leak is still subject to the investigation, so there was no reach-out to individual users, but rather a general message to all users on the website out of transparency,” Regnier explained.
The cyberattack was detected on October 22 and the EC said last week that it had largely been contained. The spokesperson declined to comment on Monday on whether the incident was over, and said attribution could only be made once the investigation is concluded.
Euronews reported that the Commission suspects a China-backed threat group. According to the publication, the attack has yet to be fully contained.
The EC said the intrusion involved AI, but it did not publicly identify the tool leveraged by the hackers. According to Euronews, the suspected China link is based partly on the use of Artex, an AI-powered penetration testing framework with Chinese roots that has been widely used by threat actors.

articles.title: Prepare Market Data for Forecasting with NVIDIA Megatron Core
articles.text:
Market data arrives as a stream of trades and quotes: every execution, bid, and ask, timestamped to the microsecond. Preparing this data for AI-based market forecasting requires turning price and volume histories into consistent inputs for model training and inference. A common first step is aggregating the data into bars—one row per instrument per time unit—with price, volume, and other statistics. Neural networks can learn patterns from these histories across instruments and forecast horizons.
NVIDIA Megatron Core is an open-source library of GPU-optimized components for training transformer models at scale. Megatron-LM is a GitHub repository that combines that library with preconfigured training scripts. A preprocessing script turns intraday market bars into model-ready tensors, and a dataset provider feeds them into Megatron’s distributed training loop.
This post shows how to preprocess market-bar data and train a model with Megatron-LM to forecast returns and trading volume across multiple horizons.
Forecast returns and trading volume
Price and volume remain continuous features. A learned patch embedding turns each group of observations into a model input without converting market values into text.
A common data interface supports training a shared forecasting model on histories from many instruments. Each training window belongs to one instrument and includes its identifier, so the model can learn instrument-specific behavior within shared parameters. You can also explore longer contexts, different sampling frequencies, and additional features through the same interface.
The example forecasts returns and trading volume at several horizons from the same context. Quantitative researchers can use these outputs to study short-term market behavior, trading activity, or execution timing. Point and interval forecasts address different research questions while using the same input representation.
You can change the model architecture, optimizer, or training duration while reusing a prepared dataset. Preprocessing records the patch size, context length, and forecast horizons in the saved metadata, making the data configuration an explicit part of each experiment.
A consistent representation also separates the source feed from the model. Data from a new vendor or sampling scheme can follow the same row schema, while the dataset provider supplies the same batch fields. Figure 1 shows the pipeline from market bars to training.
From price and volume to model-ready sequences
The input is a directory of Parquet files with one row per bar and Symbol, Date, Timestamp, Close, and Volume columns, plus optional numeric feature columns. Bars can come from different vendors and sampling schemes, such as one-minute or sub-minute aggregates of tick data. Keep each instrument’s trading day in one file and the files in chronological order. The script sorts each instrument’s daily observations by timestamp. The script derives within-day log returns and log volumes itself, so the overnight gap never enters the inputs. The preprocessor treats rows as observation steps and leaves gaps unchanged. Align the data upstream if you need a regular time grid.
preprocessing.py groups consecutive bars for one instrument on one trading day into patches—the model’s tokens—and slides fixed-length context windows over them.
Each patch retains the features of its constituent rows. For example, eight bars per patch and 32 patches per window provide 256 observations in a sequence of 32 model positions. An instrument ID identifies the series, and each patch carries its position within the trading day (Figure 2).
Run preprocessing and training
Before running the example, see the preprocessing README for environment setup, input-file requirements, configuration options, and output tensor formats.
First, preprocess the market bars into training-ready tensors:
python examples/financial_timeseries/preprocessing.py \
    --data-dir /data/bars --out-dir /data/tensors \
    --patch-len 8 --context-len 32 --window-stride 16 \
    --time-units-per-day 390 --horizons 1,2,5,15 \
    --target-mode cumulative --no-allow-overnight-targets
Then, run the Megatron training example with the saved tensors:
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 -m examples.financial_timeseries.pretrain_ts \
    --ts-data-path /data/tensors --dataloader-type cyclic \
    --num-layers 4 --hidden-size 256 --num-attention-heads 4 \
    --seq-length 32 --max-position-embeddings 32 \
    --micro-batch-size 64 --global-batch-size 256 --train-iters 2000 \
    --lr 3e-4 --min-lr 3e-5 --lr-decay-style cosine --lr-warmup-iters 100 \
    --tokenizer-type NullTokenizer --bf16 \
    --log-interval 50 --eval-interval 500 --eval-iters 20 \
    --save /data/ckpt --save-interval 2000
This small model shows the expected input and output formats. Use it to check that preprocessing, the data loader, target masking, and loss computation work together before substituting your forecasting architecture.
You can replace this model while keeping the data layer unchanged. forward_step calls the model with patches (B, L, P, F), inst_id (B,), and patch_tod (B, L). loss_func expects a dictionary with return and volshare tensors of shape (B, L, H), with one forecast per context position and horizon. Any MegatronModule that takes those three inputs and returns that dictionary can replace it.
Defining forecast targets
Each window includes future targets for every context position, so one forward pass produces forecasts throughout the context rather than only at the end. A causal forecasting model uses only the history available at each position.
Forecast horizons can be defined in observation steps or patches. A point target uses the return and volume at a future step; a cumulative target uses the summed log return and total volume over the interval. Volume targets are represented on a log scale. Figure 3 shows both target definitions for the same context.
For regular one-minute bars, a horizon of five observation steps corresponds to five minutes. For event-based data, it counts events.
Efficient data loading for distributed training
The data pipeline consists of two stages: preprocessing and data loading. Preprocessing builds the features, patches, windows, and targets offline, then writes them as PyTorch tensor files: train.pt, val.pt, test.pt, and meta.pt. Training reads these saved tensors, keeping Parquet parsing and target construction outside the training loop.
Prepare once, reuse across runs
During preprocessing, the script handles files in order and uses array operations for regular bar layouts, with a per-instrument path for irregular observations. It computes each instrument’s target sequence once and reuses it across overlapping windows. Temporary memory-mapped arrays hold the completed split tensors before they are saved to disk.
The saved metadata records instrument mappings, feature names, patch and context lengths, forecast horizons, and normalization statistics. Model and dataset settings can be checked against the same description before training.
Map tensors and share batches
The data loader reads the saved splits and supplies batches for training or inference. Validation checks that required keys are present, sample counts align, and the stored context length matches the model. Each worker opens the saved file lazily through memory mapping; fetching a sample copies only its selected rows into private memory.
Within each tensor-parallel group, rank zero reads the microbatch and broadcasts it to the other ranks. Megatron’s sampler handles data-parallel sampling and can reshuffle and cycle through the saved windows for the requested number of training iterations. This connects the market-data interface to the training loop, parallelism, and checkpointing used by the forecasting model.
Preserving time in financial modeling
The outputs are split by date into training, validation, and test sets. A window is retained only when its entire context and future observations needed for the longest forecast horizon fall within the same split. This keeps validation or test observations from entering training windows or training targets.
An embargo removes trading days from the end of the training period before validation begins; validation and test are adjacent. The script also checks that the context patches used by different splits do not overlap. These safeguards address cross-split leakage that could introduce forward-looking bias.
Per-horizon target statistics are computed from the training split only. If you standardize targets, use these statistics during training, validation, and testing. Future evaluation data therefore does not determine the target scaling applied in training. The example trainer leaves targets unscaled.
Session boundaries are configurable. Input log returns reset at the start of each day. For cumulative forecasts, targets can include the overnight move; intraday-only targets instead mask horizons that cross the close. A separate setting keeps the input context within one trading day when that matches the task. The loader reconstructs valid-target masks from the saved values, so the loss can exclude unavailable targets.
These settings make the forecasting question explicit: which history is visible, how far ahead the target reaches, and whether the model is predicting within a session or across sessions.
Getting started
Use the preprocessing script and Megatron dataset provider with your own market-bar Parquet files. The input schema, tensor formats, and configuration options are documented in the preprocessing README, alongside a training example that connects the data interface to a forecasting model.
Choose the sampling frequency, context length, and forecast horizons that match your research question. Prepare the dataset, check its metadata and split counts, and use the saved tensors in a Megatron training run. Then experiment with other instruments, feature sets, and model configurations.

articles.title: How Canada’s Pharmacy Shift Prepared MedMe for the US Market
articles.text:
When Canadians talk about healthcare access, the conversation often centres on finding a family doctor. But for many of us, a pharmacy is closer to home, making it one of the most convenient places to get expert advice and treatment.
According to Purya Sarmadi, CEO and co-founder of MedMe Health, 90 percent of North Americans live within about five miles (eight kilometres) of a neighbourhood drugstore. He sees an opportunity to use that access better as provinces expand pharmacists’ responsibilities, from treating common infections to helping patients manage chronic conditions like diabetes and asthma.
“We invest in this because the distance between installing software and delivering care is where most clinical programs stall.”
Purya Sarmadi, MedMe
His company provides an AI-enabled platform for connecting the whole patient journey, from booking and intake to clinical documentation and billing. Since 2019, the Toronto-based digital health startup has grown to serve over 40 percent of the Canadian pharmacy market, supporting more than 30 million patient interactions, according to the company.
MedMe is now bringing that experience to the US, where pharmacies are beginning to take on the clinical role that their Canadian counterparts have been developing, albeit with the added challenge of navigating a more complicated payment system.
“We have shown in Canada what pharmacists can do once they are authorized, paid, and equipped to practice to their full scope, and we intend to make that the standard for pharmacy practice everywhere,” Sarmadi told BetaKit.
Canada’s head start
MedMe deliberately chose Canada as a place to develop its platform alongside pharmacies already putting new models of care into practice.
“Canadian provinces expanded pharmacists’ scope of practice and began paying pharmacies for clinical services years before most US states,” said Sarmadi.
By 2020, the pandemic was bringing more patients into pharmacies for vaccinations and testing, broadening their view of what pharmacists could offer, he added. As demand grew, the number of locations using MedMe rose from about 100 to nearly 1,200 in ten weeks, according to the company.
Working with those businesses revealed two recurring problems, said Sarmadi. Patients didn’t always know what was available at their local pharmacy, leaving appointment slots unfilled, while manual intake systems, phone scheduling, and documentation completed after hours made consultations time-consuming and costly to deliver.
Among its solutions, MedMe introduced Patient Concierge, an AI agent that answers the phone and contacts patients to coordinate refills or schedule deliveries. Its Clinical Assistant drafts consultation notes for pharmacists to review and sign. One Calgary pharmacist puts the cost at about 18 cents a consult, the company says.
But introducing clinical programs also changed how the whole store operated, from staffing and training to measuring returns, Sarmadi said. It meant MedMe’s approach had to go beyond technology. The company built READY, an implementation framework that involves pharmacists and managers in designing routines that fit appointments around dispensing, trains staff one-on-one during launch, and monitors adoption. Locations go live only when their teams are prepared.
“We invest in this because the distance between installing software and delivering care is where most clinical programs stall,” said Sarmadi.
He points to Nova Scotia as an example of how technology can support a larger clinical role for pharmacies. Since 2023, the province has funded a network of Community Pharmacy Primary Care Clinics, which is credited with a decline of close to 10 percent in emergency room visits for non-urgent and less urgent cases.
The Pharmacy Association of Nova Scotia selected MedMe to build and run the booking platform for all 44 clinics, giving patients a direct way to arrange a visit as pharmacies become an established part of the province’s primary care network. The province’s 811 health advice line also directs callers there when it’s the right setting for their care.
That experience gives MedMe a model to draw on as US states invest in community pharmacies to improve access to care in rural areas.
Taking the experience south
MedMe is drawing on its Canadian experience to support its US rollout; it’s now live in more than 350 US pharmacies, with further launches planned through 2027. Critically, they bring an understanding of the correct sequence of steps needed to make clinical care viable.
“Scope expands first, billing pathways follow, and then comes the operational work of building patient demand, delivering care efficiently, changing how the pharmacy runs and, fundamentally, what it is for,” explained Sarmadi. “We entered the US having already built for each of those stages.”
The company also brought its Canadian-built online booking and patient outreach tools, along with experience helping teams adapt to new ways of working. Sarmadi likens that shift to a large company adopting a new customer relationship management system, which requires rethinking roles, processes, and reporting, rather than simply installing software.
“The point is to get the pharmacist in front of the patient at exactly the right moment, and far more often than happens today.”
Purya Sarmadi, MedMe
“Every rollout we run in the US therefore covers the whole operation,” he said.
Unlike Canada’s provincially funded programs with set fees, however, American pharmacies face multiple payers with different coverage and billing requirements. Rejected or denied claims can leave staff chasing payments, making expanding clinical roles more challenging. MedMe’s platform is designed to handle rejection and denial management on its customers’ behalf.
At Pucci’s Pharmacy in Sacramento, Calif., for instance, the owner previously relied on four separate systems for scheduling and intake, documentation, dispensing, and outside billing. He and his clinical pharmacist spent days calling health plans, while some denied claims went unpursued, according to Sarmadi.
Since moving onto MedMe in September 2025, the store has logged about 2,700 clinical appointments. It now handles around 300 a month, up from 140 last winter, and 41 percent of patients book online themselves.
Processing claims across multiple businesses also gives MedMe insight into which payers deny particular treatments, and why. The company incorporates those findings into billing rules and automation used across its platform, reducing the need for each customer to learn through its own trial and error.
Future of pharmacy care
Sarmadi sees a future where pharmacy care continues between appointments. Pharmacists would have access to patients’ medication histories and readings from home monitors, while AI would help coordinate follow-up and routine outreach. If blood pressure readings change or a refill goes uncollected, for example, the team could reach out rather than wait for the patient’s next visit.
“What AI shouldn’t do is make the clinical call,” he said. “The point is to get the pharmacist in front of the patient at exactly the right moment, and far more often than happens today.”
Aaron Bast, managing director at Graphite Ventures, which has invested in MedMe, sees the company’s Canadian roots as a key strength as it pursues its global ambitions.
“MedMe is exactly what we mean by Scale Canadian,” he said. “Purya and the team built where pharmacy care was changing first, earned the trust of Canada’s pharmacies, and are now bringing a proven playbook to a much larger market. Canadian companies don’t have to leave to win globally. They can take what they’ve built in Canada as a model for international success.”
PRESENTED BY
Check out Scale Canadian for more stories of those building in Canada and scaling globally.
Feature image courtesy MedMe.

articles.title: South Korean power giant confirms data breach - KEPCO says incident affected 1.5 million people
articles.text:
South Korean power giant confirms data breach - KEPCO says incident affected 1.5 million people
Two KEPCO services were compromised
- South Korea’s state-owned utility KEPCO discloses breach affecting roughly 1.5 million customers, employees, and partners
- Stolen data included personal identifiers, contact information, banking details, billing records, and employee information
- The company contained the intrusion, notified authorities, and warned affected individuals to watch for phishing and fraud
Roughly 1.5 million people have had their sensitive data exposed when threat actors broke into Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO) and accessed two of its systems. The company confirmed the news in a breach notification issued and signed by the company’s president, Kim Dong-cheol.
In the data breach notice, KEPCO said that it spotted the attack on November 20 and soon after determined that “some customer information stored in its IT systems” had been leaked.
Two services were exposed: KEPCO ON, an integrated customer service platform used for things like bill inquiries and payments, and the company’s electronic procurement system (SRM) which handles purchases, construction projects, and similar. KEPCO ON exposed primarily electricity customers, while SRM did the same for system users, the notice further states.
Two services, 1.5 million victims
“Upon becoming aware of the incident, KEPCO immediately blocked access from external IP addresses and suspended the affected services,” it said in the machine-translated announcement. “It also conducted a thorough assessment of the relevant IT systems and promptly implemented the necessary measures.”
In total, data on 1.5 million people was nabbed: 650,000 KEPCO ON customers, 420,000 SRM customers, and 442,000 KEPCO and partner company employees.
KEPCO is South Korea’s state-owned electricity utility and the country’s largest power company. It generates almost all of the country’s electricity and manages virtually all distribution. Last year it had approximately 22,670 employees and served more than 25 million customers, including households, businesses, and industries.
The South Korean energy powerhouse split the KEPCO ON leaked information into 12 categories: electricity customer numbers, names, unique identification information (resident registration numbers or foreign resident registration numbers), telephone numbers, addresses, bank names, account numbers, account holder names, credit card issuers, card numbers, cardholder names, and electricity billing and payment information.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
For SMR, company representatives lost names, unique identification information (resident registration numbers or foreign resident registration numbers), email addresses, and company addresses.
For KEPCO employees and partner company employees, the attackers stole names, affiliations, employee identification numbers, mobile phone numbers, email addresses, and company telephone numbers.
Asian critical infrastructure in the crosshairs
As soon as it spotted the intrusion, the company said it launched an investigation, set up a dedicated channel to communicate directly with affected individuals, and reported the incident to the authorities. It also warned its customers to be wary of incoming emails and other forms of communications and told them to expect an influx of scam messages.
"We take this incident very seriously and sincerely apologize to the public for the concern and distress we have caused,” said KEPCO President Kim Dong-cheol. "We will thoroughly investigate the cause of the information leak and fundamentally improve our information security framework."
The company did not say who broke into its systems, or how. However, BleepingComputer found a new thread on a dark web forum, from a threat actor claiming to be behind the breach. The actor is going by the name “Noiem” and, in a thread posted on November 19, said they grabbed KEPCO user data, supplier records, and bidding and contract documents. The data has not yet been analyzed by independent researchers, so it is not yet known if the claims are legitimate or not.
Asian countries, specifically Japan and South Korea, experienced a series of cyberattacks against critical infrastructure organizations, as well as key enterprises. In April 2025, SK Telecom, the country's largest mobile operator, disclosed a major breach involving BPFDoor malware, which resulted in the exposure of approximately 26.96 million records containing sensitive SIM-related information. KT, another major telecommunications provider, suffered a similar fate, affecting more than 16,600 customers and resulting in fraudulent transactions.
