articles.title: Homo erectus lived in the rainforest alongside Denisovans
articles.text:
This artist's illustration shows one take on what Homo erectus might have looked like in its rainforest home near Baxian Cave, Guangxi, China.
Credit:
Garciart/Joannes-Boyau
This artist's illustration shows one take on what Homo erectus might have looked like in its rainforest home near Baxian Cave, Guangxi, China.
Credit:
Garciart/Joannes-Boyau
Homo erectus was walking around mainland Asia at least 60,000 years more recently than archaeologists thought. A handful of teeth from two caves in southern China’s Guangxi Province just filled in a significant gap in the fossil record of a region that’s vital to the story of how our genus, Homo, took over the world.
The chemical makeup of the teeth’s enamel suggests that, over the course of their lives, these Homo erectus moved across surprisingly large distances and made their living in dense tropical rainforests—an environment we’d previously assumed that only our species had ever gained a real foothold in. And one of the teeth offers a strong clue that Homo erectus probably shared this vast landscape with the Denisovans.
A handful of teeth with a lot to say
Baxian and Naxian are a pair of limestone caves that lie 15 kilometers apart along a karst valley corridor in southern China. University of Copenhagen paleoanthropologist Frido Welker and his colleagues unearthed a total of nine hominin teeth from among the more than 18,000 bones and fragments from non-hominin animals found there. Macquarie University paleoanthropologist Kira Westaway and her colleagues analyzed proteins and chemical isotopes from the enamel of five of these teeth.
Proteins in teeth are sturdier than DNA, so they’re more likely to survive a few hundred thousand years. But like DNA, proteins contain variations that can help identify the species they came from. Four of the five teeth in the study had distinctly Homo erectus proteins in their enamel; the fifth seems to be some other hominin species, most likely a Denisovan (more on that below).
The hominin teeth and the thousands of animal bone fragments had accumulated in a cement-like rock called breccia. Based on luminescence dating (a method that measures how long it’s been since mineral grains were last exposed to sunlight) of the cave sediments, along with the ratios of uranium isotopes in the bones themselves, it looks like that breccia formed sometime between 324,000 and 184,000 years ago. That’s a wide range, but it’s enough to show that Homo erectus lived in what’s now southern China at least 60,000 years longer than we’ve previously realized.
Homo erectus emerged in Africa sometime before 2 million years ago, and they had reached East and Southeast Asia—including the islands of Indonesia—by around 1.7 million years ago. The most recent Homo erectus fossils anywhere else in mainland Asia date to somewhere between 420,000 and 400,000 years ago. Fossils from the Indonesian island of Java, however, reveal that Homo erectus held on in the islands up until at least 177,000 to 108,000 years ago. That makes it a little surprising that nobody had found traces of Homo erectus on the mainland during that 200,000- to 300,000-year gap.
These nine teeth help fill in some of that gap, showing that Homo erectus was still around on the mainland all that time after all. On its own, that would be nontrivial, but the teeth also shed light on how these long-dead hominins lived, what the world around them looked like, and how this handful of hominins was related to the rest of their species. And it turns out we’ve been drastically underestimating Homo erectus.
Credit:
Kira Westaway, Macquarie University
Credit:
Kira Westaway, Macquarie University
Homo erectus and Denisovans were neighbors
Four of the five teeth that Welker and his colleagues sequenced proteins from clearly belonged to Homo erectus. Careful measurements of the other four—things like the shape and dimensions of the crown, the roots, and the place where the outer layer of enamel meets the inner layer of dentine—suggest these also belonged to Homo erectus.
But the ninth tooth, from Baxian, has proteins that don’t match any known Homo erectus variants, and the shape also looks decidedly un-Homo–erectus-like, “strongly suggesting the presence of a hominin population other than Homo erectus in Baxian Cave,” wrote Welker and his colleagues in their recent paper in the journal Nature.
But who were those other hominins? The enigmatic ninth tooth looks like it belonged to a Denisovan (or Homo longi, if you prefer). But Welker and his colleagues can’t be absolutely sure, because its proteins don’t exactly match any known Denisovan sequence, either (and there’s no clearly identified Denisovan lower second molar enamel-dentine junction to compare it to). But we do know that Denisovans lived in the wider region of mainland Asia at the time, based on fossils from other sites, and there’s no evidence of any other species running around at the same time.
“It therefore seems plausible that the Homo erectus population represented by the fossils from Naxian and Baxian Cave on the mainland existed in relatively close proximity to Denisovan hominins,” wrote Welker and his colleagues.
Now, to clarify, Naxian and Baxian Caves weren’t (as far as anyone knows) places where hominins actually lived. The bones and teeth there seem to have been carried in by porcupines, with the result that “why do porcupines collect bones?” is now part of your faithful correspondent’s search history [EDITOR’S NOTE: my search history now includes “there are porcupines in China?”]. So the presence of this tooth doesn’t mean that Homo erectus and Denisovans were roommates. But it does mean they were living in the same general area at around the same time; based on the territorial habits of modern porcupines, the teeth probably came from within an area of less than 100 square kilometers. So there’s a nonzero chance that Homo erectus and Denisovans might have interacted in some way, although we have no way to know what that interaction might have looked like.
Not long after this, our species showed up in the area, and we know for a fact that our species interacted, ahem, very closely with Denisovans in this part of the world. Exactly when Homo sapiens arrived is still a matter of some debate, but some fossils from southern China that may be Homo sapiens date as far back as 100,000 or 120,000 years ago, before the major out-of-Africa migration. So for a brief period of time, there may have been at least two and maybe three species of hominins living in the rainforests of what’s now southern China.
Professor Yingqi Zhang looks out the wide entrance of Baxian Cave toward the alluvial plain.
Credit:
Kira Westaway, Macquarie University
Professor Yingqi Zhang looks out the wide entrance of Baxian Cave toward the alluvial plain.
Credit:
Kira Westaway, Macquarie University
Tracing how Homo erectus populations moved around
While the enamel proteins from four of the Baxian and Naxian teeth are clearly Homo erectus, they have a slightly different version of one particular protein—one amino acid swapped for another in the sequence that makes up the protein ameloblastin. This variant is clearly different from every other Asian Homo erectus fossil with proteins that researchers have sequenced. That means they’re probably part of a different genetic population (a group of hominins that live in the same area and mostly interbred among themselves).
There are a handful of other Homo erectus fossils from elsewhere in Asia that share one amino acid substitution with these four, but the Baxian and Naxian ones have another substitution that the other four don’t have, which means that at some point, their population branched off from the others. By plotting that kind of information on what’s called a phylogenetic tree, anthropologists can begin to map out how different groups of Homo erectus are related and how they may have moved around in time and space. And what we’re learning is pretty cool.
“The phylogenetic analysis suggests that, although based on sparse data, this hominin population [at Baxian and Naxian Caves] might have diverged before the divergence of the common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans,” wrote Welker and his colleagues. That divergence happened more than 600,000 years ago. And half a millennium after that, it seems, one group of Homo erectus still living in southern Asia may have met some long-lost cousins.
This map shows the location of the study sites in China.
Credit:
Westaway et al. 2026
This map shows the location of the study sites in China.
Credit:
Westaway et al. 2026
Once again, Homo sapiens isn’t that special
Isotopes of the chemical elements carbon and oxygen in the enamel of not just the Homo erectus teeth, but teeth from several animal species like elephants (both the pygmy Stegodon and the full-size version), rhinos, apes, and relatives of modern cattle, strongly point to the area around Baxian and Naxian Caves having been a densely canopied tropical rainforest during the Middle Pleistocene.
Different types of plants use slightly different chemical processes to do photosynthesis, so they end up with different amounts of the isotopes carbon-12 and carbon-13; the ratios of those isotopes in the teeth of whatever ate the plants (in this case, pygmy elephants and Homo erectus, among others) can reveal the makeup of the local environment. At Baxian and Naxian Caves, those ratios point to a forest where the trees’ upper branches form a thick, closed canopy above the forest floor. Westaway and her colleagues say the signals look very similar to rainforests in the Amazon Basin today.
Meanwhile, the ratio of two oxygen isotopes, oxygen-18 and oxygen-16, can shed light on ancient climate conditions; higher amounts of oxygen-18, like the ones in all five teeth from Baxian and Naxian Caves, tend to signal warmer, wetter climates. All of those clues together point to tropical rainforest, a challenging environment that most anthropologists had previously assumed that only Homo sapiens were clever and adaptable enough to make a living in.
That idea, that we were the only hominins capable of making a go of it in tropical rainforests, was so entrenched that it has been considered a possible explanation for the lack of Homo erectus fossils in southern Asia after about 400,000 years ago. Around this time, the climate became warmer and wetter, allowing dense, closed-canopy tropical rainforests to spread.
“In southeast Asia, recent isotopic observations of […] expansion of rainforest in the Middle to early Late Pleistocene have been associated with the disappearance of non-Homo sapiens hominin taxa, seemingly unable to shift from mixed savanna-woodland habitats to these increasingly closed forests,” wrote Westaway and her colleagues.
Even on Java, where Homo erectus lasted until almost 100,000 years ago, those last groups seem to have lived in small patches of more open woodlands, while rainforests spread across the rest of the islands—another correlation that gives anthropologists reason to think the spread of rainforests may have had a hand in the extinction of Homo erectus.
However, the evidence from Baxian and Naxian Caves suggests Homo erectus could survive in the rainforest, “even if such habitats did not represent its primary ecological niche,” as Westaway and her colleagues put it. That doesn’t mean that every group of Homo erectus was as successful at adapting to spreading rainforests—it’s safe to assume there were cultural and social differences among the groups that might have made some more adaptable than others. But it does mean that we’ve been drastically underestimating our late cousins, and we may need to rethink what we’ve assumed were the limits of their world.
An image of the entrance to Naxian Cave revealing a small opening that stretches back ~50 m to a fossil chamber.
Credit:
Kira Westaway, Macquarie University
An image of the entrance to Naxian Cave revealing a small opening that stretches back ~50 m to a fossil chamber.
Credit:
Kira Westaway, Macquarie University
Well-traveled little hominins
Other evidence in the enamel of the Baxian and Naxian Caves teeth underscores that point, revealing that a few of these Homo erectus individuals spent their childhoods as much as 250 kilometers away from the cave where their teeth ended up. Bedrock in different places has different ratios of the isotopes strontium-87 and strontium-86; plants take up dissolved strontium through their roots, and eventually it replaces some of the calcium in the bones (or tooth enamel) of the animals that eat the plants. So the ratio of strontium isotopes in your bones can be traced to the area of bedrock where your food was grown during the final years of your life, while the ratio in your tooth enamel is a souvenir of the bedrock where your food was grown when you were around 2 to 6 years old and forming your adult teeth. (Modern food systems are going to be a massive headache for future archaeologists.)
All four Homo erectus teeth that Westaway and her colleagues studied suggested that their erstwhile owners had either moved around between different areas or ate food gathered from different areas when they were very young. Some of those strontium ratios match bedrock as far away as northern Vietnam, about 250 kilometers away from Baxian and Naxian Caves, mostly through closed-canopy rainforest.
In other words, a handful of teeth offer enough fragments of a story to show us “that Homo erectus was not ecologically excluded from rainforest environments and that long-distance mobility into those environments may have been a common behavioral pattern rather than exceptional behavior by isolated individuals,” wrote Westaway and her colleagues. “Whether these adaptations were specific to the late-surviving populations in southern China alone remains to be seen, but further stable isotope work on other Middle Pleistocene sites is vital to address this question.”

articles.title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
articles.text:
Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.
GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.
Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.
Some have managed to get the game to boot on PC, but recompiling the full game won’t be easy — even with help from AI tools like Claude. Take-Two is trying to slow this progress, and its IP enforcement team targeted the main GitHub repository for Leonida and more than 2,900 forks of it, claiming that it “infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI.”
PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.
At this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

articles.title: Garmin déploie sa mise à jour de novembre 2026 : voici les nouveautés pour votre montre ou compteur GPS
articles.text:
Les montres Garmin continuent de gagner des fonctions bien après leur achat, et les propriétaires de Fenix ou de Forerunner ont d’ailleurs pris l’habitude de guetter les notes de version. Mi-novembre, ces notes ont surtout fait parler d’elles pour une nouveauté inattendue : un profil pour son chien. Garmin a depuis mis en ligne le récapitulatif de sa mise à jour de novembre 2026.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quelle est la meilleure montre connectée Garmin ? Notre sélection des meilleurs modèles selon votre activité
            
Ce PDF liste les nouvelles fonctions et précise surtout quel modèle reçoit quoi. Le déploiement est gratuit, il a commencé et doit s’étaler sur les prochaines semaines.
Toutes les montres du tableau ont droit aux profils canins, des Venu aux Instinct 3, en passant par les Fenix E, Fenix 8 et Fenix 9, les Enduro 3 et 4 ou la MARQ Gen 3. Il suffit de créer le profil de l’animal dans l’application Garmin Connect, puis de l’associer à ses activités. On peut aussi lancer un type d’activité dédié comme « Run with Dog », qui ajoute le chien automatiquement.
Une carte plus lisible, réservée au haut de gamme
Garmin a aussi redessiné la carte des activités de marche et de course. Elle met désormais en avant les sentiers et les chemins, avec un affichage plus épuré. Par contre, seules la Venu X1, la Forerunner 970 et la gamme Fenix en profitent. La Venu 4, la Vivoactive 6 et les autres Forerunner ne sont pas concernées, logique puisqu’elles ne gèrent pas la cartographie en local.
Garmin Locate, apparue cet été avec la Fenix 9, arrive maintenant sur presque toutes les montres du tableau, sauf les Instinct. Cette fonction partage la dernière position connue de la montre avec des contacts de confiance, choisis dans l’application Garmin Messenger. Sans forfait inReach, l’abonnement satellite de Garmin, la montre doit être connectée en Bluetooth au téléphone : c’est donc le smartphone qui transmet la position.
Côté entraînement, le nouveau plan vélo Garmin Cycling Coach pour débutants arrive sur les Venu X1 et Venu 4, la D2 Air X15, les Forerunner 170 et 570, la famille Fenix et tous les compteurs Edge du tableau. La Vivoactive 6 et les Forerunner 70 et 970 n’y ont pas droit. L’Instinct 3 gagne de son côté un mode de récupération, c’est-à-dire des options affichées à l’écran quand la montre ne répond plus. Les autres montres du tableau avaient déjà cette fonction.
Google Maps arrive enfin sur les compteurs Edge
Les compteurs GPS Edge 540, 840, 1040, 550, 850, 1050, MTB et 1060 peuvent désormais recevoir un point ou un lieu envoyé depuis Google Maps sur un smartphone Android. Le compteur calcule ensuite un itinéraire adapté au vélo. Les possesseurs d’iPhone pouvaient déjà le faire depuis Plans, l’application de cartes d’Apple : les utilisateurs d’Android ne font donc que rattraper leur retard.
Le plan « Challenger » de Garmin Cycling Coach s’adresse quant à lui aux cyclistes débutants et occasionnels, avec des séances basées sur la fréquence cardiaque. D’après les captures publiées par Garmin, ce plan demande trois à quatre jours d’entraînement par semaine et un capteur de fréquence cardiaque, le capteur de puissance restant optionnel. Le plan « Achiever », destiné aux cyclistes confirmés, exige au contraire les deux capteurs et cinq à sept jours par semaine.
    Pour aller plus loin
Quels sont les meilleurs compteurs GPS pour vélo ? Notre sélection
            
Le reste vient du récent Edge 1060 : GroupRide permet de rejoindre une session de groupe à proximité, avec partage de position en direct, messagerie entre cyclistes et défis en montée. Pour ça, il faut un smartphone et l’application Garmin Connect. Les Edge MTB, 550, 850 et 1050 reçoivent aussi Garmin Messenger : avec le smartphone, on peut envoyer des messages depuis le compteur vers d’autres appareils Garmin ou vers des proches qui ont l’application.
Comment récupérer la mise à jour
Garmin conseille d’activer les mises à jour automatiques sur la montre ou le compteur. Le téléchargement se fait alors en arrière-plan, via Garmin Connect. Pour forcer l’installation, allez dans les paramètres de la montre, rubrique Système, puis Mise à jour logicielle. articles.title: Ecologistas quieren soltar en el Pirineo catalán un felino superdepredador extinto desde 1930
articles.text:
En 1930 se cazó el último lince boreal en libertad del que hay constancia en Cataluña, y su piel acabó expuesta en la comarca del Ripollès, tal y como recoge la Fundación para la Conservación del Quebrantahuesos. Casi un siglo después, dos asociaciones ecologistas plantearon en octubre de 2025 devolver este felino al Pirineo catalán con una prueba piloto que todavía está lejos de convertirse en realidad.
Quién lo propone y cómo. La idea parte de Amics del Parc Natural de l’Alt Pirineu y de ADLO Pirineo, que quieren soltar varios machos castrados en el Parque Natural del Alt Pirineu, el espacio protegido más grande de Cataluña. Los animales podrían llegar de Rumanía, cuya población de los Cárpatos se mantiene sin grandes cambios o crece poco a poco, según el balance de la Comisión Europea para 2017-2023. ¿Y por qué castrados? Pues porque, según sus impulsores, así no podrían reproducirse, y el experimento se quedaría en un ensayo controlado para ver qué efecto tiene su presencia en el ecosistema.
Un felino mucho mayor que el ibérico. El lince boreal (Lynx lynx), también llamado euroasiático, es el mayor felino de Europa. También es bastante más corpulento que el lince ibérico, al que WWF presenta como su pariente más pequeño. Puede medir entre 60 y 75 centímetros de altura y pesar hasta 30 kilos, según la ficha de la especie del Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica, y entre sus presas están los corzos y los rebecos y, en ocasiones, los ciervos.
La propuesta ha despertado inquietud en algunos sectores ligados al medio rural y a la gestión de la fauna, que temen que su llegada afecte a las poblaciones de ciertas especies silvestres y altere el equilibrio actual del territorio. Los promotores defienden lo contrario, que su presencia ayudaría a recuperar procesos ecológicos perdidos hace décadas y que, al ser ejemplares estériles, el riesgo sería menor. Vamos, que no podrían crear por su cuenta una población estable. Eso sí, el debate ya va más allá del ensayo, porque la gran pregunta es qué pasaría si algún día se planteara soltar linces fértiles.
La sombra del lince ibérico. Otro de los puntos que generan dudas es la posible relación con el lince ibérico (Lynx pardinus), cuya recuperación ha costado lustros de trabajo y más de 100 millones de euros, según la estrategia de conservación de España y Portugal. De hecho, un estudio liderado por la Estación Biológica de Doñana, del Consejo Superior de Investigaciones Científicas (CSIC), concluyó en enero de 2024 que ambas especies llegaron a cruzarse en el pasado.
Los investigadores analizaron el ADN de linces prehistóricos hallados en Andújar, Alcanar y el Algarve, y vieron que “los linces modernos compartían más material genético con su especie hermana, el lince euroasiático, que los linces más antiguos”, según explicaba María Lucena, primera autora del trabajo, en la nota de prensa de la Estación Biológica. Aquella hibridación pudo ayudar a aumentar la diversidad genética del lince ibérico, pero José Antonio Godoy, coautor del trabajo, advierte en la misma nota de que no se pueden predecir las consecuencias de una futura hibridación, natural o intencionada, en una especie cuya viabilidad genética todavía no está garantizada.
Un camino administrativo largo. En octubre de 2025 la propuesta estaba en una fase muy inicial. Según la misma fundación, el borrador del plan tiene que pasar primero por el parque natural, que lo elevaría a la Generalitat de Cataluña, y el Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico únicamente lo estudiaría si la Generalitat diera su visto bueno. Las asociaciones, por su parte, insistían en que se trataría de una experiencia limitada y sin posibilidad de reproducción.
Pero un año después el planteamiento ha cambiado. El 13 de octubre de 2026, las dos asociaciones y otras cuatro entidades ecologistas pidieron a la Dirección General de Políticas Ambientales y Medio Natural de la Generalitat que recuperara y actualizara el plan de viabilidad para reintroducir el lince boreal anunciado en 2016, que nunca llegó a ejecutarse. En ese comunicado ya no hablan de machos castrados, sino de traer ejemplares no esterilizados de otras regiones europeas si los estudios lo avalan.

articles.title: Confira o Olhar Digital News na íntegra (24/11/2026)
articles.text:
Veja os destaques do Olhar Digital News desta terça-feira (24/11).
Tesla e SpaceX negociam fusão que pode dar ainda mais poder a Elon Musk
A Tesla e a SpaceX estão negociando uma fusão avaliada em US$ 3,5 trilhões. A expectativa é que o negócio seja fechado até o fim deste ano, de acordo com informações do jornal britânico Financial Times. Para definir os termos da operação, que seria realizada integralmente por meio de ações, as empresas de Elon Musk designaram cinco integrantes de seus conselhos de administração.
Retorno de Jensen Huang à Nvidia pode ter feito Trump lucrar milhões
A intervenção de Donald Trump para convencer o conselho da Nvidia a reconduzir Jensen Huang ao comando da empresa pode ter valorizado em até US$ 15 milhões a participação do presidente dos Estados Unidos na fabricante de chips. A estimativa é do Financial Times, com base em declarações financeiras de Trump. Os documentos indicam que ele poderia possuir até 370 mil ações da companhia em setembro, mas não revelam a quantidade exata nem eventuais negociações posteriores.
El Niño e aquecimento global levam temperatura da Terra a novo recorde
A Terra registrou o dia com a maior anomalia de temperatura já medida: na última sexta-feira (20), a temperatura média global ficou 2,12°C acima dos níveis pré-industriais. Os dados preliminares são do Serviço de Mudanças Climáticas Copernicus, da Europa, e representam novo alerta sobre a intensidade do aquecimento do planeta. O recorde é resultado da combinação entre as mudanças climáticas provocadas pela atividade humana e um episódio excepcionalmente forte do fenômeno El Niño.
Rússia pode lançar bomba nuclear ao espaço ainda em 2026
O secretário-geral da Otan, Mark Rutte, afirmou nesta terça-feira (24) que a aliança militar está preparada para se defender contra quaisquer ameaças no espaço. A declaração é uma resposta a uma investigação realizada pela imprensa da Alemanha com base em informações de serviços de inteligência ocidentais e que aponta que a Rússia estaria preparando o lançamento de uma bomba nuclear ao espaço ainda neste ano.
Alessandro Di Lorenzo é editor do Olhar Digital e formado em jornalismo pela Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul (UFRGS).
André Milhomem integra a equipe de redes sociais do Olhar Digital e do programa Olhar Digital News.

articles.title: How Trump and Silicon Valley forced Nvidia to take Jensen Huang back
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (seated-L) speaks with US President Donald Trump during a meeting with AI executives at the White House.
Credit:
Kevin Dietsch / Staff | Getty Images News
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (seated-L) speaks with US President Donald Trump during a meeting with AI executives at the White House.
Credit:
Kevin Dietsch / Staff | Getty Images News
On Monday morning, Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters to rapturous applause from employees lining the walkways above him. Huang was visibly moved as one colleague threw themselves into his arms for a hug.
The spectacular reinstatement of the chief executive of Nvidia, less than two weeks after he resigned in a scandal over an affair with a customer and suspected Chinese spy—as well as a second reported affair with a subordinate—caught even the company’s most senior executives by surprise.
The abrupt reversal by Nvidia’s board was spurred by President Donald Trump, who applied pressure to the board over the weekend after watching what was once America’s most valuable company as well as the wider tech sector haemorrhage value last week.
It was the culmination of frenetic lobbying by a “war room” of Huang’s Silicon Valley allies, who pulled in Trump and vice-president JD Vance, according to people familiar with the events. They argued the Nvidia founder was personally integral to the health of the US AI industry, and therefore the stock market and entire economy.
“Great men make great mistakes. But nobody has ever been like this, not Elon Musk, not anyone. All the success we’re enjoying, all the tech gains, that’s all down to one guy,” said an ally of Huang.
But one of the most remarkable comebacks in corporate history, which called to mind Sam Altman’s brief ousting at OpenAI, still leaves the semiconductor giant at the heart of the AI boom in treacherous waters.
Nvidia and Huang face probes by the FBI and SEC, congressional investigations, and difficult questions over governance and Huang’s personal connections to a suspected Chinese spy allegedly involved in chip smuggling.
Even after gaining nearly $1 trillion in market value on the news of Huang’s return on Monday, Nvidia is worth about a fifth less than it was a month ago.
Huang told employees on Monday he had “made some very terrible mistakes, and I’m going to work on coming back.” Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang declined to comment.
The talks that culminated in an Nvidia board meeting late on Sunday were so secretive that even interim Chief Executive Officer Colette Kress was kept out of the discussions, the people said.
Trump personally spoke to the board in Huang’s defense, triggering an about-face days after it had categorically ruled out a return. The board said it was confident Huang posed no national security risk after “input from senior levels of the United States government,” but that its internal investigation would continue.
The seeds of Huang’s comeback were sown within hours of his resignation on November 12, which came after reports of affairs with a company executive and a woman named Alice Huang, an executive at a Singapore-based Nvidia client called Megaspeed, now at the center of chip smuggling allegations.
Allies in Silicon Valley rallied around him. A small group of Huang’s supporters, including Uber founder Travis Kalanick, venture capitalists Gavin Baker, Brad Gerstner, and Marc Andreessen, as well as Goldman Sachs executive John Underwood, leapt to action, according to people familiar with the matter, making the case in public and in private for Huang’s reinstatement.
Andreessen Horowitz declined to comment. The other members of the group did not respond.
Within 24 hours of Huang’s resignation, Baker and Gerstner published an open letter to Nvidia’s board urging them to leave “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.”
Their effort had Huang’s backing, the FT reported last week. On Tuesday, Huang confirmed he was prepared to step back into the role.
While the board’s chair, Harvey Jones, publicly insisted Huang could not return, Kress spent last week looking to steady the ship with a strong quarterly earnings report and promises to expedite pay rises and equity grants as Nvidia shares plummeted. A company “all-hands” meeting on Wednesday featured a show of unity from its top executive team, to the tune of Tom Petty’s “I Won’t Back Down.”
Behind the scenes, Huang’s allies in his “kitchen cabinet” began lobbying the White House and other power brokers in Washington.
One arranged a phone call between Huang and Vance last week that lasted 45 minutes. During the conversation, Huang defended his positions on US semiconductor export controls and remote access to chips, and his dealings with Megaspeed.
Vance, a former venture capitalist who was mentored by Peter Thiel and has raised millions of dollars from Silicon Valley, was seemingly persuaded by the entreaties of Huang and his allies, who are probably a crucial source of funding if Vance decides to run for president.
“Everyone who was important in the tech world was beating his door down,” said the person.
“He wasn’t doing it to help raise dollars. That never even came up. But he clearly understands that half of US GDP depends on Nvidia right now… the Nasdaq is up 7 percent. If you think that’s happening without Jensen, you’re crazy,” they added.
Over the course of the weekend, Trump and Vance’s engagement focused on convincing the board that Huang’s affair with Alice Huang did not mean he was exposed as a potential national security risk.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went out on Sunday to soften his earlier stance, having a week before accused the company of artificially inflating its revenue through illicit China sales and called for a wholesale leadership shake-up.
Those involved in the campaign viewed Bessent’s reversal as evidence they were making progress. Trump’s intervention with the board proved decisive.
On Monday, after Huang was returned to his post, Baker posted on X: “This is why America is the greatest country on earth. Every part of Jensen’s story would have only been possible in America.”
Inside Nvidia, employees responded to Huang’s return with a mixture of elation and surprise. Even those who had quietly hoped for Huang’s reappointment told the FT they had not expected it to happen so quickly.
One longtime employee said that staff who had known Jensen for years were shocked at the context of his downfall, in particular the surge in press reports about his well-known brutal management style.
“He has always behaved like this. People of a certain generation are thinking: why now?” said one.
Despite running Nvidia for 33 years and owning 3.5 percent of the company, Huang does not have the supervoting shares that enable other founder-CEOs, such as Mark Zuckerberg, to overrule their boards.
“If I’m Jensen Huang, my first question today is, ‘How can I get me some of those super voting shares so I can tell everybody to fuck off next time,’” said one person who had worked with Huang in Washington.
Huang’s return does not signal an end to the company’s troubles. Trump on Monday said the US attorney general’s office had “done a very thorough investigation” into Huang’s conduct and “exonerated” him. But both Democratic and Republican lawmakers on Monday were outraged.
Huang and Nvidia’s general counsel, Tim Teter, have been summoned to congressional hearings next week.
No member of the cabinet apart from Vance had publicly endorsed Huang’s return on Monday. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, himself under scrutiny over Nvidia’s ability to sell to Megaspeed on his watch, was not involved in the board discussions, according to one person close to him.
Internally, Huang’s personal management style, exercising close control over subordinates aided by his daughter and son-in-law, with no formal succession planning, has led to scrutiny about governance.
One longtime associate of board chair Jones said the decision to reinstate Huang would do little to assuage public concern and market worries around AI.
“The midterm elections showed that the wider public is deeply skeptical about all things AI,” the person said. “The Jensen affair masks a growing market consensus that the debt-leveraged speculative data center build-out is quite fragile.”
It also does nothing to reduce scrutiny of Nvidia’s board, which is stacked with longtime Huang allies and lacks any major tech or national security figures.
“While we are happy to have Jensen back, the on-again, off-again response from the board is, frankly, clown-like,” Bernstein analysts wrote on Monday, adding that it “brings up legitimate questions as to their judgment and process, which has to make one wonder how they come to their other important decisions.”
Others were more blunt. “Corporate governance has gone the way of the dodo,” said one large Nvidia investor.

articles.title: Designing A Microarchitecture From Formal Proof To Full-System
articles.text:
Combining architectural proof, software-driven verification, simulation, emulation, and cloud-based compute infrastructure.
Data center and high-performance computing workloads are pushing CPU designers to deliver higher per-watt throughput and support complex multicore systems. Meeting these goals requires specialized compute cores. This reality is forcing engineers to rethink not only how cores are built, but also which instruction set architecture (ISA) can scale efficiently, support software validation, and still create product differentiation. To meet these challenges, a lean R&D team from a startup company in Austin, Texas, chose the RISC-V ISA as the foundation for its first CPU IP microarchitecture.
Designing the microarchitecture involved balancing software-visible architectural behavior, RTL implementation details, and internal performance and power tradeoffs, which together introduced verification requirements that extended well beyond isolated hardware blocks. When these interactions are not addressed early in development, system-level issues can emerge later, making them more difficult to resolve. These decisions also expanded the scope of verification. The core had to be validated with actual software under full-system scale, including interactions that extend beyond individual hardware blocks.
To manage the complexity, the engineers adopted a formal-first verification strategy. By applying formal analysis during the design cycle, key architectural properties were proven before transitioning to large-scale simulation and system bring-up. Formal verification handled block-level functionality and end-to-end checks of functional intent. Simulation and emulation addressed long-running behavior in the full-core environment. Some failures may not emerge until the design has run for tens of millions of cycles under full operating system (OS) stress.
The design and verification group used a tightly integrated Cadence tool flow spanning architectural proof, software-driven verification, simulation, emulation, and cloud-based compute infrastructure. Figure 1 below illustrates a type of multicore CPU architecture that the Cadence verification methodology is designed to validate.
Fig. 1: A representative multicore CPU subsystem showing the processors, cache hierarchy, and system interfaces that engineers verify as the RTL design evolves. (Source: Cadence)
The Jasper Formal Verification Platform supported the implementation of a formal-first methodology to validate architectural intent early in the design. Formal Property Verification was applied across the fetch, decode, execution, and instruction-flow paths to ensure that key correctness properties were maintained throughout the pipeline. Jasper Superlint identified structural and coding issues early, preventing common RTL problems from propagating into later verification stages. Jasper XPROP addressed X-propagation risks associated with initialization and reset behavior, reducing simulation uncertainty and increasing confidence in system-level results. These results were then used to focus long-running simulation and emulation workloads on architecturally sensitive areas rather than simply increasing regression volume.
While formal verification established early architectural correctness, validating full OS behavior required executing long instruction streams, which challenged the practical limits of traditional simulation. To address this requirement, a snippet-based simulation flow was developed using the Xcelium Logic Simulator. This allowed long-running software execution to be divided into manageable segments while maintaining architectural state and full debug visibility across boundaries.
To exercise the design under realistic system conditions, the team ran Linux as the primary software workload on a QEMU-based virtual platform. The workload advanced in one-million-cycle increments, with the complete architectural state captured at each checkpoint to create a reusable snippet representing a defined window. Each snippet was then loaded into Xcelium with full signal visibility, allowing engineers to debug a specific region without rerunning the entire OS boot sequence.
Across the full verification flow, approximately 120 snippets were generated, enabling analysis of instruction streams spanning more than 35 million cycles. Extended instruction-stream execution also tested interrupt handling and exercised pipeline behavior. This approach reduced the turnaround time for long software workloads from days to hours and enabled detailed root-cause analysis of complex interactions. Xcelium achieved a simulation rate of approximately 100,000 cycles per second while preserving full debug visibility.
Debugging was done using Verisium Debug, which provided traceability across long instruction sequences and preserved context across simulation runs. This capability enabled efficient analysis of failures observed under software stress without sacrificing visibility.
Combining formal proof with logic simulation enabled a consistent way to connect the results and measure progress across verification stages. Within the platform, Verisium Manager provided a central dashboard for test planning and coverage tracking against defined targets. This unified view showed which coverage targets had been met, where gaps remained, and where to focus next. Verisium Debug complemented these capabilities by maintaining traceability across extended runs and linking simulation and emulation results.
The company transitioned to the Cadence Palladium Enterprise Emulation Platform for Linux bring-up and multicore software workloads. The platform provided the speed and hardware/software visibility needed to execute complete operating-system boot sequences. The team booted Linux on a single-core system in 50 minutes and on a dual-core system in 90 minutes. This confirmed system functionality and architectural scalability. Additionally, the engineers verified coherency and interrupt handling while identifying performance hotspots in concurrent workloads.
Cadence OnCloud platform provided the scalable compute capacity needed to maintain that visibility as verification workloads grew more complex. This emulation stage exposed system-level behavior, supported validation of operation and scalability, and made full-system bring-up practical within the engineering schedule.
By leveraging Cadence OnCloud, compute resources could be scaled to match verification demand during peak periods without requiring a fixed infrastructure commitment at the start of the project. At the same time, built-in security aligned with industry standards such as ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27017 helped ensure that sensitive IP remained protected throughout the process. The project validated both the approach and the platform.
The company uncovered complex interactions between cores and subsystems to achieve first-silicon success. For a small team, the biggest constraint was not methodology or tooling. It was the amount of work that could realistically be pushed through the system at any given time. Using a Cadence verification tool flow removed that barrier by providing additional capacity when verification demand peaked and turnaround time directly affected development momentum. The team could prioritize critical work instead of scaling back verification to fit the available infrastructure.
First-silicon success provided evidence that the cloud environment could meet the verification demands of a complex CPU design. Future processor development can move more system-level validation into the pre-silicon phase. At-speed prototypes provide a way to evaluate multicore operation and hardware-software interactions before silicon. On-demand access to emulation and prototyping capacity can expand with changing design needs, allowing system-level integration work to begin earlier without requiring an in-house lab.

articles.title: Ya están disponibles las ofertas de TP-Link y Tapo para este Black Friday: cámaras de seguridad, sensores, routers y mucho más
articles.text:
El Black Friday se ha convertido en el mejor momento del año para comprar. Mucho más si tenemos en cuenta que en pocas semanas entramos en periodo navideño y donde podemos adelantar las compras y regalos para ahorrarnos un buen dinero. TP-Link es una de esas marcas que más y mejores descuentos anuncian para el Black Friday. Esto es especialmente importante si tenemos en cuenta el portfolio tan amplio que tiene, y que va desde cámaras de seguridad hasta robots aspiradores.
Cámaras de vigilancia
Son cada vez más habituales en casas, comercios y oficinas. Tanto en exterior como en interior. Poder saber lo que está pasando cuando no estamos, es algo que cada vez valora más la gente. Que en los últimos años se haya disparado la venta de cámaras de vigilancia se debe principalmente a dos motivos. El primero es su democratización ya que hasta hace no mucho era una inversión cara pero que, gracias a marcas como TP-Link y su línea Tapo, cualquier persona puede acceder a una. El segundo motivo es la comodidad de poder ver lo que pasa desde nuestro teléfono móvil. No necesitamos grandes monitores, sólo nuestro smartphone.
Un aspecto importante a tener en cuenta es que cuando hablamos de algo tan delicado como nuestra intimidad y la de nuestra casa, no podemos recurrir a una marca cualquiera de vigilancia. Basta con dejarse caer por cualquier ecommerce, por ejemplo Amazon o PcComponentes, para comprobar las buenas valoraciones que tiene Tapo por parte de sus clientes.
Almacenamiento local y en la nube, posibilidad de grabar con dos lentes a la vez ( por ejemplo para hacer zoom con una mientras la otra sigue grabando toda la zona), el uso de la inteligencia artificial para detectar objetos y personas o la posibilidad de grabar con una altísima calidad de imagen, incluso de noche, son algunas de las ventajas que ofrecen los equipos Tapo. Además, hay cámaras de todos los precios, perfectas para cada tipo de usuario. Aquí tienes algunas recomendaciones de las mejores cámaras de seguridad que puedes encontrar durante estos días del Black Friday.
- Tapo C665G KIT – Cámara 4G con panel solar, ideal para lugares sin conexión Wi-Fi. Precio Black Friday: 154,99 €.
- Tapo C660 KIT / TC92 KIT – Cámara exterior 4K con alimentación solar, ideal para mantener vigilada la vivienda durante las vacaciones y controlar lo que ocurre en casa estés donde estés, sin preocuparte por recargar la batería constantemente. 109,24 €.
- Tapo C545D – Cámara exterior de doble lente para cubrir diferentes ángulos. 75,95 €.
- Tapo C260 – Cámara de vigilancia interior 4K con funciones de IA y reconocimiento facial gratuitas. También puede utilizarse como babycam para vigilar al pequeño y recibir notificaciones cuando detecta que está llorando. 54,99 €.
- Tapo C210 / TC72 – Cámaras interiores para vigilar diferentes habitaciones. Pack de 1: 22,99 €; pack de 2: 43,18 €.
Pero además de cámaras, también puedes completar tu sistema de seguridad con estos dos elementos, un timbre inteligente y un sensor de movimiento:
- Tapo D210 / TD21 – Timbre inteligente con vídeo para ver quién llama a la puerta. Por sólo 54,99 euros.
- Tapo T100 – Sensor de movimiento para activar automatizaciones en casa. Por sólo 12,64 euros.
Además de las cámaras, el ecosistema Tapo cuenta con el Tapo H500 (151,99 €), un hub inteligente que permite conectar y gestionar de forma centralizada hasta 16 cámaras y 64 sensores Tapo desde una misma plataforma. Incorpora 16 GB de almacenamiento interno, ampliable hasta 16 TB mediante un disco duro HDD o SSD , y mejora las capacidades de IA de las cámaras. Todo ello con almacenamiento local y funciones inteligentes sin necesidad de contratar suscripciones adicionales.
Sistemas Wi-Fi Mesh y routers
La realidad es que la conexión que ofrece el router de las operadoras es bastante mejorable. A nada que la casa tiene los muros un poco más gruesos o alguna habitación (como la cocina) genera interferencias, la calidad de la conexión cae en picado.
En los tiempos actuales, donde millones de personas trabajan desde casa, consumen contenido en streaming o tienen cámaras de vigilancia conectadas a la red, una buena conexión a Internet es importantísima. De nada sirven las tarifas de 10 gigas de las operadoras si luego realmente, llegan reales 100 o 300 megas.
Cambiar el router de la compañía por un router de una marca como Deco, es una opción muy inteligente que te permite ahorrar dinero desde el primer día. Pero montarte una red mesh en tu casa u oficina es una decisión maestra.
A continuación te dejamos una recomendación con packs de dos y tres nodos para cubrir la mayor parte posible y siempre con la mejor calidad de red. Y si no necesitas una red mesh, los routers y repetidores de Archer son súper top. Te dejamos también dos de diferentes precios según se ajuste más a tu bolsillo.
- Deco BE65 (pack de 2) – Sistema Wi-Fi 7 Mesh tribanda que permite disfrutar de una conexión rápida y estable en toda la casa, incluso cuando hay muchos dispositivos conectados al mismo tiempo. Gracias a sus nodos adicionales, podrás ampliar la cobertura Wi-Fi y olvidarte de las zonas sin señal. Cada unidad cuenta con cuatro puertos Ethernet de 2,5 Gbps y un puerto USB 3.0, ideal para conectar dispositivos por cable y aprovechar al máximo una conexión de fibra de alta velocidad. 349,99 €.
- Deco BE65 (pack de 3) – Para viviendas más grandes o con mayores necesidades de cobertura. 499,99 €.
- Deco BE3600 (pack de 3) / Deco BE25 – Sistema Wi-Fi 7 Mesh de doble banda. Sus tres nodos trabajan juntos para crear una única red Wi-Fi, permitiendo moverte de una habitación a otra sin tener que cambiar de red. Ambos modelos ofrecen velocidades Wi-Fi de la misma categoría, pero el Deco BE25 destaca por incorporar puertos Ethernet de 2,5 Gbps, ideales para conectar dispositivos por cable y aprovechar conexiones de Internet de alta velocidad. 211,95 €.
- Deco BE3600 (pack de 2) / Deco BE25 – Sistema Wi-Fi 7 Mesh para mejorar la cobertura doméstica. 179,99 €.
- Archer NX600 – Router 5G para disponer de conexión a Internet mediante red móvil. Ideal para segundas residencias, casas rurales o lugares donde no llega la fibra óptica. 277,87 €.

Enchufes y luces inteligentes
Es otra de las pequeñas revoluciones que han sufrido las casas. Con la popularización de los asistentes de voz, como Alexa o Google, muchas personas pueden controlar con la voz o desde el teléfono móvil cualquiera de sus electrodomésticos o luces en casa. Encender la luz poco antes de que lleguemos o cuando no estamos en casa para simular que sí estamos, o apagar un electrodoméstico conectado a la red. Las posibilidades son enormes con las luces y enchufes inteligentes de TP-Link, que además son compatibles con todos los asistentes de voz.
Aquí te dejamos lo que, a nuestro parecer, son las mejores opciones tanto si estás empezando a domotizar tu casa como si quieres añadir nuevos elementos. Una bombilla, una tira LED y un enchufe inteligente que parten de los 9,25 euros.

Limpieza inteligente
Se trata de una de las categorías más novedosas dentro del catálogo de TP-Link Tapo: su robot aspirador. El mejor ayudante para tener la casa limpia de una manera totalmente autónoma. Sólo hay que programarlo con la aplicación para que salga a aspirar y pasar la mopa unos días determinados y listo, cuando lleguemos a casa estará limpia. Su estación de carga también puede vaciar el depósito de residuos (para que no tengamos que hacerlo nosotros) y limpiar y secar las mopas para dejarlas perfectamente para la siguiente limpieza.
El Tapo RV50 Pro Omni destaca especialmente por su estación de autolimpieza todo en uno, diseñada para que tengas que preocuparte lo mínimo posible por el mantenimiento del robot. Se encarga de automatizar tareas como el vaciado del polvo, el lavado de las mopas y su secado, ofreciendo una experiencia de limpieza mucho más cómoda y reduciendo las tareas de mantenimiento del día a día.

Lo mejor de todo es que su precio es bastante bueno, más incluso teniendo en cuenta el descuento.
Estos han sido sólo algunos de los productos que más nos han llamado la atención, pero hay muchísimos más por lo que si no has encontrado el adecuado, visita la web de TP-Link y su sección exclusiva para el Black Friday y haz que tu casa sea más inteligente, más segura, mejor conectada y más limpia.

articles.title: What’s New for Game Developers: AI Animation and RTX Tools
articles.text:
This month’s NVIDIA game development updates help teams bring new graphics, animation, and local AI capabilities into their engines while balancing image quality, performance, and creative intent.
This post covers:
- Developer lessons from the War Thunder NVIDIA DLSS 5 integration
- NVIDIA Kimodo animation generation in Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview
- NVIDIA In-Game Inferencing SDK 1.8 updates for RTX Spark, speech recognition, and Vulkan
- NVIDIA RTX Dynamic Illumination 3.2 and RTX Path Tracing 1.9 improvements for lighting, integration, and debugging
- Nsight developer tools updates for Fall of 2026
How Gaijin raised War Thunder’s realism using NVIDIA DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering
In an interview, Gaijin Entertainment shares how it integrated DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering into War Thunder’s Dagor Engine while preserving the game’s established visual identity. The team explains how it adapted its color management pipeline to evaluate DLSS 5 in sRGB before post-processing and UI, then map the results back to linear HDR, saying “DLSS 5 delivers improved highlights and shadows while introducing a new level of microcontrast that we simply haven’t been able to achieve before. The result is a more natural, lifelike image, with finer detail and a stronger sense of realism.”
The team also discusses tuning DLSS 5 against its reference look to preserve vehicle markings, surface wear, and material properties, as well as evaluating image quality and performance separately across air, ground, and naval combat. The interview offers developers practical lessons on balancing lighting and material enhancements with their game’s art direction, with ON/OFF comparisons highlighting rainy, overcast scenes.
Read the full War Thunder interview.
NVIDIA Kimodo is the first model in Unreal Engine 5.9’s guided animation framework
Kimodo brings its animation research into Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview, which introduces a guided animation framework and a set of Sequencer tools that help animators work directly with AI motion-generation models. Kimodo is the first model integrated with it, enabling animators to generate character motion right inside Sequencer. The integration pairs GPU-accelerated motion generation with the familiar timeline editor workflow.
Animators can describe a motion with a text prompt, draw a spline path for the character to follow, and set target poses at specific frames. The model generates motion that follows these constraints, so teams decide where characters move and how they pose at key moments, bringing creative control into the animation.
Explore the Unreal Engine 5.9 Preview release notes and the Kimodo research project.
NVIDIA In-Game Inferencing SDK 1.8 expands platform and model support
The NVIDIA In-Game Inferencing SDK helps developers integrate NVIDIA ACE on-device. ACE is a suite of AI technologies designed to help middleware and game developers build knowledgeable, actionable, and conversational in-game characters. The SDK supports multiple inference backends across GPU and CPU hardware, giving teams a common interface for running AI alongside game graphics.
Version 1.8 focuses on platform support and the inference components used in language and speech workflows. Key updates include:
- RTX Spark: Hardened platform support for developers building applications
- Updated inference backends: Newer llama.cpp and whisper.cpp versions
- Expanded speech recognition: Support for the Parakeet automatic speech recognition (ASR) model through whisper.cpp
- Vulkan integration: Added support for the Vulkan priority API
- Additional bug fixes across the SDK.
Explore the NVIDIA In-Game Inferencing SDK.
NVIDIA RTX Dynamic Illumination 3.2 adds sampling improvements and reservoir debugging tools
RTX Dynamic Illumination 3.2 is available on GitHub with updates for developers integrating ReSTIR lighting into their renderers. The release adds new sampling options for ReSTIR DI, adds RTX Spark support, and expands the tools used to inspect lighting reservoirs.
Release highlights include:
- Stratified low-discrepancy sampling for ReSTIR DI spatial resampling
- A fallback sample feature for ReSTIR DI
- Enhanced reservoir visualization for direct illumination, global illumination, and path tracing, giving developers more ways to inspect the samples used by each technique
- RTX Spark support
- Updated Donut and NVRHI components, along with bug fixes
Explore the RTXDI SDK and samples on GitHub.
NVIDIA Real-Time BVH Viewer 1.0 brings live acceleration structure inspection to D3D12 and Vulkan
NVIDIA Real-Time BVH Viewer 1.0 is now available on GitHub. The utility shows ray tracing acceleration structures while a game or renderer is running. It helps developers understand TLAS and BLAS contents, validate acceleration structure updates, and debug geometry-related ray tracing issues.
The viewer integrates at the graphics API level through Direct3D 12 and Vulkan libraries. Developers send acceleration structure builds, copies, queue submissions, and frame boundaries to the viewer, which displays the results in a separate window. Separate windows with its own camera allows it to inspect TLAS independently from the in-game camera.
To inspect an existing title without changing its code, developers can use the included sampler. It attaches the viewer to a running D3D12 or Vulkan process and serves as an integration sample.
Release highlights include:
- Visualization modes for primitive, geometry, instance, and cluster IDs, BLAS addresses, instance masks and flags, and acceleration structure update state
- Per-pixel trace time heatmaps that show which parts of a scene cost the most to trace
- Support for various geometry filters: flags, types and ray culling
- Support for Clustered geometry in D3D12
- Vendor-agnostic integration with optional vendor-specific paths, plus builds for Windows x64 and RTX Spark
Access the BVH Viewer on github and download the v1.0.0 release.
RTX Path Tracing 1.9 adds an introductory sample and SHaRC integration
NVIDIA RTX Path Tracing 1.9 gives developers a more accessible starting point for adding ray-traced lighting and studying a real-time path tracing pipeline.
The intro sample uses a hybrid deferred renderer to introduce lighting features one at a time across nine selectable steps. Developers can progress from image-based lighting and screen-space effects to ReSTIR DI, path-traced indirect lighting, and SHaRC radiance caching.
SHaRC is also integrated into the main real-time path tracer and enabled by default, providing additional indirect-lighting information to DLSS Ray Reconstruction. Other updates include:
- RTX Spark support
- Performance optimizations including real-time subsampling, overlapping DLSS Ray Reconstruction with the next frame’s path tracing, and GPU-side acceleration-structure instance generation
- Expanded NEE-AT light sampling support for up to two million lights and clustering of emissive triangles into light levels of detail
- A new design document describing the real-time path tracing pipeline, plus updated dependencies, fixes, and rendering improvements
Read the RTX Path Tracing 1.9 release notes and explore the Intro Sample.
RTX Global Illumination 2.9 adds improved diffuse GI sample and SER support
Release highlights for NVIDIA RTX Global Illumination 2.9 include:
- A new IndirectDiffuse sample introducing a deferred renderer that uses NRC or SHaRC for indirect diffuse illumination, complete with shadow mapping, sky lighting, and visualization modes
- Shader Execution Reordering (SER) support for Direct3D 12 (Shader Model 6.9) and Vulkan, toggleable directly from the UI
- Additional bug fixes and performance enhancements
NVIDIA Nsight Graphics and Nsight Systems Introduce DLSS-FG Support, Agentic AI Tooling
Video 1. NVIDIA Nsight Graphics 2026.4 release spotlight, highlighting DLSS Frame Generation analysis and agentic AI tooling
NVIDIA Nsight Graphics 2026.4 and Nsight Systems 2026.6 introduce support for analyzing applications using DLSS Frame Generation (DLSS-FG). When integrating DLSS Frame Generation and Multi-Frame Generation into a title, it is important to understand both the work submitted by the application and the pacing of the frames presented to players.
In Nsight Graphics, GPU Trace now displays application and presented frames on separate timeline rows, while Graphics Capture preserves the DLSS-FG workload for inspection during capture and replay. Nsight Systems distinguishes generated frames from application frames and correlates them with CPU frame ranges. DLSS-FG support in both tools requires Streamline SDK 2.12 or newer.
The new releases also introduce agentic AI tooling for graphics development. A new Nsight Graphics MCP server enables compatible AI agents to capture applications, inspect and debug captures, and analyze GPU traces. Nsight Systems includes skill files that guide AI agents in diagnosing CPU bottlenecks, frame stutter, and CPU-GPU synchronization overhead.
Download Nsight Graphics and Nsight Systems.
Resources for game developers
Check out the full list of game developer resources and stay up to date with the latest NVIDIA game development news:
- Subscribe to our newsletter (select gaming as your industry)
- Follow us on social: X, LinkedIn, Facebook, and YouTube
- Join our Discord community

articles.title: Social media platforms could face billions of dollars in fines after Australian Government passes Digital Duty of Care bill
articles.text:
The Australian Federal Government is about to pass Digital Duty of Care legislation that could see social media platforms find billions of dollars if users are found to be harmed online.
Labour, with support from the Greens, this week agreed on the final structure of the bill which will see it get through the Parliament in the last sitting session of the year.
The Liberal-National Coalition has opposed to the bill and raised concerns about freedom of speech.
The bill is designed to protect users if they feel they have been harmed by harrowing and harmful content on online.
Australians will also be able to launch legal actions against these big tech companies if they feel they have been harmed.
Tech companies could be subjected to fines of up to $109 million or five per cent of global revenue if they break the rules.
Last year Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, earned more than $200 billion and if found guilty in a Digital Duty of Care claim could be forced to pay an estimated $10 billion.
The bill has already drawn criticism from the Trump administration which expressed “serious concerns” saying it was a threat to free speech.
“Preserving a free open internet and protecting freedom of expression online are top priorities for the Trump administration,” the US Embassy said.
This move comes almost a year after the under-16 social media ban, which was designed to shield younger users from potentially harmful online content.
The Digital Duty of Care Bill will also provide control for users over their algorithm.
“Big tech has a choice now: work to make your platform safer. Work with parents to be able to make the engagement online with their kids safer,” Greens communication spokeswoman Sarah Hanson-Young told ABC News.
Under the Digital Duty of Care Bill there have been several amendments, including allowing users over 16 to opt out of algorithms.
Bill also gives the eSafety Commissioner unprecedented power to issue removal notices on what it considers to be adult content.
The bill will also establish an independent ombudsman to give users a course of action to help resolve issues with these big tech companies and social media platforms.
As it stands, individuals who want to take on the social media platforms we’ll have to navigate a long and complex path under the existing consumer protection laws.
The Digital Duty of Care Bill will streamline that process with the aim of assisting users who feel they have been harmed.
At the same time it is also being designed to put the big social media companies on notice and to make the necessary changes to their platforms and rethink their approach to the content they are sharing.

articles.title: CortexSpark Ventures launches Rs 1,000 Cr deeptech fund
articles.text:
CortexSpark Ventures launches Rs 1,000 Cr deeptech fund
CortexSpark Ventures will back deeptech startups that have created IP and looking to translate this into commercial applications
CortexSpark Ventures, a venture capital firm focused on deeptech and artificial intelligence segment, has launched a Rs 1,000 crore fund with an additional greenshoe option of Rs 400 crore.
Founded by former Infosys executives Vinay Peshwa and Sanjay Khanduri, the company will focus on startup investments across spacetech, defence tech, embodied AI and robotics, enterprise AI, medtech & Bio-AI, and energy and advanced materials.
According to a statement, CortexSpark Ventures aims to back startups developing intellectual property and solving complex technological challenges. The firm's investment thesis focuses on startups with defensible intellectual property, strong technical foundations, experienced founders and clear pathways to commercialisation. It aims to bridge the gap between scientific innovation and commercial scale through capital, technical expertise and strategic support.
"India has built world-class technology services companies. The next opportunity is to create globally competitive technology product companies driven by original research and intellectual property,” said Vinay Peshwa, Managing Partner, CortexSpark Ventures.
The philosophy of this VC firm is, “The venture fund for AI, by AI,” as it aims to combine AI-enabled investment processes with scientific expertise, human judgement and global networks.
The fund's Investment Committee is chaired by Manoj Kohli, former country head of SoftBank Group and ex-CEO & MD of Bharti Airtel. The other advisors are N Vedachalam, former Director of ISRO's Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre and Ashutosh Sharma, former Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, Government of India.
"India has the scientific talent, engineering capabilities and entrepreneurial ambition to build globally competitive deep-tech companies. What is needed is an investment ecosystem that understands breakthrough technologies and supports their journey to commercial scale,” said Manoj Kohli, Chairman of the Investment Committee, CortexSpark Ventures.
According to this VC firm, deeptech startups often face longer development cycles, complex technical risks and higher capital requirements and it aims to address these challenges through scientific evaluation, commercial due diligence and active support for founders.
The firm is also developing CortexSpark OS, an AI-enabled fund management platform designed to support deal sourcing, screening, due diligence and portfolio monitoring.

articles.title: Un SUV électrique allemand à 25 000 € ? Le coup de poker d’Opel avec un géant chinois
articles.text:
S’il est impossible de contrer l’ennemi, autant se joindre à lui. Beaucoup ne seront certainement pas d’accord avec cette affirmation. C’est pourtant ce qu’a fait Opel en signant un accord de coopération avec Leapmotor valable pour les prochaines années. Les fans du Blitz hurleront à coup sûr au sacrilège. Mais vu la situation actuelle, il serait assez bête de vouloir se renfermer sur soi-même.
Surtout que Leapmotor fait partiellement partie du groupe Stellantis. Bref, les fondations étaient en réalité déjà toutes préparées… Mais pour quels produits ? Toute une portée, visiblement ! Et le premier de la série sera un SUV électrique inédit du segment C qui arrivera en 2028. Il complètera donc la gamme Opel aux côtés du Mokka, du Frontera et du Grandland et ne remplacera pas un modèle existant.
Pas question d’un simple modèle chinois rebadgé
Et pour ceux qui s’attendaient au pire, non, ce futur véhicule ne sera pas bêtement un Leapmotor rebadgé. Opel partira bien de zéro en appliquant un design assurément allemand gage d’un minimum de personnalité. La marque souligne que ce modèle sera adapté aux goûts européens. Ce SUV reprendra donc l’identité stylistique du Blitz avec la calandre Vizor dotée d’un logo rétroéclairé.
Des lignes tendues appliquées sur une carrosserie épurée sont donc attendues. Côté dimensions, Florian Huettl, le PDG d’Opel, cherche à placer ce modèle au milieu de sa gamme de SUV : « nous visons le segment C moyen, qui mesure 4,50 mètres, ce qui placera ainsi [cette future voiture] entre le Frontera et le Grandland. Il s’agit d’un marché très porteur au Royaume-Uni et en Europe qu’Opel n’a pas encore couvert ».
De vrais boutons à bord et un prix d’attaque fixé à 25 000 €
Est-ce la solution miracle pour remettre le constructeur sur les rails ? Oui, aux yeux de Huettl : « nous considérons ce véhicule comme un atout majeur pour renforcer notre présence sur ce marché […]. Opel est solidement implanté dans le nord et l’est de l’Europe. Ce sont nos marchés historiques et leur particularité est qu’ils sont davantage attirés par les SUV du segment C et les véhicules électriques ». Espérons que le châssis sera aussi réglé à l’européenne…
À bord, Opel met un point d’honneur à conserver les commandes physiques, comme le confirme Huettl, « nous étudions comment tirer le meilleur parti de l’expertise de Leapmotor en matière d’architectures électroniques […]. Mais l’important, c’est que nous sommes Opel, et nous utiliserons de vrais boutons ». Niveau tarification, le constructeur vise une entrée de gamme aux alentours des 25 000 €, soit à peine plus haut que le Frontera.
