Source : Auto Express

articles.title: 6 bonnes raisons de donner sa chance à Blade Runner 2099, au même niveau que les films ?
articles.text:
Attendue avec autant de curiosité que de prudence par les fans, la série Blade Runner 2099 possède la lourde tâche de perpétuer l’héritage d’un monument de la pop culture. Libre adaptation du roman « Les androïdes rêvent-ils de moutons électriques ? » (1966) de Philip K. Dick, le film Blade Runner (1982) de l’immense Ridley Scott a contribué à définir l’esthétique des œuvres dystopiques au cinéma. Audacieux mélange entre SF et néo noir, il nous plonge dans l’enquête de Rick Deckard (Harrison Ford), un flic torturé qui appartient à une division spéciale, les « Blade Runner », chargée de traquer les Réplicants jugés déviants.
Dans ce Los Angeles pluvieux et situé en 2019, une entreprise privée, Tyrell Corporation, détient le monopole de création des Réplicants, des androïdes biosynthétiques utilisés comme de la main d’œuvre corvéable à merci. Avec son esthétique cyberpunk, ses looks eighties et ses décors extérieurs époustouflants, Blade Runner demeure un classique du genre, immédiatement reconnaissable. On vous donne 6 bonnes raisons de donner une chance à sa suite en série.
1. Replonger dans le monde hypnotique de Blade Runner
Comme bon nombre de films avant-gardistes, Blade Runner a connu une sortie en salles contrastée : échec aux Etats-Unis, le film devient un succès à l’étranger. Les critiques ont été dures, mais il a remporté des prix prestigieux (Bafta et Prix Hugo). Au fil des années et avec la sortie d’un Director’s Cut, Blade Runner acquiert le statut de film culte.
Trente-cinq ans après sa sortie, Denis Villeneuve réalise une suite fleuve, Blade Runner 2049, portée par Ryan Gosling. Esthétiquement éblouissant et cohérent avec la mythologie installée dans le premier film, il convainc une grande partie de la critique mais son rythme lent et son ambiance froide ne séduisent pas le grand public.
Avec deux films marquants et une série d’animation, Blade Runner : Black Lotus (2021), Blade Runner a acquis un noyau dur de fans, impatients de découvrir la dernière itération d’un univers devenu franchise, la série Blade Runner 2099.
2. Ridley Scott a eu (un peu) son mot à dire
Dans un marché audiovisuel qui se replie sur les IP (Intellectual Property) – des récits déjà connus du public comme des romans, podcasts, films etc. – la création d’une série autour de l’univers de Blade Runner fait sens. La peur numéro une des fans, bien légitime, reste de voir leur film préféré dilué dans une production cheap ou que cette suite vienne contredire la mythologie de l’œuvre originale.
Dans ce genre d’entreprise risquée, la présence des créateurs du matériel d’origine rassure. Créée par Silka Luisa, la série a pu compter sur Ridley Scott, producteur exécutif sur le projet. Le producteur Broderick Johnson a confirmé en interview : « Ridley Scott a participé à cette version depuis le début, en décidant de la temporalité, si cent ans, cinquante ans ou autre s’était passé. Il était impliqué dans tout le projet, jusqu’à donner son avis sur les montages des épisodes et tout le reste. »
L’avis de Ridley Scott est toutefois demeuré consultatif. Un peu plus tôt dans l’année, le réalisateur de The Dog Stars (2026) regrettait d’avoir perdu le contrôle créatif de Blade Runner (moyennant un beau chèque !). « Je ne peux pas blâmer mes avocats et mes agents de l’époque, mais d’une manière ou d’une autre, nous avons laissé filer les droits de Blade Runner. Et quand on n’est pas l’auteur du texte, on ne possède pas l’œuvre. »
Des propos qui reflètent l’amertume du réalisateur de n’avoir pas pu réaliser Blade Runner 2049. À l’époque, il avait laissé sa place à Denis Villeneuve pour réaliser Alien : Covenant. Ridley Scott se console d’ailleurs avec la franchise Alien, dont il est resté propriétaire. Il a notamment produit la série Alien : Earth.
3. La série rebat les cartes de la mythologie
Silka Luisa a imaginé l’histoire de Blade Runner 2099 en continuité avec les deux précédents films. La série prend place un demi-siècle après le long-métrage de Denis Villeneuve. Les Réplicants ont pris le pouvoir dans un Los Angeles en proie au réchauffement climatique. Les oppressés d’hier sont devenus les oppresseurs d’aujourd’hui. Voilà qui offre des possibilités narratives intéressantes.
Ce sont eux les nouveaux « Blade Runner », qui traquent leurs propres anciens modèles présentant un danger pour l’ordre public et traitent les humains comme des citoyens de seconde-zone.
L’histoire débute quand Cora, une humaine en cavale, décide de se faire passer pour une Réplicante dans le but de protéger son frère. Le subterfuge fonctionne et elle enquête bientôt aux côtés d’Olwen, une Réplicante en fin de vie chargée de « mettre à la retraite » son ancien partenaire Réplicant.
Côté mythologie, la showrunneuse s’intéresse également à la généalogie des Réplicants et notamment aux tous premiers modèles Nexus One. Voilà qui devait créer quelques nouveaux fils de discussions sur Reddit ! Si la série fait référence à Deckard, Silka Luisa a fait savoir qu’elle ne trancherait pas la question de la nature de ce personnage culte, humaine ou Réplicant. Un choix fort sage : Harrison Ford et Ridley Scott eux-mêmes sont en désaccord sur la question !
4. Un duo féminin qui déménage
La série Blade Runner 2099 repose sur la dynamique d’un duo de personnages féminins, Olwen et Cora, incarnées par Michelle Yeoh, reine hollywoodienne des films d’action (Tigre et Dragons, Everything Everywhere, All at Once) et la très demandée Hunter Schafer (Euphoria, Hunger Games : La Ballade du serpent et de l’oiseau chanteur). Les deux actrices brillent autant dans les séquences d’action que dans les scènes plus émouvantes.
La relation entre ces deux femmes dures à cuire, qui ont plus en commun qu’elles ne le pensent, constitue le cœur battant de la série. Au fil de leur enquête, elles vont apprendre à s’apprivoiser et à dépasser leurs préjugés respectifs sur les Réplicants et les humains.
C’est une très bonne idée de proposer un buddy movie au féminin, là où les deux précédents films étaient centrés sur des personnages masculins et plaçaient leurs protagonistes féminines dans des rôles très secondaires et sexualisés (les IA nues de Blader Runner 2049, la petite-amie parfaite de K, où la très passive Rachel dans le premier film). Adieu le male gaze : la mini-série prouve que les questions existentielles se conjuguent autant au féminin qu’au masculin.
5. Une fresque ambitieuse
Pour faire revivre le Los Angeles futuriste de Blade Runner, Amazon Prime n’a pas lésiné sur le budget : 160 millions de dollars pour huit épisodes d’une heure. Réalisés par Jonathan Van Tulleken, les deux premiers épisodes mettent en scène un univers qualifié de « Sunshine Noir », ou le genre du polar se marie avec une photographie grillée par le soleil. Esthétiquement ambitieuse, la série alterne diverses ambiances, dont quelques séquences pluvieuses, clin d’oeil à celles du film de 1982.
L’exigence artistique se fait sentir dans le choix des plans, le travail sur la lumière, l’utilisation d’outils rétro-futuristes (n’oublions pas que Blade Runner a anticipé Facetime !) ou encore l’ampleur et la diversité des décors présents. Sans être la claque visuelle des premiers films (elle n’a ni le budget nécessaire, ni la primeur de la nouveauté pour ça), la série s’inscrit dans leur continuité et leur fait honneur.
6. Une SF plus actuelle que jamais
Depuis la sortie du premier Blade Runner, au début des années 80, notre rapport aux œuvres de science-fiction a évolué au fil des innovations technologiques de la vraie vie. Certains aspects du film ont vu si juste que nous vivons déjà dans Blade Runner. Si les voitures volantes ne sont pas à l’ordre du jour (sniff…), l’intelligence artificielle, contrôlée par des entreprises privées, est en train de révolutionner notre monde. Et la question de l’autonomie de l’IA contre les intérêts des humains commence très sérieusement à se poser !
À rebours des séries ultra-rythmées et de nos vies minutées, la série prend son temps pour nous raconter son histoire et nous immerger dans son univers mi-inquiétant, mi-fascinant. Le choix d’une photographie solaire s’appuie aussi sur la réalité du réchauffement climatique en cours.
Sous le bon vieux genre du thriller, les thématiques soulevées par la série – les rapports de domination entre humains et machines, la quête d’immortalité, la puissance des souvenirs et notre tragique propension à l’autodestruction – se révèlent encore plus d’actualité qu’il y a cinquante ans. Sans apporter de grandes réponses définitives, Blade Runner 2099 est une invitation à la réflexion et à la contemplation.
Le verdict
Blade Runner 2099
Voir la fiche
On a aimé
- Un duo féminin convaincant
- Une fresque ambitieuse esthétiquement
- Une série qui prend son temps
- Une SF aux thématiques actuelles
On a moins aimé
- Des personnages badass mais un peu froids
- Elle n’égale pas la claque visuelle des deux premiers films
Avec son esthétique soignée et son univers toujours aussi hypnotique, Blade Runner 2099 réussit à prolonger intelligemment la mythologie imaginée par Ridley Scott. Sans chercher à rivaliser avec la puissance visuelle des deux films, cette mini-série ambitieuse apporte un souffle nouveau à la franchise, notamment grâce à son formidable duo féminin incarné par Michelle Yeoh et Hunter Schafer. Elle renoue avec la dimension contemplative de la saga tout en actualisant ses questionnements sur l’intelligence artificielle, le pouvoir et la condition humaine. Une proposition de science-fiction élégante, immersive et profondément actuelle, qui mérite largement le détour.

articles.title: Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken werben schon, der Staat lässt wohl auf sich warten
articles.text:
Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken legen los – doch der Staat verspätet sich
Während sich Banken und Versicherer schon eine Werbeschlacht um das neue Altersvorsorgedepot liefern, werden Verbraucher noch länger auf die staatliche Variante warten müssen. Eigentlich sieht die neue Form der staatlich geförderten privaten Altersvorsorge vor, dass nicht nur Broker und Banken das neue Produkt anbieten. Auch der Staat sollte ein Altersvorsorgedepot auflegen.
Wie das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND) berichtet, wird das staatliche Depot aber zum Start am 1. Januar nicht zur Verfügung stehen. Aus Regierungskreisen heißt es, mit der Einführung sei frühestens im Sommer 2027 zu rechnen. Grund für die Verzögerung ist, dass die Verordnung für das öffentlich organisierte Angebot länger dauert als gedacht.
Die Rechtsverordnung muss auch noch festlegen, welche Institution das Angebot verwalten soll. Im Gespräch sind unter anderem Bundesbank, KfW und Deutsche Rentenversicherung. Das Gesetz zum Altersvorsorgedepot ist seit Ende Mai in Kraft.
Das Altersvorsorgedepot ist der Nachfolger der Riester-Rente und soll es den Deutschen leichter machen, breit gestreut am Kapitalmarkt fürs Alter zu sparen. Dafür gibt es staatliche Zuschüsse von bis zu 540 Euro pro Jahr sowie zusätzlich 300 Euro jährlich je kindergeldberechtigtem Kind. Anlegen können Sparer:innen in ETFs, Aktienfonds und Anleihen.
Das vom Staat bereitgestellte Produkt ist dabei als Benchmark gedacht, um die Kosten im Zaum zu halten. Es soll Sparer:innen jährlich nur 0,2 Prozent der Anlagesumme kosten. Außerdem kann es als Maßstab dienen, um die Konditionen von Banken und Versicherern vergleichen zu können.
Werbeschlacht ums Altersvorsorgedepot
Schon jetzt locken viele Banken, Versicherer und Broker mit Angeboten für den Riester-Nachfolger, die sie frei gestalten können. Für sie alle gilt allerdings: Wer ein Altersvorsorgedepot auflegt, muss auch ein Standarddepot im Angebot haben, dessen Kosten bei einem Prozent Effektivkosten im Jahr gedeckelt sind.
Im Wettbewerb zeichnen sich zum Start allerdings deutlich geringere Kosten ab. Teils bieten Banken und Broker das Standarddepot unter bestimmten Bedingungen fast kostenlos an. Verbraucherschützer sehen den entstehenden Angebotsdschungel und die aggressive Werbung für das Altersvorsorgedepot allerdings kritisch. Denn Anbieter könnten zwar jetzt mit günstigen Konditionen um Kund:innen werben, die Gebühren aber mit der Zeit nach oben schrauben.
Die Verbraucherzentrale Baden-Württemberg kritisierte daher zuletzt den Verordnungsentwurf des Bundesfinanzministeriums, der regelt, welche Kosten und Informationen die Anbieter beim Altersvorsorgedepot offenlegen müssen. Der soll eigentlich dafür sorgen, dass Sparer:innen die Angebote besser durchschauen und vergleichen können.
Laut den Verbraucherschützer:innen werden die Kosten aber weiterhin nicht vollständig ausgewiesen. Auch wie stark Entgelte die Rendite schmälern, sei für Verbraucher:innen undurchsichtig. Damit blieben Probleme bestehen, die schon von der Riester-Rente bekannt sind. Lösen lässt sich das aus Sicht der Verbraucherschützer:innen erst, wenn ein öffentlicher Träger ein Standarddepot ohne Vertriebsinteresse anbietet.
Bis dahin hätten Verbraucher:innen keine echte Alternative, die frei von Verkaufsanreizen, Kostenfallen und irreführenden Werbepraktiken ist. Ein erster Anbieter wurde von der Verbraucherzentrale bereits wegen irreführender Werbung erfolgreich abgemahnt.
;)) Heiße Mädchen warten auf dich — Miss4.fun

articles.title: McDonald's Japan data breach exposes customer location information
articles.text:
McDonald's Japan, the fast-food giant's Japanese subsidiary, has disclosed a data breach after attackers accessed a database containing sensitive information for users of the company's official smartphone app.
Founded in 1940, McDonald's is now a multinational fast-food chain that operates more than 40,000 restaurants in more than 100 countries and serves tens of millions of customers daily.
In a Friday statement, the company's Japanese subsidiary confirmed that threat actors gained access to its official app's database and said the exposed information includes the users' product purchase history, IP addresses, mobile device location data, and customer management IDs (which cannot be used to identify the customers' email addresses or member IDs).
McDonald's Japan also added that the exposed data doesn't include the affected customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, or credit card information.
While it has yet to reveal when it detected the attack or how many individuals had their data stolen, the company said a follow-up investigation found no service disruption or misuse of official apps as a result of the incident.
"We are working to invalidate any credentials used for unauthorized access, investigate the relevant systems, and report to the Personal Information Protection Commission," it said. "In addition, we will strive to strengthen security measures and prevent recurrence."
This isn't the first data breach to affect McDonald's in recent years, with the fast food giant disclosing a breach in June 2021 after attackers breached its systems and stole information belonging to employees and customers from the US, South Korea, and Taiwan.
In 2017, McDonald's also patched a cross-site scripting (XSS) security flaw that affected its official website and exposed customers' plain-text passwords.
Japanese companies under attack
Last month, Burger King Japan also disclosed a major data breach after attackers stole 11.18 million customer records that were later leaked online.
The two incidents affecting the two Japanese fast food chains add to a large wave of cyberattacks impacting high-profile Japanese companies since the start of the year, including Japan Airlines, entertainment system maker Daiichi Kosho, cloud and digital infrastructure firm IDC Frontier, Japanese publishing giant Nikkei, cloud and data center service provider Sakura Internet, taxi operator Nihon Kotsu, telecommunications giant KDDI, and many others.
Macnica researcher Yutaka Sejiyama has logged 288 cybersecurity incidents affecting Japanese organizations involving personal information theft or exposure since the start of the year.
Sejiyama found that attackers are now probing websites and APIs for access-control, configuration, and authentication weaknesses, and exploiting known (n-day) vulnerabilities to find other victims.

Good morning! ☀️️️
Jensen Huang was quite possibly the happiest man in tech yesterday. The name most synonymous with NVIDIA and the graphics processing units (GPUs) powering the AI boom is back at the helm.
After a tough couple of weeks in which revelations about Huang’s personal life became public, and he resigned as chief executive officer, NVIDIA’s board reinstated him on Monday as President, CEO, and Board Director. The stock market seemed to love the decision: NVIDIA shares surged more than 30% after the announcement, adding nearly $1 trillion to the company’s market value and reversing much of the previous rout.
Good one for Huang. But he wasn’t the only one celebrating yesterday. We also did a thing: TechCabal launched TC Mzansi after months of brainstorming and refining the product. The reception has been worth every drop of sweat we put into making it happen. Key ecosystem leaders have already signed up to read the newsletter every week. I’m not sure why you’re still stalling, but if you change your mind, subscribe here.
—Emmanuel
TC Mzansi, our newsletter covering South African tech, launches today.
Features
From Phathisani: Why TC Mzansi needed to exist
Yesterday, I had the pleasure of seeing the first edition of our latest newsletter, TC Mzansi, land in readers’ inboxes for the very first time. It is an exciting milestone, not just because we are launching a new newsletter, but because we are creating space for stories I believe deserve a much bigger audience.
When we started thinking about TC Mzansi, one question kept coming up: are we telling enough stories about the innovation happening right on our doorstep?
South Africa’s tech ecosystem is often viewed through big funding rounds, established startups, and headline-grabbing deals. Those stories matter, but they are only part of the picture. Across townships, rural communities, university labs, and smaller cities, young entrepreneurs are building solutions to everyday problems, often with limited resources but plenty of ingenuity.
That is the gap TC Mzansi wants to close.
The name was deliberate. Mzansi is more than an informal name for South Africa. It speaks to our identity, diversity, and the communities that make this country the Rainbow Nation. We wanted a product rooted in our realities, giving a platform to stories that rarely make the mainstream technology conversation.
Every edition will bring you closer to the people, businesses, and ideas shaping our digital future. Expect startup stories, emerging technologies, investment developments, policy shifts, and innovation beyond the major tech hubs. We will also explore connections between South Africa and the wider Southern African Development Community (SADC) region.
For me, TC Mzansi is about widening the lens. Innovation doesn’t only happen in boardrooms or venture capital meetings. Sometimes, it starts with someone in a township solving a community problem.
Those are the stories worth telling. And we’re here to tell them.
If you missed yesterday’s edition, you can still read it here. But you mustn’t miss the stories I’ve got in store for you next Monday; subscribe here.

M&A
Shoprite buys 40% stake in telecoms group
Shoprite started out selling groceries. Then it began helping customers send money and pay bills. Afterward, it launched its own mobile service. Now, the retailer is making a bigger play.
What happened? Shoprite, South Africa’s largest grocery retailer, is buying a 40% stake in DN Invest (DNI) for about R3.6 billion ($206.8 million). DNI is an investment group with interests in telecoms, fibre Internet, mobile devices, and fintech, with a portfolio that includes 3G Mobile, a SIM and handset distributor; Frogfoot, a fibre network operator; Vox Telecom, an Internet service provider; and Hypa, which provides affordable fibre services.
Explain like I’m new here: Shoprite has been building a financial services business alongside its grocery operations. It launched the Money Market Account in 2022, giving customers a low-cost transactional account to pay bills and send money, and offers money transfers through Shoprite Send. The retailer also operates K’nect Mobile, a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO), launched in March 2021, that sells prepaid airtime and data. It does not own the mobile towers that carry calls and internet traffic; instead, it uses Cell C’s network.
What does Shoprite get out of this? The deal gives Shoprite access to companies that sell SIM cards and phones, provide internet services, and build digital financial products, giving it a faster route to expanding beyond its existing offering. DNI generates more than R11 billion ($631.9 million) in annual revenue and over R1.2 billion ($68.9 million) in earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA). Shoprite also has the option to eventually buy the remaining shares, potentially taking its ownership to 100%, subject to agreed terms and regulatory approval.

Telecoms
Absa partners with Vodacom to combine banking and mobile services
South African banks—and even retailers (read: Shoprite)—are getting into the telecoms business, but Absa, the country’s third-largest lender by assets, has decided to take a different route. Instead of launching its own mobile network like rivals Capitec and FNB, the banking giant has partnered with Vodacom, the country’s largest mobile operator by subscribers.
Together, they plan to offer customers a mix of banking services, mobile connectivity, loyalty rewards, and smartphone financing. The partnership could give Absa a way into the mobile market without having to run its own network.
Explain like I’m new here: In South Africa, banks have discovered that mobile connectivity can be another way to keep customers using their services. Tier 1 banks, including Capitec, FNB, Standard Bank, and Nedbank, all operate bank-branded mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) services. As MVNOs, banks run mobile networks that rely on white-label services from telecom operators. FNB Connect and Capitec Connect use Cell C’s infrastructure, while Standard Bank Connect and Nedbank Connect use MTN’s network.
Banks explore this route to deepen customer loyalty, create more reasons for people to use their apps and generate revenue from services beyond traditional banking.
State of play: In October 2025, Absa told local publication TechCentral that it was preparing to launch an MVNO and had spent six months researching what would persuade customers to switch to an Absa-branded SIM card. However, by June, Absa said it was still assessing different MVNO models and wanted to ensure any offering delivered real value, according to TechCentral.
But it appears the delay will not be a denial, as Absa is now trying to kick things into full gear. Yet, Absa seems cautious; the approach feels on-brand for a bank that chose to partner with blockchain firm Ripple to expand into crypto custody in August—at least recently.
Absa has not said why it moved from preparing an MVNO launch to partnering with Vodacom. However, the partnership makes sense at a glance; Vodacom will provide the connectivity andAbsa brings its banking services and customer relationships. Each company will continue managing its own customers. Absa gets to offer mobile services without the expense and complexity of running a network itself.

Economy
Africa’s cheap phones aren’t so cheap anymore
You walk into a phone shop looking for a basic Android. Nothing fancy, just something that can run WhatsApp, your banking app, and maybe take decent pictures. The seller tells you the price, and suddenly you’re asking about fairly used phones instead.
Across Africa, even the cheapest smartphones are becoming harder to afford.
According to research firm Omdia, smartphone shipments across the continent fell 40% to 13.7 million units in Q3 2026, down from 22.8 million in the previous year.
Explain like I’m new here: Shipments are the phones manufacturers send to shops and distributors, not necessarily the number customers buy. But they offer a useful picture of demand. When phones become harder to sell, manufacturers and retailers order fewer of them.
State of play: Nigeria recorded the steepest decline among major markets, at 47%, followed by Egypt at 41% and Kenya at 35%. South Africa fared better, with a 20% drop, partly because more buyers can spread payments through mobile contracts.
Between the lines: The biggest decline was among smartphones priced below $100, where shipments plunged nearly 70%. Meanwhile, basic feature-phone shipments grew 27%.
Here’s the problem: Rising manufacturing costs are making cheap smartphones less profitable to produce. Manufacturers are raising prices or reconsidering those models, while customers who can’t afford the increase keep their old phones or buy secondhand (fairly used devices).
Africa’s average smartphone price even reached $222, a ten-year third-quarter high. But buyers aren’t necessarily upgrading to better phones. Many are simply being priced out of new ones.
Zoom out: Omdia expects shipments to fall another 25% in 2027. Companies like M-KOPA and Vodacom are offering instalment payments to help buyers, but spreading the cost doesn’t reduce it. If even a basic smartphone requires a payment plan, getting connected becomes another household expense people have to budget for carefully.

articles.title: Huang reportedly admitted to more than two affairs to Nvidia's board
articles.text:
In a complete U-turn, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO and president of the chipmaker, just a fortnight after he resigned.
During a meeting before his reinstatement, however, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Early in November, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a letter to employees. At the time, he was ostensibly talking about his relationship with Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (not related to Jensen). Later, it was reported that he’d also had a relationship with Nvidia’s VP of health, Kimberly Powell.
Afterwards, Reuters reported that he also had an affair with another employee.
It’s not clear which affairs Huang admitted to during this recent conversation with Nvidia’s board of directors.
Huang’s return was spurred by a personal intervention from the U.S. government, Nvidia’s board said in a statement on Monday, and President Donald Trump apparently called the board to bat for Huang’s reinstatement.
The Wall Street Journal reports that over the weekend, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance that the Justice Department wasn’t investigating Huang and there was no evidence that he was a national security risk, after which both contacted the company’s board.
Huang received a “hero’s welcome” at Nvidia’s HQ, with several employees applauding his return.

articles.title: Cómo bajar el brillo del iPhone más allá del mínimo con la función Reducir punto blanco
articles.text:
La pantalla del iPhone puede seguir resultando intensa aun cuando el regulador de brillo está cerca del mínimo. Para esos casos, Reducir punto blanco incorpora una capa adicional de ajuste que rebaja la fuerza de los colores más luminosos. La herramienta forma parte de las opciones de Accesibilidad de Apple y se controla desde los ajustes del sistema.
El recurso puede ser útil al leer de noche, consultar mensajes en una habitación con poca luz o utilizar el teléfono antes de dormir. No cambia el contenido de las aplicaciones ni reemplaza la configuración de brillo, pero permite combinar ambos controles. Esta guía reúne datos clave, la ruta para activarlo y un método para tenerlo disponible mediante un atajo.
Qué hace Reducir punto blanco en el iPhone
Reducir punto blanco disminuye la intensidad de los blancos y de otros tonos muy claros que muestra el panel. Al activarlo, la interfaz, las páginas web, las fotografías y los menús se perciben menos brillantes. El efecto se aplica a toda la pantalla, de modo que no requiere modificar una aplicación por vez ni cambiar el contenido guardado en el dispositivo.
La opción incluye un control deslizante para definir el nivel de reducción. Cuanto más alto sea el porcentaje elegido, más tenue se verá la imagen. Conviene probarlo junto al regulador de brillo habitual, disponible desde el Centro de control o en Ajustes > Pantalla y brillo. El resultado depende del modelo, el contenido visual y la luz del lugar.
Dónde se encuentra el ajuste para reducir el punto blanco
La ruta general dentro de iOS es Ajustes > Accesibilidad > Pantalla y tamaño del texto > Reducir punto blanco. Al ingresar en ese apartado aparece un interruptor para habilitar la función. Debajo se muestra el regulador que permite aumentar o disminuir el efecto sin salir de la misma pantalla.
Los nombres de los menús pueden presentar ligeras variaciones según el idioma del teléfono o la versión instalada de iOS. Si no se localiza la función, una alternativa es usar el campo de búsqueda de Ajustes y escribir “Reducir punto blanco”. La herramienta se integra en el menú de visualización de Accesibilidad, junto a otros controles relacionados con el contraste y los colores.
Cómo se activa y se ajusta la intensidad
Primero hay que abrir Ajustes, tocar Accesibilidad y seleccionar Pantalla y tamaño del texto. Luego se debe buscar Reducir punto blanco y mover el interruptor a la posición activa. En ese instante, el iPhone modifica la apariencia del panel y habilita el control de porcentaje, que puede desplazarse hacia la izquierda o la derecha.
Para definir una intensidad adecuada, es preferible observar texto, fondos claros e imágenes mientras se mueve el regulador. Un valor moderado puede ser suficiente en interiores poco iluminados; un nivel alto genera una reducción más marcada. El cambio es reversible de inmediato: basta con desactivar el interruptor o volver a ajustar el porcentaje cuando la pantalla deba verse con mayor luminosidad.
Puede usarse junto al brillo automático y Night Shift
Reducir punto blanco funciona de manera independiente del brillo automático. Esta otra función adapta la iluminación de la pantalla a las condiciones del entorno cuando está habilitada. Por eso, el iPhone puede mantener activas ambas opciones: una reduce la intensidad de los tonos claros y la otra modifica el brillo general conforme cambia la luz ambiental.
También es posible combinarla con Night Shift, que modifica la temperatura de color de la pantalla durante un horario definido o hasta el día siguiente. Night Shift reduce los tonos fríos, mientras que Reducir punto blanco disminuye la intensidad de los elementos brillantes. Cada ajuste afecta un aspecto distinto de la visualización, por lo que sus efectos pueden acumularse.
Qué conviene revisar si la pantalla queda muy tenue
Si la pantalla parece oscura incluso al aumentar el brillo, el primer paso es comprobar si Reducir punto blanco permanece activado y qué porcentaje tiene configurado. También se puede abrir el Centro de control para subir el brillo. Estas dos revisiones permiten distinguir si la menor luminosidad proviene del regulador común o de la opción de accesibilidad.
En caso de que el efecto no responda como se espera, conviene desactivar temporalmente Night Shift y verificar los ajustes de Pantalla y brillo. La ubicación exacta de las herramientas puede cambiar con las actualizaciones de iOS, pero la búsqueda dentro de Ajustes ayuda a encontrarlas. El interruptor de Reducir punto blanco conserva el último porcentaje elegido hasta que el usuario lo modifique.

articles.title: La mejor oferta del Black Friday en auriculares solo estará disponible durante unas horas

MediaMarkt ha vuelto a lanzar una de sus mejores ofertas a través de su sección de Ofertas del Día con unos Sony WH-1000XM4C a muy buen precio. Los auriculares de la marca se pueden comprar ahora mismo por 188 euros (antes 279 euros), pero solo durante unas horas: la oferta finalizará mañana, 25 de noviembre, a las 09:00 horas.

Por otro lado, si bien es cierto que el diseño y la cancelación activa de ruido se mantiene igual, sí que hay cambios en el sonido. En este sentido, los Sony WH-1000XM4C ahora cuentan con 10 ecualizadores, un modo juego y un botón Quick Access para utilizar apps como YouTube Music o Apple Music, entre otras.

articles.title: Un immense centre de données IA de Meta s’installe près de chez lui, il monte un business lucratif qui livre de l'eau aux ouvriers du chantier pour 21 900 € par semaine
articles.text:
Un immense centre de données IA de Meta s’installe près de chez lui, il monte un business lucratif qui livre de l'eau aux ouvriers du chantier pour 21 900 € par semaine
David Rodgers habite près du chantier du plus grand centre de données IA de Meta en Louisiane. Lui est alors venu l’idée de fonder la société Ice Queen. Son business ? livrer de l'eau aux ouvriers du site. Et c’est très lucratif : les entreprises de construction lui achètent chaque palette plusieurs jusqu'à 21 900 € par semaine.
Le centre de données IA de Meta s'appelle Hyperion et est bâti en ce moment même près de Holly Ridge. C'est en décembre 2024 que les travaux ont commencé aux abords de cette communauté rurale et agricole du nord-est de l'État. Certains résidents ont alors eu l'idée de créer leur entreprise pour répondre aux besoins des milliers d'ouvriers du chantier. Ice Queen fait partie de ces sociétés lucratives.
Ice Queen vend de l'eau aux entreprises du chantier
En 2025, David Rodgers l'a lancée avec Linda Edwards, son ancienne associée. Les deux fondateurs vendent des sacs de glace à 3 $ pièce, soit environ 2,75 €. Les produits sont conservés dans une semi-remorque garée près du site et les livraisons se font avec un camion distinct.
Ice Queen propose aussi des machines à café, des gobelets, des réfrigérateurs et des micro-ondes aux équipes. Et ce n'est pas tout puisqu'elle vend des sachets d'électrolytes Liquid I.V. que Linda Edwards a décrits comme des produits essentiels pour des ouvriers très déshydratés.
"C'est sur les palettes d'eau que nous faisons le plus d'argent, parce que c'est une question de sécurité. La chaleur et tout ça", a expliqué David Rodgers au média étasunien Business Insider. Les journalistes ont relevé près de 37 degrés pendant leur reportage.
David Rodgers achète l'eau par camions entiers et achemine chaque semaine de 30 à 40 palettes vers les entreprises du site. Ice Queen les facture environ 600 $ pièce, soit près de 550 €. À ce rythme, ces livraisons représentent un chiffre d'affaires hebdomadaire de 18 000 à 24 000 $, soit environ 16 400 à 21 900 €.
En juillet 2026, Meta a annoncé un investissement de plus de 50 milliards de dollars dans Hyperion. On parle de bâtiments qui totaliseront près de 93 hectares pour une puissance informatique de 5 gigawatts. Au pic des travaux, le chantier sera mené par plus de 7 500 ouvriers.
Un business lucratif mais des nuisances
En 2025, le café HeBrews Coffee & Eats de la commune voisine de Rayville a ouvert une deuxième adresse face au site avec un point de vente qui vend 450 repas aux équipes deux fois par mois. "Nous avons préparé 900 burritos et 2 500 cafés lors de la semaine consacrée à la sécurité", a raconté Shelbie Stephenson, responsable de cet établissement.
En avril 2025, Tim Allen a ouvert la taqueria Holy Tacos à Rayville. Ses prestations de traiteur pour le chantier ? 4 000 à 7 000 $, soit environ 3 650 à 6 400 €. Il a estimé qu'environ 40 % de son activité mensuelle dépend directement de Meta.
En revanche, les résidents interrogés par Business Insider ont dénoncé le trafic près de l'école primaire de Holly Ridge, le bruit, la poussière et l'éclairage nocturne. Des reproches que l'on retrouve dans la bouche de nombreuses personnes qui vivent près d'un centre de données face à une forte activité très polluante.
Meta a répondu en annonçant près de 270 millions de dollars investis dans les routes locales et l'installation de nouveaux feux de circulation. Pas sûr que cela fasse baisser les nuisances que dénoncent les habitants.

articles.title: EEUU sigue soñando con su tren de alta velocidad: California puso la primera piedra hace casi 12 años, ha gastado más que el AVE Madrid-Barcelona y aún no transporta pasajeros
articles.text:
El tren de alta velocidad de California es un proyecto que tiene una idea muy clara. Para cualquier europeo resultará familiar. Se trata de crear un nuevo tren que conecte dos grandes ciudades. En el caso de esta línea serán San Francisco y Los Ángeles (en menos de tres horas). Para ello se van a construir trenes capaces de circular a más de 350 km/h.
La primera piedra oficial se colocó en Fresno el 6 de enero de 2015. Hasta noviembre de 2026 han pasado casi 12 años. Antes están los años de planificación y contratación. Hay una auditoría estatal que indica que se dio el visto bueno para empezar a trabajar en octubre de 2013.
Hay que diferenciar entre los gastos realizados y las previsiones del plan de negocio de 2026. Hasta febrero se han invertido 15.041 millones de dólares (aproximadamente 12.700 millones de euros). Es más que la construcción del AVE Madrid-Barcelona (8.966,7 millones de euros), pero no es exactamente comparable por el año y alcance de la obra. Además, no hay corrección de inflación. En cuanto a la cantidad total del proyecto californiano, son unos 126.100 millones de dólares.
Una línea que debía abrir en 2020
Los californianos aprobaron en 2008 bonos por unos 10.000 millones de dólares para desarrollar alta velocidad. El plan de ese año estimaba que se invertirían unos 33.000 millones de dólares. La fecha de apertura inicial estaba prevista en 2020, pero esto quedó en el pasado sin ponerlo en marcha.
Lo que se pretendía era unir todo el territorio (norte-sur) con futuras prolongaciones hacia Sacramento y San Diego. Las obras se concentran en el Valle Central (entre Merced y Bakersfield). Se están haciendo viaductos y cruces a distinto nivel, traslados de servicios y, además, se está preparando la plataforma sobre la que irán los trenes.
Aún hay que transformar todas estas obras en un ferrocarril (para pasajeros). En el contrato de vías se ha fijado que debería empezar a tenderse el 30 de noviembre de 2026. Además de la propia vía, se incluyen otros elementos como electrificación, control de trenes y comunicaciones. Se prevé que en 2032-2033 se complete el primer tramo operativo.
Los terrenos y la financiación retrasaron la obra
Algunos de los problemas eran conocidos. En una auditoría estatal de 2018 se concluía que se había contratado la construcción sin contar con todos los terrenos necesarios. También había algunas dificultades pendientes de acuerdos de traslados de redes de servicios. Como consecuencia de estas demoras, se han tenido que incorporar costes adicionales (personal, material y maquinaria).
También ha habido problemas de financiación (los fondos están divididos) y de cambios políticos. Aún hay más, ya que no está garantizado todo el dinero necesario para completar la conexión entre San Francisco y Los Ángeles.
Lo único claro es que California continúa trabajando en su sistema de alta velocidad, aunque han pasado casi 12 años desde que se puso la primera piedra, y no tienen un servicio de pasajeros.

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
  November 12, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Santa Barbara. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:

Deep learning-based control of electrically evoked activity in human visual cortex. Neuron, 2026; DOI: 10.1016/j.neuron.2026.07.006

articles.title: Check Point Security Management Servers Hacked in AI-Assisted Campaign
articles.text:
A threat actor has been using AI-enabled offensive tools in a broad campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers, threat intelligence firm GreyNoise reports.
As part of the campaign, which the security firm started tracking in early October and is likely still ongoing, a threat actor tracked as GreyNoise Threat 13 (GT13) has been conducting scanning, exploitation, and control activities from 99 IP addresses, many associated with disposable network infrastructure.
According to GreyNoise, GT13 targeted at least 22 organizations from the energy, engineering, financial services, government, manufacturing, mining, and transportation sectors across the US, the UK, Australia, Austria, China, France, Germany, Hong Kong, the Netherlands, South Korea, and other geographies.
GreyNoise believes the threat actor has been using agentic harnesses and systems to weaponize vulnerabilities, find vulnerable assets, and automatically exploit them. The automated operations were complemented by hands-on-keyboard activity.
“We witnessed the GT13 actor use 99 IP addresses, all of which were either egresses through ExpressVPN or compromised victim Check Point devices, including activity over 1400+ network sessions, 800+ command line artifacts, and 1200+ files downloaded, uploaded, or created,” GreyNoise says.
In one instance, GreyNoise tracked the activity to October 2, when the threat actor forged a signed admin session cookie to gain administrative access to an HFS server. The attacker obtained SSH access to the server, which was used to scan the environment and exfiltrate data.
“The GT13 adversary had access to the victim Check Point Security Management servers before they compromised the HFS server. We could not determine when or how the attacker gained access to those Check Point assets,” the company notes.
The attacker deployed tools such as Nmap, Chisel, Impacket, Paramiko, and other Python utilities and scripts, performed reconnaissance, lateral movement, and privilege escalation. They used one victim’s server as a hop to save command results and data exfiltrated from 24 previously compromised Check Point Security Management servers.
Between October 20 and 26, in addition to gaining deeper access to the victim’s environment, the threat actor conducted bulk actions against 21 other victim Check Point devices. GT13 issued a bulk certificate-management task to 24 servers across the 22 organizations. The task failed, but the threat actor collected the responses on the relay server in text files.
“These files contained the victim IP addresses and were in incrementing IP order, indicating an automation looped through them to run the commands on the compromised Check Point servers and deliver them via scp to this exfil folder. Each file was delivered from victim infrastructure, showing that each of the compromised devices holds the SSH private key that matches the public key planted on the hop,” GreyNoise says.
The activity within the first victim’s environment also involved the use or attempted exploitation of vulnerabilities such as CVE-2026-61500 (Rejetto HFS), CVE-2023-4966 and CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole), CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF), CVE-2020-1472 and CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2021-26855 and CVE-2021-34473 (Microsoft Exchange), and CVE-2021-21972 and CVE-2023-34048 (VMware vCenter).
GreyNoise says it confirmed threat actor activity against Check Point Security Management servers between October 17 and November 2, when it stopped observing it. However, the company believes the campaign is still ongoing as GT13 had persistent access to the compromised servers.
“We believe the actor has separate agentic harnesses and systems weaponizing vulnerabilities, scanning for vulnerable assets, and automatically exploiting them to gather sets of systems that can be later used for operational relays or true targets. We suspect some of the foibles in the timeline reflect agentic offensive operations,” GreyNoise notes.

articles.title: Frankfurt-based CommerzVentures closes €50 million Fund IV, betting on early-stage FinTech and AI
articles.text:
CommerzVentures, a Frankfurt-based specialist venture capital firm focused on financial services, has closed its fourth fund at €50 million.
The fourth fund — CommerzVentures IV (Fund IV) — is anchored by Commerzbank and is deliberately smaller than its predecessors; the firm managed over €550 million across three prior funds, including €300 million in Fund III.
“Fund IV is deliberately smaller because we want to invest earlier. We aim to combine early conviction with the experience, industry connections and hands-on support founders need to build their businesses,” said Judith Vogel, Partner, CommerzVentures.
Founded in 2014, CommerzVentures is a specialist financial services investor having backed more than 40 companies across its three previous funds. Its notable portfolio companies include eToro, iwoca, Mambu, and Marqeta, several of which have gone on to achieve significant scale or public listings.
The CommerzVentures IV is jointly led by general partners Heiko Schwender and Vogel, supported by venture partners and senior advisers. The pair have backed companies including Deblock, eToro, Marqeta, and Unique, supporting these startups through major growth phases, and in some cases, through to public listing.
With Fund IV, CommerzVentures is making a strategic shift from its past funds to focus on earlier-stage investing. It argues this shift also reflects a maturing FinTech ecosystem, with the strongest companies reaching revenue faster, scaling more quickly, and moving through funding rounds at a pace that rewards investors who come in earliest.
“In financial services, a strong AI product is only the starting point. Founders also need to earn trust, navigate regulation, and connect to complex infrastructure. That is where our experience and network can make a difference,” said Schwender, Partner, CommerzVentures.
The firm says the new fund will back founders building at the intersection of AI and financial services, though it will also selectively back adjacent sectors such as supply chain and cybersecurity, where its financial services expertise and network can add tangible value.
CommerzVentures says its co-founders, Patrick Meisberger and Stefan Tirtey, will continue overseeing CommerzVentures’ existing funds. “We are proud of what CommerzVentures has built together with our founders, our team and Commerzbank as anchor investor. We are delighted to see Heiko and Judith lead Fund IV into its next chapter,” said Meisberger.
The Fund IV will deploy capital at Seed and early Series A stages, primarily across the EU, the UK and Switzerland. CommerzVentures plans to build a portfolio of around 25 companies with Fund IV and ,with its new investment thesis, the firm is positioning itself to catch the next wave of FinTech and AI innovation at its earliest stages.

articles.title: Databricks has “very strong growth plans” for Canada
articles.text:
San Francisco-based data and AI platform Databricks, which already employs more than 500 people across Canada, intends to expand its presence in the country over the coming years.
The privately held software giant first began building a presence in Canada about seven years ago. Today, Databricks has around 300 employees at its Vancouver research and development hub, and “well over” 200 in Toronto, predominantly in go-to-market (GTM) positions.
Canada is a “tier-one” market
Since 2024, Databricks has grown its Canadian business by over 125 percent. In an interview with BetaKit, Databricks vice-president and general manager of Canada, Jim Lambe, said the firm sees a lot more room to expand with Canadian companies operating in energy, financial services, retail, technology, and telecommunications, as well as public sector organizations.
Lambe said Databricks considers Canada a “tier-one” market, revealing that the business has some “very strong growth plans for the country over the next 12 to 24 months,” as it builds out its local GTM, solution engineering, and forward-deployed engineering (FDE) teams.
Since 2024, Databricks has grown its Canadian business by over 125 percent.
“We’re building out all of those teams here in Canada,” Lambe added.
Databricks sells software designed to help other businesses and organizations store, manage, and analyze data, and build AI products. The company’s Canadian clients include Hydro-Québec, Rogers Communications, and TD Bank.
Two of Databricks’ co-founders, CTO Matei Zaharia and chief architect Reynold Xin, also have ties to Canada: Zaharia grew up in Toronto and attended the University of Waterloo, while Xin studied at the University of Toronto.
Lambe, who joined Databricks in June 2025 to help expand the company’s presence in Canada, did not disclose any specific hiring targets.
At the moment, Databricks’ current job postings list 27 open roles in Canada across both technical and sales-oriented functions.
RELATED: Databricks and Ada execs on what’s fuelling the Gen Z AI backlash
Lambe said FDEs in particular will be “a huge focus” as prospective customers seek “a more guided journey” to adopting AI.
On the back of strong investor demand for companies supporting the AI boom, The Wall Street Journal recently reported that Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars in a new funding round that would value the company at about $225 billion USD ($323 billion CAD).
Lambe said Databricks’ Canadian customers are leveraging AI for everything from real-time financial fraud detection to analyzing investor calls and regulating how oil and gas flow.
“What’s really interesting about what we’re starting to see in Canada is each one of the industries that we talked about … are going deeper and deeper and deeper into their use and adoption of AI,” Lambe added.

articles.title: ‘Bye AI music’: Tidal announces full ban on AI-generated songs — as Deezer reveals 57% of people have AI tunes lurking in their playlists
articles.text:
Tidal says it’s ‘banning’ AI music from December — streaming giant will delete 27 million songs from its library and reject 80,000 AI-generated tracks a day
Making music human again
- Tidal says it's banning all 100% AI-generated music from its service
- The policy will start from December 9 and lead to 29 million track deletions
- Meanwhile, Deezer research has discovered most music streaming users unknowingly have AI music in their playlists
As Spotify gears up to launch its AI-powered remix and covers feature in 2027, Tidal is moving in the opposite direction — announcing today that it’s banning all AI-generated tracks from its platform, starting on December 9.
The news, announced on X, follows its decision back in July to demonetize and label 100% AI-generated recordings. This time, it’s getting rid of them completely. This will result in roughly 29 million songs being deleted, and an estimated 80,000-85,000 rejected songs per day.
It's also a move that makes sense for Tidal, with the streaming service revealing that roughly 6% of its catalog is currently AI-generated, and that roughly 43% of all tracks added over the last 90 days have been AI.
However, there’s clearly not much appetite for those tracks, because 96% of all AI-badged tracks got zero streams in the last 90 days.
Unpopular yet hard to avoid
Recent research from rival Deezer suggests the public have little interest in listening to AI music — and that when AI music is listened to, it’s often done so unknowingly. The streaming service's "international barometer", conducted by Ipsos across nine countries this month, concluded that while 57% of people now have fully AI-generated music in their playlists, 74% of people don’t think they do.
It also found that 67% of people fear that AI could reduce creativity in music production, and 69% believe that AI-generated music threatens the livelihood of musicians.
Based on those numbers, it’s safe to say that fully AI-generated music isn’t particularly popular and risks clogging up music services. The more AI-generated tracks there are in circulation, the more people will unknowingly listen to them — or become more accepting of the idea, which could harm the industry in the long term.

Tidal's decisive step will, then, likely prove a popular one with listeners. Spotify has, to be fair, recently introduced its AI Persona tags to help you differentiate real artists from AI-generated ones. But it might require a stronger stand from Spotify and Apple Music before fully AI-generated is once again banished to the margins.

articles.title: Amazon says hackers’ AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
articles.text:
Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.
The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.
“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said.
Made for defenders, but attackers like it too
Cairn is an open source AI problem-solving engine whose first validated domain is autonomous penetration testing. Users give it a task or goal and, optionally, hints for achieving it. A server maintains a shared graph containing facts and hints. A dispatcher reads the graph, schedules tasks, manages containers, and writes the protocol. The dispatcher can then assign each project to a dedicated worker container, each of which runs multiple agents concurrently. Cairn is model-agnostic and can be used on worker back ends, including Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Researchers from security firm Palo Alto Networks have also observed Cairn being used with GLM 5.2, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and DeepSeek V4 Pro.
Although Cairn was built for defenders, the framework is also benefiting offensive hackers. Earlier this month, Palo Alto Networks said hackers used the framework to target organizations in the semiconductor, defense, and civil society sectors.
