articles.title: Austrália ameaça Google e Meta com multas de até 5% da receita global
articles.text:
A Austrália está preparando legislação que pode impor multas de até 5% da receita global de empresas, como Google e Meta, caso elas não adotem medidas para impedir a circulação de conteúdos nocivos em suas plataformas. A proposta faz parte de pacote de regras que pretende responsabilizar empresas de tecnologia pelos riscos presentes em seus serviços digitais.
O acordo foi negociado entre o governo australiano e o partido Os Verdes, abrindo caminho para a aprovação parlamentar ainda nesta semana. A iniciativa estabelece obrigação de cuidado digital (Digital Duty of Care), que exige que as empresas identifiquem e reduzam riscos antes que eles provoquem danos aos usuários.
A proposta também prevê que indivíduos possam processar plataformas por prejuízos sofridos no ambiente digital. Com isso, a legislação amplia a responsabilização das companhias, que poderão enfrentar consequências financeiras e judiciais caso não cumpram as novas exigências.
Quais conteúdos poderão gerar multas?
A legislação pretende alcançar diferentes tipos de material considerado prejudicial, incluindo:
- Abuso sexual infantil;
- Imagens íntimas falsas divulgadas sem consentimento;
- Violência de gênero;
- Conteúdos que incentivem automutilação;
- Material relacionado ao terrorismo.
O projeto também busca combater recursos considerados viciantes nas plataformas digitais, ampliando a responsabilidade das empresas sobre a maneira como seus serviços são projetados e utilizados.
A proposta não se limita às redes sociais. O conjunto de regras abrange diferentes serviços digitais, incluindo aplicativos, mecanismos de busca e chatbots de inteligência artificial (IA).
Leia mais:
- Tesla e SpaceX negociam fusão de US$ 3,5 trilhões até o fim do ano
- Huawei é condenada por roubo de segredos comerciais nos EUA
- Ex-funcionário da OpenAI acusado de espionagem será solto com fiança milionária
Multas podem chegar a 5% da receita global
- Um dos pontos mais significativos da negociação é o aumento das penalidades financeiras;
- A proposta anterior estabelecia um limite de 109 milhões de dólares australianos para determinadas violações. Com o acordo entre o governo e Os Verdes, o teto poderá chegar a 5% da receita global das empresas;
- A mudança aumenta consideravelmente a exposição financeira de gigantes, como Google e Meta, cujas operações movimentam bilhões de dólares anualmente;
- Além das multas, a possibilidade de processos individuais representa outra frente de pressão. Usuários poderão buscar reparação judicial quando sofrerem danos relacionados à atuação das plataformas.
Empresas temem remoção excessiva de conteúdo
Embora o setor de tecnologia reconheça a importância de proteger usuários, especialmente crianças e pessoas vulneráveis, as novas regras também provocam preocupação entre empresas e representantes da indústria.
Uma das principais críticas envolve a definição do que será considerado conteúdo prejudicial. As companhias temem que a possibilidade de multas elevadas incentive uma moderação excessivamente rigorosa, levando à remoção de publicações mesmo quando não houver violação clara das regras.
O receio é que as plataformas passem a retirar conteúdos preventivamente para evitar penalidades, afetando também materiais legítimos e discussões públicas.
O debate coloca a Austrália diante de desafio regulatório: ampliar a proteção dos usuários sem criar incentivos para restrições excessivas à circulação de informações na internet.
Com o acordo político, o país avança em proposta que pode estabelecer novas obrigações para grandes empresas de tecnologia e influenciar o debate internacional sobre a responsabilidade das plataformas digitais.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: TikTok was down
articles.text:
Earlier on Tuesday, TikTok experienced some issues, with videos, search results, favorites, and other features not loading as they usually do, following a slew of other outages over the past couple of weeks. Videos sometimes wouldn’t load in the For You feed on my iPhone, and search results occasionally didn’t show up as expected in the app on iOS or Android, or on the web.
TikTok was down
TikTok says a ‘brief technical issue’ impacted access to the platform.
Even trying to pull up a profile would show a blank page, while links to videos are dead in the water too. However, as of 3:45PM ET or so, things appear to be working normally again. Downdetector showed around 25,000 reports of issues at around 2:56PM ET, and many people on social media were saying that TikTok was down for them.
“We experienced a brief technical issue that impacted access to TikTok,” TikTok’s Jessica Casano-Antonellis tells The Verge. “The issue has been resolved. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.”
Update, November 24th: Added statement from TikTok.

articles.title: Adyen’s co-founder Pieter van der Does to retire as Co-CEO; Ingo Uytdehaage to become sole CEO
articles.text:
Pieter van der Does, co-founder and Co-CEO of Dutch Fintech Adyen, is stepping down from his executive role after 20 years at the helm of one of Europe’s most prominent technology companies.
In an announcement on 23 November 2026, marking Adyen’s 20th anniversary, the company said van der Does will retire on 31 December 2026, and Ingo Uytdehaage, Co-CEO since 2023, will become sole CEO
“After 20 years, this is the right moment for me to step down on a positive note and with a very good feeling. Adyen has been my life’s work, and I’m incredibly proud of what our teams and customers have built together over the past two decades. Ingo and I have worked very closely together as Co-CEOs, and now we have completed the transition,” said van der Does, co-founder and co-CEO of Adyen.
Arnout Schuijff and van der Does launched Adyen in 2006, and the company was formally incorporated on 23 November 2006, when Schuijff visited a notary in Amsterdam to formally establish the company. Van der Does, who was on a sabbatical in Brazil at the time, followed the proceedings remotely over Skype.
Before starting Adyen, the co-founders had previously worked together at payments company Bibit, and their shared ambition became Adyen, which means “doing it again” in Surinamese. In his farewell letter, Van der Does says, “Adyen outgrew our wildest imagination.”
Since its early days in Amsterdam, Adyen has grown into a global FinTech processing more than €1.4 trillion annually. It serves over one billion shoppers per year across more than 29 offices worldwide and counts customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, eBay, and Microsoft.
The company listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in 2018 and has sustained double-digit annual growth since 2007. It has also expanded beyond payments into a broader enterprise financial operating system following the acquisitions of loyal technology firm Talon.One and billing platform Orb.
The leadership transition comes weeks after the company posted robust third-quarter performance results. During Q3 2026, the company reported net revenue of €738.1 million, a 23% year-on-year increase, while processed volume climbed 30% year-on-year to €451.1 billion. The platforms segment stood out during the quarter, with net revenue up 46% year-on-year. Adyen also guided net revenue growth of 21% to 23% on a constant currency basis for the full year.
In a statement, the company confirmed that the CEO transition will not impact its financial objectives and the leadership change had been in the making for over three years through a co-CEO model. “We have been planning this transition for more than three years with the Co-CEO model. It took some time for all the pieces to fall into place, but the moment is now,” Van der Does wrote in his company-wide letter.
As part of the transition, Van der Does will remain available to the company as an advisor, while the Supervisory Board chair Herna Verhagen said the company is ready for its next chapter.
Uytdehaage, who has worked alongside Van der Does for more than 15 years, acknowledged the opportunity to keep building and the responsibility to shape the next stage.
“Pieter built more than a company. He built a culture that shapes how we make decisions, how we treat each other and how we put our merchants first, and it will outlast any one of us,” he added.

articles.title: One terminal command gave my forgotten Android device a desk job
articles.text:
My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don’t meet your daily driving needs. It’s tucked out of view, living out its life in a drawer until being erased and donated after someone asks why you’re holding onto outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren’t hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use.
The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what’s currently playing in your browser.
Credit:
Nick Indge
The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what’s currently playing in your browser.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life in “the drawer.”
Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Installation is a doddle
Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn’t have been simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as easy as plugging the tablet in to my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service, so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you’d like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device.
Developer options and ADB are required for USB setup.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Developer options and ADB are required for USB setup.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I already had developer mode initialized on the tablet but had to go back and allow ADB over USB in settings. The total installation time from copying the script from the project website to everything running on my PC and tablet was less than a minute. The app is MIT-licensed, works on Android 5.0 or later, and requires sideloading, since it is not available on the Google Play Store.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Credit:
Nick Indge
The installation script also prints its own uninstall script before it finishes. So often these days, getting rid of an unwanted app feels more difficult than installing it, so I appreciate the straightforward approach the developer has implemented.
The script can install the APK directly to your device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
The script can install the APK directly to your device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
What your device becomes
The first time you fire up PhoneBox, you get live performance and diagnostic information from your PC, along with several pages of optional content that can be tweaked for your local setup to display information that’s pertinent to your uses.
Want to check on your system resources in-game?
Credit:
Nick Indge
Want to check on your system resources in-game?
Credit:
Nick Indge
Where PhoneBox really starts to shine is the widget catalog—a collection of free add-ons that can be added as pages to the tablet’s cycling page layouts. There are more general widgets, such as RSS feeds that display news highlights from your chosen sources, or simple displays like timers or world clocks.
No shortage of available add-ons.
Credit:
Nick Indge
No shortage of available add-ons.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I opted for a few different widgets that caught my eye. One let me view my library of installed Steam titles and launch them on my PC with a simple tap of the tablet screen. Another allows me to control smart home entities hosted by my Home Assistant server. I was controlling the lights in my office from my tablet within seconds of adding the widget. It’s brilliant.
Home Assistant connected device controls on PhoneBox.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Home Assistant connected device controls on PhoneBox.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Setting up additional widgets is as simple as adding them to the page layout from the PC’s web interface and hitting save. As soon as I updated things from the PC, the connected tablet immediately began reflecting the changes. I haven’t had the chance to test most of the 131 current options in the widget catalog, but the ones I did try were simple to modify and worked on the first try.
I can launch installed Steam Library titles from the tablet controls.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I can launch installed Steam Library titles from the tablet controls.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Some frictions
While I didn’t have any major issues with PhoneBox, I did notice a couple of early annoyances along the way. Windows users should be aware that the PC companion app on that OS is currently unsigned, and they should expect a SmartScreen notification when attempting to install the software.
All control settings live in the web interface rather than the phone or tablet you’re connecting. When I first started messing with PhoneBox, I noticed it displayed my weather location as Tallinn. Nothing against the capital of Estonia, but that’s not weather information that does me much good here in the US Midwest. When I went into the widget settings to change the report location, there was nothing to be found. It turns out that you have to change those settings from the general user preferences section rather than within the widget itself. Not a deal-breaker by any means, but a slight hiccup for someone who was new to the software.
Connecting the Android tablet with my PC over USB was totally painless, but I never got the wireless route to work in my testing. Users are meant to generate a QR code from the PhoneBox web interface on their PC and connect it to their device by scanning the code with their phone/tablet. Every time I tried to scan the code from my device’s camera app, the tablet refused. There’s no QR scanner built into the PhoneBox app, so if your camera app won’t cooperate, the documented path dead-ends. USB was my intended route anyway and works great, but if you’re planning a wireless-only setup, be prepared for possible friction. The documented flow needs your device camera to open the pairing link, and mine wasn’t in the mood.
I may have to go back and try the wireless mode again.
I may have to go back and try the wireless mode again.
These minor gripes should be smoothed over before the release of 1.0. The project is early, but it seems to be moving quickly. I tested and installed PhoneBox version 0.9.29, which was one of several releases pushed to the project’s GitHub in as many days. One item of history worth noting: On November 20, the project published a high-severity security advisory covering versions 0.9.23 and earlier. The vulnerability potentially allowed another app running on the connected Android device to execute commands or receive stored credentials from the host PC. The flaw no longer existed by the time I tested the package in version 0.9.29, but it’s a good reminder that you’re installing something with deep system access and should exercise appropriate caution.
Is it worth trying?
As long as you’re part of the group that has an old phone or tablet lying around somewhere, and these days I expect that most of us are, then it’s an emphatic yes. Repurposing old devices to find new lives is one of the things that keeps me a tech hobbyist. I love finding genuinely useful and practical applications for devices that have been pushed aside by their manufacturers in favor of the latest and greatest in the lineup.
Monitor all your system processes live.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Monitor all your system processes live.
Credit:
Nick Indge
PhoneBox took a tablet that was forgotten in a junk drawer and destined for donation and gave it a new lease on life. I haven’t spent a single penny, but I now have a useful secondary display on my desk. The tablet is powered via a dedicated USB port on my PC, and only goes to sleep when my main monitor displays do. Go dig through those mystery drawers in your house, because this one is worthwhile.
Nick Indge is a Senior Technology Reporter at Ars Technica covering hardware, embedded systems, and self-hosted infrastructure. A former security investigator turned tech writer, he writes to help readers escape subscription traps and regain ownership of their digital lives. He lives in Chicagoland with his family and a goofball husky.

articles.title: Via Láctea é mais pesada do que se imaginava
articles.text:
A Via Láctea é ainda mais massiva do que algumas estimativas anteriores sugeriam. Uma nova análise realizada por astrônomos da colaboração Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) calculou que nossa galáxia possui aproximadamente 1,19 trilhão de vezes a massa do Sol. O resultado representa a estimativa mais precisa já produzida sobre a massa total da nossa galáxia.
O cálculo considera tanto a matéria comum quanto a matéria escura, componente invisível que exerce influência gravitacional sobre estrelas e outros objetos cósmicos.
A dificuldade de determinar esse número está justamente no fato de que não conseguimos observar toda a massa da Via Láctea diretamente. Estimativas anteriores variavam bastante, indo de 500 bilhões a três trilhões de massas solares.
O novo trabalho, ainda disponível como preprint e sem revisão por pares, combina grande quantidade de dados astronômicos com diferentes métodos de cálculo para reduzir essa incerteza.
Como os cientistas calcularam a massa da Via Láctea?
- Para estimar a massa da galáxia, os pesquisadores analisaram 10.036 estrelas dos tipos RR Lyrae e estrelas do ramo horizontal azul, identificadas nos dados da segunda publicação do DESI (Data Release 2);
- Essas estrelas têm característica importante para o estudo: apresentam luminosidade relativamente previsível. Isso permite que os astrônomos estimem suas distâncias com maior precisão;
- As estrelas analisadas estavam distribuídas a distâncias entre aproximadamente dez e 95 quiloparsecs do centro galáctico;
- A equipe também comparou os dados com o catálogo da missão Gaia, da Agência Espacial Europeia (ESA, na sigla em inglês), para acompanhar os movimentos desses objetos;
- A partir dessas informações, os pesquisadores aplicaram quatro métodos diferentes para calcular quanta massa seria necessária para produzir os movimentos observados das estrelas;
- Antes de utilizar os procedimentos na Via Láctea, a equipe testou os métodos em seis galáxias simuladas, cuja massa já era conhecida. Isso permitiu avaliar a precisão dos cálculos e identificar possíveis distorções provocadas por limitações nas observações.
Leia mais:
- Veja uma galáxia satélite da Via Láctea brilhando no céu; saiba como
- Sistemas planetários da Via Láctea dividem-se em duas famílias
- Foto brasileira da Chapada dos Veadeiros sob a Via Láctea vence prêmio mundial
Matéria escura representa parte importante da massa
Um dos principais desafios para determinar a massa de uma galáxia é que as estrelas e outros objetos visíveis representam apenas uma parte de seu conteúdo.
A Via Láctea, assim como outras galáxias, é dominada pela matéria escura. Embora não interaja com a luz da mesma maneira que a matéria comum, ela exerce influência gravitacional e contribui para manter a estrutura galáctica.
Por isso, simplesmente somar a massa das estrelas observáveis produziria um resultado muito inferior à massa necessária para explicar os movimentos registrados dentro da galáxia.
Os pesquisadores estimaram que a Via Láctea possui 1,19 trilhão de massas solares, com margem de incerteza de aproximadamente 11%.
A equipe também calculou que existem cerca de 636 bilhões de massas solares dentro de raio de 260 mil anos-luz a partir do centro galáctico. Nesse caso, a incerteza estimada é menor, de aproximadamente 8%.
Estimativa ainda pode mudar
Apesar da precisão alcançada, os próprios pesquisadores reconhecem limitações no trabalho.
Os métodos utilizados partem de duas premissas: que a Via Láctea apresenta formato esférico e que está em equilíbrio dinâmico, ou seja, que sua estrutura não sofre alterações significativas ao longo do tempo.
Entretanto, a galáxia é dinâmica e pode não apresentar distribuição perfeitamente esférica. Essas características podem influenciar os resultados dos cálculos.
Por isso, os cientistas defendem que futuras pesquisas aprimorem tanto os dados observacionais quanto os modelos teóricos utilizados para estimar a massa galáctica.
O estudo foi disponibilizado no repositório científico arXiv, mas ainda não passou por revisão por pares. Isso significa que outros especialistas ainda precisam avaliar formalmente os métodos e resultados apresentados.
Mesmo com essas ressalvas, a pesquisa representa avanço na compreensão da estrutura da Via Láctea e da quantidade de matéria que compõe nossa galáxia.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas.
Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.
Along with attempting to dismiss Trump’s involvement, Huang reportedly said he also didn’t return because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.” He added that, “no story has been more tortured than this one in human history,” Kabas reports. Instead, Huang said the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation,” while receiving assurance from the government that he posed no national security threat, according to the NYT.
Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12th, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees, including vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. On Monday, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and member of the board — a decision the White House said Trump was “totally involved in.” Trump also confirmed that he worked with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, were also in favor of Huang’s return.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the government “has no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a risk to national security, adding that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” that he engaged in “unlawful conduct.” Nvidia is still facing an investigation over its accounting practices, according to Reuters. The company is also carrying out its own internal investigation surrounding reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st to answer questions about national security concerns, and Democrats are already planning to press Huang about his return, as well as Trump’s involvement.
Even after all this, Huang reportedly said he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.” He also acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct, adding that he is attending therapy daily, Bloomberg reports. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang said, according to the NYT. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”

articles.title: Q&A: How Everstone Brings Where Winds Meet to Life with NVIDIA DLSS 5
articles.text:
Where Winds Meet moves between distant mountain landscapes, bustling streets, and quiet moments with its characters. For Everstone Studio, bringing more realistic lighting and materials to this wuxia world means keeping its aesthetics, recognizable characters, and carefully composed atmosphere intact.
The team’s ongoing work with NVIDIA DLSS and Streamline provided a foundation for integrating DLSS 5. Artists and engineers evaluated its lighting and material enhancements against the game’s art direction, balancing visual gains with additional performance overhead.
We sat down with art director Muzi Li and engine tech lead Cory Zhou to discuss the studio’s integration approach, preserving character identity, the changes that stood out in Jiangnan, and why developers should account for DLSS 5 early in their rendering budgets.
What made DLSS 5 a fit for Where Winds Meet?
The world of Where Winds Meet encompasses landscapes and towns, as well as countless details in how people interact with their surroundings. Players might be gazing into the distance from a mountain one moment, then walking down a bustling street the next. We want these scenes to be more than beautiful; we want players to feel their different weather conditions, times of day, and moods.
What attracts us to DLSS 5 is the room it gives us to explore lighting and materials further. It builds on the image already produced by the game engine, using neural rendering to enhance lighting and material details.
Our goal isn’t to pursue greater visual impact for its own sake. It’s to make these details work in harmony with the original art direction: distant landscapes should retain their poetic atmosphere, while nearby buildings and characters should have a believable sense of texture.
What were your art team’s first thoughts of DLSS 5?
Our first impression was that the interplay of light and shadow had gained greater depth. When sunlight falls on buildings, fabrics, and characters, the result feels more than just a sharper image. DLSS 5 identifies and tones down overly bright highlights while bringing out more detail in those areas. It also fills in ambient-light details and subtle highlights in the shadows, and recognizes the properties of materials.
How did you integrate DLSS 5 into your pipeline?
We have consistently integrated the latest DLSS technologies and kept our NVIDIA Streamline integration up to date. As a result, our rendering pipeline already had strong support for DLSS, providing a solid foundation for adopting DLSS 5. This ongoing investment made the upgrade a natural extension of our existing technology roadmap and helped ensure a smooth integration process.
How did artists and engineers use DLSS 5 controls to preserve art direction across characters, materials, and lighting?
In any given scene, we look at whether characters remain recognizable, whether materials such as fabric, leather, and metal are still visually distinct, and whether changes in lighting and shadow disrupt the scene’s original mood.
NVIDIA provides developers with options for model selection and controls over aspects such as structural and tonal strength. For us, artists and engineers need to communicate and iterate based on what we see on screen. One setting might make the environment more striking, but if faces or the overall color palette drift away from the intended look, we need to find a different balance.
We want to strike the right balance between visual gains, performance cost, and player preferences, while giving players choices wherever possible.
How did you evaluate DLSS 5 image quality and performance?
Our evaluation focuses on three key areas: visual quality, performance overhead, and alignment with the game’s artistic direction. Our testing to date indicates that enabling DLSS 5 introduces additional performance overhead, so we assess that cost alongside the visual improvements it delivers.
In developing Where Winds Meet, we have consistently explored different graphics technologies to support a wide range of player preferences. In our internal playtesting, DLSS 5 delivered a distinct visual experience, enhancing the overall presentation of our environments and their sense of immersion.
Based on these findings, we plan to give players the option to enable or disable DLSS 5. Our approach to visual tuning will be guided by the art team’s creative vision, including selecting the DLSS 5 model that best matches the intended aesthetic. We also aim to make relevant visual controls available to players wherever possible, allowing them to tailor the image to their preferences.
On balance, our evaluation has been positive, taking into account the visual improvements, performance overhead, and flexibility offered to players.
How does DLSS 5 affect characters?
What matters is whether characters feel more naturally part of the world while retaining their own distinctive presence.
For example, when a character walks from sunlight into the shade beneath an eave, changes in lighting and materials can help them feel more naturally grounded in the environment. The way different clothing materials respond to light can also give them a stronger presence. At the same time, we pay close attention to whether faces and costumes remain recognizable.
Which scene best demonstrates the improvements?
We find that Jiangnan is where DLSS 5 makes the biggest visual improvement. \When adjusting the settings, we use DLSS 5 to soften highlights in the original scene lighting that can appear too harsh, while adding a greater sense of depth between buildings. DLSS 5 can recognize ambient color from the sun and fill in details in darker areas, giving shadows more depth and material detail. Many buildings in Jiangnan feature wood and tiled roofs; DLSS 5 can fill in lifelike wood and roof-tile details.
As for the image that best showcases the effect, it will reveal itself during each player’s own journey: perhaps at a street corner just after the rain has cleared, or at an old ferry crossing bathed in the setting sun—a quiet moment that makes you stop and linger.
What advice would you give other developers adopting DLSS 5?
First, account for DLSS 5 performance requirements early in your rendering budget. For projects targeting high frame rates, reserve sufficient performance headroom and evaluate the balance between visual benefits and performance cost in representative gameplay scenarios.
Second, work closely with the NVIDIA team throughout integration and tuning to understand the technology’s capabilities and available controls. Align that work with your project’s artistic direction and performance targets.

articles.title: How Can AI Build Faster And Better Silicon For Physical AI?
articles.text:
Shortening the path from design intent to verified implementation could put custom silicon within reach of more teams.
The age of physical AI is here, and with it comes a significant increase in the demand of custom silicon.
By 2025, five million industrial robots were operating worldwide. As these systems become more capable, their demands on silicon become more distinct. Each must balance computation and memory with the realities of power, latency, reliability, and security.
Fig. 1: Annual installations of industrial robots, 5 largest markets, 2025. Source: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics 2026. Chart redrawn by ChipAgents.
For humanoid robots in particular, application-specific hardware can provide the agility and speed required to perform specialized tasks in real time. As those requirements diverge, specialized ASICs become more attractive, because they can be optimized for the exact workloads, latency targets, power envelopes, and operating environments of a particular system.
The constraint to this innovation is development speed: AI models and software evolve faster than the conventional silicon tape out cycles, creating a need to accelerate the entire path from design intent and exploration to physical implementation and validation.
For agentic AI to deliver that acceleration, it must meet three requirements.
Agents need a shared, persistent representation of the design and the engineering knowledge behind it. A design ontology provides structure: it connects design flows, RTL design, verification, verification tools, error diagnosis and repair, synthesis, timing, and PPA optimization methodologies. Organization-specific methodologies and prior decisions add the rationale for how the design should evolve. To remain useful across tasks, this context must track provenance, design versions, and dependencies, so agents can distinguish current evidence from assumptions or superseded results.
Consider a 3D-IC, where logic, memory, die-to-die interfaces, packaging, power delivery, and thermal behavior are coupled. An RTL change that preserves functional behavior can alter switching activity, placement, or interconnect demand, affecting timing, power integrity, and temperature after implementation. Persistent context helps agents trace those dependencies across die and system boundaries, identify which analyses and verification results may no longer be valid, and invoke the appropriate tools to reassess them. AI then also converts improvement from specific cases into reusable knowledge, helping reduce recurring mistakes and repeated investigation across similar tasks.
Second, agents must carry design objectives through many dependent steps, measuring progress against verified engineering outcomes: functional correctness, physical feasibility, and target power, performance, and area within schedule and compute budgets.
Novel architectures for physical AI introduce more configurations, interfaces, and corner cases. Accelerating individual tasks delivers limited value if downstream verification or physical implementation cannot converge. Every action must therefore serve the overall objective, with explicit acceptance criteria guiding execution and determining when the work is complete.
This requires co-optimizing models, tools, and compute across the workflow. Complex reasoning may benefit from a larger model, repeatable operations from deterministic procedures, and numerical analysis from specialized engineering tools. CPU and GPU allocation, memory capacity, and parallel execution must be selected according to their contribution to the final result. The relevant measure is total time and cost to a validated outcome.
Third, all systems produced must be held to a critical standard of verifiability and security.
Physical AI applications operate in the real world, often in environments where failures can create direct safety risks. Specialized hardware also introduces hardware-specific security requirements and potential vulnerabilities that must be identified and verified before deployment. Agentic AI can help automate portions of that process by checking implementations against security requirements, surfacing potential vulnerabilities, and generating additional verification scenarios. That being said, to achieve an entirely autonomous workflow, you need traceable decisions, reproducible tool runs, explicit verification assumptions, and engineer review and signoff. Trust in this system is dependent on the evidence supporting each engineering decision.
At ChipAgents, we’re building toward a question: what would it take to make chip development 10× faster? Our approach brings organizational design ontology, physics-aware models, and LLM agents together in IC-STAR, the chip neural engine powering our platform. We study how models and multi-agent orchestration can work together to reach verified outcomes faster, with lower inference cost. Our ambition is to shorten the path from design intent to verified implementation, which could put custom silicon within reach of more teams, opening new possibilities for machines that sense, move, and act. We see a future where more engineering ideas make it beyond the drawing board and into the world.

articles.title: Le Black Friday au service des têtes en l’air : l’Apple AirTag de deuxième génération passe à 25€ chez Amazon
articles.text:
Bien pratique pour retrouver des affaires égarées ou pour suivre une valise à la trace, l’AirTag de deuxième génération est actuellement disponible pour 25 € au lieu de 35 € chez Amazon à l’occasion du Black Friday.
Vous possédez un iPhone et vous avez tendance à chercher votre trousseau de clés ou votre sac à main trois fois par semaine ? C’est le signe qu’il faut vous équiper d’un AirTag… Voire de plusieurs. En ce moment chez Amazon, l’Apple AirTag de deuxième génération coûte 25 €.
Ce petit accessoire permet d’associer un objet à l’application Localiser d’iOS, afin de le retrouver plus facilement en cas de perte. Il est important de noter que cette balise s’adresse exclusivement aux utilisateurs de l’écosystème Apple.
L’Apple AirTag de deuxième génération est à 25 € chez Amazon, soit 10 € de moins que son tarif Apple de 35 €.
Pourquoi choisir l’AirTag de deuxième génération ?
- Pour retrouver vos affaires à proximité : le haut-parleur intégré permet de faire sonner la balise lorsqu’un objet se cache dans la maison.
- Pour le réseau Localiser : les appareils Apple passant près de l’AirTag peuvent relayer sa position même lorsqu’il n’est pas à portée de votre propre iPhone.
- Pour sa pile remplaçable : une pile bouton CR2032 assure plus d’un an d’autonomie, sans besoin de recharge régulière.
Une aide pour les petits oublis du quotidien
Glissé dans une poche de sac ou fixé à un trousseau avec un accessoire adapté, l’AirTag peut être consulté directement au sein de l’app Localiser présente sur l’iPhone. Il ne faut que quelques instants pour le configurer. Ensuite, il y a deux cas de figure : soit l’AirTag est situé à proximité de votre position, et, dans ce cas, la fonction Localisation précise vous guide vers l’objet associé si votre iPhone est compatible. Soit il n’est pas à portée, mais les iPhone d’autres utilisateurs le captent : vous pouvez donc quand même savoir où il se trouve.
Cette deuxième génération améliore notamment la portée et le volume sonore, deux progrès évoqués dans notre test de l’AirTag 2, qui lui a donné la note de 8 sur 10.
Un réseau étendu, mais pas un suivi permanent
L’AirTag 2 s’utilise sans abonnement à payer, et il est parfaitement intégré à l’écosystème d’Apple. En revanche, la remontée de sa position à distance dépend des appareils Apple qui passent à proximité : si votre objet est perdu dans un endroit où personne ne circule, il est malheureusement possible que vous ne sachiez pas où il se trouve précisément.
✅ Les points forts
- Intégration à l’application Localiser.
- Haut-parleur et portée améliorés.
- Pile CR2032 remplaçable par l’utilisateur.
❌ Les limites
- Configuration réservée aux appareils Apple compatibles.
- Accessoire de fixation à acheter séparément pour les clés.
Pour équiper un sac, une valise ou un trousseau de clés, l’AirTag d’Apple est utile, surtout à 25 € pendant le Black Friday Amazon.
L’AirTag 2 a tout pour devenir indispensable aux utilisateurs d’iPhone qui égarent régulièrement leurs affaires ou qui souhaitent ajouter une aide à la localisation peu coûteuse à leurs bagages. À ce prix, il est même envisageable d’en acheter plusieurs.
Mais attention, si vous utilisez un smartphone Android, alors vous ne pouvez pas utiliser l’AirTag 2. Dans ce cas, vous devez vous tourner vers une balise adaptée à votre terminal. Il faut aussi noter qu’Apple demande iOS 26.2.1 ou une version ultérieure afin d’utiliser cet accessoire.

articles.title: Activision estudia usar los chats de voz de Discord para entrenar a los NPC de Call of Duty
articles.text:
Activision presentó una solicitud de patente para un sistema que podría aprender de las conversaciones de voz de los jugadores y asociarlas con acontecimientos de un videojuego. La propuesta contempla aplicaciones externas como Discord y TeamSpeak como posibles fuentes de audio. Luego, un modelo de aprendizaje automático podría generar respuestas para personajes controlados por la computadora, conocidos como NPC.
El documento, titulado Methods and Systems for Applying Machine Learning to Generate Gameplay Audio, fue presentado el 16 de julio de 2026 y publicado por la Oficina de Patentes y Marcas de Estados Unidos el 12 de noviembre. Una aplicación de esta idea podría verse en un juego como Call of Duty: por ejemplo, un NPC podría festejar una eliminación o burlarse del jugador después de una derrota con una frase inspirada en las conversaciones que suelen darse durante las partidas.
Cómo aprenderían los NPC de las conversaciones
El sistema identificaría eventos que el juego puede reconocer, como una eliminación, la muerte del jugador, una victoria o el final de una ronda. Luego, buscaría fragmentos de audio cercanos a esos momentos para asociar una reacción con lo ocurrido.
La descripción ofrece como ejemplo analizar los diez segundos anteriores y posteriores a un evento. Así, si un compañero celebra una baja o se burla después de que alguien pierda, el modelo podría relacionar esas palabras y su tono con el momento correspondiente. La patente plantea utilizar esas asociaciones para entrenar una red neuronal, un tipo de programa que aprende patrones a partir de ejemplos.
En una partida posterior, ante una situación similar, el sistema podría producir una respuesta para un personaje controlado por la computadora. En un escenario de Call of Duty, por ejemplo, un enemigo virtual podría reaccionar con una frase de celebración después de derrotar al jugador, mientras que un compañero controlado por la IA podría felicitarlo por una jugada destacada.
La intención sería que los diálogos sonaran vinculados con lo que acaba de pasar, en vez de limitarse a frases grabadas que se repiten sin importar el contexto. El sistema también podría considerar elementos como el idioma del jugador para adaptar las respuestas.
Discord aparece como una fuente posible de audio
La solicitud contempla que la partida y la aplicación de voz sean programas independientes. En ese escenario, el sistema usaría marcas de tiempo para alinear lo que se dijo en Discord con el instante de juego correspondiente. TeamSpeak también aparece como ejemplo de servicio externo; el documento menciona además otras posibilidades, como el chat integrado en el juego.
Esto permitiría relacionar una exclamación espontánea con una jugada concreta. Si alguien dice «¡qué buena!» justo después de una baja, el sistema podría asociar esa reacción con el evento y tomarla como ejemplo para generar respuestas similares de un personaje virtual en otra partida.
La patente también plantea filtros para excluir contenido ofensivo. Sin embargo, la publicación no detalla cómo se informaría a los usuarios ni qué controles tendrían sobre el uso de sus conversaciones. Tampoco explica cómo se resolverían situaciones en las que varias personas hablan al mismo tiempo o comentan algo que no tiene relación con la jugada.
Una propuesta para crear diálogos más naturales
El sistema busca que los NPC respondan de manera más contextual a los sucesos del juego. En un título de acción como Call of Duty, esto podría traducirse en enemigos que celebran una victoria, reaccionan a una derrota o provocan al jugador después de una baja, con expresiones inspiradas en la forma en que se comunican las personas durante una partida.
Para lograrlo, la tecnología analizaría ejemplos de voz asociados con eventos y usaría esos datos para generar nuevas respuestas. La patente describe así una alternativa a los diálogos pregrabados: personajes que adaptan lo que dicen al momento de juego y al tipo de reacción que suele acompañarlo.
La solicitud presenta una posibilidad técnica, no una función anunciada para los jugadores. Aun así, muestra cómo Activision explora el uso de inteligencia artificial para que los personajes virtuales reaccionen con mayor naturalidad y se parezcan más a los compañeros que comparten una partida en línea.

articles.title: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits
articles.text:
OpenAI and Cisco launched an open-source Linux security tool named Shirudo that deploys temporary runtime protections to block vulnerability exploitation while administrators prepare and roll out patches, without restarting services.
Shirudo leverages the eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) mechanism in Linux to monitor for suspicious activity and deploy targeted protections called "shields."
eBPF is a Linux technology that lets programs run in a controlled environment within the operating system's kernel without modifying its source code or requiring a restart.
It enables real-time monitoring of system and network activity, performance analysis, and enforcement of targeted security protections, making it an ideal operational basis for Shirudo.
Shirudo’s shields aim to block malicious behavior in a targeted way, leaving legitimate application operations undisturbed. OpenAI highlights four core capabilities for the tool:
- Live protection: Blocks vulnerable code paths without restarting systems, letting operators assess shield impact before enforcing them.
- AI-assisted defense: Enables agents to investigate vulnerabilities, develop shields, and validate their effectiveness, with deployment remaining under human control.
- Trusted deployment: Uses cryptographic signatures, Linux's eBPF verifier, and kernel security controls to prevent unauthorized modifications.
- Hardware-backed verification: Uses Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) to provide verifiable records of shields being loaded or removed.
OpenAI and Cisco researchers tested custom-generated shields and demonstrated that they could successfully block a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without interrupting its operation.
Marcus Hutchins, principal threat researcher at managed detection and response company Expel, says that while there is "genuinely so much runtime exploit mitigation potential with eBPF," it may not be a good idea to let AI agents write rules that could impact the kernel.
He also noted that the tool's "capabilities are limited to Linux because Mac/Windows haven't implement the components needed to be effective."
Researchers at Isovalent, a cloud networking and security company acquired by Cisco in 2024, explain that "Shirudo is a rewrite of Tetragon," an open-source eBPF-based runtime security platform the company introduced in 2022, which also serves as the foundation for Cisco's existing Live Protect technology.
Shirudo is designed for agentic control plane, and a configurable degree of autonomy when it comes to deploying mitigations. Isovalent says the tool isn’t limited to eBPF and can also modify application or userspace runtime bytecode to extend protection where needed.
When a shield is deployed, they also provide operators with hit counts, giving them insight into attempted exploits and where defenses need strengthening.
The two companies plan to provide “ready-to-use” mitigations in the form of tested shields, along with vulnerability disclosures, until patching is possible. Shields will be distributed as cryptographically signed ‘.bee’ packages through an OCI registry.
Isovalent says that Shirudo can be activated through a command-line interface and doesn’t require a daemon to run permanently on the machine.
"The Shirudo project is only the beginning, but it already shows the true potential of combining agents as a workforce with machine interfaces to let agents output what they are best at: code," the researchers say.
They expect the tool to evolve and other projects to emerge around it, to the point of building self-defending that can run applications and agents side by side.
Shirudo is open-source (BSD + GPL) and comes with a quick-start guide as well as "getting started" documentation from Isovalent.
In a deep-dive webinar on December 15, OpenAI will provide a technical rundown of how the tool works and how it combines eBPF and artificial intelligence to detect and counter new attacks.

articles.title: Google Cloud confirms 30 role cuts in India, rejects claims of wider layoffs
articles.text:
Google Cloud confirms 30 role cuts in India, rejects claims of wider layoffs
However, Google Cloud has not identified the teams involved or disclosed the exit terms.
Google Cloud has confirmed that around 30 roles in India were eliminated last week due to work reprioritisation. It, however, rejected online claims that much of its local workforce had been affected.
“These rumors are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organizational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritization of work,” the company said in response to a user on X.
However, Google Cloud has not identified the teams involved or disclosed the exit terms. Anonymous posts on workplace forum Blind mention abrupt dismissals and short resignation deadlines, but these allegations remain unverified.
The clarification comes as Google Cloud is expanding its business rapidly. Its parent company Alphabet’s third-quarter results showed cloud revenue rising 103% year on year to $30.7 billion, driven by demand for AI infrastructure, AI services, and the wider cloud platform.
However, strong business growth does not mean every team or role is expanding at the same pace. This discrepancy is visible across the technology sector.
In 2023, Google announced 12,000 job cuts globally. Since then it since made smaller, targeted reductions. Reuters reported that Google expanded voluntary exit offers to some employees in five countries this summer as it managed costs amid heavy AI investment.
Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 eligible employees in October this year, indicating the wider trend of 'workforce adjustment' in the industry.
India remains a major market for cloud infrastructure. Amazon Web Services broke ground on an expanded data centre in Hyderabad in July. It said it plans to invest more than $21 billion in Indian cloud and AI infrastructure between 2026 and 2030.
Meanwhile, the Government of India issued a cloud selection framework in March, guiding ministries to choose services according to the sensitivity and criticality of their data, including hybrid-cloud options that combine public and private infrastructure.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Un employé d’Apple dépense 100 000 € pour acheter une voiture électrique de 1996 abandonnée dans une fourrière, les ingénieurs qui l’avaient conçue l’aident à la restaurer
articles.text:
Un employé d’Apple dépense 100 000 € pour acheter une voiture électrique de 1996 abandonnée dans une fourrière, les ingénieurs qui l’avaient conçue l’aident à la restaurer
Billy Caruso, employé d'Apple, a dépensé près de 100 000 € pour une voiture électrique des années 1990 retrouvée dans une fourrière d'Atlanta. Il s'agit d'une EV1, un modèle que General Motors avait presque entièrement détruit. Ce sont pourtant les ingénieurs à l'origine de la voiture qui l'ont aidé à la restaurer.
Ce collectionneur des premières électriques a découvert l'annonce grâce au message d'un ami, la veille de la fin des offres. "Je n'en croyais pas mes yeux quand j'ai vu une EV1 verte dans une vente aux enchères de fourrière", a-t-il expliqué.
Une voiture électrique lancée en 1996 par GM
C'est le 28 octobre 2025 qu'il l'a emporté pour 104 000 $ hors frais, environ 100 000 €. La voiture ne roulait plus avec un pare-brise cassé, de l'eau infiltrée et, plus insolite, des ratons laveurs qui avaient élu domicile à l'emplacement de la batterie. General Motors n'a jamais vendu l'EV1 aux particuliers
C'est en 1996 que General Motors a lancé l'EV1, une voiture pensée d'emblée pour l'électrique, avec une structure en aluminium et un coefficient de traînée de 0,19. Pour les particuliers, il n'était possible que de la louer. À la fin du programme, GM a récupéré les voitures et en a détruit la plupart. Quelques exemplaires ont rejoint des musées et universités une fois rendus inutilisables.
La rareté explique donc ce prix, puisque GM parle de la première vente publique d'une EV1. Celle de Billy Caruso, un modèle de 1997, porte le nom de V212 car il s'agit de la 212e EV1 produite. La police de l'université Clark Atlanta l'avait déclarée abandonnée sur son campus.
Billy Caruso a lancé la restauration avec Jared Pink, créateur de la chaîne The Questionable Garage sur YouTube. Leur objectif était de faire rouler V212 le 14 novembre 2026, trente ans jour pour jour après la sortie de la première EV1.
General Motors a finalement aidé à sauver une EV1.
General Motors a aidé à restaurer la voiture
Mark Reuss, président de General Motors, a suivi le projet en vidéo et a invité l'équipe à Warren, dans le Michigan. "Quoi qu'il vous faille, nous vous aiderons", a-t-il promis. Billy Caruso et ses partenaires ont alors rencontré des ingénieurs et responsables du programme EV1.
Le service design de General Motors a prélevé le pare-brise, une vitre de custode et des boîtiers de jonction sur V159, une EV1 rouge que GM conservait. L'équipe de Billy Caruso a mis la voiture à nu avant de poser des vitres neuves, de rénover l'habitacle et de refaire la peinture.
C'est le 14 novembre 2026, au bout de douze mois de travaux, que V212 a repris la route à Fairfield, dans l'Ohio. Selon GM, aucun particulier n'avait conduit d'EV1 depuis plus de deux décennies. Billy Caruso a ensuite présenté sa voiture à d'anciens membres du programme à l'université Kettering de Flint.
"J'ai occupé beaucoup de très bons postes dans ma carrière. Mon préféré, de loin, a été mon passage sur l'EV1", a confié Linda Ludek Brouns, ancienne ingénieure de la chaîne de traction.

articles.title: Une arnaque vise les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets en France : comment éviter de se faire piéger ?
articles.text:
Nous avons ici affaire à une arnaque sophistiquée qui cible plus particulièrement les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets. Plusieurs victimes ont été recensées en France ces derniers jours, avec des montants dérobés allant de 500 à plus de 1 000 euros. Il faut dire que cette arnaque est difficilement repérable. Une victime peut effectuer un paiement ou retirer de l’argent en saisissant son code PIN, sans rien remarquer. Cependant, un point précis peut alerter sur la situation.
Une minuscule caméra et un lecteur de carte piégé pour vider vos comptes bancaires
Une nouvelle arnaque, particulièrement élaborée, a été repérée à plusieurs reprises ces derniers jours en France. Cette arnaque vise plus particulièrement les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets. En d’autres termes, tous les dispositifs qui demandent d’insérer une carte bancaire et de saisir un code PIN. Le mode de fonctionnement de cette arnaque est, il faut le dire, sophistiqué. Comme l’explique BFMTV, les arnaqueurs parviennent à intégrer un dispositif dans le lecteur de carte d’un système de paiement. Ce dispositif est ensuite capable d’intercepter les données échangées avec la puce de la carte bancaire. Il est ici plus précisément question de skimming, une technique qui consiste à insérer un boîtier très fin dans le lecteur afin de récupérer les données de la carte.
En parallèle, les arnaqueurs placent une minuscule caméra juste au-dessus du pavé numérique destiné à saisir le code bancaire. Ainsi, les escrocs disposent finalement des données de la carte bancaire, mais aussi du code confidentiel de leur victime. Selon les témoignages publiés en ligne par certaines victimes, les montants dérobés vont de 500 à plus de 1 000 euros.
Comment ne pas tomber dans le piège de cette arnaque
Autant dire que ce type d’arnaque bancaire n’est pas facilement repérable. Cependant, un point précis peut alerter sur la situation. En effet, le dispositif utilisé par les arnaqueurs demande à la victime de recomposer son code PIN. Par conséquent, si un système de paiement vous demande de composer une seconde fois votre code bancaire, il est vivement conseillé de changer de borne ou de faire preuve de la plus grande prudence, en mettant un terme à la transaction et en appelant par exemple un membre du personnel.
Veillez également à masquer le pavé numérique avec votre autre main lorsque vous saisissez votre code PIN. Pour rappel, les escrocs peuvent dissimuler une minuscule caméra juste au-dessus de celui-ci afin de filmer la saisie de votre code confidentiel. Faites également attention au terminal de paiement. Les arnaqueurs ayant placé d’autres appareils pour enregistrer les données bancaires des victimes, des anomalies peuvent être présentes (éléments inhabituels ou mal fixés).
Enfin, privilégiez le paiement sans contact et surveillez de près vos comptes bancaires. En cas de transaction anormale, contactez votre banque sans attendre.

articles.title: ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Review
articles.text:
While much of the attention in the market for AI inference has been focused on servers and datacenter-scale deployments, the heart and soul of the modern AI revolution started with video cards. And that is where it still beats on today, overshadowed by servers but still an important market segment overall.
Within the AMD ecosystem, the company has taken a very visible pivot in how it markets and categorizes its professional video cards. The Radeon Pro lineup, once the backbone of AMD’s workstation graphics efforts, has become the Radeon AI Pro lineup, and the backbone of AMD’s add-in video card/AI accelerator efforts. The flagship for this line, in turn, is the Radeon AI Pro R9700, a 32GB VRAM card that AMD and its partners are positioning as a more budget-friendly alternative to NVIDIA’s RTX PRO Blackwell lineup of workstation cards.
Today we are taking a look at one of those R9700 cards in the form of ASUS’s Turbo Radeon AI Pro R9700. The sub-$2000 card have been heavily optimized for workstation use, balancing graphics needs and display outputs with the ability to fit up to four cards into a single system for larger AI workloads.
ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Hardware Overview
As AMD is not selling their own reference design workstation cards for this generation, it falls to AMD’s partners to sell the cards instead. Which is a production strategy that they are well-accustomed to on the consumer side of matters, but is a bit more unusual for a workstation card.
Notably, AMD has been keeping their Radeon Pro partners on a rather short leash with card designs. AMD is curating a very specific image for a very specific market here, not the least of which is the ability to install multiple cards in a single workstation. As a result, though AMD is not selling their reference card their partner cards are all quite similar in their high-level design as dual slot blowers, a form factor you will not readily find outside of workstation video cards these days.
That brings us to ASUS’s Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700. ASUS has long been a heavyweight in the world of video cards, so it is no surprise to see them jump on board producing a Radeon Pro card.
ASUS’s R9700 card is, in all practical application, exactly what you would expect from a workstation card given the form factor and the AMD’s constraints. This is a dual slot video card that follows the PCIe specifications to a T in terms of width and height, in order to ensure that it (and perhaps a few of its friends) can fit into a workstation chassis.
| ASUS Turbo Radeon AI R9700 Specifications |  |  |  | 
| CUs | 64 |  |  | 
| AI Accelerators | 128 |  |  | 
| GPU Boost Clockspeed | 2.92GHz |  |  | 
| Peak Matrix Throughput (FP8) | 382.7 TFLOPS |  |  | 
| Peak Vector Throughput (FP32) | 47.8 TFLOPS |  |  | 
| Memory | 32GB GDDR6 |  |  | 
| Memory Bandwidth | 640GB/sec (20Gbps x 256-bits) |  |  | 
| ECC | Yes (Linux Only) |  |  | 
| Infinity Cache | 64MB |  |  | 
| I/O | PCIe Gen5 x16 |  |  | 
| TBP | 300W |  |  | 
| Form Factor | PCIe CEM (Air Cooled) |  |  | 
| Dimensions | 267 x 111 x 40 mm (10.5 x 4.4 x 1.6 in) |  |  | 
| Architecture | RDNA 4 |  |  | 
| GPU | Navi 48 |  |  | 
Under the hood, the card is powered by AMD’s Navi 48 GPU, which is the most powerful RDNA 4 GPU offered in this generation. The GPU offers 64 of AMD’s CUs, which in turn is comprised of a total of 4096 shading units for vector math and 128 AI accelerator cores for matrix operations.
With a peak clock speed of 2.92GHz, this gives the R9700 a peak matrix math throughput of 382.7 TFLOPS with dense FP8 math, or double that with sparsity. One of the key improvements in this generation of RDNA architecture is the addition of FP8 support, which not only further improves the compute throughput of the card, but it better aligns AMD’s hardware with the general trends in the industry towards lower precision weights, and fitting a large number of weights within a given amount of memory.
On that note, as is traditional for a workstation card, AMD and ASUS have packed the R9700 with as much memory as the card can handle. With Navi 48 sporting a 256-bit bus, the card has been equipped with 32GB of GDDR6 memory organized as 16 2Gbit chips in clamshell mode. Above all else, memory support is a key differentiator between AMD’s consumer and professional cards, so 32GB is something you will only find on the Radeon AI Pro cards.
The GDDR6 memory itself is clocked at 20Gbps, allowing for a total of 640GB/second of memory bandwidth for the card. Soft ECC is also available, though only under Linux (and even then, it has to be manually enabled). This allows for an extra degree of reliability for systems and racks based around the card.
Navi 48 itself is somewhere between a mid to high-end GPU as far as die size (357mm2) and transistor counts (53.9B) go, which makes it a bit of an oddity within AMD’s lineup as far as card progression is concerned. AMD did not produce a true high-end GPU this generation, and as a result the R9700 actually has less VRAM than the previous-generation 48GB Radeon Pro W7900. This means that it is a step back in terms of overall memory capacity, but AMD is looking to make up the difference with compute throughput, thanks in large part to the newer chip architecture.
One advantage of being a smaller chip, however, is that it keeps TDPs in check. AMD (and ASUS’s) Total Board Power figure for the card is just 300 Watts, which makes it relatively easy to keep a blower-style card cooled without a blowout on noise. This also means that even 4 cards in a system is not going to result in excessive power requirements, though it will certainly be pushing the limits of a single power supply.
ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Build and Design
As far as video card designs go, ASUS’s Turbo Radeon AI Pro R9700 is a very typical dual slot blower design. With a need to ensure that the card can be installed in multiples together, ASUS has kept things tightly tuned to PCIe specifications, with a dual slot card measuring 10.5 inches long and 4.4 inches high.
Interestingly, the blower design here is open-backed, that is, the back side of the card has open vents so that the card can pull in air from both sides of the card.
The fan itself is a pretty typical blower design. According to ASUS they are using dual ball bearings here.
Taking a look at the rear of the card, we can better see the venting cut into the card’s PCB and its shroud. For that matter, we can also see that the card even has a shroud on its back side. As noted earlier, the 32GB of GDDR6 is organized in a clamshell configuration on the R9700, meaning that 8 chips are on the rear of the card and need to be protected and cooled, just as with all of the chips on the front side of the card.
Being that this is a workstation card, ASUS has also put some thought into their power connector placement. The Turbo R9700 uses an ATX 12V-2×6 connector, which has been placed on the rear of the card instead of the top, another workstation-centric design element that makes it easier to install multiple cards in a system. The 12V-2×6 connector is rated for up to 600W, so the 300W TBP R9700 is well within the cable’s limits.
Meanwhile, at the front of the card we find a not too subtle reminder that this is a video card, with 4 display outputs – the maximum number of displays the Navi 48 GPU can drive. ASUS has given their card a triple DisplayPort plus single HDMI port configuration. The DisplayPorts are all DisplayPort 2.1a, while the HDMI port supports HDMI 2.1b. Coupled with DSC, and the card can drive displays at up to 12K in resolution.
Otherwise, besides the display outputs, the rest of the front of the card is almost entirely vent cut-outs. 300W is still a lot of heat to expel from a blower card, so ASUS does not hold back here, and you can clearly see the fins from the heatsink running within the card.
With our hardware tour complete, let us take a look at the performance of the Turbo R9700
Somewhat late to the Party, but . . . *clink*
Great coverage!
I spent < $3K on two similar beasties, and they are quite pert (esp. with the Radiance engine) :)
I liked seeing the Qwen latency curves alongside throughput. On a workstation shared by a chat tool and a batch queue, I’d use the time to first token to set the daytime concurrency limit and save the bigger batches for overnight.

articles.title: China se hizo un hueco regalando sus modelos de IA. Para competir con OpenAI y Anthropic, Z.ai lanza GLM-5.4 primero de pago
articles.text:
En cuestión de laboratorios de IA, hay actualmente dos estilos principales: los que acostumbran a liberar los pesos y aquellos que prefieren mantenerlos cerrados y cobrar por usarlos. La tendencia había colocado a los laboratorios chinos del lado abierto y a los estadounidenses en la acera contraria, aunque poco a poco las líneas se juntan. Z.ai es la prueba.
Nuevo modelo insignia: GLM-5.4. Si el anterior ya era bueno en tareas como la programación, la empresa ajusta esas capacidades con un cambio de arquitectura que apunta a la eficiencia. Según Z.ai, GLM-5.4 es su primer modelo insignia con arquitectura Loop Transformer.
Según la empresa, GLM-5.4 rinde como modelos de entre 2 y 3 billones de parámetros, aunque de momento no ha presentado los benchmarks. Ofrece hasta 200 tokens por segundo fuera de las horas punta (entre 70 y 80 cuando hay más carga), admite hasta un millón de tokens de contexto, incluye modo de razonamiento y suma visión a su especialidad, la programación.
Como pegas, la propia Z.ai reconoce que el nuevo modelo tiende a enredarse en razonamientos demasiado largos. Y las primeras pruebas independientes apuntan hacia esa misma dirección: en KingBench 4 tardó 431 minutos frente a los 109 de Gemini 4 Neon. GLM-5.4 gastó unas 15 veces más tokens.
No hay pesos abiertos ni fecha para ellos. El anuncio del nuevo modelo nos deja por escrito las capacidades y la posibilidad de probarlo en las suscripciones que Z.ai ofrece a los usuarios: actualmente está en todos los planes de GLM Coding Plan. La API aún no está disponible. Y no lo estará hasta que finalice la evaluación de seguridad.
Con la presentación de GLM-5.3, Z.ai prometió publicar los pesos dos semanas después, algo que terminó cumpliendo con ciertos matices: dejó atrás la licencia MIT para exigir una revisión de seguridad a los proveedores que facturen más de 10.000 millones de dólares. Con GLM-5.4 la empresa dice que publicará los pesos cuando complete el endurecimiento de seguridad, un paso que investigadores chinos proponen convertir en norma para todos los modelos abiertos. Z.ai no ha marcado fecha alguna.
Para competir hay que restringir. Los laboratorios chinos usaban sus modelos open source para captar la atención, pero seguían cobrando por la inferencia a través de suscripciones y APIs. Con GLM-5.1, Z.ai ya empezó a subir precios. Ahora aprovecha que su GLM ya es de sobra conocido y valorado para ponerle un peaje a lo Anthropic u OpenAI, con la seguridad como argumento oficial. ¿Quieres usarlo? Paga.
Dos velocidades. Z.ai no cierra por completo la puerta: con GLM-5.3-Flash demostró que puede liberar modelos "pequeños" con pesos abiertos desde el primer día. En Estados Unidos, Nvidia, Microsoft y compañía defienden los pesos abiertos como el futuro de la IA, así que las líneas se juntan desde las dos aceras. El problema es para quien eligió GLM precisamente porque podía descargarlo. Como Revolut, que puso a 2.000 ingenieros a programar con GLM-5.3 ejecutándolo en sus propios servidores.
GLM-5.4 no podrá ejecutarse en local, al menos de momento: o pagar por la suscripción de Z.ai o esperar a la liberación del modelo sin que haya fecha para que eso ocurra. Y la compañía ya avisa de que su próxima iteración, “significativamente más grande”, estará lista pronto. La duda es si llegará con pesos o con peaje.
Imagen de portada | Z.ai
En Xataka | Entre expandir sus modelos de IA por todo el mundo o protegerlos, China tiene muy clara su decisión

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.text:
Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
- Date:
  November 11, 2026
- Source:
  ETH Zurich
- Summary:
  Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
- Share:
A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.
The breakthrough, described in the journal Science, introduces a different approach to quantum computer design. Instead of closely integrating information processing and storage, as many existing systems do, Chu's team has developed an architecture that gives these functions more distinct roles.
Quantum Memory Inspired by Conventional Computers
The researchers drew inspiration from the basic design of everyday digital computers. In a conventional machine, the central processing unit (CPU) carries out calculations while information is held separately in working memory, commonly called random access memory (RAM). The arrangement of these components plays an important role in determining how efficiently a computer operates.
Chu's quantum system follows a similar principle. A superconducting qubit acts as the processing and control unit, performing a role comparable to that of the central processing unit (CPU). Meanwhile, a separate quantum memory temporarily holds the information needed during calculations, allowing the processor to retrieve and modify it as necessary.
The major difference lies in how that information is stored.
"In our quantum working memory, however, information is not stored electromagnetically -- as is usually the case today -- but rather in the form of mechanical vibrations," explains Chu.
Quantum computers take advantage of unusual properties of quantum physics, including superposition, which allows quantum systems to exist in combinations of different states, and entanglement, which creates powerful connections between quantum states. These effects could eventually enable quantum machines to tackle certain extremely complicated calculations much faster than conventional computers, including some problems that are currently beyond their practical capabilities.
Why Vibrating Quantum Memory Could Be Better
One of the greatest challenges in quantum computing is maintaining precise control over quantum information. The states used for calculations are delicate, and even small disturbances can cause information to be lost. To perform calculations reliably, the processor and memory must interact closely enough to transfer and manipulate quantum states with high precision.
In the new system, microscopic structures called mechanical resonators hold information in particular patterns of vibration. When the superconducting qubit needs that information, it accesses the stored vibrational state, performs the required operation, and returns the modified information to memory.
Many existing quantum computers instead use electromagnetic memory alongside superconducting qubits. Researchers understand these technologies well, and they can be combined to provide extremely accurate control over quantum states, including reading, changing, and manipulating stored information.
However, electromagnetic memory systems have a significant disadvantage. They can occupy considerable space, making it difficult to expand experimental quantum devices into the larger, more capable computers that researchers and industries ultimately need.
Mechanical resonators offer several potential advantages. They are substantially smaller, allowing more compact designs. They can also support numerous different patterns of vibration, providing opportunities to store more information simultaneously than conventional electromagnetic memory.
Another important benefit is that mechanical vibrations can preserve quantum states for longer periods before the stored information begins to fade. Longer storage times could make it easier to carry out complicated calculations that require information to remain available throughout multiple processing steps.
New Quantum Computer Passes Major Tests
The research published in Science provides the first experimental demonstration that mechanical resonators can work together with superconducting qubits to carry out quantum computations. The results establish that vibration-based memory is a feasible alternative to electromagnetic storage.
The achievement goes beyond simply storing information. Chu's team demonstrated that its architecture can handle both relatively straightforward calculations and more demanding quantum operations.
To evaluate the system, the researchers tested two important computational techniques: the quantum Fourier transform and period finding. Both are fundamental tools in quantum computing and require a computer to coordinate multiple quantum states with considerable precision.
"The Quantum Fourier Transform is a fundamental computational procedure required for many quantum algorithms. The period-finding algorithm we implemented served as a demonstration of how this procedure can be used," explains Igor Kladaric, doctoral student in Chu's team and co-author of the publication.
Successfully completing these tasks requires the system to store, control, and maintain coherent relationships among multiple quantum states at the same time. The experiments showed that the new architecture can meet these requirements, providing strong evidence that it can support genuine quantum computation rather than simply function as a memory device.
A Promising Step Toward Powerful Quantum Computers
One of the most significant findings is that the new system can, in principle, carry out all the fundamental operations needed for arbitrary quantum computations. This means the architecture has the essential capabilities required for a programmable, general-purpose quantum computer.
However, demonstrating those capabilities in an experimental chip is only the beginning. The next major challenge is scaling the technology to larger systems with greater processing power while preserving the precision and reliability demonstrated in the laboratory.
Chu and her colleagues are continuing to investigate how their approach can be developed further. Its long-term success will depend on whether mechanical quantum memory can remain effective as more components and increasingly complex computations are added.
Practical quantum computers powerful enough for widespread scientific and industrial applications are still some distance away. Nevertheless, by showing that tiny mechanical vibrations can serve as compact, capable quantum memory, the ETH Zurich team has demonstrated a promising new route toward making those machines a reality.
Story Source:
Materials provided by ETH Zurich. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Yu Yang, Igor Kladarić, Martynas Skrabulis, Michael Eichenberger, Stefano Marti, Simon Storz, Jonathan Esche, Raquel García Bellés, Max-Emanuel Kern, Andraz Omahen, Arianne Brooks, Marius Bild, Matteo Fadel, Yiwen Chu. Mechanical resonator–based quantum computing. Science, 2026; 392 (6801): 972 DOI: 10.1126/science.aef4139
