articles.title: "Más adictivo que la historia principal": las telenovelas de Megamundo atrapan a los jugadores de 'GTA VI'
articles.text:
En uno de los primeros días tras el estreno de GTA VI, un usuario de Reddit presumió de haber visto la televisión de Leonida dos horas seguidas. Dicho de otro modo: la tele del juego funciona exactamente igual que una tele de verdad. Es solo un ejemplo de las múltiples distracciones que ofrece el mundo de 'GTA VI', escalofriantemente realista cuando el ocio resulta ser tan adictivo como su contrapartidas reales.
Culebrón tropical. Una parte de los más de 39 millones de jugadores únicos en PS5 y de las 683 millones de horas que se invirtieron en el juego según Sony, estuvo viendo el canal de Megamundo, la parodia de Telemundo que emite telenovelas en español. Una de ellas, 'El destino extiende sus alas', remite sin disimulo a 'Pasión de gavilanes', y pronto comenzaron a brotar reacciones de jugadores enganchados a capítulos de unos 20 minutos, en un canal que muchos dicen que es "más adictivo que la historia principal".
Dibujitos. Weazel, otra cadena ficticia de la saga, estrenaba también 'Macca & Friends', una serie animada protagonizada por un caimán rosa que, por cierto, viene como figura en la caja de coleccionista de 400 dólares. La serie cuenta con su propio trailer y no tiene nada que envidiar a las series de animación para adultos que vemos en streaming. El trailer juega también al mundo ficticio de Leonida, y fijaba el estreno para el día del lanzamiento del juego.
Remedy lo hizo antes. Este jugueteo no es nuevo: 'Max Payne 2' ya metía en sus televisores varias series completas, aunque breves, entre ellas unos dibujos animados protagonizados por la mascota oficiosa de la saga. Con 'Macca & Friends', sin embargo, este juego de espejos se ha hecho a lo grande: Rockstar North encargó episodios de 'Macc & Friends' a un estudio de animación externo, lo que da buena cuenta de la ambición y el cuidado por el detalle del estudio.
Solo fisgar. Desde antes del lanzamiento sabíamos que podríamos pasar las horas muertas fisgando redes sociales desde nuestro móvil. Snapmatic, la parodia de Instagram, va evolucionando y recibiendo actualizaciones según avanza el juego. Lo que realmente engancha, como en las redes sociales auténticas, son los comentarios que reciben los posts, tan mezquinos como los de cualquier red real. Jason y Lucia pueden seguir cuentas pero no publicar, un grado extra de sofisticación que tampoco habría sido muy de extrañar.
La vida cañón. Todo esto forma parte de un fenómeno más amplio, y que va más allá de las quejas de la manosfera porque hay que hacer demasiados recados domésticos para mantener viva la relación de Jason con Lucía. El juego te ofrece la posibilidad, aunque no te obliga, de hacer muchas, muchas más tareas intrascendentes. El streamer Stable Ronaldo pasó 40 minutos pintando el dormitorio y, al terminar, volvió a empezar porque temía que el azul le hiciera parecer un crío. Otro se quejaba de llevar seis horas cortándose el pelo, haciendo la compra y eligiendo flores sin haber robado un coche. Y en sus primeras 12 horas con el juego, nuestro compañero Alejandro Alcolea hablaba de cómo había invertido un rato en dar de comer a una serpiente llamada Dolores.
Biblioteca de barrio. Hay 34 revistas, libros y cómics, y hay que localizar y leer 30 de ellos para completar el juego al cien por cien. Entre ellos, libros infantiles o un volumen sobre la unidad militar ORCA. No es lo único con lo que pasar el tiempo sin coger un arma: podrás catalogar 62 especies de aves y, en casa, una consola, la JoySystem, con la que jugar en la tele del salón.
Parodia redonda. Para quienes jugamos a 'GTA VI', pero también disfrutamos del juego como espectadores, nos sentimos casi en el centro de un experimento mental cuando invertimos horas en ver a streamers jugar a un juego en el que a su vez pasan horas sumergidos en una actividad pasiva sin componente lúdico. Un uróboros con forma de laberinto de espejos que hace que nos replanteemos la fórmula de la sátira que poníamos en duda antes de la llegada del juego: con su agujero negro de horas, 'GTA VI' es la mejor parodia jamás vista de un mundo real en el que estamos esclavizados por la economía de la atención.

articles.title: Jensen Huang reveló a la junta directiva de Nvidia más relaciones extramatrimoniales antes de su regreso
articles.text:
Jensen Huang, cofundador y director ejecutivo de Nvidia, confirmó ante la junta directiva de la compañía nuevas relaciones extramatrimoniales durante una reunión, según reveló The Wall Street Journal. El encuentro se produjo horas antes de que los directores votaran por unanimidad su reincorporación al cargo, apenas 11 días después de haber renunciado.
El propio Huang ya había admitido semanas atrás una infidelidad vinculada a Alice Huang, una ejecutiva señalada por autoridades estadounidenses por presuntos nexos con inteligencia china. Pero la reunión del domingo sumó un capítulo que, según las fuentes citadas por el diario, va más allá de los dos vínculos que ya habían trascendido públicamente.
Qué reveló Huang ante la junta directiva
Durante el encuentro, los directores interrogaron a Huang durante varias horas sobre su conducta, su transparencia y su franqueza respecto a los episodios. Según el reporte, el ejecutivo mostró arrepentimiento por su comportamiento y reconoció “aventuras adicionales más allá de las dos que habían sido ampliamente reportadas”.
El texto no precisa el número exacto de relaciones adicionales ni la identidad de las personas involucradas, aunque otras coberturas periodísticas sugieren que la cifra total de vínculos alegados podría llegar a por lo menos cuatro.
Pese a la decisión de reincorporarlo, la junta concluyó que Huang había violado el código de conducta de la empresa, tanto por sostener esas relaciones como por no haberlas revelado a tiempo. La compañía indicó que la investigación independiente sobre si el directivo fue blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera continuará, con la cooperación plena del ejecutivo.
Según trascendió, Huang también se habría reconciliado con su esposa, Lori Huang, en paralelo a las conversaciones con el directorio.
Cuáles son las relaciones señaladas en los reportes
Antes de la confesión del domingo, Huang ya había sido vinculado con al menos tres relaciones extramatrimoniales. La primera, reconocida públicamente por el propio ejecutivo, involucra a Alice Huang, exejecutiva de la firma de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur Megaspeed, bajo investigación del Departamento de Comercio por posible desvío de chips hacia China.
The New York Times reportó posteriormente una segunda relación, esta vez con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de salud de Nvidia, quien reportaba directamente a Huang. Tras el anuncio de su renuncia, Reuters informó sobre una tercera relación con otra empleada de la compañía cuya identidad no fue revelada.
No está claro si las “aventuras adicionales” que Huang mencionó ante la junta el domingo incluyen a esta tercera empleada sin identificar o corresponden a vínculos completamente nuevos.
Jensen Huang ya regresó a Nvidia
La junta acordó el regreso de Huang, tras el respaldo del presidente Donald Trump, quien publicó en Truth Social que la reincorporación sería la mejor decisión “para la empresa, y también, para Estados Unidos”. El mandatario reconoció ante el Journal que había querido intervenir antes, pero dudaba de poder lograrlo: “El clima se volvió cada vez más propicio a medida que la acción de la compañía comenzó a derrumbarse”.
El fiscal general Todd Blanche le habría transmitido a Trump que Huang no era objeto ni blanco de una investigación del Departamento de Justicia y que no existía evidencia de que representara un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. En una llamada a CNBC, Trump afirmó que el directivo había sido “exonerado”: “Creemos que está bien, está absolutamente bien”, dijo, y lo calificó como un “tesoro nacional”.
En el comunicado oficial de reincorporación, el presidente de la junta, Harvey C. Jones, señaló que los directores “creen que Jensen es la persona indicada para liderar Nvidia” y que su regreso “es lo mejor para los accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes”. El propio Huang expresó sentirse “honrado de regresar a Nvidia” y agradeció el respaldo recibido durante la transición.
El lunes, al volver a la oficina, el ejecutivo recibió una bienvenida con ovaciones de empleados que coreaban “te amamos, Jensen”. La noticia de su reincorporación impulsó la acción de Nvidia más de un 31%, hasta 165,05 dólares, tras la caída registrada la semana anterior.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.text:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.
Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds
Understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.
However, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.
At RUN, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.
Tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.
To appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.
Making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.
Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling
To observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.
In the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.
The researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.
Simon Maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "By varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond."
This approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.
What makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.
This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.
"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.
A Surprising 500-Attosecond Delay
To understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with Prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit."
Their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.
At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.
For example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit."
The team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.
The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.
A Hidden Tradeoff Between Space and Time
Raffael Spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "The more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially."
In other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.
To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.
This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.
Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.
The findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.
Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?
Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.
One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.
Transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.
Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.
"In the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains Prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.
The implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.
"In the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant CMOS technology," adds Prof. Rupert Huber.
That possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.
For Repp and Huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.

Materials provided by University of Regensburg. Original written by Karoline Stürmer. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

articles.title: ¿A qué hora se estrena ‘Blade Runner 2099’ en Amazon Prime Video?
articles.text:
La nueva serie de Blade Runner 2099 por fin se estrena en todo el mundo para devolver a la mítica saga de ciencia ficción a su máximo esplendor. El filme original de Ridley Scott, que cumple ya casi 45 años, es una de las historias más legendarias del género. Tanto que en 2017 se estrenó una secuela, Blade Runner 2049, dirigida por Denis Villeneuve. Ahora, es turno de una tercera entrega, esta vez en forma de serie. Pero, ¿a qué hora y dónde se estrena Blade Runner 2099?
Cincuenta años después de los sucesos de la segunda película, Los Ángeles ha renacido, aunque no a manos de la humanidad. Cora, una fugitiva que intenta dejar de huir de una vez por todas, adopta una última identidad: la de Blade Runner. Obligada a asociarse con Olwen, una replicante a la que le quedan pocos días de vida, da caza a un fugitivo que oculta una verdad capaz de hacer colapsar su frágil ciudad.
En cuanto a dónde podrá verse, a diferencia de otros títulos, aquí no depende para nada del territorio. En Estados Unidos, España, Latinoamérica y en el resto del mundo, Blade Runner 2099 estará disponible únicamente en Amazon Prime Video. La plataforma de streaming alberga los derechos exclusivos del proyecto, que confían que sea uno de los mejores lanzamientos televisivos del año.
Hora de estreno de Blade Runner 2099
En cuanto a la hora de estreno de Blade Runner 2099, en Estados Unidos se emitirá el martes 24 de noviembre a las 21:00h E.T. En España y Latinoamérica, llegará a Amazon Prime Video en la conversión horaria de cada país:
- España: 3:00 h. del miércoles 25 de noviembre.
- México, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica: 20:00 h.
- Perú, Colombia, Panamá, Ecuador: 21:00 h.
- Venezuela, Bolivia, República Dominicana, Puerto Rico: 22:00 h.
- Chile, Paraguay, Argentina, Brasil, Uruguay: 23:00 h.
Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
A partir de ese momento, Amazon Prime Video estrenará simultáneamente los 8 episodios de Blade Runner 2099. Es decir, en lugar de optar por un estreno semanal, como con otros títulos, la compañía ha decidido lanzar toda la serie de golpe. Una manera de ofrecer a sus suscriptores la posibilidad de ver toda la historia del tirón y a su ritmo, sin tener que esperar siete largos días para ver cómo continúa.

articles.title: Amazon is knocking almost $50 off six months of Apple TV
articles.text:
Streaming deals aren’t as plentiful as they used to be, but they’re still around if you know where to look. One that caught our eye is an offer for Apple TV for those with an Amazon account in the US. Apple’s streaming service usually costs $14.99 per month, but following this page will let you get it for $6.99 for your first six months (totaling $42 versus $90 without the deal). Amazon hasn’t shared how long this offer will be available for, so I’d strike on it sooner than later.
Amazon is knocking almost $50 off six months of Apple TV
Instead of paying $14.99 per month, you can pay just $7 for six months when you subscribe through Amazon.
The subscription includes exclusive access to Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches, not to mention a bunch of acclaimed shows like Severance, Silo, The Morning Show, Pachinko, Pluribus, Slow Horses, and many more. (Yo Gabba GabbaLand is amazing for kids who enjoy music.) The service also somewhat recently added movies made outside of Apple’s studios, including classics like Arrival, Dead Poets Society, and Anchorman, to name a few. While the service is technically free of ads, Apple advertises plenty of its own original programming as skippable preroll ahead of content.

articles.title: GTA 6 : Rockstar a caché un très gros secret qui vient d’être découvert par les joueurs
articles.text:
Un portail caché dans GTA 6 qui permet de replonger dans le Vice City de 2002. Et, au bout de la quête, Jason, l’un des deux héros du jeu, repart avec la chemise hawaïenne de Tommy Vercetti et sa moto.
Pour les puristes prêts à retourner chaque mètre carré de Leonida, le studio a dissimulé un véritable voyage dans le temps, pensé comme un hommage à GTA Vice City.
Un portail secret caché derrière un code de triche de 2002 sur GTA 6
On doit la découverte au youtubeur australien Memeio, qui vient de mettre en lumière un easter egg de GTA 6 de grande ampleur La quête cachée commence dans la tour radio Badger R&D, à Key Lento, où un interrupteur affiche le logo du Malibu Club sur une télévision. Il faut ensuite activer, dans l’ordre, douze sous-stations électriques réparties sur la carte, sans voyage rapide ni changement de personnage. Les lettres peintes sur leurs murs forment « LIFEISPASSINGMEBY », le code de triche de GTA Vice City qui accélérait l’horloge du jeu. Un SMS envoie alors le joueur au réacteur 2 de la centrale de Turtle Head, à visiter entre 19 h et 6 h. Oui, le voyage dans le temps se mérite.
Un portail violet y apparaît. En le traversant, Jason quitte les graphismes réalistes de GTA 6 pour les personnages anguleux et les textures d’époque de la PlayStation 2. Il se retrouve dans le célèbre Malibu Club, recréé tel qu’il apparaissait il y a vingt-quatre ans. La nostalgie est là.
Danny Dyer reprend le rôle de Kent Paul
Tommy Vercetti n’apparaît pas en personne : seules sa chemise et sa moto reviennent, en guise de récompenses. Ray Liotta, qui lui prêtait sa voix, est mort en mai 2022. Pour la voix d’époque, Rockstar Games a rappelé l’acteur Danny Dyer, qui reprend le rôle de Kent Paul, l’impresario britannique survolté de Vice City.
Pour tenter l’aventure, il faut avoir atteint le chapitre 3 de l’histoire, qui ouvre toute la carte de Leonida.

articles.title: Thomson embarque Fire TV sur des TV LCD LED avec Alexa
articles.text:
Le système d’exploitation Fire TV réunit sur un seul écran d’accueil les services de streaming, les applications et les chaînes de télévision en direct. C’est un équivalent à Google TV, Tizen OS, webOS, Titan OS ou encore Vidaa. Chaque membre du foyer peut créer un profil individuel. Le téléviseur propose alors des recommandations adaptées aux goûts de chacun.
    Pour aller plus loin
Meilleure TV qualité/prix en 2026 : notre sélection de télés 4K pas chères à moins de 500 €
            
La télécommande Bluetooth intègre la commande vocale Alexa. D’après le fabricant, un appui sur le bouton microphone permet de rechercher un contenu, de lancer une application, de modifier des réglages ou de consulter la météo. Il autorise aussi le pilotage d’appareils connectés compatibles, une ampoule par exemple. Un tableau de bord Smart Home affiche ces équipements directement à l’écran. Des touches de raccourci donnent par ailleurs un accès direct à Prime Video, à Netflix et au navigateur Amazon Silk.
Les téléviseurs sous Google TV offrent des fonctions similaires, et les modèles Samsung sous Tizen OS proposent aussi une interface pour contrôler les objets connectés de la maison.
Immersion à 360° et design innovant : pour le Black Friday, la barre de son Samsung HW-Q995H passe à 890 € chez la Fnac, soit 600 € de remise.
Les applications telles que Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, YouTube, Spotify, Apple TV et DAZN sont accessibles. On peut également compter sur une compatibilité AirPlay, du Wi-Fi bi-bande (2,4 et 5 GHz), un port Ethernet et le Bluetooth 5.0.
Image HD ou Full HD, son Dolby et connectique
La marque propose deux définitions. Le 32HF2S34 est un modèle HD, avec une dalle LCD rétroéclairée par LED (Direct LED) de 1 366 x 768 pixels. Le 40FF2S34 est en Full HD, soit 1 920 x 1 080 pixels.
Les deux téléviseurs prennent en charge le format HDR10, la base dans ce domaine. Ce format améliore en théorie les contrastes et la richesse des détails. Thomson ne communique cependant pas la luminosité de ses dalles, qui affichent 8 bits et une fréquence de 50 Hz selon la fiche technique officielle. Sur ce type d’écran d’entrée de gamme, le bénéfice du HDR risque donc d’être modeste.
Côté audio, les deux téléviseurs décodent le Dolby Audio et le Dolby Digital Plus, ainsi que le DTS Virtual:X. Thomson indique une puissance de 12 watts (2 x 6 watts) pour le 32 pouces et de 16 watts (2 x 8 watts) pour le 40 pouces. Le triple tuner reçoit l’antenne terrestre, le câble et le satellite sans boîtier supplémentaire. Les deux ports HDMI 1.4 (dont un compatible ARC), le port USB 2.0 et le Bluetooth permettent de brancher consoles de jeux, barres de son et autres appareils.
Ces modèles visent le segment des petits écrans abordables. Face à eux, TCL et Xiaomi misent sur Google TV et Hisense sur Vidaa, souvent avec des dalles 4K à partir de 43 pouces, une taille où Thomson vend aussi des modèles 4K comme le 43QG7C14. Les Thomson misent plutôt sur Fire TV, sur Alexa et sur la garantie de 3 ans. Cette durée est supérieure aux deux ans légaux en vigueur dans l’Union européenne.
Disponibilité et prix des TV Thomson sous Fire TV
Le Thomson 32HF2S34 est affiché à 179,90 euros sur la boutique officielle de Thomson, tandis que le modèle de 40 pouces, le 40FF2S34, y est vendu 199 euros en promotion au lieu de 249 euros. On les trouve aussi chez Amazon, Cdiscount ou Darty, avec des prix qui varient selon les vendeurs.

articles.title: Ladybird, un navegador creado desde cero sin usar el motor de Chrome, ya se puede probar
articles.text:
Ladybird, un navegador de internet con un motor propio, escrito desde cero y no basado en el de Chrome, Safari ni Firefox, está disponible desde el 23 de noviembre en versión alfa para Mac y Linux. Su fundador, Andreas Kling, lo anunció en el sitio del proyecto. Una versión alfa es una primera etapa pública de pruebas.
Kling advirtió que algunas páginas no funcionarán y que el programa fallará a veces. También señaló que no hace promesas sobre la seguridad y pidió a los especialistas que intenten vulnerarlo e informen cómo.
El proyecto pide a los usuarios que reporten desde el propio navegador los sitios que se vean mal. Tras un cierre inesperado, el usuario puede leer el informe del error y decidir si lo envía. Los detalles figuran en la política de privacidad del proyecto.
Qué es un motor de navegador y por qué importa
El motor es la parte del navegador que lee el código de una página web y la convierte en lo que se ve en pantalla. El sitio de Ladybird sostiene que solo un puñado de motores sustentan toda la web y que cada uno depende de una empresa con intereses propios.
Este navegador se define como independiente: según su sitio, no es una bifurcación de Chromium, Gecko ni WebKit, los motores que usan Chrome y Edge, Firefox y Safari respectivamente, y no utiliza código de Blink, WebKit ni Gecko.
El proyecto surgió dentro de SerenityOS, un sistema operativo hecho por voluntarios. Phoronix, un medio especializado en software libre, informó que el navegador lleva cuatro años de desarrollo dedicado desde que se separó de ese proyecto.
La página del proyecto aclara que ya no sigue la cultura de escribirlo todo desde cero y que usa bibliotecas de terceros para tareas comunes, como formatos de imagen, audio y video, cifrado y gráficos, incluidas algunas que usan otros navegadores.
Sin publicidad ni acuerdos con buscadores
Ladybird cuenta con el respaldo de una organización sin fines de lucro con estatus 501(c)(3), figura legal de Estados Unidos. Según su sitio, no tiene “acuerdos de búsqueda por defecto”, monedas digitales ni otras formas de monetizar a los usuarios. Es gratuito y de código abierto.
Sus patrocinadores hacen donaciones sin condiciones, afirma el proyecto, y no tienen voz en la hoja de ruta técnica. El equipo de ingenieros a tiempo completo es pequeño. El proyecto dice que buscará mantener siempre 18 meses de fondos para operar.
Coherente con eso, el navegador no fija un buscador al abrirse: el usuario elige entre opciones como Google, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia o Kagi. Incluye un bloqueador de contenido, pero no admite extensiones ni importar datos de otros navegadores.
La versión se distribuye como canal de actualizaciones automáticas. Para Mac, OMG! Ubuntu precisa que solo funciona en equipos con chip Apple. En Linux hay un paquete Flatpak y repositorios para Ubuntu y Fedora, según Phoronix. Los desarrolladores web pueden probar sus sitios con WebDriver, una herramienta de pruebas automáticas.
El análisis de OMG! Ubuntu encontró un resultado desigual: las funciones básicas, como marcadores, historial y pestañas verticales, funcionan, pero incluso un video de YouTube en 480p se vio entrecortado, y no es apto para plataformas de streaming como Netflix o Spotify.
Windows no tiene versión todavía. El proyecto indica que sus ingenieros se concentran en Mac y Linux y que la compatibilidad con Windows llegará en una etapa posterior. Los teléfonos Android y iPhone tampoco son prioridad hasta que las versiones de escritorio estén más avanzadas.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.text:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.
The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.
Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult
Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.
This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.
"In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," says Egues.
To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.
The term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.
Although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.
"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.
A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal
The proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.
Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.
These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.
"In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.
The key to the new approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.
The researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.
Crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.
"It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.
How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information
To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.
One common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.
The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.
According to the new research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.
"Our study showed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.
This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.
A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage
Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.
Ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect."
The researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.
"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," says Egues.
This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.
That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.
Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor
The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.
Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.
Whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.
The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.
Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.
"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small."
The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially important. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.
Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance
In quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.
This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.
The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.
"Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.
The approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.
This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.
Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy
To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.
These calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.
The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.
According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.
The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.
However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.
Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?
Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.
The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.
What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.
"All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.
This makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain important challenges.
The research offers two potentially significant advances.
From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.
From a technological perspective, the study shows how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.
If future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.
More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.

articles.title: 1.5 Million Impacted by Data Breach at South Korean Electric Company KEPCO
articles.text:
South Korean state-owned electric company Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO, KRX: 015760, NYSE: KEP) has disclosed a data breach impacting approximately 1.5 million people.
The incident, the company says, involved KEPCO ON, its integrated customer service portal, and the supplier relationship management (SRM) platform, which handles procurement and service contracts.
KEPCO attributed the incident to an external attacker and noted the growing sophistication of AI-driven cyberattacks. It did not disclose how the attacker gained access or confirm that AI was used in this breach.
According to KEPCO, it suspended the affected services immediately after discovering the incident, blocked external access, conducted a thorough review of the relevant systems, and took remediation actions.
On November 20, the company confirmed that data was exfiltrated from its systems, including electricity customer and SRM user information.
From KEPCO ON, the hackers stole the personal information of 650,487 people, including names, addresses, phone numbers, unique ID numbers, customer numbers, card numbers and details, bank names, bank account numbers, account-holder names, card issuers, cardholder names, and billing/payment details.
Additionally, the information of 869,761 individuals was stolen from the SRM systems: the names, unique ID numbers, email addresses, and company addresses of 426,827; and the names, affiliation, employee IDs, email addresses, phone numbers, and company phone numbers of 442,934 (including KEPCO staff and partners’ employees).
The company has notified the affected individuals directly and reported the incident to the relevant authorities. It is also strengthening its security against AI-assisted attacks, and will share details on the exposure of financial information with government and financial institutions.
KEPCO’s disclosure followed a November 19 post on a dark web forum by a user operating under the handle Noiem, who reportedly claimed to have stolen KEPCO user and supplier data, as well as bidding and contract documents.
South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) has launched an investigation into the incident, noting that KEPCO received an email from the hacker, verified sample data received from the sender, and confirmed a dark web posting. PIPC has not attributed the data breach to Noiem.

articles.title: ¡Ya es oficial! ‘Ted Lasso’ tendrá temporada 5 en Apple TV
articles.text:
Tan solo unos pocos meses después del final de su temporada 4, Apple ha renovado oficialmente Ted Lasso para una temporada 5. Su exitosa serie regresará una vez más, curiosamente, después de que llegase a su presunto final en la tercera entrega hace unos años. la compañía y los fans pidieron que el proyecto continuase con nuevas historias y, finalmente, el equipo creativo liderado por Jason Sudeikis encontró la forma.
En la cuarta temporada, Ted regresaba a Ritchmond para entrenar al equipo femenino del club. Ahora, con la temporada 5 de Ted Lasso oficialmente en marcha en Apple TV, se espera que el proyecto continúe. En realida,d esta renovación tiene todo el sentido del mundo. Según la base de datos de Nielsen, el estreno de la cuarta temporada acumuló 296,6 millones de minutos de visionado en sus dos primeros días.
Estas cifras convirtieron a la temporada 4 de Ted Lasso en el estreno más visto de la historia de Apple TV. Por encima de cualquiera de las entregas anteriores y de otras series de éxito como Severance o For All Mankind. Ante un triunfo de esta magnitud, a la compañía no le quedaba otra opción que dar luz verde a una temporada más. Y es probable que próximamente también llegue una renovación para la sexta temporada, pues Sudeikis ya sugirió que le interesaba hacer un nuevo arco de tres entregas.
Qué pasará en la temporada de Ted Lasso
La cuarta temporada de la serie dejó algunos frentes abiertos sobre los que Ted Lasso deberá construir a partir de ahora en su temporada 5. Por ejemplo, Ted le dejaba el puesto de entrenadora del equipo femenino a Alice Chilton. A partir de los siguientes episodios, Ted solo será entrenador asistente junto a Beard.
Por otro lado, Roy Kent dejaba de ser el entrenador del equipo masculino al aceptar la oferta de entrenar al Chelsea. Además, Keeley y él esperan un hijo. Y, por su parte, Rebecca por fin se ha comprometido con Matthijs, así que es bastante probable que veamos la boda en la siguiente temporada.

articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La souris Logitech MX Master 4 Graphite à 99,99 €
Actuellement notée 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, la Logitech MX Master 4 brille par sa préhension agréable, ses deux molettes et ses clics silencieux au quotidien. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 99,99 € chez Amazon, Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 7 % et 7,99 € d'économie.
Logitech propose avec la MX Master 4 une souris pour la bureautique pensée pour optimiser la navigation au quotidien. Succédant à la MX Master 3, elle intègre une zone de retour haptique ainsi qu'un menu radial Active Ring configurable via l'application Logi Options+. Ce modèle s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo grâce à sa construction soignée et ses commandes complètes.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la Logitech MX Master 4 descend à 99,99 € chez Amazon, Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit environ 7 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (107,98 €). Cela représente une économie de 7,99 €.
Deux molettes et des commandes étendues pour le bureau
Cette souris s'adresse aux utilisateurs qui passent de longues heures devant des tableurs ou des logiciels de création. Comme l'a relevé notre test complet, la présence de deux molettes distinctes permet de gérer indépendamment le défilement vertical et le défilement horizontal. La liaison sans fil s'effectue au choix en Bluetooth ou via une connexion radio 2,4 GHz, complétée par un mode filaire si nécessaire.
Logitech MX Master 4
Points forts
- Préhension agréable.
- Construction de qualité.
- Intégration de l'Active Ring réussie.
- Clics silencieux.
- Deux molettes de défilement.
- Connectivité Bluetooth 2,4 GHz ou filaire.
Points faibles
- Non adaptée à toutes les mains.
- Assez lourde.
L'Active Ring au banc d'essai et un gabarit imposant
L'intégration de la fonction Active Ring offre un raccourci direct vers plusieurs outils personnalisables, ce qui accélère les actions répétitives en bureautique. Les clics restent discrets pour travailler en open space sans gêner ses collègues. Sa forme volumineuse et son poids marqué la destinent en revanche aux grandes mains, ce qui élimine les utilisateurs à la recherche d'une souris légère et compacte.
Logitech G502 X Plus : l'autre option face au Logitech MX Master 4
La Logitech G502 X Plus propose une formule différente, davantage orientée vers les jeux vidéo tout en restant utilisable au travail. Elle embarque des interrupteurs optiques hybrides, un capteur Hero 25K très réactif et de nombreux boutons programmables, même si son poids conséquent peut aussi se faire sentir après plusieurs heures.
Actuellement notée 5/5 dans nos tests, la Logitech G502 X Plus s'avère 20,00 € moins chère que la Logitech MX Master 4 remisée, mais cette dernière reste mieux équipée pour la productivité grâce à sa seconde molette horizontale.
Logitech G502 X Plus
Points forts
- Qualité de construction.
- Polyvalence gaming et bureautique.
- Nombreux boutons paramétrables.
- Molette inclinable et débrayable.
- Capteur très précis.
- Rétroéclairage bien intégré.
- Bouton "sniper" modulaire.
Points faibles
- Pas de version pour gauchers.
- Pas de Bluetooth.
- Un peu lourde pour du FPS.

articles.title: Firefox 161 updates that can help save time over the holidays
articles.text:
Lighten the holiday load with these four Firefox 161 updates
The holiday season, the festive season, the “how is the year almost over?” season. Whatever you call it, there’s a lot to get done. Gifts to buy, meals to plan, travel details to sort out, all while your regular responsibilities refuse to take time off.
In Firefox 161, we’re introducing a few new updates that can help you save time during the busiest months of the year, plus a new place to browse when you have a few minutes to cross something off your list. So you can cut down on the time spent prepping for the holidays, and get back to the people you’re doing it all for.
Set VPN rules for individual sites
Searching for the perfect gift? You might want to use a VPN to compare how prices differ by region. Sites like your bank or favorite streaming service, however, might work better without it.
Firefox’s free built-in VPN on desktop now lets you choose which sites automatically open with VPN on, and which open with it off. This way, your preferences are applied automatically, and you can save time skipping the constant toggling on/off every time you visit a different site.
Open the VPN panel from your toolbar and select Manage VPN rules, or go to Settings → Privacy & Security → VPN → Manage VPN rules. Add a website and choose Always on or Always off. Once a rule is set, that site will automatically open with your VPN preferences on future visits.
Bonus: VPN data is unlimited through January 31, 2027, so now’s the perfect time to experiment with rules and find the setup that works best for you. Check VPN availability in your region and sign in with a Mozilla account to get started.
Listen to pages when your hands are full
Already available on desktop, the ability to read pages aloud in Reader View is now rolling out on Firefox for Android. So when holiday prep keeps your hands busy, you can catch up on that article you’ve been saving while you untangle the tree lights, or hear the next step in your cookie recipe without getting flour on your phone.
On Android, tap the Reader View icon in the address bar, then tap the headphones icon in the pop-out menu. You can play, pause, rewind, fast-forward, adjust the playback speed, or choose a voice. You can even keep listening with your screen off. For added privacy, Firefox uses only voices that work directly on your device, so the page text and audio stay there.
Meet the Fire button in Classic Window: A faster way to start fresh
Anyone who shares a computer with family knows the risk: one stray autofill suggestion or search history entry, and the gift you spent weeks planning and searching for is no longer a surprise. Before you hand the computer over to the next person, press the 🔥 button in your desktop toolbar in Classic Window to help keep your gifts a secret until the big day.
If you’ve used the 🔥 button in Private Window, you’ll recognize the icon. There, it lets you quickly reset your private browsing session. It’s now gradually rolling out to Classic Window on desktop, where it does something different: it gives you easily accessible control over the data Firefox saves as you browse.
It’s always in reach, so you can clear your browsing and downloads history, cookies and site data, temporary files, saved form info, and website permissions and preferences directly from your toolbar. If you choose to delete everything, you’ll be signed out of sites and your current window will close, and Firefox will open a new one for you to start fresh. Because you’ve got enough to do without hunting through settings to clear it all.
If you don’t want to delete everything or close your open window, you can choose which browsing data to delete and your current window will remain open.
Browse Firefox from your car dashboard
You can now download the Firefox app directly from Google Play in cars with Google built-in. Whether you are waiting for your kid at school pick-up, charging your EV between long drives, or taking a breather in the parking lot before braving the holiday shopping frenzy, you can use Firefox right from your parked car’s dashboard. Less squinting at a mobile screen; more getting stuff done.
The best part? Our commitment to privacy comes along for the ride. Firefox is built on the principle that not even Mozilla should know which websites you visit or what you do there, and your browsing history will never be shared with the car manufacturer.
A little time back this holiday season
When your day is already full, even a few small shortcuts can help. We hope the new improvements in Firefox 161 make it easier to get things done online – not only during the holiday rush, but also long after the decorations come down.
To learn about the other new features released in Firefox 161, check out our newest release notes. And once you’ve given them a go, let us know what you think on Mozilla Connect.

articles.title: L'Asus ZenBook 14 s'affiche à 749,99 € à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'ordinateur Portable Asus ZenBook 14 (Snapdragon X) 16 Go / 256 Go à 749,99 €

Un écran OLED fidèle et une connectique adaptée au quotidien
Le principal atout de cet Asus ZenBook 14 réside dans son affichage. La dalle OLED affiche une excellente fidélité des couleurs avec un delta E mesuré à 2,6 par notre laboratoire, garantissant des teintes naturelles sans dérive visible à l'œil nu. L'ordinateur intègre également une connectique variée avec deux ports USB-C, un port USB-A et une sortie HDMI, ce qui évite de recourir systématiquement à des adaptateurs externes lors des déplacements professionnels. Points forts
- Châssis bien fini.
- Dalle Oled bien calibrée.
- Connectique complète.
- Autonomie correcte.
Points faibles

- Partie graphique très limitée.
- SSD d'entrée de gamme.
- Seulement 150 Go disponibles.
Quelques concessions sur la gestion des reflets et le stockage

- Partie graphique vaillante.
- Dalle Oled…
Points faibles

- Écran sujet aux reflets.
- Pas de wifi 7.

These are the gifts developers will actually want
The developer you’re shopping for hasn’t shared their holiday wish list with you yet? Check out these gifts, plus our Black Friday discount all week long.
Some people tell you exactly what they want for the holidays, but some people just don’t. The gifts, the decor, the food, for all of it, you have to guess at what they might like. You trawl thousands of gift guide lists titled “the definitive gift guide for 2026,” but none of the guides are quite right for that special person. That is, until this one came along.
As long as that person in your life is a developer.
We won’t say it’s the definitive guide for the developer in your life (or for yourself, we won’t judge), but we have brought together a few of our favorite pieces from the GitHub Shop for you to pick from.
Get building
At GitHub Universe this year we brought our brand new GitHub x Omnitype Bauer Lite Keyboard Kit to the Makerspace for our attendees to build. To say it was popular is an understatement. Each GitHub-exclusive Bauer Lite kit arrives in a randomly selected color combination and includes a hot-swap PCB with RGB underglow, Omnitype Hawk linear switches, dye-sublimated PBT keycaps, and the essential hardware and tools for a hands-on custom build. Get traveling

Super fans unite
